name: Chimborazo
blurb: At 20,548 ft its summit is the farthest point from Earth's center, thanks to the equatorial bulge. Look for its broad glaciated dome.

name: Damavand
blurb: At 18,406 ft, the highest volcano in Asia and the highest peak in Iran, a near-perfect cone just 40 miles from Tehran. Look for a white summit standing far above the Alborz range, often with a sulfur plume.

name: Denali
blurb: At 20,310 ft North America's highest peak. It rises about 18,000 ft from its base, a bigger base-to-summit climb than Everest's. Look for a white massif towering over everything else in the Alaska Range.

name: Dubai
blurb: From pearl-diving town to global city in about 50 years. Look for the Burj Khalifa, 2,717 ft and the tallest building in the world, and the palm-shaped artificial islands off the coast.

name: Grand Canyon
blurb: 277 miles long, up to 18 miles wide and over a mile deep, cut through rock nearly 2 billion years old at the bottom. Look for the thin green Colorado River in the depths and the forested North Rim, about 1,000 ft higher than the South.

name: Greenland ice sheet (east coast)
blurb: Up to about 2 miles thick, enough ice to raise global sea level about 24 ft if it all melted. Look for the edge where the white sheet breaks into glaciers flowing between black coastal mountains.

name: Greenland ice sheet (west coast)
blurb: About 660,000 square miles, up to about 2 miles thick. On the west side, summer melt leaves bright blue lakes on the surface. Look for turquoise pools and streams on white ice.

name: Hong Kong
blurb: More skyscrapers than any other city, packed between steep green hills and Victoria Harbour. Look for Victoria Peak above the towers, container ships in the harbor, and the airport on flattened, reclaimed Chek Lap Kok.

name: K2
blurb: At 28,251 ft the second-highest mountain on Earth and far harder and deadlier to climb than Everest; it wasn't climbed in winter until 2021. Look for a steep, near-perfect pyramid rising above the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers.

name: Kangchenjunga
blurb: At 28,169 ft, the third-highest mountain on Earth. The first climbers in 1955 stopped a few feet short of the top out of respect for local beliefs, a tradition many have kept. Look for a massive white wall with five summits.

name: Kilimanjaro
blurb: At 19,341 ft, Africa's highest point and the tallest free-standing mountain on Earth, rising about 16,000 ft above the surrounding plains. Look for the broad snowy summit of Kibo with its shrinking glaciers, often floating above cloud.

name: Matterhorn
blurb: At 14,692 ft, the Alps' most recognizable peak, its four faces lined up almost exactly with the compass points. Four of the seven men on the first ascent in 1865 died on the way down. Look for the lone crooked pyramid above Zermatt.

name: Mont Blanc
blurb: At about 15,770 ft, the highest peak in the Alps and western Europe, its summit an ice cap that grows and shrinks a few feet year to year. Look for the broad white dome and the Mer de Glace glacier snaking toward Chamonix.

name: Mount Cameroon
blurb: At about 13,250 ft the highest peak in West Africa, rising straight from the Gulf of Guinea coast in one of the wettest places on Earth. It erupts every couple of decades, including in 1999 and 2000.

name: Mount Erebus
blurb: At 12,448 ft the southernmost active volcano on Earth, with one of the few long-lived lava lakes anywhere. In 1979 Air New Zealand Flight 901 flew into its lower slopes on a sightseeing flight, killing all 257 aboard.

name: Mount Everest
blurb: 29,032 ft. At a 35,000 ft cruise you're only about a mile above the highest point on Earth.

name: Mount Fuji
blurb: Japan's highest peak at 12,388 ft, a near-perfect cone. When it last erupted in 1707, ash fell on Tokyo 60 miles away.

name: Mount Logan
blurb: Canada's highest peak at 19,551 ft, with possibly the largest base of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth. Its summit plateau is a vast icefield; look for the long white massif above the Seward and Hubbard glaciers.

name: Mount Rainier
blurb: At 14,411 ft it rises 13,000 ft above everything around it, the most prominent peak in the lower 48, and it carries more glacier ice than any other US mountain outside Alaska. Some Seattle-Tacoma suburbs sit on its old mudflows.

name: New York City
blurb: More than 8 million people in five boroughs. Look for the Hudson and East rivers as dark lines boxing in Manhattan's towers, and Central Park as a dark rectangle in the middle of the lights at night.

name: Puncak Jaya
blurb: At about 16,020 ft, the highest island peak on Earth and the summit of Oceania. It sits 4 degrees south of the equator yet still holds the last scraps of tropical glacier ice. The vast Grasberg mine scars the ridge next door.

name: Vinson Massif
blurb: At 16,050 ft the highest peak in Antarctica, in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains, first climbed in 1966. Look for a great white massif rising out of the ice sheet.

name: Aconcagua
blurb: At 22,837 ft the highest mountain outside Asia and the high point of both the Southern and Western Hemispheres. Flights between Santiago and Mendoza pass close by; look for the tallest snowy massif towering over the surrounding Andes.

name: Aletsch Glacier
blurb: The longest glacier in the Alps, about 14 miles, flowing past the Jungfrau region in a smooth curve. Look for the dark moraine stripes running its length like lanes on a white highway.

name: Baekdu Mountain
blurb: A 9,003-ft volcano on the China-North Korea border. Its eruption around 946 was one of the largest in recorded history. Look for Heaven Lake filling the caldera.

name: Baffin Island fjords
blurb: Baffin Island's east coast has some of the world's tallest sea cliffs, carved by glaciers into fjords lined with walls thousands of feet high. Look for deep blue fingers of water slicing into dark, flat-topped mountains.

name: Bangkok
blurb: More than 10 million people on the Chao Phraya River, once laced with canals. Look for the river looping through, the Grand Palace's gold roofs on the east bank, and Wat Arun's spire opposite.

name: Bogda Peak
blurb: At 17,864 ft the high point of the eastern Tian Shan, rising about 40 miles east of Urumqi. Look for a triple-crowned snow summit above the Turpan desert, with Heavenly Lake at its northern foot.

name: Chicago
blurb: The city built the first skyscrapers and reversed its own river in 1900. Look for the dead-straight lakefront, the grid running inland to the horizon, and the Willis Tower's stepped black profile.

name: Chongqing
blurb: A megacity on steep hills where the Jialing River meets the Yangtze, famous for its layered roads and trains through buildings. Look for the Yuzhong peninsula of towers at the confluence. At night its lights stack up the slopes.

name: Columbia Icefield
blurb: The largest icefield in the Rocky Mountains, about 125 square miles. Its meltwater reaches three oceans: Pacific, Atlantic and Arctic. Look for the Athabasca Glacier tongue reaching toward the Icefields Parkway.

name: Crater Lake
blurb: At 1,943 ft, the deepest lake in the US. It fills the hole left when Mount Mazama blew apart about 7,700 years ago. Look for Wizard Island, a cinder cone near the west rim.

name: Dhaulagiri
blurb: The world's seventh-highest peak at 26,795 ft. It faces Annapurna across the Kali Gandaki gorge, one of the deepest on Earth. Look for a huge white pyramid standing apart from its neighbors.

name: Dolomites
blurb: Pale dolomite rock that glows pink and orange at sunset, rising in sheer towers to 10,968 ft at the Marmolada. Look for the bright, almost white cliffs standing up out of green high meadows.

name: Eiger / Jungfrau
blurb: The Eiger's North Face drops about 5,900 ft, once the deadliest wall in the Alps. Next door is the 13,642-ft Jungfrau, with Europe's highest railway station tunneled up to the saddle below it. Look for the Aletsch Glacier flowing south.

name: Grand Teton
blurb: At about 13,770 ft it rises some 7,000 ft straight out of Jackson Hole with no foothills in between, the result of a fault that is still lifting the range. Look for the jagged spire at the center of the skyline.

name: Guangzhou
blurb: One of China's three biggest cities, on the Pearl River where it begins to spread into the delta. Look for the 1,982-ft Canton Tower with its pinched waist, and the river winding through towers. At night the tower lights in shifting colors.

name: Gunung Raung
blurb: At about 10,900 ft, one of Java's highest volcanoes, with a deep summit caldera over a mile wide. Its 2015 ash closed Bali's airport. Look for the smoking crater at Java's eastern end.

name: Hubbard Glacier
blurb: North America's largest tidewater glacier, about 75 miles long, ending in a calving face roughly 6 miles wide. Unlike most glaciers it has been advancing, and twice dammed Russell Fjord into a lake, in 1986 and 2002.

name: Ichinsky
blurb: The only active volcano in Kamchatka's Sredinny Range, about 11,800 ft and heavily glaciated. Look for a lone ice-covered massif rising from the forested spine of the peninsula, well inland from the eastern volcano chain.

name: Klyuchevskaya Sopka
blurb: This point marks Klyuchevskaya Sopka, at about 15,600 ft the highest active volcano in Eurasia and one of the most active anywhere. Look for a near-perfect snow cone with neighboring peaks clustered around it, often trailing steam.

name: Kluane Icefields
blurb: The largest icefield outside the polar regions, surrounding Mount Logan, Canada's highest peak at 19,551 ft. Look for an endless white plateau with glaciers flowing out in every direction.

name: Lake Louise / Banff peaks
blurb: Glacier silt called rock flour turns the lakes here a milky turquoise. Look for Lake Louise below the Victoria Glacier and, nearby, Moraine Lake under its ring of peaks, both vivid against dark forest and gray rock.

name: Malaspina Glacier
blurb: The world's largest piedmont glacier, a lobe of ice spread across about 1,500 square miles of coastal plain, bigger than Rhode Island. Look for the dark moraine stripes folded into zigzags across its surface.

name: Manaslu
blurb: The world's eighth-highest peak at 26,781 ft, its name means mountain of the spirit. Look for a tall white summit with long, corniced ice ridges.

name: Mount Agung
blurb: Bali's highest peak at about 9,900 ft and its holiest mountain. Its 1963 eruption killed over 1,000 people, and ash in 2017 shut the airport. Look for the tall cone with the Besakih temple complex on its slope.

name: Mount Ararat
blurb: Turkey's highest peak at 16,854 ft, a snowcapped dormant volcano tradition links to Noah's Ark. It rises about 14,000 ft above the plain, with smaller Little Ararat beside it; look for the giant white massif near the Armenian and Iranian borders.

name: Mount Blackburn
blurb: At 16,390 ft the highest peak in the Wrangell Mountains and the fifth-highest in the US, an old volcano worn down and buried in ice. The Kennicott Glacier pours off its flanks toward the ghost mine town of Kennecott.

name: Mount Cook / Southern Alps
blurb: New Zealand's highest peak at 12,218 ft. A 1991 rock avalanche knocked about 33 ft off its summit. Look for the triple-crested ridge and the long, gray Tasman Glacier on its east side.

name: Mount Elbrus
blurb: At 18,510 ft it's the highest peak in Europe, a dormant volcano with two summits and a cap of more than 20 glaciers. Look for the twin white domes standing clear of the main Caucasus ridge.

name: Mount Etna
blurb: Europe's tallest active volcano at about 11,000 ft, erupting so often that its height keeps changing. Look for a huge dark cone dominating eastern Sicily, often with a steam plume and black lava streaks.

name: Mount Hood
blurb: Oregon's highest peak at 11,249 ft, holding a dozen glaciers and skiable most of the year at Timberline Lodge. Look for the sharp snowy pyramid about 50 miles east of Portland, often the first Cascade peak you spot.

name: Mount Humboldt
blurb: New Caledonia's second-highest peak at about 5,300 ft. Its slopes are red, nickel-rich rock; New Caledonia holds some of the world's largest nickel reserves. Look for rust-red ridges with sparse scrub.

name: Mount Karisimbi
blurb: Rwanda's highest point at about 14,800 ft, the tallest of the Virunga volcanoes, on the border with Congo. Its summit is sometimes white with hail; look for the biggest cone in the chain, mountain gorilla habitat on its slopes.

name: Mount Kenya
blurb: Africa's second-highest mountain, an eroded volcano straddling the equator with its summit at about 17,060 ft. Glaciers survive near the top but are shrinking fast. Look for a jagged rock core above broad forested slopes.

name: Mount Kerinci
blurb: At about 12,480 ft, the highest volcano in Indonesia and the tallest peak on Sumatra. Look for a steep, steaming cone above tea plantations and rainforest in Kerinci Seblat park.

name: Mount Robson
blurb: At 12,972 ft the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies, rising nearly 10,000 ft above the valley along the Yellowhead Highway. Look for a massive layered wall usually wearing its own cloud cap, with Berg Glacier on the north side.

name: Mount Saint Elias
blurb: At 18,008 ft the second-highest peak in both the US and Canada, rising from the Gulf of Alaska only about 10 miles inland. Look for the lone sharp pyramid straddling the Alaska-Yukon border.

name: Mount Shasta
blurb: At 14,179 ft it rises about 10,000 ft above the surrounding land, visible for more than 100 miles. Look for the second cone, Shastina, on its west flank, and the Whitney Glacier, the largest in California.

name: Mount St. Helens
blurb: In 1980 the north face collapsed in the largest landslide ever recorded and took 1,300 ft off the summit. Look for the horseshoe crater opening to the north.

name: Mount Slamet
blurb: At about 11,250 ft, the second highest peak on Java and one of its most active volcanoes. Look for a broad, isolated cone towering over central Java's farmland.

name: Mumbai
blurb: Built on seven islands that were joined by centuries of landfill, now home to about 20 million people. Look for the Bandra-Worli Sea Link's cable-stayed towers and, at night, the curve of Marine Drive, called the Queen's Necklace.

name: Namcha Barwa
blurb: At 25,531 ft the eastern anchor of the Himalaya; the Yarlung Tsangpo wraps around its base in the Great Bend, carving one of the deepest gorges on Earth. Look for the river looping around the white massif.

name: Nanda Devi
blurb: At 25,643 ft, the highest mountain entirely in India, ringed by a near-continuous wall of peaks. In 1965 a CIA team lost a plutonium-powered spy device on its slopes that was never found. Look for a twin-summited white tower.

name: Nanga Parbat
blurb: At 26,660 ft, the world's ninth-highest peak, nicknamed Killer Mountain. Its Rupal Face rises about 15,000 ft, one of the tallest mountain walls on Earth. Look for a huge white massif standing apart at the western end of the Himalaya.

name: Norwegian fjords (Sognefjord)
blurb: Norway's coast is so carved by fjords that its full shoreline runs tens of thousands of miles. The Sognefjord, the longest and deepest, runs more than 120 miles inland and over 4,000 ft deep. Look for dark water threading between snowy plateaus.

name: Ojos del Salado
blurb: At about 22,600 ft the highest volcano on Earth, straddling the Chile-Argentina border in the driest corner of the Andes. Look for a pale, snow-streaked summit rising from tan and red desert.

name: Pico Basilé
blurb: At about 9,900 ft, the highest point in Equatorial Guinea, rising straight above the capital Malabo on Bioko Island. Look for a forested cone filling most of the island's north half.

name: Pico Cristóbal Colón
blurb: Colombia's highest peak, about 18,700 ft, only around 26 miles from the Caribbean in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the world's highest coastal range. Look for snow above tropical forest, with the sea in the same view.

name: Pico de Orizaba
blurb: Mexico's highest peak at 18,491 ft and the third-highest in North America, with the country's largest glacier. Look for a perfect white cone towering over everything between Mexico City and the Gulf coast.

name: Piton des Neiges
blurb: At about 10,070 ft, the highest point in the Indian Ocean, an extinct volcano on Reunion. Erosion carved three huge amphitheaters into it; look for the cirques of Cilaos, Mafate and Salazie radiating from the summit.

name: Popocatepetl
blurb: At about 17,800 ft, one of the world's most watched volcanoes: millions of people live within 60 miles of it, and it vents ash and steam almost constantly. Look for the steep snowy cone with a plume from its crater.

name: Rinjani
blurb: At about 12,220 ft, Lombok's giant. Its ancestor Samalas blew apart in 1257 in one of the largest eruptions of the past few thousand years. Look for the crescent crater lake with a young cone growing inside it.

name: Rio de Janeiro
blurb: Granite domes rise straight out of the city between ocean and bay: Sugarloaf at about 1,300 ft and Corcovado at about 2,300 ft, with Christ the Redeemer on top. Look for the beach crescents of Copacabana and Ipanema and the lagoon behind them.

name: San Francisco
blurb: Built on 49 square miles at the tip of a peninsula. Look for the Golden Gate Bridge to the north, Golden Gate Park as a long green strip to the ocean, and the skyline clustered at the Bay's edge.

name: Semeru
blurb: Java's highest peak at about 12,060 ft, puffing small ash clouds every few minutes for decades. Its 2021 eruption killed over 50 people. Look for the gray cone and plume south of the Bromo caldera.

name: Shanghai
blurb: About 25 million people, China's biggest city. Look for the Bund's old waterfront facing Pudong's towers across the Huangpu River, including the twisting Shanghai Tower, one of the tallest buildings in the world at 2,073 ft.

name: Shenzhen
blurb: A small border town until 1980, when it became China's first special economic zone; now well over 17 million people. Look for the Ping An Finance Center, one of the tallest buildings in the world, and Hong Kong just across the river.

name: Shiveluch
blurb: Kamchatka's northernmost active volcano and one of its most explosive; a 2023 eruption collapsed its lava dome and sent ash miles high. Look for a broad, scarred massif with a horseshoe-shaped collapse scar opening south.

name: Singapore
blurb: About 6 million people on an island nation of under 300 square miles. Look for Marina Bay Sands' three towers joined by a ship-shaped roof, and the strait crowded with anchored ships waiting on one of the busiest ports in the world.

name: Sydney
blurb: The 1932 Harbour Bridge's steel arch spans about 1,650 ft, and the Opera House's white shells sit on the point beside it. Look for the deep harbor branching into dozens of coves and bays.

name: Tambora
blurb: Its 1815 eruption was the largest in recorded history, killed tens of thousands and caused 1816's Year Without a Summer across Europe and North America. Look for the huge caldera, about 4 miles wide, on Sumbawa.

name: Tokyo
blurb: The world's largest metro area, about 37 million people. Look for the green square of the Imperial Palace, Tokyo Bay's reclaimed islands, and on clear days Mount Fuji's cone to the southwest.

name: Vatnajokull
blurb: Iceland's largest ice cap and Europe's second-largest, about 3,000 square miles, sitting on top of active volcanoes like Grímsvötn and Bárðarbunga. Look for white ice spilling down to the south coast in broad outlet tongues and black sand plains.

name: Volcán Tajumulco
blurb: At about 13,800 ft, the highest point in Central America. Look for the twin summit near the Mexican border, highest of the line of cones along Guatemala's Pacific side.

name: Wuhan
blurb: Three old cities where the Han River meets the Yangtze. Look for the Y-shaped river junction, the bridges across the Yangtze, and countless lakes, including East Lake, one of the largest inside any Chinese city.

name: Yosemite Valley / Half Dome
blurb: Half Dome's sheer granite face rises nearly 5,000 ft above the valley floor, and El Capitan's wall is about 3,000 ft. Look for the dome's flat cut side and the deep U-shaped valley carved by glaciers.

name: Arjuno-Welirang
blurb: A twin volcano south of Surabaya; Welirang means sulfur, and miners still carry yellow blocks down from its vents. Look for two connected peaks above the Malang highlands.

name: Austfonna
blurb: Svalbard's largest ice cap, with well over 100 miles of sea-facing ice cliff, one of the longest glacier fronts in the Northern Hemisphere. Look for a smooth white dome ending abruptly in a cliff line at the sea.

name: Bahamas banks
blurb: Shallow underwater banks so clear and bright that they glow turquoise even from cruise altitude. Look for the sharp edge where the pale shallows drop off into the deep blue Tongue of the Ocean.

name: Batura Sar
blurb: At about 25,570 ft, the highest peak of the Batura range in the Karakoram, above the Hunza Valley. Look for a long, ice-laden wall with the Batura Glacier below.

name: Belukha Mountain
blurb: At about 14,780 ft, the highest peak in Siberia and the Altai, on the Russia-Kazakhstan border. Look for twin snow summits and long glaciers, sacred to local Altai belief.

name: Bosphorus
blurb: A 19-mile strait splitting Istanbul between Europe and Asia, under half a mile wide at its narrowest. Look for three suspension bridges and lines of tankers threading the S-bends.

name: Bråsvellbreen
blurb: The southern lobe of the Austfonna ice cap, which surged in the 1930s and pushed its front miles out to sea. Look for a long, straight ice wall facing open water or sea ice.

name: Buntu Rantemario
blurb: Sulawesi's highest peak at about 11,400 ft, in the Latimojong range. Look for dense mountain forest above the Toraja highlands, famous for their boat-roofed houses.

name: Cerro Chirripó
blurb: At about 12,530 ft the highest point in Costa Rica, and on a clear morning you can see both the Pacific and the Caribbean from the top. Look for bare, glacier-carved summits above cloud forest.

name: Cerro del Bolsón
blurb: The high point of the Sierra de Aconquija, around 18,000 ft, a wall that rises out of the hot lowlands of Tucumán and Catamarca. Look for snow on the crest above green valleys on one side and desert on the other.

name: Changsha
blurb: Hunan's capital on the Xiang River. Look for Orange Isle, a long thin island splitting the river through the middle of town, and the green ridge of Yuelu Mountain on the west bank.

name: Chengdu
blurb: Sichuan's capital, home of the giant panda breeding base, fed by Dujiangyan, an irrigation system over 2,000 years old that still waters the plain. Look for concentric ring roads on a dead-flat plain, often under haze.

name: Cotopaxi volcano
blurb: At 19,347 ft one of the highest active volcanoes, a near-perfect cone with a glacier cap. Look for its white cone south of Quito.

name: Edgeøyjøkulen
blurb: The ice cap on Edgeøya, Svalbard's third-largest island, known for walruses and polar bears. Look for white domes over a low island, with outlet glaciers reaching the coast.

name: Emi Koussi
blurb: At about 11,200 ft the highest peak in the Sahara, a shield volcano in Chad's Tibesti mountains. Look for its huge summit caldera, several miles across, in otherwise empty desert.

name: Etonbreen
blurb: A big outlet glacier draining the west side of the Austfonna ice cap into Wahlenbergfjorden. Look for a wide white tongue ending in a fjord, often fringed with icebergs.

name: Faroe Islands
blurb: Eighteen steep, treeless islands in the North Atlantic, with cliffs dropping straight into the sea. Look for green slopes cut by dark basalt layers and narrow fjords between islands.

name: Finisterre Range
blurb: A coastal range in northern Papua New Guinea, uplifted so fast that ancient coral reefs now stand as terraces on the nearby Huon Peninsula. Look for steep ridges falling to the Vitiaz Strait.

name: Gangkhar Puensum
blurb: At about 24,800 ft the highest unclimbed mountain on Earth, and likely to stay that way: Bhutan has banned mountaineering on its high peaks out of respect for local beliefs. Look for a long, heavily glaciated massif on the Tibet border.

name: Getz Ice Shelf
blurb: A ribbon of floating ice about 350 miles long on the Marie Byrd Land coast, pinned between a string of islands. It sheds more meltwater into the warming ocean below than almost any other Antarctic ice shelf.

name: Glacier National Park
blurb: About 150 glaciers were here in 1850; only a couple of dozen remain. Look for knife-edge ridges, the Going-to-the-Sun Road cut into cliffs, and long glacier-carved lakes like Lake McDonald.

name: Great Barrier Reef
blurb: The largest coral reef system on Earth: about 2,900 reefs spread over 1,400 miles, visible from space. Look for turquoise patches and pale ribbons scattered across deep blue water offshore.

name: Greenland ice sheet
blurb: About 660,000 square miles of ice, up to about 2 miles thick, holding enough water to raise sea level about 24 ft. From above, a flat white expanse to the horizon.

name: Gunnbjørn Fjeld
blurb: At about 12,120 ft, the highest point in Greenland and the entire Arctic. It's a nunatak, a peak poking through the ice sheet. Look for dark rock summits above glaciers flowing to the east coast.

name: Gunung Binaiya
blurb: The highest point on Seram in the Moluccas at about 9,900 ft, inside Manusela National Park. Look for a limestone crest above unbroken rainforest running the length of the island.

name: Ha Long Bay
blurb: Around 1,600 limestone islands and pillars rise from emerald water in the Gulf of Tonkin, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for hundreds of jungle-topped towers scattered across the bay.

name: Haleakala
blurb: Rises to 10,023 ft, and its summit valley is 7 miles long and about 2,600 ft deep. Look for the rust-and-gray cinder cones scattered across its floor.

name: Hangzhou
blurb: Marco Polo called it the finest city in the world. Look for West Lake, ringed by green hills and causeways on the city's west edge, and the wide Qiantang River, famous for one of the world's largest tidal bores.

name: Hinlopenbreen
blurb: A large glacier calving into Hinlopen Strait, the channel separating Spitsbergen from Nordaustlandet. Look for a broad ice front facing the strait, with crevasse lines across the surface.

name: Hoover Dam / Lake Mead
blurb: Hoover Dam is 726 ft tall and holds back Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the US when full. Drought since 2000 has dropped the water so far that a white 'bathtub ring' of bleached rock lines the shore; look for it.

name: Ismoil Somoni Peak
blurb: At 24,590 ft, the highest mountain of the former Soviet Union, named Stalin Peak and then Communism Peak before Tajikistan renamed it. Look for an enormous glaciated massif above the Fedchenko Glacier region of the Pamirs.

name: Jabal an Nabi Shu'ayb
blurb: At about 12,000 ft the highest point on the Arabian Peninsula, just west of Sanaa. Look for terraced slopes climbing a bare ridge that is far greener than the desert to the east.

name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
blurb: About 18,360 ft, towering over the old town of Lijiang; its glaciers are among the southernmost in the Northern Hemisphere. Look for the jagged white ridge of 13 peaks rising out of green Yunnan hills.

name: Jakarta
blurb: One of the world's fastest-sinking cities: parts of the north drop several inches a year as groundwater is pumped out. Indonesia is moving its capital to Nusantara on Borneo. Look for the sprawl meeting the bay's sea walls.

name: Kongur Tagh
blurb: At 25,095 ft the highest peak in the eastern Pamir, towering over the Kashgar plain. It wasn't climbed until 1981. Look for a massive icy ridge just north of Muztagh Ata's rounded dome.

name: Koryaksky
blurb: A symmetrical cone of about 11,300 ft looming over Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, the peninsula's main city. Look for the sharp white peak just north of Avacha Bay, paired with the lower, flat-topped Avachinsky beside it.

name: Kronotsky
blurb: Often called one of the most perfect volcanic cones on Earth, it rises about 11,600 ft beside Kronotsky Lake in a nature reserve that also holds the Valley of the Geysers. Look for the sharp ribbed cone above a large lake.

name: Kuala Lumpur
blurb: The 1,483-ft Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004, and Merdeka 118 now tops them. The name means muddy confluence; look for the twin silver spires among green hills.

name: Lake Baikal
blurb: The deepest lake on Earth at 5,387 ft and the oldest, about 25 million years. It holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water. Look for the crescent shape, nearly 400 miles long, and Olkhon Island off the west shore.

name: Lake Como
blurb: Shaped like an upside-down Y, it's one of the deepest lakes in Europe, about 1,350 ft. Look for Bellagio at the point where the three arms meet, with Alps rising straight from the water.

name: Lake Geneva
blurb: One of the largest lakes in Western Europe, a 45-mile crescent shared by Switzerland and France. Look for Geneva at the western tip, where the Jet d'Eau fountain shoots about 460 ft into the air.

name: Lake Powell
blurb: Glen Canyon Dam created it in 1963, flooding a canyon country maze into a lake about 186 miles long. Look for a white bathtub ring on red rock walls, marking how far the water has dropped.

name: Lake Tahoe
blurb: About 1,645 ft deep, the second-deepest lake in the US, sitting at 6,225 ft in the Sierra Nevada. The water is so clear you can see down 60 ft or more. Look for the deep blue against granite peaks, and Emerald Bay's turquoise notch on the southwest shore.

name: Lanín
blurb: A lone, snow-covered cone of about 12,300 ft straddling the Argentina-Chile border, towering over the lakes and forests around it. It is the emblem of Argentina's Neuquén province.

name: Lofoten
blurb: Jagged granite peaks rising straight out of the Norwegian Sea above the Arctic Circle, with red fishing cabins along the shore. Look for a chain of saw-toothed islands trailing southwest.

name: London
blurb: About 9 million people along the Thames. Look for the river's loops past Parliament and the Tower, the towers of Canary Wharf on the Isle of Dogs, and the green rectangle of Hyde Park.

name: Manicouagan Crater
blurb: A ring lake about 45 miles across, filling what's left of a crater blasted by an asteroid some 214 million years ago. Look for the giant blue ring around a central island, easy to spot from cruise.

name: Margherita Peak
blurb: At 16,763 ft, the highest point of the Rwenzori, Africa's legendary Mountains of the Moon, and the third-highest summit in Africa. Its glaciers sit almost on the equator and are shrinking fast. Look for ice above dense cloud forest.

name: Mauna Kea
blurb: 13,803 ft above the sea, but over 33,000 ft from its base on the ocean floor, taller than Everest by that measure. Look for the white observatory domes clustered on the summit, sometimes under snow.

name: Mawson Peak
blurb: At about 9,000 ft, the highest mountain on Australian territory outside Antarctica, an active volcano on remote, glacier-covered Heard Island. Look for a white cone rising straight out of the Southern Ocean.

name: Mayon Volcano
blurb: Famous for the most symmetrical cone anywhere, about 8,080 ft, and one of the Philippines' most active volcanoes. Look for the perfect pyramid rising from flat farmland above Legazpi, often with a wisp of steam at the top.

name: Mercedario
blurb: About 22,000 ft, one of the highest peaks in the Andes, in San Juan province north of Aconcagua. Look for a big glaciated massif standing out from the brown, dry ranges around it.

name: Mont Saint-Michel
blurb: A medieval abbey crowning a tidal island, where tides among the strongest in Europe flood the bay in hours. Look for the pointed silhouette rising from vast tan sand flats, linked to shore by a thin bridge.

name: Monte San Lorenzo
blurb: Around 12,100 ft, the second-highest peak in Patagonia, on the Argentina-Chile border, heavily glaciated and wrapped in storms. Look for a broad ice-covered massif rising above the Patagonian steppe.

name: Monte San Valentin
blurb: At about 13,300 ft the highest peak in Patagonia, rising from the Northern Patagonian Ice Field. Look for a broad white dome above a sea of ice, with glaciers flowing toward Laguna San Rafael.

name: Monument Valley
blurb: Red sandstone buttes rising up to 1,000 ft from the desert floor, made famous by decades of Westerns. Look for the Mittens, two buttes with thin spires standing beside them like thumbs.

name: Moscow
blurb: Russia's capital grows in rings around the Kremlin: the Garden Ring, the Third Ring and the 68-mile MKAD beltway. Look for the Moskva River looping through and Stalin's seven wedding-cake towers.

name: Mount Adams
blurb: Washington's second-highest peak at 12,276 ft and, by volume, one of the biggest volcanoes in the Cascades. Look for the broad, rounded white bulk east of Mount St. Helens, much wider than it is pointed.

name: Mount Apo
blurb: The highest peak in the Philippines at about 9,700 ft, a dormant volcano with steaming vents above Davao City. Look for the broad forested summit, often cloud-capped, west of Davao Gulf.

name: Mount Assiniboine
blurb: An 11,870-ft pyramid on the BC-Alberta border, often called the Matterhorn of the Rockies. Look for a sharp horn shape standing above lakes and glaciers south of Banff.

name: Mount Baker
blurb: At 10,781 ft, after Rainier the most heavily glaciated of the Cascade volcanoes, and its ski area set a world record for snowfall in one season. Look for the white cone east of Bellingham, visible from Seattle and Vancouver.

name: Mount Balbi
blurb: The highest point on Bougainville Island, a volcano with steaming craters rising from dense rainforest. Look for a high ridge at the north end of the island's mountain spine, usually capped in cloud.

name: Mount Bazardüzü
blurb: At about 14,650 ft it's Azerbaijan's highest peak, and the Russian border runs over the summit, making it Russia's southernmost point. Look for snow and glaciers on the main crest of the Greater Caucasus.

name: Mount Cereme
blurb: At about 10,100 ft, the highest mountain in West Java, a lone cone near the coast at Cirebon. Look for a single tall volcano standing apart on the plain.

name: Mount Fairweather
blurb: At about 15,300 ft, it rises from sea level within about 15 miles of the Gulf of Alaska, one of the steepest coastal reliefs anywhere, and is the highest point in British Columbia. Look for glaciers pouring down to the ocean.

name: Mount Gahinga
blurb: The smallest of the Virunga volcanoes, about 11,400 ft, on the Rwanda-Uganda border, its gentle slopes covered in bamboo forest. Look for a low rounded cone beside the taller, sharp Muhabura.

name: Mount Gladstone
blurb: A high peak in the Finisterre Range of northern Papua New Guinea. Look for steep, jungle ridges dropping toward the Vitiaz Strait.

name: Mount Gongga
blurb: At 24,790 ft, Sichuan's highest peak and the easternmost mountain over 23,000 ft on Earth, rising more than 20,000 ft above the Dadu River gorge. Look for a sharp white pyramid towering over everything around it.

name: Mount Hayes
blurb: At 13,832 ft the highest peak of the eastern Alaska Range, clearly visible from Fairbanks on a clear day. Look for a heavily glaciated massif standing above the Tanana valley to the north.

name: Mount Kazbek
blurb: A 16,581-ft dormant volcano on the Georgia-Russia border, where Georgian legend chained Amirani, the local Prometheus. Look for the glaciated summit above the Darial gorge, with the tiny Gergeti Trinity Church on a ridge below.

name: Mount Lucania
blurb: At about 17,200 ft Canada's third-highest peak. Bradford Washburn and Robert Bates reached the top in 1937 and then had to walk out more than 150 miles. Look for the broad icy summit north of Mount Logan.

name: Mount Marcus Baker
blurb: At 13,176 ft the highest peak of the Chugach Mountains, wrapped in some of the biggest icefields in coastal Alaska. Look for the white summit above the Knik Glacier northeast of Anchorage.

name: Mount Meru
blurb: At 14,968 ft, Tanzania's second-highest mountain, about 45 miles from Kilimanjaro. Its east side collapsed in a huge prehistoric landslide; look for a horseshoe crater opening east with a younger ash cone growing inside.

name: Mount Pavlof
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes in the Aleutian arc, erupting every few years and often sending ash up to jet cruising altitudes. Look for the steep snowy cone beside its twin, Pavlof Sister, near the tip of the Alaska Peninsula.

name: Mount Ruapehu
blurb: The North Island's highest peak at about 9,180 ft, with ski fields on its flanks and a hot acidic lake in its crater. In 1953 a lahar from that lake caused the Tangiwai rail disaster, which killed 151 people.

name: Mount Siple
blurb: A huge shield volcano of about 10,200 ft rising straight from the ocean on Siple Island, off the coast of Marie Byrd Land. Look for a smooth white dome surrounded by sea ice.

name: Mount Taftan
blurb: A volcano near Iran's border with Pakistan, rising to about 12,900 ft over the Baluchistan desert, with sulfur vents still steaming at the summit. Look for a lone peak and yellow-stained crater.

name: Mount Waddington
blurb: At 13,186 ft the highest peak entirely in British Columbia, buried deep in the Coast Mountains behind huge glaciers. Look for a jagged rock spire rising out of icefields between the coast and the interior plateau.

name: Mount Whitney
blurb: At 14,505 ft the highest point in the lower 48, only about 85 miles from Badwater in Death Valley, the lowest. Look for the jagged granite crest rising like a wall above Owens Valley and the town of Lone Pine.

name: Mount Sumbing
blurb: At about 11,000 ft, one of Java's highest peaks, paired with its near-twin Sindoro across a saddle. Look for two big cones side by side with farm terraces climbing high up their slopes.

name: Na Pali Coast
blurb: Sea cliffs rising up to about 4,000 ft along Kauai's north shore, so steep no road has ever been built along them. Look for knife-edge green ridges and deep valleys dropping straight into the surf.

name: Nanjing
blurb: China's capital under the Ming and later the Republic. Its Ming city wall, about 22 miles around originally, is one of the longest ever built. Look for the Yangtze to the northwest and Purple Mountain to the east.

name: Nanning
blurb: Guangxi's capital, nicknamed the Green City for its tree-lined streets and parks. Look for the Yong River's big S-bends cutting through the city; at night it is a bright cluster ringed by dark hills.

name: Negribreen
blurb: A glacier on Spitsbergen's east coast that surged dramatically starting in 2016, speeding up many times over. Look for a heavily crevassed, broken surface where it meets Storfjorden.

name: Nile Valley / Pyramids
blurb: The Great Pyramid stood 481 ft tall and was the tallest structure on Earth for about 3,800 years. Look for three pyramids in a diagonal line on the desert edge, with Cairo's sprawl pressing right up against them.

name: Olav V Land
blurb: A largely ice-covered region of northeastern Spitsbergen, named for Norway's King Olav V. Look for broad white ice fields broken by dark nunataks and glaciers flowing out to the coast.

name: Panama Canal
blurb: About 50 miles from ocean to ocean, opened in 1914. Ships climb 85 ft through locks to Gatun Lake, once the largest man-made lake in the world. Look for lines of ships waiting at each end.

name: Paris
blurb: The Seine draws a long arc through the city, with the Île de la Cité in the middle. Look for the Eiffel Tower, the Arc de Triomphe with 12 avenues radiating from it, and the Périphérique ring road. At night it glows gold.

name: Penny Ice Cap
blurb: An ice cap of about 2,300 square miles in Auyuittuq National Park, a remnant of the ice sheet that once covered Canada. Look for a vast white plateau with glaciers draining to the fjords.

name: Pico Bolívar
blurb: Venezuela's highest peak at 16,332 ft, above the city of Mérida. Its glaciers have melted away, and Venezuela is now the first country in modern times to lose all its glaciers. Look for a jagged rock summit and the cable car line to neighboring Pico Espejo.

name: Pico Duarte
blurb: The highest peak in the Caribbean at about 10,100 ft, in the Cordillera Central of the Dominican Republic. Frost is common on top, a rare thing in the tropics. Look for pine-covered ridges above the cloud deck.

name: Pico do Fogo
blurb: Cape Verde's highest point at about 9,300 ft, a cone rising inside a huge caldera where villagers grow grapes. The 2014 eruption destroyed those villages; look for the dark cone and fresh black lava on the caldera floor.

name: Ras Dashen
blurb: Ethiopia's highest peak at about 14,900 ft, in the Simien Mountains. Its plateau breaks off in cliffs thousands of feet tall, home to gelada monkeys found nowhere else. Look for the sheer escarpments and deep gorges.

name: Rio de Janeiro bays
blurb: Rio wraps around Guanabara Bay between granite peaks and rainforest. Look for Sugarloaf at the bay's mouth, Copacabana's long curving beach, and the Christ statue on 2,300-ft Corcovado.

name: Ritacuba Blanco
blurb: About 17,700 ft, the highest peak of the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy, home to some of Colombia's last and fastest-shrinking glaciers. Look for a white crest above dark lakes and high páramo grassland.

name: Ross Ice Shelf
blurb: The largest ice shelf on Earth, a floating plate of ice about the size of France. Its seaward edge is a cliff about 400 miles long and up to 160 ft high, the Barrier that blocked early explorers.

name: Sabalan
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 15,780 ft in northwest Iran, Iran's third-highest peak. A small lake fills the summit crater and stays frozen much of the year. Look for a snowy cone standing alone over the plain.

name: Santorini caldera
blurb: A Bronze Age eruption around 1600 BC blew out the island's center and may have helped end Minoan Crete. Look for the drowned crater ringed by cliffs about 1,000 ft high, white villages along the rim, and dark new islands in the middle.

name: Sauyr Zhotasy
blurb: At about 12,500 ft the top of the Saur range, sitting right on the Kazakhstan-China border above dry steppe. Look for a snowcapped ridge rising out of brown semi-desert.

name: Seoul
blurb: Over 9 million people in the city and roughly half of South Korea in the wider metro. Look for the wide Han River crossing east to west under more than two dozen bridges, with granite mountains rising between neighborhoods.

name: Severny Island ice cap
blurb: Covers much of the northern island of Novaya Zemlya, one of the largest ice caps in Europe. The archipelago was the Soviet nuclear test site, including the 1961 Tsar Bomba. Look for a white dome cut by outlet glaciers.

name: Shenyang
blurb: Northeast China's largest city, home to Mukden Palace, built by the Manchu rulers before they took Beijing, and site of the 1931 Mukden Incident that opened Japan's invasion. Look for the Hun River along the south side.

name: Shishapangma
blurb: At 26,335 ft the lowest of the 14 peaks over 26,000 ft and the only one entirely inside Tibet. Look for a long icy summit ridge rising north of the main Himalayan crest.

name: Stikine Icecap
blurb: A large icecap straddling the Alaska and British Columbia border in the Coast Mountains, feeding glaciers that run down to the sea. Look for a white plateau broken by jagged peaks.

name: Table Mountain
blurb: A flat-topped wall about 3,560 ft high and nearly 2 miles across, standing right behind Cape Town. When the southeaster blows, cloud pours over the edge in a white sheet locals call the tablecloth.

name: Teide
blurb: At 12,188 ft, Spain's highest peak, and measured from the sea floor one of the tallest volcanoes on Earth. Look for the brown cone on Tenerife rising out of a vast caldera floor, often poking above a sea of cloud.

name: Terich Mir
blurb: At about 25,290 ft, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, towering over Chitral. Look for a huge, lone white pyramid with glaciers on all sides.

name: Thwaites Glacier
blurb: Roughly the size of Florida and nicknamed the Doomsday Glacier: it holds enough ice to raise sea level about 2 ft, and warm ocean water is melting it from below.

name: Tomort
blurb: A peak in the Karlik Tagh, the eastern end of the Tian Shan, above the Hami oasis. Look for a short snowy range standing out from the Gobi desert around it.

name: Toronto
blurb: The CN Tower, at 1,815 ft, was the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1975 to 2007. Look for it on the lakeshore, with the Toronto Islands sheltering the harbor and Billy Bishop airport.

name: Tupungato Volcano
blurb: A 21,500-ft giant east of Santiago. In 1947 the airliner Star Dust vanished in a storm near its summit; wreckage began emerging from a glacier on the mountain in the late 1990s, half a century later.

name: Uluru
blurb: A single sandstone monolith rising about 1,140 ft above flat red desert, nearly 6 miles around. Look for a lone rust-colored loaf with nothing else on the horizon, and the domes of Kata Tjuta about 16 miles west.

name: Venice lagoon
blurb: Venice is built on 118 small islands in a lagoon of about 200 square miles. Look for the city's fish shape, the 2.4-mile road and rail bridge to the mainland, and the long barrier island of the Lido.

name: Vestfonna
blurb: Svalbard's second-largest ice cap, covering the western half of Nordaustlandet. Look for a white dome with fjords cutting into its edges and a dark, bare coastline.

name: Vesuvius / Bay of Naples
blurb: In 79 AD it buried Pompeii and Herculaneum, and about 600,000 people now live in its red zone. Look for the cone inside the older Somma rim, rising above the curve of the Bay of Naples.

name: Xuelian Feng
blurb: "Snow Lotus Peak," about 21,700 ft, in the central Tian Shan, with several sharp summits arranged like petals. Look for a cluster of white peaks and long glaciers flowing off them.

name: Yushan Main Peak
blurb: At 12,966 ft, Taiwan's highest peak and taller than Mount Fuji, which is why Japan renamed it Niitakayama, New High Mountain. Look for a rocky crest on the island's central spine, sometimes dusted with snow.

name: Åsgardfonna
blurb: A large ice field in Ny-Friesland, northeastern Spitsbergen, named for the realm of the Norse gods. Look for a high white plateau feeding glaciers down to the fjords.

name: Abu Dhabi
blurb: The UAE's capital, built on islands in the Gulf. Look for the white domes of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Louvre's flat dome on Saadiyat Island, and the Yas Marina circuit.

name: Alsek Glacier
blurb: Ends in Alsek Lake near the mouth of the Alsek River, one of the few rivers that cuts all the way through the coastal mountains from Canada. Look for icebergs floating in the gray lake at the glacier's snout.

name: Altun Shan
blurb: At about 19,100 ft, the highest point in Gansu province, rising from the Altun range, the mountain wall between the Tarim Basin deserts and the Tibetan Plateau. Look for a glaciated summit above bare, dun-colored ridges with salt flats and dunes to the north.

name: Annapurna I
blurb: At 26,545 ft the 10th-highest peak, and in 1950 the first 8,000-meter peak ever climbed. Its avalanche-prone south face made it one of the deadliest mountains. Look for the long white wall north of Pokhara.

name: Aral Sea
blurb: Once the world's fourth-largest lake, it lost about 90% of its water after Soviet planners diverted its rivers for cotton in the 1960s. Look for a pale salt desert of old seabed where open water used to be.

name: Atlasov Island
blurb: A single volcano, Alaid, forms this whole island and at about 7,500 ft is the highest peak in the Kuril chain. Look for a nearly perfect cone rising straight out of the sea at the chain's northern end.

name: Baltoro Glacier
blurb: A 39-mile glacier leading to Concordia, ringed by four of the world's peaks over 26,000 ft, including K2. Look for a long ice river striped with dark medial moraines like lanes on a highway.

name: Barbeau Peak
blurb: At about 8,580 ft, the highest point in Nunavut and in all of eastern North America, on Ellesmere Island. Look for a peak barely breaking through the ice of a vast icecap.

name: Batura Glacier
blurb: One of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions, about 35 miles, ending near the Karakoram Highway at Passu. Look for a gray, rubble-covered ice tongue reaching down to the Hunza valley.

name: Beerenberg
blurb: The world's northernmost active volcano above sea level, rising about 7,500 ft straight out of the Arctic Ocean on remote Jan Mayen. Look for a glacier-covered cone with ice tongues reaching down to the sea.

name: Beijing
blurb: Laid out on a strict north-south axis around the Forbidden City, with ring roads in concentric squares out to the Sixth Ring. Look for the long yellow-roofed palace rectangle and Tiananmen Square at its south end.

name: Bryce Canyon
blurb: Not really a canyon but a row of eroded amphitheaters on a plateau edge above 8,000 ft, packed with thousands of orange hoodoo spires. Look for the bright orange scalloped rim against green forest.

name: Buni Zom
blurb: A peak of about 21,500 ft in the Hindu Raj range, east of Chitral. Look for a snowy crest above the Mastuj valley.

name: Busan
blurb: South Korea's second city and its biggest port, one of the busiest container ports in the world. Look for the city squeezed between steep hills and the sea, with the Gwangan Bridge arcing across the bay and Haeundae Beach just east.

name: Canyonlands
blurb: The Green and Colorado rivers meet here in a maze of canyons cut 2,000 ft into red rock. Look for the Island in the Sky mesa and the pale White Rim ledge tracing the canyons below it.

name: Cayambe
blurb: At about 18,996 ft its south slope is the highest point on the equator and the only place on it with snow. Look for its glaciers northeast of Quito.

name: Cerro El Manchao
blurb: The high point of the Sierra de Ambato in Catamarca, a dry range that rises sharply between desert basins in northwest Argentina. Look for a long brown ridge that may carry winter snow.

name: Cerro General Belgrano
blurb: The summit of the Sierra de Famatina, about 20,000 ft, above the old mining town of Chilecito, where a century-old cable car once hauled gold ore down the mountain. Look for snow above red and ochre slopes.

name: Cerro Macá
blurb: A glacier-covered volcano near the fjords of Chile's Aysén region, rising almost from sea level near Puerto Aysén. Look for its icy cone above the dense green forest and channels.

name: Cerro Tamaná
blurb: A high summit of Colombia's Western Cordillera, where the Andes drop into the rain-drenched Chocó forest toward the Pacific. Look for a forested crest often wrapped in cloud.

name: Chakragil
blurb: About 22,000 ft, a heavily glaciated peak in the Kongur group west of Kashgar. Look for steep ice faces rising almost straight from the desert edge.

name: Charleston Peak
blurb: At 11,916 ft, the highest point in Southern Nevada, only about 35 miles west of the Las Vegas Strip. Look for snow in winter above desert.

name: Cho Oyu
blurb: The world's sixth-highest peak at 26,864 ft, about 20 miles west of Everest on the Tibet border. Look for a broad, flat-topped white summit.

name: Dalian
blurb: A port at the tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, with Port Arthur, scene of the Russo-Japanese War, at its very end. Look for the city draped over green hills between deep bays.

name: Death Valley
blurb: Badwater Basin sits 282 ft below sea level, the lowest point in North America, and the valley holds the world's hottest recorded air temperature, 134°F. Look for the white salt flats on the valley floor.

name: Dempo
blurb: South Sumatra's highest volcano, with a greenish acid crater lake at the top and tea plantations wrapped around its lower slopes. Look for neat rows of tea giving way to forest and a steaming summit.

name: Dena
blurb: At about 14,470 ft, the highest peak of the Zagros Mountains. Look for a long, snowy ridge among the parallel folded ranges of southwest Iran.

name: Deriba Caldera
blurb: The summit crater of Jebel Marra, a volcano rising to about 10,000 ft out of the Darfur plains. Look for a round caldera holding two lakes, one inside a smaller crater.

name: Distaghil Sar
blurb: At about 25,870 ft, the highest peak of the Hispar Muztagh in the Karakoram. Look for an ice-covered summit above the long Hispar Glacier.

name: Doha
blurb: Wraps around a crescent bay with a 4-mile corniche. Look for the West Bay towers on the north shore, I.M. Pei's Museum of Islamic Art on its own island, and the reclaimed loops of the Pearl.

name: El Altar volcano
blurb: A collapsed volcano whose ring of jagged peaks holds a green crater lake, Laguna Amarilla. Look for the horseshoe of peaks.

name: El Mela
blurb: Only about 13,650 ft, but it rises nearly 9,600 ft above its surroundings, making it one of the most prominent peaks in Argentina. Look for a big bare massif in the dry ranges of La Rioja, rust and brown with little vegetation.

name: Florida Keys
blurb: The Overseas Highway runs 113 miles across about 40 bridges, including the Seven Mile Bridge. Look for a dotted line of islands and causeways arcing through turquoise water toward Key West.

name: Folgefonna
blurb: Norway's third-largest glacier, above the Hardangerfjord, where people ski in summer. Look for a long white ice cap on a plateau right above deep blue fjord water.

name: Foshan
blurb: An old crafts and manufacturing city joined to Guangzhou's west side so tightly the two read as one. Look for continuous city, factory roofs and fish ponds across the flat Pearl River Delta.

name: Fuyul Sojol
blurb: Central Sulawesi's highest mountain, about 9,500 ft, on the island's northern arm. Look for a forested ridge rising steeply from the coast, often lost in cloud.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
blurb: Its 4,200-ft main span was the world's longest when it opened in 1937. The color, International Orange, was chosen partly so ships could see it in fog.

name: Great Bear Lake
blurb: The largest lake entirely in Canada, about 12,000 square miles, straddling the Arctic Circle. Ice covers it for most of the year; look for its sprawling outline of five long arms meeting in the middle.

name: Great Salt Lake
blurb: A 1959 railroad causeway cut the lake in two. The saltier north half turned pink from salt-loving microbes; look for the ruler-straight line between the colors.

name: Great Slave Lake
blurb: North America's deepest lake at about 2,000 ft, with Yellowknife on its north shore. In winter, ice roads run across it; look for the dramatic East Arm, where the shore turns to rocky cliffs and islands.

name: Gunung Leuser
blurb: The namesake of Leuser National Park in northern Sumatra, about 10,200 ft. The surrounding forest is the last place where orangutans, tigers, rhinos and elephants live together. Look for unbroken green mountains.

name: Gurla Mandhata
blurb: At 25,243 ft it faces sacred Mount Kailash across Lake Manasarovar. Look for the huge snow massif rising directly from the lake's southern shore.

name: Gyala Peri
blurb: At 23,930 ft it faces Namcha Barwa across the Yarlung Tsangpo's Great Bend, the gorge between them more than three miles deep. Look for the twin massifs with the dark river slot between.

name: Hefei
blurb: Anhui's capital, which grew from a small city to over 9 million people and became a hub for science and electric vehicles. Look for the big Chao Lake just to the southeast.

name: Hekla
blurb: Medieval Europe called it the gateway to hell, and it has erupted at least 20 times since 1104. Look for a long ridge rather than a cone, often snow-streaked, with dark lava fields spread around it.

name: Hofsjökull
blurb: Iceland's third-largest glacier, a near-round ice dome in the empty highlands with a volcanic caldera hidden beneath it. Look for a white disk sitting alone in brown desert between the two bigger ice caps.

name: Houston
blurb: The fourth-largest US city and the biggest with no zoning code, so towers rise far from downtown. Look for the Ship Channel lined with refineries to the east and freeway interchanges stacked five levels high.

name: Huascarán
blurb: Peru's highest peak at 22,205 ft. In 1970 an earthquake-triggered avalanche off its north face buried the town of Yungay, killing about 20,000 people. Look for a huge twin-summited white mass above the Santa valley.

name: Hyderabad
blurb: City of the Nizams, built around the Charminar in 1591. Look for Hussain Sagar, a big lake with a giant Buddha statue standing in the middle, and the glass towers of HITEC City to the west.

name: Illimani
blurb: At about 21,100 ft, the four-summited wall that hangs over La Paz, the city's constant backdrop. Look for a long white ridge to the southeast if you fly into El Alto, with La Paz spilling down its canyon below.

name: Incheon
blurb: The tides here run over 30 ft at their extremes, which made MacArthur's 1950 landing such a gamble. Look for the 13-mile Incheon Bridge and Songdo's new towers on reclaimed land.

name: Istanbul
blurb: Straddles Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus. Look for the Golden Horn inlet, the domes and minarets of Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque on the old peninsula, and bridges strung between the continents.

name: Jabal Al-Majaz
blurb: One of the summits of southwestern Saudi Arabia's escarpment mountains, where the land climbs steeply from the Red Sea coastal plain to the Asir plateau. Look for terraced slopes and a sharp drop to the west.

name: Jebel Shams
blurb: Oman's highest peak at nearly 10,000 ft. Its edge drops into Wadi Ghul, called the Grand Canyon of Arabia. Look for a deep gorge slicing the bare brown range.

name: Jinan
blurb: The City of Springs: dozens of artesian springs feed Daming Lake in the middle of town. Look for the lake, and the Yellow River running past the north edge of the city, raised between high levees.

name: Jiuding Shan
blurb: About 16,400 ft, the highest peak of the Longmen range, the mountain wall that rises abruptly from the western edge of the Sichuan Basin. On rare clear days it is visible from Chengdu. Look for snow above a sudden escarpment.

name: Kamet
blurb: At 25,446 ft, near the Tibet border; when Frank Smythe's team summited in 1931 it was the highest peak anyone had climbed. Look for a big pyramid-shaped massif with the Tibetan Plateau's brown country beyond.

name: Koyo Zom
blurb: At about 22,550 ft, the highest peak of the Hindu Raj range, on the Chitral-Gilgit border. Look for icy peaks above deep valleys.

name: Kronebreen
blurb: One of the fastest-flowing glaciers in Svalbard, calving into Kongsfjorden near Ny-Ålesund, one of the world's northernmost settlements. Look for a wide ice front with brown meltwater plumes in the fjord.

name: Kuh-e Bandaka
blurb: At about 22,300 ft one of the highest peaks of the Hindu Kush in northeastern Afghanistan's Badakhshan. Look for a big glaciated summit standing apart among brown, deeply cut ranges.

name: Kīlauea
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes on Earth; its 2018 eruption destroyed about 700 homes and collapsed the summit crater. Look for the Halemaumau pit inside the caldera and black lava fields running to the sea.

name: Kūh-e Hezār
blurb: About 14,770 ft, one of the highest peaks in Iran, rising out of the desert of Kerman province. Look for a snowy summit above bare, brown country.

name: Lake Balkhash
blurb: A crescent about 375 miles long that is fresh in the west and salty in the east, the two halves joined by a narrow strait. Look for the color shift along the long curve across the Kazakh desert.

name: Lake Erie
blurb: The shallowest Great Lake, averaging just 62 ft deep, so it warms fastest in summer and is prone to vivid green algae blooms. Look for the long hook of Long Point jutting from the Ontario shore.

name: Lake Huron
blurb: The second-largest Great Lake, with more shoreline than any other thanks to roughly 30,000 islands, including Manitoulin, the largest island in any lake. Look for Georgian Bay's rocky, island-scattered east side.

name: Lake Ladoga
blurb: Europe's largest lake, about 6,800 square miles. In the Siege of Leningrad its ice carried the Road of Life, the only supply route into the city. Look for the island-strewn skerries of the northern shore.

name: Lake Malawi
blurb: About 360 miles long and over 2,000 ft deep, it holds more fish species than any other lake, most of them brightly colored cichlids found nowhere else. Look for the Livingstone Mountains walling its northeast shore.

name: Lake Maracaibo
blurb: Often called South America's largest lake, though it's really a brackish bay open to the Caribbean. Thousands of oil wells dot it, and Catatumbo lightning flashes over its south end on many nights. Look for the 5-mile bridge across its narrow north neck.

name: Lake Michigan
blurb: The only Great Lake entirely inside the US, joined to Lake Huron at the Straits of Mackinac so the two are really one lake. Look for the tall sand dunes lining much of the eastern shore.

name: Lake Ontario
blurb: The smallest Great Lake by area but deep, reaching 802 ft. It takes the Niagara River's water and sends it out the St. Lawrence. Look for Toronto's skyline on the northwest shore.

name: Lake Superior
blurb: The largest freshwater lake on Earth by area, about 31,700 square miles, holding roughly 10% of the world's surface fresh water. It could cover North and South America in a foot of water. Look for its wolf's-head shape.

name: Lake Tanganyika
blurb: The world's longest freshwater lake at about 410 miles, and the second deepest at about 4,800 ft. Look for a long, narrow lake filling the floor of the Rift Valley between steep walls.

name: Lake Victoria
blurb: Africa's largest lake, about 23,000 square miles, roughly the size of West Virginia. The White Nile leaves it at Jinja, Uganda. Look for a sea-sized lake with island-filled bays.

name: Lake Winnipeg
blurb: About 9,400 square miles, one of the largest lakes in the world and a leftover of glacial Lake Agassiz. In summer, algae blooms streak it green, visible from orbit. Look for the narrow waist between its north and south basins.

name: Langjökull
blurb: Iceland's second-largest glacier, about 70 miles from Reykjavík, with a tourist ice tunnel bored into it. Look for a long white dome with dark lava fields and the Thingvellir rift valley to its southwest.

name: Las Vegas
blurb: A metro of over 2 million in the Mojave, with almost nothing around it. At night look for the bright grid of the valley floor surrounded by pitch-black desert, and the Strip as the brightest stripe down the middle.

name: Lednik Shmidta
blurb: The ice cap that buries almost all of Schmidt Island, a lonely speck in the Kara Sea off Severnaya Zemlya. Look for a smooth white dome rising out of sea ice, ending in low ice cliffs at the shore.

name: Leighbreen
blurb: An outlet glacier on Nordaustlandet in the far northeast of Svalbard. Look for white ice reaching down to a coastline that is frozen or ice-choked for much of the year.

name: Lenin Peak
blurb: At 23,406 ft on the Tajik-Kyrgyz border, one of the most climbed 7,000-meter peaks in the world. In 1990 an avalanche here killed 43 climbers. Look for a broad white dome above the grassy Alay Valley.

name: Llullaillaco
blurb: At about 22,100 ft one of the highest volcanoes on Earth. In 1999 archaeologists found three Inca child mummies near its summit, frozen so well they are among the best-preserved ever found.

name: Lomonosovfonna
blurb: One of Svalbard's highest ice fields, drilled by scientists for ice cores holding centuries of climate history. Look for a broad white plateau feeding glaciers in every direction.

name: Los Angeles
blurb: A basin of nearly unbroken city between the mountains and the Pacific. Look for the downtown tower cluster, the Hollywood Hills, and freeways running to every horizon. At night it's an endless orange grid.

name: Macculloch Glacier
blurb: An outlet glacier in northern Baffin Island. Look for a white tongue curling between dark plateaus toward a fjord or sea ice.

name: Makati City
blurb: Manila's financial district, where many of the Philippines' biggest companies have their headquarters. Look for the tight cluster of towers along Ayala Avenue, the largest skyline in the country.

name: Makushin Volcano
blurb: The broad, glacier-capped volcano on Unalaska Island, looming over the fishing port of Dutch Harbor. It steams regularly and has been studied as a geothermal power source for the town.

name: Marapi
blurb: One of Sumatra's most active volcanoes, above the town of Bukittinggi. A surprise eruption in December 2023 killed two dozen hikers. Look for the bare, ash-gray summit paired with Singgalang across the valley.

name: Maromokotro
blurb: Madagascar's highest peak at about 9,440 ft, in the remote Tsaratanana massif in the north. Look for rugged forested mountains rising above the red, eroded hills of the plain.

name: Melbourne
blurb: The Rip, the mouth of Port Phillip, is only about 2 miles wide, so the bay reads almost like an inland sea. Look for the Yarra winding into a tight downtown grid and the long West Gate Bridge over the river mouth.

name: Merapi
blurb: Indonesia's most active volcano, looming over Yogyakarta, with hundreds of thousands of people living on its flanks. Its 2010 eruption killed more than 300. Look for the gray, ash-streaked cone and its growing lava dome.

name: Miami
blurb: Look for Biscayne Bay and its chain of man-made islands, the long Miami Beach barrier island, and the thick cluster of Brickell towers on the bay. West of the city the Everglades start abruptly.

name: Monacobreen
blurb: Named for Prince Albert I of Monaco, who funded Arctic expeditions here, it calves into Liefdefjorden in northwest Spitsbergen. Look for a wide ice front, often with a brown sediment plume in the fjord.

name: Monarch Mountain
blurb: About 11,600 ft, a broad summit rising from its own ice cap in the Coast Mountains above Bella Coola. Look for a big rock dome surrounded by glaciers flowing in every direction.

name: Moncong Lompobatang
blurb: An old volcano of about 9,400 ft just southeast of Makassar, the high point of Sulawesi's southern tip. Look for a broad, eroded cone with farmland climbing its lower slopes.

name: Mono Lake
blurb: A salty, alkaline lake at least 760,000 years old, more than twice as salty as the ocean. When Los Angeles diverted its streams in 1941 the level dropped, exposing tufa towers. Look for the black and white islands in the middle.

name: Mount Aragats
blurb: At 13,420 ft the highest point in Armenia, an old volcano whose four summits ring a collapsed crater. Look for a broad snowy massif northwest of Yerevan, across the valley from Mount Ararat.

name: Mount Arfak
blurb: The high point of the Arfak Mountains, about 9,600 ft, on the Bird's Head of New Guinea above Manokwari. The forest here is famed for birds of paradise. Look for green ridges and the twin Anggi lakes.

name: Mount Athos
blurb: A marble peak of about 6,670 ft rising straight from the sea at the tip of a peninsula home to some 20 Orthodox monasteries, where women have been barred for a millennium. Look for the lone pyramid at the end of the finger.

name: Mount Bona
blurb: At 16,550 ft the highest volcano in the US and the fourth-highest peak, almost completely buried under ice. Glaciers flowing off it feed the great ice fields straddling the Alaska-Yukon border.

name: Mount Chiginagak
blurb: A glacier-clad volcano on the Alaska Peninsula. Around 2005 an acidic lake formed in its summit crater, then burst out and sent acid water downstream, killing the fish in a lake below.

name: Mount Elbert
blurb: At 14,440 ft the highest point in Colorado and the entire Rocky Mountains, rising above Twin Lakes near Leadville. Look for a broad, rounded giant rather than a sharp spire, the tallest in the Sawatch Range.

name: Mount Elgon
blurb: An extinct volcano on the Uganda-Kenya border with one of the largest intact calderas in the world and a base about 50 miles across. Look for the huge ring of peaks around a high, flat crater floor.

name: Mount Erciyes
blurb: Central Anatolia's highest peak at about 12,850 ft, looming over Kayseri with a ski resort on its flanks. Its ancient eruptions helped lay down the soft rock that became Cappadocia's fairy chimneys; look for the lone snowy massif south of the city.

name: Mount Francais
blurb: The highest peak of Anvers Island off the Antarctic Peninsula, rising more than 9,000 ft above the sea near Palmer Station. Look for an ice-clad summit above glaciers calving into the water.

name: Mount Giluwe
blurb: At about 14,330 ft, Papua New Guinea's second-highest mountain and one of the highest volcanoes in Oceania. Look for a broad dome of grassland rising over the highlands.

name: Mount Griggs
blurb: A steaming, glacier-streaked volcano on the edge of the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes in Katmai National Park. Look for the gray ash-filled valley left by the 1912 Novarupta eruption at its foot.

name: Mount Halcon
blurb: About 8,500 ft, the highest point on Mindoro and one of the hardest climbs in the Philippines, with steep slopes cloaked in rainforest. Look for a dark green massif often capped in cloud.

name: Mount Iliamna
blurb: A 10,000-ft volcano across Cook Inlet from the Kenai Peninsula, almost always trailing a wisp of steam from summit vents. Look for the glaciated cone rising straight up from the inlet's west shore.

name: Mount Jefferson
blurb: Oregon's second-highest peak at 10,497 ft, a steep, glaciated spire deep in wilderness with no easy route to the top. Look for the jagged white summit standing alone between Mount Hood and the Three Sisters.

name: Mount Kapalatmada
blurb: The highest point on Buru in the Moluccas, about 8,900 ft. Look for a forested massif at the island's northwest, rising steeply from the sea.

name: Mount Kirkpatrick
blurb: At about 14,900 ft one of the highest peaks of the Transantarctic Mountains. Fossils of Cryolophosaurus, a crested Jurassic dinosaur, were found near its summit. Look for dark rock bands above the ice.

name: Mount Kosciuszko
blurb: Australia's highest mainland peak at 7,310 ft, named by a Polish explorer for Tadeusz Kosciuszko. It's a gentle summit you can walk up. Look for rounded, treeless tops, snowy in winter.

name: Mount Minto
blurb: At about 13,700 ft the highest peak of the Admiralty Mountains in northern Victoria Land. Look for a white summit above glaciers flowing toward the Ross Sea.

name: Mount Oku
blurb: At about 9,900 ft the highest peak in Cameroon's grasslands, with a crater lake near its summit. It belongs to the same volcanic field as Lake Nyos, whose gas burst killed about 1,700 people in 1986.

name: Mount Paget
blurb: At 9,629 ft, the highest point on South Georgia, rising straight out of the Southern Ocean and buried in glaciers. Look for a jagged white crest with ice flowing down to the sea on both sides.

name: Mount Parry
blurb: At about 8,300 ft the highest point of Brabant Island in the Palmer Archipelago off the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for an ice-capped island rising steeply from the sea.

name: Mount Pelée
blurb: Its 1902 eruption wiped out Saint-Pierre, then Martinique's largest town, killing about 28,000 people in minutes. One famous survivor was a prisoner in a thick-walled cell. Look for its cloud-capped summit over the island's north end.

name: Mount Pico
blurb: Portugal's highest mountain at about 7,700 ft, a volcano rising straight from the Atlantic on Pico Island in the Azores. Look for a sharp cone, often poking above the clouds, with black lava vineyards along the shore.

name: Mount Popomanaseu
blurb: Often given as the highest peak in the Solomon Islands, on the forested spine of Guadalcanal. Look for the highest ridges of the island's interior, usually cloud-covered.

name: Mount Pulag
blurb: At 9,606 ft, the highest peak on Luzon and third highest in the Philippines, famous for its sea of clouds at dawn. Look for grassy, bald summit slopes above pine forest in the Cordillera.

name: Mount Saramati
blurb: At about 12,550 ft, the highest peak in Nagaland, straddling the India-Myanmar border in the Naga Hills. Look for a high crest, sometimes snow-dusted in winter, above deep, forested valleys.

name: Mount Sibbald
blurb: A high peak of New Zealand's Southern Alps, east of the main divide near Lake Tekapo's headwaters. Look for glaciated summits above braided gray riverbeds.

name: Mount Sidley
blurb: At about 14,000 ft the highest volcano in Antarctica, with a huge caldera breached on its south side, in Marie Byrd Land. Look for the semicircular crater wall above the ice sheet.

name: Mount Siguniang
blurb: At 20,505 ft, the highest of the Four Girls Mountains, four peaks in a row west of Chengdu said to be four sisters. Look for a steep snow summit leading a line of lower white peaks.

name: Mount Sir Sandford
blurb: About 11,500 ft, the highest peak in the Selkirk Mountains, a sharp horn above big icefields north of Rogers Pass. Look for a steep summit standing above the glaciers around it.

name: Mount Sir Wilfrid Laurier
blurb: About 11,500 ft, the top of the Premier Range in the Cariboo Mountains, where peaks are named for Canadian prime ministers. Look for a glaciated massif west of the Yellowhead Highway near Valemount.

name: Mount Stephenson
blurb: At about 9,800 ft the highest point of Alexander Island, the large island off the west side of the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for a white summit above an island locked in sea ice.

name: Mount Suckling
blurb: A summit of about 12,000 ft in the Owen Stanley Range in southeastern Papua New Guinea. Look for cloud-wrapped ridges above dense rainforest.

name: Mount Süphan
blurb: Turkey's second-highest volcano at about 13,300 ft, on the north shore of Lake Van. Look for a broad snowy cone rising from the shoreline of the huge, deep blue soda lake.

name: Mount Tagubud
blurb: A forested summit in the mountains of eastern Mindanao, part of the rugged spine that runs along the island's Pacific side. Look for unbroken dark green ridges and deep river valleys.

name: Mount Torbert
blurb: At about 11,400 ft the highest peak of the Tordrillo Mountains, a glaciated volcanic range across Cook Inlet west of Anchorage. Look for the ice-covered massif beside its neighbor, Mount Spurr.

name: Mount Tullu Demtu
blurb: Ethiopia's second-highest peak at about 14,360 ft, on the Sanetti Plateau of the Bale Mountains, the largest stretch of Afro-alpine land in Africa and stronghold of the rare Ethiopian wolf. Look for a broad, treeless high plateau.

name: Mount Victoria
blurb: Highest point of the Owen Stanley Range at about 13,250 ft, roughly 45 miles north of Port Moresby. Look for a high ridge above deep, jungled gorges.

name: Mount Vineuo
blurb: The high point of Goodenough Island, one of the most precipitous islands on Earth, rising about 8,300 ft in a few miles. Look for a dark island rising straight from the sea.

name: Mount Vsevidof
blurb: A tall, symmetrical snow cone at the southwest end of Umnak Island in the eastern Aleutians, rising about 7,000 ft straight out of the stormy North Pacific.

name: Mount Wilhelm
blurb: Papua New Guinea's highest peak at 14,793 ft. On a clear day you can see both the north and south coasts from the summit. Look for a rocky crest with small lakes in glacial valleys.

name: Mount Argopuro
blurb: An old volcano of about 10,100 ft in East Java, crossed by one of the longest hiking routes on the island. Look for a broad forested massif with grassy meadows near the top.

name: Muztagh Ata
blurb: "Father of Ice Mountains," 24,757 ft, so smooth and rounded that people ski down from the summit. Look for the broad white dome beside Karakul Lake and the Karakoram Highway.

name: Nanchang
blurb: Jiangxi's capital, where the 1927 Nanchang Uprising marks the founding of the People's Liberation Army. Look for the Gan River with Tengwang Pavilion on its bank, flowing north to Poyang Lake.

name: Nevado de Colima
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 14,000 ft, the twin of Volcán de Colima next door, one of the most active volcanoes in Mexico. Look for the older, higher peak with a smoking cone just to its south.

name: Nevado de Toluca
blurb: At about 15,350 ft, Mexico's fourth-highest peak, with two lakes, the Sun and the Moon, inside its crater. Look for the bowl breached on its east side and the lakes within it.

name: Nevado del Huila
blurb: At about 17,600 ft the highest volcano in Colombia, which woke up in 2007 after centuries of quiet. Look for a long, glaciated ridge of summits in the Central Cordillera, sometimes with a steam plume.

name: Nevado del Ruiz
blurb: In 1985 a small eruption melted summit ice and sent mudflows down a valley that buried the town of Armero, killing about 23,000 people. Look for the glaciated summit above Colombia's coffee country.

name: Niagara Falls
blurb: Horseshoe Falls is about 2,600 ft wide, and much of the river is diverted around it to power plants, more at night than by day. Look for the curved Canadian falls and the white mist plume rising between two downtowns.

name: Oliver Glacier
blurb: An outlet glacier in northern Baffin Island, in country with almost no people for hundreds of miles. Look for a white ice tongue between dark, flat-topped plateaus.

name: Opala
blurb: A remote volcano in southwestern Kamchatka, set apart from the main eastern chain with a large caldera beside it. Look for an isolated snowy summit rising from empty tundra and forest.

name: Osaka
blurb: Japan's merchant city and kitchen. Look for Osaka Castle in its moats, and Kansai International on its artificial island in Osaka Bay, built in the 1990s.

name: Palmer Archipelago
blurb: A chain of mountainous, ice-covered islands off the west coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, including Anvers and Brabant. Look for glaciated peaks rising from channels full of icebergs.

name: Panama City
blurb: A dense skyline on the Bay of Panama at the canal's Pacific entrance. Look for the arch of the Bridge of the Americas over the canal, the Amador Causeway, and ships anchored offshore waiting their turn.

name: Peak la Selle
blurb: Haiti's highest point at about 8,790 ft. Pine forest still covers some of its slopes in a country that has lost most of its trees. Look for the green ridge east of Port-au-Prince near the Dominican border.

name: Perito Moreno Glacier
blurb: Its 3-mile-wide front stands about 240 ft above Lago Argentino, and it periodically dams the lake until the ice bridge collapses in a spectacular rupture. Look for the jagged ice wall against milky turquoise water.

name: Pico da Bandeira
blurb: About 9,480 ft, and for a long time believed to be Brazil's highest point until surveys in the 1960s found higher peaks in the Amazon. Look for bare granite summits above the green Serra do Caparaó.

name: Pico da Neblina
blurb: At about 9,800 ft the highest point in Brazil, on the Venezuelan border in the Amazon, named for the mist that hides it so often it wasn't identified as the country's top until the 1960s. Look for a dark peak rising out of rainforest.

name: Pico de São Tomé
blurb: The highest point of São Tomé and Príncipe at about 6,600 ft, a volcanic summit buried in cloud forest. Look for the high forested center of the island, near the dramatic volcanic plug of Pico Cão Grande to the south.

name: Pidurutalagala
