blurb: Sri Lanka's highest point at 8,281 ft, above the hill town of Nuwara Eliya and its tea estates. The summit holds a military radar and TV masts and is closed to the public. Look for neat green tea terraces on the slopes below.

name: Pik Dankova
blurb: At about 19,600 ft, one of the highest peaks of the Kokshaal-Too range on the Kyrgyzstan-China border. Look for a heavily glaciated crest above the Tarim Basin's desert edge.

name: Pik Karla Marxa
blurb: About 22,000 ft, the highest peak of the Shakhdara range in the southwestern Pamirs, looking across the Panj River into Afghanistan. Look for a broad, glacier-covered summit above deep gorges.

name: Pinatubo
blurb: Its 1991 eruption was the second-largest of the 20th century and cooled the whole planet by about 1 degree F for a year. Look for the turquoise crater lake and the gray ash valleys fanning out across central Luzon.

name: Puncak Mandala
blurb: One of the highest peaks in New Guinea at about 15,600 ft, the top of the Jayawijaya range. It once carried an ice cap that has since melted away. Look for bare rock summits above the clouds.

name: Qingdao
blurb: A German concession from 1898 to 1914, which left it red-roofed villas and Tsingtao beer. Look for the Jiaozhou Bay Bridge, one of the longest bridges over water in the world, crossing the bay west of the city.

name: Salar de Uyuni
blurb: The largest salt flat on Earth, about 4,000 square miles at nearly 12,000 ft. It's so flat that satellites use it for calibration, and after rain it becomes a giant mirror. Look for blinding white with no visible edge.

name: Salcantay
blurb: At 20,574 ft it towers over Machu Picchu, which sits at the end of a ridge running off its flank, and the popular Salkantay trek to the ruins crosses a pass just below its ice. Look for the lone glaciated summit standing apart from the green ranges around it.

name: San Gorgonio Mountain
blurb: At 11,503 ft the highest point in Southern California, above San Gorgonio Pass and its wind farms. Look for a broad bare summit, often snowy in winter, north of the I-10 corridor to Palm Springs.

name: San Jacinto Peak
blurb: At 10,834 ft, its north face drops about 10,000 ft to the desert in a few miles, one of the steepest escarpments in North America. Look for the granite wall right above Palm Springs and the aerial tramway line up its side.

name: San Pedro
blurb: At about 20,200 ft one of the highest active volcanoes on Earth, paired with its older neighbor San Pablo in the Atacama. Look for the twin peaks joined by a high saddle above the desert.

name: Sara Sara
blurb: A remote glaciated volcano in Peru's southern Andes, about 18,000 ft, where archaeologists recovered an Inca child sacrifice in the 1990s. Look for an isolated snowcapped massif above deep canyons and dry plateau.

name: Seattle
blurb: Squeezed onto an isthmus between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, with Lake Union in the middle. Look for the 605-ft Space Needle, and floating bridges carrying highways across Lake Washington.

name: Socompa
blurb: A volcano of about 19,800 ft on the Argentina-Chile border. Thousands of years ago its side collapsed in one of the largest known landslides, spreading a fan of debris far across the desert to its northwest.

name: Suzhou
blurb: Called the Venice of the East for its canals and classical gardens. Look for Lake Tai to the west, Jinji Lake's modern district to the east, and the arched Gate of the Orient tower, nicknamed the Big Pants.

name: Sydney Harbour
blurb: One of the world's great natural harbors, a drowned river valley with countless coves and bays. Look for the Harbour Bridge's steel arch and the white sails of the Opera House on the point beside it.

name: Talgar peak
blurb: At about 16,330 ft, the highest peak of the Trans-Ili Alatau, the range that forms Almaty's backdrop. Look for a glaciated summit due southeast of the city.

name: Taranaki Maunga
blurb: A near-perfect cone of about 8,260 ft standing alone on New Zealand's west coast. The national park boundary is nearly a circle, so look for a round ring of dark forest against green farmland around the peak.

name: Tatamailau
blurb: Timor-Leste's highest point at about 9,720 ft, topped by a statue of the Virgin Mary that pilgrims climb to before dawn. Look for a grassy summit ridge above deeply eroded valleys.

name: Three Sisters
blurb: Three volcanoes over 10,000 ft lined up north to south, the tallest of them South Sister at 10,358 ft. Look for the trio of snowy peaks in a row west of Bend, with smaller Broken Top beside them.

name: Tianjin
blurb: Beijing's port city. Look for the Hai River winding through the center past old foreign concession buildings, and the Tianjin Eye, a Ferris wheel built on a bridge over the river.

name: Tolbachik
blurb: A pair of volcanoes, flat-topped Plosky and pointed Ostry, whose fissure eruptions in 1975 and 2012 poured out vast lava fields. Look for black lava flows spreading across the forest south of the Klyuchevskaya group.

name: Triglav
blurb: Slovenia's highest peak at 9,396 ft, so central to national identity that its three-headed outline is on the flag. Look for a gray limestone summit with a huge north face dropping into the Vrata valley.

name: Tronador
blurb: The name means Thunderer, for the boom of ice avalanches off its glaciers. An extinct volcano of about 11,400 ft on the border west of Bariloche; look for a broad ice-capped massif above Lake Nahuel Huapi.

name: Ulawun
blurb: One of Papua New Guinea's most active volcanoes, a tall, steep cone on New Britain's north coast. Look for a symmetrical peak rising straight from the shore, often with a plume of steam or ash.

name: Vancouver
blurb: Mountains rise straight from the sea on the city's north side. Look for the forested Stanley Park peninsula, the Lions Gate Bridge across the harbor mouth, and the glassy towers of the downtown peninsula.

name: Xiamen
blurb: An island city linked to the mainland by bridges and causeways, with Gulangyu island just off its west shore. Look for the round island, the busy harbor, and Kinmen, held by Taiwan, only a few miles east.

name: Yellowstone Lake
blurb: At 7,733 ft, the largest lake above 7,000 ft in North America, and its West Thumb bay is itself a volcanic caldera. It freezes over for about half the year. Look for geyser basins steaming along the west shore.

name: Zhuhai
blurb: A coastal special economic zone next to Macau, the start of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, about 34 miles long including an undersea tunnel. Look for the bridge snaking across the Pearl River estuary.

name: Zhupanovsky
blurb: Not one peak but a ridge of four overlapping cones, roughly 9,600 ft, north of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky. Look for a long snowy crest with several summits in a line rather than a single cone.

name: Zion Canyon
blurb: The Virgin River carved this canyon about 15 miles long with sandstone walls up to 2,000 ft high, in places only a few dozen feet apart at The Narrows. Look for the deep red and cream slot.

name: Abercrombie Mountain
blurb: At about 7,300 ft one of the highest summits in Washington's Selkirk Mountains, just south of the Canadian border. Look for a bare, rounded crest above the Pend Oreille and Columbia valleys.

name: Acotango
blurb: A volcano of about 19,900 ft on the Bolivia-Chile border, one of the three snowy Quimsachata peaks near Sajama National Park. Look for the glaciated cone above the brown altiplano.

name: Aj Bogd
blurb: Highest peak of the Gobi-Altai range, rising above the desert in southwest Mongolia. This is the last refuge of the Gobi bear, one of the rarest bears on Earth. Look for a dark massif surrounded by tan gravel plains.

name: Aleutian volcanoes
blurb: The Aleutian arc strings dozens of active volcanoes along more than 1,000 miles of islands between Alaska and Kamchatka. On a clear day look for snowy cones lined up across the sea like stepping stones.

name: Amalfi Coast
blurb: A 30-mile stretch on the south side of the Sorrento Peninsula where pastel towns cling to cliffs above the sea. Look for lemon terraces and Positano spilling down the slopes, with Capri off the western tip.

name: Anamudi
blurb: At about 8,840 ft, the highest peak in India south of the Himalayas. Its grassy slopes are home to the rare Nilgiri tahr. Look for a rounded summit above the tea estates of Munnar.

name: Andes near Santiago
blurb: The snowy wall east of Santiago rises over 17,000 ft within about 30 miles of the city. On a clear day, Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia at 22,838 ft, stands out to the north.

name: Antisana volcano
blurb: A glaciated volcano of about 18,700 ft east of Quito whose watershed helps supply the city's water. Look for its broad white summit.

name: Antofalla
blurb: A volcano topping 20,000 ft in the Puna de Atacama, one of the driest high plateaus on Earth. Look for the dark peak above white salt flats and red and ochre lava slopes.

name: Api
blurb: Far western Nepal's highest peak at about 23,400 ft, near the border with India and Tibet. Look for a snowy summit above deep valleys.

name: Arenal
blurb: A near-perfect cone that erupted almost constantly from 1968 to 2010; its first blast destroyed the village of Tabacón. Look for the lake beside it.

name: Askja
blurb: A caldera in Iceland's highland desert where Apollo astronauts trained in the 1960s. Look for the blue lake Oskjuvatn, one of Iceland's deepest, and beside it the small milky-turquoise Viti crater.

name: Ata Kang La Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the mountains of southeastern Tibet, one of the wettest, most heavily glaciated corners of the plateau. Look for white ice spilling from high ridges into green, forested valleys.

name: Atlas Mountains (Toubkal)
blurb: Jebel Toubkal, 13,671 ft, is the highest peak in North Africa, and its snow is visible from Marrakech about 40 miles away. Look for the white crest rising straight out of the brown plain.

name: Ausangate
blurb: A 20,945-ft sacred peak, the highest near Cusco, where thousands of pilgrims climb to its glaciers each year for the Qoyllur Rit'i festival. The striped Rainbow Mountain sits on its flank; look for the broad ice cap above red and ochre hills.

name: Bairiga
blurb: A glaciated peak of nearly 23,000 ft in the eastern Nyenchen Tanglha of southeast Tibet. Look for a cluster of sharp white summits above deep, forested valleys.

name: Baja California / Sea of Cortez
blurb: The peninsula runs about 775 miles, separated from mainland Mexico by the Gulf of California, which Jacques Cousteau called the world's aquarium. Look for bare desert mountains dropping straight into deep blue water.

name: Balneário Camboriú
blurb: Brazil's answer to Dubai: a small beach town packed with some of the tallest residential towers in Latin America. The towers shade the sand in the afternoon, so the beach was widened in 2021. Look for a wall of high-rises on a curved bay.

name: Ben Nevis / Highlands
blurb: At 4,413 ft, the highest mountain in the British Isles, and its summit is in cloud most of the year. A weather observatory operated on top from 1883 to 1904. Look for the huge cliffs of the north face above Glen Nevis and Fort William.

name: Big Sur coast
blurb: About 90 miles where the Santa Lucia Mountains plunge into the Pacific, one of the longest stretches of undeveloped coast in the lower 48. Look for Highway 1 clinging to the cliffs and its arched bridges over canyons.

name: Bilafond Glacier
blurb: A Karakoram glacier on the front line of the Siachen conflict between India and Pakistan, under Bilafond La pass. Look for a white ice river between steep, snowy ridges.

name: Blue Mountain Peak
blurb: Jamaica's highest point at about 7,400 ft. The range's cool, misty slopes grow Blue Mountain coffee, one of the world's priciest. Look for the green ridge east of Kingston, often under cloud.

name: Bonneville Salt Flats
blurb: A remnant of ice-age Lake Bonneville, so flat you can see the Earth's curvature, and the site of land speed records for over a century. Look for a vast blinding white floor west of the Great Salt Lake.

name: Braldu Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the north side of the central Karakoram, flowing toward the remote Shaksgam valley. Look for a long, debris-streaked ice river in a sea of jagged peaks.

name: Brammah Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Kishtwar Himalaya flowing off Brammah, a steep granite peak. Look for a gray, rubble-streaked ice river winding between sharp, snowy ridges.

name: Bárðarbunga
blurb: A huge volcano hidden under the Vatnajokull ice cap. Its 2014 to 2015 fissure eruption at Holuhraun was Iceland's largest in over 200 years; look for that dark new lava field north of the ice edge.

name: Calar Gallinero
blurb: A high, flat-topped summit in the dry ranges of Almería and Granada in southeastern Spain, some of the most arid country in Europe. Look for rounded bare ridges above badlands and olive groves.

name: Calbuco
blurb: In April 2015 it erupted with almost no warning after decades of quiet, sending a towering ash column over Puerto Montt and Lake Llanquihue. Look for the jagged, truncated summit compared with smooth Osorno nearby.

name: Cancun / Riviera Maya
blurb: Cancun's hotel zone sits on a barrier strip shaped like the number 7, between the Caribbean and Nichupte Lagoon. Look for that seven, with the coast running south as the Riviera Maya toward Tulum.

name: Cape Cod
blurb: A sandy arm flexed out 60-plus miles into the Atlantic, left behind by retreating glaciers about 18,000 years ago. Look for the curled fist of Provincetown at the tip and the long white beach of the outer shore.

name: Cappadocia
blurb: Soft volcanic rock here eroded into thousands of cone-shaped fairy chimneys, many carved into homes and churches, with whole underground cities below. At dawn look for dozens of hot-air balloons over the pale, ridged valleys.

name: Caucasus crest
blurb: The wall between Russia and Georgia, often counted as Europe's southern edge. Look east of here for Mount Kazbek, a 16,558-ft glacier-capped volcano, and west for Elbrus, Europe's highest at 18,510 ft.

name: Central Rimo Glacier
blurb: Middle branch of the Rimo glacier system near the Siachen Glacier, feeding the Shyok River. Look for wide ice streaked with dark moraine bands in barren, high terrain.

name: Cerro Castillo
blurb: About 8,800 ft, a castle-shaped crown of basalt towers above Chile's Carretera Austral in Aysén. Look for a row of dark turrets with a glacier and a green lake beneath.

name: Cerro Las Minas
blurb: Honduras' highest point at about 9,400 ft, in Celaque National Park, whose name means "box of water" for the cloud forest streams. Look for a dark green, cloud-wrapped massif in the west.

name: Cerro Marahuaca
blurb: A tepui in Venezuela's Amazonas state, a sheer-walled table mountain topping out above 9,000 ft, among the highest of the tepuis. Look for flat-topped cliffs above unbroken jungle.

name: Cerro Nube
blurb: The high point of the mountains of southern Oaxaca, above cloud forest. Look for forested ridges falling to the Pacific coast.

name: Cerro Pintado
blurb: The high point of the Serranía del Perijá, the range forming the Colombia-Venezuela border south of the Guajira desert. Look for a forested ridge between Colombian farm valleys and the Lake Maracaibo basin.

name: Cerro Tristeza
blurb: A summit of the Turimiquire massif in northeastern Venezuela, the coastal mountains behind Cumaná. Look for forested ridges dropping steeply toward the Caribbean.

name: Cerro de la Majadita
blurb: A summit over 20,000 ft in the high Andes of San Juan province, in a remote, arid stretch near the Chilean border. Look for a pale peak among dry, snow-streaked ranges.

name: Chaitén
blurb: Thought dormant for thousands of years, it erupted in 2008 and buried the town of Chaitén below in ash and mudflows. Look for the steaming lava dome inside its caldera and gray dead forest on its flanks.

name: Chamar
blurb: A snowy peak of about 23,500 ft, the highest of the Sringi Himal, about 16 miles east of Manaslu. Look for a jagged white crest above deep valleys.

name: Channel Islands
blurb: Five of the eight islands form a national park sometimes called the Galápagos of North America. Look for dry, rugged islands off the Santa Barbara coast, with kelp beds along their shores.

name: Childs Glacier
blurb: Calves straight into the fast-moving Copper River, sometimes sending waves across to the opposite bank. Look for the ice cliff facing the gray river beside the old Million Dollar Bridge.

name: Chitwan National Park
blurb: Nepal's first national park, founded in 1973, and a stronghold of the greater one-horned rhino and Bengal tiger. Look for dark sal forest and grassland along the Rapti and Narayani rivers in the flat Terai lowlands.

name: Chiāntar Glacier
blurb: A long glacier in Pakistan's Hindu Kush near the Afghan border, the source of the Yarkhun River. Look for a white ice river at the head of a deep, dry valley.

name: Chomolhari
blurb: About 24,000 ft, rising straight above the Bhutan-Tibet border at the head of the Paro valley and sacred to Bhutanese Buddhists. Look for a huge white wall standing alone over brown Tibetan plateau on its north side.

name: Cinque Terre
blurb: Five medieval fishing villages wedged into cliffs on the Italian Riviera, linked by footpaths and a railway tunnel. Look for clusters of colorful houses in the folds of steep, terraced hills.

name: Cliffs of Moher
blurb: Sheer cliffs about 700 ft high running for about 5 miles along Ireland's west coast. Look for the dark, flat-topped wall of rock, with O'Brien's Tower near the highest point and the Aran Islands offshore.

name: Cloud Peak
blurb: At 13,167 ft the highest summit of the Bighorn Mountains, standing over a wilderness of granite and glacial lakes. Look for the broad gray massif with a deep cirque gouged into its northeast face.

name: Columbia River Gorge
blurb: The river cuts an 80-mile canyon up to 4,000 ft deep through the Cascades, widened by Ice Age floods from glacial Lake Missoula. Look for the green west end turning to dry brown hills to the east.

name: Concepción
blurb: One of two volcanoes that form Ometepe Island in Lake Nicaragua, a steep active cone of about 5,300 ft. Look for the figure-eight island with this sharp cone at one end and lower, forested Maderas at the other.

name: Copahue
blurb: A volcano on the Argentina-Chile border with an acidic crater lake, often steaming. The spa village of Copahue on the Argentine side is built around its hot springs and bubbling mud.

name: Copper Canyon
blurb: A system of six linked canyons covering an area several times larger than the Grand Canyon, deeper in places. The Chihuahua al Pacífico railway threads through it; look for deep green-and-tan folds in the Sierra Madre.

name: Coropuna
blurb: Peru's highest volcano at roughly 21,000 ft, carrying one of the largest ice caps in the tropics. Look for a long, flat-topped white massif with several summits, unmistakable above the brown altiplano.

name: Corsica mountains
blurb: Corsica is a mountain range rising from the sea, with Monte Cinto at about 8,900 ft only a couple of dozen miles from the coast. Look for snow on gray granite ridges above the deep blue Mediterranean.

name: Cumbre Vieja
blurb: The volcanic ridge forming southern La Palma; its 2021 eruption ran for 85 days and buried more than 1,600 buildings under lava. Look for the black lava field running from the new cone down to a fresh delta on the coast.

name: Dansketinden
blurb: At roughly 9,300 ft, the highest peak of the Stauning Alps in northeast Greenland, a tangle of granite spires and glaciers just north of Scoresby Sund, the world's largest fjord system. Look for jagged dark peaks between white ice rivers.

name: Daxue Mountain
blurb: A high, forested peak in southwestern Yunnan's Lincang highlands, above tea-growing country. Look for steep green ridges with patchwork farmland in the valleys.

name: Dead Sea
blurb: Its shore, more than 1,400 ft below sea level, is the lowest land on Earth, and the water is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean. Look for the turquoise grid of mineral evaporation ponds at the south end.

name: Devils Tower
blurb: The first US national monument (1906), a stump of volcanic rock rising 867 ft above its base, ribbed with giant columns. Look for a lone flat-topped tower above the pine and prairie of the Belle Fourche valley.

name: Diamond Head / Waikiki
blurb: A tuff cone about 300,000 years old, named by 19th-century British sailors who mistook its calcite crystals for diamonds. Look for the crater rim at the end of Waikiki's beach and hotel strip.

name: Doddabetta
blurb: At 8,652 ft, the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, just above the hill station of Ooty. Look for rolling tea estates and eucalyptus plantations on the slopes around it.

name: Drang-Drung Glacier
blurb: An ice cap on October Revolution Island in Severnaya Zemlya, one of the last archipelagos on Earth to be mapped, in the 1930s. Look for smooth white domes ending at the sea.

name: Drangajökull
blurb: Iceland's northernmost glacier and the only one in the Westfjords, a flat white cap above fjords cut like fingers into the coast. It has held up better than Iceland's other glaciers.

name: Dubrovnik / Dalmatian coast
blurb: A walled medieval city on a Dalmatian coast of more than a thousand islands. Look for the orange roofs and stone walls of Dubrovnik's old town on a rock jutting into the Adriatic.

name: Dunheger
blurb: A summit on the remote Mongolia-China border in the far western Gobi, where the Altai foothills meet desert. Look for bare, dark ridges with no trace of green.

name: Dykh-Tau
blurb: The second-highest peak in the Caucasus at about 17,070 ft, on the Bezengi Wall. Look for a huge, steep ice pyramid among glaciers north of the Georgian border.

name: Ecrins / Meije
blurb: The Barre des Écrins is the highest peak in France outside the Mont Blanc massif, about 13,460 ft, and the neighboring Meije was the last major Alpine summit to be climbed, in 1877. Look for heavily glaciated jagged rock.

name: El Chichón
blurb: Its 1982 eruption killed about 2,000 people and put enough sulfur into the stratosphere to cool the planet. Look for the crater, now holding a vivid turquoise acid lake, in the Chiapas jungle.

name: Eyjafjallajokull / Myrdalsjokull
blurb: In 2010 Eyjafjallajökull's eruption shut European airspace for days, the biggest air-travel shutdown since World War II. Its larger neighbor Mýrdalsjökull hides Katla, a more powerful volcano. Look for two ice caps side by side above the black south-coast sands.

name: Farallones de Cali
blurb: A rugged range of peaks rising west of Cali, protected as a national park, between the city and the Pacific lowlands. Look for steep, cloud-capped ridges above the Cauca Valley's sugarcane fields.

name: Flathead Lake
blurb: The largest natural freshwater lake by area west of the Mississippi in the lower 48, about 30 miles long below the Mission Mountains. Look for Wild Horse Island and cherry orchards along the east shore.

name: Frankfurt am Main
blurb: Germany's financial capital, with the only real skyscraper cluster in the country, nicknamed Mainhattan. Look for the towers along the Main River and the big airport in the forest to the southwest.

name: Galdhøpiggen
blurb: At about 8,100 ft, the highest mountain in Norway and in all of Scandinavia. Look for a dark summit ringed by glaciers in the heart of Jotunheimen.

name: Galeras
blurb: A volcano right above the city of Pasto. In 1993 it erupted during a scientific conference field trip, killing six volcanologists in its crater. Look for the crater on the hills west of the city.

name: Gannett Peak
blurb: Wyoming's highest point at 13,804 ft, deep in the Wind River Range. Its flanks hold the largest glaciers in the American Rockies; look for white ice spilling off the crest along the Continental Divide.

name: Garibaldi / Whistler peaks
blurb: Mount Garibaldi is a dormant volcano at 8,786 ft, and its lava once dammed Garibaldi Lake. Look for that turquoise lake, the dark spire of the Black Tusk, and the Whistler ski runs to the north.

name: Gateway Arch
blurb: At 630 ft, the tallest arch in the world, exactly as wide as it is tall. Look for the stainless steel curve glinting on the Mississippi riverfront, often throwing a long shadow across downtown St. Louis.

name: George Town
blurb: The old port on Penang Island, a UNESCO site for its colonial shophouses and temples. Look for the two long bridges, the newer one about 15 miles, linking the island to the mainland across the strait.

name: Georgian Bay / Thirty Thousand Islands
blurb: The world's largest freshwater archipelago, with tens of thousands of granite islands. Look for pink-gray rock islands scattered across blue water along the east shore of Georgian Bay.

name: Gibraltar
blurb: The Rock rises 1,398 ft at the mouth of the Mediterranean, with Morocco visible across the strait. Look for the airport runway cutting across the isthmus, with the main road crossing right over it.

name: Gobi Desert
blurb: Where the first nests of dinosaur eggs were found, in the 1920s. Most of it is bare rock and gravel rather than sand, and it's cold: winters drop well below zero. Look for brown plains and low ranges.

name: Golden Hinde
blurb: About 7,200 ft, the highest point on Vancouver Island, in the heart of Strathcona Park and named for Francis Drake's ship. Look for a dark rock summit above small glaciers and lakes in the island's center.

name: Gora Kurumdy
blurb: About 21,700 ft, one of the highest summits of the Trans-Alay Range, on Kyrgyzstan's border with China. Look for a heavy white crest above the flat, green Alay Valley to the north.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring
blurb: Grand Prismatic, about 370 ft across, is the largest hot spring in the US, with rings of orange microbe mats around a deep blue center. Old Faithful, a few miles south, erupts roughly every 90 minutes.

name: Great Sand Dunes
blurb: The tallest sand dunes in North America, rising about 750 ft, piled against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. Look for a tan patch of rippled sand pressed up against dark, often snowy peaks.

name: Great Smoky Mountains
blurb: The most visited national park in the US. The smoke is a blue haze from compounds the forest itself gives off. Look for layered blue ridges fading into the distance, topped by 6,643-ft Clingmans Dome.

name: Grinnell Glacier
blurb: An ice cap on the Meta Incognita Peninsula of southern Baffin Island, across Frobisher Bay from Iqaluit. Look for a white patch on dark, rolling uplands above the bay.

name: Grossglockner
blurb: At 12,461 ft Austria's highest peak, with the Pasterze, the country's longest glacier, curling around its base. Look for a sharp pyramid above a long tongue of ice and the switchbacks of the High Alpine Road.

name: Guallatiri, Chile
blurb: A volcano of about 19,900 ft in Chile's far north that almost always trails a fumarole plume from its summit. Look for the glaciated cone with a white wisp, above Lauca's lakes and altiplano.

name: Guiyang
blurb: Guizhou's capital sits on a karst plateau about 3,500 ft up, prized for cool summers, and has become China's big-data hub, with Apple's China iCloud center nearby. Look for high-rises crammed between steep green hills.

name: Gunung Galunggung
blurb: In 1982 British Airways Flight 9 flew through its ash at night and lost all four engines before restarting them and landing in Jakarta. Look for the horseshoe crater with a small lake inside.

name: Gyong Glacier
blurb: A glacier near the Siachen conflict zone in the eastern Karakoram, among the highest battlefields on Earth. Look for gray ice between sharp, snowy ridges.

name: Hallasan
blurb: South Korea's highest peak at about 6,400 ft, a broad shield volcano that forms nearly all of Jeju Island, with a crater lake at the top. Look for the gentle dome in the middle of the island, dotted with hundreds of small cinder cones.

name: Haramosh Peak
blurb: At about 24,300 ft, a steep peak above the Indus near Gilgit, notorious for a 1957 expedition tragedy. Look for a big white mountain above the dusty Indus gorge.

name: Hardangerjøkulen
blurb: Norway's sixth-largest glacier, near Finse, where The Empire Strikes Back filmed its planet Hoth scenes in 1979. Look for a white ice cap on a bare plateau beside the Oslo-Bergen railway.

name: Hawkes Heights
blurb: A high point in the mountains of Victoria Land near the Ross Sea. Look for ice-covered ridges and nunataks above glaciers flowing to the coast.

name: High Tatras
blurb: The highest part of the Carpathians, peaking at 8,711 ft, and one of the smallest true alpine ranges in the world, only about 16 miles long. Look for sharp granite peaks dotted with glacial lakes.

name: Highway Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Auyuittuq National Park beside Akshayuk Pass, a classic Arctic trekking route lined with granite walls. Look for white ice spilling into a deep, steep-sided valley.

name: Hochkönig
blurb: About 9,650 ft, a limestone massif south of Salzburg topped by a shrinking plateau glacier, the Übergossene Alm. Look for a pale, cliff-ringed block with a flat white top.

name: Hoher Dachstein
blurb: About 9,800 ft, the top of a limestone massif with the easternmost big glaciers of the Alps, above the lake town of Hallstatt. Look for a white glacier plateau framed by sheer gray walls.

name: Hotaka Mountains
blurb: The Hotaka group tops out at Okuhotaka, about 10,470 ft, Japan's third-highest peak. Look for the jagged granite ridge above the Kamikochi valley in the Northern Alps.

name: Huaynaputina
blurb: Its eruption in 1600 was the largest in South America's recorded history, and the ash cooled the Northern Hemisphere enough to bring famine to Russia. There's no tall cone; look for a gray crater scar in a deep valley.

name: Hüiten Peak
blurb: Mongolia's highest point at about 14,350 ft, in the Tavan Bogd massif where China, Russia and Mongolia meet. Look for the Potanin Glacier, Mongolia's largest, flowing off its flank.

name: Iguazu Falls
blurb: About 275 separate drops spread over nearly 2 miles on the Argentina-Brazil border, larger than Niagara. Look for the white spray of the Devil's Throat, a U-shaped chasm where half the river plunges.

name: Ijen
blurb: Its crater lake is the most acidic large lake on Earth, a milky turquoise, and at night burning sulfur gas glows electric blue. Look for the green-blue lake inside a steep gray crater at Java's eastern tip.

name: Incahuasi
blurb: A volcano of about 21,700 ft on the Argentina-Chile border whose name means house of the Inca in Quechua; Inca ruins sit near its summit. Look for the broad, mostly snowless peak in the desert Andes.

name: Independence Peak
blurb: About 22,800 ft, the highest peak of the Yazgulem range in the Pamirs, formerly called Revolution Peak. Look for steep ice faces above the glaciers of the central Pamirs.

name: Irazú Volcano
blurb: The highest volcano in Costa Rica at about 11,260 ft. Ash from its 1963 eruption fell on San José during a visit by President Kennedy. Look for the crater lake.

name: Issyk-Kul
blurb: Sitting at about 5,300 ft in the Tian Shan, it's one of the largest mountain lakes in the world, and it's slightly salty, so it never freezes. Look for a deep blue oval walled by snowy ranges.

name: Izalco
blurb: Born in a farm field in 1770 and erupting almost nonstop until 1958, it was called the Lighthouse of the Pacific by sailors. Look for a bare black cone beside the greener, older Santa Ana volcano.

name: Iztaccihuatl
blurb: Its name means White Woman, and the four summits of this 17,160-ft ridge look like a woman lying on her back. Look for the long white profile, head to chest to knees, just north of Popocatepetl.

name: Jargalant Hayrhan
blurb: A high, often snow-dusted massif rising above the lake basins of western Mongolia. Look for a white-capped block standing alone over brown steppe and shimmering salt lakes.

name: Jezercë
blurb: At about 8,800 ft the highest peak of the Accursed Mountains and of the whole Dinaric Alps, in northern Albania. Look for a jagged limestone crest above the deep Valbona and Theth valleys.

name: Jiaozi Snow Mountain
blurb: About 13,800 ft, the closest snow peak to Kunming, white in winter. Look for a high, flat-topped ridge north of the city above deep river gorges.

name: Johor Bahru
blurb: Faces Singapore across the narrow Strait of Johor, joined by a 1924 causeway that is one of the busiest land border crossings in the world. Look for the causeway and the reclaimed islands of Forest City to the west.

name: Jostedalsbreen glacier
blurb: Mainland Europe's largest glacier, about 180 square miles, with arms like Nigardsbreen and Briksdalsbreen reaching down toward green valleys. Look for a long white ice ridge between deep fjords.

name: Juyan Lake
blurb: The end lake of the Heihe River in the Gobi, it dried up completely in 1992 as farmers upstream took the water, and has been partly refilled since the 2000s. Look for a patch of water and salt in desert.

name: Kangju Kangri
blurb: A glaciated peak in eastern Ladakh, in high, dry country near the Chinese frontier. Look for an icy summit above brown desert valleys.

name: Kangto
blurb: About 23,000 ft, the highest point of Arunachal Pradesh, on the disputed line between India and Tibet. Look for a big icy massif rising above the jungle foothills of the eastern Himalaya.

name: Kanlaon Volcano
blurb: The highest peak on Negros Island at about 8,000 ft and one of the most active volcanoes in the Philippines. Look for a forested cone with a bare gray summit crater above sugarcane country.

name: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre
blurb: Australia's lowest point, about 50 ft below sea level, and its largest lake when full, which happens only a few times a century. Most years look for a blinding white salt crust in red desert.

name: Kawagarbo
blurb: At about 22,100 ft Yunnan's highest peak and sacred to Tibetan Buddhists, it has never been climbed. A 1991 avalanche killed all 17 members of a Sino-Japanese expedition. Look for the icy pyramid above the Mekong gorge.

name: Kaziranga National Park
blurb: Home to about two-thirds of the world's greater one-horned rhinos, on the Brahmaputra floodplain. Look for tall grassland and oxbow lakes along the river's south bank.

name: Kaçkar Dağı
blurb: At 12,917 ft, the highest peak of the Pontic Mountains above Turkey's Black Sea coast, with small glaciers on its north side. Look for jagged granite peaks above cloud forest on the sea side and dry slopes inland.

name: Keele Peak
blurb: At about 9,750 ft the highest point of the Mackenzie Mountains, near the Yukon-Northwest Territories border. Look for a gray glaciated summit above a sea of empty ridges.

name: Kelimutu
blurb: Kelimutu's three crater lakes sit side by side yet change color independently, from turquoise to green, red-brown or black. Look for the trio of colored pools on the summit of central Flores.

name: Kennedy Space Center
blurb: The 526-ft Vehicle Assembly Building, built to stack Saturn V moon rockets, is one of the largest buildings by volume in the world. Look for the giant white box with the flag, and launch pads 39A and 39B on the beach.

name: Khövsgöl Lake
blurb: Mongolia's largest lake by volume, holding most of the country's fresh water, at about 5,400 ft near the Russian border. Locals call it Baikal's younger sister. Look for a long blue lake between forested mountains.

name: Kinyeti
blurb: South Sudan's highest peak at 10,456 ft, in the Imatong Mountains near the Ugandan border. Look for a forested massif rising far above the surrounding savanna.

name: Koh-i Belandtarin
blurb: A high peak in the Wakhan Corridor, Afghanistan's thin panhandle squeezed between Tajikistan and Pakistan to reach China. Look for snowy summits above wide, bare glacial valleys.

name: Kongsvegen
blurb: A glacier flowing into Kongsfjorden beside Kronebreen, near the research town of Ny-Ålesund. Look for two glaciers merging into one wide ice front.

name: Korab
blurb: At about 9,070 ft, the highest point of both North Macedonia and Albania, sitting right on the border. Look for a long, rocky ridge holding snow into summer.

name: Kuh-e Chuk Shakh
blurb: A high summit in the Hindu Kush of Badakhshan, northeastern Afghanistan, in a region of glaciers and deep, roadless valleys. Look for snow-capped ridges rising above brown slopes.

name: Kunming
blurb: The "Spring City" sits at about 6,200 ft, mild all year despite being in the subtropics. Look for Dian Lake, Yunnan's largest, stretching south from the city with the Western Hills rising steeply along its shore.

name: Kwatna Peak
blurb: A glaciated summit in the Coast Mountains near Bella Coola, where peaks rise straight out of long saltwater inlets. Look for ice and dark rock above a narrow fjord.

name: Bazman
blurb: A 11,500-ft volcano rising alone from the deserts of southeastern Iran, in Baluchestan. Look for a dark cone and lava flows standing out against pale gravel plains.

name: La Soufrière
blurb: The volcano at the north end of St. Vincent; its explosive eruption in 2021 forced about 20,000 people to evacuate. Look for a broad crater rim, bare gray slopes, and ash-scoured valleys running to the sea.

name: Lac d'Annecy
blurb: Often called one of the cleanest lakes in Europe, a turquoise lake in the French Alps. Look for the old town of Annecy at its northern tip, with mountains rising from the shore.

name: Lagoa dos Patos
blurb: South America's largest coastal lagoon, about 3,900 square miles, with Porto Alegre at its north end. Look for the long, straight sand barrier separating it from the Atlantic, and the outlet at Rio Grande.

name: Lake Albert
blurb: A Rift Valley lake on the Uganda-Congo border. The Nile flows in at its northern end and straight out again. Look for steep escarpments rising from both shores.

name: Lake Balaton
blurb: The largest lake in Central Europe, about 48 miles long but averaging only about 10 ft deep. Look for the long, narrow lake with the Tihany peninsula almost cutting it in half.

name: Lake Chad
blurb: Once one of Africa's largest lakes, it has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s. Look for a patchwork of marsh, open water and islands where four countries meet.

name: Lake Constance
blurb: Germany, Switzerland and Austria share this lake but have never agreed on where the borders run on the water. The Rhine flows in at one end and out the other. Look for the long lake with the island of Lindau at the eastern end.

name: Lake Edward
blurb: A Rift Valley lake on the Uganda-Congo border, inside Virunga and Queen Elizabeth national parks. Look for the Kazinga Channel linking it to Lake George to the northeast.

name: Lake Garda
blurb: Italy's largest lake, narrow and fjord-like in the north, broadening into a wide basin in the south. Look for the long, thin Sirmione peninsula poking into the southern shore.

name: Lake Inari
blurb: Finland's third-largest lake, deep in Sami country north of the Arctic Circle, with around 3,000 islands. Look for a maze of water, rock and pine frozen for about half the year.

name: Lake Kivu
blurb: Its deep water holds huge amounts of dissolved methane and carbon dioxide, a rare and dangerous mix; Rwanda now pipes some of the methane out for power. Look for steep green hills and island-dotted bays.

name: Lake Lucerne
blurb: A lake of tangled arms between steep mountains, where the founding of Switzerland is said to have been sworn at the Rütli meadow. Look for the cross-shaped outline and Lucerne at its northwest end.

name: Lake Maggiore
blurb: A long lake split between Italy and Switzerland. Look for the Borromean Islands in the bay near Stresa, one entirely covered by a baroque palace and terraced gardens.

name: Lake Mweru
blurb: Split between Zambia and Congo, about 80 miles long and one of Africa's big fishing lakes. Look for the Luapula River's swampy delta at the south end and the steep escarpment along the Congo shore.

name: Lake Nasser
blurb: Over 300 miles long, this reservoir formed behind the Aswan High Dam in the 1960s. The temples of Abu Simbel were cut up and moved to keep them above the water. Look for blue fingers reaching into the desert.

name: Lake Nicaragua
blurb: Central America's largest lake, about 3,200 square miles, where bull sharks swim in from the Caribbean up the San Juan River. Look for Ometepe, an island made of two volcanoes joined by a narrow neck.

name: Lake Onega
blurb: Europe's second-largest lake at about 3,700 square miles. Its island of Kizhi holds a 22-domed wooden church built without nails. Look for long fingers of water reaching north, scraped out by ice-age glaciers.

name: Lake Peipus
blurb: Europe's fifth-largest lake, on the Estonia-Russia border. In 1242 Alexander Nevsky defeated the Teutonic Knights on its frozen surface in the Battle on the Ice. Look for a wide, featureless basin with low marshy shores.

name: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway
blurb: At about 24 miles, the longest continuous bridge over water in the world by Guinness reckoning; for roughly 8 miles in the middle, drivers can't see land. Look for two thread-thin parallel spans running straight across the lake.

name: Lake Sevan
blurb: One of the world's largest high-altitude lakes, at about 6,200 ft. Soviet irrigation projects drained its level by more than 60 ft. Look for the deep blue lake and the peninsula holding the 9th-century Sevanavank monastery.

name: Lake Tana
blurb: Ethiopia's largest lake and the source of the Blue Nile, with old monasteries on its islands. Look for the river leaving its southern shore near Bahir Dar.

name: Lake Tengger
blurb: A lake at the edge of the Tengger Desert in western China. Look for a patch of water among sand dunes.

name: Lake Titicaca
blurb: At about 12,500 ft, often called the highest navigable lake in the world, covering about 3,200 square miles between Peru and Bolivia. Look for deep blue water and the narrow Strait of Tiquina splitting it in two.

name: Lake Toba
blurb: The largest volcanic lake on Earth, filling the crater of a supereruption about 74,000 years ago. Look for Samosir, an island roughly the size of Singapore, in the middle of the lake.

name: Lake Zurich
blurb: A long, curved lake with Zurich at its northern tip. Look for the causeway and bridge at Rapperswil that pinch the lake in two, and the steep Alps beyond its southern end.

name: Lassen Peak
blurb: The southernmost Cascades volcano, 10,457 ft, and one of the largest lava domes on Earth. It erupted from 1914 to 1917; the scars of that blast are still visible on its northeast side.

name: Lefka Ori
blurb: The White Mountains of western Crete, topping out near 8,050 ft, with more than 30 summits over 6,500 ft. The Samaria Gorge cuts through them to the sea. Look for pale limestone, often snow-streaked into spring.

name: Leirungshøi
blurb: A high summit north of Jotunheimen, in the mountains around Lom. Look for snowfields and glaciers on dark, rocky ridges.

name: Licancabur
blurb: A near-perfect cone of about 19,400 ft above San Pedro de Atacama, with one of the highest lakes on Earth in its summit crater. Look for the green Laguna Verde at its foot on the Bolivian side.

name: Llaima
blurb: One of Chile's most active volcanoes, about 10,250 ft, in Conguillío National Park. Look for black lava flows threading through forests of monkey-puzzle trees below the snowy cone.

name: Loch Ness
blurb: About 750 ft deep, it holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined. Look for a dead-straight dark lake, 23 miles long, filling the Great Glen fault.

name: Longs Peak
blurb: At 14,259 ft, the only fourteener in Rocky Mountain National Park, recognizable from Denver by its flat top and sheer east face, the Diamond. Look for the squared-off summit standing above the Front Range crest.

name: Los Glaciares National Park
blurb: Home to Perito Moreno glacier and Fitz Roy, fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Look for glacier tongues ending in milky turquoise Lago Argentino and Lago Viedma.

name: Macau
blurb: Gambling revenue here has outstripped Las Vegas. Land reclamation fused two islands into the Cotai strip of mega-casinos; look for the golden lotus of the Grand Lisboa and the long bridge to Hong Kong.

name: Mackinac Bridge
blurb: Five miles long, with the longest suspension span between anchorages in the Western Hemisphere, joining Michigan's two peninsulas since 1957. Look for the ivory towers and green deck over the Straits.

name: Mallorca (Tramuntana)
blurb: The Serra de Tramuntana, a limestone mountain range running along Mallorca's northwest coast, is a UNESCO site. Look for gray peaks dropping straight into the sea.

name: Manhattan
blurb: 1.6 million people on 23 square miles. Look for Central Park, a perfect 2.5-mile green rectangle cut into the grid.

name: Maroon Bells / Elk Mountains
blurb: Two 14,000-ft peaks of crumbly maroon mudstone near Aspen, among the most photographed mountains in North America and nicknamed the Deadly Bells for their loose rock. Look for the reddish striped pyramids above Maroon Lake.

name: Melimoyu
blurb: A glaciated stratovolcano in Chile's Aysén region, rising near the coast among fjords and rainforest. Look for a broad ice-capped cone above dark green forest and channels.

name: Mesa Verde National Park
blurb: Ancestral Puebloans built nearly 600 cliff dwellings here around the 1200s, including the 150-room Cliff Palace, then left within a few generations. Look for a long green-topped mesa sliced by deep canyons.

name: Meteor Crater
blurb: A hole about three-quarters of a mile wide and 550 ft deep, blasted by an iron meteorite about 50,000 years ago, one of the best-preserved impact craters on Earth. Look for the raised rim of the round pit.

name: Mexico City
blurb: Over 21 million people on the bed of a drained lake about 7,350 ft up, and parts of it sink by inches a year. Look for the green rectangle of Chapultepec Park and volcanoes like Popocatépetl to the southeast.

name: Miami Beach
blurb: A barrier island across Biscayne Bay from Miami, holding one of the world's largest collections of Art Deco buildings. Look for causeways crossing the bay and a thin strip of hotels lining the beach.

name: Milford Sound
blurb: Actually a glacier-carved fjord, with walls rising almost vertically from the water and Mitre Peak topping 5,500 ft. It is one of the wettest inhabited places on Earth. Look for a narrow dark inlet cutting deep into steep green mountains.

name: Mississippi River delta
blurb: The river drops sediment from 41% of the lower 48 here, building a bird's-foot delta out into the Gulf. Look for muddy brown plumes fanning into blue water and thin fingers of marsh along each channel.

name: Misti
blurb: A near-perfect cone of about 19,100 ft that towers over Arequipa, Peru's second city, which is built of white volcanic stone. Look for the symmetrical peak with a snow-dusted tip right beside the city sprawl.

name: Moldoveanu Peak
blurb: Romania's highest point at 8,346 ft, in the Făgăraș Mountains, the steepest stretch of the Carpathians. Look for a bare, sharp ridge with glacial lakes in the hollows below; the Transfăgărășan road crosses nearby.

name: Molokai sea cliffs
blurb: Among the tallest sea cliffs in the world, rising more than 3,000 ft along Molokai's north shore. Look for the Kalaupapa peninsula, the former leprosy settlement, on a flat shelf at the cliffs' foot.

name: Mont Orohena
blurb: The highest point in French Polynesia at about 7,350 ft, the eroded core of the volcano that built Tahiti. Look for knife-edge green ridges and deep valleys radiating from the island's center.

name: Monte Pissis
blurb: At about 22,300 ft one of the three highest peaks in the Americas, yet so remote in the Catamarca puna that few people have heard of it. Look for a long, glaciated massif rising above multicolored desert.

name: Monte Rosa
blurb: The second-highest massif in the Alps, topping out at about 15,200 ft. The Capanna Margherita hut on one summit is the highest building in Europe. Look for a wide wall of glaciers and peaks east of the Matterhorn.

name: Monte Shipton
blurb: A peak in the heavily glaciated Cordillera Darwin of Tierra del Fuego, named for the explorer Eric Shipton. Look for ice-covered mountains dropping into the channels near the Beagle Channel.

name: Monterey Bay
blurb: A near-perfect crescent bay between Santa Cruz and Monterey, hiding a submarine canyon as deep as the Grand Canyon. Look for the smooth curve of beach and dunes linking the two towns.

name: Mount Asama
blurb: One of Japan's most active volcanoes; its 1783 eruption killed over 1,000 people and left the jumbled Onioshidashi lava field. Look for a bare, often steaming cone above the resort town of Karuizawa.

name: Mount Aso
blurb: One of the largest calderas on Earth, about 15 miles long, with towns, rice fields and a railway inside it. Look for the steaming Nakadake crater in the center of the huge green bowl.

name: Mount Aspiring / Tititea
blurb: At 9,951 ft, the highest peak outside the Aoraki/Mount Cook area, called the Matterhorn of the South for its sharp pyramid. Look for the white horn rising above surrounding glaciers.

name: Mount Bandai
blurb: In 1888 its north side collapsed in an eruption, burying villages and damming rivers into Lake Hibara and the colored Goshikinuma ponds. Look for the horseshoe scar facing north, with Lake Inawashiro to the south.

name: Mount Batur
blurb: An active cone inside a caldera about 8 miles across, a favorite sunrise hike in Bali. Look for the crescent Lake Batur beside the cone and black lava flows from its 20th-century eruptions.

name: Mount Choqa
blurb: A roughly 13,400-ft shield volcano in Ethiopia's Gojjam highlands whose slopes feed about two dozen Blue Nile tributaries. Look for a broad dome scored by radiating streams inside the great loop of the Blue Nile gorge.

name: Mount Cleveland
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes in the Aleutians, a near-perfect cone that makes up the western half of Chuginadak Island. An astronaut on the space station reported one of its eruptions in 2006 before ground monitors did.

name: Mount Coleman
blurb: A glaciated peak of about 10,300 ft above the Icefields Parkway between Banff and Jasper, named for geologist A.P. Coleman. Look for its ice-streaked slopes above the parkway's valley.

name: Mount Dawson
blurb: About 11,000 ft, the highest peak in Canada's Glacier National Park, south of Rogers Pass in the Selkirks. Look for a cluster of sharp summits above the big Illecillewaet and Deville icefields.

name: Mount Drum
blurb: A heavily eroded volcano of about 12,000 ft at the western end of the Wrangell Mountains, rising alone above the flat Copper River basin. Look for a lone white pyramid above the green lowland.

name: Mount Dulang-dulang
blurb: The second-highest peak in the Philippines at 9,639 ft, the top of the Kitanglad Range in Bukidnon. Look for a long forested massif rising out of the pineapple plantations of the Bukidnon plateau.

name: Mount Edith Cavell
blurb: At 11,033 ft, named for a British nurse executed in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium. Look for the hanging Angel Glacier spread like wings on its north face above Jasper.

name: Mount Farnham
blurb: About 11,400 ft, the highest peak in the Purcell Mountains, above the Columbia Valley west of Invermere. Look for a tall rock tower beside glaciers on the west side of the Rocky Mountain Trench.

name: Mount Foraker
blurb: At 17,400 ft the third-highest peak in the US, standing just southwest of Denali. Its Dena'ina name, Sultana, is often translated as the woman, Denali's wife. Look for the second giant to Denali's left.

name: Mount Foster
blurb: At about 6,900 ft the highest point of Smith Island in the South Shetlands, a sharp, ice-armored ridge rising straight from stormy seas. Look for a long narrow island crowned by glaciers.

name: Mount Gaudry
blurb: A summit on Adelaide Island off the west coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, named by Charcot's French expedition. Look for ice-covered mountains above glaciers spilling into the sea.

name: Mount Genyen
blurb: A 20,354-ft peak sacred to Tibetan Buddhists, with a monastery at its foot, in the Shaluli range near Litang. Look for a glacier-draped summit above high grassland and lakes.

name: Mount Guiting-Guiting
blurb: At 6,752 ft it rises almost directly out of the sea on tiny Sibuyan Island, with a jagged sawtooth summit ridge that makes it one of the hardest climbs in the Philippines. Look for a knife-edged crest above dense forest.

name: Mount Haku
blurb: One of Japan's three holy mountains, alongside Fuji and Tateyama, at about 8,900 ft. Look for a broad, snow-streaked summit rising above the Hokuriku coast.

name: Mount Hanang
blurb: About 11,200 ft, an isolated extinct volcano rising alone from the plains of north-central Tanzania. Look for a lone forested cone with bare grassland all around.

name: Mount Hasan
blurb: A twin-summited volcano of about 10,700 ft in central Anatolia; a mural at nearby Çatalhöyük, some 9,000 years old, may show it erupting. Look for the lone double peak southeast of Aksaray.

name: Mount Hesperus
blurb: The highest peak of the Revelation Mountains, a remote, rarely climbed range at the southwest end of the Alaska Range. Look for steep granite and ice spires with no roads anywhere near.

name: Mount Hope
blurb: At about 10,600 ft the highest peak of the Eternity Range in Palmer Land, at the southern end of the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for a white summit above a vast ice plateau.

name: Mount Ida
blurb: Crete's highest peak at about 8,060 ft, known as Psiloritis. Greek myth says Zeus was raised in a cave on its slopes. Look for a bare, rounded summit at the center of the island.

name: Mount Isto
blurb: Generally considered the highest peak of the Brooks Range, at roughly 9,000 ft, in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. Look for glaciers on the north side of the range, rare this far into the Arctic.

name: Mount Jinfo
blurb: A flat-topped karst mountain south of Chongqing, ringed by sheer limestone cliffs and part of the South China Karst World Heritage site. Look for a table-topped massif with vertical walls above green hills.

name: Mount Karthala
blurb: An active volcano on Grande Comore, one of the most active in the world, with a vast summit caldera. Look for the dark crater above dense forest.

name: Mount Katmai
blurb: In 1912 the nearby Novarupta eruption, the largest of the 20th century, drained the magma beneath Katmai and its summit collapsed. Look for the caldera, about 2 miles across, holding a lake ringed by ice.

name: Mount Kimball (Alaska)
blurb: A glaciated peak of about 10,300 ft in the eastern Alaska Range, between Delta Junction and Tok. Look for its ice-capped summit above the Tanana valley to the north.

name: Mount Kinabalu
blurb: At 13,435 ft, Borneo's highest peak rises straight out of the rainforest. Look for the bare granite summit plateau, broken into jagged spires, often poking above a cloud deck.

name: Mount Kita
blurb: Japan's second-highest peak at about 10,480 ft, after Fuji, in the Southern Alps. Look for a steep pyramid with a big east face, with Fuji visible to the east.

name: Mount Lister
blurb: At about 13,200 ft the highest peak of the Royal Society Range, which forms the skyline across McMurdo Sound from Antarctica's main research base. Look for a massive white wall above the sound.

name: Mount Longonot
blurb: A young stratovolcano rising from the floor of Kenya's Rift Valley, about 9,100 ft, with a crater roughly a mile across and a forest growing inside it. Look for the round crater rim near Lake Naivasha.

name: Mount Loolmalasin
blurb: About 12,100 ft, the highest peak of the Crater Highlands, just northeast of the Ngorongoro Crater. Look for high green slopes beside the deep crater bowls.

name: Mount Malindang
blurb: About 7,900 ft, an old volcano in northwestern Mindanao whose forested slopes are a protected natural park. Look for a broad, dark green massif with a small crater lake on its side.

name: Mount Mantalingajan
blurb: Palawan's highest point at 6,841 ft, on the long narrow island's southern spine. Look for a forested ridge running down the middle of the island with sea visible on both sides.

name: Mount Markham
blurb: At about 14,300 ft one of the highest peaks in the Transantarctic Mountains, a twin-summited massif seen by Scott's expedition in 1902 and named for Clements Markham. Look for its broad white bulk above the Ross Ice Shelf.

name: Mount McDonald
blurb: A peak in Victoria Land, East Antarctica, among the ranges that rise between the polar plateau and the Ross Sea. Look for dark rock poking through glaciers.

name: Mount Murphy
blurb: A deeply eroded volcano of about 9,000 ft on the coast of Marie Byrd Land, overlooking the Amundsen Sea. Look for a massive ice-covered mountain at the edge of floating ice shelves.

name: Mount Nyenchen Tanglha
blurb: At 23,497 ft the highest peak of its range, standing over Namtso, one of the highest large lakes in the world, northwest of Lhasa. Look for the turquoise lake beside the white ridge.

name: Mount Odin
blurb: Baffin Island's highest peak at about 7,040 ft, in Auyuittuq National Park. Look for granite peaks above glaciers and ice-filled fjords.

name: Mount Odin
blurb: A glaciated peak of nearly 10,000 ft in the Monashee Mountains, west of the Arrow Lakes in southeastern BC. Look for ice-streaked rock above long, narrow lakes.

name: Mount Olympus
blurb: Home of the Greek gods and Greece's highest peak at about 9,570 ft, rising almost from the shore of the Aegean. Look for the rocky summit ring with deep ravines, often capped in cloud.

name: Mount Ontake
blurb: A 10,060-ft volcano whose surprise eruption in September 2014 killed 63 hikers at the summit on a sunny autumn day. Look for the broad gray summit area with its crater ponds.

name: Mount Queen Bess
blurb: About 10,800 ft, a glaciated peak in the Coast Mountains named for Queen Elizabeth I. Look for a sharp summit rising from icefields between the coast inlets and the Chilcotin plateau.

name: Mount Ratz
blurb: About 10,100 ft, the highest peak of the Stikine Icecap area near the Alaska border, in some of the most heavily glaciated terrain in North America. Look for a rock summit rising from a sea of ice.

name: Mount Redoubt
blurb: A 10,197-ft volcano across Cook Inlet from Anchorage. In 1989 a KLM 747 flew into its ash cloud and lost all four engines, gliding for minutes before crews restarted them.

name: Mount Roraima
blurb: A 9,219-ft table mountain where Venezuela, Brazil and Guyana meet, ringed by cliffs about 1,300 ft high. It inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's The Lost World. Look for a flat-topped block with waterfalls pouring off its walls.

name: Mount Rossel
blurb: A peak in the mountains of Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica, where scattered ranges poke through the ice sheet. Look for dark rock rising from an endless white plain.

name: Mount Sanford
blurb: A 16,237-ft shield volcano in the Wrangell Mountains whose south face drops about 8,000 ft in roughly a mile, one of the steepest walls in North America. Look for a broad white dome above the Copper River basin.

name: Mount Satima
blurb: The highest point of the Aberdare Range at about 13,100 ft, a moorland plateau in the Kenyan highlands. Look for a broad, treeless top above dense bamboo and forest.

name: Mount Shir (Yazd Province)
blurb: Shir Kuh, about 13,370 ft, rises southwest of the desert city of Yazd and catches snow that feeds its qanats. Look for a white-capped massif surrounded by sand-colored plain.

name: Mount Sikaram
blurb: At about 15,600 ft the highest peak of the Spin Ghar range on the Afghanistan-Pakistan border, above the Tora Bora caves. Look for the snowy crest of a long east-west wall of mountains south of Jalalabad.

name: Mount Sinabung
blurb: Quiet for about 400 years, it woke in 2010 and erupted on and off for a decade, emptying villages around it. Look for gray pyroclastic scars down its flanks in Sumatra's Karo highlands.

name: Mount Tahan
blurb: The highest point in Peninsular Malaysia at 7,175 ft, deep inside Taman Negara, one of the oldest rainforests on Earth. Look for an unbroken carpet of forested ridges with no roads.

name: Mount Tahat
blurb: At about 9,500 ft the highest point in Algeria, a volcanic peak in the Hoggar Mountains in the heart of the Sahara. Look for dark volcanic plugs and lava fields rising from pale desert.

name: Mount Taibai
blurb: At 12,359 ft, the highest peak of the Qinling Mountains, the range that divides north and south China in climate, crops and cuisine. Look for a bare summit with glacial cirques above forested ridges.

name: Mount Takahe
blurb: A huge, snow-covered shield volcano of about 11,300 ft in Marie Byrd Land, so symmetrical it looks like a white dome. Look for its round summit caldera rising alone from the ice sheet.

name: Mount Tapulao
blurb: About 6,700 ft, the highest peak of the Zambales Mountains west of Luzon's central plain. Look for pine-topped ridges and old mining roads scarring the upper slopes.

name: Mount Terror
blurb: The extinct 10,700-ft shield volcano beside Erebus on Ross Island, named after HMS Terror, one of the two ships of James Clark Ross's 1841 expedition. Look for the broad white dome east of Erebus's steaming summit.

name: Mount Tom White
blurb: A glaciated peak in the eastern Chugach Mountains, above the Bering Glacier and Copper River country. Look for ice-draped ridges between huge glaciers flowing to the Gulf of Alaska.

name: Mount Ulysses
blurb: About 9,900 ft, the highest peak of the Muskwa Ranges in the northern Canadian Rockies, far from any road. Look for a glaciated massif in empty, roadless mountains.

name: Mount Unzen
blurb: A 1792 collapse here set off a tsunami that killed about 15,000 people. In 1991 a pyroclastic flow killed 43, including volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft. Look for the new lava dome, Heisei Shinzan.

name: Mount Veniaminof
blurb: A massive volcano on the Alaska Peninsula with an ice-filled summit caldera about 5 miles across, and a small cone in the ice that erupts every few years. Look for the flat white crater on a broad snowy mountain.

name: Mount Washington
blurb: Only 6,288 ft, but in 1934 the weather station here clocked a 231 mph gust, a world record that stood for 62 years. Look for the bare, rocky summit above treeline with an auto road switchbacking up.

name: Mount Xuebaoding
blurb: At 18,333 ft, the highest peak of the Min Mountains, rising above the travertine pools of Huanglong. Look for a sharp, snow-covered pyramid above forested gorges.

name: Mulanje Massif
blurb: A granite massif rising abruptly from tea plantations to about 9,850 ft at Sapitwa, the highest point in south-central Africa. Look for a huge sheer-sided block standing alone above the plains of southern Malawi.

name: Musala
blurb: At about 9,600 ft the highest peak in Bulgaria and the entire Balkan Peninsula, in the Rila Mountains south of Sofia. Look for a rounded granite summit ringed by small glacial lakes.

name: Mälaren
blurb: Sweden's third-largest lake. Stockholm sits on islands where it drains into the Baltic. Look for a maze of bays, islands and channels stretching west from the city.

name: Nagoya
blurb: Japan's car-making heartland: Toyota is just to the east. Look for Nagoya Castle with its golden roof fish, the port on Ise Bay, and Centrair airport on its own island offshore.

name: Nat Ma Taung
blurb: Also called Mount Victoria, the highest peak in Chin State at about 10,000 ft, famous for rhododendrons and rare birds. Look for a lone high ridge above endless forested hills.

name: Nemjung
blurb: A peak of about 23,400 ft in the Peri Himal, north of Manaslu near Tibet. Look for an icy summit among dozens of glaciated peaks.

name: Nemrut
blurb: A volcano on the west shore of Lake Van whose ancient lava flows dammed the lake. Its caldera holds a large crescent-shaped freshwater lake beside a small hot one; look for the ring with blue water inside.

name: Nevado Mismi
blurb: A glacial stream on this peak has long been considered the most distant source of the Amazon, about 4,000 miles from the river's mouth. Look for a dark ridge streaked with snow above the Colca Canyon.

name: Nevado de Chañi
blurb: Around 19,000 ft, the high point above the valleys of Jujuy and Salta, where an Inca child offering was found near the summit. Look for a snow-capped peak rising above a green valley on the dry side of the Andes.

name: Ngoc Linh
blurb: At about 8,500 ft, the highest peak of Vietnam's Central Highlands, famous for a rare wild ginseng that grows on its slopes. Look for a forested massif rising above remote, cloud-filled valleys.

name: Ningbo
blurb: Its port, merged with Zhoushan, handles more cargo tonnage than almost any other on Earth. Look for the 22-mile Hangzhou Bay Bridge snaking across open water to the north.

name: Niokolo-Koba National Park
blurb: Senegal's largest national park, savanna and gallery forest along the Gambia River, one of West Africa's last refuges for lions and chimpanzees. Look for the river winding through dry woodland toward the Guinea border.

name: Noijin Kangsang
blurb: About 23,600 ft, its glaciers hang close to the Lhasa-Gyantse road at Karo La pass. Look for the snowy massif just west of Yamdrok Lake's scorpion-shaped turquoise water.

name: Northeast Greenland National Park
blurb: The world's largest national park, about 375,000 square miles, bigger than all but about 30 countries. Almost nobody lives there; look for ice sheet, glaciers and long fjords.

name: Noshaq
blurb: At about 24,580 ft, Afghanistan's highest peak, on the border with Pakistan at the eastern Hindu Kush. Look for a snowy massif above the Wakhan Corridor.

name: Olympic Mountains
blurb: Mount Olympus, 7,980 ft, carries the Blue Glacier and wrings out so much Pacific rain that the valleys below hold temperate rainforest. Look for snowy peaks in a tight cluster across Puget Sound from Seattle.

name: Osorno
blurb: A near-perfect snow cone of about 8,700 ft, often called the Fuji of the Andes, rising over Lake Llanquihue. Look for its white summit glacier mirrored in the lake.

name: Otgontenger
blurb: At about 13,150 ft, the highest peak of the Khangai Mountains, crowned by a permanent ice cap. It is sacred, and the state holds ceremonies to honor it. Look for the white dome over green valleys.

name: Outer Banks
blurb: About 200 miles of thin barrier islands, in places barely a few hundred yards wide, where the Wright brothers made the first powered flight in 1903. Look for a pencil line of sand between the Atlantic and wide brown sounds.

name: Outlook Peak
blurb: Highest point of Axel Heiberg Island at about 7,250 ft, in the high Arctic. Look for a dark peak breaking through an icecap above white fjords.

name: Pacaya
blurb: One of Guatemala's most active volcanoes, about 20 miles south of Guatemala City, where hikers roast marshmallows over lava vents. Look for a dark, often steaming cone with fresh black flows on its flanks.

name: Palm Jumeirah
blurb: An artificial island shaped like a palm tree, built from sand dredged off the Gulf floor and ringed by a crescent breakwater. Look for the trunk, the villa-lined fronds, and the Atlantis hotel at the top of the crescent.

name: Parbati Parbat
blurb: A glaciated peak of about 21,700 ft at the head of the Parvati Valley in Himachal Pradesh. Look for big ice faces above the deep valley, whose hot springs at Manikaran draw pilgrims far downstream.

name: Parângu Mare
blurb: At 8,264 ft, the top of the Parâng Mountains in Romania's Southern Carpathians, with the Transalpina, the country's highest road, crossing the range. Look for a long grassy crest dotted with small glacial lakes.

name: Parícutin
blurb: In 1943 it burst out of a farmer's cornfield and grew over 1,000 ft in its first year, burying two villages. A church tower still sticks out of the lava; look for a dark cinder cone ringed by black flows.

name: Pauhunri
blurb: About 23,400 ft on the Sikkim-Tibet border. When Alexander Kellas reached the top in 1911 it was the highest summit anyone had climbed. Look for broad snow slopes above the brown Tibetan plateau to the north.

name: Peak Pobeda, Sakha
blurb: The highest point of the Chersky Range in northeastern Siberia, about 10,000 ft, in some of the coldest inhabited country on Earth. Look for a cluster of small glaciers above endless bare ridges and taiga.

name: Pedra da Mina
blurb: At about 9,180 ft, the highest point in São Paulo state, in the Serra da Mantiqueira. Look for bare rocky summits on the ridge above the Paraíba valley, roughly halfway between Rio and São Paulo.

name: Phou Bia
blurb: The highest point in Laos at about 9,250 ft. Its surroundings were long a restricted military zone after the war. Look for forested mountains southeast of the Plain of Jars.

name: Pic Macaya
blurb: About 7,700 ft, Haiti's second-highest peak, protecting some of the country's last cloud forest. Look for a dark green massif at the western tip of the southern peninsula.

name: Picacho del Diablo
blurb: At about 10,150 ft the highest point in Baja California, in the Sierra San Pedro Mártir, from which you can see both the Pacific and the Gulf of California. Look for a jagged granite summit above the gulf's desert coast.

name: Pichincha Volcano
blurb: Quito sprawls up its eastern slope. Guagua Pichincha erupted in 1999 and dusted the city with ash. Look for the TelefériQo cable car line climbing toward the summit.

name: Pico Naiguatá
blurb: At 9,072 ft, the highest peak of El Ávila, the green wall between Caracas and the Caribbean. Look for the ridge rising sharply from the sea on one side and the city packed into its valley on the other.

name: Pik BAM
blurb: The high point of the Kodar Range in Siberia, named for the Baikal-Amur Mainline railway that runs below it. Look for jagged, snowy peaks above the empty taiga north of Chita.

name: Pik Chimtarga
blurb: At about 18,000 ft, the highest summit of the Fann Mountains, a compact range famous for turquoise lakes. Look for a snowy peak surrounded by bright blue lakes such as the Kulikalon and Alauddin lakes.

name: Pik Semionova Tien-Shanskogo
blurb: The highest peak of the Kyrgyz Range at about 16,060 ft, on the skyline south of Bishkek. Look for glaciers and snow on a long ridge above the Chüy Valley.

name: Pik Skalisty
blurb: A high peak of the Turkestan range on the southern edge of Kyrgyzstan, near Tajikistan. Look for glaciated summits above deep valleys and the Fergana basin to the north.

name: Pikes Peak
blurb: At 14,115 ft, the view from its summit inspired Katharine Lee Bates to write America the Beautiful in 1893. Look for the massive pink granite peak looming directly over Colorado Springs, with a road switchbacking to the top.

name: Piton de la Fournaise
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes on Earth, erupting every year or two on Reunion. Look for the horseshoe-shaped caldera open to the sea, with fresh black lava streaking down to the coast.

name: Piz Bernina
blurb: At 13,284 ft, the easternmost 4,000-meter peak in the Alps and the highest in the Eastern Alps. Look for the Biancograt, a knife-edge snow ridge leading straight to the summit above the Morteratsch Glacier.

name: Poco Likang
blurb: One of the volcanic highlands of western Flores. Look for steep green ridges and terraced rice fields climbing toward forested summits.

name: Poyang Lake
blurb: China's largest freshwater lake when full, but it breathes with the Yangtze: in dry winters and droughts it can shrink to a fraction of its size. Look for braided channels and grassy mudflats where open water was months before.

name: Poás Volcano
blurb: One of the widest active craters on Earth, holding a hot, acidic turquoise lake. It sits just north of San José airport. Look for the steaming crater.

name: Profitis Ilias
blurb: The summit of the Taygetus range at about 7,890 ft, towering over Sparta. A small chapel to the Prophet Elijah sits on top. Look for a sharp pyramid at the crest of the long ridge down the Peloponnese.

name: Puget Sound
blurb: A drowned network of glacier-carved channels, some deeper than 900 ft, threaded by the biggest ferry system in the US. Look for long fingers of water and wooded islands between Seattle and the Olympic Mountains.

name: Puy de Dôme
blurb: The tallest of the Chaine des Puys, a line of about 80 young volcanic cones in the Massif Central and a UNESCO site. Look for the summit antenna and the row of rounded, wooded cones marching north and south.

name: Puy de Sancy
blurb: At about 6,190 ft, the highest point in the Massif Central, the eroded remains of a big old stratovolcano. Look for sharp ridges and ski runs above the Dordogne's source.

name: Puyehue-Cordón Caulle
blurb: Its 2011 eruption sent an ash cloud around the Southern Hemisphere, grounding flights in Buenos Aires, Australia and New Zealand. Look for the long fissure ridge and gray ash fields beside the volcano's cone.

name: Pyongyang
blurb: North Korea's showcase capital on the Taedong River, with very little traffic. Look for the 105-story pyramid of the Ryugyong Hotel. At night it's one of the few lit patches in a country that is almost entirely dark.

name: Pyrenees crest (Aneto)
blurb: Aneto, 11,168 ft, is the highest peak in the Pyrenees and carries the range's largest remaining glacier. Look for the white ice patch on its north face above the Spanish valleys.

name: Qinghai Lake
blurb: China's largest lake, a salty inland sea of about 1,700 square miles sitting near 10,500 ft on the Tibetan Plateau. Look for a vast blue oval ringed by grassland and mountains.

name: Queen Mary's Peak
blurb: A 6,765-ft volcano that is essentially all of Tristan da Cunha, the most remote inhabited island on Earth, about 1,500 miles from the nearest mainland. Look for a cone often wrapped in cloud, with the one small settlement on the flat northwest shore.

name: Quilotoa
blurb: A crater about 2 miles wide filled by a vivid green-blue lake, a favorite hike in Ecuador's Andes. Look for the lake.

name: Qurnat as Sawda'
blurb: Lebanon's highest point at about 10,130 ft, in Mount Lebanon right above the Cedars of God, among the last groves of the biblical cedars. Look for a long, bare summit plateau, snowy in winter.

name: Riyadh
blurb: Grew from a mud-brick oasis town to a metro of about 7 million in under a century. Look for the Kingdom Centre, the tower with a huge opening near the top, and the city grid running out into the Najd desert.

name: Roque de los Muchachos
blurb: La Palma's highest point at 7,949 ft, on the rim of the huge Caldera de Taburiente, home to one of the world's major observatories. Look for a cluster of white telescope domes on the crater edge, often above the clouds.

name: Sahara dunes (Erg Chebbi)
blurb: Morocco's classic Sahara dunes, rising up to about 500 ft beside the village of Merzouga. Look for a compact field of orange-gold dunes abruptly rising from flat, dark stony desert.

name: Saimaa
blurb: Finland's largest lake is a maze of some 14,000 islands and home to the Saimaa ringed seal, found nowhere else. Look for water and forest broken into a jigsaw puzzle.

name: Sakurajima
blurb: Across the bay from Kagoshima, it erupts small ash plumes hundreds of times a year. A 1914 eruption poured out enough lava to join the island to the mainland. Look for the plume and the lava bridge on its east side.

name: Salton Sea
blurb: California's largest lake was created by accident in 1905, when the Colorado River broke through an irrigation canal and flooded a desert basin for two years. Look for a long lake ringed by pale exposed shoreline.

name: San Francisco Peaks
blurb: The remains of a collapsed volcano north of Flagstaff, topped by 12,633-ft Humphreys Peak, Arizona's highest point, and sacred to the Hopi and Navajo. Look for a ring of summits around a hollow, often snowy above ponderosa forest.

name: San Juan Islands
blurb: A cluster of more than 170 named islands and reefs between Washington and Vancouver Island, where orcas hunt salmon. In 1859 a shot pig nearly started a US-British war here. Look for a maze of dark green islands and ferry lanes.

name: Sangay volcano
blurb: One of the most continuously active volcanoes on Earth, erupting more or less nonstop for centuries in a remote corner of Ecuador's Andes. Look for gray ash streaks across its snowy cone.

name: Santa María
blurb: In 1902 it blew out its whole southwest side in one of the largest eruptions of the 20th century. Look for the perfect cone and, on its scarred flank, the gray Santiaguito lava domes still puffing ash.

name: Saser Kangri
blurb: At about 25,170 ft, the highest peak of the Saser Muztagh in the Karakoram, just south of the Siachen Glacier. Look for a huge glaciated massif above Ladakh's Nubra Valley.

name: Sat Peak
blurb: A summit in the high ranges of the western Pamirs in Tajikistan, among glaciers and deep river valleys. Look for snow-covered ridges and gray ice streams above brown, barren slopes.

name: Semenov-Tyan-Shanskiy peak
blurb: The highest peak of the Dzungarian Alatau, about 15,160 ft, on the Kazakhstan-China border. Look for glaciers on a lone high range rising out of the steppe east of Lake Balkhash.

name: Serson Ice Shelf
blurb: One of the ice shelves along Ellesmere Island's north coast, which has broken up badly since the 2000s. Look for flat, ridged ice fastened to the shore at the top of the continent.

name: Shiprock
blurb: A volcanic neck rising about 1,600 ft from the flat Navajo Nation desert; its Navajo name means rock with wings. Look for the jagged dark peak with thin walls of rock running away from it like spokes.

name: Sierra Nevada (Mulhacen)
blurb: Mulhacén, at 11,414 ft, is the highest peak in mainland Spain, and on very clear days you can see the mountains of Morocco from the top. Look for a long snowy crest above Granada, with the Alhambra and the city on the plain below.

name: Sierra Nevada crest
blurb: The range is a giant tilted block: gentle on the west, but the east face drops about 10,000 ft to the Owens Valley. Look for the jagged granite crest, small glaciers and hundreds of lakes in its basins.

name: Sinai mountains
blurb: Barren red and gray granite where tradition places Mount Sinai, at about 7,500 ft, with Egypt's highest peak, Mount Catherine, beside it. Saint Catherine's Monastery, from the 6th century, sits in the valley below.

name: Skihist Mountain
blurb: About 9,700 ft, the highest peak in the Lillooet Ranges, above the Fraser Canyon near Lytton. Look for a glaciated summit between the dry canyon to the east and wetter coast ranges to the west.

name: Snaefellsjokull
blurb: The glacier-capped volcano where Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth begins. Look for a white cone at the tip of the long Snaefellsnes peninsula, often visible across the bay from Reykjavik.

name: Snake River Canyon / Hells Canyon
blurb: The deepest river gorge in North America, nearly 8,000 ft from the Seven Devils peaks down to the Snake River, deeper than the Grand Canyon. Look for the river's thin line far below the Idaho-Oregon ridges.

name: Soufrière
blurb: At about 4,800 ft, the highest peak in the Lesser Antilles, an active volcano on Guadeloupe's Basse-Terre. Look for a bald, steaming lava dome poking out of the rainforest, often wrapped in cloud.

name: Soufrière Hills
