blurb: Eruptions starting in 1995 buried Plymouth, Montserrat's capital, and left the south of the island an exclusion zone. Look for gray ash valleys and the ruined town spilling down to the sea.

name: South Rimo Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Kyrgyzstan's Tien Shan, retreating fast into a growing meltwater lake right next to the Kumtor gold mine. Look for a white tongue ending in a pale lake beside terraced pits.

name: Stromboli
blurb: Called the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean, it has erupted in small bursts every few minutes for at least 2,000 years. Look for the cone with a black landslide scar, the Sciara del Fuoco, running to the sea.

name: Sven Hedin Glacier
blurb: A glacier on Ellesmere Island, named for the Swedish explorer Sven Hedin. Look for a white ice river reaching the coast through bare, brown polar desert.

name: Sīm Gang Glacier
blurb: A broad glacier in the Biafo region of the Karakoram, near the vast ice basin trekkers call Snow Lake. Look for a wide white bowl of ice ringed by granite spires.

name: Tapuae-o-Uenuku
blurb: At 9,465 ft, the highest peak in New Zealand outside the Southern Alps, in the Inland Kaikoura Range. Look for a high, often snowy summit above dry Marlborough hills.

name: Taxtakörpü SA
blurb: A reservoir in northeastern Azerbaijan between the Caucasus foothills and the Caspian coast, built to store water for Baku and farmland. Look for a blue lake in dry, hilly country.

name: Tebulosmta
blurb: About 14,700 ft, the highest peak in Chechnya and of the eastern Greater Caucasus, on the Georgian border. Look for a snowy summit above deep, steep-sided valleys.

name: Terra Nivea
blurb: A small ice cap on the Meta Incognita Peninsula of southern Baffin Island, near Iqaluit. Its name means "snowy land" in Latin. Look for a white patch on dark, bare upland.

name: Thabana Ntlenyana
blurb: At about 11,420 ft, the highest peak in southern Africa, on Lesotho's high basalt plateau. Lesotho's lowest point is higher than any other country's. Look for treeless highlands cut by deep river gorges.

name: Tian Shan
blurb: The Celestial Mountains stretch about 1,500 miles across Central Asia and top out at 24,406 ft. Look for a wall of snow and glaciers between the desert basins of Xinjiang.

name: Tonle Sap
blurb: Southeast Asia's largest lake swells to several times its size each monsoon as the Mekong backs up and forces the Tonle Sap River to flow backward. Look for floating villages and drowned forests.

name: Uludoruk
blurb: At about 13,570 ft, the highest peak of the Cilo Mountains in Turkey's far southeast near Iraq, carrying some of the country's largest glaciers. Look for a jagged white crest above deep, dry gorges.

name: Urmia Lake
blurb: Once one of the largest salt lakes in the world, it has shrunk dramatically from damming and drought. Look for the lake turned red by algae, and the causeway that cuts across its middle.

name: Vancouver Island mountains
blurb: A rugged spine running the length of the island, topping out at about 7,200 ft at the Golden Hinde in Strathcona Park. Look for snowfields and long fjords cutting in from the open Pacific side.

name: Veten Mountain
blurb: A peak in western Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica, where isolated mountains poke through the ice sheet near the coast. Look for dark rock standing above flat white ice.

name: Villarrica Volcano
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes in South America, with a lava lake sometimes visible in its summit crater. It towers about 9,300 ft over the resort town of Pucón and Lake Villarrica.

name: Virunga National Park
blurb: Africa's oldest national park, founded in 1925, home to mountain gorillas and Nyiragongo, whose lava lake has been one of the largest on Earth. At night look for its red glow.

name: Viso
blurb: Monte Viso, about 12,600 ft, stands alone at the edge of the Italian Alps like a perfect pyramid. The Po, Italy's longest river, rises at its foot. Look for the isolated sharp peak west of Turin.

name: Volcan Baru
blurb: Panama's highest point at about 11,400 ft; on a clear day the summit offers views of both the Pacific and the Caribbean. Look for a dark forested massif near the Costa Rican border, often wrapped in cloud.

name: Volcan de Fuego / Agua
blurb: Fuego erupts almost constantly, and its 2018 pyroclastic flows killed hundreds. Look for its ash plume beside twin Acatenango, with the cleaner cone of Agua across the valley above Antigua.

name: Volcán Momotombo
blurb: A near-perfect cone on the north shore of Lake Managua; in 2015 it erupted for the first time in over a century. Look for the symmetrical gray peak at the lake's edge with the small island cone of Momotombito offshore.

name: Volcán Tacaná
blurb: A roughly 13,300-ft volcano straddling the Guatemala-Mexico border, the second highest peak in Central America. Look for coffee country on its lower slopes giving way to a bare summit.

name: Volcán Wolf
blurb: At about 5,600 ft the highest point in the Galápagos, on Isabela Island. It is the only home of the pink iguana. Look for the caldera.

name: Vänern
blurb: The largest lake in the European Union, about 2,180 square miles. Look for a huge two-lobed lake, split by the Kålland peninsula, so big it reads like an inland sea.

name: Vättern
blurb: Sweden's second-largest lake, long, narrow and unusually clear. Look for a slim blue lake running about 80 miles north-south, with one long island, Visingsö, in its southern half.

name: Wasatch Range
blurb: Rises about 7,000 ft straight up from the Salt Lake City suburbs and catches some of the deepest, driest powder in the country. Look for ski runs cut into the slopes and deep canyons slicing the front.

name: Washington DC Mall
blurb: About 2 miles of lawn from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, with the 555-ft Washington Monument in the middle. Look for the white obelisk and its long shadow, the Reflecting Pool, and the Capitol dome at the east end.

name: Wedge Mountain
blurb: At about 9,500 ft the highest peak in Garibaldi Provincial Park, just north of Whistler. Look for a wedge-shaped summit with glaciers on its flanks and a turquoise lake below.

name: Western Summit of Corno Grande
blurb: At about 9,550 ft, the highest point of the Apennines, in the Gran Sasso. Its north side shelters the Calderone, once Europe's southernmost glacier. Look for a jagged limestone crest above the Campo Imperatore plateau.

name: Wheeler Peak
blurb: Nevada's second-highest peak at 13,063 ft, in Great Basin National Park, with groves of bristlecone pines more than 4,000 years old. Look for the gray summit and its north-facing glacier cirque.

name: White Cliffs of Dover
blurb: Chalk cliffs up to 350 ft high, made from the skeletons of tiny sea creatures, and Britain's first sight for anyone crossing from France. Look for the bright white wall along the coast next to Dover's busy ferry port.

name: White Sands
blurb: The largest gypsum dunefield on Earth, about 275 square miles of white sand. It's surrounded by a missile range; look for a bright white patch in the Tularosa Basin, unmistakable from cruise.

name: Wildspitze
blurb: At about 12,380 ft the second-highest peak in Austria and the top of Tyrol, ringed by the glaciers of the Ötztal Alps. Look for a twin-topped white summit above a sea of ice.

name: Wuxi
blurb: Grand Canal city on the north shore of Lake Tai. Look for the lake's huge sheet of water and, on its shore at Lingshan, a bronze Buddha about 290 ft tall.

name: Xi'an
blurb: Capital of China on and off for more than a thousand years and the eastern start of the Silk Road. Its Ming city wall, about 8.5 miles around, still frames the center; look for the walled rectangle with the Bell Tower at its middle.

name: Yangra
blurb: Also called Ganesh I, about 24,350 ft, the high point of the Ganesh Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border. Look for the icy crown between the Langtang and Manaslu ranges.

name: Yerupajá
blurb: Peru's second-highest peak at 21,768 ft, the crown of the compact Cordillera Huayhuash. Look for a sharp, fluted ice ridge above a string of turquoise glacial lakes.

name: Zard Kuh
blurb: About 13,850 ft in the central Zagros, its snow is the source of both the Karun, Iran's largest river, and the Zayandeh Rud that runs through Isfahan. Look for a snowy ridge above folded mountains.

name: Zugspitze
blurb: Germany's highest peak at about 9,720 ft, right on the Austrian border. Three cable cars and a cog railway reach the summit. Look for the rocky crest above Garmisch-Partenkirchen and the green Eibsee lake at its foot.

name: Öræfajökull
blurb: Iceland's highest peak, Hvannadalshnukur at about 6,920 ft, sits on its rim. Its 1362 eruption was the most explosive in Iceland's recorded history; look for the broad ice dome with glaciers spilling down to the black sand plains.

name: Aberdeen Lake
blurb: A big lake on the Thelon River in the Nunavut tundra, upstream of Baker Lake. Look for a long lake in open, treeless country, frozen most of the year.

name: Acamarachi
blurb: A sharp, steep cone of about 19,800 ft in the Atacama, with Inca ruins on its summit. Look for the pointed peak rising above salt lakes and desert.

name: Adwa
blurb: A shield volcano in the Afar rift, where Africa is slowly pulling apart. Look for dark lava and pale cracks crossing an otherwise bare, sun-baked plain.

name: Aira Caldera
blurb: The northern bowl of Kagoshima Bay is a caldera about 12 miles across, left by an eruption roughly 30,000 years ago. Look for the round inner bay, with Sakurajima on its southern rim.

name: Ajusco
blurb: The highest peak in Mexico City at about 12,900 ft, a forested volcano on its southern edge. Look for the dark green mountain above the sprawl.

name: Akademia Nauk
blurb: A caldera holding Karymsky Lake; in 1996 an eruption burst up through the lake itself, boiling the water and killing its fish. Look for a round lake sitting in a volcanic basin next to the active Karymsky cone.

name: Akhtang
blurb: One of the many smaller volcanoes in Kamchatka's central Sredinny Range, a sparsely visited, roadless region. Look for a modest snow-streaked summit among forested ridges.

name: Akita-Komagatake
blurb: An active volcano in northern Honshu famous for alpine wildflower fields. Look for its red-brown summit craters near round Lake Tazawa, the deepest lake in Japan.

name: Alcedo Volcano
blurb: A volcano on Isabela Island in the Galápagos whose caldera floor hosts one of the largest wild giant tortoise populations. Look for its crater.

name: Alexander von Humboldt National Park
blurb: One of the most biologically diverse places in the Caribbean, rugged rainforest mountains in eastern Cuba named for the explorer who studied the island. Look for steep green ridges running to the north coast.

name: Alney
blurb: Part of the Alney-Chashakondzha volcanic massif in Kamchatka's Sredinny Range, far from any road. Look for a broad glaciated summit rising above the ridge-and-valley country of the peninsula's interior.

name: Amadjuak Lake
blurb: A large lake on southern Baffin Island that drains north into Nettilling Lake. Look for a broad lake in bare, rocky Arctic tundra, frozen for most of the year.

name: Ambang
blurb: A volcano in North Sulawesi's highlands, with steaming craters and fumaroles in hilly farmland. Look for forested ridges and patches of bare, sulfur-stained ground.

name: Amboseli National Park
blurb: Elephants roam swamps and a dry lakebed under Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain at 19,341 ft. Look for green swamp patches in dusty plain with the snowcapped peak just across the border.

name: Amery Ice Shelf
blurb: Fed by the Lambert Glacier, it fills a long bay on the East Antarctic coast. In 2019 it calved an iceberg about the size of Greater London, its biggest in more than 50 years.

name: Ampato
blurb: In 1995 climbers found Juanita, an Inca girl sacrificed some 500 years ago, frozen near its summit after a neighboring eruption melted the ice. Look for a broad white summit of about 20,600 ft west of the Colca Canyon.

name: Amundsen Glacier
blurb: About 90 miles long, flowing from the polar plateau through the Queen Maud Mountains to the Ross Ice Shelf. Named for Roald Amundsen, who reached the Pole by way of a neighboring glacier.

name: Ankaratra
blurb: A volcanic massif south of Antananarivo, its summit around 8,600 ft among Madagascar's highest points. Look for a high grassy plateau with old cones, cut by red-earth erosion scars.

name: Antofagasta de la Sierra
blurb: A volcanic field in the high Puna of Catamarca, around a small oasis town of the same name. Look for black lava flows and cinder cones spilled across pale desert and salt flats.

name: Antuco
blurb: A symmetrical cone in Chile's Biobío region that dammed Laguna del Laja with its lava. Look for the dark lava flows running down to the lake's shore.

name: Aracar
blurb: A lone, nearly 20,000-ft cone near the Chile border in Salta province, with a small lake in its summit crater. Look for the symmetrical peak rising out of the barren Puna.

name: Arches National Park
blurb: More than 2,000 natural stone arches in red sandstone, including Landscape Arch, which spans about 290 ft. Look for the parallel fins of red rock lined up like slices of bread.

name: Argentière Glacier
blurb: Flows down toward the village of Argentière in the Chamonix valley, below Aiguille Verte. A hydropower intake taps meltwater from under it. Look for a long white tongue between steep granite walls.

name: Arnasai Lakes
blurb: Part of a lake system that didn't exist before 1969, when Syr Darya floodwater was released from the Chardara Reservoir into a desert depression. Look for shallow, reedy blue water strung across the Kyzylkum steppe.

name: Asacha
blurb: A glaciated volcanic massif in southern Kamchatka, south of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky in a stretch of coast packed with volcanoes. Look for snowy ridges with eroded crater walls near the Pacific shore.

name: Atlanta
blurb: Built where two railroads met, it now has the busiest airport in the world by passengers. Look for the dense tree canopy that earns it the name city in a forest, and three tower clusters: Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead.

name: Atsonupuri
blurb: A volcano on Iturup in the southern Kurils, its cone sitting inside an older caldera on a peninsula. Look for a sharp cone with a ring-shaped rim at the narrow neck of the island.

name: Aucanquilcha
blurb: A volcano of about 20,000 ft in the Atacama whose sulfur mine near the summit was once among the highest mines in the world. Look for the mine road switchbacking up its yellow-streaked slopes.

name: Augustine Volcano
blurb: An island volcano in lower Cook Inlet that erupted in 1976, 1986 and 2006. Look for an almost perfectly round island with a lone gray cone, streaked by flows running down to the sea.

name: Axel Heiberg Glacier
blurb: Roald Amundsen's team climbed this glacier from the Ross Ice Shelf to the polar plateau in 1911, on the way to becoming the first to reach the South Pole. It is named for a Norwegian backer of the expedition.

name: Aydar Lake
blurb: Born in 1969 when floodwater from the Chardara Reservoir was diverted into a desert basin, it is now one of Central Asia's larger lakes. Look for a long blue streak across the sands of the Kyzylkum Desert.

name: Azhdahak
blurb: The highest peak of Armenia's Gegham range at about 11,800 ft, an extinct volcano with a small lake in its summit crater. Look for the snowy summit between Lake Sevan and the Ararat plain.

name: Badlands National Park
blurb: Eroded buttes and pinnacles banded in tan, pink and gray, with some of the richest fossil mammal beds in the world. Look for the jagged pale wall where the South Dakota prairie suddenly breaks off.

name: Bagabag
blurb: A small volcanic island off the north coast of mainland Papua New Guinea, near Madang. Look for a round green island with a crater-shaped interior in open sea.

name: Bakening
blurb: A large, deeply eroded volcano west of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, glaciers carving into its old flanks. Look for a broad snowy massif with radiating ridges set back from the coastal cones.

name: Baker Lake
blurb: A big lake fed by the Thelon River, with Nunavut's only inland community on its shore, close to the geographic center of Canada. Look for a broad lake in open tundra leading east toward Hudson Bay.

name: Baluan Island
blurb: A small volcanic island south of Manus in Papua New Guinea's Admiralty Islands. Look for a round, forested island surrounded by reef and turquoise shallows.

name: Banc d'Arguin National Park
blurb: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic: shallow tidal flats that host millions of wintering shorebirds from Europe and Siberia. Look for sand dunes running straight into turquoise shallows and pale banks offshore.

name: Band-e Amir National Park
blurb: Six deep-blue lakes in the Hindu Kush at about 9,500 ft, held back by natural travertine dams. Afghanistan's first national park, created in 2009. Look for vivid blue strings in bare tan mountains.

name: Beardmore Glacier
blurb: One of the largest valley glaciers in the world, about 100 miles long. Shackleton found it in 1908 as a highway to the polar plateau, and Scott's party died on the ice shelf after descending it in 1912.

name: Becharof Lake
blurb: Alaska's second-largest lake, about 35 miles long, on the Alaska Peninsula below volcanic peaks. Look for a big blue lake in empty tundra with no roads at all leading to it.

name: Beloye Lake
blurb: Its name means White Lake: a nearly round, very shallow lake roughly 30 miles across on the Volga-Baltic Waterway, with the medieval town of Belozersk on its south shore. Look for a round blue disk in dark forest.

name: Białowieża National Park
blurb: Part of the last large primeval lowland forest in Europe, straddling the Belarus border, and home to the largest herd of free-roaming European bison. Look for a solid dark block of forest surrounded by farmland.

name: Bosten Lake
blurb: Xinjiang's largest lake, roughly 400 square miles, fed by Tian Shan snowmelt on the edge of the Tarim Basin. Look for a big blue lake with reedy margins and bare mountains to the north.

name: Bras d'Or Lake
blurb: A tidal inland sea filling the middle of Cape Breton Island, salty water joined to the Atlantic by narrow channels. Alexander Graham Bell summered at Baddeck on its shore. Look for a branching lake in wooded hills.

name: Bratsk Reservoir
blurb: One of the largest reservoirs in the world by volume, formed by damming the Angara River in the 1960s. Look for long arms of water winding through taiga.

name: Breiðafjörður
blurb: A broad bay in western Iceland said to hold thousands of small islands and skerries. Look for the Snæfellsnes peninsula and its glacier-capped volcano along the bay's southern edge.

name: Brokopondo Reservoir
blurb: Formed in 1964 when the Afobaka Dam flooded about 600 square miles of rainforest, mainly to power an aluminum smelter. Dead tree trunks still stand in its water; look for a branching lake in green jungle.

name: Brunt Ice Shelf
blurb: Home to Britain's Halley VI research station, built on skis so it can be towed; it was moved inland in 2017 when a growing crack threatened it. Large icebergs broke away in 2021 and 2023.

name: Buckle Island
blurb: One of the Balleny Islands, an ice-covered volcanic chain in the Southern Ocean off Antarctica. Almost the whole island is glacier, ending in sheer ice cliffs at the sea.

name: Bukhtarma Reservoir
blurb: A huge reservoir on the Irtysh River whose dam also raised nearby Lake Zaysan, making one long body of water. Look for a winding lake squeezed between the foothills of the Altai.

name: Byrd Glacier
blurb: One of the biggest outlets of the East Antarctic ice sheet, about 85 miles long and 15 wide, squeezing through the Transantarctic Mountains to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed flow lines streaming through the gap.

name: Cabaray
blurb: A volcano on the Bolivian altiplano near the Chilean border, one of many peaks rising from the high dry plateau. Look for a dark cone among tan plains and salt flats.

name: Cahora Bassa Reservoir
blurb: One of Africa's largest reservoirs, about 150 miles long, filling a gorge on the Zambezi behind a dam finished in 1974. Look for a long, narrow lake snaking between steep, dry hills.

name: Caichinque
blurb: A volcano in the high Atacama east of the Salar de Atacama, one of many dry peaks along the Andean crest. Look for dark lava slopes above pale salt flats.

name: Callaqui
blurb: A long, ridge-shaped volcano in Chile's Biobío region, capped by glaciers and dotted with vents along its crest. Look for its elongated white summit instead of a single cone.

name: Canada Glacier
blurb: Spills into Taylor Valley in the McMurdo Dry Valleys, one of the few large areas of Antarctica with no ice cover. Look for the white tongue ending in a sheer cliff on the bare brown valley floor.

name: Canaima National Park
blurb: Home to Angel Falls, at 3,212 ft the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, and to the sheer-walled tabletop mountains called tepuis. Look for the flat-topped mesas rising from the rainforest.

name: Caniapiscau Reservoir
blurb: Québec's largest reservoir, over 1,600 square miles, at the head of the James Bay hydro project, diverting the Caniapiscau River west toward La Grande. Look for a flooded maze of islands and bays.

name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
blurb: Underground is the Big Room, a single chamber of about 8 acres, and summer evenings bring hundreds of thousands of free-tailed bats out of the entrance. From above, look for the Guadalupe Mountains' rugged limestone reef rising from the desert.

name: Cedar Lake
blurb: A large lake in central Manitoba enlarged by the Grand Rapids hydro dam just downstream, near the north end of Lake Winnipeg. Look for a broad lake in flat boreal forest and wetland.

name: Central Island
blurb: A volcanic island in the middle of Lake Turkana, the world's largest desert lake, with crater lakes of its own home to crocodiles. Look for small round lakes inside the island against the lake's jade water.

name: Cerro Azul
blurb: In 1932 the Quizapu crater on its flank blew in one of the largest eruptions of the 20th century, dropping ash as far away as Uruguay and Brazil. Look for the cone beside the gaping Quizapu crater.

name: Cerro Bayo Complex
blurb: A cluster of volcanic peaks in the high Puna de Atacama of Catamarca, among the cones and salt flats along the Argentina-Chile border. Look for pale, mostly snowless summits above the desert.

name: Cerro El Cóndor
blurb: A high, remote volcano in the Puna of Catamarca, part of the cluster of 20,000-ft-class peaks near the Chilean border. Look for dark lava slopes in dry, mostly snowless desert.

name: Cerro Paniri
blurb: A high volcano in the Atacama northeast of Calama, near the Chile-Bolivia border. Look for its dark, mostly snowless slopes above the desert valleys.

name: Cerro Tuzgle
blurb: A volcano of about 18,000 ft in the Puna of Jujuy province. Look for its dark lava flows fanning out across the pale high plateau, with salt flats nearby.

name: Chachani
blurb: At about 19,900 ft the highest of the three volcanoes ringing Arequipa, a sprawling cluster of domes rather than one cone. Look for the broad snowy massif just north of the city, with sharp El Misti to its right.

name: Chagulak Island
blurb: A small, steep volcanic island in the remote Islands of Four Mountains, central Aleutians. It is essentially one cone rising from the sea, home to large seabird colonies and little else.

name: Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park
blurb: An ancient quartzite plateau in the Brazilian highlands with canyons, crystal outcrops and dozens of waterfalls. Look for rugged pale ridges rising out of the cerrado savanna.

name: Cheboksary Reservoir
blurb: A long reservoir on the Volga between Nizhny Novgorod and Cheboksary, kept for decades below its planned level because filling it would drown too much land. Look for the river widening into a broad, shallow lake.

name: Chikurachki
blurb: The highest volcano on Paramushir in the northern Kurils and one of the chain's most active. Look for a tall snowy cone with dark ash stripes on the island's northern ridge.

name: Chiles volcano
blurb: A glaciated volcano straddling the Ecuador-Colombia border, rising above high, treeless páramo grasslands. Look for its snowy summit just west of the Pan-American Highway crossing.

name: Chilika Lake
blurb: Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, about 400 square miles, home to Irrawaddy dolphins and huge flocks of migratory birds in winter. Look for the long sandbar holding it back from the Bay of Bengal.

name: Chobe National Park
blurb: One of the highest concentrations of elephants in Africa, along the Chobe River. Look for the river and its floodplain where Botswana, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe nearly meet.

name: Chott Ech Chergui
blurb: A vast salt lake on Algeria's high plateaus between the Tell and Saharan Atlas ranges, more than 60 miles long. Look for a long pale band of salt crust and shallow water in brown steppe.

name: Chott Merouane
blurb: A salt lake in northeastern Algeria lying below sea level, part of the same depression as Chott Melrhir. Look for a white salt crust with patches of shallow water at the edge of the Sahara.

name: Chott el Djerid
blurb: The largest salt pan in the Sahara, where Luke Skywalker's Tatooine home was filmed in Star Wars. Look for the straight causeway road running across the white crust.

name: Cleveland
blurb: Its Cuyahoga River caught fire in 1969, helping spark the Clean Water Act. Look for the river's crooked course through the steel mills to Lake Erie, and the Terminal Tower downtown.

name: Cofre de Perote
blurb: A broad volcano of about 14,000 ft named for the boxy rock block on its summit, which looks like a strongbox (cofre). Look for the square-topped peak covered in antennas, west of Xalapa.

name: Coiba
blurb: A penal colony until 2004, which left the island's forest and surrounding reefs largely untouched; it is often called the largest island in Central America. Look for a big green island off Panama's Pacific coast with no towns.

name: Comoé National Park
blurb: One of the largest protected areas in West Africa, about 4,400 square miles of savanna threaded by gallery forest. Look for green strips of trees tracing the Comoé River through dry grassland.

name: Copiapó volcano
blurb: A volcano of about 19,700 ft in the Atacama east of the city of Copiapó, with Inca ruins near its summit. Look for the broad dry peak among colored desert slopes.

name: Corcovado Volcano
blurb: A sharp, glaciated cone on the Chilean mainland across the gulf from Chiloé Island. Look for its pointed summit rising almost from the sea above dense rainforest.

name: Cormorant Lake
blurb: A lake in the boreal forest of northern Manitoba, near the edge of the Canadian Shield. Look for an irregular lake among dark spruce and bog, frozen white much of the year.

name: Cot Seulawah Agam
blurb: A forested volcano near Banda Aceh at the northern tip of Sumatra. Look for a wooded massif rising above the rice paddies on the road between the capital and the north coast.

name: Cotacachi
blurb: A volcano of about 16,200 ft above the market town of Otavalo. Look for Cuicocha's crater lake at its foot.

name: Cree Lake
blurb: A large, clear lake in the remote north of Saskatchewan, deep in the boreal forest. Look for a big irregular body of water with sandy points and islands in dark forest.

name: Cuicocha
blurb: A crater lake about 2 miles wide with two islands in the middle, at the foot of Cotacachi. Look for the lake with islands.

name: Cumbal
blurb: Colombia's southernmost volcano, near the Ecuador border, with a glaciated summit. Look for its snowy peak above green highland pastures.

name: Daisen
blurb: Called Hoki Fuji for its cone shape from the west, at about 5,700 ft it is the highest peak in western Honshu's Chugoku region. Look for a jagged north wall and ski slopes above the Sea of Japan.

name: Daisetsuzan Volcanic Group
blurb: The roof of Hokkaido, inside Japan's largest national park. Its top peak, Asahidake, at about 7,500 ft, is the island's highest. Look for steaming vents and a broad, snow-patched plateau.

name: Dallas
blurb: A big city with no navigable water, it grew on railroads and oil money instead. Look for Reunion Tower's lit ball and the white arch of the Margaret Hunt Hill Bridge over the Trinity River floodplain.

name: Darial Gorge
blurb: The Terek River's gorge through the Caucasus, the route of the Georgian Military Road and the Russia-Georgia border crossing. Look for the narrow cleft below the glaciers of Mount Kazbek.

name: Darién National Park
blurb: Covers the heart of the Darién Gap, the only break in the Pan-American Highway between Alaska and Argentina. Look for dense rainforest and mountains along the Colombian border with no roads at all.

name: Dawson-Lambton Glacier
blurb: A broad, crevassed ice stream flowing off the plateau to the Caird Coast on the Weddell Sea, with an emperor penguin colony near its mouth. Look for a wide river of ice cutting through the flat coastal shelf.

name: Denman Glacier
blurb: Its bed lies in the deepest land canyon on Earth, about 11,500 ft below sea level. The glacier drains enough ice to raise global seas about 5 ft.

name: Descabezado Grande
blurb: Its name means big headless one: a flat-topped volcano whose summit crater is filled with ice. Look for the truncated white plateau in the Andes east of Talca.

name: Detroit
blurb: The Motor City, and the one big US city where Canada lies directly south, across the Detroit River. Look for the round towers of the Renaissance Center on the riverfront and Belle Isle in the river.

name: Devils Lake
blurb: A lake with no natural outlet, so wet years just pile up: since 1993 it has risen roughly 30 ft and swallowed farms and roads. Look for drowned fields and dead trees standing in its spreading margins.

name: Dome A
blurb: The highest point of the Antarctic ice sheet at about 13,400 ft, where satellites have recorded some of the coldest surface temperatures on Earth, below minus 130 F. China's Kunlun Station sits near the top.

name: Dome C
blurb: Site of the French-Italian Concordia Station at about 10,600 ft. An ice core drilled here reached ice about 800,000 years old, one of the longest climate records ever recovered.

name: Dome F
blurb: Japan's Dome Fuji station sits near this ice summit at about 12,500 ft. Cores drilled here reach back roughly 700,000 years.

name: Domuyo
blurb: At roughly 15,400 ft the highest peak in Patagonia, nicknamed the roof of Patagonia. Its flanks are dotted with hot springs and geysers. Look for the big snowy massif in northern Neuquén.

name: Dongting Lake
blurb: China's second-largest freshwater lake swells hugely in summer floods and shrinks to channels and grassland in dry winters. Look for the lake's broad shallows and the Yangtze along its northern edge.

name: Doña Juana
blurb: A volcano in southwestern Colombia, in Nariño near the border with Cauca. Look for its forested flanks above deep valleys.

name: Doñana National Park
blurb: Marshes, dunes and pine forest at the mouth of the Guadalquivir, one of Europe's largest wetlands and a refuge of the Iberian lynx. Look for the vast flat marsh that floods in winter and white dunes along the Atlantic.

name: Dubawnt Lake
blurb: A large lake in the Nunavut barren lands, so far north and cold that its ice can linger well into summer. Look for a sprawling lake in treeless tundra.

name: Dukono
blurb: A volcano on northern Halmahera that has been erupting more or less continuously since 1933. Look for a gray ash plume drifting off a remote, jungle-covered ridge.

name: East Antarctic Ice Sheet
blurb: The bulk of Antarctica's ice, close to 3 miles thick in places, holding enough to raise sea level about 170 ft. It rests mostly on bedrock above sea level, which makes it far steadier than its western neighbor.

name: Ebeko
blurb: A small but frequently erupting volcano on Paramushir, its ash often falling on the town of Severo-Kurilsk just a few miles away. Look for a low, steaming summit above the town on the island's north end.

name: Eiríksjökull
blurb: A table mountain formed when lava erupted under the Ice Age ice sheet, now capped by its own glacier. Look for the flat white top and steep sides rising above the western highlands.

name: Eldgjá
blurb: A volcanic canyon about 25 miles long that, around 939 AD, poured out one of the largest lava floods in human history. Look for a long dark gash running across the highlands near Myrdalsjokull.

name: Emas National Park
blurb: Its termite mounds glow green at night from bioluminescent click beetle larvae. Look for a big rectangle of native grassland surrounded on all sides by geometric soy fields.

name: Etosha National Park
blurb: Centered on Etosha Pan, a dry salt flat of about 1,800 square miles that is easy to see from space. Look for a vast white-green blank in the bush, glaring bright on sunny days.

name: Everglades
blurb: A river of grass: a sheet of water inches deep flowing slowly south across Florida toward Florida Bay. Look for vast flat sawgrass marsh dotted with tree islands, cut by canals and the Tamiami Trail.

name: Eyjafjörður
blurb: Iceland's longest fjord, about 37 miles, with Akureyri, the largest town in the north, near its head. Look for the narrow fjord between snowy mountains and the island of Hrísey near its mouth.

name: Faydat Umm Shuwayjah
blurb: A low depression in the desert of southern Iraq that holds water after rains. Look for a pale flat basin in sand and gravel desert.

name: Faydat al Jawbu
blurb: A shallow desert basin in western Iraq that floods after rare heavy rains. Look for a pale, flat depression in empty desert.

name: Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf
blurb: The second-largest ice shelf on Earth, about 165,000 square miles of floating ice in the Weddell Sea. Look for a flat white plain ending in a long cliff above the sea.

name: Fimbul Ice Shelf
blurb: Named for the Fimbulwinter of Norse myth, it fronts the Queen Maud Land coast and is fed by the fast Jutulstraumen ice stream. Look for a long tongue of ice jutting out to sea.

name: Fiordland National Park
blurb: New Zealand's largest national park, with Milford and Doubtful sounds carved into its coast by glaciers. Look for long narrow fiords reaching inland between steep dark peaks, often under cloud in one of the country's wettest regions.

name: Firth of Forth
blurb: Three bridges from three centuries cross it side by side, led by the red cantilever Forth Bridge of 1890, a UNESCO site. Look for the estuary east of Edinburgh with the bridges lined up at its narrows.

name: Fort Jesus
blurb: A Portuguese fort built in 1593 to guard Mombasa's harbor, laid out roughly in the shape of a human figure. Look for the ochre ramparts at the harbor entrance on Mombasa Island.

name: Fourpeaked Mountain
blurb: A glacier-covered volcano near the top of the Alaska Peninsula that nobody counted as active until 2006, when it erupted for the first time in thousands of years. Look for steam vents breaking through its ice.

name: Fuss Peak
blurb: A symmetrical cone forming the southwest tip of Paramushir in the northern Kurils. Look for a lone, sharp peak rising from the sea at the end of the island.

name: Gamalama
blurb: This volcano is the island of Ternate, whose cloves made it a prize fought over by Portuguese, Spanish and Dutch traders. Look for the round island-cone with the town wrapped around its shore.

name: Gangotri Glacier
blurb: The source of the Ganges, about 19 miles long, ending at an ice cave called Gaumukh, the "cow's mouth," a Hindu pilgrimage site. Look for a gray, debris-covered tongue below high Garhwal peaks.

name: Garajonay National Park
blurb: Laurel forest on La Gomera, a relic of evergreen woods that covered southern Europe millions of years ago, kept alive by trade-wind clouds. Look for a green, cloud-wrapped plateau atop the island's deep ravines.

name: Garamba National Park
blurb: The last wild northern white rhinos lived here until poaching wiped them out in the 2000s. Today it's a patchwork of tall-grass savanna and forest on the South Sudan border, guarded against armed poachers.

name: Gareloi Volcano
blurb: The whole of Gareloi Island in the western Aleutians is this one volcano, a snowy cone over 5,000 ft rising straight from the Bering Sea with steaming vents near the summit.

name: Geirangerfjord
blurb: A UNESCO-listed fjord where waterfalls like the Seven Sisters pour down cliffs thousands of feet high, and cruise ships squeeze in all summer. Look for a narrow S-bend of deep green water walled in by steep mountains.

name: Geureudong
blurb: A volcanic massif in Aceh's central highlands, near the Gayo coffee country around Takengon. Look for forested slopes above highland valleys and Lake Laut Tawar.

name: Gir National Park
blurb: The last place on Earth where Asiatic lions live in the wild. Look for a block of dry teak forest standing out from the farmland of the Saurashtra peninsula.

name: Gods Lake
blurb: A large, island-filled lake in northeastern Manitoba, reachable only by air or winter road. Look for a sprawling lake with clear water and rocky shores in endless boreal forest.

name: Gorky Reservoir
blurb: A huge reservoir on the Volga formed by a dam in the 1950s. Look for a broad, river-like lake in forest and farmland upstream of Nizhny Novgorod.

name: Gouin Reservoir
blurb: A huge reservoir at the head of the Saint-Maurice River, created by a dam finished in 1918. Look for an extraordinarily ragged outline of interlocking bays, peninsulas and islands in the boreal forest.

name: Gowd-e Zerah
blurb: The lowest point of the Sistan Basin, a salt pan that fills only in very wet years when the Helmand River's floods overflow from the Hamun lakes. Most of the time, look for a pale crust of salt in the desert.

name: Great Sitkin Volcano
blurb: Just north of Adak in the Andreanof Islands, this volcano began erupting in 2021 and has slowly filled its summit crater with a thick dome of lava. Look for the dark lava pancake inside the snowy rim.

name: Gros Morne National Park
blurb: Its Tablelands are a slab of Earth's mantle pushed to the surface, so barren and rust-colored they look like another planet. Look for that tan plateau beside green mountains and the steep-walled fjord of Western Brook Pond.

name: Guhkesjávri
blurb: A lake in the Sami country of the far north, its name meaning long lake in Northern Sami. Look for a narrow lake on the bare, rolling plateau of birch scrub and bog, frozen half the year.

name: Gunung Guntur
blurb: An active volcano above the town of Garut in West Java, with bare, sandy slopes from its 19th-century eruptions. Look for a gray scar among green farmland.

name: Gunung Mulu National Park
blurb: Holds Sarawak Chamber, one of the largest known underground chambers on Earth, and Deer Cave, where millions of bats stream out at dusk. Look for rainforest-covered limestone ridges and the peak of Gunung Mulu at about 7,800 ft.

name: Gunung Muria
blurb: A volcano on Java's north coast that stood on its own island until silt filled the strait, within the last few centuries. Look for a lone wooded massif rising from the flat coastal plain.

name: Gunung Rajabasa
blurb: A volcano at the southern tip of Sumatra, facing Krakatoa across the Sunda Strait. Look for a forested cone above the ferry port of Bakauheni and the coast.

name: Soputan
blurb: Soputan is one of North Sulawesi's most active volcanoes, often erupting ash and lava from its bare summit. Look for a gray cone above green highlands south of Manado.

name: Guri Reservoir
blurb: Held back by Guri Dam on the Caroní River, which generates the bulk of Venezuela's electricity and is one of the largest hydro plants in the world. Look for a sprawling, many-armed reservoir of dark water in green savanna.

name: Gødstrup Lake
blurb: A small lake in the flat farmland of central Jutland, near Herning. Look for a patch of water among fields and plantations.

name: Hachimantai
blurb: A broad volcanic plateau in northern Honshu, with ponds, bogs and hot springs. In late spring, a snowmelt pond near the top forms a giant eye shape locally called the Dragon's Eye.

name: Hamun-e Helmand
blurb: The Iranian part of the Hamun wetlands, fed by the Helmand River from Afghanistan. Look for marsh or a dry basin depending on the year, with Mount Khajeh rising in the middle.

name: Hardangerfjord
blurb: Norway's second-longest fjord at about 110 miles, famous for its spring fruit blossom along the shores. Look for the long branching fjord with glacier-topped Folgefonna on its southern side and the long suspension bridge near its inner arms.

name: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
blurb: Home of Kīlauea and Mauna Loa, the largest active volcano on Earth. Look for black lava fields running to the sea and the plume from Kīlauea's summit crater; at night it can glow orange.

name: Herbert Island
blurb: A round volcanic island in the Islands of Four Mountains, central Aleutians, crowned by a summit caldera about 2 miles wide. Look for the crater ringed by snow in open ocean.

name: Herðubreið
blurb: Called the queen of Icelandic mountains, a flat-topped table mountain formed by an eruption under Ice Age ice. Look for its steep-sided cake shape alone on a black lava desert.

name: Hongze Lake
blurb: One of China's largest freshwater lakes, a shallow basin on the Huai River held in on its east side by a long, centuries-old dike. Look for a broad flat sheet of water ringed by rice paddies and fish ponds.

name: Hualālai
blurb: An 8,271-ft volcano above Kona that last erupted in 1801. Kona's airport sits on that lava; look for the runway cut through black rock, with resorts set like green patches in the flows.

name: Hulun Lake
blurb: One of China's largest lakes, in the grasslands of Inner Mongolia near the Russian and Mongolian borders. Look for a big, oval lake in flat green steppe.

name: Huuhtijärvi
blurb: One of the countless lakes of Finland's eastern lake district. Look for a patch of water among dark spruce forest.

name: IJsselmeer
blurb: Once the saltwater Zuiderzee, it became a freshwater lake when the 20-mile Afsluitdijk sealed it off in 1932. Look for that ruler-straight dike across the water, and the reclaimed polders around it.

name: Ichkeul National Park
blurb: A World Heritage lake near Bizerte that switches from fresh in winter to salty in summer and hosts hundreds of thousands of wintering ducks and geese. Look for the lone mountain, Jebel Ichkeul, rising from the lake's south shore.

name: Iiruunjärvi
blurb: One of the many lakes in central Finland's flat forest country. Look for open water among woodland and bog.

name: Iliamna Lake
blurb: Alaska's largest lake, about 77 miles long, home to one of the few freshwater seal populations in the world and a legendary lake monster. Its waters feed Bristol Bay, the biggest sockeye salmon run on Earth.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord
blurb: Home of Sermeq Kujalleq, one of the fastest-moving glaciers in the world, which may have calved the iceberg that sank the Titanic. Look for the fjord jammed solid with icebergs out to Disko Bay.

name: Ironbridge Gorge
blurb: The world's first cast-iron bridge, finished in 1779, spans the Severn here, and the gorge is often called the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution. Look for a wooded valley with the river winding through.

name: Irruputuncu
blurb: A volcano on the Chile-Bolivia border with active fumaroles and sulfur deposits near its summit. Look for yellow and white streaks on its dark slopes.

name: Isanotski Peaks
blurb: A jagged, glacier-carved volcano on Unimak Island, nicknamed Ragged Jack for its broken spires. It stands right beside Shishaldin, whose smooth cone makes a striking contrast.

name: Island Lake
blurb: A big lake in northeastern Manitoba aptly named for its many islands, home to several fly-in First Nations communities. Look for a maze of water and wooded islands on the Canadian Shield.

name: Isluga
blurb: A volcano in Chile's Isluga National Park in the far north, with steaming fumaroles near its summit. Look for the dark cone above altiplano grasslands and llama pastures.

name: Itaipu Reservoir
blurb: About 520 square miles of water on the Paraná River behind Itaipu Dam, one of the world's biggest hydropower producers, shared by Brazil and Paraguay. Look for the long dam wall at the reservoir's southern end.

name: Jakobshavn Glacier
blurb: One of the fastest glaciers on Earth, it drains about 6% of the Greenland ice sheet into the Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO site. Look for a fjord packed with icebergs.

name: Jasper National Park
blurb: The largest park in the Canadian Rockies at about 4,200 square miles, holding the Columbia Icefield and Athabasca Glacier. Look for glaciers, turquoise lakes and the Athabasca valley.

name: Jaú National Park
blurb: One of the largest forest parks in South America, nearly 9,000 square miles, cut by tea-colored blackwater rivers. Look for dark winding rivers through endless canopy.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
blurb: India's first national park, founded in 1936, where Project Tiger began in 1973. Look for the Ramganga reservoir, a long lake winding between forested Himalayan foothills.

name: Jiuzhaigou Valley
blurb: A valley of blue, green and turquoise lakes stepped by travertine dams and waterfalls, damaged by a 2017 earthquake and since reopened. Look for jewel-colored pools strung along forested valleys in northern Sichuan.

name: Kahuzi-Biéga National Park
blurb: Named for two extinct volcanoes, Kahuzi and Biega, this park west of Lake Kivu is the main stronghold of Grauer's gorilla, the largest gorilla of all. Look for the two summits above the rainforest.

name: Kainji Lake
blurb: A large reservoir on the Niger River behind Kainji Dam, finished in 1968, one of Nigeria's biggest hydropower plants. Look for a long lake stretching north through the savanna, bordered by a national park.

name: Kama Reservoir
blurb: A long reservoir on the Kama River above Perm, built in the 1950s as part of the Volga-Kama hydropower chain. Look for a broad, branching ribbon of water through dark taiga.

name: Kambalny
blurb: Kamchatka's southernmost active volcano, near the peninsula's tip; in 2017 it erupted for the first time in centuries. Look for a snowy cone close to Kurile Lake and the narrowing southern end of the peninsula.

name: Kao
blurb: The highest point in Tonga, an almost perfect volcanic cone of about 3,400 ft forming its own uninhabited island. Look for the steep green cone in the sea beside the flatter, active island of Tofua.

name: Karaca Dağ
blurb: A broad shield volcano in southeastern Turkey; genetic studies point to its slopes as where einkorn wheat was first domesticated. Look for a huge, gently sloped dome dotted with small cones, west of Diyarbakır.

name: Karangetang
blurb: One of Indonesia's most active volcanoes, forming the north end of the small island of Siau. Look for a steaming, sometimes glowing summit above a village-lined shore.

name: Kasba Lake
blurb: A remote lake near the Nunavut border, famous among anglers for giant lake trout and reached only by air. Look for a big, clear lake at the edge of the tree line, spruce thinning to open tundra.

name: Ebulobo
blurb: A steep, isolated stratovolcano on the south coast of central Flores. Look for a lone symmetrical cone rising almost from the sea.

name: Lokon
blurb: Lokon and its twin Empung tower over the flower-growing town of Tomohon near Manado; the active crater sits in the saddle between them. Look for a gray vent between two green peaks.

name: Keoladeo National Park
blurb: Better known as Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, a man-made wetland that was once a maharaja's duck-hunting reserve, now winter home to hundreds of bird species. Look for shallow marshes and dikes in the dry plains west of Agra.

name: Khan Tengri
blurb: At about 23,000 ft counting its ice cap, a marble pyramid on the Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and China border. Its name means Lord of the Sky, and the rock glows red at sunset. Look for the sharp lone peak above long glaciers.

name: Khangar
blurb: A volcano in the Sredinny Range with a summit caldera holding a lake, among the few explosive centers in central Kamchatka. Look for a round crater lake set in a snowy rim.

name: Khangchendzonga National Park
blurb: Surrounds Kangchenjunga, at 28,169 ft the third-highest mountain on Earth, and its glaciers. Look for the massive snow wall of its five summits on the Nepal border, visible from far out over the plains.

name: Khanka
blurb: The Russian Far East's largest freshwater lake, split by the Russia-China border and very shallow. Look for a narrow sandbar on the Chinese side that walls off a smaller lake from the main one.

name: Khar-Us Lake
blurb: A big freshwater lake in Mongolia's Great Lakes Depression, fed by the Khovd River and fringed by reeds. Look for a broad lake with a marshy delta on the dry steppe, linked by a channel to Khar Lake.

name: Khodutka
blurb: A volcano in southern Kamchatka known for the hot springs on its flanks. Look for a rounded snowy summit among the cluster of peaks south of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky.

name: Khyargas Nuur
blurb: A large, salty lake in the dry Great Lakes Depression of western Mongolia. Look for a deep blue lake in a desert basin of brown hills, with sandy, bare shores.

name: Kluane National Park and Reserve
blurb: Holds Mount Logan, at 19,551 ft Canada's highest peak, and the largest icefield outside the polar regions. Look for vast glaciers flowing out of a sea of ice and peaks.

name: Korovin Volcano
blurb: The frequently steaming volcano at the north end of Atka Island in the central Aleutians, looming above the small village of Atka. Its summit crater has held a hot acidic lake.

name: Krasheninnikov
blurb: Two overlapping cones built inside an older caldera, just south of Kronotsky Lake in the Kronotsky Reserve. Look for a pair of snowy summits within a ring-shaped rim.

name: Kremenchuk Reservoir
blurb: Ukraine's largest reservoir by area, a wide stretch of the Dnipro held back by a dam at Kremenchuk. Look for a vast lake in flat farmland.

name: Krka National Park
blurb: The Krka River tumbles down a chain of travertine falls, and a power plant here began sending AC electricity to Šibenik in 1895. Look for a narrow canyon opening into lakes inland from Šibenik.

name: Krýsuvík
blurb: A steaming geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula, part of the volcanic zone that has erupted repeatedly since 2021 near Keflavik airport. Look for yellow and rust hot ground and small lakes, with fresh black lava a few miles west.

name: Kuju Mountains
blurb: A cluster of volcanic peaks in central Kyushu topping out at about 5,880 ft, the highest on the Kyushu mainland. Look for steaming vents and grassland highlands, with Aso's caldera to the south.

name: Kumpupintil Lake
blurb: Long called Lake Disappointment, the name an explorer gave it in 1897 when he found salt instead of fresh water. A huge salt pan in the Little Sandy Desert, sacred to the Martu people. Look for white crust among red dunes.

name: Kuybyshev Reservoir
blurb: Europe's largest reservoir, about 2,500 square miles of the Volga, held back by the dam at Tolyatti. Look for the wide, branching water and the forested Zhiguli Hills at the Samara Bend.

name: La Garita Caldera
blurb: About 28 million years ago it produced one of the largest known explosive eruptions on Earth. Erosion has worn the caldera away, but it measures roughly 22 by 47 miles in the San Juan Mountains.

name: Lac Bienville
blurb: A large, island-studded lake in the subarctic interior of Nunavik, northern Québec, where taiga thins toward tundra. Look for a ragged outline of bays among sparse forest and bare rock.

name: Lac Courte Oreilles
blurb: Its French name means 'short ears'. A deep glacial lake in Wisconsin's north woods near Hayward, home of the Lac Courte Oreilles Ojibwe. Look for a many-lobed blue lake among countless smaller ones.

name: Lac La Martre
blurb: A large lake northwest of Yellowknife, home to the Tlicho community of Whatì. Look for a broad, island-dotted lake in boreal forest, frozen white for much of the year.

name: Lac Seul
blurb: A long, dammed lake in northwestern Ontario on the English River, its water level raised for hydropower. Look for a maze of bays and islands stretching across dark boreal forest.

name: Lac la Ronge
blurb: A big lake on the edge of the Canadian Shield with over a thousand islands, beside the town of La Ronge. Look for the line where flat southern forest gives way to rocky, island-strewn Shield.

name: Lago Deseado
blurb: A long forest-lined lake in Argentine Tierra del Fuego, near the Chilean border. Look for a narrow blue lake running east-west between mountains.

name: Lago Tucuruí
blurb: A reservoir of roughly 1,100 square miles on the Tocantins River behind Tucuruí Dam, one of Brazil's largest. It flooded rainforest, leaving dead trees standing in the water among hundreds of islands.

name: Lagoa Mirim
blurb: A large coastal lagoon shared by Brazil and Uruguay, linked to Lagoa dos Patos by a natural channel. Look for its long shape behind a wide strip of sandy coast and wetlands.

name: Lake Abaya
blurb: The largest lake in Ethiopia's Rift Valley, colored reddish-brown by suspended sediment. Look for its rusty water beside the bluer Lake Chamo to the south, with the town of Arba Minch between them.

name: Lake Athabasca
blurb: A huge lake straddling Alberta and Saskatchewan. Its south shore holds the Athabasca Sand Dunes, some of the most northerly large active dunes on Earth. Look for pale sand against dark forest.

name: Lake Ağgöl
blurb: A shallow lake and wetland in the Kura-Aras lowland, protected as a national park for its migrating waterbirds. Look for open water and reed beds surrounded by cotton fields and dry plain.

name: Lake Bangweulu
blurb: Its name means 'where the water meets the sky'. A shallow lake surrounded by vast seasonal swamps, home to the rare shoebill stork. Look for blue water fading into a huge green-brown wetland with no clear shoreline.

name: Lake Barlee
blurb: One of Western Australia's largest salt lakes, dry most years. When rare rains fill it, huge flocks of banded stilts arrive to breed. Look for a sprawling white pan with ragged, island-studded edges in red goldfields country.

name: Lake Biwa
blurb: Japan's largest lake, about 260 square miles, and one of the oldest on Earth at roughly 4 million years. It waters Kyoto and Osaka; look for the long blue lake just over the hills northeast of Kyoto.

name: Lake Champlain
blurb: About 120 miles long, splitting Vermont from New York and reaching into Quebec. In 1998 Congress briefly declared it the sixth Great Lake, then backed down weeks later. Look for the long, narrow blue line with the Adirondacks to the west.

name: Lake Chany
blurb: The largest lake in western Siberia, a shallow, salty lake on the steppe with ragged bays and reedy islands. Look for an irregular lake in flat farmland and marsh.

name: Lake Chapala
blurb: Mexico's largest freshwater lake, about 50 miles long, just south of Guadalajara. Look for a long shallow lake with the towns of Chapala and Ajijic along its north shore.

name: Lake Chew Bahir
blurb: A shallow salt lake on the Ethiopia-Kenya border that is dry for much of the year. Look for a white salt flat at the southern end of the Rift.

name: Lake Chilwa
blurb: A shallow lake on the Malawi-Mozambique border with no outlet, so it shrinks and swells with the rains and has dried out completely more than once. Look for a wide lake ringed by marsh and reed.

name: Lake Claire
blurb: The largest lake entirely within Alberta, part of the Peace-Athabasca Delta inside Wood Buffalo National Park. Look for a shallow lake surrounded by a maze of channels and marsh.

name: Lake Cowan
blurb: A long salt lake beside the mining town of Norseman, where the Eyre Highway sets off across the Nullarbor. Look for a bright white, branching salt pan cutting through dark eucalyptus woodland.

name: Lake Eyasi
blurb: A seasonal salt lake below the Rift Valley wall, home to the Hadza, some of the last hunter-gatherers in Africa. Look for a long, pale pan at the foot of a steep escarpment.

name: Lake Frome
blurb: A huge salt lake east of the Flinders Ranges that is almost always dry. Look for a vast white pan against red desert, with the ridges of the Flinders rising to the west.

name: Lake Gairdner
blurb: A salt lake over 100 miles long whose hard white crust hosts annual land-speed racing. Look for a dazzling white pan against red earth, with rocky islands sticking up from the salt.

name: Lake General Carrera/Buenos Aires
blurb: Split between Chile and Argentina, it's about 700 square miles of vivid turquoise glacial water. On the Chilean shore, waves have carved swirling caves into marble. Look for the color, which stands out against the dry steppe to the east.

name: Lake Gogebic
blurb: The largest inland lake in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, a long, narrow lake running about 14 miles through hardwood forest. Look for a slim blue strip in unbroken woods, frozen white in winter.

name: Lake Hammar
blurb: A big lake in the Mesopotamian Marshes, drained by Saddam Hussein's government in the 1990s and partly reflooded after 2003. Look for marsh and open water near Basra.

name: Lake Isabella
blurb: A reservoir formed by damming the Kern River in 1953, in the southern Sierra Nevada. Look for an irregular blue lake in dry, brown hills.

name: Lake Kariba
blurb: By volume, the world's largest man-made lake, about 175 miles long, created when the Kariba Dam blocked the Zambezi in 1959. Look for the curved concrete dam wall at its northeast end, on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

name: Lake Kyoga
blurb: A shallow lake in central Uganda that the Victoria Nile flows through, its edges choked with papyrus swamp. Look for long, spidery arms of water reaching into green wetlands.

name: Lake Mackay
blurb: Straddling the Western Australia and Northern Territory border, it's one of Australia's largest lakes: over 1,000 square miles of salt crust that holds water only after rare floods. Look for a vast white pan dotted with islands in red desert.

name: Lake Mai-Ndombe
blurb: A shallow lake in the Congo rainforest whose name means "black water" for its tea-colored water. It swells greatly each rainy season. Look for dark water fingers in the forest.

name: Lake Malawi National Park
blurb: Covers the Nankumba Peninsula and islands at the south end of Lake Malawi, home to hundreds of brightly colored cichlid fish species found nowhere else. Look for rocky wooded headlands jutting into the lake near Cape Maclear.

name: Lake Managua
blurb: A big lake beside Nicaragua's capital, long polluted by the city's sewage. Look for Momotombo, a perfect volcanic cone rising from the lake's northwest shore.

name: Lake Manitoba
blurb: One of the three big leftovers of glacial Lake Agassiz, a long, shallow lake on the prairie northwest of Winnipeg. Look for its narrow waist, the Narrows, where the north and south basins meet.

name: Lake Manzala
blurb: The largest lake in the Nile Delta, a shallow brackish lagoon next to Port Said. Look for a maze of fish farms and islands beside the Suez Canal.

name: Lake Melville
blurb: Despite the name, a tidal saltwater estuary reaching far inland from the Labrador coast, with the town of Happy Valley-Goose Bay at its west end. Look for a long saltwater arm through dark forest.

name: Lake Mistassini
blurb: Québec's largest natural lake, about 900 square miles, long and narrow and split by chains of islands. Look for its parallel arms running northeast-southwest, aligned with the old glacial grain of the land.

name: Lake Mweru Wantipa
blurb: A shallow, often swampy lake between Lake Mweru and Lake Tanganyika whose size swings dramatically with the rains. Look for marshy water inside Mweru Wantipa National Park, below a rift escarpment.

name: Lake Nigat
blurb: The reservoir behind the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, Africa's largest hydroelectric project. Look for long arms of water reaching into wooded hills near the Sudan border.

name: Lake Nipigon
blurb: The largest lake entirely within Ontario, about 1,870 square miles, draining south into Lake Superior. Look for dark water dotted with islands and cliff-edged shores of ancient volcanic rock.

name: Lake Ohrid
blurb: One of Europe's oldest lakes, over a million years old, shared by North Macedonia and Albania. Look for a deep blue oval between mountains, with the old town of Ohrid on the northeast shore.

name: Lake Sacajawea
blurb: The pool of the Snake River behind Ice Harbor Dam, a few miles above where the Snake meets the Columbia near the Tri-Cities. Look for a winding blue ribbon through dry, tan basalt plateau.

name: Lake Saint Clair
blurb: A shallow, heart-shaped lake averaging about 11 ft deep, linking Lakes Huron and Erie, with a dredged channel for freighters. Look for the bird's-foot delta of the St. Clair River on its north side.

name: Lake St. John
blurb: A broad lake about 27 miles long, draining out through the Saguenay River. Each summer swimmers race across it. Look for the flat farmland ring around the lake against dark forest beyond.

name: Lake Tengiz
blurb: A shallow salt lake on the Kazakh steppe, part of a UNESCO site and home to the world's northernmost flamingos. Look for a pale, irregular lake with salt-white margins in flat grassland.

name: Lake Tharthar
blurb: Iraq's largest lake, a desert depression filled in the 1950s by diverting Tigris floodwater. Look for a big blue lake in sandy desert between the Tigris and Euphrates.

name: Lake Tuz
blurb: Turkey's second-largest lake and one of the saltiest in the world, supplying much of the country's salt. In summer it shrinks to a dazzling white crust; look for pink patches where flamingos breed.

name: Lake Volta
blurb: The largest reservoir in the world by surface area, about 3,300 square miles, formed behind Ghana's Akosombo Dam in 1965. Look for long branching arms of water running north through savanna.

name: Lake Winnipegosis
blurb: Another remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz, a long, narrow lake running north-south west of Lake Winnipeg. Look for a slender lake edged by marsh where prairie farmland gives way to boreal forest.

name: Lake Woods
blurb: An ephemeral lake in the Northern Territory outback that fills only after big wet-season rains and can dry to a bare pan. Look for a pale basin or a sheet of floodwater in red-brown scrub.

name: Lake Zaysan
blurb: A large lake in a basin between the Altai and the Tarbagatai ranges near the Chinese border, now merged with the Bukhtarma Reservoir downstream. Look for a broad lake in a dry valley with mountains on both sides.

name: Lake Argyle
blurb: Lake Argyle, filled by the Ord River Dam in the early 1970s, is one of Australia's largest reservoirs and home to tens of thousands of freshwater crocodiles. Look for a huge, island-studded lake among red Kimberley ranges.

name: Lambert Glacier
blurb: Often called the largest glacier in the world, about 250 miles long and up to 60 miles wide, draining roughly 8% of the Antarctic ice sheet into the Amery Ice Shelf.

name: Lars Christensen Peak
blurb: The summit of Peter I Island in the Bellingshausen Sea, one of the most remote and least-visited islands on Earth. Look for an almost entirely ice-capped volcano rising from the pack ice.

name: Larsen Ice Shelf
blurb: Its Larsen B section, about the size of Rhode Island, shattered within weeks in 2002, and Larsen C shed a Delaware-sized iceberg in 2017. It hugs the east side of the Antarctic Peninsula.

name: La Cumbre
blurb: The volcano of Fernandina, the youngest and most active of the Galápagos. Look for its deep caldera and fresh black lava flows.

name: Lascar
blurb: The most active volcano in the northern Chilean Andes. A major eruption in 1993 dropped ash as far as Buenos Aires. Look for a steam plume above the summit craters, east of the Salar de Atacama.

name: Lautaro
blurb: An ice-covered volcano inside the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, the only active volcano on the ice sheet. Look for dark ash stains on the white ice.

name: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
blurb: About 600 square miles of white sand dunes on Brazil's northeast coast. Rain pools between the crests in the first half of the year, so look for a white sea of crescent dunes dotted with blue and green lagoons.

name: Lesser Slave Lake
blurb: One of Alberta's biggest lakes, about 60 miles long, in the boreal forest north of Edmonton. Look for a long east-west lake with sandy beaches along its shore.

name: Leverett Glacier
blurb: The US South Pole Traverse climbs this glacier from the Ross Ice Shelf to the polar plateau, letting tractor convoys haul fuel to the Pole. Look for a long ice stream threading the Queen Maud Mountains.

name: Lewotobi
blurb: A pair of volcanoes on Flores locally called the husband and wife. The male peak's eruption in November 2024 killed about 10 people and disrupted Bali flights. Look for two cones side by side.

name: Linzor
blurb: A volcano on the Chile-Bolivia border in the Atacama, near the El Tatio geyser field. Look for its dark, eroded summit on the high dry plateau.

name: Lonquimay
blurb: Its 1988 eruption began on Christmas Day, building a new cone named Navidad on its flank. Look for the dark lava flow running down from the young cone into the forest.

name: Lopevi
blurb: An active volcano in central Vanuatu that forms its own island; residents left after eruptions in the 1960s. Look for a steep, nearly perfect cone rising straight from the sea, sometimes with a plume.

name: Los Katíos National Park
blurb: Swamps and lowland jungle on the Panama border, part of the Darién Gap where the Pan-American Highway simply stops. Look for the wide, braided Atrato River delta pushing into the Gulf of Urabá.

name: Mahaiganyanhu
blurb: A salt lake in the Qaidam Basin, one of the driest places in China. Look for pale salt flats and evaporation ponds set in a barren gray desert floor ringed by mountains.

name: Makian
blurb: A volcano that forms an entire small island off Halmahera, with a big summit crater. Eruptions have repeatedly forced its villagers to evacuate. Look for a round island with a notched summit.

name: Malinche
blurb: A dormant volcano of about 14,600 ft standing alone between Puebla and Tlaxcala, named after Hernán Cortés's interpreter. Look for the broad, eroded peak, sometimes snow-dusted, east of the Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl pair.

name: Mammoth Cave National Park
blurb: The world's longest known cave system, with more than 400 miles mapped under these hills. Look for the Green River winding through forest; the caves themselves are all below.

name: Mana Pools
blurb: A Zambezi River floodplain where old river channels leave pools that draw elephants, hippos and buffalo in the dry season, a World Heritage site. Look for the wide braided Zambezi with Zambia's escarpment rising across it.

name: Manas National Park
blurb: Tiger and elephant country on the Bhutan border, along the braided Manas River. Look for grassland and forest where the Himalayan foothills meet the plain.

name: Manovo-Gounda St. Floris National Park
blurb: On UNESCO's danger list since 1997 after poaching stripped much of its wildlife. Look for savanna and floodplains in northern Central African Republic.

name: Marion Island
blurb: A remote volcanic island in the Southern Indian Ocean, home to a South African research station and huge colonies of penguins and albatrosses. Look for a green-and-black island with a snowy, cratered interior.

name: Matanuska Glacier
blurb: About 27 miles long and 4 miles wide at its toe, one of the largest Alaska glaciers you can drive to, right off the Glenn Highway. Look for the white tongue filling the head of the Matanuska River valley.

name: McMurdo Ice Shelf
blurb: Next to McMurdo Station, Antarctica's largest research base, and home to its airfields. Look for the shelf's dirty, debris-strewn surface beside Ross Island and the smoking cone of Mount Erebus.

name: Menengai
blurb: One of the largest volcanic calderas in Africa, roughly 7 miles across, right on the edge of the city of Nakuru. Look for the huge oval rim and dark lava-covered floor just north of town.

name: Mentolat
blurb: An ice-filled volcano on Magdalena Island in the fjords of Chile's Aysén region. Look for the glaciated crater above dense rainforest and channels.

name: Merelava
blurb: A single volcanic cone forming an island in Vanuatu's Banks group, steep-sided with villages perched on its slopes. Look for a small, symmetrical island rising sharply out of the ocean.

name: Michinmahuida
blurb: A broad, glacier-covered volcano above the town of Chaitén, in Pumalín Park. Look for its long white summit ridge behind Chaitén's smaller gray caldera.

name: Minnesota Glacier
blurb: Separates the Sentinel Range, home to Vinson Massif, Antarctica's highest peak, from the Heritage Range in the Ellsworth Mountains. It is named for the University of Minnesota geologists who mapped the area.

name: Miñiques Volcano
blurb: A volcano in the high Atacama beside the Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, deep blue lakes with flamingos. Look for the two lakes at its foot.

name: Mont Ross
blurb: At about 6,070 ft, the highest point of the Kerguelen Islands, a glaciated old volcano so remote and stormy it was first climbed only in 1975. Look for ice on the summit above a maze of fjords.

name: Monte Burney
blurb: A glacier-covered volcano in the fjords of far southern Chile, near the southern end of the Andean volcano chain. Look for its icy cone rising from the channels.

name: Montejaque reservoir
blurb: A dam built in the 1920s on porous limestone; the water drained away through caves underneath, so the reservoir almost never fills. Look for a small basin, usually dry, among rugged hills.

name: Montréal
blurb: An island in the St. Lawrence, named for Mount Royal, the forested hill in the middle with a park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Look for the Olympic Stadium's leaning tower on the east side.

name: Morne Diablotins
blurb: At 4,747 ft the highest peak in Dominica, a dormant volcano wrapped in rainforest and home to the island's rare parrots. Look for the cloud-capped summit in the island's north.

name: Morne Watt
blurb: A volcanic peak in southern Dominica near the Boiling Lake, a flooded fumarole that bubbles at near boiling. Look for steam in the valley.

name: Mount Adatara
blurb: A volcano in Fukushima immortalized in a poem about the true sky above it. Look for a broad ridge with a bare, sulfur-gray crater on the west side.

name: Mount Akagi
blurb: A broad, many-peaked volcano in Gunma north of Tokyo, with a caldera lake, Onuma, at its center. Look for the lake ringed by peaks on the wide, gently sloping massif.

name: Mount Akutan
blurb: One of the most active volcanoes in the Aleutians, with a summit caldera holding a young cinder cone. The island below it also hosts one of the largest seafood processing plants in North America.

name: Mount Alayta
blurb: A broad shield volcano in Ethiopia's Afar depression, one of the hottest, lowest and most volcanically active places on Earth. Look for dark lava flows fanning across the desert.

name: Mount Amagi
blurb: A group of old, deeply eroded volcanoes forming the spine of the Izu Peninsula, famous from Kawabata's story The Izu Dancer. Look for forested ridges between Fuji and the sea.

name: Mount Aniakchak
blurb: A caldera 6 miles across, blown out in a huge eruption about 3,500 years ago, inside one of the least-visited national park units in the US. Look for Surprise Lake in the crater's floor.

name: Mount Arayat
blurb: A lone extinct volcano rising about 3,400 ft straight out of the flat rice plain of central Luzon. Look for the solitary forested hump east of Clark, impossible to miss on the plain.

name: Mount Awu
blurb: The largest volcano on Sangihe island, north of Sulawesi, with a history of deadly eruptions in the 1700s and 1800s. Look for a wide crater near the island's north end.

name: Mount Ayalu
blurb: A volcano in the Afar rift, part of a chain of vents marking where the African continent is tearing open. Look for black lava against tan desert.

name: Mount Bachelor
blurb: A young, symmetrical cone of about 9,000 ft west of Bend, home to one of the largest ski areas in the Northwest. Look for the smooth snow cone with lift lines on its north side, just south of the Three Sisters.

name: Mount Belinda
region: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
blurb: The volcano on Montagu Island in the South Sandwich chain, which erupted from 2001 to 2007 and sent lava down to the sea. Look for a glacier-covered island with a dark summit cone and a dark smudge of lava on the ice.

name: Mount Bental
blurb: A dormant volcanic cone in the Golan Heights with an old army bunker on top, looking straight over the Syrian border. Look for a small round peak among a line of cones on the plateau.

name: Mount Besar
blurb: A volcano in the Barisan range of southern Sumatra, the spine of mountains running the length of the island. Look for forested peaks above plantations.

name: Mount Bosavi
blurb: An extinct volcano in Papua New Guinea's highland rainforest whose crater, about 2.5 miles wide, made headlines in 2009 when a BBC team found new species inside, including a giant woolly rat. Look for the forest-filled crater ring.

name: Mount Chōkai
blurb: Called Dewa Fuji, at about 7,340 ft it rises straight from the Sea of Japan coast. Look for a big cone with snow lingering into summer, standing alone above the shore.

name: Mount Douglas
blurb: A glaciated volcano at the head of the Alaska Peninsula, across Shelikof Strait from Kodiak. Its summit crater holds a small hot, acidic lake hidden among the ice.

name: Mount Egon
blurb: A volcano near Maumere in eastern Flores, with a bare summit crater above forested slopes. Look for a gray-topped cone near the north coast.

name: Mount Eniwa
blurb: A volcano above Lake Shikotsu near New Chitose Airport, which hosted the men's and women's downhill at the 1972 Sapporo Olympics. Look for a steep cone on the lake's northwest shore.

name: Mount Fentale
blurb: A caldera volcano beside the Awash valley that set off a swarm of strong earthquakes in late 2024 and early 2025 as magma pushed underground. Look for the summit crater and dark lava flows on its flanks.

name: Mount Gamkonora
blurb: The highest volcano on Halmahera, in Indonesia's Maluku islands. Look for a long, cratered summit ridge above rainforest along the island's west arm.

name: Mount Gassan
blurb: The holiest of the Dewa Sanzan, three sacred mountains of Yamabushi mountain ascetics. Snow lingers so long that people ski here in summer. Look for a broad, rounded summit with snowfields.

name: Mount Gede
blurb: Twin of Pangrango, these volcanoes form a national park just south of Jakarta's sprawl. Look for the steaming crater and the green ridges above the tea estates of Puncak.

name: Mount Hermon
blurb: At 9,232 ft, the highest point in Syria, straddling the Lebanese border, with a ski area on its southern slopes. Its snowmelt feeds the springs of the Jordan River. Look for a long snowcapped ridge above dry hills.

name: Mount Hibok-Hibok
blurb: An active volcano on the small island of Camiguin, whose 1951 eruption killed hundreds. Look for the forested peak rising over a round island with reefs and a white sandbar offshore.

name: Mount Hokkaido Koma
blurb: A volcano near Hakodate whose 1640 summit collapse sent a tsunami that killed about 700 people. Look for the jagged peak above the lake-dotted Onuma park.

name: Mount Hudson
blurb: Its 1991 eruption was one of the largest of the century, burying Patagonian sheep ranches under ash. Look for its ice-filled caldera in the remote mountains of Aysén.

name: Mount Iraya
blurb: A volcano on Batan Island in the Batanes, the Philippines' northernmost province. Look for a green cone above rolling grassland and cliffs, between Luzon and Taiwan.

name: Mount Isarog
blurb: A large dormant volcano east of Naga City, its rainforested slopes a national park. Look for a broad, deeply eroded massif with a crater open to the east.

name: Mount Iwaki
blurb: Called Tsugaru Fuji, at about 5,330 ft the highest peak in Aomori prefecture. Look for a lone cone surrounded by apple orchards on the Tsugaru plain.

name: Mount Kalatungan
blurb: A dormant volcano in Bukidnon, one of the highest peaks on Mindanao, cloaked in mossy forest. Look for a long forested ridge rising above the plateau's pineapple plantations.

name: Mount Kanaga
blurb: A symmetrical, snow-capped cone on the north end of Kanaga Island in the western Aleutians, growing inside the broken rim of an older volcano.

name: Mount Kawi
blurb: An old volcano west of Malang in East Java, known for its pilgrimage shrines. Look for wooded slopes rising from sugar cane fields.

name: Mount Klabat
blurb: The highest point of North Sulawesi, a forested cone just east of Manado. Look for a single big volcano close to the city and the airport.

name: Mount Kupe
blurb: A forested mountain of about 6,900 ft in western Cameroon, a sacred site for local peoples and a hotspot for rare birds. Look for the green dome rising above the plantations.

name: Mount Kusatsu-Shirane
blurb: Home of Yugama, a turquoise acid crater lake, and of a surprise 2018 eruption that hit a ski area. Look for the bright blue-green lake in a gray crater above the hot spring town of Kusatsu.

name: Mount Liamuiga
blurb: The highest point on St. Kitts at about 3,800 ft, a dormant volcano with a crater wrapped in rainforest. Look for the green peak at the island's northwest end, above old sugarcane land.

name: Mount Makiling
blurb: A dormant volcano south of Manila, home to the University of the Philippines Los Baños and the legend of the forest spirit Maria Makiling. Look for the forested peak on the south shore of Laguna de Bay.

name: Mount Manengouba
blurb: A broad volcano in western Cameroon whose summit caldera holds two crater lakes, known locally as the male and female lakes. Look for the twin lakes in the grassy crater.

name: Mount Matutum
blurb: A forested cone near General Santos City in southern Mindanao, surrounded by pineapple plantations. Look for a lone, symmetrical peak rising above the patchwork of fields.

name: Mount Meakan
blurb: An active volcano beside Lake Akan in eastern Hokkaido. Look for a bare, steaming summit next to the green cone of Oakan across the lake.

name: Mount Nantai
blurb: An old eruption's lava dammed Lake Chuzenji at its foot, creating the lake and the 318-ft Kegon Falls. Look for a symmetrical cone above the lake near Nikko.

name: Mount Okmok
blurb: A caldera about 6 miles across on Umnak Island. Its eruption in 43 BC has been linked to the cold, famine years in Rome after Caesar's murder. Look for the huge ring with small cones inside.

name: Mount Parnassus
blurb: About 8,060 ft, the mountain above Delphi, sacred to Apollo and the Muses. Today it carries Greece's biggest ski area. Look for a broad limestone massif north of the Gulf of Corinth, snowy in winter.

name: Mount Ragang
blurb: An active volcano in central Mindanao in the Lanao region, deep in forested highlands. Look for a symmetrical cone rising from rugged green country southeast of Lake Lanao.

name: Mount Rausu
