blurb: At about 5,450 ft, the highest point of the Shiretoko Peninsula, a wild World Heritage site with brown bears and winter sea ice. Look for a peak on the narrow peninsula's spine.

name: Mount Rishiri
blurb: A near-perfect volcanic cone rising about 5,650 ft straight out of the sea off northern Hokkaido, called Rishiri Fuji. Look for a round island that is all mountain.

name: Mount Salak
blurb: A jagged volcano above Bogor; in 2012 a Sukhoi Superjet on a demo flight flew into its slopes. Look for several craggy peaks wrapped in forest just south of the Jakarta sprawl.

name: Mount Shari
blurb: A volcano at the base of the Shiretoko Peninsula above the town of Shari. Look for a cone between the Sea of Okhotsk coast and the Shiretoko peaks.

name: Mount Sibayak
blurb: A small, popular volcano above the hill town of Berastagi, with hot springs at its base. Look for a bare, steaming summit crater near the bigger Sinabung.

name: Mount Sindoro
blurb: At about 10,300 ft, a near-perfect cone paired with Sumbing across a saddle in Central Java. Look for terraced farms climbing almost to the summit.

name: Mount Spurr
blurb: An 11,070-ft volcano about 75 miles west of Anchorage. In 1992 its Crater Peak vent dropped ash on the city and shut the airport. Look for the broad icy massif at the head of Cook Inlet.

name: Mount Suswa
blurb: A Rift Valley volcano with a crater inside a crater; the inner pit circles a raised block like an island in a moat. Look for the concentric rings south of Lake Naivasha, and the lava tubes riddling its slopes.

name: Mount Tai
blurb: China's most sacred mountain, where emperors performed rites to heaven for more than 2,000 years. At 5,069 ft it isn't tall, but it rises sharply from the North China Plain; look for a rocky summit lined with temples, reached by thousands of stone steps.

name: Mount Talamau
blurb: The highest peak in West Sumatra, also called Ophir, sitting almost on the equator. Look for a forested massif with small summit lakes.

name: Mount Talang
blurb: An active volcano near Solok in West Sumatra, with a pair of lakes on its flank. Look for a steaming cone above rice fields and two lakes side by side.

name: Mount Tarumae
blurb: An active volcano near New Chitose Airport with a lava dome plugging its summit crater. Look for the dark dome on top, on the south side of Lake Shikotsu.

name: Mount Tendürek
blurb: A large shield volcano in eastern Turkey, south of Mount Ararat, with lava fields spreading across the plain around it. Look for the broad dark dome and black lava tongues near the Iranian border.

name: Mount Tokachi
blurb: An active volcano in central Hokkaido; its 1926 eruption melted snow into a mudflow that killed 144 people. Look for steaming craters on a bare gray summit.

name: Mount Wilis
blurb: A broad, eroded old volcano in East Java between Madiun and Kediri. Look for a wide forested massif with no clear cone.

name: Mount Karang
blurb: A volcano in Banten at Java's western end, near the city of Serang. Look for a wooded cone above farmland not far from the Sunda Strait.

name: Mount Patuha
blurb: A volcano south of Bandung known for Kawah Putih, a crater lake that shifts between pale turquoise and white. Look for the milky lake inside a pale crater among tea estates.

name: Mount Tampomas
blurb: A lone volcano near Sumedang, northeast of Bandung. Look for an isolated cone standing over the West Java lowlands.

name: Mutnovsky
blurb: A steaming volcano south of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky with a glacier inside its crater and a geothermal power plant on its flank. Look for a broken, ash-streaked crater with fumarole steam and snowfields.

name: Nahanni National Park Reserve
blurb: One of the first World Heritage Sites, named in 1978. The South Nahanni drops 315 ft at Virginia Falls, about twice the height of Niagara, then runs through canyons up to 3,300 ft deep. Look for the river snaking between mountain walls.

name: Nairobi National Park
blurb: The only national park on the edge of a capital city: giraffes and rhinos graze with Nairobi's skyline behind. Look for open savanna next to the runways of Jomo Kenyatta International.

name: Namtso
blurb: At about 15,500 ft, one of the highest large lakes on Earth, a sacred Tibetan lake of roughly 700 square miles. Look for turquoise water with the snowy Nyenchen Tanglha range along its southern shore.

name: Nettilling Lake
blurb: The largest lake on Baffin Island, over 2,100 square miles, sitting right on the Arctic Circle. Look for a huge lake with a ragged, island-filled east end in bare, rocky tundra.

name: Neusiedl Lake
blurb: A steppe lake on the Austria-Hungary border so shallow (about 6 ft at most) that it dried out completely in the 1860s. Look for a huge belt of reeds around a pale, wind-stirred lake.

name: Nevado del Quindío
blurb: A volcanic summit in Colombia's Los Nevados National Park, near Nevado del Ruiz. Its glaciers have largely or entirely melted. Look for the high bare peak among the park's ridges.

name: Nizhnekamsk Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Kama River at Naberezhnye Chelny, home of the KAMAZ truck plant. Look for a broad river-lake through flat forest and farmland.

name: Noel Kempff Mercado National Park
blurb: Built around the Huanchaca Plateau, whose sheer sandstone walls rise from the Amazon forest; some link it to Conan Doyle's The Lost World. Look for the cliff-edged tableland and waterfalls.

name: Northern Patagonian Ice Field
blurb: About 1,600 square miles of ice in Chile, beneath Monte San Valentín. Its San Rafael Glacier was long the closest tidewater glacier to the equator. Look for ice tongues feeding milky lakes.

name: Novosibirsk Reservoir
blurb: Called the Ob Sea, a long reservoir on the Ob River just above Novosibirsk, built in the 1950s. The science town of Akademgorodok sits in the pines on its shore. Look for the dam and the long lake behind it.

name: Nueltin Lake
blurb: A big, sprawling lake straddling the Manitoba-Nunavut border right at the tree line. Look for a ragged lake full of islands, with scattered spruce to the south and open tundra to the north.

name: Nærøyfjord
blurb: One of the narrowest fjords in the world, in places only about 800 ft across between walls more than 5,000 ft high, and a UNESCO site. Look for a thin slit of water branching off the inner Sognefjord.

name: O'Higgins/San Martín Lake
blurb: The deepest lake in the Americas, about 2,740 ft, its many arms spreading across the Chile-Argentina border. Look for milky turquoise water colored by glacier flour, with the O'Higgins Glacier feeding its western end.

name: Ollagüe
blurb: A volcano of about 19,300 ft straddling the Bolivia-Chile border, with a fumarole still steaming near its summit. Look for its plume and the white salt flats at its base.

name: Opinaca Reservoir
blurb: Part of the James Bay hydro project, built to divert the Eastmain River north into the La Grande system. Look for flooded, island-strewn water spreading across flat taiga.

name: Pantelleria Island
blurb: A volcanic island closer to Tunisia than to Sicily, famous for capers and sweet wine. Look for the green crater lake called the Mirror of Venus and the island's black lava coast.

name: Las Vegas Strip
blurb: Most of the 4-mile Strip lies outside Las Vegas city limits. Look for the black glass Luxor pyramid at the south end and the Sphere, a 366-ft LED ball, just east of the main drag.

name: Payun Matru
blurb: A broad shield volcano with a summit caldera, surrounded by hundreds of black cinder cones and lava flows in Mendoza's La Payunia reserve. Look for a dark, cratered moonscape spread over the steppe.

name: Petrified Forest National Park
blurb: Logs of 200-million-year-old wood turned to quartz lie across the Painted Desert, cut by I-40 and old Route 66. Look for red, purple and gray banded badlands.

name: Philadelphia
blurb: William Penn laid out its grid in 1682 between the Delaware and Schuylkill rivers. Look for City Hall's tower, topped by a statue of Penn, at the center of the grid where Broad and Market streets cross.

name: Pine Island Glacier
blurb: With Thwaites, one of the fastest-changing glaciers in Antarctica, flowing a couple of miles a year and shedding large icebergs every few years. Look for its long, fractured tongue reaching into Pine Island Bay.

name: Porak
blurb: A volcano on the Armenia-Azerbaijan border in the Vardenis range east of Lake Sevan. Look for dark lava flows spreading down its slopes.

name: Potanin Glacier
blurb: Mongolia's largest glacier, flowing off the Tavan Bogd massif where Mongolia, China and Russia meet. Look for a long white ice river in otherwise dry brown mountains.

name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
blurb: An underground river that flows about 5 miles through a limestone cave before emptying into the sea, one of the longest navigable ones in the world. Look for jagged karst mountains plunging into the sea on Palawan.

name: Puracé
blurb: An active volcano southeast of Popayán in Puracé National Park, with a sulfur mine on its flank. Look for steam and yellow sulfur on its upper slopes.

name: Purnululu National Park
blurb: Home of the Bungle Bungle Range, beehive-shaped sandstone domes striped orange and black, barely known outside the region until the 1980s. Look for the cluster of rounded, banded domes in the outback.

name: Päijänne
blurb: Finland's second-largest lake and its deepest, about 310 ft. Helsinki drinks from it through a 75-mile tunnel bored through bedrock. Look for a long lake running north-south.

name: Qarhan Playa
blurb: China's largest salt lake and a major source of potash fertilizer. The Qinghai-Tibet Railway and a highway cross it on a bed of salt. Look for huge rectangular evaporation ponds in shades of blue and green.

name: Quebrada de Humahuaca
blurb: A roughly 96-mile valley of striped mountains in red, purple and green, used as a trade route for 10,000 years and now a UNESCO site. Look for the Rio Grande's braided bed winding between colored ridges.

name: Red Lake
blurb: The largest natural lake entirely within Minnesota, split into Upper and Lower Red Lake by a narrow peninsula. Look for two big, round basins joined at a pinch in flat bog and forest.

name: Reindeer Lake
blurb: Saskatchewan's second-largest lake, straddling the border with Manitoba, known for very clear water. Look for a long sheet of water crowded with islands in the forested Shield.

name: Reventador
blurb: A volcano on the Amazon side of Ecuador's Andes. Its 2002 eruption dropped ash on Quito. Look for its plume.

name: Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf
blurb: Fronts Queen Maud Land on the Weddell Sea, named for Norwegian aviator Hjalmar Riiser-Larsen, who flew with Amundsen over the North Pole in 1926. Look for a flat white plain ending in sea cliffs.

name: Rincón de la Vieja Volcano
blurb: An active volcano in Guanacaste with fumaroles, mud pots and hot springs. Look for its crater above the dry forest.

name: Robert-Bourassa Reservoir
blurb: Behind one of the largest hydro plants in North America, whose powerhouse is carved deep underground. Look for the stepped spillway, nicknamed the Giant's Staircase, cut into rock at the reservoir's western end.

name: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon
blurb: A UNESCO site of about 445 uninhabited limestone islands, many undercut by the sea into mushroom shapes. Look for green knobs scattered across turquoise water, with dark reef edges between them.

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
blurb: Trail Ridge Road crosses it at 12,183 ft, the highest continuous paved road in the US, and Longs Peak tops out at 14,259 ft. Look for Longs Peak's flat summit and bare tundra along the Continental Divide.

name: Rukwa Lake
blurb: A shallow, salty lake in a branch of the Rift Valley in southwestern Tanzania, whose size swings widely with the rains. Look for a long lake between steep escarpments.

name: Rybinsk Reservoir
blurb: When it filled in the early 1940s it was the largest man-made lake in the world, drowning the town of Mologa and hundreds of villages. Look for a huge, shallow sheet of water, about 1,800 square miles, where the Volga meets the Sheksna.

name: Réservoir La Grande 3
blurb: One of the chain of reservoirs on the La Grande River that make up the James Bay hydro project. Look for flooded valleys and drowned hills turned islands across flat, lake-dotted taiga.

name: Réservoir Laforge 1
blurb: A reservoir in the James Bay hydro system, part of the works that divert the Caniapiscau River's flow west to La Grande. Look for an island-strewn lake in sparse northern forest.

name: Salar de Coipasa
blurb: Bolivia's second-largest salt flat, just north of Salar de Uyuni, with a small lake in its center. Look for a white plain ringed by volcanoes.

name: Salonga National Park
blurb: Africa's largest tropical rainforest reserve, about 13,000 square miles, reachable mainly by river. It's the only park protecting bonobos; look for unbroken canopy cut by dark winding rivers.

name: Samariá Gorge National Park
blurb: A gorge about 10 miles long through Crete's White Mountains, among the longest in Europe. At the Iron Gates its walls close to about 13 ft apart; look for the cleft opening onto the Libyan Sea.

name: San Carlos
blurb: A volcano on the southwest side of Bioko Island, the wetter, wilder end of Equatorial Guinea's main island. Look for forested slopes dropping to the Gulf of Guinea.

name: San José
blurb: A volcano of about 19,200 ft on the Argentina-Chile border at the head of the Cajón del Maipo, one of the closest big volcanoes to Santiago. Look for glaciers on its summit.

name: Sangeang Api
blurb: An island volcano off Sumbawa whose 2014 eruption cancelled flights to Darwin and Bali for days. Look for an uninhabited round island with a twin-peaked summit.

name: Saratov Reservoir
blurb: A long reach of the Volga between Samara and the dam at Balakovo, one of the river's chain of hydropower lakes. Look for a broad ribbon of water through flat steppe and farmland.

name: Sorik Marapi
blurb: Sorik Marapi, a volcano in North Sumatra with a summit crater lake. Look for a cone rising above the forested Barisan range near Panyabungan.

name: Sarychev Peak
blurb: The volcano covering most of tiny Matua Island; astronauts on the ISS photographed its 2009 eruption punching a hole through the clouds. Look for a round island almost entirely made of one cone.

name: Sarygamysh Lake
blurb: A salty lake in a desert depression on the Turkmenistan-Uzbekistan border, filled mostly by irrigation drainage since the 1960s. Look for a big blue lake in empty brown desert.

name: Schlei
blurb: A narrow, 25-mile arm of the Baltic winding into Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, looking more like a river than a sea inlet. The Viking town of Hedeby stood at its head; look for the long thin blue ribbon.

name: Scoresby Sound
blurb: The largest fjord system in the world, branching more than 200 miles into East Greenland. Look for a vast maze of deep inlets and icebergs among bare mountains.

name: Sequoia National Park
blurb: Home to General Sherman, the largest tree on Earth by volume, with 14,505-ft Mount Whitney on its eastern edge. Look for the Sierra Nevada crest and deep Kaweah canyons.

name: Serra da Capivara National Park
blurb: Holds one of the largest collections of prehistoric rock paintings in the Americas, on red sandstone cliffs. Look for a canyon-cut escarpment rising above gray-green caatinga scrub.

name: Shackleton Glacier
blurb: About 70 miles long, flowing from the polar plateau through the Queen Maud Mountains to the Ross Ice Shelf, and named for Ernest Shackleton. Look for a broad ice river between dark rock walls.

name: Shackleton Ice Shelf
blurb: Fed partly by the Denman Glacier, it fringes the Queen Mary Coast of East Antarctica. Charles Wilkes sighted part of it in 1840, and Douglas Mawson's 1911 to 1914 expedition named it for Ernest Shackleton.

name: Shalkarteniz
blurb: A salt lake on the dry plains of central Kazakhstan that is often mostly dry. Look for a pale, crusted basin with a thin skin of water, bright white against the brown steppe.

name: Shatt al Gharsah
blurb: A salt pan that dips below sea level, Tunisia's lowest point. Star Wars sets for Mos Espa still stand in the desert nearby. Look for a pale crust stretching west toward Algeria.

name: Sierra Negra
blurb: A volcano on Isabela Island in the Galápagos with one of the largest calderas on Earth, roughly 6 by 4 miles. Look for its oval crater.

name: Siling Lake
blurb: Now Tibet's largest lake: it overtook Namtso in the 2000s as glacier melt kept it growing. A saline lake at about 14,900 ft on the bare Changtang plateau; look for its ragged shoreline of drowned bays.

name: Simien Mountains National Park
blurb: Cliffs drop more than 3,000 ft off the Simien escarpment, home of gelada monkeys, with Ras Dashen at 14,928 ft nearby. Look for the sheer wall and the jagged pinnacles below it.

name: Singgalang
blurb: A quiet volcano facing Marapi across the valley at Bukittinggi, with a small crater lake hidden near its summit. Look for the greener of the two big cones.

name: Skelton Glacier
blurb: Edmund Hillary's party used it in 1957 to climb onto the polar plateau, then drove modified farm tractors on to the South Pole. Look for a long ice ramp rising from the Ross Ice Shelf into the mountains.

name: Smallwood Reservoir
blurb: One of the largest reservoirs in the world by area, created in the 1970s to feed the Churchill Falls power station, among the biggest in North America. Look for a vast tangle of flooded lakes and islands.

name: Sobradinho Reservoir
blurb: One of the largest reservoirs in the world by area, damming the São Francisco River in Brazil's dry northeast. Several towns were flooded and rebuilt to make it. Look for a vast lake in brown scrubland.

name: Solway Firth
blurb: An estuary marking the England to Scotland border, where the tide runs out across miles of sands and mudflats with dangerous speed. Look for vast shining sandbanks and channels between Cumbria and Dumfries and Galloway.

name: Songkhla Lake
blurb: Thailand's largest natural lake, a lagoon draining into the Gulf of Thailand at Songkhla. Look for the long shallow water, its northern end fading into marsh, behind a thin coastal strip.

name: Sotará
blurb: A volcano in southwestern Colombia south of Popayán, in the high Andes of Cauca. Look for its summit above the forested highlands.

name: Southern Indian Lake
blurb: A big lake on the Churchill River that was raised and dammed in the 1970s to send most of the river's flow south into the Nelson for hydropower. Look for a vast, island-studded lake in boreal forest.

name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
blurb: About 6,500 square miles, the largest ice mass in the Southern Hemisphere outside Antarctica. It spills dozens of glaciers into lakes and fjords. Look for white ice with jagged peaks rising through it.

name: Sumaco
blurb: An isolated cone east of Ecuador's main Andes, rising from the Amazon jungle. Look for its peak above the forest.

name: Sundarbans National Park
blurb: Part of the world's largest mangrove forest and home to Bengal tigers that swim between islands. Look for a maze of tidal channels braiding through dark green forest where the Ganges meets the sea.

name: Svartisen
blurb: Norway's second-largest glacier, straddling the Arctic Circle. One arm, Engabreen, reaches down close to sea level. Look for white ice on high ground above a fjord.

name: Swiss National Park
blurb: Founded in 1914, the oldest national park in the Alps, and among the strictest: no hunting, no camping, stay on the trail. Look for the forested valleys and limestone peaks in the Lower Engadine near the Italian border.

name: Syvash Bay
blurb: A web of shallow, very salty lagoons cut off from the Sea of Azov by the long Arabat Spit. Look for water tinted pink and red by salt-loving algae in summer.

name: Taapaca
blurb: A volcano of about 18,400 ft above the town of Putre in Chile's far north. Look for its snow-capped summit above the green Lluta valley.

name: Tacora
blurb: A volcano in Chile's far north near the Peru border, once mined for sulfur. Look for its snowy summit above the high plain.

name: Tanaga
blurb: The tallest of a cluster of volcanoes on Tanaga Island in the western Aleutians, near Adak. Look for the snowy cone at the island's north end, often wrapped in cloud.

name: Tanghe Shuiku
blurb: A reservoir in northern Henan, at the foot of the Taihang Mountains. Look for a lake in a valley where farmland gives way to hills.

name: Tarso Toussidé
blurb: A volcano in Chad's Tibesti mountains next to the Trou au Natron, a deep caldera whose floor is crusted white with natron salt. Look for the white-floored pit in dark rock.

name: Tatra National Park
blurb: The High Tatras, the highest range in the Carpathians, topped by Gerlachovský štít at about 8,710 ft. Look for a compact cluster of sharp granite peaks and glacial lakes rising abruptly from the flat Poprad basin.

name: Taunshits
blurb: A small volcano in eastern Kamchatka between the Kronotsky and Karymsky groups, in a district dense with cones. Look for a modest summit with a collapse scar among bigger snowy neighbors.

name: Taymyr
blurb: One of the largest lakes north of the Arctic Circle, on the Taymyr Peninsula at Asia's northern tip. Ice-covered most of the year; look for a long, branching lake in bare tundra.

name: Taï National Park
blurb: One of the last big blocks of primary rainforest in West Africa, home to chimpanzees that crack nuts with stone tools. Look for intact dark forest with a hard edge against farmland.

name: Tecuamburro
blurb: A forested volcanic complex south of Guatemala City, with a small acid crater lake and steaming ground. Look for wooded cones above the coastal plain.

name: Telica
blurb: One of Nicaragua's most persistently active volcanoes, in the Maribios chain northwest of León, with a deep crater that often glows at night. Look for a gray summit with a steam plume in the line of cones.

name: Three Gorges Reservoir Region
blurb: The world's largest hydroelectric dam backs up the Yangtze for about 400 miles. More than a million people were relocated. Look for the long winding river widened into a lake through steep gorges.

name: Tinguiririca Volcano
blurb: A volcano on the Argentina-Chile border in central Chile, with hot springs below. Look for its snowy summit above the green valley of Termas del Flaco.

name: Tongariro National Park
blurb: New Zealand's oldest national park, gifted by Maori chiefs in 1887, with three active volcanoes. Look for Ruapehu, the North Island's highest peak at about 9,200 ft, and the near-perfect cone of Ngauruhoe, Mount Doom in the Lord of the Rings films.

name: Torres del Paine National Park
blurb: The granite towers and black-capped Cuernos rising over turquoise lakes in Chilean Patagonia. Look for vertical spires next to the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.

name: Tres Vírgenes
blurb: Three volcanic peaks in the desert of Baja California Sur, near the old copper town of Santa Rosalía on the Gulf of California. A geothermal power plant sits on their flank.

name: Tromen
blurb: A volcano in northern Neuquén with young black lava flows spreading across the steppe below it. Look for the dark flows against the tan desert and the lagoon at its foot.

name: Trondheimsfjord
blurb: Norway's third-longest fjord, about 80 miles of wide, sheltered water reaching inland past Trondheim. Unusually, its shores are gentle farmland rather than cliffs. Look for a broad inland sea with the city on its southern shore.

name: Três Marias Reservoir
blurb: A huge reservoir on the São Francisco River in Minas Gerais, built in the 1950s and 60s for hydropower and flood control. Look for a sprawling lake with long branching arms reaching into the cerrado savanna.

name: Tsimlyansk Reservoir
blurb: A Don River reservoir filled in 1952 alongside the Volga-Don Canal, big enough that locals call it the Tsimlyansk Sea. Look for a wide, ragged blue band running more than 100 miles across the steppe.

name: Tulare Lake
blurb: Once the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, drained for farming until it vanished. It came back in 2023 after record snow. Look for the grid of farmland in the basin floor.

name: Tunka valley
blurb: A rift valley in Buryatia west of Lake Baikal, part of the same crack in the crust that made the lake. Small volcanic cones dot its floor beneath the jagged Tunka range to the north.

name: Tunupa volcano
blurb: A volcano over 17,000 ft on the northern shore of the Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat. Look for its red, ochre and purple striped slopes against the blinding white salt.

name: Turrialba
blurb: Reawakened around 2010 after over a century of quiet, it has repeatedly dropped ash on San José and closed the airport. Look for its gray crater above green farms.

name: Tutupaca
blurb: A volcano in southern Peru whose summit partly collapsed in an 1802 eruption, sending a debris avalanche across the valley. Look for a snowy peak with a collapse scar in the high, arid Andes near the Chilean border.

name: Tyatya
blurb: A volcano on the northern tip of Kunashir in the southern Kurils, with a younger cone inside an older one. Look for the cone-in-a-cone shape near the coast.

name: Ubinas
blurb: Peru's most active volcano, with a deep crater in a truncated summit and regular ash eruptions that dust nearby villages. Look for a flat-topped gray cone east of Arequipa, sometimes trailing a brown plume.

name: Ulungur Lake
blurb: A large lake in the dry Junggar Basin of northern Xinjiang, fed by the Ulungur River out of the Altai Mountains. Look for a broad blue lake set in brown steppe and desert.

name: Upsala Glacier
blurb: One of the largest glaciers in South America and one of the fastest retreating, calving into an arm of Lago Argentino. Look for a long tongue of ice ending in turquoise water dotted with icebergs.

name: Uturuncu
blurb: A Bolivian volcano of about 19,700 ft, quiet for some 250,000 years, yet the ground around it has been rising for decades over a huge body of magma below. Look for the snow-patched peak in the barren altiplano.

name: Valley of Flowers National Park
blurb: An alpine meadow around 11,000 to 12,000 ft that bursts into hundreds of flower species each monsoon, made famous by mountaineer Frank Smythe in 1931. Look for the green glacial valley between snowy peaks.

name: Varangerfjord
blurb: A wide Arctic fjord opening east toward the Barents Sea, near the Russian border. Unlike most Norwegian fjords, it faces east. Look for low, treeless tundra shores on a broad gray inlet.

name: Vembanad
blurb: India's longest lake, the heart of Kerala's backwaters, where houseboats drift between rice paddies below sea level. Look for a long lagoon running south from Kochi, edged by coconut palms and canals.

name: Viedma Lake
blurb: A long glacial lake fed by the Viedma Glacier, Argentina's largest. Look for milky blue water, with the granite spires of Fitz Roy rising near its northwest end.

name: Volcán Maipo
blurb: A symmetrical cone of about 17,300 ft on the Argentina-Chile border, standing inside the much larger Diamante caldera. Look for its reflection in Laguna del Diamante at its foot.

name: Volcán San Cristóbal
blurb: Nicaragua's highest volcano, about 5,700 ft, at the northern end of the Maribios range and frequently puffing gas. Look for the tallest cone in the chain of volcanoes running parallel to the Pacific coast.

name: Volgograd Reservoir
blurb: The last big reservoir on the Volga, held back by the hydro dam just upstream of Volgograd and stretching hundreds of miles north toward Saratov. Look for a broad river-lake through flat, brown steppe.

name: Votkinsk Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Kama River downstream from Perm, held back by a dam at Tchaikovsky. Look for a wide river-lake winding south through forest and farmland.

name: Vygozero
blurb: A large Karelian lake that became part of the White Sea-Baltic Canal, dug largely by Gulag prisoners in the early 1930s. Look for a sprawling, island-studded lake in dark taiga forest.

name: W National Park
blurb: Named for the double bend in the Niger River that traces a W along its edge, it is part of a huge protected area shared by Niger, Benin and Burkina Faso. Look for the river looping through dry savanna.

name: Warsaw
blurb: About 85% of the city was destroyed in World War II, and the Old Town was rebuilt brick by brick. Look for the 778-ft Palace of Culture and Science, Stalin's gift, beside the Vistula.

name: West Antarctic Ice Sheet
blurb: Much of it rests on bedrock far below sea level, which leaves it exposed to warm ocean water creeping underneath. Melted, it would raise global sea level by roughly 11 ft.

name: West Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating shelf off the East Antarctic coast, part of the long fringe of ice facing the Indian Ocean. Look for a flat white plain dotted with icebergs grounded along its edge.

name: Williston Lake
blurb: British Columbia's largest body of fresh water, formed when the W.A.C. Bennett Dam blocked the Peace River in 1968. Look for long arms of water winding through mountain valleys in the Rockies' northern trench.

name: Wiyâshâkimî Lake
blurb: Two round basins long thought to be twin impact craters; dating later showed the impacts were millions of years apart. Look for the ring of islands in the western basin, the clearest crater outline.

name: Wollaston Lake
blurb: The world's largest lake that drains naturally in two directions: north toward the Arctic Ocean and east toward Hudson Bay. Look for a big island-studded lake in the northern Saskatchewan Shield.

name: Wood Buffalo National Park
blurb: Canada's largest national park at about 17,300 square miles, bigger than Switzerland, home to the world's largest beaver dam and the last wild whooping crane flock. Look for the vast Peace-Athabasca Delta.

name: Wrangell–St. Elias National Park and Preserve
blurb: The largest US national park at 13.2 million acres, about six Yellowstones, with nine of the 16 highest US peaks including 18,008-ft Mount St. Elias. Look for vast glaciers and ice fields.

name: Yate
blurb: A glaciated volcano rising above the head of the Reloncaví Estuary in southern Chile, east of Puerto Montt. Look for its icy cone above the dark-green fjord and forest.

name: Yathkyed Lake
blurb: A large lake on the Kazan River in the Nunavut barren lands, in caribou country. Look for a sprawling lake in treeless tundra, frozen most of the year.

name: Yucamane
blurb: A young, symmetrical stratovolcano in Peru's Tacna region, about 18,200 ft. Look for a lone snow-tipped cone rising from the barren high desert near the Chilean border.

name: Zheltovsky
blurb: A volcano near the southern tip of Kamchatka, close to Kurile Lake and the Pacific coast. Look for a snowy cone in the volcanic cluster at the peninsula's narrow end.

name: Þrándarjökull
blurb: A small ice cap in the empty eastern highlands of Iceland, inland from the East Fjords. Look for a patch of white on a dark, bare plateau, well east of the much larger Vatnajökull.

name: Aagaard Glacier
blurb: Flows east off the Antarctic Peninsula toward the Weddell Sea side, where the coast is fringed by ice shelves. Look for a broad ice stream merging into the flat shelf ice.

name: Aaron Glacier
blurb: A glacier near the Thiel Mountains, an isolated range in the deep interior roughly 350 miles from the South Pole. Look for ice flowing around low dark peaks in an otherwise flat white plain.

name: Abbot Ice Shelf
blurb: Nearly 300 miles long, filling the gap between Thurston Island and the Eights Coast, with several ice-covered islands locked inside it. Look for a flat white plain with smooth domes where islands lie buried.

name: Abel Tasman National Park
blurb: New Zealand's smallest national park, a coast of golden sand beaches and granite headlands at the top of the South Island. Look for curving tan beaches and green-blue estuaries along Tasman Bay.

name: Abidjan
blurb: Côte d'Ivoire's largest city wraps around the Ébrié Lagoon, separated from the Atlantic by a thin barrier strip. Look for the Plateau's towers on a peninsula and bridges crossing the lagoon.

name: Abisko National Park
blurb: Above the Arctic Circle on the shore of Lake Torneträsk, and one of the best places on Earth for the northern lights thanks to a rain shadow that keeps skies clear. Look for Lapporten, a perfect U-shaped glacial valley to the west.

name: Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise National Park
blurb: One of Italy's oldest national parks, founded in 1923, and the last stronghold of the Marsican brown bear. Look for beech-covered mountains and the Barrea lake in the central Apennines.

name: Absheron National Park
blurb: At the tip of the Absheron Peninsula east of Baku, with gazelles and Caspian seals offshore. Look for the flat sandy spit pointing into the Caspian.

name: Aby Lagoon
blurb: A large coastal lagoon in southeastern Côte d'Ivoire near the Ghana border, separated from the Gulf of Guinea by a strip of sand. Look for dark water edged by forest and palms.

name: Academy Glacier
blurb: A large glacier in the Pensacola Mountains that feeds the Foundation Ice Stream, one of the big ice streams draining into the Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf. Look for broad flow lines between widely spaced ranges.

name: Acosta Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Ellsworth Land coast, between the Bellingshausen and Amundsen Seas in West Antarctica. Look for a broad stream of ice running out to the frozen coast.

name: Adams Glacier
blurb: An outlet glacier on the Budd Coast of Wilkes Land, not far from Australia's Casey Station. Look for a crevassed ice stream meeting the sea ice.

name: Adie Inlet
blurb: An ice-filled inlet on the east coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, fed by glaciers off the central plateau. Look for white ice shelf and floating ice where glaciers meet the sea.

name: Adirondacks
blurb: Adirondack Park covers 6 million acres, bigger than Yellowstone, Yosemite, Grand Canyon, Glacier and Olympic combined. Look for rounded forested peaks and thousands of lakes, topped by 5,344-ft Mount Marcy.

name: Aeronaut Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land, the mountainous coast west of the Ross Sea. Look for an ice stream winding between bare, dark peaks toward the coast.

name: Agalina Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers draining the mountainous spine of the Antarctic Peninsula, the fastest-warming part of the continent. Look for a crevassed tongue of ice running down to the sea between dark rock.

name: Ahern Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Ahlmann Glacier
blurb: Flows east off the Antarctic Peninsula toward the Larsen Ice Shelf side, named for Swedish glaciologist Hans Ahlmann. Look for a broad ice stream merging into flat shelf ice.

name: Ahmedabad
blurb: India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, founded in 1411. Gandhi set out from his ashram here on the 1930 Salt March. Look for the Sabarmati River lined with long concrete riverfront promenades through the center.

name: Ahrnsbrak Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Heritage Range of the Ellsworth Mountains, the range that also holds Antarctica's highest peak. Look for ice flowing between steep, banded rock ridges.

name: Aibi Lake
blurb: A shallow salt lake near the Kazakh border that has shrunk dramatically as its rivers were diverted to farms. Look for a pale lake ringed by wide white salt flats, a source of frequent dust storms.

name: Airy Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the southern Antarctic Peninsula, a remote stretch of ice-buried mountains seldom visited even by researchers. Look for flow lines in the ice between rocky ridges.

name: Aitkenhead Glacier
blurb: Flows off the Trinity Peninsula, the very northern tip of the Antarctic mainland, closest point to South America. Look for a short ice stream reaching the sea among icebergs.

name: Akagera National Park
blurb: Rwanda's only savanna park, along the Tanzanian border, where lions returned in 2015 and black rhinos in 2017. Look for a chain of lakes and papyrus swamp on the east side, rolling grassland to the west.

name: Akebono Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Prince Olav Coast of East Antarctica, in the area mapped by Japan's research program; akebono is Japanese for dawn. Look for ice flowing down to the sea ice.

name: Alam-Kuh
blurb: Iran's second-highest peak at about 15,910 ft, in the Alborz. Its sheer granite north wall is one of the great big-wall climbs of Asia. Look for the glaciated face above the Caspian side.

name: Albanus Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, deep in the interior a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for a river of ice threading between bare, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Albone Glacier
blurb: Flows east off the Antarctic Peninsula toward the Weddell Sea side, where the coast is fringed by ice shelves. Look for a broad ice stream merging into the flat shelf ice.

name: Albrecht Penck Glacier
blurb: A Victoria Land glacier named for Albrecht Penck, the German geographer who studied ice age glaciation in the Alps. Look for an ice stream winding between bare, dark peaks.

name: Alexandria
blurb: Founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC, Egypt's second city stretches about 20 miles along the Mediterranean. Look for the curving Corniche, the Eastern Harbor, and the round tilted disc of the new library.

name: Algarve coast
blurb: Portugal's south coast, famous for golden limestone cliffs, sea arches and caves like Benagil. Look for honey-colored rock broken into coves, with long sandy beaches and lagoons farther east.

name: Algie Glacier
blurb: Drains ice from the polar plateau down through the Transantarctic Mountains, some of the emptiest country on Earth. Look for flow lines and crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Alt Glacier
blurb: One of hundreds of valley glaciers in the coastal ranges of northern Victoria Land, some of the most rugged terrain in Antarctica. Look for white ice rivers between sharp, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Altafjord
blurb: Alta sits at its head, known for 6,000-year-old rock carvings. In WWII the battleship Tirpitz hid in one of its side arms. Look for a broad Arctic fjord with the town and its river delta at the inner end.

name: Altarduken Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the mountains of Queen Maud Land whose Norwegian name means the altar cloth. Look for a white sheet of ice draped between dark rock peaks.

name: Altyn-Emel National Park
blurb: Home of the Singing Dune, a lone sand dune several hundred feet high that hums in dry wind. Look for a single pale dune in the brown steppe north of the Ili River.

name: Alvand
blurb: A granite massif of about 11,700 ft above Hamadan, ancient Ecbatana, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Look for snow above the city and its green orchards.

name: Alyabiev Glacier
blurb: Like many features on Alexander Island, Antarctica's largest island, it is named for a composer, here the Russian Alexander Alyabyev. Look for ice flowing between dark ridges toward George VI Sound or the open sea.

name: Ambergris Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula, where ice pours off a narrow high plateau into fjords and bays. Look for a white ice stream ending at a calving front among floating bergs.

name: Amisk Lake
blurb: A large lake near Flin Flon on the Saskatchewan-Manitoba border, at the edge of the rocky Canadian Shield. Look for open water among granite outcrops and dark forest.

name: Ammassalik Fjord
blurb: A fjord beside Tasiilaq, the largest town on Greenland's east coast. Look for steep mountains, glaciers and drift ice in the water most of the year.

name: Amne Machin
blurb: A 20,610-ft massif sacred to Tibetans, who walk a multi-day pilgrimage circuit around it. The Yellow River loops around its base. Look for a broad, heavily glaciated block on the open plateau.

name: Andfjorden
blurb: A broad, deep Arctic channel between the islands of Andøya and Senja, where sperm whales and orcas come close to shore. Look for open water flanked by jagged island mountains.

name: Angikuni Lake
blurb: A lake on the Kazan River in the Nunavut barren lands. Look for a ragged lake in open tundra laced with eskers and countless smaller ponds, frozen most of the year.

name: Angilaaq Mountain
blurb: Highest point of Bylot Island, off northern Baffin. Look for a snowy, glaciated island cut by long ice tongues.

name: Angna Mountain
blurb: A peak on Baffin Island's Cumberland Peninsula, near the Arctic Circle. Look for bare peaks among glaciers and fjords.

name: Anna Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the South Shetland Islands, the ice-capped chain north of the Antarctic Peninsula dotted with research stations. Look for ice cliffs meeting dark water along the island shore.

name: Anuchin Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Queen Maud Land named for Russian geographer Dmitry Anuchin, in a region mapped by Soviet expeditions. Look for ice flowing around dark rock peaks.

name: Apfel Glacier
blurb: Near the Bunger Hills, a rare ice-free oasis of bare rock and lakes on the East Antarctic coast. Look for dark, ice-free ground beside the white glacier.

name: Aphrodite Glacier
blurb: Flows east off the Antarctic Peninsula toward the Weddell Sea side, where the coast is fringed by ice shelves. Look for a broad ice stream merging into the flat shelf ice.

name: Arago Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula, where ice pours off a narrow high plateau into fjords and bays. Look for a white ice stream ending at a calving front among floating bergs.

name: Arc Dome
blurb: Highest point of the Toiyabe Range at 11,773 ft, rising over the empty center of Nevada. Look for a long range, snowy in winter, above sagebrush valleys.

name: Arena Glacier
blurb: Flows off the Trinity Peninsula, the very northern tip of the Antarctic mainland, closest point to South America. Look for a short ice stream reaching the sea among icebergs.

name: Argentina Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the South Shetland Islands, the ice-capped chain north of the Antarctic Peninsula dotted with research stations. Look for ice cliffs meeting dark water along the island shore.

name: Argonaut Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land, the mountainous coast west of the Ross Sea. Look for an ice stream winding between bare, dark peaks toward the coast.

name: Argosy Glacier
blurb: Drains ice from the polar plateau down through the Transantarctic Mountains, some of the emptiest country on Earth. Look for flow lines and crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Armstrong Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the southern Antarctic Peninsula, a remote stretch of ice-buried mountains seldom visited even by researchers. Look for flow lines in the ice between rocky ridges.

name: Arnarfjörður
blurb: One of the largest fjords in the Westfjords of Iceland, branching into smaller fjords. Look for the Dynjandi waterfall, which spreads like a bridal veil down a mountainside near its head.

name: Arnavad Peak
blurb: A summit in the ranges of the western Pamirs in Tajikistan, where steep mountains drop into the gorges of the Panj and its tributaries. Look for snowy ridges above narrow green valley floors.

name: Arthur Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land, the remote West Antarctic coast facing the Amundsen and Ross Seas. Look for ice flowing between isolated peaks toward the coast.

name: Artillery Lake
blurb: A long, narrow lake northeast of Great Slave Lake, right at the tree line. Look for a slim lake with scattered spruce at its south end giving way to bare tundra at the north.

name: Asafiev Glacier
blurb: Like many features on Alexander Island, Antarctica's largest island, it is named for a composer, here the Russian Boris Asafyev. Look for ice flowing between dark ridges toward George VI Sound or the open sea.

name: Ashuanipi Lake
blurb: A long lake in western Labrador near the Quebec border, in iron-mining country. Look for a narrow, winding lake among low forested hills and bog, frozen white much of the year.

name: Ashworth Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Assender Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Enderby Land on the East Antarctic coast facing the Indian Ocean. Look for ice flowing between scattered rock outcrops toward the sea.

name: Astafjorden
blurb: A sheltered fjord in Troms threading between islands south of Harstad. Look for a winding channel among mountainous islands, with small farms clinging to the shoreline.

name: Astrolabe Glacier
blurb: Ends in a floating tongue beside France's Dumont d'Urville Station in Adélie Land, named for the ship of explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville. Look for the glacier tongue among rocky islets and sea ice.

name: Atatürk Reservoir
blurb: Formed by Atatürk Dam on the Euphrates, finished in 1990, one of the largest dams in the world. Look for a sprawling, many-armed lake in bare brown hills of southeastern Turkey.

name: Atikonak Lake
blurb: A large, irregular lake in western Labrador, south of the Smallwood Reservoir. Look for a maze of bays and islands in dark boreal forest, frozen white much of the year.

name: Atkinson Glacier
blurb: A northern Victoria Land glacier among some of the most rugged coastal ranges in Antarctica. Look for a white ice river between sharp, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Atlin Lake
blurb: British Columbia's largest natural lake, with its north tip poking into the Yukon. Look for a long blue lake hemmed in by glaciers and icefields to the west.

name: Attlee Glacier
blurb: Drains the high plateau of Graham Land, the northern half of the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for a narrow river of crevassed ice between steep, dark peaks.

name: Aubry Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the far north of the Northwest Territories, above the Arctic Circle. Look for an irregular lake in thinly treed tundra dotted with countless smaller ponds.

name: Aukštaitija National Park
blurb: Lithuania's first national park, created in 1974, a maze of more than 100 lakes linked by streams. Look for the patchwork of lakes in pine forest.

name: Aulavik National Park
blurb: On northern Banks Island in the Arctic, with the highest density of muskoxen on Earth. Look for treeless brown tundra cut by the Thomsen River, often called the northernmost navigable river in North America.

name: Auster Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Enderby Land on the East Antarctic coast facing the Indian Ocean. Look for ice flowing between scattered rock outcrops toward the sea.

name: Austin
blurb: The Texas Capitol here is taller than the US Capitol. Look for Lady Bird Lake, the dammed Colorado River through downtown; summer dusk brings over a million bats out from under the Congress Avenue Bridge.

name: Austreskorve Glacier
blurb: Flows through the mountains of Queen Maud Land, where the East Antarctic ice sheet spills toward the coast. Look for rock peaks standing like islands in a white sea.

name: Aveiro Lagoon
blurb: A shallow lagoon behind a long Atlantic sandbar, laced with canals and salt pans, which earned Aveiro the nickname Portugal's Venice. Look for neat rectangular salt pans and a channel cut through the dunes to the sea.

name: Aviator Glacier
blurb: One of the larger glaciers of Victoria Land, named for the pilots who flew in support of Antarctic research. Look for a wide, crevassed ice stream ending in a floating tongue on the Ross Sea.

name: Avsyuk Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers draining the mountainous spine of the Antarctic Peninsula, the fastest-warming part of the continent. Look for a crevassed tongue of ice running down to the sea between dark rock.

name: Aylmer Lake
blurb: A large, ragged lake in the barren lands northeast of Yellowknife, beyond the tree line. Look for a sprawling lake in open tundra, frozen white for most of the year.

name: Azimuthbjerg
blurb: One of the rock peaks of southeast Greenland's coast, where mountains break through the edge of the ice sheet. Look for dark ridges between glaciers spilling toward the sea.

name: Aýrybaba
blurb: Turkmenistan's highest point at about 10,300 ft, in the Köýtendag range on the Uzbek border. Look for a limestone ridge rising from desert, with deep canyons on its flanks.

name: Babadağ
blurb: A 6,460-ft mountain rising straight out of the sea above Ölüdeniz's blue lagoon, one of the world's best-known paragliding launches. Look for the bright lagoon and sandbar at its foot, and canopies drifting down.

name: Babine Lake
blurb: Often called the largest natural lake entirely within British Columbia, about 110 miles long and famous for its sockeye runs. Look for a long, narrow lake running northwest through forest.

name: Bader Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula, where ice pours off a narrow high plateau into fjords and bays. Look for a white ice stream ending at a calving front among floating bergs.

name: Baga Bogd
blurb: A peak of the Gobi-Altai rising above flat desert basins. Look for the abrupt line where bare mountains meet tan gravel plains, often with dry lake beds nearby.

name: Baghdad
blurb: Founded in 762 as a perfectly round walled city. Look for the Tigris looping through the city in tight meanders, with palm groves along its banks.

name: Bahaya
blurb: One of the high points of the dry mountains of northeastern Somalia, near the Horn of Africa. Look for bare, rust-brown ridges cut by dry riverbeds running to the Gulf of Aden.

name: Baiyang Lake
blurb: The largest freshwater wetland in the North China Plain, a patchwork of reed beds and channels next to the Xiong'an New Area. Look for a grid of reed islands and waterways in flat farmland.

name: Balchen Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land named for Bernt Balchen, the Norwegian-American pilot who flew Richard Byrd over the South Pole in 1929. Look for ice flowing between isolated peaks toward the coast.

name: Balish Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Heritage Range of the Ellsworth Mountains, the range that also holds Antarctica's highest peak. Look for ice flowing between steep, banded rock ridges.

name: Balsfjorden
blurb: A long fjord reaching south from the Tromsø area into the mountains of Troms. Look for a narrow arm of water with snowy peaks rising on both sides and the main road running along its shore.

name: Baltimore
blurb: At Fort McHenry in 1814, Francis Scott Key watched the British bombardment and wrote the Star-Spangled Banner. Look for the star-shaped fort at the harbor mouth and the Inner Harbor at the head of the Patapsco.

name: Bandhavgarh National Park
blurb: One of the densest tiger populations in India, with a ruined fort on its central cliffs. Look for forested hills around the flat-topped Bandhavgarh hill.

name: Barber Glacier
blurb: One of hundreds of valley glaciers in the coastal ranges of northern Victoria Land, some of the most rugged terrain in Antarctica. Look for white ice rivers between sharp, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Barcus Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the southern Antarctic Peninsula, a remote stretch of ice-buried mountains seldom visited even by researchers. Look for flow lines in the ice between rocky ridges.

name: Bardiya National Park
blurb: The largest wilderness in Nepal's Terai lowlands, known for tigers. Look for the braided Karnali River spilling out of the hills along its western edge, with forest and grassland to the east.

name: Barnett Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land, the mountainous coast west of the Ross Sea. Look for an ice stream winding between bare, dark peaks toward the coast.

name: Barrett Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, deep in the interior a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for a river of ice threading between bare, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Barsakelmes Lake
blurb: A remnant of water on the dried bed of the Aral Sea, near the former island of Barsakelmes, whose name means you go and don't come back. Look for pale salt flats around it.

name: Bartrum Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Bartók Glacier
blurb: Like many features on Alexander Island, Antarctica's largest island, it is named for a composer, here the Hungarian Béla Bartók. Look for ice flowing between dark ridges toward George VI Sound or the open sea.

name: Bashful Peak
blurb: At about 8,000 ft the highest point in Chugach State Park, just outside Anchorage. Look for a jagged gray summit above Eklutna Lake in the mountains northeast of the city.

name: Baskatong Reservoir
blurb: A big reservoir on the Gatineau River in western Québec, popular for fishing and cottages. Look for a sprawling, many-armed body of water flooded into rolling forested hills.

name: Batnfjorden
blurb: A short fjord off the Romsdal coast in Gjemnes. Look for a small inlet among wooded hills and farmland, branching from the larger channels between Molde and Kristiansund.

name: Battye Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Prince Charles Mountains, part of the vast Lambert Glacier system that empties into the Amery Ice Shelf. Look for ice flowing past dark mountain blocks.

name: Bayano Lake
blurb: Panama's second-largest lake after Gatun, created when the Bayano River was dammed in the 1970s. Look for a branching reservoir with drowned-forest inlets east of Panama City.

name: Beaman Glacier
blurb: Flows through the Transantarctic Mountains of Victoria Land, where ice from the polar plateau squeezes between ranges on its way toward the Ross Sea. Look for crevassed ice between rock walls.

name: Beaver Glacier
blurb: Drains ice from the polar plateau down through the Transantarctic Mountains, some of the emptiest country on Earth. Look for flow lines and crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Beitstadfjorden
blurb: The innermost basin of the Trondheimsfjord, reaching up to Steinkjer. Look for a wide, almost lake-like bay at the end of a narrow strait, ringed by farmland.

name: Bellsund
blurb: A wide fjord on Spitsbergen's west coast, south of Isfjorden, splitting into long arms with glaciers spilling into them. Look for a broad inlet with ice tongues and striped, barren mountains on both shores.

name: Bengaluru
blurb: India's tech capital sits about 3,000 ft up on the Deccan Plateau, which keeps it milder than most Indian cities. Look for dozens of lakes and reservoirs scattered through the sprawl, built as tanks centuries ago.

name: Berill Mountain
blurb: One of the high summits of the Suntar-Khayata range in Yakutia, a remote cluster of glaciers in one of the coldest places in the Northern Hemisphere. Look for white ice tongues among dark, treeless ridges.

name: Bernardo O'Higgins National Park
blurb: Chile's largest national park, covering much of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, where Pío XI, one of the few advancing glaciers, reaches the sea. Look for ice and fjords.

name: Berry Glacier
blurb: Flows through Marie Byrd Land, one of the least visited parts of Antarctica and one of the few that no country claims. Look for streaks of crevassed ice heading for the sea.

name: Bhalu Lek
blurb: A ridge in western Nepal's middle hills, below the high Himalaya. Look for terraced slopes and forest stepping up to the snow line to the north.

name: Bicaz Canyon
blurb: A tight limestone gorge in the Eastern Carpathians with walls about 1,000 ft high, squeezed so narrow the road runs under overhanging rock. Look for the thin slot just east of the Red Lake.

name: Big Moose Lake
blurb: A small Adirondack lake where a 1906 drowning became a murder case, and later the basis for Theodore Dreiser's novel An American Tragedy. Look for a forest-ringed lake among dozens of others.

name: Big Trout Lake
blurb: A large lake in Ontario's far north, home to the Kitchenuhmaykoosib Inninuwug First Nation and reachable mostly by air or winter road. Look for open water ringed by flat, dark forest.

name: Bingham Glacier
blurb: Flows east off the Antarctic Peninsula toward the Weddell Sea side, where the coast is fringed by ice shelves. Look for a broad ice stream merging into the flat shelf ice.

name: Biogradska Gora
blurb: Protects one of the last stands of primeval forest in Europe, with trees centuries old around glacial Biograd Lake. Look for a small lake in a dense dark-green valley in the mountains of northern Montenegro.

name: Bistcho Lake
blurb: A remote lake in Alberta's far northwest corner, near the British Columbia and Northwest Territories borders. Look for a broad, island-dotted lake in unbroken boreal forest and muskeg.

name: Bjarnarfjörður
blurb: A small fjord on Iceland's remote Strandir coast in the Westfjords, known for natural hot springs. Look for a short inlet between flat-topped basalt mountains.

name: Bjugnfjorden
blurb: A small fjord on the Fosen peninsula, northwest of Trondheim. Look for a sheltered inlet cutting into low, green coastal hills facing the open Norwegian Sea.

name: Black Glacier
blurb: One of hundreds of valley glaciers in the coastal ranges of northern Victoria Land, some of the most rugged terrain in Antarctica. Look for white ice rivers between sharp, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Black Lake
blurb: A lake on the Fond du Lac River in far northern Saskatchewan, near the Dene community of the same name. Look for a long body of water in sparse forest on the way to Lake Athabasca.

name: Blackwall Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, deep in the interior a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for a river of ice threading between bare, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Blaiklock Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Shackleton Range named for Ken Blaiklock, surveyor on the 1955 to 1958 Commonwealth Trans-Antarctic Expedition. Look for ice wrapping around dark rock spurs.

name: Blue Glacier
blurb: Flows from the Royal Society Range to McMurdo Sound across from Ross Island, named by Scott's first expedition for its blue ice. Look for a broad ice lobe on the coast west of McMurdo Station.

name: Blue Mountains National Park
blurb: Named for the blue haze given off by eucalyptus oil, these are sandstone plateaus cut by deep canyons just west of Sydney. Look for flat-topped forested ridges ending in sheer orange cliffs.

name: Blue Ridge
blurb: The eastern rampart of the Appalachians, followed for 469 miles by the Blue Ridge Parkway. Look for the long single ridge line rising above the Virginia Piedmont, often tinted blue by haze.

name: Bluenose Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the tundra of western Nunavut, near the Arctic coast. Look for an irregular lake in treeless country dotted with smaller ponds, frozen most of the year.

name: Blyde River Canyon
blurb: One of the largest canyons in the world and among the greenest, about 16 miles long and over 2,500 ft deep. Look for the Three Rondavels, round hut-shaped peaks above the dammed lake.

name: Blåmannsisen
blurb: An ice cap in Nordland, Norway, near the Swedish border. Look for a white plateau with bare gray rock and meltwater lakes around its edges.

name: Boboiob
blurb: One of the higher summits of the Kurama range in northern Tajikistan, the mountains at the western edge of the Fergana Valley. Look for bare ridges above the irrigated green of the valley.

name: Bogotá
blurb: One of the highest big capitals in the world, at about 8,700 ft on a high Andean plateau. Look for the green Monserrate ridge rising abruptly along the city's east side.

name: Boknafjord
blurb: The great fjord system north of Stavanger, fanning into the Ryfylke fjords. A road tunnel being dug under it will be among the longest and deepest undersea road tunnels in the world. Look for a wide bay dotted with islands.

name: Bolon
blurb: A large, shallow floodplain lake beside the Amur River near Amursk. Look for a broad sheet of water among marshes and channels in the wide Amur lowland.

name: Boom Gorge
blurb: The Chu River's gorge between Bishkek and Lake Issyk-Kul, carrying the main road and a railway between bare mountains. Look for the narrow green valley climbing toward the big blue lake.

name: Borah Peak
blurb: Idaho's highest peak at about 12,660 ft. The 1983 Borah Peak earthquake raised the range and dropped the valley floor, leaving a fresh fault scarp still visible. Look for the bare limestone crest of the Lost River Range.

name: Borchgrevink Glacier
blurb: A big Victoria Land glacier ending in a floating tongue on the Ross Sea, named for Carsten Borchgrevink, who led the first party to winter on the Antarctic mainland, in 1899. Look for the tongue jutting into the sea.

name: Borchgrevinkisen
blurb: A glacier in Queen Maud Land whose Norwegian name honors Carsten Borchgrevink, leader of the first party to winter on the Antarctic mainland. Look for ice flowing around dark rock peaks.

name: Borgarfjörður
blurb: A wide fjord in western Iceland crossed by a long causeway and bridge to the town of Borgarnes. Look for the bridge cutting across shallow tidal flats.

name: Borgarfjörður Eystri
blurb: A small fjord in Iceland's far east, known for colorful rhyolite mountains and a puffin colony. Look for a village tucked at the head of the fjord under orange and pink hills.

name: Borjomi Gorge
blurb: A forested valley of the Mtkvari River in central Georgia, famous for the Borjomi mineral water bottled here since the 1800s. Look for the dark green slopes of a national park on either side.

name: Bosque Fray Jorge National Park
blurb: Valdivian-style rainforest kept alive by coastal fog in semi-arid northern Chile, hundreds of miles from similar forest. Look for green patches on coastal hilltops above dry scrub.

name: Boston
blurb: Much of the city sits on fill: Back Bay was a tidal marsh until the 1800s. Boston Common, set aside in 1634, is the oldest public park in the US; look for it beside the Charles River basin.

name: Botev Peak
blurb: About 7,800 ft, the highest point of the Balkan Mountains that run across the middle of Bulgaria, named for the poet and revolutionary Hristo Botev. Look for a grassy dome topped by a weather station and tower.

name: Bou-Hedma National Park
blurb: Protects one of the last stands of Saharan acacia savanna in Tunisia, where scimitar-horned oryx and addax have been reintroduced. Look for the ridge of Jebel Bou-Hedma above the dry steppe.

name: Bowin Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, deep in the interior a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for a river of ice threading between bare, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Brandau Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Brandberg
blurb: Namibia's highest mountain at about 8,440 ft, a single granite dome rising from flat desert. It shelters thousands of rock paintings, including the White Lady. Look for a dark, round massif roughly 15 miles across.

name: Brisbane
blurb: Built on the loops of the Brisbane River, which winds through the city in tight bends. Look for the steel Story Bridge downtown and the river snaking out to Moreton Bay.

name: Brofjorden
blurb: A deep-water fjord on Sweden's west coast, home to Sweden's largest oil refinery at Lysekil. Look for the refinery's tanks and jetties on a rocky, island-studded coastline.

name: Brown Peak
blurb: The highest point of Sturge Island in the Balleny Islands, a remote volcanic chain far off the Antarctic coast. Look for an ice-capped island alone in the Southern Ocean.

name: Brunonia Glacier
blurb: A glacier on South Georgia, the mountainous sub-Antarctic island where Shackleton made his famous crossing in 1916. Look for white ice pouring off dark peaks into the sea.

name: Buenos Aires
blurb: Spread across the flat pampas on the Río de la Plata, the widest river estuary in the world, so muddy it looks like brown sea. Look for the dense grid against the water and Avenida 9 de Julio cutting through it.

name: Buffalo
blurb: At the east end of Lake Erie, where the Niagara River drains toward the falls about 20 miles north. Look for the Peace Bridge to Canada and the concrete grain elevators along the Buffalo River.

name: Buffalo Lake
blurb: A lake south of Great Slave Lake in the forest of the southern Northwest Territories. Look for a broad lake in flat boreal forest and muskeg.

name: Buir Lake
blurb: A large lake on the grasslands of eastern Mongolia, at the Chinese border. Look for a broad oval of water in flat steppe, with a river draining north toward Hulun Lake in China.

name: Bukadaban Feng
blurb: About 22,500 ft in the Kunlun Mountains on the Qinghai-Xinjiang line, among the highest points of the Hoh Xil plateau. Look for a long white ridge above a sea of empty, lake-dotted tableland.

name: Bumhpa Bum
blurb: A remote peak in Kachin State, among the forested ranges of Myanmar's far north. Look for steep, roadless ridges, snow-free most of the year.

name: Bundala National Park
blurb: Sri Lanka's first Ramsar wetland, a chain of shallow coastal lagoons and salt pans on the dry southeast coast that draws flamingos in winter. Look for the pale lagoons strung behind the beach.

name: Bunnefjorden
blurb: The quiet inner arm of the Oslofjord, running south from the capital. Look for a narrow finger of water with forested shores and summer cabins, just south of Oslo's harbor.

name: Bunner Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land, the remote West Antarctic coast facing the Amundsen and Ross Seas. Look for ice flowing between isolated peaks toward the coast.

name: Buyu Balease
blurb: A high point of central Sulawesi, in mountains largely covered by rainforest. Look for a forested crest rising above the island's interior valleys, often in cloud.

name: Bénoué National Park
blurb: Savanna woodland along the Bénoué River in northern Cameroon. Look for the wide sandy river through dry bush.

name: Bøkfjorden
blurb: A fjord near Kirkenes, a few miles from the Russian border. Look for a sheltered inlet in low, rocky tundra, with the town and its port on the shore.

name: Bømlafjorden
blurb: A broad sound south of Bergen, crossed underneath by one of the deepest road tunnels in the world, part of the Triangle Link. Look for open water between the island of Bømlo and the mainland.

name: Børgefjell National Park
blurb: One of Norway's wildest mountain parks, roadless and remote, on the Nordland-Trøndelag border near Sweden. Look for rounded snowy peaks, glacial lakes and treeless plateau with no settlements at all.

name: Cabañeros National Park
blurb: Called Spain's Serengeti for its open grassy plains dotted with trees and herds of red deer, between ridges of the Montes de Toledo. Look for the flat plain framed by wooded hills.

name: Cabonga Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir in La Vérendrye Wildlife Reserve, in the forests of western Québec. Look for an extremely ragged, island-filled shoreline, typical of a flooded Shield landscape.

name: Cadman Glacier
blurb: Drains the high plateau of Graham Land, the northern half of the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for a narrow river of crevassed ice between steep, dark peaks.

name: Cairngorms National Park
blurb: The UK's largest national park, with a high plateau so cold and bare it holds Arctic-style tundra and snow patches into summer. Look for the broad, rounded granite mountains and the dark corries cut into them.

name: Cairo
blurb: The largest city in Africa and the Arab world, on the Nile just above the Delta. Look for the river with Zamalek and Roda islands, and on the western desert edge the Pyramids of Giza.

name: Calgary
blurb: The Bow and Elbow rivers meet downtown, with the Rockies about 50 miles west. Look for the tight cluster of towers rising from an endless prairie grid.

name: Cambridge Glacier
blurb: Flows through the Transantarctic Mountains of Victoria Land, where ice from the polar plateau squeezes between ranges on its way toward the Ross Sea. Look for crevassed ice between rock walls.

name: Canham Glacier
blurb: One of hundreds of valley glaciers in the coastal ranges of northern Victoria Land, some of the most rugged terrain in Antarctica. Look for white ice rivers between sharp, snow-streaked ridges.

name: Canyon Glacier
blurb: Drains ice from the polar plateau down through the Transantarctic Mountains, some of the emptiest country on Earth. Look for flow lines and crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Capitol Reef National Park
blurb: Built around the Waterpocket Fold, a 100-mile-long wrinkle in the Earth's crust. Look for the long tilted ridge of colored rock running north to south across the desert.

name: Cardiel Lake
blurb: A lake with no outlet in the empty steppe of Santa Cruz province, Patagonia. Look for a deep blue lake set in dry brown plateau.

name: Carlson Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the southern Antarctic Peninsula, a remote stretch of ice-buried mountains seldom visited even by researchers. Look for flow lines in the ice between rocky ridges.

name: Carroll Inlet
blurb: An inlet on the English Coast of West Antarctica, filled by ice shelf rather than open water. Look for flat white ice between low ice-covered headlands.

name: Casa de Piedra Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Colorado River where it forms the border of La Pampa and Río Negro provinces in northern Patagonia. Look for a long lake of blue water in barren scrubland.

name: Cerro El Centinela (Torreón)
blurb: A hill rising over the Torreón area in the dry north of Mexico, among desert ranges around the Laguna region. Look for brown, bare slopes above flat irrigated farmland.

name: Cerro El Potosí
blurb: At about 12,200 ft, the highest peak in Nuevo León, southwest of Monterrey, crowned with a relict pine forest and antenna masts. Look for a high summit above dry plains.

name: Cerro El Toro
blurb: A summit of roughly 20,000 ft in San Juan province where climbers found a frozen Inca sacrifice, the El Toro mummy, in 1964. Look for a snowy peak in dry, empty Andes near the Chilean border.

name: Cerro Las Conchas
blurb: A peak in the rugged Sierra Madre del Sur of coastal Michoacán. Look for steep, forested ridges folding down toward the Pacific.

name: Cerro Peña Nevada
blurb: One of the highest summits of the Sierra Madre Oriental at about 11,600 ft, in southern Nuevo León. Look for a forested crest above dry desert to the west.

name: Cerro Tía Chena
blurb: A peak in the ranges west of Monterrey, where the Sierra Madre Oriental folds into rocky ridges. Look for the sharp gray folds of limestone.

name: Chagan Lake
blurb: Famous for winter fishing done the old way: crews cut holes in thick ice and haul huge nets under it with horse-drawn winches. In summer look for a wide shallow lake on the flat steppe of western Jilin.

name: Chamechaude
blurb: At about 6,830 ft, the highest summit of the Chartreuse range, home of the monks and their green liqueur, just north of Grenoble. Look for a limestone wedge with a sheer cliff face above forest.

name: Changla
blurb: A glaciated peak in far western Tibet near the Nepal border. Look for scattered snow summits above dry, rust-colored plateau.

name: Chaos Glacier
blurb: Flows to the Ingrid Christensen Coast of East Antarctica, not far from Australia's Davis Station. Look for a heavily crevassed ice stream meeting the sea ice.

name: Charlotte
blurb: The second-largest US banking center after New York, home to Bank of America. Look for the cluster of Uptown towers and, to the north, the long arms of Lake Norman, a Duke Energy reservoir.

name: Charybdis Glacier
blurb: Flows from the Prince Charles Mountains into the Amery Ice Shelf, named for the whirlpool of Greek myth. Look for a band of churned, crevassed ice where it joins the shelf.

name: Charyn Canyon
blurb: About 95 miles long and often compared to the Grand Canyon, with red rock towers in its Valley of Castles. Look for the red gash cut into flat steppe east of Almaty.

name: Chatsquot Mountain
blurb: A glaciated summit in the Kitimat Ranges of the Coast Mountains, inland from the fjords around Kitimat. Look for dark rock and ice above deep forested valleys.

name: Chaupi Orco
blurb: At about 19,800 ft the highest peak of the Cordillera Apolobamba on the Bolivia-Peru border, where the Andes start to drop toward the Amazon. Look for glaciers above dark lakes and steep green valleys.

name: Chavez Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Ellsworth Land coast, between the Bellingshausen and Amundsen Seas in West Antarctica. Look for a broad stream of ice running out to the frozen coast.

name: Cheekha Dar
blurb: About 11,850 ft on the Iran-Iraq border, Iraq's highest point. Look for snowy ridges of the Zagros above the green valleys of Iraqi Kurdistan.

name: Cherangany Hills
blurb: A forested range in western Kenya rising to about 11,000 ft, above the Kerio Valley escarpment of the Rift. Look for green hills and tea farms on the rim of the deep valley.

name: Chiemsee
blurb: Bavaria's largest lake, nicknamed the "Bavarian Sea." King Ludwig II built a copy of Versailles on one of its islands. Look for the islands near the western shore, with the Alps just south.

name: Chiribiquete National Park
blurb: Colombia's largest national park, where flat-topped sandstone tepuis rise sheer out of the Amazon canopy, their walls covered in tens of thousands of ancient rock paintings. Look for the dark tablelands breaking the green.

name: Chiricahua Peak
blurb: At nearly 9,800 ft the top of the Chiricahua Mountains, a sky island of pine and fir rising from desert grassland in Arizona's southeast corner. Look for a dark forested range among pale flats.

name: Chott el Hodna
blurb: A salt lake in the Hodna basin, a closed depression ringed by mountains in northern Algeria. Look for a pale oval of salt flats and seasonal water.

name: Christensen Glacier
blurb: Glacier on Bouvet Island, often called the most remote island on Earth, almost entirely covered in ice and more than 1,000 miles from any land. Look for a white dome rising from the open Southern Ocean.

name: Christiaensen Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Queen Maud Land, the Norwegian-claimed sector of East Antarctica, where dark nunataks poke through the ice sheet. Look for ice flowing around bare rock peaks.

name: Churchill Lake
blurb: One of a chain of lakes along the upper Churchill River system in northwest Saskatchewan. Look for a long, irregular lake in flat boreal forest scattered with bogs and smaller lakes.

name: Cilento, Vallo di Diano and Alburni National Park
blurb: Italy's second-largest national park, from mountains down to a coast that includes the Greek temples of Paestum. Look for the temples on the plain near the sea south of Salerno.

name: Cima Brenta
blurb: One of the highest summits of the Brenta Dolomites at about 10,330 ft, west of Trento. Look for pale towers and walls of dolomite rock, separate from the main Dolomites to the east.

name: Clarke Glacier
blurb: One of three Antarctic glaciers with this name, this one on the Antarctic Peninsula, where ice pours off a narrow plateau into fjords. Look for a white ice stream ending at a calving front.

name: Clarke Glacier
blurb: One of three Antarctic glaciers with this name, this one in Marie Byrd Land, the remote coast facing the Amundsen Sea. Look for ice flowing between isolated peaks toward the coast.

name: Clarke Glacier
blurb: One of three Antarctic glaciers with this name, this one in Victoria Land, west of the Ross Sea. Look for an ice stream winding between bare, dark peaks toward the coast.

name: Cleaves Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Clinton-Colden Lake
blurb: A big, island-filled lake in the barren lands of the Northwest Territories, beyond the tree line. Look for a tangle of water and bare rock in open tundra, frozen white most of the year.

name: Col Nudo
blurb: About 8,100 ft, the high point of the Alpago pre-Alps above Lake Santa Croce, near the Vajont dam disaster site. Look for a bare limestone ridge at the edge of the plain.

name: Cold Lake
blurb: A deep, clear lake straddling the Alberta-Saskatchewan border. Canada's busiest fighter base, CFB Cold Lake, sits nearby. Look for the round lake with the town on its western shore.

name: Coleman Glacier
blurb: Flows through Marie Byrd Land, one of the least visited parts of Antarctica and one of the few that no country claims. Look for streaks of crevassed ice heading for the sea.

name: Columbia Glacier
blurb: One of the fastest-retreating glaciers in the world, pulling back about 12 miles since 1980. Its icebergs are why the Exxon Valdez left the shipping lane in 1989 before grounding on Bligh Reef.

name: Columbus
blurb: Ohio's largest city and capital, home to Ohio State. Look for the horseshoe of Ohio Stadium beside the Olentangy River and the Scioto River curving past downtown.

name: Congaree National Park
blurb: The largest stretch of old-growth bottomland hardwood forest left in the southeastern US, with some of the tallest trees in eastern North America. Look for dark canopy on the Congaree River floodplain southeast of Columbia.

name: Conger Glacier
blurb: Feeds the area of the Conger Ice Shelf, which collapsed in March 2022, the first recorded ice shelf collapse in East Antarctica. Look for broken ice and open water along the coast.

name: Connemara National Park
blurb: Quartzite peaks, bogs and lakes in western Ireland, part of the Twelve Bens range. Look for the pointed summits and dark bog pools near Kylemore.

name: Contwoyto Lake
blurb: A long Arctic lake that marks the far end of the Tibbitt to Contwoyto winter road, the ice road that supplies the diamond mines north of Yellowknife. Look for a narrow, winding lake in bare tundra.

name: Cook Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating shelf on the George V Coast of East Antarctica, fed by the Cook Ice that drains part of the Wilkes Subglacial Basin. Look for a flat white plain ending in low cliffs.

name: Cooke Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Ellsworth Land coast, between the Bellingshausen and Amundsen Seas in West Antarctica. Look for a broad stream of ice running out to the frozen coast.

name: Corcovado National Park
blurb: National Geographic called it the most biologically intense place on Earth. Look for unbroken rainforest covering the Osa Peninsula down to the Pacific beaches.

name: Cornwall Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Shackleton Range, an isolated block of mountains near the head of the Filchner Ice Shelf. Look for ice wrapping around dark rock spurs.

name: Craters of the Moon
blurb: A lava field covering about 600 square miles of Idaho, where Apollo astronauts trained in 1969. Look for a black, rough sea of lava flows and cinder cones cutting across the sagebrush plain.

name: Crazy Peak
blurb: Highest peak of the Crazy Mountains at 11,214 ft, an island range rising out of the plains north of I-90. Look for a tight cluster of sharp, snowy peaks with prairie all around.

name: Cross Lake
blurb: A lake on the Nelson River in northern Manitoba, home to the Cross Lake First Nation. Look for a rocky, island-dotted lake where the big river widens through the boreal forest.

name: Crosson Ice Shelf
