blurb: A small, rapidly thinning ice shelf in the Amundsen Sea next to Thwaites Glacier, fed by the Smith and Pope Glaciers. Look for fractured floating ice between the bigger glaciers.

name: Curonian Spit National Park
blurb: A 61-mile sand spit shared with Russia, with some of the highest drifting dunes in Europe. Look for the thin sand strip between the Curonian Lagoon and the Baltic.

name: Cát Tiên National Park
blurb: One of the largest lowland tropical forests left in southern Vietnam, along the Dong Nai River. Vietnam's last Javan rhino was poached here in 2010. Look for the river looping through unbroken forest.

name: Cévennes National Park
blurb: Robert Louis Stevenson crossed these hills with a donkey in 1878. Look for the high limestone causses split by deep gorges, and the bare granite dome of Mont Lozère.

name: Dadès Gorges
blurb: A gorge through the High Atlas with red cliffs and rounded rocks called monkey fingers, plus one of Morocco's most photographed hairpin roads. Look for the green ribbon of palms along the river.

name: Danmark Fjord
blurb: A long, remote fjord in far northeast Greenland, named after the 1906 to 1908 Danmark Expedition, whose leader and two companions died before they could get home. Look for a narrow channel of ice through barren land.

name: Danube Bend
blurb: Where the Danube, after flowing east, turns sharply south between volcanic hills on its way to Budapest. Look for the river's elbow at Visegrád, with the hilltop castle above.

name: Dar es Salaam
blurb: Tanzania's biggest city and main port, on a natural harbor on the Indian Ocean. Look for the narrow harbor entrance, offshore coral islands, and the cable-stayed Tanzanite Bridge across Msasani Bay.

name: Dargomyzhsky glacier
blurb: Like many features on Alexander Island, Antarctica's largest island, it is named for a composer, here the Russian Alexander Dargomyzhsky. Look for ice flowing between dark ridges toward George VI Sound or the open sea.

name: Dauphin Lake
blurb: A shallow lake on the farmland of western Manitoba, below the Riding Mountain escarpment. Look for a round lake surrounded by a patchwork of fields, with the forested escarpment rising to the south.

name: Davidson Glacier
blurb: Flows down from the Chilkat Range toward Lynn Canal south of Haines, ending behind a forested moraine and a small meltwater lake. Look for the white tongue on the west shore of the canal.

name: Deception Glacier
blurb: Flows through the Transantarctic Mountains of Victoria Land, where ice from the polar plateau squeezes between ranges on its way toward the Ross Sea. Look for crevassed ice between rock walls.

name: Delhi
blurb: India's capital, a vast sprawl of over 30 million in the metro, on the Yamuna River. Look for the wide boulevards of Lutyens' New Delhi radiating from India Gate, and the river's floodplain on the east side.

name: Denver
blurb: The Mile High City sits exactly 5,280 ft up at the edge of the plains. Look for the downtown cluster on the South Platte River with the wall of the Front Range rising behind it.

name: Deosai National Park
blurb: One of the highest plateaus in the world, averaging about 13,500 ft, home to Himalayan brown bears. Look for broad rolling green-brown plains among the mountains of Gilgit-Baltistan, snowbound much of the year.

name: Deschambault Lake
blurb: A lake in the boreal forest of east-central Saskatchewan, on the rocky edge of the Canadian Shield. Look for a convoluted shoreline and scattered islands among dark spruce.

name: Desembarco del Granma National Park
blurb: Fidel Castro's yacht Granma ran aground here in 1956 to start the revolution. The coast is a staircase of uplifted marine terraces; look for limestone steps climbing from the sea.

name: Deseret Peak
blurb: At 11,031 ft, the highest point of the Stansbury Mountains, rising west of the Salt Lake Valley above the Great Salt Lake's south shore. Look for a rocky summit with glacial bowls above Tooele Valley.

name: Devon Ice Cap
blurb: One of the largest ice caps in the Canadian Arctic, covering the east of Devon Island, the largest uninhabited island on Earth. Look for a smooth white dome with glaciers spilling into the sea.

name: Dhaka
blurb: One of the most densely populated cities on Earth, surrounded by rivers and low wetlands. Look for the packed gray sprawl, the Buriganga River on the south side, and water everywhere in the monsoon.

name: Diamond Peak
blurb: At about 12,200 ft, the highest point of Idaho's Lemhi Range. Look for a sharp gray summit on a long, bare ridge rising out of the sagebrush valleys of eastern Idaho.

name: Dibble Glacier
blurb: An outlet glacier on the Wilkes Land coast that pushes a long floating ice tongue out to sea. Look for the tongue jutting into the sea ice.

name: Dickey Glacier
blurb: One of many glaciers cutting through the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that holds back the polar plateau above the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for crevassed ice between dark rock walls.

name: Dicksonfjorden
blurb: A remote Svalbard fjord branching north off the great Isfjorden system, ringed by barren layered mountains. Look for a narrow inlet with braided glacial rivers spreading across its head.

name: Dirfi
blurb: The highest point of Euboea, Greece's second-largest island, at about 5,720 ft. Look for a forested ridge rising over the island's midsection, with the narrow Euripus strait to the west.

name: Djebel Chélia
blurb: At about 7,600 ft the highest peak in northern Algeria, in the Aurès Mountains, with cedar forest on its slopes. Look for a broad dark massif above dry plateaus.

name: Dnieper Reservoir
blurb: The Dnipro behind the DniproHES dam at Zaporizhzhia, first built in 1932. Look for the dam just upstream of Khortytsia, the large island once home to the Zaporizhian Cossacks.

name: Dnieper-Bug Estuary
blurb: The shared mouth of the Dnipro and Southern Bug rivers, with Mykolaiv up the Bug arm. Look for the long, curved Kinburn Spit nearly closing the estuary off from the Black Sea.

name: Dniester Canyon
blurb: The Dniester River winds through deep, looping meanders cut into the Podolian Upland, one of the longest canyons in Europe. Look for tight horseshoe bends lined with steep wooded banks.

name: Dniester Lyman
blurb: The Dniester River's estuary, closed off from the Black Sea by a narrow sandbar. Look for the medieval fortress at Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi on the western shore.

name: Doi Inthanon
blurb: Thailand's highest peak at 8,415 ft, with twin royal pagodas built on a ridge near the summit. Look for the two pagodas and a radar dome on the forested ridge southwest of Chiang Mai.

name: Dongguan
blurb: One of the world's great factory towns: about 10 million people in a sprawl between Guangzhou and Shenzhen. It barely has a center. Look for endless low industrial blocks with the Pearl River estuary to the west.

name: Dorrer Glacier
blurb: Drains ice from the polar plateau down through the Transantarctic Mountains, some of the emptiest country on Earth. Look for flow lines and crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Dorsoidong Co
blurb: A remote saline lake on the high Changtang plateau of northern Tibet, above 15,000 ft and far from any road. Look for blue water among tan, rolling, uninhabited uplands.

name: Doré Lake
blurb: A lake in the boreal forest of northwest-central Saskatchewan. Look for a large irregular body of water ringed by dark forest, one of many lakes scattered across this flat country.

name: Dotson Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating shelf on the Amundsen Sea coast, the part of West Antarctica that is losing ice fastest as warm ocean water melts it from below. Look for flat white ice ending in a sheer edge against dark sea or pack ice.

name: Douglas Glacier
blurb: One of the glaciers feeding the Antarctic Peninsula's ice shelves, a river of ice moving a few feet a day between dark rock ridges. Look for crevasse lines running down its length.

name: Dovrefjell–Sunndalsfjella National Park
blurb: Home to Norway's wild musk oxen and to Snøhetta, which tops out at about 7,500 ft. Look for broad barren highlands with the snowy massif rising above them, crossed by the Oslo-Trondheim railway and highway.

name: Drygalski Fjord
blurb: A narrow fjord at the southern tip of South Georgia, walled by dark peaks with a glacier calving at its head. Look for a slot of water cutting into an icy, mountainous island.

name: Du Toits Peak
blurb: About 6,500 ft, one of the highest summits in the Cape Fold Mountains near Paarl, above the Du Toitskloof Pass and tunnel. Look for gray sandstone crags above the vineyards of the Cape Winelands.

name: Dufek Massif
blurb: A rocky range in the Pensacola Mountains poking through the ice near the Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf, made of layered igneous rock. Look for dark cliffs and ridges standing out of an otherwise white plain.

name: Dunn Peak massif
blurb: A rugged massif in the Shuswap Highlands north of Kamloops, above the North Thompson River valley. Look for bare rocky summits rising from forested ridges.

name: Dzūkija National Park
blurb: Lithuania's largest national park, pine forest on sandy soil along the Merkys River, famous for mushroom picking. Look for unbroken forest and sand dunes inland.

name: Dålk Glacier
blurb: A coastal glacier near Prydz Bay in East Antarctica, close to the Larsemann Hills and its cluster of research stations. Look for crevassed ice spilling into the sea between bare brown hills.

name: Eastmain Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Eastmain River, one of the newer pieces of Québec's James Bay hydro development. Look for a flooded, irregular lake spreading across flat taiga.

name: Edmonton
blurb: The northernmost North American city of over a million, split by the North Saskatchewan River's deep green valley, the largest urban parkland in North America. Look for the winding wooded ribbon through the grid.

name: Edward VIII Ice Shelf
blurb: A small ice shelf filling a bay on the Kemp Coast of East Antarctica, named for the king who abdicated in 1936. Look for flat floating ice tucked between rocky headlands.

name: Eiskar Glacier
blurb: The only glacier in the Carnic Alps, a small ice field tucked in a north-facing cirque below Monte Coglians on the Austria-Italy border. Look for a white pocket under a gray limestone wall.

name: Ekström Ice Shelf
blurb: Germany's Neumayer III research station sits on this floating shelf, built on hydraulic legs so it can be jacked up as snow piles around it. Look for the dead-flat ice ending in a straight cliff at the sea.

name: Elbe Sandstone Mountains
blurb: Not peaks so much as a maze of sandstone towers and gorges along the Elbe, known as Saxon Switzerland. Look for pale rock pillars poking out of dark forest beside the river's tight bends.

name: Elivai Malai
blurb: A high point of the Western Ghats in Kerala, near the Palakkad Gap, the only major break in the range. Look for forested ridges and the low gap where roads and rail cross.

name: Ellis Glacier
blurb: One of the glaciers flowing off the high plateau of Dronning Maud Land toward the coast. Look for streaks and crevasses where moving ice drags past nunataks, rocky peaks just breaking the surface.

name: Embalse Cerros Colorados
blurb: Part of a complex of dams and lakes on the Neuquén River north of Neuquén city, in Patagonian desert. Look for blue water against red and tan badlands.

name: Embree Glacier
blurb: A glacier draining the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains, home to Vinson Massif, Antarctica's highest peak at about 16,050 ft. Look for ice threading between steep dark summits.

name: Endurance Glacier
blurb: On Elephant Island, where 22 of Shackleton's men camped for four and a half months in 1916 waiting for rescue. Named for his lost ship. Look for ice pouring off the island's steep cliffs into the sea.

name: Ennadai Lake
blurb: A lake on the Kazan River in southern Nunavut, near the tree line. Look for a long lake in open tundra with scattered patches of spruce to the south.

name: Entuziasty Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land named by Soviet expeditions (the name means 'enthusiasts'). Look for flowing ice cutting between the dark peaks that line this coast.

name: Erskine Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's Graham Land coast, feeding into a fjord-like inlet. Look for crevassed ice tumbling from the plateau between dark mountain walls to open water or sea ice.

name: Eufaula Lake
blurb: The largest lake entirely within Oklahoma, a sprawling reservoir on the Canadian River. Look for its long, many-fingered arms reaching into wooded hills, with hundreds of miles of winding shoreline.

name: Exasperation Inlet
blurb: A glacier-fed inlet on the east coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, in the region of the Larsen ice shelves that have broken up since the 1990s. Look for glaciers spilling into ice-choked water.

name: Exodus Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains, the range that splits East and West Antarctica. Look for a ribbon of ice flowing between rocky peaks.

name: Exum Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Ellsworth Land, West Antarctica, one of many flowing toward the Bellingshausen Sea coast. From above, expect white ice with faint flow lines and the occasional dark nunatak.

name: Faber Lake
blurb: A lake in the boreal forest northwest of Yellowknife, in Tlicho country. Look for an island-dotted lake among the dark spruce and countless smaller lakes of the Canadian Shield.

name: Falak Sar
blurb: The highest peak in Swat at about 19,400 ft, at the head of the upper Swat valley. Look for a white pyramid over green valleys.

name: Falcon International Reservoir
blurb: A Rio Grande reservoir on the US-Mexico border, made by a dam completed in 1954. In droughts the ruins of the flooded town of Guerrero Viejo reappear. Look for a long lake in dry brush country.

name: Fansipan
blurb: At 10,312 ft, the Roof of Indochina, the highest peak in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. Since 2016 a cable car has carried visitors to the top from near Sa Pa. Look for the summit temples above terraced rice valleys.

name: Fedafjorden
blurb: A small fjord on Norway's southern coast near Kvinesdal. Look for a narrow inlet winding into wooded hills, opening onto the North Sea.

name: Fendley Glacier
blurb: A glacier in northern Victoria Land, among the jagged ranges facing the Ross Sea. Look for ice spilling between sharp dark peaks toward the coast.

name: Fengari
blurb: At about 5,280 ft on tiny Samothrace, one of the highest island peaks in the Aegean. In the Iliad, Poseidon sat up here to watch the Trojan War. Look for a granite mountain filling almost the whole island.

name: Fernan Vaz Lagoon
blurb: A large coastal lagoon in Gabon at the mouth of the Ogooué delta, near Loango National Park. Look for dark water fringed by mangroves and rainforest.

name: Finger Lakes
blurb: Eleven long, thin lakes clawed out by glaciers. Cayuga is about 38 miles long and Seneca is over 600 ft deep. Look for the parallel blue strips running north-south, ringed by vineyards.

name: Fisher Glacier
blurb: A large glacier flowing into the Lambert Glacier system, which drains about 8% of the Antarctic ice sheet into the Amery Ice Shelf. Look for long flow stripes converging downstream.

name: Flogeken Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land, one of many Norwegian-named ice streams flowing between the ranges toward the coast. Look for crevasse fields where ice squeezes past rock.

name: Folda
blurb: A wide stretch of open water off Norway's coast, long dreaded by sailors because it lies exposed to North Atlantic swells. Look for a broad gap in the island shelter between low rocky skerries.

name: Folda
blurb: A fjord in Nordland north of Bodø, branching inland among steep mountains. Look for long arms of dark water reaching past the coastline toward snow-capped peaks.

name: Foldfjorden
blurb: A fjord on the Nordmøre coast of western Norway. Look for a sheltered arm of water with green, steep-sided shores between the island-studded coast and the mountains.

name: Foundation Ice Stream
blurb: A major ice stream carrying ice from the interior into the Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf, the second largest ice shelf on Earth. Look for faint stripes on the surface tracing its flow.

name: Foz de Lumbier
blurb: A short, sheer limestone gorge on the Irati River in Navarre, home to a colony of griffon vultures. An old railway line once ran through it in tunnels. Look for the narrow notch in the ridge.

name: Franca Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's east side. Look for ice draining off the Peninsula's spine toward the Weddell Sea.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt Lake
blurb: Backed up about 150 miles behind Grand Coulee Dam, the biggest power producer in the US, reaching almost to the Canadian border. Look for the massive concrete dam at the lake's southwest end.

name: Fraser Canyon
blurb: The Fraser River squeezes through it on its way to Vancouver, narrowing to about 115 ft at Hell's Gate. Two transcontinental railways run along opposite walls; look for the tracks clinging to the cliffs.

name: Frierfjord
blurb: A fjord at Porsgrunn lined by the Herøya industrial park, one of Norway's oldest heavy-industry sites. Look for the narrow channel, the factory complex on its peninsula, and the bridges crossing the fjord.

name: Fulufjället National Park
blurb: Home to Njupeskär, Sweden's tallest waterfall, and to Old Tjikko, a spruce whose root system has been dated to about 9,500 years old. Look for the bare, flat-topped mountain plateau along the Norwegian border.

name: Gangshiqia Peak
blurb: A glaciated summit of the Qilian Shan, the range on the northeastern rim of the Tibetan Plateau, above 17,000 ft. Look for snow and ice on the crest above the desert corridor of Gansu.

name: Gardner Inlet
blurb: A long inlet on the Lassiter Coast at the base of the Antarctic Peninsula, filled by the Ronne Ice Shelf's edge. Look for glaciers flowing out of the mountains into flat shelf ice.

name: Garry Lake
blurb: A large lake on the Back River in the Nunavut barren lands. Look for a sprawling, island-filled lake in treeless tundra, frozen most of the year.

name: Gauja National Park
blurb: Red sandstone cliffs line the Gauja River valley around Sigulda and its medieval castles. Look for the forested valley winding northeast of Riga.

name: Geladaindong Peak
blurb: A 21,722-ft ice peak in the Tanggula Mountains whose glaciers feed the source of the Yangtze, Asia's longest river. Look for a cluster of white glaciers above braided meltwater streams on the high plateau.

name: Gilchrist Glacier
blurb: A coastal glacier on the Budd Coast of Wilkes Land, East Antarctica, near Australia's Casey Station. Look for ice meeting the sea in a jagged front.

name: Gillett Ice Shelf
blurb: A small ice shelf on the Oates Coast of East Antarctica, south of New Zealand. Look for flat floating ice edged by cliffs and sea ice.

name: Glacier Peak
blurb: Washington's most remote volcano, about 10,500 ft, hidden deep in wilderness and barely visible from any city. Look for a glaciated summit among the jagged North Cascades, east of Everett.

name: Glenveagh National Park
blurb: A castle on Lough Veagh in the Donegal hills, where golden eagles were reintroduced in 2000. Look for the long narrow lake in a glacial valley.

name: Gluvreklett Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land, one of the many Norwegian-named ice streams of this coast. Look for ice flowing past isolated rocky peaks.

name: Goldsmith Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Coats Land, flowing toward the Filchner Ice Shelf at the head of the Weddell Sea. Expect broad white ice with faint flow stripes and the odd rocky outcrop.

name: Gombe National Park
blurb: Where Jane Goodall began studying chimpanzees in 1960, the longest-running wild chimp study anywhere. Look for the narrow strip of forested valleys running down to the shore of Lake Tanganyika.

name: Good Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, part of the Transantarctic chain at the edge of the Ross Ice Shelf, only a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for ice between bare peaks.

name: Goodenough Glacier
blurb: A large glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's Black Coast, flowing into the George VI Sound area. Look for broad crevassed ice heading toward the sea.

name: Goose Lake
blurb: A shallow, sometimes dry lake straddling the California-Oregon border. Look for a long pale lake in high desert with the Warner Mountains on its east side.

name: Gora Babash-Ata
blurb: A high point of the Babash-Ata range in southern Kyrgyzstan, above walnut forests and the Fergana Valley. Look for bare ridges rising above green foothills.

name: Gora Bakchigir
blurb: A summit in the Shugnan region of the southwestern Pamirs, among some of the steepest valleys in Central Asia. Look for snow above deep gorges running down to the Afghan border.

name: Gora Bozbu-Too
blurb: A summit on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley in western Kyrgyzstan. Look for brown, folded ridges above the irrigated green valley floor.

name: Gordon Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Shackleton Range near the Filchner Ice Shelf. Look for ice flowing between ridges of dark exposed rock.

name: Gorges du Gardon
blurb: A limestone gorge through dry garrigue scrubland that ends near the Pont du Gard, the 2,000-year-old Roman aqueduct bridge. Look for the green river winding between pale cliffs.

name: Gorongosa National Park
blurb: Lost most of its large animals in Mozambique's civil war and has become one of Africa's best-known restoration projects since 2004. Look for the floodplain around Lake Urema, with Mount Gorongosa rising to the west.

name: Gough Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, draining toward the Ross Ice Shelf a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for ice ribbons between bare summits.

name: Gran Campo Nevado
blurb: An ice cap on Chile's Muñoz Gamero Peninsula in the far south, among the wettest places in Patagonia. Look for a white dome with glaciers spilling toward fjords.

name: Granville Lake
blurb: A widening of the Churchill River in northern Manitoba. Look for a long, island-studded lake following the river through rocky boreal forest on the Canadian Shield.

name: Greater Chimgan
blurb: At about 10,900 ft, the main peak of the Chimgan massif, the mountain getaway an hour or so northeast of Tashkent. Look for a bare summit above the turquoise Charvak Reservoir.

name: Gressitt Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land's coastal ranges facing the Ross Sea. Look for ice pouring between sharp, dark peaks.

name: Griffiths Glacier
blurb: A glacier near the McMurdo Dry Valleys, some of the driest places on Earth, where almost no snow falls. Look for the contrast between ice tongues and brown, ice-free valley floors.

name: Grintovec
blurb: At 8,392 ft, the highest peak of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps, the bare limestone wall visible from Ljubljana. Look for pale gray summits above dark forest north of the city.

name: Guartelá Canyon
blurb: One of the largest canyons in Brazil, carved by the Iapó River through sandstone in the Paraná highlands. Look for a winding dark gash through green farmland and grassland.

name: Guiana Amazonian Park
blurb: The largest national park in France and the whole EU, unbroken Amazon rainforest along the borders with Suriname and Brazil. Look for canopy from horizon to horizon.

name: Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida Heritage Site
blurb: A Haida protected area on Haida Gwaii, including the old village of SGang Gwaay with standing totem poles. Look for rugged islands and fjords.

name: Göygöl National Park
blurb: Its lake, Göygöl, formed when the 1139 Ganja earthquake brought down part of Mount Kapaz and dammed a river. Look for a small blue lake below forested mountains.

name: Ha Gorge
blurb: A narrow slot canyon in eastern Crete, cutting deep into the Thripti mountains above the north coast. Look for the dark notch in the bare limestone face near the Gulf of Mirabello.

name: Haas Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains near the head of the Ross Ice Shelf, deep in the Transantarctic range. Look for ice threading between rocky peaks.

name: Hagen Fjord
blurb: A remote fjord in Peary Land, northern Greenland, named after Niels Peter Høeg Hagen, who died on the Danmark Expedition in 1907. Look for ice-covered water between bare brown mountains.

name: Hall Lake
blurb: A remote lake on the Melville Peninsula in the Nunavut Arctic. Look for a lake in bare, rocky tundra, frozen for most of the year.

name: Hamoun-e Puzak
blurb: The Afghan arm of the Hamun wetlands, fed by rivers from the Afghan highlands. Once rich reed marsh, it has dried almost completely in droughts. Look for green reed beds or a pale dry basin, depending on the year.

name: Hamra National Park
blurb: A small patch of untouched old-growth forest in central Sweden, kept as a sample of what the region's woods looked like before logging. From the air it blends into the surrounding conifer and bog.

name: Hanoi
blurb: Vietnam's capital is a city of lakes on the inside of a broad bend of the Red River. Look for West Lake, the biggest, a nearly 2-square-mile sheet of water just north of the old center.

name: Har Hu
blurb: A remote brackish lake above 13,000 ft in the Qilian Mountains, on the northern edge of the Tibetan Plateau. Look for a blue oval in a high, treeless basin, often framed by snowy ridges.

name: Harbin
blurb: Russian-built railway city famous for its Ice and Snow Festival, with ice palaces cut from the frozen Songhua River, where winter nights often drop below 0 F. Look for the wide river with Sun Island across from downtown.

name: Harbord Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Scott Coast of Victoria Land, flowing toward the Ross Sea. Look for ice running from the mountains down to a floating tongue.

name: Hardisty Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the boreal forest north of Great Slave Lake, near the community of Gamètì. Look for a ragged lake among the countless lakes and rock of the Canadian Shield.

name: Hargreaves Glacier
blurb: A glacier near Prydz Bay on the Ingrid Christensen Coast, East Antarctica. Look for crevassed ice meeting the sea or fast ice.

name: Harhiraa
blurb: A glaciated summit in Mongolia's far west, near the town of Ulaangom and the huge lake Uvs Nuur. Look for snow above brown, treeless ridges.

name: Hasagt Hairhan
blurb: One of the high, snowy massifs of the Mongolian Altai, rising over dry steppe and salt lakes. Look for a white crest standing over a sea of brown.

name: Haydn Inlet
blurb: An inlet on Alexander Island, Antarctica, one of many features there named for composers. Look for a white bay of shelf ice framed by ice-covered mountains.

name: Hayford Peak
blurb: At about 9,900 ft, the highest peak in the Sheep Range north of Las Vegas, inside the Desert National Wildlife Refuge. Look for a rocky crest above bare desert valleys.

name: Hei Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land flowing between the region's rocky ranges. Look for crevasse fields where the ice speeds up between peaks.

name: Heitō Glacier
blurb: A glacier named by Japanese expeditions on the Prince Olav Coast, near Lützow-Holm Bay. Look for ice meeting fast ice and open sea.

name: Hemis National Park
blurb: India's largest national park, high desert ranges known for one of the densest snow leopard populations anywhere. Look for brown, barren peaks south of the Indus near Leh.

name: Hette Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land's Sør Rondane area. Look for ice flowing past dark granite peaks.

name: Hewitt Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Alexandra Range of the Transantarctic Mountains, near the Beardmore Glacier route Shackleton and Scott used toward the Pole. Look for ice between high rock walls.

name: Hiawatha Glacier
blurb: In 2018 scientists found a 19-mile-wide impact crater buried beneath it, among the 25 largest known on Earth. Look for the rounded edge of the ice sheet bulging toward the coast.

name: Higashi-naga-iwa Glacier
blurb: A glacier named by Japanese expeditions on the Prince Olav Coast. The name means 'east long rock'. Look for ice flowing past an elongated rock outcrop toward the sea.

name: Hill Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Palmer Land on the southern Antarctic Peninsula. Look for ice draining off the plateau with faint flow lines and crevasses.

name: Hirkan National Park
blurb: Relict Hyrcanian forest in the Talysh Mountains on the Iranian border, a woodland that survived the Ice Ages. Look for dense green ridges above the Caspian coast.

name: Hjeltefjorden
blurb: The main channel northwest of Bergen, between the mainland and the Øygarden islands. Look for a long straight sound full of ship traffic, with low, rocky, island-fringed shores.

name: Hjälmaren
blurb: Sweden's fourth-largest lake, west of Stockholm, with the city of Örebro near its western end. Look for a long, shallow lake in farmland, just south of the much bigger Mälaren.

name: Hkusam Mountain
blurb: A steep peak rising almost straight from Johnstone Strait near Sayward on northern Vancouver Island. Look for a rocky summit above the channel where ferries and cruise ships run the Inside Passage.

name: Hlubeck Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Ellsworth Land, West Antarctica, draining toward the Bellingshausen Sea. Expect white ice with faint flow stripes.

name: Hmuifang
blurb: A ridge of about 5,300 ft south of Aizawl, known for grassy hilltops above forest in Mizoram's parallel north-south ranges. Look for long ridges lined up like corrugations.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
blurb: Vietnam's largest city, around 9 million people, wrapped around tight loops of the Saigon River. Look for Landmark 81 at about 1,500 ft, the country's tallest building, and the airport sitting right inside the city.

name: Hochtor
blurb: About 7,800 ft, the top of the Gesäuse, a cluster of limestone walls above the Enns River gorge in Styria. Look for steep gray cliffs rising straight out of a narrow green valley.

name: Hollingsworth Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land flowing toward the Ross Sea coast. Look for ice spilling between dark coastal peaks.

name: Hong Lake
blurb: Hubei's largest lake, a shallow lake on the Yangtze floodplain. Look for open water bordered by a patchwork of fish ponds.

name: Hornsund
blurb: Svalbard's southernmost major fjord, ringed by tidewater glaciers and home to a Polish research station. Look for a wide inlet with ice cliffs at the end of each glacier and jagged black peaks between them.

name: Horsens Fjord
blurb: A shallow fjord on Jutland's east coast, leading to the town of Horsens. Look for a long inlet dotted with small, low islands such as Endelave and Hjarnø near its mouth.

name: Hoseason Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Kemp Coast of East Antarctica. Look for crevassed ice reaching the sea between rocky headlands.

name: Hot Springs National Park
blurb: The oldest federally protected area in the US, set aside in 1832 for its thermal springs. Look for Bathhouse Row and downtown in a narrow valley among forested ridges.

name: Hottah Lake
blurb: A large, ragged lake south of Great Bear Lake in the Northwest Territories. Look for a lake full of islands and long bays in thin boreal forest on the Canadian Shield.

name: Howson Peak
blurb: A glaciated summit in the Coast Mountains south of Smithers and Terrace in northern BC. Look for ice and rock among rows of snowy ridges.

name: Hrútafjörður
blurb: A long, narrow fjord in northwest Iceland, traditionally the dividing line between the island's west and north. Look for Route 1 running along the shore of the slim inlet.

name: Huangmaojian Peak
blurb: At about 6,300 ft the highest point in Zhejiang province, in the Fengyang mountains near the Fujian border. Look for a forested ridge rising above terraced valleys.

name: Huantsán
blurb: An ice peak of about 20,900 ft, the highest in the southern Cordillera Blanca, the most heavily glaciated tropical range on Earth. Look for steep fluted snow faces above the long Santa River valley.

name: Huaytunas Lake
blurb: One of the many shallow lakes in the Llanos de Moxos, the seasonally flooded savanna of Bolivia's Beni lowlands. Look for a squarish lake surrounded by grassland.

name: Hudson Bay coast
blurb: Churchill sits here, the polar bear capital of the world: bears gather each fall waiting for the bay to freeze so they can hunt seals. Look for flat tundra dotted with countless ponds meeting gray sea ice or open water.

name: Hull Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Marie Byrd Land coast of West Antarctica, facing the Ross and Amundsen seas. Look for ice flowing to a floating tongue.

name: Humboldt Glacier
blurb: Its front is about 68 miles wide, the widest tidewater glacier in the Northern Hemisphere. Look for a long, straight ice cliff along the sea.

name: Hwange National Park
blurb: Zimbabwe's largest national park and home to one of Africa's biggest elephant populations, drawn to pumped waterholes in the dry season. Look for flat bush and Kalahari sand along the Botswana border.

name: Hyefjorden
blurb: A small fjord arm in Sogn og Fjordane, between the outer coast and the glaciers inland. Look for a narrow inlet with steep, forested sides and a village at its head.

name: Hålisen Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land, among the Norwegian-named ice streams of the region. Look for ice moving past nunataks, rocky summits poking through.

name: Ibapah Peak
blurb: At 12,087 ft, the high point of the Deep Creek Range near the Nevada line, rising nearly 8,000 ft above the Great Salt Lake Desert. Look for a lone snowy range standing out of white salt flats.

name: Iddefjorden
blurb: A long, narrow fjord that forms part of the border between Norway and Sweden. Look for a slim ribbon of water through forest, crossed at its inner end near Halden.

name: Ikh Bogd
blurb: Highest summit of the Gobi-Altai's Ikh Bogd massif. The 1957 Gobi-Altai earthquake, one of the largest ever on land, ripped a fault scarp along its foot. Look for a sharp line where mountain meets plain.

name: Ilmen
blurb: A big, shallow lake at the cradle of Russia: Veliky Novgorod sits where the Volkhov River drains it to the north. Look for a broad lake in flat, marshy country, with the city at its outlet.

name: Ilısu Reservoir
blurb: When Ilısu Dam on the Tigris filled in 2020, it drowned the ancient town of Hasankeyf, inhabited for thousands of years. Look for a long, winding lake in dry hills.

name: Imandra
blurb: The largest lake on the Kola Peninsula, beside the Khibiny Mountains and the mining towns of Apatity and Monchegorsk. Look for a long, branching lake with the bare Khibiny massif rising on the east side.

name: Independence Fjord
blurb: One of the northernmost fjords on Earth, more than 100 miles long, in Peary Land. Peary thought it was a channel separating Greenland from land to the north; look for a long frozen corridor through barren country.

name: Isalo National Park
blurb: A sandstone massif carved into canyons, ridges and pinnacles in southern Madagascar. Look for the jagged ridges and gorges rising from bare grassland.

name: Isefjord
blurb: A large, branching fjord in northern Zealand, Denmark, whose side branch, Roskilde Fjord, reaches the old cathedral town of Roskilde. Look for its many lobes and inlets in flat green farmland.

name: Isle Royale National Park
blurb: A roadless island in Lake Superior, about 45 miles long, where wolves and moose have been studied since 1958, the longest-running predator-prey study in the world. Look for a long, narrow island of parallel ridges pointing northeast.

name: Isle of Wight / Needles
blurb: A diamond-shaped island of about 150 square miles off England's south coast. At its western tip, look for the Needles: three white chalk stacks running out to sea with a lighthouse on the last one.

name: Ivankovo Reservoir
blurb: The first reservoir on the Volga, filled in 1937 and nicknamed the Moscow Sea. It feeds the canal that supplies much of Moscow's water. Look for a broad, flooded river valley in forest.

name: Ivindo National Park
blurb: Gabon rainforest straddling the equator, where the Ivindo River crashes over the Kongou and Mingouli falls. Look for white water breaking the dark river in an unbroken canopy.

name: Ivvavik National Park
blurb: The first Canadian national park created through an Indigenous land claim agreement, in 1984, protecting calving grounds of the Porcupine caribou herd. Look for bare mountains running down to the Beaufort Sea coast.

name: Jabal Al Harim
blurb: The highest point of Oman's Musandam Peninsula at about 6,850 ft, above fjord-like inlets on the Strait of Hormuz. Look for bare rock ridges diving into blue water.

name: Jabal al-Lawz
blurb: At about 8,400 ft, one of the highest peaks in northwestern Saudi Arabia, and one of the few places in the kingdom that sometimes gets snow. Some claim it is the biblical Mount Sinai. Look for a bare granite massif near the Gulf of Aqaba.

name: Jacksonville
blurb: The largest city by area in the contiguous US, about 875 square miles. Look for the wide St. Johns River curving through downtown with several bridges, and the Atlantic beaches to the east.

name: Jacobel Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land, West Antarctica. Expect broad white ice with faint flow lines toward the Ross Ice Shelf.

name: Jakupica
blurb: A limestone massif south of Skopje topping out near 8,300 ft. Look for a bare, high plateau above forested foothills.

name: Janq'u Uma
blurb: About 21,000 ft, one of the highest peaks of Bolivia's Cordillera Real, above the town of Sorata near Lake Titicaca. Look for a snowy massif along the east shore of the lake.

name: Jelbart Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating ice shelf on the Princess Martha Coast of Dronning Maud Land, near the Fimbul Ice Shelf. Look for flat white ice ending in a straight cliff at the sea.

name: Jirisan
blurb: The highest peak on the South Korean mainland at 6,283 ft, centerpiece of the country's first national park, created in 1967. Look for a long forested ridge running east to west for miles.

name: Jones Glacier
blurb: A glacier in East Antarctica near the Shackleton Ice Shelf. Expect white ice with flow lines heading to the coast.

name: Jupiter Glacier
blurb: One of several planet-named glaciers on Alexander Island, off the Antarctic Peninsula, flowing into George VI Sound. Look for ice meeting the long, narrow channel of the Sound.

name: Jutulstraumen Glacier
blurb: One of the largest ice streams in Dronning Maud Land, feeding the Fimbul Ice Shelf. The name is Norwegian for 'giant's stream'. Look for a broad crevassed river of ice cutting between mountains.

name: Jökulsárgljúfur
blurb: A canyon carved by glacial floods along the Jökulsá á Fjöllum, home to Dettifoss, one of the most powerful waterfalls in Europe. Look for Ásbyrgi, a horseshoe canyon said in legend to be Odin's horse's hoofprint.

name: Kajmakčalan
blurb: About 8,280 ft on the Greece-North Macedonia border, scene of a fierce World War I battle in 1916. A small chapel on the summit holds Serbian soldiers' remains. Look for a bare, rounded crest above Lake Vegoritida.

name: Kakisa Lake
blurb: A lake in the southern Northwest Territories near the Mackenzie Highway, with the small Dene community of Kakisa on its shore. Look for a broad lake in flat boreal forest.

name: Kakum National Park
blurb: Famous for a canopy walkway strung between giant trees more than 100 ft above the forest floor, just north of Ghana's coastal forts. Look for unbroken rainforest amid farmland.

name: Kallavesi
blurb: A lake full of islands in Finland's lake district, with the city of Kuopio on its shore. Look for a maze of water and forest, with Puijo hill above the city.

name: Kamianske Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Dnipro above the city of Kamianske in central Ukraine. Look for a broad stretch of river backed up into a lake through flat, intensely farmed country.

name: Kamilukuak Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the barren lands of southern Nunavut. Look for an irregular lake in open tundra crowded with smaller ponds, frozen most of the year.

name: Kaminak Lake
blurb: A lake in the barren lands of Nunavut's Kivalliq region, inland from Hudson Bay. Look for a ragged lake in treeless tundra, frozen most of the year.

name: Kangerdlugssuaq Fjord
blurb: A large fjord on Greenland's remote east coast, one of the biggest on that side, fed by the Kangerdlugssuaq Glacier. Look for a wide fjord clogged with icebergs from one of Greenland's fastest glaciers.

name: Kangerlussuaq Fjord
blurb: A fjord about 120 miles long in West Greenland, leading to Kangerlussuaq airport near the ice sheet edge. Look for a long, narrow channel through bare brown hills with the white ice sheet beyond.

name: Kangiqtualuk Uqquqti
blurb: Also called Sam Ford Fjord, on Baffin Island, lined with granite walls and spires thousands of feet high that draw big-wall climbers. Look for towering rock faces dropping straight into the ice-covered fjord.

name: Kanha National Park
blurb: Sal and bamboo forest that saved the hard-ground barasingha deer from extinction. Look for open meadows scattered inside large green forests.

name: Kaniv Reservoir
blurb: A Dnipro reservoir south of Kyiv, held back by a dam at Kaniv, where the poet Taras Shevchenko is buried on a hill above the river. Look for a wide river-lake with wooded bluffs.

name: Kanjiroba Himal
blurb: A remote range of about 22,600 ft in western Nepal, near Shey Phoksundo National Park. Look for snowy peaks above dry valleys.

name: Karachi
blurb: Pakistan's largest city and main port, home to roughly 20 million people on the Arabian Sea. Look for the harbor and Manora's long breakwater, the Clifton beachfront, and sprawl running off into dry brown country.

name: Karpinsky Glacier
blurb: Part of the Rimo glacier system in the eastern Karakoram near the Siachen conflict zone. Its meltwater feeds the Shyok River. Look for long, debris-striped ice between brown, barren ridges.

name: Kaskawulsh Glacier
blurb: In 2016 this glacier retreated so far that its meltwater switched rivers, draining the Slims River within days, the first documented case of modern "river piracy." Look for a long ice tongue with dark moraine stripes.

name: Kayrakkum Reservoir
blurb: Nicknamed the Tajik Sea, a reservoir on the Syr Darya at the western end of the Fergana Valley. Look for a big blue lake in dry brown country, ringed by green irrigated fields.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
blurb: The world's only floating national park: mats of vegetation called phumdis drifting on Loktak Lake, last home of the rare sangai deer. Look for the lake dotted with brown-green floating mats and fishing rings.

name: Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord
blurb: A long fjord system in East Greenland with walls rising thousands of feet, banded in red, yellow and gray sedimentary rock. Look for the striped cliffs and icebergs drifting below.

name: Keller Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the forested interior of the Northwest Territories, west of Great Bear Lake country. Look for a lake in dark spruce and muskeg, frozen white for much of the year.

name: Kennedy Peak
blurb: A peak of about 8,900 ft in the Chin Hills, fought over by British and Japanese forces in 1943 and 1944. Look for grassy ridges above deep valleys.

name: Kenting National Park
blurb: Taiwan's southernmost tip, where coral reefs, raised coral terraces and beaches meet the Bashi Channel. Look for the peninsula narrowing to the white Eluanbi lighthouse.

name: Khantayskoye Lake
blurb: A long lake on the Putorana Plateau, raised by the Khantayka hydro dam that powers Norilsk. Look for a deep, narrow lake between flat-topped, cliff-sided mountains in roadless Arctic wilderness.

name: Khao Luang
blurb: At about 6,000 ft, the highest peak of southern Thailand, rising over Nakhon Si Thammarat. Look for a big forested massif cloaked in cloud above rubber plantations.

name: Khar Lake
blurb: A freshwater lake in western Mongolia's Great Lakes Depression, joined by a channel to Khar-Us Lake upstream. Look for a broad lake in dry steppe, with sandy desert country close to its shores.

name: Khasi Hills
blurb: These hills hold Cherrapunji and Mawsynram, two of the wettest places on Earth, where monsoon winds slam into the first high ground north of Bangladesh. Look for a sharp wall rising from the flat green delta.

name: Khuvkhoitun
blurb: A high point of Kamchatka's Sredinny Range, the central spine of the peninsula. Look for snowy summits in country with no roads and almost no people.

name: Kichatna Spire
blurb: The highest of the Cathedral Spires, sheer granite towers in the Kichatna Mountains west of Denali prized by big-wall climbers. Look for needle-like rock between glaciers.

name: Kichenside Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Kemp Coast of East Antarctica. Look for crevassed ice reaching the sea between rocky outcrops.

name: Killarney National Park
blurb: Ireland's first national park, around the Lakes of Killarney, home to the country's only native red deer herd. Look for three lakes beneath the MacGillycuddy's Reeks.

name: King's Peak
blurb: Utah's highest point at 13,528 ft, in the Uinta Mountains, the highest east-west range in the lower 48. Look for a broad gray summit above a long chain of glacial basins and lakes.

name: Kings Canyon
blurb: Sheer sandstone walls about 300 ft high ring a gorge in Watarrka National Park, between Alice Springs and Uluru. Look for the pale cliff edge cutting through red desert ridges.

name: Kinshasa
blurb: One of the largest cities in Africa, facing Brazzaville across the Congo River, the closest pair of capitals in the world after Rome and Vatican City. Look for the wide Pool Malebo and the rapids downstream.

name: Kirkby Glacier
blurb: A glacier in northern Victoria Land, among steep ranges near the Ross Sea. Look for ice ribbons between jagged dark peaks.

name: Kirkpatrick Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Marie Byrd Land coast of West Antarctica. Look for ice flowing to the sea past rocky ridges.

name: Kispiox Mountain
blurb: A peak in the Skeena country of northern BC, above the Kispiox valley near Hazelton. Look for a forested ridge with bare alpine slopes near the top.

name: Kluane Lake
blurb: Yukon's largest lake. In 2016 its main inflow, the Slims River, dried up within days when the retreating Kaskawulsh Glacier sent its meltwater the other way, a case of river piracy. Look for turquoise water beside the Alaska Highway.

name: Kobuk Valley National Park
blurb: Above the Arctic Circle, it holds the Great Kobuk Sand Dunes, with dunes up to about 100 ft high. Look for a patch of tan sand amid tundra and the winding Kobuk River.

name: Kohler Glacier
blurb: Feeds the Dotson Ice Shelf on the Amundsen Sea coast, the region of West Antarctica where glaciers are speeding up and thinning fastest. Look for ice flowing to a flat floating shelf.

name: Kolahoi Peak
blurb: Called the Matterhorn of Kashmir, about 17,800 ft, with a shrinking glacier that feeds the Lidder River through Pahalgam. Look for a sharp rock pyramid above the Kashmir Valley.

name: Kolkheti National Park
blurb: Wetlands of the Rioni delta around Lake Paliastomi near Poti, the ancient Colchis where Jason went for the Golden Fleece. Look for the lake and marsh behind the Black Sea shore.

name: Kootenay Lake
blurb: A long, deep, fjord-like lake in southeastern British Columbia, with the town of Nelson on its West Arm. Look for a narrow blue lake between steep forested ranges.

name: Kovdozero
blurb: A large reservoir on the Kovda River in the south of the Kola Peninsula, dammed for hydropower. Look for a lake crowded with islands in dark taiga close to the Arctic Circle.

name: Kozara National Park
blurb: Mountain forest in northern Bosnia and a WWII battlefield, marked by a monument at Mrakovica. Look for the wooded ridge rising from flat farmland.

name: Krasnoye Lake
blurb: A lake on the tundra of Chukotka in Russia's far northeast. Look for open water in treeless, flat plain.

name: Kreitzer Glacier
blurb: A glacier near the Amery Ice Shelf in East Antarctica. Expect white ice with flow lines and scattered dark nunataks.

name: Krkonoše National Park
blurb: The Czech Republic's highest mountains, topped by Sněžka at 5,259 ft on the Polish border. The Elbe rises here; look for bare rounded summits above the treeline.

name: Kubenskoe
blurb: A long, shallow lake north of Vologda, about 35 miles end to end. A tiny island holds the remains of Spaso-Kamenny, one of northern Russia's oldest monasteries. Look for a thin lake angled through forest and marsh.

name: Kvænangen
blurb: A wide, branching fjord in northern Troms. Look for broad water reaching into mountains, with the long E6 highway snaking over the heights above it.

name: Kyiv Reservoir
blurb: Nicknamed the Kyiv Sea, it begins just upstream of the capital. The Pripyat River, which flows past Chernobyl, enters at its northern end. Look for a vast lake against the green north of Kyiv.

name: Kåfjorden
blurb: A branch of the Lyngen fjord system in Troms, beneath the steep Lyngen Alps. Look for a narrow arm of water with sharp, snowy peaks rising straight from the shore.

name: Köprülü Canyon
blurb: A pine-lined gorge in the Taurus Mountains above Antalya, crossed by a Roman stone bridge still in use and popular for rafting. Look for the green river threading through steep forested walls.

name: La Camperona
blurb: A limestone summit in the Cantabrian Mountains of northern León, in the range that separates green Asturias from the dry Spanish meseta. Look for pale rock ridges above beech forest and high pastures.

name: La Grande 4 Reservoir
blurb: The upstream reservoir on the La Grande River in the James Bay hydro project, deep in Québec's taiga. Look for a sprawl of flooded valleys and new islands in a lake-speckled landscape.

name: Lac Brochet
blurb: A lake in far northern Manitoba near the tree line, beside the Dene community of the same name. Look for an irregular lake in thin spruce forest, frozen white much of the year.

name: Lac Evans
blurb: A large lake on the Broadback River in the James Bay region of Québec. Look for a long, island-dotted body of water in flat, burn-scarred boreal forest.

name: Lac Joseph
blurb: A big, island-dotted lake in western Labrador, part of the vast lake-and-forest plateau feeding the Churchill River. Look for a sprawling lake among spruce and bog.

name: Lac Kipawa
blurb: A sprawling lake in Québec's Témiscamingue region, with a shoreline so convoluted it looks like spilled ink. Look for countless narrow bays and islands in hilly forest.

name: Lac Manouane
blurb: A large lake in the forests north of Lac Saint-Jean in Québec. Look for a ragged outline of bays and islands set in rolling, unbroken boreal forest.

name: Lac Maunoir
blurb: A remote lake in the far north of the Northwest Territories, just above the Arctic Circle. Look for a long, irregular lake in sparse forest and tundra, frozen most of the year.

name: Lac Minto
blurb: A big lake in Nunavik, northern Québec, near the tree line, drained by the Leaf River toward Ungava Bay. Look for a long, island-dotted body of water among bare rock and scattered spruce.

name: Lac Naococane
blurb: A large lake in Québec's remote central plateau, crowded with islands. Look for a complex maze of water and land in flat, sparse boreal forest.

name: Lac Payne
blurb: A large lake on the Ungava Peninsula in Nunavik, well north of the tree line. Look for a long sheet of water in bare, glacier-scoured tundra, frozen much of the year.

name: Lac Plétipi
blurb: A big lake in the remote forest of central Québec, north of the Saguenay region. Look for an irregular body of water with long bays reaching into dark boreal forest.

name: Lac Sakami
blurb: A long lake near the La Grande hydro complex in the James Bay region of Québec. Look for a narrow band of water in flat taiga dotted with smaller lakes and bogs.

name: Lac aux Feuilles
blurb: A large body of water near Tasiujaq in Nunavik, opening toward Ungava Bay in the treeless far north of Québec. Look for long arms of water among bare, glacier-scraped hills.

name: Lac de Gras
blurb: A barren-lands lake at the center of Canada's diamond rush: the Diavik mine sits on an island in it, its open pits held back from the lake by dikes. Look for the grey pits and rock piles on the tundra.

name: Lac des Bois
blurb: A remote lake in the far north of the Northwest Territories, just above the Arctic Circle. Look for a lake in thin spruce forest and tundra dotted with smaller ponds.

name: Lac Île-à-la-Crosse
blurb: On its shore, Île-à-la-Crosse has been a fur-trade post since the 1770s, one of the oldest communities in Saskatchewan. Look for a long lake on the Churchill River with the village on a peninsula.

name: Lacha
blurb: A shallow lake in Russia's north near the old town of Kargopol, source of the Onega River. Look for a broad oval lake in flat forest and marsh.

name: Lagdo Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the Benue River in northern Cameroon, built in the early 1980s for power and irrigation. Look for a broad lake in savanna country.

name: Lago de Coari
blurb: A huge lake formed where the Coari River widens before meeting the Amazon, with the river town of Coari at its mouth. Look for dark water branching like fingers into the rainforest.

name: Lagos
blurb: One of Africa's largest cities, spread across islands and lagoons. Look for the Third Mainland Bridge, about 7 miles across the lagoon, and the reclaimed sand of Eko Atlantic on the ocean side.

name: Laguna Superior
blurb: A big coastal lagoon on the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, fished by Ikoots (Huave) communities on the sandbar that separates it from the Pacific. Look for the thin strip of land between lagoon and ocean.

name: Lagune Iguéla
blurb: A coastal lagoon in Loango National Park, Gabon, where forest, savanna and beach meet. Look for dark water separated from the Atlantic by a thin strip of sand.

name: Lagune Ndogo
blurb: A coastal lagoon in southern Gabon full of islands, between rainforest and the Atlantic. Look for dark, island-dotted water behind the beach.

name: Lahore
blurb: The Mughal heart of Pakistan. The Badshahi Mosque, finished in 1673, faces Lahore Fort across a courtyard; look for its three white marble domes and red sandstone walls beside the walled old city.

name: Lake Abitibi
blurb: A shallow lake straddling the Ontario-Québec border, sprinkled with hundreds of islands. Look for its two connected basins, split by a narrows, in flat clay-belt forest and farmland.

name: Lake Akşehir
blurb: A shallow lake in central Turkey that has shrunk badly from drought and irrigation. Look for a pale basin, often more mud and salt than water, below the Sultan Mountains.

name: Lake Alaotra
blurb: Madagascar's largest lake, surrounded by the island's biggest rice-growing area. Its reed beds are the only home of the Alaotra gentle lemur. Look for a shallow lake ringed by marsh and a wide patchwork of paddies.

name: Lake Alexandrina
blurb: Where the Murray River, Australia's longest, ends before reaching the sea. Barrages built in the 1940s keep the ocean out. Look for the lake next to the long, thin Coorong lagoon.

name: Lake Annean
blurb: A seasonal salt lake in the Murchison goldfields near Meekatharra, dry and white most of the year. Look for a pale, irregular pan among red earth and mulga scrub.

name: Lake Bardawil
blurb: A long, shallow salt lagoon on the north coast of Sinai, cut off from the Mediterranean by a thin curving sandbar. Look for the sand strip sweeping along the coast.

name: Lake Beyşehir
blurb: Turkey's largest freshwater lake, about 250 square miles, dotted with islands. Look for a big blue lake against the mountains of the Taurus range to the west.

name: Lake Borgne
blurb: Not really a lake but a lagoon of the Gulf of Mexico, east of New Orleans. British boats beat a US gunboat flotilla here in 1814, just before the Battle of New Orleans. Look for open water fringed by fading marsh.

name: Lake Brunner / Moana
blurb: The largest lake on New Zealand's West Coast, ringed by rainforest, with the TranzAlpine railway stopping at the village of Moana on its north shore. Look for a round, dark lake in deep green bush.

name: Lake Carnegie
blurb: A large ephemeral salt lake on the edge of the Gibson Desert that fills only in very wet years. Look for a white, ragged-edged pan, sometimes tinted by shallow water, in empty red country.

name: Lake Chamo
blurb: A Rift Valley lake known for its big Nile crocodiles, in Nechisar National Park. Look for its blue water beside the reddish Lake Abaya to the north.

name: Lake Chukchagirskoye
blurb: A remote lake in the Amur basin of the Russian Far East, ringed by bog and taiga. Look for an irregular lake in flat, roadless wetland.

name: Lake Clark
blurb: A long glacial lake about 40 miles long, heart of Lake Clark National Park, reachable only by plane or boat. Look for turquoise water between steep mountain walls west of Cook Inlet.

name: Lake Eppalock
blurb: A reservoir on the Campaspe River supplying Bendigo, set in dry sheep and wheat country in central Victoria. Look for a branching lake whose shoreline shrinks visibly in drought years.

name: Lake Eğirdir
blurb: Turkey's second-largest freshwater lake, in the Lake District, with the town of Eğirdir built out on a peninsula. Look for a long, narrow lake between steep mountains.

name: Lake Hazen
blurb: One of the northernmost large lakes on Earth, on Ellesmere Island in Quttinirpaaq National Park. Ice covers it most or all of the year; look for a long lake between glaciated mountains.

name: Lake Izabal
blurb: Guatemala's largest lake, linked to the Caribbean by the Río Dulce. A Spanish fort, Castillo de San Felipe, guards the outlet against pirates. Look for the lake against green mountains.

name: Lake Keitele
blurb: A large lake in central Finland's lake district, long and studded with islands. Look for a long lake running north-south through forest.

name: Lake Kisale
blurb: A lake on the Lualaba River in the Upemba Depression of southern Congo, surrounded by floodplain and papyrus marsh. Look for open water in a broad green wetland.

name: Lake Kulunda
blurb: The largest lake in Altai Krai, a shallow, salty lake in the flat Kulunda Steppe near the Kazakh border. Look for a broad round lake among farmland and smaller salt lakes.

name: Lake Labaz
blurb: A large lake in the Taymyr lowland far north of the Arctic Circle. Look for a broad, irregular lake surrounded by tundra pocked with thousands of smaller ponds.

name: Lake Livingston
blurb: One of the largest lakes in Texas, a Trinity River reservoir that supplies much of Houston's water. Look for a long, wide lake in the East Texas Piney Woods with a dam across its southern end.

name: Lake Malombe
blurb: A small lake on the Shire River just south of Lake Malawi, the first stop for water leaving the big lake on its way to the Zambezi. Look for a flat oval just below Lake Malawi's southern tip.

name: Lake Marion
blurb: South Carolina's largest lake, a Santee Cooper reservoir that flooded swamp forest in the 1940s. Look for stands of cypress still growing in the shallow upper end.

name: Lake Marqaköl
blurb: A mountain lake high in the Kazakh Altai, protected in a nature reserve and frozen much of the year. Look for a long blue lake cupped in forested ridges near the Chinese border.

name: Lake Michigan shore
blurb: The only Great Lake entirely inside the US, about 300 miles long and big enough that the far shore drops below the horizon. Look for the pale line of sand dunes and bluffs where farmland meets open blue water.

name: Lake Qarun
blurb: The ancient lake of the Faiyum, far larger in pharaonic times; what remains is today's salty Lake Qarun. Look for a blue lake with green farmland on one shore and bare desert on the other.

name: Lake Murray
blurb: Papua New Guinea's largest lake, which swells to several times its dry-season size in the wet season. Look for a many-armed body of brown water in flat, unbroken lowland rainforest.

name: Lake Musters
blurb: A deep freshwater lake near Sarmiento in Chubut, Patagonia, next to the shallow Colhué Huapi. Look for a blue lake in dry steppe beside its paler neighbor.

name: Lake Natron
blurb: So alkaline and hot that few animals survive, yet it is the main breeding ground for East Africa's lesser flamingos. Look for blood-red and pink patches from salt-loving microbes, and the volcano Ol Doinyo Lengai to the south.

name: Lake Nipissing
blurb: A shallow lake averaging about 15 ft deep, with the city of North Bay on its east shore. It drains west through the French River into Georgian Bay, an old voyageur route.

name: Lake Okeechobee
blurb: At about 730 square miles it's one of the largest freshwater lakes in the lower 48, yet averages only about 9 ft deep. Look for the earthen Herbert Hoover Dike ringing the shore.

name: Lake Orivesi
blurb: Part of the Saimaa system in eastern Finland, broken up by islands and peninsulas into narrow channels. Look for a jigsaw of water and forest.

name: Lake Pend Oreille
blurb: Idaho's largest lake, more than 1,100 ft deep. It's so deep and quiet that the US Navy tests submarine designs here, 300 miles from the ocean. Look for its long arms among the forested mountains.

name: Lake Pihkva
blurb: The southern part of the Peipus lake system, also called Lake Pskov, linked to the main lake by a narrow channel. Look for its marshy delta shores and the Estonia-Russia border running through the water.

name: Lake Razelm
blurb: Romania's largest lake, a brackish lagoon on the southern edge of the Danube Delta. Look for a broad sheet of water behind thin sandbars along the Black Sea coast.

name: Lake Saint Pierre
blurb: A wide, shallow stretch of the St. Lawrence between Montreal and Québec City, a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Ocean ships follow a dredged channel down the middle; look for its straight line through the open water.

name: Lake Salvador
blurb: A brackish lake in the marshes southwest of New Orleans, part of the Barataria estuary. Look for open water surrounded by bayous, cypress swamp and marsh crisscrossed by straight oil-field canals.

name: Lake Sasykkol
blurb: Part of the Alakol chain of lakes in eastern Kazakhstan, a shallow, reedy lake on a migratory bird flyway. Look for a flat water body with marshy edges in a dry basin.

name: Lake Shala
blurb: Filling a volcanic caldera, it's the deepest lake in Ethiopia's Rift, about 870 ft, and its alkaline water draws flocks of flamingos. Look for steep caldera walls next to shallow Lake Abijatta.

name: Lake Sidenreng
blurb: A shallow lake in South Sulawesi's farmland, which floods out across the surrounding rice paddies in wet season. Look for a broad lake surrounded by rice fields.

name: Lake Simcoe
blurb: Toronto's big cottage-country lake, about 280 square miles, famous for winter ice fishing when whole villages of huts appear on the ice. Look for Kempenfelt Bay, the long arm reaching west to Barrie.

name: Lake Skadar
blurb: The largest lake in the Balkans, shared by Montenegro and Albania, its edges fringed with reeds, water lilies and hundreds of bird species. Look for a broad lake with a green, marshy north shore and limestone mountains on the south.

name: Lake St. Joseph
blurb: A long lake at the head of the Albany River in northwestern Ontario, part of whose flow is diverted west into the Lac Seul system for hydropower. Look for a narrow band of water in endless boreal forest.

name: Lake St. Lucia
blurb: The heart of South Africa's iSimangaliso Wetland Park, the largest estuary system in Africa, home to hippos and crocodiles. Look for the long lake behind towering forested coastal dunes.

name: Lake Sulunga
blurb: A shallow, seasonal lake in the dry interior of central Tanzania that shrinks and spreads with the rains. Look for pale salty flats and patches of water among dry bush.

name: Lake Sélingué
blurb: A reservoir on the Sankarani River in southern Mali, made by the Sélingué Dam to supply hydropower to Bamako. Look for a branching lake spreading across the green savanna.

name: Lake Tacarigua o Valencia
blurb: Venezuela's largest freshwater lake has no outlet to the sea, and it has been rising for years, flooding neighborhoods on its shores. Look for a greenish lake with small islands, ringed by the sprawl of Valencia and Maracay.

name: Lake Tasiujaq
blurb: A large tidal lake on Hudson Bay's east coast, also called Lac Guillaume-Delisle, joined to the sea by a narrow gap. Look for the row of steep, tilted ridges running along its shore.

name: Lake Taupō
blurb: New Zealand's largest lake, about 240 square miles, fills the caldera of a supervolcano whose eruption around 26,500 years ago was one of the biggest of the last 100,000 years. Look for the big lake in the North Island's middle.

name: Lake Texoma
blurb: Formed by Denison Dam on the Red River, finished in 1944, one of the largest reservoirs in the US. It straddles the Texas-Oklahoma line; look for a broad, many-armed lake in rolling country.

name: Lake Timiskaming
blurb: A long, narrow lake on the Ontario-Québec border, carried by the Ottawa River through a geological rift valley. Look for a slender ribbon of water running roughly north-south between steep, forested banks.

name: Lake Towuti
blurb: The largest of Sulawesi's ancient Malili Lakes, home to fish and snails found nowhere else. Look for a clear lake in forested hills, near the nickel mines of Sorowako.

name: Lake Tshangalele
blurb: A reservoir formed by the Mwadingusha Dam on the Lufira River near Likasi, in Congo's copper belt. Look for a lake with marshy edges in savanna.

name: Lake Tumba
blurb: A shallow lake in the Congo rainforest near Mbandaka. Bonobos live in the forests around it. Look for dark water surrounded by unbroken forest.

name: Lake Winnebago
blurb: Wisconsin's largest inland lake, nearly 30 miles long but only about 15 ft deep on average. Look for Oshkosh on the west shore, home of the giant EAA AirVenture fly-in each summer, and Fond du Lac at the south tip.

name: Lake Zway
blurb: A freshwater Rift Valley lake south of Addis Ababa, with island monasteries. Local legend says the Ark of the Covenant was once hidden on one of them. Look for its islands, ringed by farmland.

name: Lake of the Woods
blurb: Over 14,000 islands crowd this lake shared by Ontario, Manitoba and Minnesota. The border quirk here, the Northwest Angle, is the only part of the lower 48 north of the 49th parallel.

name: Laksefjord
blurb: A broad Arctic fjord in Finnmark between the Nordkinn and Porsanger peninsulas. Look for treeless rolling plateaus around a wide inlet opening north to the Barents Sea.

name: Lalla-Khedidja
blurb: The highest peak of the Djurdjura range in Kabylie, about 7,600 ft, often snowcapped in winter within sight of the Mediterranean. Look for a sharp limestone ridge east of Algiers.

name: Lama
blurb: A long lake at the edge of the Putorana Plateau west of Norilsk, set between steep, flat-topped mountains. Look for a fjord-like lake cutting into the plateau's stepped cliffs.

name: Land Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Marie Byrd Land coast of West Antarctica, flowing into the sea. Look for crevassed ice ending at a floating front.

name: Langskavlen Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land. Look for ice flowing past dark rocky peaks toward the coast.

name: Law Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains near the Beardmore Glacier, the route Shackleton and Scott took to the polar plateau. Look for ice between high, rocky walls.

name: Lazarev Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating shelf on the Princess Astrid Coast, named for Mikhail Lazarev of the 1820 Russian expedition that was among the first to sight Antarctica. Look for flat ice ending in a straight seaward cliff.

name: Lednik Petrova
blurb: Ice cap covering Schmidt Island, a small, almost entirely glaciated island in the Kara Sea far above the Arctic Circle. Look for a white dome sitting in pack ice or dark open water.

name: Leech Lake
blurb: One of Minnesota's largest lakes, famous for its ragged outline of long bays and points. Much of it lies within the Leech Lake Reservation. Look for a starfish-shaped lake in pine forest.

name: Lennon Glacier
blurb: A glacier on Alexander Island off the Antarctic Peninsula, where many features carry composers' and musicians' names. Look for ice flowing toward George VI Sound.

name: Lerchenfeld Glacier
blurb: A glacier feeding the Filchner Ice Shelf region near the Weddell Sea. Expect broad white ice with faint flow lines.

name: Lima
blurb: One of the driest capitals in the world, on desert cliffs above the Pacific, where it almost never rains but a grey fog called garúa hangs for months. Look for green parks atop the cliffs at Miraflores.

name: Liushi Shan
blurb: At over 23,000 ft one of the highest points of the western Kunlun, on the barren high desert near Aksai Chin. Look for an isolated ice cap above lifeless brown plateau and salt lakes.

name: Liv Glacier
blurb: Named by Amundsen for Liv Nansen, daughter of the explorer Fridtjof Nansen. It cuts through the Queen Maud Mountains from the polar plateau down to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for a long ice highway between peaks.

name: Llancanelo Lake
blurb: A shallow salt lagoon in southern Mendoza, near Malargüe, protected for its flamingos and other waterbirds. Look for a wetland in arid volcanic country with dark lava fields nearby.

name: Lobéké National Park
blurb: Rainforest in Cameroon's southeast corner, part of the Sangha Trinational with the Congo and Central African Republic. Look for unbroken canopy and forest clearings.

name: Loch Long
blurb: A narrow sea loch running into the hills west of Glasgow; the Royal Navy's Coulport nuclear weapons depot sits on its shore. Look for a long, steep-sided slot of water reaching north into the Arrochar Alps.

name: Loe Nekan
blurb: A peak in the bare mountains of northern Balochistan, near Quetta. Look for brown ridges and dry valleys with no snow most of the year.

name: Loi Leng
blurb: Highest point of Myanmar's Shan State, a lone massif above the Shan Plateau. Look for a high, dark ridge rising over rolling farmland.

name: Loi Pangnao
blurb: A peak in eastern Shan State near the Mekong and the borders of Laos and Thailand. Look for forested ridges and twisting river valleys.

name: Lokka Reservoir
blurb: Finland's largest reservoir, flooded across Lapland bogland in the 1960s. Look for a broad, shallow lake in flat, empty country north of the Arctic Circle.

name: Long Island / Hamptons
blurb: About 118 miles long, the largest island in the contiguous US, splitting at its east end into two forks like a fish tail. Look for the thin barrier beaches on the south shore and the Hamptons' estates along the dunes.

name: Long Lake
blurb: A narrow lake in the hills of western Maine, about 11 miles long, running north from the town of Bridgton. Look for a thin blue strip among dense forest and smaller ponds.

name: Longgan Lake
blurb: A shallow lake on the Yangtze floodplain at the Anhui-Hubei border, one of many lakes that store the river's summer floods. Look for open water edged by fish ponds and rice paddies.

name: Longyangxia Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir on the upper Yellow River whose dam also anchors one of the world's largest solar farms. Look for the vast dark grid of panels on the plateau beside the water.

name: Lopé National Park
blurb: Patches of grassland left over from drier ice-age times sit inside rainforest along the Ogooué River, home to some of the largest mandrill groups ever recorded. Look for the savanna islands in the green.

name: Lough Neagh
blurb: The largest lake in the British Isles, about 150 square miles, supplying much of Northern Ireland's water. Look for a broad, roughly square lake in flat farmland just west of Belfast.

name: Ludeman Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains near the head of the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for ice flowing between bare rock summits.

name: Lunpo Gangri
blurb: About 23,300 ft, the highest peak of the Gangdise (Transhimalaya) range north of the Himalaya. Look for a white massif rising from the dry, wide Tibetan plateau.

name: Lysefjord
blurb: Cliffs rise almost straight up 3,000 ft along its length. Pulpit Rock juts out nearly 2,000 ft above the water, and Kjerag's boulder hangs wedged in a crack. Look for a dark, ruler-straight slot running east from Stavanger's islands.

name: M'Goun
blurb: At about 13,350 ft, one of the highest peaks of Morocco's High Atlas, a long massif rather than a single spike. Look for snow in winter on a whaleback crest over dry, red valleys.

name: MacAlpine Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the tundra of central Nunavut. Look for a large, irregular lake in open, treeless country dotted with smaller ponds, frozen most of the year.

name: MacKay Lake
blurb: A long lake in the barren lands northeast of Yellowknife, along the route of the winter ice road to the diamond mines. Look for a narrow lake in bare tundra, frozen white for most of the year.

name: Madidi National Park and Integrated Management Natural Area
blurb: One of the most biodiverse places on Earth, running from Andean peaks to Amazon lowland. Look for steep forested valleys dropping east to the plains.

name: Magdalenefjorden
blurb: A small fjord on Spitsbergen's northwest coast, ringed by glaciers and jagged peaks, a favorite stop for Arctic cruise ships. Look for a short inlet with white ice tongues reaching the water on every side.

name: Mago National Park
blurb: Savanna and riverine forest in the Lower Omo Valley, where the Mursi people live. Look for the Mago River joining the Omo through dry bush.

name: Maja e Këndrevicës
blurb: A limestone summit of about 7,000 ft in southern Albania, inland from Vlorë and the Ionian coast. Look for a bare gray ridge above the coastal mountains.

name: Mallery Lake
blurb: A tundra lake in Nunavut's Kivalliq region, far beyond the tree line. Look for dark open water set in a brown and green plain pocked with thousands of smaller ponds.

name: Manam
blurb: One of Papua New Guinea's most active volcanoes, a near-perfect cone island about 6 miles wide. A 2004 eruption forced the whole island to evacuate. Look for a cone rising straight from the sea, often steaming.

name: Mandioré Lake
blurb: A big lake in the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland, straddling the Brazil-Bolivia border beside the Paraguay River. Look for open water among flooded grassland, with forested hills on the Bolivian side.

name: Manirang
blurb: About 21,600 ft on the border of Kinnaur and the high desert of Spiti. Look for a snow summit with brown, nearly treeless valleys on its Spiti side.

name: Manuel Antonio National Park
blurb: One of Costa Rica's smallest national parks and one of its most visited. Look for Punta Catedral, a forested headland tied to the mainland by a narrow sandy neck.

name: Manych-Gudilo
blurb: A long, shallow salt lake in the Manych depression, the low trough once seen as the boundary between Europe and Asia. Look for a thin ribbon of water stretching across the dry steppe, with islands that host bird colonies.

name: Mar Menor
blurb: One of Europe's largest saltwater lagoons, cut off from the Mediterranean by La Manga, a 13-mile sand strip lined with high-rises. In 2022 it became the first ecosystem in Europe granted legal personhood.

name: Mariager Fjord
blurb: Often called Denmark's longest fjord, more than 20 miles, narrow and winding through eastern Jutland. Look for a thin blue ribbon cutting through the countryside to the Kattegat.

name: Marojejy National Park
blurb: A granite mountain rising from rainforest in northeast Madagascar, home of the silky sifaka. Look for steep green peaks with clouds stuck to the summit.

name: Mars Glacier
blurb: One of the planet-named glaciers on Alexander Island, off the Antarctic Peninsula, flowing east into George VI Sound. Look for ice meeting the long, narrow Sound.

name: Masoala National Park
blurb: Madagascar's largest protected area, where rainforest runs straight into the Indian Ocean. Look for the forested peninsula across the bay from Maroantsetra.

name: Matobo National Park
blurb: Granite hills of piled boulders and balancing rocks, rich in San rock art, with Cecil Rhodes buried on a dome called World's View. Look for the lumpy, bare granite domes in the bush south of Bulawayo.

name: Mawhpung Bum
blurb: A remote summit in the forested mountains of Kachin State. Look for unbroken jungle ridges with almost no roads.

name: McClary Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Fallières Coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, flowing into Marguerite Bay. Look for crevassed ice dropping between mountains to the sea.

name: McDonald Ice Rumples
blurb: Here the floating Brunt Ice Shelf runs aground on a seabed rise, crumpling the ice into ridges and crevasses. Britain's Halley station sits on the same shelf. Look for a patch of wrinkled, chaotic ice on otherwise flat white.

name: McDonald Peak
blurb: At 9,820 ft, the highest of the Mission Mountains, rising nearly 7,000 ft above the Flathead Valley. Look for a sheer, snowy wall east of the valley, with Flathead Lake to the north.

name: Medicine Lake Volcano
blurb: By volume the largest volcano in the Cascades, a broad shield so gentle it barely looks like a mountain. Look for Glass Mountain's obsidian flow and the lava tubes of Lava Beds National Monument to the north.

name: Mela Taung
blurb: A peak in the Dawna Range along the Myanmar-Thailand border. Look for long, forested ridges running north-south.

name: Mercantour National Park
blurb: Bronze Age people carved tens of thousands of figures into the rocks of the Vallée des Merveilles, and wolves returned here from Italy in the 1990s. Look for high peaks just north of Nice.

name: Merowe Reservoir
blurb: Formed by the Merowe Dam, completed in 2009 at the Nile's Fourth Cataract, displacing tens of thousands of people. Look for a long blue lake winding through bare desert.

name: Mertz Glacier
blurb: Its floating tongue, about 50 miles long, was knocked off in 2010 when a giant iceberg rammed it. Named for Xavier Mertz, who died in 1913 on Douglas Mawson's sledging journey. Look for an ice tongue ending abruptly in the sea.

name: Mikumi National Park
blurb: The main highway from Dar es Salaam to Zambia runs straight through it, so lions and elephants can be seen from the road. Look for the wide Mkata floodplain ringed by mountains.

name: Milan
blurb: Italy's business capital. Look for the white Gothic Duomo at the hub, ring roads tracing the old city walls, and San Siro stadium to the west.

name: Mill Stream Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains near the Beardmore region. Look for ice between bare, dark peaks.

name: Mille Lacs Lake
blurb: One of Minnesota's largest lakes, a round basin of about 200 square miles. In winter thousands of ice-fishing houses form temporary towns on it. Look for the dots of shanties and plowed roads across the ice.

name: Miller Peak
blurb: The high point of the Huachuca Mountains, about 9,500 ft, just a few miles from the Mexican border. Look for a forested ridge rising out of desert grassland, with the San Pedro River valley to the east.

name: Milne Ice Shelf
blurb: Canada's last fully intact ice shelf until 2020, when it lost about 40% of its area in a single collapse. Look for flat, rippled ice along Ellesmere Island's north coast.

name: Milwaukee
