blurb: Three rivers meet here before emptying into Lake Michigan. Look on the lakefront for Calatrava's art museum, whose white wing-like sunscreen opens and folds like a bird.

name: Mingachevir reservoir
blurb: The largest reservoir in the Caucasus, formed by a dam on the Kura River in the 1950s. Look for a long blue lake with the city of Mingachevir at its southeast end.

name: Minneapolis
blurb: Grew up around St. Anthony Falls, the only true waterfall on the Mississippi, which powered its flour mills. Look for the Chain of Lakes on the southwest side and the river cutting a gorge through town.

name: Mizri Ghar
blurb: A peak in the mountains of the tribal belt near the Afghan border. Look for steep, rocky ridges and narrow valleys.

name: Mjøsa
blurb: Norway's largest lake, about 60 miles long, with Lillehammer at its north end. The paddle steamer Skibladner, in service since 1856, still sails it. Look for a long, narrow lake in farmland and forest north of Oslo.

name: Mole National Park
blurb: Ghana's largest wildlife refuge, savanna woodland where elephants come to drink at a waterhole below the park lodge. Look for open woodland and red laterite roads in the dry north.

name: Molson Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the boreal forest of northern Manitoba, east of Lake Winnipeg. Look for an irregular, island-dotted lake in dense spruce, one of thousands scattered across the Canadian Shield.

name: Monfragüe National Park
blurb: Rocky ridges where the Tagus cuts through Extremadura, with one of Europe's largest colonies of black vultures. Look for the dammed river winding through cork-oak pasture and the castle on its crag.

name: Monkh Saridag
blurb: About 11,450 ft, the highest peak of the Sayan Mountains, on the Russia-Mongolia border just north of Lake Khövsgöl. Look for a snowy summit between Siberian forest and the long blue lake.

name: Monmouth Mountain
blurb: A glaciated peak in the Coast Mountains north of Pemberton, in the ranges between the coast and the dry interior. Look for snow and rock above deep green valleys.

name: Mont Forel
blurb: About 11,000 ft, one of the highest peaks in Greenland, rising out of the ice sheet inland from the east coast. Look for a big snow pyramid standing far above the surrounding ice.

name: Mont Marion-Dufresne
blurb: The highest point of Ile de l'Est in the Crozet Islands, a subantarctic volcanic island with no people and huge penguin colonies. Look for steep, cloud-wrapped slopes above surf-battered cliffs.

name: Mont Panié
blurb: New Caledonia's highest point at about 5,340 ft, on the wet northeast coast and wrapped in rainforest with plants found nowhere else. Look for a dark-green ridge dropping straight to a reef-lined sea.

name: Montalto
blurb: The high point of the Aspromonte at about 6,410 ft, at the toe of Italy's boot. A bronze statue of Christ the Redeemer stands on top. Look for forested ridges with views of the Strait of Messina and Etna.

name: Monte Cimone
blurb: The highest peak of the northern Apennines at about 7,100 ft, crowned by a weather and climate observatory. Look for a bare summit with buildings and antennas, and ski runs on its slopes.

name: Monte Gordo
blurb: The highest point on São Nicolau in Cape Verde, a volcanic peak whose upper slopes catch enough moisture to stay green on an otherwise arid island. Look for the high forested center of the island.

name: Montreal Lake
blurb: A long lake in the boreal forest of central Saskatchewan, north of Prince Albert National Park. Look for a narrow north-south body of water in dark, flat forest.

name: Moosehead Lake
blurb: Maine's largest lake, about 40 miles long, in country so wild that floatplanes are the local taxis. Look for Mount Kineo, a sheer 700-ft cliff rising straight out of the water midway up the lake.

name: Moran Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula near Marguerite Bay. Look for ice spilling between mountains toward the coast.

name: Morelli Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Ellsworth Land, West Antarctica. Expect white ice with faint flow lines heading toward the Bellingshausen Sea.

name: Moscow University Ice Shelf
blurb: Fronts the Totten Glacier region of East Antarctica, where warm ocean water reaches under the ice. Totten's basin holds enough ice to raise sea levels by several feet. Look for flat floating ice meeting sea ice.

name: Mosquito Lake
blurb: A remote lake near the Nunavut border, around the tree line. Look for an irregular lake among thin spruce, bare rock and countless smaller ponds, frozen much of the year.

name: Mount Abuna Yosef
blurb: A massif of nearly 14,000 ft in Ethiopia's northern highlands, with Lalibela and its rock-cut churches in its foothills. Look for a long escarpment towering over the town's plateau.

name: Mount Addala-Shukhgelmeer
blurb: One of the highest summits in Dagestan at roughly 13,600 ft, on the Bogos range of the eastern Caucasus. Look for a glaciated crest above deep, dry gorges cut by the Avar Koysu tributaries.

name: Mount Arlan
blurb: About 6,200 ft, the high point of the Great Balkhan range, a lone desert ridge rising near Turkmenistan's Caspian coast. Look for a long rocky wall standing above flat sand and salt pans.

name: Mount Bangeta
blurb: A summit of about 13,500 ft in the Saruwaged Range of the Huon Peninsula. Look for steep, cloud-wrapped ridges above the coast.

name: Mount Benum
blurb: A remote summit of about 6,900 ft in the jungle of central Pahang, rising above the forested spine of the peninsula. Look for a lone high ridge among endless green.

name: Mount Bintang
blurb: Highest point of the Bintang Range in northern Perak, a forested ridge that runs north to the Thai border. Look for a continuous green crest with rubber and oil palm in the valleys.

name: Mount Bintumani
blurb: Sierra Leone's highest point at 6,381 ft, in the Loma Mountains. Look for a grassy summit above forest, standing well clear of the lowlands around it.

name: Mount Bulusan
blurb: A 5,135-ft active volcano at Luzon's southern tip in Sorsogon, given to sudden steam and ash blasts. Look for a symmetrical cone with a small lake at its foot.

name: Mount Cronin
blurb: A peak in the Babine Range northeast of Smithers, an old mining area in northern BC. Look for bare rocky summits above forested valleys.

name: Mount Darnley
blurb: The summit of Bristol Island in the South Sandwich chain, buried in ice and cloud most of the year. Look for a white island with dark rocky cliffs at the shore.

name: Mount Discovery
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 8,800 ft on McMurdo Sound, named by Scott for his ship Discovery. Look for a lone cone rising from the ice shelf south of McMurdo Station.

name: Mount Dyultydag
blurb: A roughly 13,500-ft massif in southern Dagestan, standing apart from the main Caucasus crest. Look for a snowy block above bare brown ridges and terraced valleys.

name: Mount Frakes
blurb: A large shield volcano of about 12,000 ft in the Crary Mountains of Marie Byrd Land. Look for a broad white dome rising gently above the West Antarctic ice sheet.

name: Mount Garrin
blurb: The crest of the Garrin range in the Zagros, about 11,800 ft, in Lorestan. Look for a long, folded limestone ridge with snow into spring.

name: Mount Guna
blurb: An old shield volcano of about 13,500 ft east of Lake Tana, source of streams that feed both the Blue Nile and the Tekezé. Look for a broad, rounded massif rising above farmed highland plateau.

name: Mount Haddington
blurb: The massive shield volcano that forms most of James Ross Island off the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, capped by an ice dome about 5,300 ft high. Look for the rounded ice cap above dark volcanic rock.

name: Mount Hakkyō
blurb: At about 6,280 ft, the highest peak in Japan's Kansai region, on the Omine range, a mountain pilgrimage route that is part of a World Heritage site. Look for forested ridges in the heart of the Kii Peninsula.

name: Mount Hikurangi
blurb: At about 5,800 ft, often billed as the first place on the world's mainland to catch the sunrise, sacred to the Ngāti Porou people. Look for the lone high peak near the East Cape.

name: Mount Hiuchi
blurb: An active volcano of about 8,080 ft in Niigata, with a lava dome summit. Look for a pale, rocky dome above forest, near the Japan Sea coast.

name: Mount Hodson
region: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
blurb: The summit of Visokoi Island in the South Sandwich chain, a glacier-covered volcano rarely visited by anyone. Look for an ice-capped island rising from the Southern Ocean.

name: Mount Igikpak
blurb: The highest peak in the western Brooks Range, rising from Gates of the Arctic National Park, a park with no roads at all. Look for a granite massif with small glaciers above wild Arctic valleys.

name: Mount Inamura
blurb: A summit of about 4,940 ft in the Shikoku mountains, overlooking forested valleys and dams of the island interior. Look for steep green ridges.

name: Mount Irving
blurb: The high point of Clarence Island, an ice-capped outlier at the eastern end of the South Shetlands, rising about 6,400 ft straight from the Southern Ocean. Look for a lone white island with cliffs dropping into dark water.

name: Mount Judge Howay
blurb: A twin-summited peak in the Coast Mountains rising above Stave Lake, north of the Fraser Valley. Look for two rock horns standing out from the mountains east of Vancouver.

name: Mount Kadam
blurb: About 10,000 ft, an old volcanic massif rising from the dry plains of Karamoja in northeastern Uganda. Look for a dark, steep-sided mountain far above the surrounding savanna.

name: Mount Kaplan
blurb: One of the high summits of the Queen Maud Mountains, the range the polar plateau spills through on its way to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for dark rock ridges poking above glaciers heading north.

name: Mount Kaputjugh
blurb: About 12,800 ft, the high point of the Zangezur range on the border between Armenia and Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan exclave. Look for a rugged, snow-streaked crest above deep, dry valleys.

name: Mount Kruzenshtern
blurb: One of the high points of Novaya Zemlya's ice-capped northern island, the Arctic archipelago where the Soviet Union set off the Tsar Bomba, the largest bomb ever detonated, in 1961. Look for ice spilling from a long spine of mountains.

name: Mount Kulal
blurb: A volcano of about 7,500 ft just east of Lake Turkana, its top wrapped in a patch of mist forest in the middle of the desert. Look for a green ridge above lava fields and the jade-colored lake.

name: Mount Kyllini
blurb: About 7,800 ft in the northern Peloponnese, said in myth to be the birthplace of Hermes. Look for a bare limestone summit above the Stymfalia basin and Lake Feneos.

name: Mount Labo
blurb: About 5,000 ft, a forested volcano in Camarines Norte on the Bicol Peninsula, with no recorded eruptions but still hot springs on its flanks. Look for a broad, heavily wooded dome.

name: Mount Lemmon
blurb: About 9,150 ft, the top of the Santa Catalina Mountains, climbing from saguaro desert to fir forest above Tucson, with the southernmost ski area in the US and a cluster of telescopes. Look for a dark forested crown above the city grid.

name: Mount Melbourne
blurb: A dormant volcano just under 9,000 ft above Terra Nova Bay in Victoria Land, still warm enough at the summit to melt ice caves and build steaming ice towers. Look for a broad white cone standing alone on the coast.

name: Mount Mitchell
blurb: At 6,684 ft, the highest point east of the Mississippi. Look for the dark spruce-fir summit of the Black Mountains, northeast of Asheville.

name: Mount Moco
blurb: At about 8,600 ft the highest peak in Angola, on the central highlands near Huambo, with rare patches of montane forest in its ravines. Look for a rocky massif above grassland.

name: Mount Morning
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 9,000 ft on the mainland southwest of McMurdo Sound, named for the relief ship that resupplied Scott's first expedition. Look for a rounded snow dome beside the flat Ross Ice Shelf.

name: Mount Moroto
blurb: About 10,100 ft, a forested mountain above the town of Moroto in Uganda's dry Karamoja region near the Kenyan border. Look for a green massif standing over brown, open plains.

name: Mount Mutis
blurb: West Timor's highest peak at about 8,000 ft, sacred to the Atoni people and cloaked in eucalyptus forest. Look for a green massif above the island's dry, brown hills.

name: Mount Narodnaya
blurb: The highest point of the Ural Mountains at about 6,210 ft, near the traditional line between Europe and Asia. Look for a rocky crest with small glaciers and cirques in otherwise flat tundra and taiga.

name: Mount Nebo
blurb: At 11,928 ft, the highest peak of the Wasatch Range, at its southern end above Nephi. Look for a long triple-summited ridge rising abruptly from the valley floor along I-15.

name: Mount Nirvana
blurb: The highest point in the Northwest Territories at about 9,100 ft, deep in the Mackenzie Mountains and one of Canada's least visited summits. Look for glaciated peaks with no roads in any direction.

name: Mount Nyangani
blurb: Zimbabwe's highest point at about 8,500 ft, a moorland plateau in the Eastern Highlands, often wrapped in cloud. Look for a flat-topped green ridge above pine plantations near the Mozambique border.

name: Mount Ossa
blurb: Tasmania's highest peak at 5,305 ft, a cluster of dolerite columns along the Overland Track. Look for rugged gray crags above lakes and buttongrass plains.

name: Mount Perseus
blurb: A glaciated summit in the Cariboo Mountains of interior BC, east of Quesnel Lake. Look for ice-streaked peaks above dense forest.

name: Mount Priestley
blurb: A peak in the Coast Mountains near the Alaska border north of Prince Rupert. Look for snowy summits above long ocean inlets.

name: Mount Prindle
blurb: A summit in the White Mountains north of Fairbanks, capped with granite tors, rock towers standing above the tundra. Look for knobby outcrops on the rounded hills.

name: Mount Rumput
blurb: A forested peak in western Sarawak close to the Indonesian border, part of the hills behind Kuching. Look for jungle ridges giving way to the flat, river-cut coastal plain.

name: Mount Rushmore / Black Hills
blurb: The four presidents' faces are 60 ft tall, carved between 1927 and 1941. From the air the Black Hills are the easier catch: look for a dark island of pine forest, over 100 miles long, rising from the tan Great Plains.

name: Mount San Antonio
blurb: Known to everyone as Mount Baldy, at 10,064 ft the highest point in Los Angeles County. Look for a bare, pale summit above the San Gabriels, often snow-white in winter behind the LA basin.

name: Mount Seguam
blurb: Seguam Island in the central Aleutians is built of two calderas joined end to end. Fresh lava flows from the 1990s still show as dark tongues against the snow.

name: Mount Shungol
blurb: A peak in the mountains of Papua New Guinea's Huon region, above deep river valleys. Look for forested ridges often hidden in cloud.

name: Mount Simpson
blurb: A peak at the eastern end of the Owen Stanley Range, near Papua New Guinea's southeast tip. Look for forested ridges falling to reef-lined coasts.

name: Mount Stuart
blurb: A huge granite block at 9,415 ft, among the highest non-volcanic peaks in Washington, rising above Leavenworth. Look for pale rock and small glaciers on its north face, apart from the main Cascade crest.

name: Mount Sylvia
blurb: A peak in the remote northern Rockies of BC, in roadless country west of the Alaska Highway. Look for bare gray ridges with patches of snow.

name: Mount Tabwemasana
blurb: Vanuatu's highest peak at about 6,165 ft, on the rugged western side of Espiritu Santo. Look for steep, cloud-covered ridges dropping straight to the coast.

name: Mount Temehani
blurb: A flat-topped volcanic plateau on Raiatea, sacred in Polynesian tradition and the only place on Earth where the tiare apetahi flower grows. Look for the long tabletop above the lagoon.

name: Mount Tod
blurb: A rounded summit north of Kamloops, home to the Sun Peaks ski resort on its flanks. Look for ski runs cut as pale lines through forest on its slopes.

name: Mount Tsurugi
blurb: About 6,410 ft, Shikoku's second-highest peak, a sacred mountain with a broad summit of bamboo grass. Look for a smooth green top above the steep Iya valley.

name: Mount Veve
blurb: The summit of Kolombangara, a nearly perfectly round volcanic island in the Solomons whose slopes climb to about 5,800 ft. Look for a circular island with forested ridges radiating from a central crater.

name: Mount Victoria, Palawan
blurb: About 5,700 ft, the high point of central Palawan's mountain spine, wrapped in some of the least disturbed forest in the Philippines. Look for a craggy, cloud-topped ridge with the sea close on both sides.

name: Mount Welel
blurb: The high point of the western Ethiopian highlands near the Sudan border, above forest and coffee country. Look for a green massif where the plateau starts to drop toward the plains of the Nile basin.

name: Mount Yong Belar
blurb: One of the highest summits in Peninsular Malaysia, on the Perak-Kelantan border in the Titiwangsa Range. Look for the mossy, cloud-wrapped crest of the main range.

name: Mousa Ali
blurb: Djibouti's highest point at about 6,650 ft, a volcano where Djibouti, Eritrea and Ethiopia meet. Look for a dark cone rising above the scorched Afar lowlands, some of the hottest ground on Earth.

name: Muddus National Park
blurb: Part of the Laponia World Heritage area, a roadless spread of ancient pine forest and vast open bogs used by Sami reindeer herders. Look for the patchwork of pale mire and dark forest.

name: Muir Glacier
blurb: John Muir explored its face in 1879, when it was a towering tidewater wall; it has since retreated more than 30 miles and no longer reaches the sea. Look for the raw gray valley it left in Muir Inlet.

name: Murphy Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's Graham Land coast. Look for ice spilling off the plateau into a fjord-like inlet.

name: Mushketov Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land, named by Soviet expeditions for the Russian geologist Ivan Mushketov. Look for ice flowing past dark peaks.

name: Myinmoletkat Taung
blurb: The highest point in Myanmar's Tanintharyi region, the long southern panhandle. Look for a jungle crest between the Andaman Sea coast and the Thai border.

name: Möng Ling Shan
blurb: A forested peak in the mountains along the China-Myanmar border. Look for steep jungle ridges with scattered clearings and terraced slopes.

name: Mönkh Khairkhan
blurb: Mongolia's second-highest peak, a glacier-capped summit in the Altai. Look for a wide white cap and tongues of ice spilling into brown valleys.

name: Nagarhole National Park
blurb: Forest on the Kabini reservoir with one of the densest populations of Asian elephants anywhere. Look for the reservoir's long fingers with forest pressing to the water.

name: Naknek Lake
blurb: The largest lake in Katmai National Park. Brooks River, where brown bears famously catch leaping salmon at Brooks Falls, flows into it. Look for its long arms reaching east into the mountains.

name: Nambung National Park
blurb: Home of the Pinnacles, thousands of limestone spires sticking out of yellow sand near the coast north of Perth. Look for the pale dune field between the coastal scrub and the ocean.

name: Namib-Naukluft National Park
blurb: One of the largest parks in Africa, holding the red dunes of Sossusvlei, some more than 1,000 ft tall, in one of the world's oldest deserts. Look for rows of orange and apricot dunes ending in white clay pans.

name: Nansen Ice Shelf
blurb: Really a floating ice shelf in Terra Nova Bay, near Italy's Mario Zucchelli station. In 2016 a long crack broke through and it calved two icebergs, one big enough to be named. Look for flat ice ending in a fresh-looking edge.

name: Napaktulik Lake
blurb: A large, ragged lake in the treeless tundra of western Nunavut, frozen for much of the year. Look for a sprawling outline of bays and islands among countless smaller ponds.

name: Naracoorte Caves National Park
blurb: World Heritage caves holding one of the richest fossil records of Ice Age megafauna in Australia. From above it looks like ordinary farmland, so look for the strips of scrub along a low limestone ridge.

name: Nashville
blurb: Music City, the home of country music. Look for the AT&T Building, nicknamed the Batman Building for its twin spires, and the Cumberland River curving past downtown.

name: National Park of American Samoa
blurb: The only US national park south of the equator, protecting rainforest, reefs and fruit bat roosts on Tutuila and the Manu'a Islands. Look for steep green ridges dropping into turquoise reef.

name: Nattaung
blurb: Highest point in the Karen Hills, east of the Sittaung River. Look for a forested crest rising from the lowland rice plains.

name: Nechako Reservoir
blurb: Created in the 1950s when the Kenney Dam reversed the Nechako River, sending water through a mountain tunnel to power an aluminum smelter at Kitimat. Look for a chain of drowned lakes with dead trees along the shores.

name: Nelson Lakes National Park
blurb: Two long glacial lakes, Rotoiti and Rotoroa, at the northern end of the Southern Alps. Look for the narrow blue lakes pointing south into beech-forested mountains.

name: Nenang
blurb: A glaciated peak in the eastern Nyenchen Tanglha range of southeast Tibet. Look for snowcaps above dark, steep valleys where Tibet drops toward forest.

name: Nerpichye Lake
blurb: Kamchatka's largest lake, a lagoon joined to the sea near the mouth of the Kamchatka River. Its name means seal lake, after the seals that swim in. Look for a broad water body just behind the coast.

name: New Orleans
blurb: The Crescent City wraps around a tight bend of the Mississippi, and much of it sits below sea level behind levees. Look for the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway, nearly 24 miles of bridge running straight over open water.

name: Ng'iro
blurb: A summit in the Ndoto and Mathews ranges of northern Kenya, forested mountains rising from dry Samburu country. Look for a green massif standing out against tan scrubland.

name: Ngoring Lake
blurb: One of two large lakes near the source of the Yellow River, at about 14,000 ft on the Tibetan Plateau. Look for a broad blue lake in rolling brown grassland, its twin Gyaring Lake just to the west.

name: Niepce Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Danco Coast of the Antarctic Peninsula, named for photography pioneer Nicéphore Niépce. Many features here honor photography pioneers. Look for ice tumbling to the sea between steep peaks.

name: Nimrod Glacier
blurb: Named for Shackleton's ship on the 1907 to 1909 expedition that came within 112 miles of the Pole. It cuts through the Transantarctic Mountains to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for a broad ice river between ranges.

name: Ninnis Glacier
blurb: Named for Belgrave Ninnis, who fell into a crevasse with a sledge and dogs on Mawson's 1912 expedition. Its floating tongue juts into the sea. Look for a long ice tongue off the George V Coast.

name: Nissum Fjord
blurb: A shallow lagoon on Jutland's North Sea coast, closed off from the sea by a thin line of dunes. Look for a sluice cutting through the sand barrier at Thorsminde.

name: Nordvestfjord
blurb: The longest branch of Scoresby Sound, reaching deep inland toward the ice sheet. Look for a deep corridor lined with huge icebergs.

name: Norfolk Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains, deep in the Transantarctic range. Look for ice between bare rock summits.

name: North Caribou Lake
blurb: A large lake in remote northwestern Ontario, far from any year-round road. Look for wide open water edged by a jigsaw of bays and islands in unbroken boreal forest.

name: North Schell Peak
blurb: At about 11,900 ft, highest peak in the Schell Creek Range, above Ely. Look for a long, high ridge often snowy into early summer.

name: Northern Velebit National Park
blurb: Bare limestone ridges over the Adriatic, riddled with some of the deepest caves in the world. Look for pale karst crests on the mainland just across from the island of Rab.

name: Norton Sound
blurb: An inlet of the Bering Sea with Nome on its northern shore, where the Iditarod sled race finishes and gold was once panned straight from the beach. Look for a wide bay with flat tundra shores, frozen much of the year.

name: Norway Glacier
blurb: A glacier high in the Queen Maud Mountains near the polar plateau, in country Amundsen crossed on his 1911 race to the Pole. Look for ice flowing between high peaks.

name: Nuup Kangerlua
blurb: The fjord system beside Nuuk, Greenland's capital, branching about 100 miles toward the ice sheet. Look for Nuuk's colorful houses at the mouth and the steep Sermitsiaq peak nearby.

name: Nyungwe Forest
blurb: Mountain rainforest in southwest Rwanda, one of the largest left in the highlands of East Africa, with chimpanzees and a canopy walkway. Its streams include a contender for the Nile's most distant source. Look for dark canopy ringed by tea plantations.

name: Obuyi Lake
blurb: A remote lake in far northern Manitoba, close to the tree line. Look for a lake among thin spruce forest, bog and countless smaller ponds, frozen white much of the year.

name: Odense Fjord
blurb: A shallow, nearly enclosed fjord on Funen's north coast, leading up to Hans Christian Andersen's hometown. Look for a broad inlet with a narrow mouth and marshy edges.

name: Odzala National Park
blurb: Founded in 1935, one of Africa's oldest parks, with dense populations of western lowland gorillas and forest elephants. Look for rainforest broken by bais, open marshy clearings where animals gather.

name: Ofotfjorden
blurb: Narvik sits on this fjord, shipping Swedish iron ore year-round because the water never freezes. In 1940 it saw major naval battles. Look for a long fjord with steep mountains, a big suspension bridge, and the ore terminal at Narvik.

name: Okanagan Lake
blurb: About 84 miles long, in a dry valley of orchards and vineyards, and supposedly home to the lake monster Ogopogo. Look for Kelowna's floating bridge crossing the middle.

name: Okstindbreen
blurb: An ice cap around Oksskolten, the highest peak in northern Norway. Look for a white field among dark, rugged peaks and lakes.

name: Omo National Park
blurb: Remote wilderness on the Omo River near Kibish, where some of the oldest known Homo sapiens fossils were found. Look for the brown river winding south toward Lake Turkana.

name: Orel
blurb: A large lake in the lower Amur valley, close to where the river nears the Pacific. Look for a broad lake next to the river's winding channels, surrounded by forest and marsh.

name: Oulujärvi
blurb: One of Finland's largest lakes, in the Kainuu region near Kajaani, known for sandy beaches. Look for a big open lake with a long peninsula reaching into it.

name: Oxford Lake
blurb: A long lake on the Hayes River, the old fur-trade canoe route to Hudson Bay, beside the community of Oxford House. Look for a winding, island-dotted lake in boreal forest.

name: Palo Duro Canyon
blurb: The second-largest canyon in the US, about 120 miles long and up to 800 ft deep, cut into the flat Texas Panhandle. Look for red and orange striped walls breaking an otherwise table-flat plain.

name: Pangaion
blurb: About 6,420 ft in eastern Macedonia, Greece. Its gold and silver mines helped fund Philip II and Alexander the Great. Look for a lone massif rising between the Strymon plain and the sea near Kavala.

name: Pankisi Gorge
blurb: A valley of the Alazani River in the foothills of the Greater Caucasus, home mainly to the Kist community. Look for the river valley opening south out of high, forested mountains.

name: Paoay Lake National Park
blurb: A small lake in Ilocos Norte near Paoay's UNESCO-listed baroque church. Local legend says a village sank beneath its waters. Look for a compact oval of water among farmland and low hills.

name: Paparoa National Park
blurb: Limestone country on the South Island's west coast, best known for the Pancake Rocks at Punakaiki, layered stacks where blowholes spout in big swells. Look for the Paparoa Range running parallel to a wild surf coast.

name: Pastra Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Trinity Peninsula at the northern tip of the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for ice reaching the sea between rocky ridges.

name: Patkhor Peak
blurb: About 20,000 ft, the highest peak of the Rushan range in the western Pamirs. Look for a glaciated summit above the Bartang and Gunt valleys.

name: Peale Inlet
blurb: An ice-filled inlet on the coast of West Antarctica facing the Amundsen and Bellingshausen seas. Look for flat shelf ice and sea ice running out from a coast of buried mountains.

name: Peckham Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains. Look for a ribbon of ice between dark peaks.

name: Peleaga
blurb: At 8,232 ft, the highest peak of Romania's Retezat Mountains, a range famous for more than 50 glacial lakes. Look for rocky summits ringed by small blue tarns.

name: Pendjari National Park
blurb: Part of the W-Arly-Pendjari complex, West Africa's last stronghold for lions and elephants. Look for savanna along the Pendjari River below the Atakora cliffs.

name: Peneda-Gerês National Park
blurb: Portugal's only national park, granite mountains along the Spanish border with reservoirs filling the valleys. Look for bare gray granite peaks and long blue dammed lakes.

name: Periyar National Park
blurb: A lake formed by the Mullaperiyar Dam in 1895 wraps through forested hills in the Western Ghats. Look for its drowned valleys with dead tree stumps poking out.

name: Peter Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land. Look for ice flowing past rocky nunataks toward the coast.

name: Petermann Glacier
blurb: In 2010 it calved an ice island of about 100 square miles, roughly four times Manhattan. Its long floating tongue runs down a fjord. Look for the narrow ice tongue between high cliffs.

name: Philippi Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Wilhelm II Coast of East Antarctica, named for a German expedition scientist. Look for crevassed ice reaching the sea.

name: Phnom Aural
blurb: At about 5,950 ft the highest point in Cambodia, in the Cardamom Mountains region southwest of Phnom Penh. Look for a forested mountain rising above flat rice country.

name: Phoenix
blurb: A desert metro of about 5 million, mostly low and spread across a near-perfect street grid. Look for green lawns and blue pools against brown desert, and mountain islands like Camelback rising from the sprawl.

name: Phou Khe
blurb: A high point in the mountains of northern Laos near the Thai border. Look for forested ridges, often patched with slash-and-burn clearings.

name: Phu Luong
blurb: One of the forested limestone and granite highs of northwest Vietnam's Hoa Binh and Son La uplands. Look for green ridges with terraced valleys and cloud often caught on the summit.

name: Phu Si Lung
blurb: A peak right on the Vietnam-China border in Lai Chau, among the highest in Vietnam at about 10,000 ft. Look for a jagged, forested crest above the deep gorges of the Da River country.

name: Phu Soi Dao
blurb: About 6,900 ft on the Thailand-Laos border, with a pine savanna on top unusual for Thailand. Look for a forested ridge with grassy, open patches on the crest.

name: Phu Xai Lai Leng
blurb: Among the highest points of the Truong Son range on the Laos-Vietnam border, at about 8,900 ft. Look for a dark, steep jungle summit standing well above the surrounding ridges.

name: Piché Lake
blurb: One of the many lakes in the boreal forest of northeastern Alberta. Look for a patch of dark water among the spruce and muskeg.

name: Pico Almanzor
blurb: At 8,504 ft, the highest peak of the Sierra de Gredos and of central Spain. Look for a granite spire above a glacial cirque holding a small lake, the Laguna Grande de Gredos.

name: Pico Ruivo
blurb: Madeira's highest point at 6,109 ft, linked by a ridge trail to Pico do Arieiro. The summit often pokes out above a sea of clouds; look for sharp volcanic ridges and deep green ravines below.

name: Pico Turquino
blurb: Cuba's highest point at about 6,470 ft, in the Sierra Maestra where Castro's rebels hid in the 1950s. A bronze bust of José Martí stands on the summit. Look for the forested ridge rising straight off the south coast.

name: Picó Bernat
blurb: A summit in the Pre-Pyrenees of Catalonia, the limestone ranges that rise between the Ebro plains and the high Pyrenees. Look for long pale escarpments above farmland and gorges.

name: Pielinen
blurb: A large lake in eastern Finland overlooked by the hills of Koli, whose view inspired Finland's national romantic painters. Look for a long lake with dark wooded hills on its western shore.

name: Pieljekaise National Park
blurb: A mountain birch forest and low fells near Arjeplog in Swedish Lapland, with the Kungsleden hiking trail running through it. Look for the bare summit rising above the lakes.

name: Pihlajavesi
blurb: Part of Lake Saimaa near Savonlinna, a maze of islands and a stronghold of the rare Saimaa ringed seal. Look for the medieval Olavinlinna castle on an island in the city.

name: Pik Lyavirdyr
blurb: A glaciated peak in the eastern Pamir near the Tajikistan-China border. Look for snowfields and glacier tongues above the high, treeless valleys of the Tashkurgan region.

name: Pik Sovetskikh Ofitserov
blurb: A high summit of the eastern Pamirs, where the mountains rise from a cold, dry plateau above 12,000 ft. Look for glaciers on the peaks and pale, treeless basins in between.

name: Pilot Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land flowing toward the Ross Sea. Look for ice between jagged coastal peaks.

name: Pindus National Park
blurb: Valia Kalda in the northern Pindus, beech and black pine forests that shelter brown bears and wolves. Look for forested mountains and bare limestone peaks west of Grevena.

name: Pinehouse Lake
blurb: A lake on the Churchill River system in northern Saskatchewan, beside the community of Pinehouse. Look for an irregular body of water in flat boreal forest dotted with bogs.

name: Pinnacles National Park
blurb: Volcanic spires that formed about 195 miles to the south and rode the San Andreas Fault north. California condors fly here. Look for the jagged rock outcrops.

name: Pittsburgh
blurb: At the Point, the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet to form the Ohio. The City of Bridges counts over 400 of them; look for the triangle of downtown between the rivers.

name: Playgreen Lake
blurb: The lake at Lake Winnipeg's northern outlet, where the Nelson River begins its run to Hudson Bay. Look for a maze of channels and islands at the big lake's top end, near Norway House.

name: Podyjí National Park
blurb: The Iron Curtain ran along this stretch of the Dyje River, which kept its canyon untouched. Look for the river making tight forested loops along the Austrian border.

name: Point Lake
blurb: A long lake at the head of the Coppermine River in the barren lands. Look for a narrow, winding lake in open tundra dotted with smaller ponds, frozen most of the year.

name: Pollino
blurb: A summit of about 7,380 ft at the heart of Pollino National Park, the largest national park in Italy, known for ancient Bosnian pines clinging to the ridges. Look for bare limestone tops above beech forest.

name: Poloniny National Park
blurb: Slovakia's easternmost park, at the Polish and Ukrainian borders, with ancient beech forests that are part of a World Heritage site. Look for rolling wooded hills topped by open grassy ridges called poloniny.

name: Port-Cros National Park
blurb: One of Europe's first marine national parks, created in 1963 around a small hilly island off Hyères. Look for the forested island just east of the bigger Porquerolles.

name: Porta Westfalica
blurb: The Weser cuts a gap through the ridge between the Wiehen and Weser Hills, the gateway into the North German Plain. Look for the giant Kaiser Wilhelm Monument on the slope above the river.

name: Portage Glacier
blurb: Its visitor center opened in 1986 looking straight at the ice; the glacier has since retreated out of view around a bend at the far end of Portage Lake. Look for the lake south of Turnagain Arm.

name: Portnyagino Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the high Arctic of the Taymyr Peninsula, frozen most of the year. Look for a lake in bare tundra crowded with smaller ponds and meandering streams.

name: Pothigai Hill
blurb: A sacred peak of the southern Western Ghats, linked in Tamil tradition to the sage Agastya and source of the Thamirabarani River. Look for forested ridges rising steeply from the plains of southern Tamil Nadu.

name: Poulter Glacier
blurb: A glacier draining from the polar plateau through the Queen Maud Mountains toward the Ross Ice Shelf, only a few hundred miles from the Pole. Look for ice between bare peaks.

name: Presidente Ríos Lake
blurb: A lake deep in the Taitao Peninsula in Chilean Patagonia, one of the wettest and least visited corners of the country. Look for dark water among forested hills and coast.

name: Prince Edward Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Elizabeth Range of the Transantarctic Mountains. Look for ice flowing between high rock walls.

name: Providence
blurb: Founded in 1636 by Roger Williams, one of the oldest cities in the US. Look for the white marble dome of the Rhode Island State House, among the largest self-supporting marble domes in the world, at the head of Narragansett Bay.

name: Pryor Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Victoria Land's coastal ranges. Look for ice spilling between dark peaks toward the sea.

name: Pukeashun Mountain
blurb: A peak in the Shuswap Highlands of interior BC, north of Shuswap Lake. Look for a bald summit above forested hills.

name: Pulicat Lake
blurb: India's second-largest brackish lagoon, behind Chilika. The barrier island separating it from the Bay of Bengal is Sriharikota, where India launches its rockets. Look for the launch pads on that long sandy strip.

name: Punta La Marmora
blurb: Sardinia's highest point at about 6,020 ft, in the Gennargentu massif. Look for a bare, rounded granite and schist crest in the island's rugged east-central interior.

name: Puula
blurb: A large lake in southern Finland's lake district, near Mikkeli. Look for open water broken by islands and forested peninsulas.

name: Pyaozero
blurb: A big, irregular lake in northern Karelia near the Arctic Circle, dammed for hydropower. Look for a maze of bays and islands in dark forest, usually frozen white for half the year.

name: Pyasino
blurb: A big tundra lake just north of Norilsk. In 2020 a diesel spill from a Norilsk power plant ran down the rivers into it, one of the worst in the Arctic. Look for a broad lake in flat tundra.

name: Pyramid Lake
blurb: A desert lake with no outlet, a remnant of ice-age Lake Lahontan, named for a pyramid-shaped tufa island. Look for an intense blue lake in bare brown mountains, with pale tufa rocks along the shore.

name: Pyrénées National Park
blurb: Home of the Cirque de Gavarnie, a mile-wide rock amphitheater where the Grande Cascade falls about 1,400 ft, one of Europe's tallest. Look for the curved wall of cliffs on the Spanish border.

name: Qamanirjuaq Lake
blurb: The Qamanirjuaq caribou herd, one of the biggest in northern Canada, takes its name from this lake and calves on the tundra around it. Look for a long, branching lake in a treeless plain.

name: Qiandao Lake
blurb: Its name means Thousand Island Lake, and it has over 1,000: hilltops left above water when the Xin'anjiang Dam flooded the valley in 1959. The ancient Lion City lies intact underwater. Look for a maze of green islands.

name: Quar Ice Shelf
blurb: A small floating ice shelf on the Princess Martha Coast of Dronning Maud Land. Look for flat ice ending in a cliff against the sea.

name: Quissama National Park
blurb: Savanna, coast and Kwanza River just south of Luanda, restocked with elephants trucked in from Botswana and South Africa in the 2000s. Look for the river mouth and coastal cliffs.

name: Quttinirpaaq National Park
blurb: Canada's northernmost park, on Ellesmere Island about 500 miles from the North Pole. It holds Barbeau Peak, at about 8,600 ft the highest point in eastern North America, rising out of ice caps.

name: Rainy Lake
blurb: Straddling the Minnesota-Ontario border, it forms much of Voyageurs National Park, with International Falls at its outlet. Look for a maze of rocky, pine-covered islands and long bays.

name: Rakiura National Park
blurb: Covers about 85 percent of Stewart Island, New Zealand's third-largest island, where kiwi sometimes forage on the beaches. Look for a rugged forested island across Foveaux Strait, its coast cut by deep inlets.

name: Rameau Inlet
blurb: An inlet on Alexander Island, Antarctica, named after the composer Jean-Philippe Rameau like the Beethoven and Mozart features nearby. Look for shelf ice framed by snowy ridges.

name: Ramsey Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains flowing to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for ice between bare peaks.

name: Ranomafana National Park
blurb: Rainforest where the golden bamboo lemur was discovered in 1986. Look for forested hills along a whitewater river in eastern Madagascar.

name: Ranthambore National Park
blurb: Famous for tigers seen in daylight and for Ranthambore Fort, a hilltop fort about a thousand years old inside the park. Look for rocky ridges and lakes where the Aravalli and Vindhya hills meet.

name: Rao Co
blurb: A peak on the Annamite spine along the Laos-Vietnam border in Ha Tinh province, nearly 7,000 ft. Look for unbroken forest ridges running north to south between the coastal plain and Laos.

name: Rapa Nui National Park
blurb: Easter Island, home to nearly 900 moai carved by the Rapa Nui. Look for the volcanic island and the crater lake of Rano Kau at its southwest corner.

name: Ras Muhammad National Park
blurb: The southern tip of Sinai, where the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba meet. Look for the pointed headland with bright coral reefs tracing its edge in the Red Sea.

name: Recovery Glacier
blurb: One of the longest glaciers in Antarctica, carrying ice hundreds of miles into the Filchner Ice Shelf, with large subglacial lakes under its head. Look for a broad, faintly striped ice river.

name: Redwood National Park
blurb: The tallest trees on Earth, including Hyperion, about 380 ft. Look for dark forest running down to the coast.

name: Reedy Glacier
blurb: A large glacier draining the West Antarctic ice sheet through the Transantarctic Mountains to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for a wide ice river between rock walls.

name: Rennick Glacier
blurb: One of the largest glaciers in Victoria Land, flowing north to the coast facing the Southern Ocean. Look for a broad river of ice between mountain ranges.

name: Repparfjorden
blurb: An Arctic fjord in Finnmark near Hammerfest, the focus of a long fight over a planned copper mine dumping waste into it. Look for low, bare shores around a wide inlet.

name: Reynolds Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land, West Antarctica. Expect white ice with flow lines heading toward the Ross Ice Shelf.

name: Reyðarfjörður
blurb: The largest fjord in eastern Iceland, home to a big aluminum smelter powered by the Kárahnjúkar dam. Look for the long gray smelter buildings on the shore.

name: Rhine Gorge
blurb: About 40 miles of river between Bingen and Koblenz lined with castles and terraced vineyards, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for the tight bend at the Lorelei rock, where the Rhine is at its narrowest.

name: Richter Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Marie Byrd Land, West Antarctica. Expect white ice with faint flow lines and occasional nunataks.

name: Riley Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula flowing into George VI Sound. Look for ice meeting the long channel between the Peninsula and Alexander Island.

name: Risnjak National Park
blurb: Named for the lynx (ris in Croatian), these dense fir and beech forests rise just behind Rijeka. Look for dark, unbroken forest on the ridges north of the city.

name: Roman-Kosh
blurb: About 5,070 ft, the highest point of Crimea, on a flat limestone plateau above the resort coast near Yalta. Look for a broad bald plateau dropping in steep cliffs toward the Black Sea.

name: Rondane National Park
blurb: Norway's first national park, created in 1962, and a refuge for wild reindeer. Look for a cluster of bare gray-brown peaks over 6,500 ft separated by deep cirques, rising from lichen-pale plateaus.

name: Ruaha National Park
blurb: One of Tanzania's largest parks, known for big elephant herds, baobabs and lions along the Great Ruaha River. Look for the sandy river channel cutting through dry bush.

name: Rugged Mountain
blurb: A jagged, glaciated peak on northern Vancouver Island, living up to its name above Nootka Sound country. Look for sharp rock teeth with small glaciers.

name: Ruinaulta
blurb: The Swiss Grand Canyon: the young Rhine cut this gorge through debris of the Flims rockslide, the largest known landslide in the Alps, about 10,000 years ago. Look for white cliffs and a green river below.

name: Rutford Ice Stream
blurb: A fast ice stream running beside the Ellsworth Mountains, home to Vinson Massif, Antarctica's highest peak. It flows into the Ronne Ice Shelf. Look for a smooth band of ice below the dark range.

name: Réservoir aux Outardes 4
blurb: A reservoir on the Outardes River, part of the Manicouagan-Outardes hydro complex on Québec's North Shore. Look for flooded valleys forming a branching lake in hilly forest.

name: Rāzna National Park
blurb: Lake Rāzna, Latvia's second-largest lake, called the sea of Latgale. Look for a broad open lake dotted with small islands in rolling farm and forest country.

name: Sabine Lake
blurb: A shallow estuary straddling the Texas-Louisiana line where the Sabine and Neches rivers meet the Gulf. Look for the refineries and ship channel of Port Arthur along its west shore.

name: Sahand
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 12,160 ft south of Tabriz. Its slopes hold the cliff village of Kandovan, where homes are carved into rock cones. Look for a broad, snow-topped massif.

name: Sahuasiray
blurb: About 19,000 ft, one of the glaciated summits of the Urubamba range that walls the north side of the Sacred Valley of the Incas. Look for a line of white peaks above the green valley floor.

name: Saint Lawrence River
blurb: Quebec City's name comes from an Algonquin word meaning "where the river narrows," and here it does, before widening into a vast estuary. Look for the walled old city on its cliff and the long Île d'Orléans just downstream.

name: Saint Petersburg
blurb: Founded by Peter the Great in 1703 on the marshy Neva delta and built across dozens of islands linked by canals. Look for the wide Neva splitting the city and the gold spire of the Peter and Paul Fortress.

name: Saipal
blurb: Western Nepal's second-highest peak, about 23,000 ft, rising in a remote part of the far west. Look for a big white summit above deep gorges.

name: Saloum Delta National Park
blurb: Mangrove islands and channels where the Saloum River meets the Atlantic, dotted with ancient shell mounds piled up by fishing communities over centuries. Look for a maze of brown creeks and green mangrove south of Dakar.

name: Salto Grande reservoir
blurb: Built jointly by Argentina and Uruguay in the 1970s on the Uruguay River, which forms the border between them. Look for a long, branching lake with the dam near Concordia and Salto.

name: San Antonio
blurb: Home of the Alamo and the River Walk. Look for the Tower of the Americas downtown and the old Spanish missions strung along the San Antonio River to the south.

name: San Diego
blurb: Wrapped around a deep natural harbor, home of much of the Navy's Pacific Fleet. Look for aircraft carriers docked at North Island, the curving Coronado Bridge, and the bulging green Point Loma peninsula.

name: San Martín Glacier
blurb: A glacier near the Filchner Ice Shelf, named by Argentine expeditions after José de San Martín. Expect broad white ice with flow lines.

name: Sandsfjord
blurb: A fjord in the Ryfylke region northeast of Stavanger, where the Suldal salmon river meets the sea at Sand. Look for a narrow arm between steep mountains and a small village at the river mouth.

name: Sandy Lake
blurb: A large lake in Ontario's far northwest, home to the Sandy Lake First Nation, connected to the outside mostly by air and winter road. Look for open water ringed by dark spruce forest.

name: Sangpang Bum
blurb: A remote peak in northern Myanmar near the Indian border, in the Patkai region. Look for steep, forested ridges with no roads.

name: Sardinia coast (Costa Smeralda)
blurb: Sardinia's Emerald Coast, developed from the 1960s by the Aga Khan into a yachting playground. Look for granite headlands, coves of turquoise water and the Maddalena islands just north.

name: Sarek National Park
blurb: Often called Europe's last wilderness: no roads, no huts to speak of, about 100 glaciers and some of Sweden's highest peaks. Look for the Rapa Valley, where a glacial river braids into a green delta.

name: Sayram Lake
blurb: An alpine lake at about 6,800 ft in the Tian Shan, called 'the last tear of the Atlantic' because it's said to be the farthest point Atlantic moisture reaches. Look for an oval of deep blue in a green mountain basin.

name: Schytt Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land flowing toward the Fimbul Ice Shelf. Look for ice moving past rocky peaks.

name: Scott Glacier
blurb: One of the great outlet glaciers of the Transantarctic Mountains, carrying ice from the polar plateau to the Ross Ice Shelf, named for Robert Falcon Scott. Look for a broad ice river between towering peaks.

name: Sebkha Sidi El Hani
blurb: A broad salt flat inland from Sousse in central Tunisia, often dry and sometimes holding a sheet of shallow water. Look for a pale, flat basin among olive groves.

name: Sebkha d'Oran
blurb: A big salt lake just south of Oran, often visible on approach to the city's airport. Look for a long white or pinkish flat stretching between hills, dry for much of the year.

name: Sedona red rocks
blurb: Red sandstone buttes and spires rising above green juniper and pine below the Mogollon Rim. Look for Cathedral Rock and Bell Rock glowing orange in low sun against dark green.

name: Segozero
blurb: One of Karelia's larger lakes, raised by a dam for hydropower. Look for a broad sheet of water among the endless forest and smaller glacial lakes of the region.

name: Selja Gorges
blurb: A deep, narrow gorge near the phosphate town of Metlaoui, where the old Lezard Rouge train winds along the cliffs. Look for the dark cut through bare tan desert ridges.

name: Selwyn Lake
blurb: A remote lake sitting on the Saskatchewan-Northwest Territories border, near where the boreal forest thins toward tundra. Look for a long lake among bare rock and scattered spruce.

name: Sendai
blurb: The City of Trees, with tree-lined avenues. The 2011 tsunami swept miles inland across the plain east of the city and flooded Sendai Airport. Look for the flat coast where the water came ashore.

name: Serra Imeri
blurb: A remote mountain range along the Brazil-Venezuela border in the Amazon, near Pico da Neblina, Brazil's highest point. Look for forested ridges and clouds rising out of flat rainforest.

name: Serra de Santa Bárbara
blurb: The highest point on Terceira in the Azores, a large volcano with a summit caldera full of peat bogs and small lakes. Look for the high western end of the island, often under cloud.

name: Sevier Lake
blurb: A terminal lake in western Utah that is usually bone dry, because the Sevier River is diverted for irrigation before reaching it. Look for a large white playa in a desert basin.

name: Seweweekspoortpiek
blurb: The highest peak in South Africa's Western Cape at 7,628 ft, named for the Seweweekspoort, a narrow gorge through the Swartberg range. Look for folded sandstone ridges above the dry Karoo.

name: Shabica Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's east coast, draining toward the Weddell Sea. Look for crevassed ice heading to a shelf edge.

name: Shaiyb al-Banat
blurb: About 7,200 ft, the highest peak of Egypt's Eastern Desert, a jagged granite mass in the Red Sea Hills west of Hurghada. Look for dark, bare rock rising between dry wadis with no green at all.

name: Sharktooth Mountain
blurb: A sharp peak in the remote Cassiar Mountains of northern BC. Look for a pointed rock summit among rolling, sparsely forested ranges.

name: Shedin Peak
blurb: A summit in the Skeena Mountains of northern BC, in roadless country north of Hazelton. Look for snowy ridges above wide forested valleys.

name: Shenandoah National Park
blurb: A long, narrow park along the crest of the Blue Ridge, with the 105-mile Skyline Drive running its whole length. Look for the forested ridge with farmland of the Shenandoah Valley to the west.

name: Shinnan Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Prince Olav Coast of East Antarctica, named by Japanese expeditions. Look for ice meeting fast ice and sea.

name: Shirase Glacier
blurb: One of the fastest-moving glaciers in Antarctica, pouring into Lützow-Holm Bay. Named for Nobu Shirase, who led Japan's first Antarctic expedition in 1910. Look for a heavily crevassed ice river reaching the sea.

name: Shirvan National Park
blurb: Semi-desert south of Baku protecting goitered gazelles. Look for flat tan plains near the Caspian shore.

name: Shivasagar lake
blurb: The reservoir behind the Koyna Dam, winding for miles through the steep Western Ghats. Look for a long, narrow lake following the valley floor between forested ridges.

name: Sibiloi National Park
blurb: On the east shore of Lake Turkana, home of Koobi Fora, where fossils of early humans have been found for decades. Look for the jade-green lake against bare desert.

name: Sierra Blanca Peak
blurb: At about 12,000 ft, rising nearly 8,000 ft above the Tularosa Basin, sacred to the Mescalero Apache. Look for its snowy top above White Sands' white dunes to the west.

name: Sierra La Madera
blurb: A desert range in central Coahuila, rising high enough to carry pine and oak forest above the Chihuahuan Desert. Look for darker green slopes above pale, dry basins.

name: Sierra de las Quijadas National Park
blurb: A red sandstone amphitheater, the Potrero de la Aguada, where pterosaur and dinosaur fossils have been found. Look for the eroded red bowl in dry scrubland.

name: Sila National Park
blurb: The high Sila plateau in Calabria, covered in tall laricio pines and dotted with reservoirs. Look for big lakes like Arvo and Cecita in dark forest on top of the mountains.

name: Siletiteniz
blurb: A shallow salt lake on the flat plains of northern Kazakhstan. Look for a pale, irregular lake with white salt margins in otherwise featureless grassland and farmland.

name: Silisili
blurb: Samoa's highest point at 6,096 ft, on the volcanic island of Savai'i, whose summit is a field of young cones in the cloud forest. Look for a broad shield of an island with dark lava flows reaching the coast.

name: Silk Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains. Look for a ribbon of ice between dark peaks.

name: Silvertip Mountain
blurb: A peak of over 8,000 ft near the US border southeast of Hope, above the Skagit Valley. Look for a pale rocky summit among the jagged North Cascades.

name: Siple Dome
blurb: A broad ice dome between two ice streams in West Antarctica, where scientists drilled a core over 3,000 ft deep. From above it's a gentle white swell with no landmarks at all.

name: Skagafjörður
blurb: A broad fjord in north Iceland known for horse breeding, with islands such as Drangey, a sheer-sided rock rising out of the bay. Look for the wide green valley at its head.

name: Slava Ice Shelf
blurb: A small ice shelf on the George V Coast of East Antarctica. Look for flat floating ice meeting sea ice.

name: Sleeping Bear Dunes
blurb: Sand dunes perched on bluffs rising about 450 ft above Lake Michigan. Named for an Ojibwe legend of a mother bear waiting for her drowned cubs, now the Manitou Islands. Look for tan bluffs against blue water.

name: Slessor Glacier
blurb: A major glacier carrying ice into the Filchner Ice Shelf beside the Shackleton Range. Look for a wide, faintly striped ice river with dark ridges along one side.

name: Slovak Karst National Park
blurb: Limestone plateaus riddled with caves that continue under the Hungarian border, including Domica. Look for flat karst tablelands broken by the deep, narrow Zádiel gorge.

name: Slītere National Park
blurb: Cape Kolka, where the Gulf of Riga meets the open Baltic, and the old Livonian fishing coast. Look for the sharp sandy point and the ripple of waves where two seas meet.

name: Snedeker Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Knox Coast of Wilkes Land, East Antarctica. Look for ice reaching the sea in a jagged front.

name: Snowbird Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the southeast Northwest Territories near the Nunavut border, at the edge of the tree line. Look for a ragged lake among spruce, rock and smaller ponds.

name: Snowdonia
blurb: Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa) is the highest mountain in Wales at 3,560 ft, and a rack railway runs to the summit. Look for glacier-carved valleys, dark lakes and slate quarries cut into the hillsides.

name: Sonfjället National Park
blurb: One of Sweden's oldest national parks, set aside in 1909 around a solitary bare-topped mountain in Härjedalen known for its brown bears. Look for the rounded massif standing alone above the forest.

name: Songhua Lake
blurb: A long, winding reservoir behind the Fengman Dam on the Songhua River, upstream of Jilin City. Look for a narrow lake snaking for miles through forested hills, frozen white in the northeast Chinese winter.

name: Souapiti Reservoir
blurb: A new reservoir formed by a Chinese-built hydroelectric dam on the Konkouré River in Guinea, filled around 2020. Look for flooded valleys in green hills.

name: Souchez Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains near the polar plateau. Look for ice between bare peaks.

name: South Henik Lake
blurb: A long tundra lake in Nunavut's Kivalliq region, just north of the tree line. Look for a narrow sweep of water threaded through bare, glacier-scraped rock and smaller ponds.

name: South Luangwa National Park
blurb: Where the walking safari was born, along a Luangwa River full of hippos and looping oxbow lagoons. Look for the meandering river and the crescent-shaped old channels beside it.

name: Soviet Constitution Peak
blurb: A Tian Shan summit east of Lake Issyk-Kul, one of many peaks given Soviet-era names. Look for glaciated ridges south of the lake's eastern end.

name: Stancomb-Wills Glacier
blurb: A big glacier on the Caird Coast whose floating tongue runs well out into the Weddell Sea, next to the Brunt Ice Shelf. Look for a long ice tongue edged by sea ice.

name: Storfjorden
blurb: A broad Arctic sound separating Spitsbergen from the islands of Edgeøya and Barentsøya, often clogged with sea ice. Look for a wide channel between glaciated coasts.

name: Storsjön
blurb: A big lake in central Sweden with the city of Östersund on its shore, famous locally for a legendary lake monster. Look for a branching lake with islands among forest and farmland.

name: Stravinsky Inlet
blurb: An ice-filled inlet on Alexander Island, Antarctica, named after Igor Stravinsky, one of dozens of composer place names there. Look for flat white shelf ice between ice-covered headlands.

name: Strom Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains flowing to the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for ice between bare peaks.

name: Stuart Lake
blurb: A lake in central British Columbia where Fort St. James was founded as a fur trading post in 1806. Look for a long lake with the town at its southeast tip.

name: Sudochye lake
blurb: A cluster of shallow, reedy lakes on the old Amu Darya delta, near what used to be the Aral Sea's southwest shore. Look for patchy water ringed by salt flats and dry former seabed.

name: Sulak Canyon
blurb: Often called the deepest canyon in Europe, roughly 6,000 ft at its deepest, which is deeper than the Grand Canyon. Look for the turquoise Chirkey reservoir, dammed in the middle of the canyon system.

name: Sumidero Canyon
blurb: Walls up to about 3,300 ft tall rise straight from the Grijalva River near Tuxtla Gutiérrez, deep enough to appear on the Chiapas state seal. Look for the dark cleft ending at a dam and reservoir.

name: Sunfix Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Antarctic Peninsula's east coast. Look for ice draining off the Peninsula's spine toward the Weddell Sea.

name: Sunset Peak
blurb: A peak of the Pir Panjal range south of the Kashmir Valley, around 15,500 ft. Look for snowy crests forming the wall between the valley and the plains of Jammu.

name: Support Force Glacier
blurb: A major glacier feeding the Filchner Ice Shelf, named for the US Navy support force behind Antarctic research flights. Look for a broad ice river with faint flow stripes.

name: Sutai Mountain
blurb: A glaciated peak on the Mongolian Altai near the Chinese border. Look for permanent snow above deep valleys and sweeping, treeless plains.

name: Sutjeska National Park
blurb: Holds Perućica, one of Europe's last primeval forests, and Maglić, Bosnia's highest peak at about 7,800 ft. Look for deep forested gorges and high bare ridges.

name: Suur-Längelmävesi
blurb: A lake in Finland's Pirkanmaa lake district east of Tampere. Look for long channels of water through forest and farmland.

name: Szczecin Lagoon
blurb: A large lagoon at the mouth of the Oder, split between Germany and Poland. Look for the island of Usedom separating it from the Baltic.

name: São Paulo
blurb: The largest city in the Southern Hemisphere, around 22 million people in the metro. Look for an unbroken sea of high-rise apartment towers to the horizon, cut by the Tietê and Pinheiros rivers and their riverside freeways.

name: Söderåsen National Park
blurb: A long ridge in Skåne cut by deep, steep-sided ravines under one of northern Europe's largest beech forests. Look for the dark, straight cleft of the main valley in the flat farmland.

name: Tablas de Daimiel National Park
blurb: A floodplain wetland where the Guadiana and Cigüela rivers meet, nearly dried out by groundwater pumping and hit by smoldering underground peat fires around 2009. Look for reed beds and pools in the flat farmland of La Mancha.

name: Tahiryuaq
blurb: One of the largest lakes on Victoria Island, deep in the Canadian Arctic, formerly called Ferguson Lake. It stays frozen most of the year; in summer look for dark water in a flat, barren landscape.

name: Taichung
blurb: Taiwan's second-largest city by population, on a broad basin between the Central Mountains and the coast. Look for the city grid filling the plain and Taichung Port's breakwaters on the coast.

name: Taipei
blurb: Sits in a basin ringed by mountains, including the volcanoes of Yangmingshan to the north. Look for Taipei 101, 1,667 ft tall and shaped like a stalk of bamboo, standing alone over the east side of the city.

name: Tajo del Almendrón
blurb: A summit in the limestone sierras above the Costa del Sol east of Málaga, where the mountains rise steeply from the Mediterranean. Look for pale, bare ridges above whitewashed villages and the coast.

name: Tama Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Prince Olav Coast, named by Japanese expeditions. Look for ice meeting fast ice and open water.

name: Tamatea / Dusky Sound
blurb: One of Fiordland's largest and most intricate fjords, full of islands. Captain Cook spent five weeks here in 1773 and brewed spruce beer against scurvy. Look for a long maze of inlets and wooded islands with no roads anywhere near.

name: Tampa
blurb: Set at the head of Tampa Bay, with Hillsborough Bay and Old Tampa Bay on either side of the Interbay Peninsula. Look for the long causeways and the Sunshine Skyway Bridge to the south.

name: Tanafjord
blurb: Where the Tana River, a great salmon river along the Finnish border, meets the Barents Sea. Look for a long Arctic fjord with bare tundra slopes and a sandy delta at its head.

name: Tangra Yumco
blurb: One of the holiest lakes of Tibet's Bon religion and one of the deepest on the plateau, at roughly 15,000 ft. Look for a long lake running north-south, with ancient beach terraces stepped high above the shore.

name: Tanquary Fiord
blurb: A fjord deep in northern Ellesmere Island, inside Quttinirpaaq National Park, about 600 miles from the North Pole. Look for a long inlet framed by glaciers and bare Arctic mountains, frozen most of the year.

name: Tarangire National Park
blurb: In the dry season elephants gather here in some of the largest herds in northern Tanzania, drawn to the Tarangire River. Look for the scattered giant baobabs dotting the savanna.

name: Taroko National Park
blurb: Named for a marble gorge carved by the Liwu River, with walls rising thousands of feet straight up. Look for the deep cleft cutting west from the coast into steep green mountains.

name: Tehek Lake
blurb: A tundra lake north of Baker Lake in Nunavut, hundreds of miles from any road. Look for a long, irregular body of water amid bare rock and a scatter of smaller ponds.

name: Tel Aviv
blurb: Founded in 1909 on sand dunes, it has thousands of white Bauhaus-style buildings, a UNESCO site called the White City. Look for the straight Mediterranean beachfront lined with hotels and the towers rising behind.

name: Tequila Volcano
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 9,600 ft above the town that gave tequila its name. Its slopes are covered in blue agave. Look for rows of blue-gray plants patterning the fields around the cone.

name: Teslin Lake
blurb: A long, narrow lake straddling the British Columbia-Yukon border. Look for the Alaska Highway running along its shore and crossing a long bridge at the village of Teslin.

name: The Broads
blurb: Lakes that are actually medieval peat pits that flooded, linked by about 125 miles of navigable rivers. Look for the lacework of water, reed beds and windmills across flat Norfolk.

name: Thudaka Peak
blurb: A summit in the Omineca Mountains of north-central BC, deep in roadless country. Look for bare rocky ridges above forest and lakes.

name: Tianmen Mountain
blurb: Famous for Heaven's Gate, a natural arch hundreds of feet tall through the cliff, reached by 999 steps and one of the longest cable cars in the world. Look for the hole through the mountain and the zigzag road below it.

name: Tidighin
blurb: The highest point of Morocco's Rif mountains at about 8,000 ft, above cedar forests near the Mediterranean coast. Look for a rocky crest, often snowy in winter, above green hills.

name: Tiewadian of Fenghuang Mountains
blurb: A summit of the Fenghuang Mountains in southern Shaanxi, part of the forested ranges between the Qinling and the Daba Shan. Look for steep green ridges above the Han River valley.

name: Tippecanoe Lake
blurb: The deepest natural lake in Indiana, a glacial lake in the state's northern lake country. Look for a small lake surrounded by cottages and farmland.

name: Titan Dome
blurb: A high ice dome between the Queen Maud Mountains and the South Pole, about 10,200 ft above sea level. From above, a vast featureless white surface with no landmarks at all.

name: Tjuvfjorden
blurb: A wide bay on the south side of Edgeøya in Svalbard, a remote polar bear stronghold. Look for low, ice-scoured coast and drifting sea ice in a broad inlet.

name: Toney Mountain
blurb: A long shield volcano in Marie Byrd Land, nearly 12,000 ft high and stretched dozens of miles along its crest, half buried by the West Antarctic Ice Sheet. Look for a low, elongated white ridge with little rock showing.

name: Tongshanjiabu
blurb: A glaciated peak of over 23,000 ft on the remote Bhutan-Tibet border, in a corner of the Himalaya that sees almost no climbers. Look for a white ridge above long valley glaciers.

name: Topo da Coroa
blurb: At 6,493 ft, the highest point on Santo Antão in Cabo Verde, a volcanic summit on the island's dry western side. Look for a bare brown cone above deeply cut ravines.

name: Topozero
blurb: A long lake in northern Karelia, one of thousands carved by the ice sheets. Look for a stretched-out lake full of islands amid unbroken taiga, frozen much of the year.

name: Tordoki Yani
blurb: A high point of the remote mountains of Khabarovsk Krai, in taiga country far from roads. Look for bare summits above endless dark forest.

name: Totten Glacier
blurb: Drains a basin holding enough ice to raise global sea levels by several feet, and warm ocean water is reaching under it. One of East Antarctica's biggest glaciers. Look for a wide ice stream ending in a floating tongue.

name: Tracy Arm
blurb: A deep, narrow fjord south of Juneau, about 30 miles long with granite walls rising thousands of feet. Look for floating ice and the twin Sawyer Glaciers at its head.

name: Tracy Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Knox Coast of East Antarctica. Look for ice reaching the sea in a jagged front.

name: Trakai Historical National Park
blurb: Trakai's red-brick castle sits on an island in Lake Galvė, a medieval seat of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania. Look for the red castle on its island west of Vilnius.

name: Trongisvágsfjørður
blurb: A fjord on Suðuroy, the southernmost of the Faroe Islands, cutting deep into the island's east side. Look for steep green slopes and villages around the water.

name: Trout Lake
blurb: A lake in the forested Precambrian Shield of northwestern Ontario near Red Lake. Look for its irregular arms and islands among the granite and spruce, one of thousands of lakes in this region.

name: Tsalka Canyon
blurb: A gorge cut into the volcanic plateau of southern Georgia, known for Dashbashi Canyon's waterfalls and a diamond-shaped glass building cantilevered over the drop. Look for the dark slot in the flat upland.

name: Tsambagarav
blurb: A broad ice-capped massif in the Mongolian Altai, standing alone above the steppe. Look for a white dome flanked by dark valleys and lakes.

name: Tsavo East National Park
blurb: Part of Tsavo, one of the largest parks in Africa, famous for red-dusted elephants and the man-eating lions of 1898. Look for the Yatta Plateau, an ancient lava flow running some 180 miles.

name: Tsaydaychuz Peak
blurb: A peak in the remote Coast Mountains of central BC, in the wilderness between the inlets and the interior plateau. Look for snow-streaked rock above forested valleys.

name: Tskaltsitela Gorge Natural Monument
blurb: A protected limestone gorge near Kutaisi; the river's name means red water. Look for the green cleft in the hills above the city in western Georgia's lowlands.

name: Tulemalu Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the barren lands of southern Nunavut, near the transition from taiga to open tundra. Look for a ragged outline of bays in a landscape of countless glacial ponds.

name: Tumucumaque National Park
blurb: One of the largest tropical forest parks in the world, about 15,000 square miles of untouched Amazon along the border with French Guiana and Suriname. Look for unbroken canopy to the horizon.

name: Tunulliarfik fjord
blurb: A fjord in South Greenland where Erik the Red founded his farm Brattahlíð around 985. Look for green pastures and sheep farms around Narsarsuaq airport at its head, with icebergs drifting in.

name: Tverregg Glacier
blurb: A glacier in Dronning Maud Land. Look for ice flowing past dark nunataks toward the coast.

name: Ubinskoye
blurb: A shallow lake on the flat West Siberian plain. Look for an irregular lake in marsh, birch woods and farmland, frozen white through the long winter.

name: Ulubey Canyon Nature Park
blurb: A long canyon system cut through soft rock on the Anatolian plateau near Uşak, its branching walls dropping several hundred feet below farmland. Look for the dendritic pattern of side gullies.

name: Uludağ
blurb: At 8,343 ft, the classical Mount Olympus of Mysia, now Turkey's best-known ski resort, rising directly above the city of Bursa. Look for a long, often snowy ridge with the city spread along its northern base.

name: Ulugh Muztagh
blurb: Close to 23,000 ft in the remote eastern Kunlun; early surveys put it far higher before a 1985 expedition measured it. Look for a solitary ice massif above the empty northern Tibetan Plateau.

name: Umboi Island
blurb: A volcanic island in the Vitiaz Strait between New Guinea and New Britain, rising to about 5,000 ft. Look for a green island with a rugged crest.

name: Umbozero
blurb: A long lake squeezed between the Khibiny and Lovozero mountain massifs on the Kola Peninsula. Look for a narrow north-south lake with bare, rounded mountains on both sides.

name: Una National Park
blurb: A park along the Una River, with cascades like Štrbački buk on the Croatian border. Look for the clear green river winding through wooded hills.

name: Underwater Lake
blurb: A remote lake in the forest and tundra of the central Northwest Territories, between Great Bear and Great Slave lakes. Look for an irregular lake among the countless lakes of the Canadian Shield.

name: Underwood Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Knox Coast of East Antarctica. Look for ice reaching the sea between rocky outcrops.

name: Utstikkar Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Mawson Coast of East Antarctica. Look for crevassed ice running to the sea.

name: Uummannaq fjord
blurb: A large West Greenland fjord system named for Uummannaq, a town at the foot of a heart-shaped mountain of about 3,800 ft. Look for icebergs and the mountain's twin-peaked red-brown rock.

name: Vanoise National Park
blurb: France's first national park, created in 1963, with glaciers and peaks over 12,000 ft between the Tarentaise and Maurienne valleys. It borders Italy's Gran Paradiso; look for the ice fields.

name: Vashi Canyon
blurb: A narrow river canyon near Firuzkuh in the Alborz mountains. A Qajar-era rock relief of Fath-Ali Shah hunting is carved into its wall. Look for the slot cutting through dry mountains east of Tehran.

name: Vefsnfjord
blurb: A fjord in Nordland with the town of Mosjøen at its head. Look for a long, sheltered arm of water running inland between forested mountains.

name: Venable Ice Shelf
blurb: A floating ice shelf on the Bellingshausen Sea coast of West Antarctica. Look for flat ice ending in a cliff against sea ice.

name: Veststraumen Glacier
blurb: A large ice stream in Dronning Maud Land feeding the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf. The name is Norwegian for 'west stream'. Expect broad ice with faint flow lines.

name: Victoria Falls National Park
blurb: The Zambezi drops about 350 ft over a mile-wide edge, and the spray plume can be seen for miles, hence the local name, the Smoke That Thunders. Look for the white column of mist and the zigzag gorges below.

name: Virgin Islands National Park
blurb: Covers more than half of St. John, much of it land Laurance Rockefeller bought and donated in 1956, plus coral reefs offshore. Look for the green hills and the white curve of Trunk Bay.

name: Vodlozero
blurb: The heart of Vodlozersky National Park, one of Europe's largest stretches of untouched northern forest. Look for a lake scattered with islands, surrounded by taiga and bog with almost no roads.

name: Voyeykov Ice Shelf
blurb: An ice shelf on the Banzare Coast of East Antarctica, named by Soviet expeditions. Look for flat floating ice meeting sea ice.

name: Vozhe
blurb: A long, shallow lake in the forests and bogs of northern Vologda, draining north toward the White Sea. Look for a narrow, pale lake with marshy, indistinct shores.

name: Wadden Sea / Frisian Islands
blurb: The world's largest unbroken system of tidal flats, a UNESCO site stretching from the Netherlands to Denmark. Twice a day the sea drains away; look for a chain of sandy islands with glistening mudflats and winding channels behind them.

name: Wadi Shab
blurb: A narrow limestone gorge running inland from the Gulf of Oman, with turquoise pools and palm groves at the bottom. Look for the dark cleft in the bare coastal mountains near Tiwi.

name: Ward Hunt Ice Shelf
blurb: Long the largest ice shelf in the Arctic, it has split and broken apart repeatedly since 2002. Look for scattered flat ice along the north coast of Ellesmere Island, among the northernmost land on Earth.

name: Webster Glacier
blurb: A glacier draining toward the Ronne Ice Shelf. Expect white ice with faint flow lines.

name: Whanganui National Park
blurb: Follows the Whanganui River through deep forested gorges; in 2017 the river was granted legal personhood, a world first. Look for the brown river winding tightly through rumpled green hill country.

name: Whillans Ice Stream
blurb: In 2013 scientists drilled through about 2,600 ft of this ice stream into Subglacial Lake Whillans and found living microbes in water sealed off from sunlight. From above, a smooth white plain.

name: Whirlwind Glaciers
blurb: A cluster of glaciers draining into Whirlwind Inlet on the Antarctic Peninsula's east coast, named for the strong winds there. Look for several ice streams converging on an inlet.

name: White Desert
blurb: Chalk eroded by wind into white mushrooms and towers in the Western Desert near Farafra. Look for a bright white patch on the tan sand, like snow in the Sahara.

name: Whitefish Lake
blurb: A lake in the barren lands east of Great Slave Lake, near the tree line. Look for a ragged lake among bare rock, scattered spruce and countless smaller ponds.

name: Wholdaia Lake
blurb: A large, island-dotted lake in the southeast Northwest Territories, on the Dubawnt River system. Look for a sprawling lake in thin spruce forest near the tree line.

name: Wilkins Ice Shelf
blurb: Broke up dramatically in 2008 and 2009, when the ice bridge linking it to Charcot Island shattered. Look for flat floating ice broken into slabs and bergs off the Peninsula's west coast.

name: Williamson Glacier
blurb: A glacier on the Budd Coast of Wilkes Land near Australia's Casey Station. Look for ice reaching the sea in a jagged front.

name: Wolstenholme Fjord
blurb: A fjord in northwest Greenland beside Pituffik Space Base, the US military's northernmost base, formerly Thule Air Base. Look for the base's runway near the fjord's south shore and glaciers along its sides.

name: Wright Upper Glacier
blurb: Sits at the head of Wright Valley in the McMurdo Dry Valleys, some of the driest places on Earth. Look for ice ending abruptly above bare brown valley floor.

name: Wuzhi Mountain
blurb: Hainan's highest peak at about 6,100 ft, named Five Finger Mountain for its row of five summits. Look for a jagged forested ridge in the island's rainforest interior.

name: Wuzhong
blurb: A Hui Muslim farming city on the irrigated Yellow River plain. Just upstream at Qingtongxia, a hillside holds 108 small white stupas in a triangle; look for green canal-fed fields against desert.

name: Xinfengjiang Reservoir
blurb: A big reservoir in Guangdong formed by a dam in the late 1950s, its water dotted with hundreds of islands that were once hilltops. Look for a green maze of islands in blue water.

name: Yamdrok Lake
blurb: One of Tibet's three sacred lakes, at about 14,600 ft, with a twisting, scorpion-like shape of long arms. Look for vivid turquoise water winding between bare brown ridges south of Lhasa.

name: Yasuni National Park
blurb: One of the most biodiverse places on Earth, sitting on top of oil. In 2023 Ecuadorians voted to stop drilling in part of it; look for straight access roads and clearings cutting into the forest.

name: Yokohama
