blurb: Japan's second most populous city and its first big port open to foreign trade, in 1859. Look for Landmark Tower, the Ferris wheel at Minato Mirai, and the white span of the Bay Bridge.

name: Yolyn Am
blurb: A deep, narrow gorge in the Gobi where shaded ice can last into summer. The name refers to the lammergeier vulture. Look for a dark cleft in the Gurvan Saikhan ridges rising from the desert.

name: Yumurtalık Lagoon
blurb: A coastal lagoon on the Ceyhan River delta, at the head of the Gulf of İskenderun. Look for shallow water and marsh behind a thin sandbar, with tankers waiting offshore.

name: Yuzhu Peak
blurb: About 20,300 ft, the highest summit of the eastern Kunlun, rising beside the Qinghai-Tibet highway and railway near Kunlun Pass. Look for a big glaciated peak above brown, treeless plateau.

name: Zakouma National Park
blurb: Chad's elephant herd, nearly wiped out by poaching, has been rebuilding since African Parks took over in 2010. Look for floodplain and savanna that turn to wetlands in the rains.

name: Zeller Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Transantarctic Mountains. Look for a ribbon of ice between dark peaks.

name: Zhari Namco
blurb: A large saline lake in western Tibet at about 15,000 ft, the shrunken remnant of a much bigger ancient lake. Look for old shorelines ringing the blue water like bathtub rings, with pale salt flats between.

name: Zhelin Reservoir
blurb: A dammed reservoir on the Xiu River that flooded a hilly valley, leaving hundreds of green islands. Look for a maze of wooded humps and fingers of water spreading out among the hills of northwest Jiangxi.

name: Zirbitzkogel
blurb: About 7,850 ft, a broad grassy summit in the Seetal Alps of Styria, gentler than the jagged limestone peaks to the north. Look for a rounded bald top above dark forest.

name: Zotikov Glacier
blurb: A glacier in the Queen Maud Mountains near the Ross Ice Shelf. Look for ice between bare rock summits.

name: Zubchatyy Ice Shelf
blurb: A small ice shelf on the Enderby Land coast. The Russian name means 'jagged', after its ragged edge. Look for flat floating ice with a toothed seaward front.

name: Þistilfjörður
blurb: A wide, shallow bay on Iceland's remote northeast coast, between the Melrakkaslétta and Langanes peninsulas. Look for low moorland and the thin finger of Langanes to the east.

name: Đerdap National Park
blurb: The Serbian side of the Iron Gates, where the Danube squeezes through a Carpathian gorge and is held back by one of Europe's largest hydroelectric dams. Look for the wide river threading tight, forested limestone walls.

name: Ķemeri National Park
blurb: Raised bogs, lakes and sulfur springs just west of Jūrmala, a spa area since the 1800s. Look for pale brown bogs dotted with dark pools on the approach to Riga.

name: Šumava National Park
blurb: The largest Czech national park, the Bohemian Forest, runs into Germany's Bavarian Forest to form one of the biggest woodlands in central Europe. Look for the long Lipno reservoir at its southeast end.

name: Abajo Peak
blurb: At 11,360 ft, the high point of the Abajo Mountains above Monticello in southeastern Utah, topped by radio towers. Look for a forested island of mountains in a sea of red canyon country.

name: Agepsta
blurb: A summit of about 10,700 ft in the western Caucasus on the Russia-Abkhazia line, above the Krasnaya Polyana ski resorts built for the 2014 Sochi Olympics. Look for snow on the crest above the valley.

name: Akanda National Park
blurb: Mangroves and mudflats around Mondah Bay just north of Libreville, a winter stop for migrating shorebirds. Look for the maze of mangrove channels beside the city.

name: Akiba
blurb: One of the summits of the western Greater Caucasus in Georgia, above forested valleys that drain toward the Black Sea. Look for snowy ridges on the main crest.

name: Al Hoceima National Park
blurb: Limestone cliffs and coves on Morocco's Mediterranean coast west of Al Hoceima, where the Rif mountains drop straight into the sea. Look for steep reddish headlands above clear water.

name: Alberto de Agostini National Park
blurb: The Cordillera Darwin in Tierra del Fuego, where glaciers spill into the Beagle Channel and fjords. Look for ice and black rock along the channel.

name: Alta Murgia National Park
blurb: A bare karst plateau in Apulia topped by Castel del Monte, Frederick II's perfectly octagonal 13th-century castle. Look for the eight-sided castle alone on a hill.

name: Altos de Nsork National Park
blurb: Rainforest on a high plateau in mainland Equatorial Guinea, near the borders with Gabon and Cameroon. Look for unbroken canopy over rolling hills.

name: Amacayacu National Park
blurb: Flooded forest on the Amazon near the triple border of Colombia, Peru and Brazil. Look for the broad brown river, its sandbars and oxbow lakes cut into unbroken jungle.

name: Amak Volcano
blurb: A small round volcanic island in the Bering Sea just off the north side of the Alaska Peninsula, a single cone rising from open water and a refuge for seabirds and sea lions.

name: Amazônia National Park
blurb: Amazon rainforest on the west bank of the Tapajós River, one of the big clear-water tributaries of the Amazon. Look for unbroken canopy along a wide blue-green river, broken by rapids upstream.

name: Amber Mountain National Park
blurb: A volcanic massif with crater lakes and rainforest above Antsiranana. Look for round crater lakes in green forest rising out of dry northern lowlands.

name: Ambitle
blurb: A volcanic island in Papua New Guinea's Feni group, east of New Ireland, known for hot springs. Look for a small forested island with a ragged crater outline in deep blue water.

name: Amboró National Park
blurb: Where the Andes, the Amazon and the Chaco meet, west of Santa Cruz. Look for steep green ridges rising from farmland.

name: Amsterdam
blurb: The 17th-century canal ring wraps the old center in concentric half-moons, and much of the city lies below sea level. Look for the curved canals fanning around the core and the wide IJ harbor to the north.

name: Anavilhanas National Park
blurb: One of the largest freshwater archipelagos on Earth, roughly 400 islands braided through the Rio Negro upstream of Manaus. Look for long green slivers in black water.

name: Andre Felix National Park
blurb: Remote savanna and woodland on the Sudan border in the far east of the Central African Republic. Look for flat bush and seasonal rivers.

name: Aparados da Serra National Park
blurb: Holds Itaimbezinho, a canyon about 3.5 miles long and up to 2,300 ft deep cut into the edge of the southern Brazilian plateau. Look for the sharp gash in green grassland where cliffs drop toward the coastal plain.

name: Appennino Lucano - Val d'Agri - Lagonegrese National Park
blurb: The Val d'Agri here sits on the largest onshore oil field in Europe, inside a mountain national park. Look for the Pertusillo reservoir and oil pads in the valley floor.

name: Arabuko Sokoke National Park
blurb: The largest surviving block of coastal forest in East Africa, just inland from Malindi and Watamu. Look for the dark forest patch amid farmland behind the beaches.

name: Araguaia National Park
blurb: Covers the northern part of Bananal Island, often called the world's largest river island, cut off by two arms of the Araguaia River. Look for the island's wetland and savanna between the meandering channels.

name: Archipiélago de Juan Fernández National Park
blurb: Juan Fernández islands, where castaway Alexander Selkirk lived four years, inspiring Robinson Crusoe. Look for steep green islands in open Pacific.

name: Arcipelago Toscano National Park
blurb: Seven islands off Tuscany, including Elba, where Napoleon spent his first exile, and Montecristo of Dumas fame. Look for Elba's mountainous outline between the mainland and Corsica.

name: Ardoukoba
blurb: A volcanic vent in Djibouti's Asal Rift, where Africa and Arabia are pulling apart. Look for black lava near Lake Assal, the lowest point in Africa.

name: Arikok National Park
blurb: Covers roughly a fifth of Aruba: cactus scrub, limestone cliffs and the rough windward coast. Look for the dry brown interior and white surf on the northeast shore.

name: Arnøyhøgda
blurb: Highest point of Arnøya, an island in the far north of Norway. Look for a mountainous island rising straight from the Arctic sea.

name: Ashdod
blurb: Founded in 1956 and home to one of Israel's two main cargo ports. Look for the port's long breakwaters on the straight Mediterranean coast south of Tel Aviv, with dunes around the city.

name: Asinara National Park
blurb: An island off northwest Sardinia that served as a prison colony and maximum-security jail until the 1990s, which kept it wild. It's known for its white donkeys; look for the long, thin bare island.

name: Assagny National Park
blurb: Coastal swamp forest and savanna near the mouth of the Bandama River, west of Abidjan. Look for lagoons and wetlands behind the Atlantic beach.

name: Atavyros
blurb: The highest point on Rhodes at about 3,990 ft. Ruins of an ancient temple to Zeus sit on the summit. Look for the bare, gray peak near the island's west coast.

name: Auckland
blurb: Built across a volcanic field of about 50 small volcanoes, on an isthmus between two harbors. Look for the symmetrical cone of Rangitoto Island offshore and the Sky Tower needle downtown.

name: Ayubia National Park
blurb: Pine and oak forest in the Galyat hills near Murree, a summer retreat from the heat of Islamabad. Look for dark forested ridges above the hill stations.

name: Ba Bể National Park
blurb: Built around Ba Bể Lake, Vietnam's largest natural lake, set among limestone mountains in the far north. Look for the long lake winding between steep karst peaks.

name: Babia Góra
blurb: At 5,659 ft, the highest Polish peak outside the Tatras, nicknamed the Mother of Bad Weather for how fast storms build on it. Look for a long bare ridge above the forest line on the Slovak border.

name: Babuyan Claro
blurb: A volcanic island in the Luzon Strait, part of the remote Babuyan group north of Luzon. Look for a small, steep green island with a cone at its center.

name: Bach Ma National Park
blurb: Mountain forest near Hue rising to a summit about 4,750 ft high, where the French built a hill station in the 1930s. Look for the green massif running down to the coast.

name: Bako National Park
blurb: Sarawak's oldest national park, a small sandstone peninsula near Kuching known for proboscis monkeys. Look for cliffs, sea stacks and pale sandy coves where the jungle meets the South China Sea.

name: Balpakram National Park
blurb: A plateau in Meghalaya's Garo Hills cut by a deep forested canyon, held sacred in Garo belief as the resting place of departed souls. Look for the gorge slicing through green hills above the Bangladesh plains.

name: Bandingilo National Park
blurb: Part of one of the largest land-mammal migrations on Earth, as hundreds of thousands of white-eared kob and other antelope cross South Sudan's grasslands. Look for flat, seasonally flooded savanna east of the Nile near Juba.

name: Banke National Park
blurb: Established in 2010 next to Bardiya to give tigers more room, it covers the forested Churia hills near Nepal's southern border. Look for a band of low, wooded ridges above the surrounding farmland.

name: Baritú National Park
blurb: Remote cloud forest in Salta on the Bolivian border, reachable by road only through Bolivia. Look for steep green ridges often under cloud.

name: Barrington Tops National Park
blurb: A high basalt plateau north of Newcastle, part of the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage area and cold enough for winter snow. Look for a flat forested tableland above deep valleys.

name: Batu Tara
blurb: A small volcanic island in the Flores Sea that woke in 2006 after more than 150 years and erupted for years. Look for a lone cone in open water, with no village on it.

name: Bayanaul National Park
blurb: Kazakhstan's first national park, created in 1985, where wind-sculpted granite and pine forest ring clear lakes in the middle of the steppe. Look for the rocky hills and lakes in flat grassland.

name: Bazaruto National Park
blurb: An archipelago off Mozambique with towering sand dunes and turquoise channels, home to one of the last dugong populations in the western Indian Ocean. Look for long white dune islands with sandbars swirling in the shallows.

name: Belezma National Park
blurb: Cedar-covered mountains in the Aurès near Batna, sheltering rare Atlas cedars. Look for dark forested ridges above dry plains.

name: Betla National Park
blurb: One of India's first tiger reserves under Project Tiger in 1973, sal forest along the Koel River with the ruins of old Palamau forts. Look for forested hills cut by the river.

name: Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park
blurb: Western Ghats forest on the Goa-Karnataka border, home to Dudhsagar Falls, about 1,000 ft tall, with a railway bridge crossing right in front. Look for the white ribbon of falls in monsoon season.

name: Bhitarkanika National Park
blurb: One of India's largest mangrove forests, with one of the country's biggest populations of saltwater crocodiles. Look for dark green mangrove laced with tidal creeks where the Brahmani and Baitarani rivers reach the Bay of Bengal.

name: Bicuari National Park
blurb: Dry woodland and grassland in southwestern Angola. Look for flat savanna and seasonal pans.

name: Big Baldy Mountain
blurb: Highest point of the Little Belt Mountains at 9,177 ft, a rounded, forested range in central Montana. Look for a broad dark-green dome with bald tops above the wheat country.

name: Big Hatchet Peak
blurb: Highest point of the Big Hatchet Mountains at about 8,350 ft, in New Mexico's bootheel near the Mexican border. Look for a jagged limestone ridge above bare desert basins.

name: Bikin National Park
blurb: A huge tract of Far East taiga along the Bikin River, prime habitat for the Amur tiger and home of the Udege people. Look for unbroken forest and the river's meanders, with no roads beyond its lower reaches.

name: Bilbao
blurb: An iron and shipbuilding city reinvented by the Guggenheim Museum, which opened in 1997. Look for the museum's curving titanium shell glinting beside the Nervión River as it winds to the sea.

name: Birmingham
blurb: Britain's second city and a heart of the industrial revolution, with more miles of canal than Venice. Look for the canal network and the Bullring's curved Selfridges building, covered in silver discs.

name: Björnlandet National Park
blurb: A small park of old forest, cliffs and boulder fields in Västerbotten, left largely alone since a forest fire long ago. It blends into the surrounding conifer forest from the air.

name: Black Pine Mountains High Point
blurb: The top of a small, isolated range in southern Idaho near the Utah line. Look for a dark, juniper-dotted block rising from flat sagebrush and farmland.

name: Black River Gorges National Park
blurb: Protects most of the native forest left on Mauritius, around deep gorges in the island's southwest. The island's highest point, Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire at about 2,700 ft, rises at its edge. Look for dark green ravines cutting the plateau.

name: Blackbuck National Park
blurb: Flat grassland near the Gulf of Khambhat, set aside for herds of blackbuck, the spiral-horned Indian antelope. Look for open plain and mudflats running to the gulf.

name: Blyznytsya
blurb: At 6,171 ft, the highest peak of the Svydovets range in Ukraine's Carpathians. Look for a bare grassy crest above spruce forest, with old glacial hollows on its flanks.

name: Blåfjella–Skjækerfjella National Park
blurb: Mountain wilderness in Trøndelag along the Swedish border, grazed by Sami reindeer herds. Look for rolling bare uplands dotted with lakes and bogs above the forest line.

name: Bocaina Mountain National Park
blurb: The Serra da Bocaina, covering some of the largest remaining Atlantic Forest between Rio and São Paulo. Look for green peaks dropping steeply to the island-studded bays near Paraty.

name: Bogani Nani Wartabone National Park
blurb: North Sulawesi rainforest where the maleo bird buries its eggs in sun-warmed or volcanically heated sand. Look for forested mountains in the island's long northern arm.

name: Bogoslof Island
blurb: The tip of an undersea volcano in the Aleutians that keeps rebuilding itself; its 2016 to 2017 eruptions reshaped the island and grounded flights with ash. Look for a small, raw gray island north of Unalaska.

name: Boma National Park
blurb: Vast grasslands and floodplains near the Ethiopian border, center of the great migration of white-eared kob, tiang and Mongalla gazelle. Look for flat seasonal wetlands stretching toward the Boma Plateau.

name: Boodjamulla (Lawn Hill) National Park
blurb: Lawn Hill Gorge, an emerald creek between red sandstone walls, plus the Riversleigh fossil beds, a World Heritage site. Look for a ribbon of green palms threading through dry red outback.

name: Borawli
blurb: One of the remote volcanoes of Ethiopia's Afar depression, where the ground sits near or below sea level and summer highs top 110 F. Look for dark lava on pale desert.

name: Border Ranges National Park
blurb: Follows the rim of the giant Tweed Volcano caldera along the Queensland border, covered in Gondwana rainforest. Look for the curving escarpment around the green Tweed Valley, with Mount Warning's spike at its center.

name: Bouba Njida National Park
blurb: Savanna in northern Cameroon where poachers on horseback killed hundreds of elephants in 2012. Look for dry woodland and river channels.

name: Boucle du Baoulé National Park
blurb: Named for the loop (boucle) of the Baoulé River northwest of Bamako, it is dry Sahel savanna scattered with prehistoric tombs and rock art. Look for the thin, tree-lined river bending through brown scrubland.

name: Bouzegza
blurb: A mountain about 30 miles east of Algiers, standing above the coastal plain where the Atlas foothills begin. Look for its wooded slopes rising from farmland.

name: Box Elder Peak
blurb: At about 9,400 ft, a summit of the Wellsville Mountains above Brigham City, part of one of the steepest ranges in the US. Look for a narrow ridge rising abruptly from the flats along the Great Salt Lake's northeast edge.

name: Brave Mountain
blurb: A summit in the rugged mountains of northern Labrador, a treeless coast of fjords and bare rock. Look for dark peaks cut by deep inlets, often snow-streaked.

name: Breitinden
blurb: The highest point on Senja, Norway's second-largest island, above fjords and Arctic sea. Look for sharp, snow-streaked ridges dropping into deep blue water.

name: Bridgeman Island
blurb: A small, eroded remnant of a volcano in Bransfield Strait in the South Shetland Islands, off the Antarctic Peninsula. Look for a dark, ice-free rock among the white islands around it.

name: Broutona
blurb: A small, uninhabited volcanic island in the central Kurils, a remnant cone eroded by the sea. Look for a speck of rugged island in open water.

name: Bruce Peninsula National Park
blurb: Limestone cliffs of the Niagara Escarpment along Georgian Bay, with clear turquoise water at the Grotto near Tobermory. Look for the pale cliff line on the peninsula's east shore.

name: Brussels
blurb: Home of the EU and NATO headquarters. Look for the Atomium, a 335-ft steel model of an iron crystal, on the north side, and the pentagon-shaped ring road around the old center.

name: Bui National Park
blurb: The Bui Dam, finished in 2013, flooded part of this park on the Black Volta. Look for the long reservoir snaking through dry woodland.

name: Burabay National Park
blurb: Called the Kazakh Switzerland: pine forest, granite peaks and lakes rising out of flat northern steppe. Look for the cluster of blue lakes in a dark green island of hills.

name: Buxa Tiger Reserve
blurb: Forest and grassland in the Dooars along the Bhutan border, with a hill fort once used as a British prison. Look for the dark forest rising into the first Himalayan foothills.

name: Cabo Orange National Park
blurb: Mangroves, savanna and floodplain at Brazil's northern tip, at the mouth of the Oiapoque River on the French Guiana border. Look for coastal mangroves and muddy Atlantic water.

name: Cabo de Hornos National Park
blurb: The storm-battered islands around Cape Horn, where the Atlantic and Pacific collide and hundreds of ships were wrecked rounding the tip of the Americas. Look for a jagged scatter of bare islands at the end of the continent.

name: Cabrera National Park
blurb: A small, nearly uninhabited archipelago about 6 miles south of Mallorca, protected land and sea together, with a medieval castle above the harbor. Look for the jagged main island and its scatter of islets in clear blue water.

name: Calanques National Park
blurb: White limestone cliffs between Marseille and Cassis, cut by narrow turquoise inlets. Look for fjord-like coves biting into bare white rock just past the city.

name: Calilegua National Park
blurb: Yungas cloud forest climbing the eastern Andes in Jujuy. Look for ridges going from green jungle to bare high peaks.

name: Cameia National Park
blurb: Floodplain grasslands and lakes in eastern Angola near the Zambian border. Look for wide grassy plains and shallow pans.

name: Campbell Bay National Park
blurb: Rainforest on Great Nicobar, near India's southernmost point. Look for unbroken jungle running down to the coast.

name: Campo Ma'an National Park
blurb: Coastal rainforest in southern Cameroon on the Equatorial Guinea border. Look for dense green canopy near the Atlantic.

name: Cangandala National Park
blurb: Angola's smallest park, created to protect the giant sable antelope, the country's national symbol. Look for woodland and grassy clearings.

name: Cap Mountain
blurb: A peak in the Franklin Mountains along the Mackenzie River. Look for a dark ridge above the wide river and its spruce lowlands.

name: Cap de la Gallina Pelada
blurb: A peak in the Serra d'Ensija in Catalonia's Pre-Pyrenees, just south of the main Pyrenees. Look for a grassy summit above steep limestone cliffs and pine forest.

name: Cape Arid National Park
blurb: A remote stretch of the south coast east of Esperance, with white beaches, granite headlands and heathland. Look for the bare granite hills and turquoise bays where the Great Australian Bight begins.

name: Cape Breton Highlands National Park
blurb: Rugged plateau at the northern tip of Cape Breton Island, circled by the Cabot Trail. Look for forested highlands ending in steep cliffs over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

name: Cape Range National Park
blurb: A limestone range with gorges on one side and Ningaloo Reef, a fringing reef you can swim to from the beach, on the other. Look for the reef line running close to the white coast.

name: Caracas
blurb: Fills a narrow valley at about 3,000 ft, walled off from the sea by the Ávila mountain. Look for the long valley packed with towers and hillsides covered with informal housing.

name: Carara National Park
blurb: Scarlet macaws roost here, and crowds watch big crocodiles from the Tárcoles River bridge at its edge. Look for the brown Tárcoles winding to the Pacific beside the forest.

name: Carrasco National Park
blurb: Cloud forest on the eastern slope of the Andes in Cochabamba, known for its oilbird caves. Look for jungle ridges below the high Andes.

name: Castle Peak
blurb: At about 11,800 ft, the highest of Idaho's White Cloud Mountains, named for their pale rock. Look for whitish summits and a scatter of small alpine lakes east of the Sawtooths.

name: Cavernas do Peruaçu National Park
blurb: A limestone canyon in northern Minas Gerais where the Peruaçu River runs through caves with entrances big enough to hold buildings, plus prehistoric rock paintings. Look for a green gorge cutting through dry cerrado scrub.

name: Cerro Cora National Park
blurb: Where the Paraguayan War ended in 1870, with the death of President Francisco Solano López. Look for isolated wooded hills rising from grassland near the Brazilian border.

name: Cerro El Carrizal
blurb: A summit in the arid ranges of Coahuila, in the Chihuahuan Desert. Look for folded limestone ridges, brown and gray, above empty flats.

name: Cerro Maltusado
blurb: A summit in the Andean foothills of Chile's lake district, near Villarrica and the volcano country. Look for forested slopes and nearby snowy cones.

name: Cerro Rosa
blurb: One of the high points of Puerto Rico's Cordillera Central, the mountain spine that runs east to west across the island. Look for steep green ridges and communication towers on the summits.

name: Chaco National Park
blurb: Quebracho forest and wetlands in Argentina's Chaco plain. Look for patches of woodland and marsh in flat farmland.

name: Chambi National Park
blurb: Built around Jebel Chambi, at about 5,000 ft the highest point in Tunisia, with Aleppo pine forest on its slopes near the Algerian border. Look for the dark wooded massif rising above dry plains.

name: Chapada Diamantina National Park
blurb: Table mountains, canyons and waterfalls in Bahia, including the flat-topped Morro do Pai Inácio. Look for mesas and sheer cliffs above green valleys.

name: Cheile Nerei-Beușnița National Park
blurb: Follows the Nera River through a limestone gorge in southwest Romania's Banat, with turquoise karst lakes and waterfalls. Look for the river's tight, wooded canyon cutting through the Anina Mountains.

name: Chicoma Mountain
blurb: Highest point of the Jemez Mountains at about 11,560 ft, sacred to Santa Clara Pueblo, just north of the Valles Caldera supervolcano. Look for the 13-mile grassy caldera ringed by forest.

name: Chiloé National Park
blurb: Temperate rainforest running down to the wild Pacific side of Chiloé Island, with long empty beaches and dunes. Look for dark green forest meeting a surf-lined shore on the island's west coast.

name: Chrea National Park
blurb: Atlas cedar forest on the Blida Atlas above the Mitidja plain, with a small ski area and Barbary macaques. Look for the dark green ridge south of Algiers.

name: Christmas Island National Park
blurb: Covers most of Christmas Island, where tens of millions of red crabs march to the sea each year to spawn. Look for the forested plateau ringed by sea cliffs.

name: Chyulu Hills
blurb: A young volcanic range of green cinder cones, home to some of the longest lava tubes in the world. Look for the ridge of cones and the black Shetani lava flow at its southern end.

name: Cincinnati
blurb: Built on hills along the Ohio River, with Kentucky on the far bank. The 1866 Roebling Suspension Bridge was a test run for the Brooklyn Bridge; look for its blue cables crossing to Covington.

name: Circeo National Park
blurb: Monte Circeo, the legendary home of the sorceress Circe, rises from a flat coast that was once the Pontine Marshes. Look for the promontory standing up like an island at the end of a long beach.

name: Clark Mountain
blurb: At about 7,900 ft the highest point in the Mojave National Preserve, rising above I-15 near the Mountain Pass rare-earth mine. Look for a dark limestone massif beside the interstate between Las Vegas and Barstow.

name: Colo
blurb: The volcano that forms Una-Una island in the Gulf of Tomini; its 1983 eruption devastated the island, but everyone had been evacuated. Look for a round island with a broad summit crater.

name: Colombo
blurb: Sri Lanka's commercial capital and main port. Look for Port City, a new district built on land reclaimed from the Indian Ocean, and the Lotus Tower, the tallest structure in South Asia.

name: Copo National Park
blurb: A block of dry Chaco forest of quebracho trees in Santiago del Estero. Look for unbroken scrub in a plain cleared for farming.

name: Coñocranra
blurb: A glaciated summit near the northern end of the Cordillera Blanca, the most heavily glaciated tropical range in the world. Look for snow and ice above deep valleys draining west to the Santa River.

name: Crocker Range National Park
blurb: The largest park in Sabah, a forested spine of mountains running parallel to the west coast just south of Mount Kinabalu. Look for a long, cloud-hung green ridge separating the coastal plain from the interior.

name: Cross River National Park
blurb: Some of Nigeria's last rainforest, home to the Cross River gorilla, the rarest gorilla subspecies. Look for unbroken dark canopy running to the Cameroon border, where it joins Korup National Park.

name: Crêt de la Neige
blurb: The highest point of the Jura Mountains at about 5,640 ft, on the long ridge above Geneva. Look for a parallel line of forested limestone ridges, with Lake Geneva and the Alps beyond.

name: Currant Mountain
blurb: Highest point of the White Pine Range at about 11,500 ft, in central Nevada. Look for a jagged limestone crest above broad sagebrush basins.

name: Cíes Islands
blurb: Three granite islands guarding the mouth of the Ría de Vigo, with cliffs facing the Atlantic and white sand beaches on the sheltered side. Look for the two northern islands joined by a sandbar and lagoon.

name: Călimani National Park
blurb: Volcanic mountains holding one of the largest calderas in the Carpathians, about 6 miles across. Look for the ring of the old crater, scarred by an abandoned sulfur mine, above dark spruce forest.

name: Dadia-Lefkimi-Soufli Forest National Park
blurb: Oak and pine hills near the Turkish border with one of Europe's last breeding colonies of cinereous vultures, among the largest birds of prey on Earth. Look for forested hills above the Evros valley.

name: Dajti National Park
blurb: The mountain wall behind Tirana, topping out above 5,000 ft, with a cable car up from the city. Look for forested slopes rising straight from the city's eastern edge.

name: Delano Peak
blurb: At 12,174 ft, the highest point of the Tushar Mountains, Utah's third-highest range, above Beaver. Look for bare, rounded summits above aspen forest and the Eagle Point ski area.

name: Des Moines
blurb: Iowa's capital, where the Raccoon River meets the Des Moines River. Look for the gold dome of the State Capitol on its hill east of the river and downtown's skywalk-linked towers.

name: Desatoya Peak
blurb: Highest point of the Desatoya Mountains at about 10,000 ft, east of Fallon. Look for a range of rounded summits above dry valleys and playa.

name: Desert National Park
blurb: One of India's largest parks, covering Thar Desert dunes near Jaisalmer, and a last stronghold of the critically endangered great Indian bustard. Look for rolling sand and scrub with little sign of farming.

name: Diamond Peak
blurb: Highest point of the Diamond Mountains at about 10,600 ft, just north of Eureka on Highway 50. Look for a long range above the flat Diamond Valley farmland.

name: Diawling National Park
blurb: Wetlands on the Mauritanian side of the Senegal River delta, across the river from Senegal's Djoudj bird sanctuary. Look for flat floodplain basins, mudflats and the river's last bends before the Atlantic.

name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
blurb: A park on Brahmaputra river islands, known for its feral horses. Look for sandbars and channels where the big river braids.

name: Dieppe Mountain
blurb: A summit in the Cassiar Mountains of northern BC, in empty country between the Stikine and the Alaska Highway. Look for rocky ridges above sparse northern forest.

name: Dinder National Park
blurb: A savanna park near Sudan's border with Ethiopia, watered by the Dinder and Rahad rivers and their oxbow wetlands, called mayas, that hold water into the dry season. Look for the winding river and green pockets in brown plain.

name: Divjakë-Karavasta National Park
blurb: A coastal lagoon park, home to Albania's colony of rare Dalmatian pelicans. Look for the big shallow Karavasta lagoon behind a thin strip of pine forest and beach.

name: Donostia / San Sebastián
blurb: Built around La Concha, a shell-shaped bay with a small island in its mouth between two green hills. The city has one of the highest densities of Michelin stars on Earth. Look for the near-perfect curve of the bay.

name: Dorrigo National Park
blurb: Subtropical rainforest on the edge of the Dorrigo Plateau, part of the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage area. Look for the sharp green escarpment where the tableland drops to the Bellinger Valley and the coast.

name: Double Mountain
blurb: The high point of the Tehachapi Mountains, near 8,000 ft, above the wind farms of Tehachapi Pass. Look for a forested crest between the Mojave Desert and the San Joaquin Valley.

name: Dry Mountain
blurb: The high point of the Last Chance Range in northern Death Valley National Park, over 8,000 ft. Look for a bare desert range above the Racetrack Playa and Eureka Valley dunes.

name: Dudhwa National Park
blurb: Tall grass and sal forest on the Nepal border, home to tigers, swamp deer and one-horned rhinos reintroduced in the 1980s. Look for the green Terai plain laced with streams and grassy swamps.

name: Duffer Peak
blurb: Highest point of the Pine Forest Range at about 9,400 ft, in the far northwestern Nevada desert. Look for a granite crest with small lakes, odd in a dry country.

name: Dzanga-Ndoki National Park
blurb: Lowland rainforest whose Dzanga Bai clearing draws forest elephants by the dozen. Look for unbroken canopy along the Sangha River.

name: Eagle Peak
blurb: At nearly 9,900 ft the highest point of the Warner Mountains in California's far northeast corner. Look for a ridge rising above the dry lake beds of Surprise Valley on its east side, toward Nevada.

name: El Cajas National Park
blurb: Treeless páramo above 10,000 ft just west of Cuenca, dotted with hundreds of glacial lakes. Look for a high, rumpled landscape sprinkled with dark ponds.

name: El Feidja National Park
blurb: Cork oak and zeen oak forest in the Kroumirie mountains on the Algerian border, a refuge for the Barbary red deer. Look for the dense green hills in an otherwise dry corner of North Africa.

name: El Leoncito National Park
blurb: Clear, dry skies made this the site of a major observatory, and its flat dry lakebed is used for land sailing. Look for the pale pan below the Andes.

name: El Paso
blurb: Faces Ciudad Juárez across the Rio Grande, together one of the largest binational metros in the world. Look for the Franklin Mountains splitting the city and the border fence tracing the river.

name: El Rey National Park
blurb: Yungas forest in a valley in Salta. Look for green ridges where the Andes drop to the Chaco.

name: Electric Peak
blurb: At 10,969 ft, the highest peak in Yellowstone's Gallatin Range, named after a member of an 1872 survey party felt electric shocks near the summit during a storm. Look for the gray peak at the park's northwest corner.

name: Elk Mountain
blurb: An isolated 11,156-ft peak at the north end of the Medicine Bow Mountains, standing alone above the plains. Interstate 80 swings around its base; look for a lone dark summit with no range around it.

name: Emory Peak
blurb: At 7,825 ft, the highest point in Big Bend National Park, the top of the Chisos Mountains, the only US mountain range entirely inside a national park. Look for a rocky crest above the desert with the Rio Grande looping south.

name: Endau-Rompin National Park
blurb: Lowland rainforest straddling the Johor-Pahang border, one of the last big tracts of it in southern Peninsular Malaysia. From above it is unbroken dark canopy, hemmed in by the orderly rows of oil palm plantations.

name: Enigma Peak
blurb: A remote summit on the west side of the Antarctic Peninsula, near Alexander Island and the frozen George VI Sound. Look for dark rock poking through ice above long, flat ice shelves.

name: Española Island
blurb: The oldest of the Galápagos islands, worn nearly flat over millions of years. Almost the entire world population of waved albatrosses nests here. Look for a low, dry island at the archipelago's southeast corner.

name: Far Mountain
blurb: A peak on the Chilcotin Plateau of central BC, part of a scatter of old volcanic mountains rising from flat forest. Look for a rounded summit standing above the plateau.

name: Faure Peak
blurb: One of the summits near the polar plateau in the Transantarctic Mountains, a few hundred miles from the South Pole. Look for dark peaks just breaking through an endless white ice sheet.

name: Femundsmarka National Park
blurb: Rocky pine wilderness on the east side of Femund, one of Norway's largest lakes, running into Sweden. Look for a jumble of small lakes, boulder fields and glacial ridges beside the long lake.

name: Fisht
blurb: A glaciated limestone peak of about 9,400 ft at the western end of the high Caucasus, visible from Sochi; the 2014 Olympic stadium was named after it. Look for the snow and ice on its broad summit above green forest.

name: Fitzgerald River National Park
blurb: One of the most plant-rich places in Australia, with well over a thousand flowering plant species on a rugged south coast. Look for the river gorges cutting through heath to the sea.

name: Flat Top Mountain
blurb: At about 12,350 ft the high point of the Flat Tops, a lava-capped plateau where a 1919 Forest Service visit to Trappers Lake helped spark the idea of protected wilderness. Look for a broad table-topped plateau with cliff edges.

name: Floreana Island
blurb: Home of the 1930s "Galapagos Affair," when a baroness and her lovers vanished or died among a handful of settlers. Its Post Office Bay barrel has passed sailors' mail hand to hand since the 1790s.

name: Fonualei
blurb: A small, active volcanic island in northern Tonga, mostly bare lava and ash. Look for a gray, sparsely vegetated island in open ocean, sometimes trailing steam.

name: Forillon National Park
blurb: The tip of the Gaspé Peninsula, where the Appalachians end in limestone cliffs at the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Look for a narrow forested headland with steep pale cliffs on its seaward side.

name: Forollhogna National Park
blurb: High rolling mountain plateau south of Trondheim with one of Norway's healthiest wild reindeer herds. Look for wide, gently rounded uplands with summer farms tucked in the valleys around it.

name: Forra
blurb: A mountain in Nordland, northern Norway, among glaciers and fjords. Look for icy summits above narrow fjords.

name: Fort Lauderdale
blurb: Called the Venice of America for its hundreds of miles of canals. Look for finger canals lined with houses and boats, Port Everglades cruise terminals, and a long line of beach high-rises.

name: Fort Worth
blurb: Where the West begins: the historic Stockyards still stage a cattle drive twice a day. Look for the forks of the Trinity River and a compact downtown about 30 miles west of Dallas.

name: Four Peaks
blurb: Four summits in a neat row in the Mazatzal Mountains, the skyline landmark east of Phoenix, topping out near 7,650 ft and often snowy in winter. Look for the distinctive four-point crest above the Salt River lakes.

name: Francs Peak
blurb: At 13,153 ft the highest point of the Absaroka Range, southeast of Yellowstone. Look for a long, dark volcanic ridge with snowfields above the Greybull River country.

name: Fundy National Park
blurb: Fronts the Bay of Fundy, which has the highest tides in the world. Look for wide red mudflats at low tide and the forested Caledonia Highlands rising behind the coast.

name: Funeral Peak
blurb: A summit of the Black Mountains above Death Valley's Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America. Look for dark, dry slopes dropping to the white salt pan below.

name: Färnebofjärden National Park
blurb: The Dalälven river spreads into a maze of islands, floodplain forest and open water here, right on the line where southern and northern Sweden's plants and animals meet. Look for the river widening into a lake full of wooded islands.

name: Galápagos National Park
blurb: About 97% of the islands' land is national park. Darwin came in 1835 and saw the finches and tortoises that shaped his theory; look for black lava fields and the big calderas on Isabela.

name: Gambela National Park
blurb: Wetlands and grassland along the Baro River on the South Sudan border, crossed by one of Africa's large antelope migrations. Look for floodplain and meandering channels.

name: Gashaka Gumti National Park
blurb: Nigeria's largest national park, climbing along the Cameroon border to Chappal Waddi, the country's highest peak at about 7,900 ft. Look for green mountains and grassy highlands above forested valleys.

name: Gearhart Mountain
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 8,370 ft in south-central Oregon, its summit a jagged rock outcrop. Look for a rugged crest above flat, dry forest and marsh country.

name: Gibraltar Range National Park
blurb: Granite plateau between Glen Innes and Grafton, with rainforest gullies, heath and boulder tors. Look for bare granite domes and outcrops poking above the forested tableland.

name: Glasgow
blurb: Scotland's biggest city, built on Clyde shipbuilding. Look for the river through town, the cranes of the Govan shipyards, and the armadillo-shaped arena on the north bank.

name: Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park
blurb: Mongolia's largest national park, spanning the Gobi with the singing dunes of Khongoryn Els and Yolyn Am, a gorge that can hold ice into summer. Look for a long band of sand dunes against dark mountain ridges.

name: Gola National Park
blurb: Sierra Leone's largest remaining block of lowland rainforest, along the Liberian border, home to pygmy hippos and chimpanzees. Look for dark canopy against the patchwork of farm clearings around it.

name: Gold Coast
blurb: A strip of high-rises lining surf beaches, backed by canal estates dug into former swamp. Look for the towers of Surfers Paradise packed along the sand and the green hinterland beyond.

name: Gonarezhou National Park
blurb: Zimbabwe's second-largest park, famous for the Chilojo Cliffs, red sandstone walls above the Runde River, and part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park. Look for the red cliff line along the river.

name: Gorkhi-Terelj National Park
blurb: Granite hills and larch forest just east of Ulaanbaatar, the capital's weekend escape. Look for rocky outcrops like Turtle Rock above the Tuul and Terelj river valleys, scattered with white ger camps.

name: Gorumara National Park
blurb: A small park in the Dooars known for one-horned rhinos, grassland and riverine forest. Look for the forest patch along the braided rivers coming off the Himalaya.

name: Gothenburg
blurb: Scandinavia's largest port, at the mouth of the Göta River. Look for the river cutting through the city, the long Älvsborg suspension bridge, and bare rocky islands of the archipelago offshore.

name: Gouraya National Park
blurb: Limestone cliffs plunging into the Mediterranean on Mount Gouraya above the port of Béjaïa. Look for the rocky green headland closing off the bay.

name: Grand Ballon
blurb: The highest summit of the Vosges at about 4,670 ft, a rounded grassy dome above the Alsace plain. On clear days the Alps are visible from it. Look for the bald top with a radar dome.

name: Grand Veymont
blurb: At about 7,680 ft, the high point of the Vercors, a limestone fortress plateau that sheltered the French Resistance in 1944. Look for the long cliff walls ringing the plateau above Grenoble.

name: Granite Peak
blurb: Montana's highest peak at 12,807 ft, in the Beartooths just north of Yellowstone. Look for a high plateau of bare granite dotted with hundreds of lakes.

name: Granite Peak
blurb: Highest summit of the Santa Rosa Range at about 9,700 ft, north of Winnemucca near the Oregon line. Look for a rugged crest over sagebrush basins.

name: Grasslands National Park
blurb: Protects some of the last untilled mixed-grass prairie in Canada, with black-tailed prairie dogs and reintroduced plains bison. Look for the Frenchman River valley and badlands breaking up the open grassland.

name: Gray Peak
blurb: A summit in the empty rolling uplands of the southern Yukon. Look for bare gray ridges above the spruce forest and long lakes typical of the territory.

name: Greenhorn Mountain
blurb: The high point of the Wet Mountains, over 12,000 ft, the range that walls off the plains southwest of Pueblo. Look for a long forested ridge rising straight from the flat grassland.

name: Guamblin Island
blurb: A remote, uninhabited island protected as a national park, sitting alone in the open Pacific off the Chonos Archipelago. Look for a single forested island well offshore from the fjord coast.

name: Guffert
blurb: A lone limestone peak of about 7,200 ft in the Brandenberg Alps of Tyrol, near the German border. Look for a pale, steep-sided summit standing apart from the wooded ridges around it.

name: Guindy National Park
blurb: One of the few national parks inside a big city, a patch of scrub forest in Chennai with blackbuck and spotted deer. Look for the dark green block amid the dense city near the IIT Madras campus.

name: Gæđgesčåkka
blurb: A mountain near the Norway-Sweden border in the far north, among Arctic plateaus and lakes. Look for snow-streaked summits and scattered lakes.

name: Hanish Islands
blurb: A volcanic island group in the southern Red Sea that Eritrea and Yemen fought over in 1995; an international tribunal awarded most of it to Yemen. Look for brown, barren islands in the shipping lane.

name: Haparanda Archipelago National Park
blurb: Islands in the far north of the Bothnian Bay, near the Finnish border, still rising out of the sea as the land rebounds from the Ice Age. Look for sand dunes and pale beaches on the low islands.

name: Heart Peaks
blurb: A young volcanic complex in far northern BC, part of the volcanic belt that runs through the Stikine country near Telegraph Creek. Look for a broad, eroded volcano with reddish and gray slopes.

name: Heilhornet
blurb: A sharp peak on Norway's Helgeland coast, rising above islands and fjords. Look for a lone horn near the sea.

name: Helagsfjället
blurb: At 5,896 ft, the highest peak in southern Sweden, carrying Sweden's southernmost glacier. Look for a bare rocky massif with a small white glacier tucked into its flank, above open tundra.

name: Hermannsdalstinden
blurb: The highest peak on Moskenesøya, at the outer tip of the Lofoten Islands, rising straight from the sea. Look for a string of jagged granite spires over deep blue fjords.

name: Hilgard Peak
blurb: At 11,316 ft, the highest in the Madison Range, west of Yellowstone. Look for sharp gray peaks above Hebgen Lake.

name: Hingol National Park
blurb: Pakistan's largest national park, on the Makran coast, with mud volcanoes and wind-carved rock formations like the Princess of Hope. Look for the Hingol River cutting through tan ridges to the Arabian Sea.

name: Hole in the Mountain Peak
blurb: At about 11,300 ft, the highest of the East Humboldt Range near Wells, named for a natural window in the rock near its summit. Look for a jagged peak over the Humboldt River valley.

name: Honolulu
blurb: Hawaii's capital spreads along Oahu's south shore. Look for Diamond Head's crater at the end of Waikiki's hotel strip, Pearl Harbor's lochs to the west, and the green Koolau ridges behind the city.

name: Hualapai Peak
blurb: The high point of the Hualapai Mountains, about 8,400 ft, a pine-covered island above the desert just southeast of Kingman. Look for a dark forested range rising from tan flats.

name: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai
blurb: Its January 2022 eruption was the largest atmospheric explosion since Krakatoa in 1883, sending a plume about 35 miles high, the tallest ever recorded. Most of the island vanished; look for two small remnant islets on a submerged caldera rim.

name: Iceworm Peak
blurb: A glaciated summit in the Kenai Mountains, part of the ice-covered spine of the Kenai Peninsula south of Anchorage. Look for icefields and glaciers draining toward the sea.

name: Ifrane National Park
blurb: Atlas cedar forest in the Middle Atlas, home to one of the largest populations of Barbary macaques. Look for dark cedar woodland and volcanic plateaus around the alpine-style town of Ifrane.

name: Indiana Dunes National Park
blurb: Sand dunes along Lake Michigan, wedged between steel mills on the Indiana shore. Look for pale dunes and forest broken by the giant industrial plants of Gary and Burns Harbor.

name: Indianapolis
blurb: Planned around a central circle with diagonal avenues. Look for the 2.5-mile oval of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway northwest of downtown, big enough to hold Churchill Downs, Yankee Stadium and the Vatican together.

name: Indravati National Park
blurb: Tiger reserve in the Bastar forests along the Indravati River, home to wild water buffalo. Look for forest along the river.

name: Innuit Mountain
blurb: A peak in the Torngat region of northern Labrador, where the highest mountains in mainland eastern Canada rise straight from the sea. Look for bare, glacier-carved rock and fjords.

name: Iona National Park
blurb: Angola's largest park, coastal Namib Desert along the Cunene River with Namibia. Look for dune fields and gravel plains running to the Atlantic.

name: Iriqui National Park
blurb: A desert park centered on the dry bed of Lake Iriqui, south of the Anti-Atlas near the Algerian border. Look for a pale flat basin ringed by dunes and dark rocky ridges, holding water only after rare rains.

name: Isiboro Sécure National Park and Indigenous Territory
blurb: TIPNIS, an Indigenous territory whose planned highway set off major protests in 2011. Look for unbroken forest and meandering rivers in the lowlands.

name: Jabal al-Tair Island
blurb: A lone volcanic island in the Red Sea that erupted in 2007 after more than a century of quiet. Look for a dark cone with black lava flows reaching the shore, alone in open water.

name: Jabuka
blurb: A tiny volcanic islet far out in the Adriatic, made of magnetic rock that can throw off ships' compasses. Look for a lone dark, sharp rock in open sea.

name: Jardines de la Reina National Park
blurb: Columbus named this chain of mangrove cays for Queen Isabella. Its reefs are famous for sharks and big groupers; look for a long string of green islets in turquoise shallows off southern Cuba.

name: Jebil National Park
blurb: Tunisia's largest national park, a sea of sand dunes at the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental. Look for long rows of dunes and rocky ridges with no roads.

name: Jigme Singye Wangchuck National Park
blurb: Forested mountains in central Bhutan, once called the Black Mountains. Look for steep forest and high ridges.

name: Johannesburg
blurb: Founded on the world's richest gold field in 1886, it's one of the biggest cities not on a river, lake or coast. Look for flat-topped yellow mine dumps along the Witwatersrand ridge and suburbs thick with planted trees.

name: Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park
blurb: Zanzibar's only national park, home to the endemic Zanzibar red colobus monkey. Look for the dark forest and mangroves bordering a shallow bay in the middle of the island.

name: Kafue National Park
blurb: Zambia's oldest and largest national park, covering about 8,600 square miles, roughly the size of Massachusetts. Look for Lake Itezhi-Tezhi in the south and the open Busanga Plains floodplain in the north.

name: Kaieteur National Park
blurb: Kaieteur Falls drops 741 ft in a single plunge, more than four times the height of Niagara. Look for the Potaro River pouring off the edge of a sandstone plateau.

name: Kanger Ghati National Park
blurb: A forest valley near Jagdalpur with the Tirathgarh falls and Kotumsar limestone caves. Look for the green gorge along the Kanger River.

name: Kansas City
blurb: Grew where the Kansas River meets the Missouri, and straddles the Missouri-Kansas state line. It calls itself the City of Fountains; look for the river bend and the airport on the north side.

name: Kaohsiung
blurb: Taiwan's biggest port and heavy-industry city. Look for the long sandbar of Cijin Island sheltering the harbor, and the 85 Sky Tower downtown, which splits into two legs at the base.

name: Karijini National Park
blurb: Deep, narrow gorges cut into the red banded-iron rock of the Hamersley Range, with pools at the bottom. Look for the dark cracks in the flat red plateau of the Pilbara.

name: Karkaraly National Park
blurb: Granite mountains covered in pine, rising out of the central Kazakh steppe like an island. Look for the dark forested hills in otherwise treeless country.

name: Kasanka National Park
blurb: Each year from about October to December, some 10 million straw-colored fruit bats roost in one patch of swamp forest here, often called the largest mammal migration on Earth. Look for the lakes and papyrus swamps.

name: Kasungu National Park
blurb: Miombo woodland along Malawi's western border with Zambia, crossed by shallow grassy valleys called dambos. From above it reads as a broad, even canopy of brown-green woodland with pale drainages winding through it.

name: Katahdin
blurb: Maine's highest peak at about 5,270 ft and the northern end of the 2,200-mile Appalachian Trail. Look for the bare granite summit and the Knife Edge ridge above lake-dotted forest.

name: Katavi National Park
blurb: One of Tanzania's most remote parks. In the dry season hundreds of hippos crowd into the shrinking pools of the Katuma River. Look for the wide floodplain and seasonal lakes in the west of the country.

name: Katon-Karagay National Park
blurb: Kazakhstan's largest national park, in the Altai on the Russian and Chinese borders, near Belukha, the highest peak in Siberia. Look for snowy peaks and glaciers above forested valleys.

name: Katowice
blurb: The heart of Poland's Silesian coal belt. Look for the Spodek arena, a flying-saucer-shaped dome downtown, and mine headframes and spoil heaps across the surrounding towns.

name: Kavir National Park
blurb: Salt flats and desert mountains at the edge of the Dasht-e Kavir southeast of Tehran, one of the last refuges of the Asiatic cheetah. Look for white salt pans against brown hills.

name: Kejimkujik National Park
blurb: Inland lakes and forest in southwestern Nova Scotia, traveled for centuries by Mi'kmaw canoe routes and marked with their petroglyphs. Look for Kejimkujik Lake and a maze of smaller lakes in dark woods.

name: Khaptad National Park
blurb: A high rolling plateau in far western Nepal, around 10,000 ft, of meadows and oak forest associated with the hermit Khaptad Baba. Look for open green pastures on a flat summit among steep forested hills.

name: Khenifiss National Park
blurb: Built around Khnifiss lagoon, a rare saltwater inlet on the Saharan coast where flamingos and migrating shorebirds stop over. Look for a long blue lagoon tucked behind a line of coastal dunes.

name: Khunjerab National Park
blurb: Runs up to the Khunjerab Pass on the China border, about 15,400 ft, one of the highest paved border crossings in the world, where the Karakoram Highway tops out. Look for the road's thread through snowy high valleys.

name: Khustain Nuruu National Park
blurb: Przewalski's horse, which had died out in the wild, was returned to these hills starting in 1992. Look for open rolling steppe and low grassy hills west of Ulaanbaatar, with the Tuul River along the south.

name: Kiang West National Park
blurb: The Gambia's largest protected area, dry woodland and mangrove creeks on the south bank of the Gambia River. Look for the wide brown river and the dark mangrove fringe along its edge.

name: Killington Peak
blurb: At 4,235 ft, Vermont's second-highest peak, home to the largest ski resort in the eastern US. Look for ski trails cut in white or green stripes down its forested slopes.

name: Kirindy Mitea National Park
blurb: Dry forest, baobabs and mangroves on Madagascar's west coast. Look for mangroves along tidal channels and dry woodland inland.

name: Kirirom National Park
blurb: A pine-covered plateau west of Phnom Penh. Look for cooler pine forest on a raised plateau.

name: Kirthar National Park
blurb: Arid mountains of the Kirthar Range north of Karachi, home to Sindh ibex and urial. Look for parallel dry ridges and pale gravel plains with almost no green.

name: Kitulo National Park
blurb: A high grassland plateau in the Southern Highlands, nicknamed the Garden of God for its wildflowers and dozens of orchid species. Look for the open, treeless upland above forested valleys.

name: Kobe
blurb: The 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake killed over 6,000 people here. Look for the city squeezed into a thin strip between the steep Rokko Mountains and the sea, with the square artificial islands of Port Island offshore.

name: Kora National Park
blurb: George Adamson of Born Free fame lived with lions here and was murdered by poachers in 1989. Look for the Tana River cutting through dry bush.

name: Kouchibouguac National Park
blurb: Barrier islands of sand and dunes enclosing warm shallow lagoons on New Brunswick's Northumberland Strait coast. Look for long pale sandbars parallel to the shore, with salt marsh and forest behind.

name: Kundelungu National Park
blurb: A high grassland plateau in Katanga cut by deep gorges, where the Lofoi Falls plunge more than 1,000 ft, among the tallest in Africa. Look for the flat-topped plateau edge.

name: Kyiv
blurb: Spread along the Dnieper. Look for the gold domes of the Pechersk Lavra and the giant Motherland statue on the high right bank, and wooded islands in the wide river below.

name: La Campana National Park
blurb: Charles Darwin climbed Cerro La Campana here in 1834. The park also protects some of the last big groves of Chilean wine palm, halfway between Santiago and Valparaíso.

name: Lago Puelo National Park
blurb: A turquoise glacial lake near El Bolsón on the Chilean border. Look for the long blue lake hemmed by forested mountains.

name: Lagodekhi Protected Areas
blurb: The oldest nature reserve in the Caucasus, founded in 1912, climbing from the Alazani Valley to Caucasus ridges on the Dagestan and Azerbaijan borders. Look for forest giving way to alpine meadow.

name: Laguna Blanca National Park
blurb: A lake on a volcanic plateau in Neuquén, a refuge for black-necked swans and flamingos. Look for a blue lake on dark lava plains.

name: Lal Suhanra National Park
blurb: Combines a patch of the Cholistan Desert, irrigated forest plantations and a lake near Bahawalpur, with a breeding program for blackbuck. Look for the sharp line where green canal farmland gives way to tan desert.

name: Lanín National Park
blurb: Built around Volcán Lanín, a snowy cone of about 12,300 ft on the Chilean border, with long glacial lakes. Look for the lone white cone.

name: Laramie Peak
blurb: A 10,272-ft landmark that Oregon Trail travelers watched for days as they crossed eastern Wyoming. Look for the dark, forested hump of the Laramie Mountains rising above open grassland.

name: Legges Tor
blurb: Tasmania's second-highest peak at 5,157 ft, on the Ben Lomond plateau, home to the state's main ski field. Look for a flat-topped dolerite plateau ringed by cliffs.

name: Lexington-Fayette
blurb: The Horse Capital of the World. In 1958 it drew one of the first urban growth boundaries in the US, so the city stops abruptly; look for horse farms with plank fences and green paddocks right at its edge.

name: Limpopo National Park
blurb: Part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park, sharing an unfenced border with South Africa's Kruger. Look for dry bush along the Shingwedzi and Limpopo rivers, and the Massingir reservoir at its southern edge.

name: Liuwa Plain National Park
blurb: Hosts Africa's second-largest wildebeest migration, across open grassland on the upper Zambezi floodplain. Look for the flat, treeless plain dotted with seasonal pans.

name: Llanganates National Park
blurb: Legend says the Inca general Rumiñahui hid Atahualpa's ransom gold in these mountains, and treasure hunters have searched ever since. Usually wrapped in cloud; look for steep, trackless ridges east of the Andes' main spine.

name: Lomami National Park
blurb: One of Africa's newest national parks, created in 2016 in a stretch of Congo rainforest where scientists described a new monkey, the lesula, in 2012. Look for unbroken canopy between big rivers.

name: Lombenben
blurb: The summit of Ambae, a big volcano in Vanuatu whose crater holds lakes; its 2017 and 2018 eruptions forced the evacuation of the entire island. Look for a long ridge-shaped island with a crater lake near the top.

name: Los Cardones National Park
blurb: Named for the candelabra cactus that stands across its slopes in Salta. Look for dry red valleys and the zigzag road of the Cuesta del Obispo.

name: Lublin
blurb: Eastern Poland's largest city, with a medieval old town and a hilltop royal castle. Nearby Majdanek, a Nazi camp, was left largely intact; look for the Bystrzyca River and Zemborzyce reservoir.

name: Lyon
blurb: France's gastronomic capital sits where the Saône meets the Rhône, with a long peninsula between them. Look for the two rivers converging and the Fourvière basilica on the hill above the old town.

name: Lökbatan Mud Volcano
blurb: A mud volcano just southwest of Baku that erupts every few years, sometimes with methane flames shooting into the air. Look for gray mud flows spread like spilled cement across the dry hills.

name: Machalilla National Park
blurb: Coastal dry forest and Isla de la Plata, nicknamed the poor man's Galápagos. Humpback whales come to breed offshore from June to September; look for the island off the mainland coast.

name: Madhav National Park
blurb: Former royal hunting grounds of the Scindias around Shivpuri, with the Sakhya Sagar lake. Look for the lake and dry forest beside the town.

name: Mahale Mountains National Park
blurb: Forested mountains rising straight out of Lake Tanganyika, with wild chimpanzees and no roads in; most visitors arrive by boat. Look for the green ridge dropping to white beaches on the lake.

name: Maiko National Park
blurb: Some of the most remote rainforest in Congo, home to okapi, Grauer's gorillas and the Congo peafowl. Look for unbroken green from horizon to horizon.

name: Malá Fatra National Park
blurb: The Malá Fatra range near Žilina, where the folk-hero outlaw Juraj Jánošík was born. Look for forested ridges with a bare crest above the Vrátna valley and the Váh River gorge at Strečno.

name: Manchester
blurb: The first great industrial city, built on cotton mills. Look for the Manchester Ship Canal running west toward the sea, with Old Trafford beside it.

name: Manila
blurb: Among the most densely populated cities on Earth. Look for the Spanish-era walled city of Intramuros on the bay, the Pasig River winding inland, and container ships crowding Manila Bay.

name: Maputo National Park
blurb: Coastal lakes, swamp forest and dunes south of Maputo Bay, joined to a marine reserve that runs down to the South African border. Look for tall vegetated dunes along the Indian Ocean with blue lakes inland.

name: Mara Mountain
blurb: A peak in Peary Land on Greenland's north coast, at about 83.5 degrees north, among the northernmost land on Earth. Look for ice-free brown mountains above the frozen Arctic Ocean.

name: Marchena Island
blurb: An uninhabited Galapagos shield volcano with a broad caldera, closed to visitors. Look for dark, fresh-looking lava flows spreading across most of the island.

name: Marys Peak
blurb: At 4,097 ft, the highest point in Oregon's Coast Range, west of Corvallis. On clear days you can see from the Pacific to the Cascades. Look for a grassy bald top above dark forest.

name: Matterhorn
blurb: Highest point of the Jarbidge Mountains at about 10,800 ft, in one of the most remote corners of Nevada near Idaho. Look for a cluster of high, sharp peaks above sagebrush.

name: McAfee Peak
blurb: Highest peak of the Independence Mountains at about 10,400 ft, north of Elko. Look for a high, rounded range with snow late into spring.

name: Mehetia
blurb: A tiny, young and uninhabited volcanic island east of Tahiti, barely a mile across. Look for a single steep cone alone in open ocean, with no reef or lagoon around it.

name: Memphis
blurb: On a bluff above the Mississippi, the home of the blues and Graceland. Look for the 32-story glass pyramid by the river, now a Bass Pro Shops, and the bridges across to Arkansas.

name: Meru National Park
blurb: Joy and George Adamson raised and released Elsa the lioness of Born Free here. Look for green riverine forest and swamp in dry bushland east of Mount Kenya.

name: Midžor
blurb: At 7,116 ft, the highest point of Serbia outside Kosovo, on the Bulgarian border in the Balkan Mountains. Look for a grassy, rounded crest above dense beech forest.

name: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
blurb: About 1,000 limestone islands and islets along Quebec's North Shore, known for monoliths, sea stacks eroded into flowerpot shapes. Look for a scatter of low islands strung along the coast.

name: Mkomazi National Park
blurb: Dry bush country along the Kenya border, continuous with Kenya's Tsavo West, with a fenced sanctuary for black rhinos. Look for the Pare and Usambara mountains rising to its south.

name: Mljet Nacionalni Park
blurb: The western end of Mljet island holds two saltwater lakes, and a 12th-century monastery sits on a tiny islet in the larger one. Look for the islet in the middle of the inland lake.

name: Moncayo
blurb: At 7,592 ft, the highest peak of the Iberian System, standing alone above the plains of Aragon and Castile. Look for a big isolated massif, often snow-topped in winter, with glacial hollows on its north side.

name: Mont Ventoux
blurb: The "Giant of Provence," about 6,270 ft, a legendary Tour de France climb. Its summit is bare white limestone scree, so it looks snow-capped even in summer. Look for the pale top above lavender country.

name: Monte Alén National Park
blurb: Equatorial Guinea's largest park, mountainous rainforest with forest elephants, gorillas and chimpanzees. Look for unbroken green hills in the middle of the mainland.

name: Monte Binga
blurb: Mozambique's highest point at about 8,000 ft, on the Zimbabwe border in the Chimanimani Mountains. Look for pale quartzite ridges rising sharply from the lowlands.

name: Monte Catria
blurb: About 5,580 ft in the Apennines of Marche. A huge cross stands on the summit, and the medieval monastery of Fonte Avellana on its slopes is mentioned by Dante. Look for a grassy dome above beech woods.

name: Monte León National Park
blurb: Wild Patagonian coast in Santa Cruz with cliffs, islands and Magellanic penguins. Look for a rugged shoreline on the windswept steppe.

name: Monte Miletto
blurb: At about 6,730 ft, the high point of the Matese massif between Molise and Campania. Look for a bare limestone crest above Lake Matese.

name: Mormon Peak
blurb: Highest point of the Mormon Mountains at about 7,400 ft, a rugged desert range northeast of Las Vegas. Look for bare, gray limestone ridges rising from the Mojave.

name: Mount Aeolus
blurb: A peak in the Front Ranges of Jasper National Park, among the gray limestone ridges east of the Athabasca valley. Look for snow-streaked rock above forested valleys.

name: Mount Alfred
blurb: A steep peak above Jervis Inlet on BC's Sunshine Coast, rising almost from sea level. Look for a sharp summit over a long, narrow fjord.

name: Mount Allen
blurb: A peak in the remote eastern Alaska interior near the Yukon border, among glaciated ridges north of the Wrangell-St. Elias ranges. Look for snowy summits above unbroken wilderness.

name: Mount Amiata
blurb: An extinct volcano of about 5,700 ft in southern Tuscany, once one of Europe's main mercury mining districts. Look for a dark, chestnut- and beech-covered dome rising over the bare clay hills of the Val d'Orcia.

name: Mount Arrowsmith
blurb: About 6,000 ft, the snowy peak behind Parksville and Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, the centerpiece of a UNESCO biosphere region. Look for a jagged summit across the Strait of Georgia from Vancouver.

name: Mount Aylmer
blurb: At about 10,400 ft the highest peak near Banff, standing over the north shore of Lake Minnewanka. Look for the pointed summit above the long blue lake east of town.

name: Mount Baldy
blurb: Above 11,400 ft in Arizona's White Mountains, a peak sacred to the White Mountain Apache, whose summit is closed to visitors. Look for a broad forested massif with open bald slopes near the top.

name: Mount Bartle Frere
blurb: Queensland's highest peak at 5,322 ft, rising from rainforest just inland of the coast south of Cairns. Look for a dark green massif usually wearing a cap of cloud.

name: Mount Bassie
blurb: A peak on Baranof Island near Sitka in Southeast Alaska, part of a rugged spine of mountains rising out of the rainforest and fjords. Look for snowfields above steep green slopes and inlets.

name: Mount Bogong
blurb: Victoria's highest peak at 6,516 ft, in the Australian Alps. Look for a broad bald summit above snow gums, white in winter.

name: Mount Derak
blurb: About 9,500 ft, the mountain that looms over Shiraz from the west. Look for a bare, gray ridge directly above the city's grid.

name: Mount Emei
blurb: One of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains, 10,167 ft, its summit topped by a huge gilded statue of the bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Look for the gold glint on the Golden Summit and the sheer cliff below it.

name: Mount Eugene
blurb: A peak in northern Ellesmere Island, near the top of the world. Look for dark peaks among glaciers and ice-choked fjords.

name: Mount Frank Rae
blurb: A peak in the remote ranges of the central Yukon. Look for rounded tundra summits above forested valleys and winding rivers.

name: Mount Gharat
blurb: The active volcano on Gaua in Vanuatu's Banks Islands, beside Lake Letas, the largest lake in Vanuatu. Look for the big lake in the island's center and the cone on its edge.

name: Mount Grappa
blurb: About 5,820 ft, one of Italy's great World War I battlefields. A massive ossuary on the summit holds the remains of more than 20,000 soldiers. Look for the round terraced memorial above the Venetian plain.

name: Mount Haldane
blurb: A lone summit near Keno and Mayo in the central Yukon's silver mining district. Look for a bare top above the Stewart River valley's spruce and muskeg.

name: Mount Hamiguitan
blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage site in Davao Oriental, known for a bonsai forest of centuries-old trees stunted knee-high on its nutrient-poor summit soils. Look for a forested ridge on a peninsula jutting into Davao Gulf.

name: Mount Harmer
region: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
blurb: The high point of Cook Island in Southern Thule, the ice-covered volcanic end of the South Sandwich Islands chain. Look for a small white island in a dark, iceberg-strewn sea.

name: Mount Hillers
blurb: At about 10,700 ft, one of the Henry Mountains, the last range in the lower 48 to be mapped. Geologists use the range as the classic example of laccoliths, magma that domed up the rock without erupting. Look for rounded peaks rising from slickrock desert.

name: Mount Jackson
blurb: At around 10,400 ft one of the highest peaks in Palmer Land, the broad southern half of the Antarctic Peninsula, named by Byrd's expedition for President Andrew Jackson. Look for a massif rising above the peninsula's ice plateau.

name: Mount Linn
blurb: The high point of the Yolla Bolly Mountains, around 8,000 ft, in a remote wilderness of the inner North Coast Ranges. Look for a bare summit above forested ridges west of the Sacramento Valley.

name: Mount Malindig
blurb: About 3,800 ft, a potentially active volcano at the southern end of heart-shaped Marinduque Island. Look for a forested cone rising right off the coast.

name: Mount Manipur National Park
blurb: Forested hills across the harbor from Port Blair, formerly named Mount Harriet. Look for the green ridge rising over the bay.

name: Mount McLoughlin
blurb: At 9,495 ft, a near-perfect Cascade volcano cone northeast of Medford. Look for a symmetrical pyramid, white in winter, south of Crater Lake.

name: Mount Moresby
blurb: The highest point of Haida Gwaii, a little under 4,000 ft, in the rain-soaked mountains of Moresby Island. Look for a forested ridge with bare rock on top above the Pacific.

name: Mount Nasorolevu
blurb: The highest point on Vanua Levu, Fiji's second-largest island, at about 3,400 ft. Look for a dark green ridge of rainforest running down the island's spine.

name: Mount Nivea
blurb: The highest point of Coronation Island in the South Orkneys, a little over 4,000 ft, named for the snow petrel. Look for an ice-covered island with a jagged crest set in pack ice or open sea.

name: Mount Oave
blurb: About 4,000 ft, the highest of the basalt spires on Ua Pou in the Marquesas. The needles are volcanic plugs left after softer rock eroded away. Look for rock towers poking out of the clouds.

name: Mount Osore
blurb: Osorezan, one of Japan's three holiest places, long believed to be a gateway to the afterlife. Look for a pale caldera lake, gray sulfur fields and a temple complex on the shore.

name: Mount Rae
blurb: A peak of about 10,500 ft in Kananaskis Country, visible from Calgary, rising above Highwood Pass, the highest paved pass in Canada. Look for the small glacier on its north side.

name: Mount Ruang
blurb: A small island volcano that erupted violently in April 2024, sending ash miles high and forcing the evacuation of the whole island. Look for a bare cone off the larger island of Tagulandang.

name: Mount Scenery
blurb: At about 2,900 ft it's the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands, on the tiny island of Saba. Look for one green cone rising straight out of the sea, its top often in cloud.

name: Mount Siegel
blurb: Highest point of the Pine Nut Mountains at about 9,450 ft, east of Carson Valley and Lake Tahoe. Look for a brown, rounded range opposite the forested Sierra.

name: Mount Sirung
blurb: A volcano on Pantar island in eastern Indonesia, with an acid crater lake on a broad summit. Look for a pale crater on the island's center.

name: Mount Spokane
blurb: At 5,883 ft the highest point near Spokane, topped by a state park and ski area. Look for ski runs cut into the forest on its flanks, about 25 miles northeast of the city.

name: Mount Stephens
blurb: A peak on the mainland coast opposite northern Vancouver Island, among the steep ranges above Knight and Kingcome inlets. Look for snowy summits rising from long fjords.

name: Mount Suribachi
blurb: The 554-ft volcano on Iwo Jima where US Marines raised the flag in 1945, in the most reproduced photograph of the war. Look for the knob at the narrow south tip of the island.

name: Mount Tipton
blurb: The high point of the Cerbat Mountains north of Kingman, a little over 7,000 ft, rising from the Mojave Desert. Look for a rugged range with a few dark trees on its crest above pale desert.

name: Mount Tobin
blurb: Highest point of the Tobin Range at about 9,800 ft, in central Nevada. The 1915 Pleasant Valley earthquake broke the ground along its foot. Look for a sharp scarp at the base of the range.

name: Mount Tomanivi
blurb: Fiji's highest peak at about 4,340 ft, on Viti Levu. The wet windward side is rainforest while the lee side is dry grassland. Look for the line where green turns to tan across the island.

name: Mount Tomorr
blurb: A long limestone ridge of about 7,900 ft above Berat, sacred to Albania's Bektashi Muslims, who climb it on pilgrimage each August. Look for a lone massif rising high above the valleys east of the city.

name: Mount Tukosmera
blurb: The highest point on Tanna in Vanuatu, at about 3,560 ft, on the same island as Mount Yasur, one of the most accessible active volcanoes on Earth. Look for Yasur's bare ash plain and steam plume to the east.

name: Mount Turnbull
blurb: A lone desert peak of over 8,000 ft on the San Carlos Apache Reservation, rising above the Gila River valley in eastern Arizona. Look for a steep, isolated mountain with a dark wooded top.

name: Mount Wilson
blurb: At about 14,250 ft the highest peak in the San Miguel Mountains, a cluster of fourteeners southwest of Telluride. Look for a jagged summit among steep, red and gray San Juan peaks.

name: Mount Wrightson
blurb: At about 9,450 ft the highest point near Tucson, in the Santa Rita Mountains, next door to the Whipple Observatory domes on Mount Hopkins. Look for a sharp summit rising from desert grassland south of the city.

name: Mount Yamantau
blurb: About 5,400 ft, the highest peak in the southern Urals and long the subject of reports of a secret Soviet-era complex dug into the mountain. Look for a broad forested summit among parallel ridges.

name: Mount Zirkel
blurb: About 12,180 ft, the namesake of a wilderness in the Park Range north of Steamboat Springs. Look for a rocky crest straddling the Continental Divide above lake-dotted basins.

name: Mungo National Park
blurb: Holds the remains of Mungo Lady and Mungo Man, about 40,000 years old, among the oldest human remains found in Australia. Look for a dry lakebed edged on the east by the Walls of China, a pale crescent of eroded dunes.

name: Mupa National Park
blurb: Woodland and grassland in southern Angola. Look for flat bush cut by seasonal river channels.

name: Médanos de Coro National Park
blurb: A field of shifting sand dunes on the narrow isthmus joining the Paraguaná Peninsula to mainland Venezuela. Look for the strip of pale dunes between two seas.

name: Nairobi
blurb: At about 5,900 ft, with a national park right on the city's edge: giraffes graze with skyscrapers behind them. Look for open savanna running straight up to the southern suburbs.

name: Namadgi National Park
blurb: Mountains covering nearly half of the Australian Capital Territory, Canberra's water catchment. Look for forested ridges of the Brindabellas southwest of the city.

name: Namdapha National Park
blurb: A huge sweep of Himalayan rainforest in Arunachal Pradesh, home to tigers, leopards, clouded leopards and snow leopards. Look for steep jungle ridges climbing to snow.

name: Nameri National Park
blurb: Forest along the Jia Bhoreli River at the foot of the Himalayas. Look for a clear braided river leaving green hills.

name: Citadelle Laferrière
blurb: The Citadelle Laferrière, the largest fortress in the Americas, sits on a 3,000-ft peak here, built by Henri Christophe after independence. Look for its ship-prow walls on the ridge.

name: National Nature Park Skole Beskids
blurb: Beech and fir forest in the Ukrainian Carpathians, south of Lviv, with deep river valleys between rounded ridges. Look for the unbroken forested mountains rolling toward the Polish border.

name: National Park of Upper Niger
blurb: Dry forest and savanna along the headwaters of the Niger River in Guinea, home to chimpanzees and hippos. Look for the young Niger winding through woodland.

name: New Taipei City
blurb: Taiwan's most populous city, about 4 million people wrapped around Taipei on three sides. Look for dense apartment blocks running up river valleys into green mountains, and the Tamsui River reaching the sea.

name: Newark
blurb: Home to Port Newark-Elizabeth, the biggest container port on the East Coast. Look for stacked containers and giant cranes along Newark Bay next to the airport runways.

name: Nimule National Park
blurb: On the Uganda border, where the White Nile enters South Sudan through the Fula Rapids. Look for the river squeezing between rocky hills before spreading out north toward Juba.

name: Nitmiluk National Park
