blurb: Built around Katherine Gorge, a chain of 13 sandstone gorges carved by the Katherine River. Look for the river zigzagging through red cliff-lined slots in the flat scrubland east of Katherine.

name: Nkasa Rupara National Park
blurb: Swamps, reed islands and channels of the Kwando-Linyanti river system in Namibia's Zambezi Region, sometimes called a mini Okavango. Look for green marsh and lagoons in an otherwise dry landscape.

name: Nki National Park
blurb: Remote rainforest in southeastern Cameroon. Look for unbroken canopy cut by rivers.

name: Nokrek National Park
blurb: Covers Nokrek, the highest peak of Meghalaya's Garo Hills, protected partly for its wild citrus, relatives of the cultivated orange. Look for forested ridges rising from the plains near the Bangladesh border.

name: Norra Kvill National Park
blurb: A tiny patch of old-growth pine and spruce in Småland, protected since 1927, with trees several hundred years old. It hides in the surrounding forest from the air.

name: Norra Sytertoppen
blurb: The high point of the Syter massif in Swedish Lapland, a cluster of bare peaks above deep glacial valleys near the Norwegian border. Look for sharp summits above treeless fells and long lakes.

name: North Gardner Mountain
blurb: Nearly 9,000 ft, one of the highest points in the dry Methow Mountains east of the North Cascades. Look for gray scree slopes above the Methow Valley, often snow-streaked into summer.

name: North Luangwa National Park
blurb: One of Zambia's wildest parks, with no permanent lodges for much of its history, where black rhinos were reintroduced after poaching wiped them out. Look for the Muchinga escarpment along its western edge.

name: Nsumbu National Park
blurb: Zambia's only stretch of Lake Tanganyika shore, with sandy beaches, rocky bays and the clear water of one of the world's deepest lakes. Look for the green hills meeting the lake.

name: Nxai Pan National Park
blurb: Salt pans and grassland north of the Makgadikgadi, with the baobab group painted by Thomas Baines. Look for pale pans in the dry Kalahari.

name: Nyika National Park
blurb: Malawi's largest national park, a rolling grassland plateau mostly above 7,000 ft, cool enough for wild orchids and pine plantations. Look for open green-gold highland standing well above the wooded lowlands around it.

name: Ofu-Olosega
blurb: Two steep, green volcanic islands in American Samoa's Manu'a group, separated by a narrow channel now crossed by a short bridge. Look for the white reef and bright lagoon wrapping Ofu's south shore.

name: Oklahoma City
blurb: One of the largest US cities by area at more than 600 square miles. Look for the 844-ft Devon Tower standing alone over a low downtown, and big lakes on the city's edges.

name: Omaha
blurb: On the Missouri River, whose meanders keep shifting. A flood in 1877 moved the channel and left Carter Lake, Iowa, stranded on the Nebraska side; look for the oxbow lake by the airport.

name: Orang National Park
blurb: Grassland and riverine forest on the Brahmaputra's north bank, nicknamed a mini Kaziranga for its rhinos. Look for grassland between river channels.

name: Organ Needle
blurb: At about 9,000 ft, the high point of the Organ Mountains, a row of jagged granite spires above Las Cruces that look like organ pipes. Look for the saw-tooth skyline east of the city.

name: Orhei National Park
blurb: Moldova's first national park, a patchwork of forest, villages and river valleys north of Chișinău. Look for wooded hills and the tight meanders of the Răut River looping around the cave monastery at Orheiul Vechi.

name: Orlando
blurb: A flat, lake-dotted metro whose biggest draw is the theme-park belt to the southwest. Look for hundreds of round lakes reflecting sun, and Walt Disney World's huge complex off Interstate 4.

name: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve
blurb: Long Beach, the Broken Group Islands and the West Coast Trail on Vancouver Island's open Pacific side. Look for long surf beaches near Tofino.

name: Pali-Aike National Park
blurb: A Patagonian volcanic field of craters and lava flows on the Argentine border, with caves holding some of the oldest traces of people in southern South America. Look for dark lava and round craters on the tan steppe.

name: Pan de Azúcar National Park
blurb: Where the Atacama, the driest nonpolar desert on Earth, runs straight into the Pacific. Humboldt penguins nest on the small island offshore; look for bare brown hills dropping to the surf.

name: Panna National Park
blurb: Tigers were wiped out here by 2009 and reintroduced, now thriving again. Look for the Ken River gorge cutting through the forested plateau.

name: Pantanal Matogrossense National Park
blurb: Sits in the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland, which floods for months each year. Look for a flat mosaic of lagoons, meandering rivers and islands of trees, silver with water in the wet season.

name: Pasig City
blurb: Home to much of Ortigas Center, Metro Manila's second big business district. Look for the Pasig River along its edge and Laguna de Bay, the country's largest lake, just to the southeast.

name: Pavilion Mountain
blurb: A broad mountain north of Lillooet in BC's dry interior, with ranchland on its high plateau. Look for open grassy slopes above the Fraser River canyon.

name: Peak 5214.1
blurb: An unnamed summit of about 17,100 ft in the eastern Pamirs, a high cold desert near the Chinese border. Look for snow-streaked peaks above wide, barren valleys.

name: Peak 5356
blurb: An unnamed summit of about 17,600 ft near Tajikistan's borders with Afghanistan and China, at the eastern end of the Wakhan region. Look for icy peaks above bleak high valleys.

name: Peak 5558
blurb: An unnamed summit of about 18,200 ft in the eastern Pamirs of Tajikistan, a region of high plateaus and glaciated ranges. Look for white peaks rising from tawny, treeless country.

name: Peak of Céüse
blurb: A horseshoe of limestone cliffs above Gap, about 6,600 ft, considered by many one of the finest sport-climbing crags on Earth. Look for the long band of pale cliffs ringing the summit.

name: Pelion
blurb: A forested ridge of about 5,330 ft above Volos, home of the centaurs in Greek myth. Look for a green, hooked peninsula curling around the Pagasetic Gulf.

name: Pench National Park
blurb: The teak forests that inspired the setting of Kipling's Jungle Book. Look for the Pench reservoir snaking through the forest on the state border.

name: Perth
blurb: One of the most isolated big cities on Earth: the nearest city of a million people, Adelaide, is about 1,300 miles away. Look for the Swan River widening into broad lakes beside downtown and the bushland of Kings Park above it.

name: Peña Ubiña
blurb: About 7,900 ft, a limestone massif on the border of Asturias and León in the Cantabrian Mountains. Look for gray crags above green Asturian valleys on one side and the drier meseta on the other.

name: Peñalara
blurb: At 7,966 ft, the highest peak of the Sierra de Guadarrama, the range that walls off Madrid's northern horizon. Look for a rounded summit with glacial lakes, often snow-covered on winter approaches to Madrid.

name: Phnom Kulen National Park
blurb: Where Jayavarman II declared the Khmer Empire in 802; carvings line the riverbed. Look for the sandstone plateau north of Angkor.

name: Phrumsengla National Park
blurb: Temperate forest in eastern Bhutan, crossed by the highway over Thrumshing La pass. Look for deep valleys and high fir ridges.

name: Pica d'Estats
blurb: The highest point in Catalonia at about 10,310 ft, on the French-Spanish border in the eastern Pyrenees. Look for a bare rock summit above a cluster of small glacial lakes.

name: Pico Mágina
blurb: At about 7,100 ft, the highest point of the Sierra Mágina in Jaén, rising out of what may be the largest olive-growing region on Earth. Look for a bare limestone massif surrounded by a sea of olive groves in neat rows.

name: Pico da Antónia
blurb: The highest point on Santiago, Cabo Verde's main island, at about 4,570 ft. Look for a jagged volcanic crest rising from the dry, terraced interior.

name: Pico da Neblina National Park
blurb: Holds Pico da Neblina, Brazil's highest peak at about 9,800 ft, its name meaning peak of mist. Look for jagged peaks rising from the rainforest on the Venezuelan border.

name: Pinzón Island
blurb: A small, steep Galapagos volcano where rats were eradicated in 2012, letting its giant tortoises hatch and survive in the wild for the first time in over a century.

name: Piper Peak
blurb: Highest peak of the Silver Peak Range at about 9,450 ft, west of Tonopah. Look for bare ridges above the white salt flats and lithium ponds of Clayton Valley.

name: Pizzo Carbonara
blurb: At about 6,490 ft, the highest peak of the Madonie and Sicily's second-highest mountain after Etna. Look for bare limestone highlands east of Palermo, sometimes snowy in winter.

name: Podocarpus National Park
blurb: Named for Ecuador's only native conifer, this cloud forest straddles the Andes between Loja and Zamora. Look for steep forested ridges and high lakes on the crest.

name: Point Pelee National Park
blurb: The southernmost tip of mainland Canada, a sharp sandspit pointing into Lake Erie that funnels migrating birds and monarch butterflies. Look for the narrow V of sand with marsh behind it.

name: Pongara National Park
blurb: Across the estuary from Libreville, its beaches are some of the most important leatherback turtle nesting sites in the world. Look for the long sandy point opposite the city.

name: Mount Popa
blurb: An extinct volcano rising from Myanmar's dry central plain, home of the nat spirits in Burmese tradition. Next to it the steep plug of Taung Kalat wears a gold-roofed monastery. Look for the green cone against brown country.

name: Portland
blurb: Nicknamed Bridgetown for the dozen bridges over the Willamette. Look for Mount Hood about 50 miles east, and Forest Park, one of the largest urban forests in the US, on the hills northwest of downtown.

name: Prague
blurb: The Vltava River curves through the city center, which escaped heavy bombing in World War II. Look for Prague Castle, one of the largest ancient castle complexes, on the hill above the river.

name: Prince Albert National Park
blurb: Boreal forest and lakes in central Saskatchewan, where the naturalist Grey Owl lived in the 1930s. Look for big lakes like Waskesiu set where aspen parkland gives way to dark spruce.

name: Prince Edward Island National Park
blurb: Red sandstone cliffs, dunes and beaches along Prince Edward Island's north shore, near the Cavendish of Anne of Green Gables. Look for the red shoreline and pale sandbars against the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

name: Pshish
blurb: A summit of about 12,400 ft in the western Caucasus near Dombay. Look for snow and glaciers on the main crest above forested valleys.

name: Pukaskwa National Park
blurb: Roadless boreal wilderness on the north shore of Lake Superior. Look for rugged granite coast and dark forest running straight into the lake, with barely a trail or building in sight.

name: Pukeamoamo / Mitre
blurb: Highest summit of the Tararua Range at about 5,150 ft, north of Wellington. Look for a ridge, often in cloud, above steep, forested valleys.

name: Puncak Trikora
blurb: At about 15,600 ft, one of the highest peaks in New Guinea. Its glacier, seen by Dutch explorers in 1909, has melted away completely. Look for a pale limestone wall above the Baliem highlands.

name: Purple Hill
blurb: A hill on New Zealand's South Island, in the foothills of the Southern Alps. Look for tussock ridges dropping to braided riverbeds.

name: Queulat National Park
blurb: Famous for its hanging glacier, which spills over a cliff and feeds waterfalls into a green lagoon along the Carretera Austral. Look for the ice tongue perched high above the valley.

name: Rajaji National Park
blurb: Forested Shivalik hills between Haridwar, Rishikesh and Dehradun, a corridor for wild elephants. Look for the Ganges leaving the mountains along the park's edge.

name: Rara National Park
blurb: Surrounds Rara Lake, Nepal's largest lake, at almost 10,000 ft. Look for a deep blue oval set in dark pine forest among the far western hills.

name: Reisa National Park
blurb: A deep canyon in northern Troms carved by the Reisa River, with Mollisfossen, one of Norway's tallest waterfalls, pouring in from the side. Look for a steep green valley cutting through bare Arctic plateau.

name: Rochester
blurb: Home of Kodak and Xerox. The Genesee River drops over a waterfall right downtown on its way to Lake Ontario; look for the river gorge cutting north through the city to the lake.

name: Rock Creek Butte
blurb: At about 9,100 ft, the highest point of the Elkhorn Mountains and of the Blue Mountains of northeast Oregon. Look for a granite crest above Baker Valley.

name: Rodna National Park
blurb: The Rodna Mountains, highest in Romania's Eastern Carpathians, topping out at about 7,560 ft on Pietrosul Rodnei. Look for a long alpine ridge with glacial lakes, often snowy well into spring.

name: Rokatenda
blurb: A volcano forming Palu'e island north of Flores; its 1928 eruption set off a tsunami that killed about 160 people. Look for a small round island with a lava dome on top.

name: Rotterdam
blurb: Europe's largest port, with docks running about 25 miles from downtown out to land reclaimed from the North Sea. Bombed flat in 1940, it rebuilt modern; look for the white Erasmus Bridge over the Maas.

name: Rubondo Island National Park
blurb: A forested island in the southwest of Lake Victoria, protected along with its surrounding waters and smaller islets. Look for the long, narrow green island in the lake.

name: Rusizi National Park
blurb: Delta wetlands where the Rusizi River enters Lake Tanganyika, near Bujumbura, home to hippos and big crocodiles. Look for marshy channels at the north tip of the lake.

name: Ruvubu National Park
blurb: Burundi's largest park, along the Ruvubu River. Look for savanna and gallery forest in the river valley.

name: Río Pilcomayo National Park
blurb: Wetlands and palm savanna on the Pilcomayo River along the Paraguay border. Look for marshes and lagoons in flat plains.

name: Saadani National Park
blurb: Tanzania's only coastal wildlife park, where savanna runs down to an Indian Ocean beach. Look for the Wami River meeting the sea and the strip of sand between bush and water.

name: Sacramento
blurb: California's capital sits where the American River joins the Sacramento, in the flat Central Valley. Look for the two rivers meeting, the tree-shaded downtown grid, and rice fields spreading beyond.

name: Saitama
blurb: Bedroom city formed in 2001 by merging several towns north of Tokyo. Look for continuous suburbs on flat plain, with the Arakawa River's wide floodplain and Saitama Super Arena near the center.

name: Salinas Peak
blurb: Highest point of the San Andres Mountains at about 8,960 ft, inside White Sands Missile Range. Look for a long ridge west of the white gypsum dunes.

name: Salt Lake City
blurb: Laid out by Brigham Young with streets wide enough to turn a wagon team. Look for the grid spreading across the valley floor, the Great Salt Lake to the west and the Wasatch rising straight up to the east.

name: Salvador
blurb: Brazil's first capital, founded in 1549, sits on a peninsula between the Atlantic and the Bay of All Saints. Look for the cliff splitting the upper and lower cities and the huge bay to the west.

name: San Félix Island
blurb: A small volcanic island about 500 miles off the Chilean coast, one of the Desventuradas Islands. A Chilean navy airstrip runs across it.

name: Sandersons Hope
blurb: A sea cliff near Upernavik rising about 3,400 ft, named by the explorer John Davis in 1587 for his backer, William Sanderson. Look for a dark wall dropping straight into Baffin Bay.

name: Santa Margarida Volcano
blurb: An extinct volcano in Catalonia's Garrotxa volcanic zone, its round crater so tidy that a small Romanesque chapel sits alone in the middle of its grassy floor. Look for a near-perfect forested ring with a green clearing inside.

name: Santiago Peak
blurb: At 5,689 ft the highest point in Orange County; with neighboring Modjeska Peak it forms Saddleback, the dip-shaped skyline seen from all over the county. Look for the two humps and the antenna farm on top.

name: Sapo National Park
blurb: Liberia's largest protected rainforest and a refuge for the rare pygmy hippo. Look for unbroken canopy in the southeast of the country.

name: Sapporo
blurb: Host of the 1972 Winter Olympics and the February Snow Festival. Look for a near-perfect grid with Odori Park, a long green strip, running across its middle, and snowy mountains to the west.

name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
blurb: Lost all its tigers to poaching by 2005 and became the first reserve in India to bring them back by relocation. Look for dry, forested Aravalli ridges between Alwar and Jaipur.

name: Satpura National Park
blurb: Satpura hills with the highest point in Madhya Pradesh, Dhoopgarh. Look for rugged forested ridges and the long Tawa reservoir.

name: Sentinel Peak
blurb: A summit in the northern Rockies of BC, near the coal country around Tumbler Ridge. Look for gray limestone ridges above forested foothills.

name: Seoraksan National Park
blurb: Granite peaks near Korea's east coast, topped by Daecheongbong at about 5,600 ft, the country's third-highest. Look for jagged pale rock ridges rising from green forest, blazing red in October.

name: Serra da Canastra National Park
blurb: Holds the source of the São Francisco River, the longest river entirely within Brazil. Look for a flat-topped highland of grassland and rock, where the young river drops off the escarpment at Casca d'Anta falls.

name: Shantar Islands National Park
blurb: Islands in the Sea of Okhotsk, iced in for much of the year, with bowhead whales in their bays. Look for rugged forested islands with steep cliffs.

name: Shark Tooth Mountain
blurb: A sharp peak in the southern Rockies of BC, above the Rocky Mountain Trench near Cranbrook and Kimberley. Look for a pointed rock summit above the trench's broad valley.

name: Sharr Mountains National Park
blurb: Kosovo's side of the Sharr range on the border with North Macedonia, with treeless ridges above 8,000 ft. Look for bare green-gray crests above the Prizren plain.

name: Shimbiris
blurb: The highest point in Somalia at about 7,900 ft, in the Cal Madow range above the Gulf of Aden. Look for a juniper-dotted ridge rising sharply from the arid coastal plain.

name: Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park
blurb: Forested hills on the northern rim of the Kathmandu Valley, supplying much of the city's water. Look for the dark green ridge of Shivapuri just beyond the dense sprawl of Kathmandu.

name: Shuklaphanta National Park
blurb: Holds some of the largest open grasslands in the Terai and one of the biggest herds of swamp deer left. Look for pale grassy meadows along the Indian border in Nepal's far southwest.

name: Sibillini Mountains National Park
blurb: Monte Vettore tops out above 8,000 ft, and the Piano Grande below it blooms with lentil and wildflower colors in early summer. Look for the flat, treeless basin ringed by mountains.

name: Sierra La Concordia (Saltillo)
blurb: One of the folded limestone ranges of the Sierra Madre Oriental around Saltillo. Look for long, curving ridges above the city and its industrial parks.

name: Sierra de La Sagra
blurb: La Sagra, about 7,800 ft, is the highest peak in northern Granada province, a lone limestone massif that holds snow late into spring. Look for a pale, isolated summit rising over high dry plateau.

name: Sierra de San Marcos
blurb: A long limestone range in central Coahuila near Cuatro Ciénegas, whose desert pools and gypsum dunes sit just to the east. Look for a dry, folded ridge above white gypsum flats.

name: Sierra de la Giganta
blurb: A rugged volcanic range running along the Gulf of California behind Loreto, its cliffs dropping almost straight into the sea. Look for brown, layered ridges between turquoise water and desert.

name: Sierra del Carmen
blurb: Its limestone cliffs face Big Bend National Park across the Rio Grande and glow pink and orange at sunset, a famous view from the Texas side. Look for a long sheer escarpment just south of the river.

name: Simlipal National Park
blurb: A large tiger reserve of sal forest in the hills of northern Odisha, with Barehipani, one of India's tallest waterfalls. Look for a dome of unbroken forest surrounded by farmland.

name: Singalila National Park
blurb: Its ridge carries Sandakphu, the highest point in West Bengal at about 11,900 ft, with a view of four of the world's five highest peaks, including Everest and Kangchenjunga. Look for the long ridge on the Nepal border.

name: Sirmilik National Park
blurb: Takes in Bylot Island and the northern tip of Baffin Island, with glaciers flowing to the sea and huge seabird colonies. Look for ice-capped mountains above the sea ice of Lancaster Sound.

name: Skarvan and Roltdalen National Park
blurb: Mountain and forest east of Trondheim, with the bare Skarvan massif rising above the wooded Roltdalen valley. Look for open summits above spruce forest and bog.

name: Skeleton Coast National Park
blurb: Named for the whale bones and shipwrecks along its fog-bound shore, where the Namib's dunes run straight into the cold Atlantic. Look for a sharp line of tan desert against gray-blue sea, often under a bank of fog.

name: Skuleskogen National Park
blurb: On Sweden's High Coast, where land is rising faster than almost anywhere after the Ice Age; old shorelines sit far above today's sea. Look for the forested hills dropping straight into the Gulf of Bothnia.

name: Slide Mountain
blurb: At 4,180 ft, the highest point in the Catskills. Look for a forested dome about 20 miles west of the Hudson River.

name: Socorro Island
blurb: The largest of Mexico's Revillagigedo Islands, about 400 miles off the coast, part of a marine reserve known for giant manta rays. A Mexican navy post sits on the island's south shore.

name: Souss-Massa National Park
blurb: Holds most of the world's wild northern bald ibis, a critically endangered bird, on the Atlantic coast south of Agadir. Look for a thin strip of dunes and cliffs where the Souss and Massa rivers meet the sea.

name: South Baldy
blurb: Highest point of the Magdalena Mountains at about 10,780 ft, west of Socorro. Look for a forested summit above the Plains of San Agustin, home of the Very Large Array radio telescopes.

name: Southwest National Park
blurb: Tasmania's largest national park, a roadless wilderness of rainforest, buttongrass plains and jagged quartzite ranges. Look for the dammed waters of Lake Pedder and the white peaks of the Western Arthurs.

name: Stenshuvud National Park
blurb: A wooded headland rising sharply from the flat coast of southeast Skåne, with long sandy beaches on either side. Look for the dark hump of forest on the Baltic shore.

name: Stockholm
blurb: Built on 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic. Look for Gamla Stan, the old town on its own small island, and an archipelago of some 30,000 islands spreading east to the sea.

name: Store Mosse National Park
blurb: The largest raised bog in southern Sweden, a wide open expanse of moss and pools in Småland. Look for the pale, treeless patch with a large lake at its edge.

name: Swasey Mountain
blurb: At about 9,700 ft, the highest point of the House Range in western Utah, a tilted fault block with a gentle east slope and steep cliffs on the west. Look for a lone ridge above the dry Tule Valley.

name: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve
blurb: Maharashtra's oldest and largest national park, home to a large tiger population. Look for Tadoba Lake and teak forest amid farmland.

name: Takamatsu
blurb: Shikoku's port on the Seto Inland Sea, known for Ritsurin Garden and udon. Ferries run to Naoshima and the other art islands. Look for the island-dotted sea and flat-topped Yashima plateau to the east.

name: Talassemtane National Park
blurb: Limestone peaks of the western Rif above Chefchaouen, protecting the Moroccan fir, found almost nowhere else. Look for gray rock ridges and deep gorges, including the natural arch known as God's Bridge.

name: Tara National Park
blurb: Forested mountains above the Drina River canyon in western Serbia, refuge of the Serbian spruce, a relic tree found almost nowhere else. Look for a dark green plateau ending at the canyon and Perućac reservoir on the Bosnian border.

name: Taveuni
blurb: Fiji's "Garden Island," a 26-mile volcanic ridge straddling the 180th meridian. It catches heavy rain and stays densely green. Look for a long, narrow island with a forested spine and reefs along its shores.

name: Tayrona National Natural Park
blurb: Where the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the world's highest coastal range, drops into the Caribbean. Look for small coves of white sand framed by giant granite boulders and jungle.

name: Tazekka National Park
blurb: Wooded mountains around Jbel Tazekka near Taza, with cedar and cork oak forest and the deep Friouato cave. Look for a forested dome standing out from the drier farmland around it.

name: Te Urewera
blurb: No longer a national park: in 2014 New Zealand made it a legal entity that owns itself, the first natural area given legal personhood. Look for endless rugged forest and the blue arms of Lake Waikaremoana in the southeast.

name: Tehran
blurb: About 9 million people climbing the slopes of the Alborz Mountains. Look for 18,400-ft Mount Damavand, a snowcapped volcano, to the northeast, and the needle of Milad Tower in the city's west.

name: Tekao
blurb: The high point of Nuku Hiva, largest of the Marquesas, at about 4,000 ft. Look for a high plateau and the sharp ridges of an old caldera, with deep bays cut into the coast below.

name: Teleno
blurb: At about 7,200 ft, the high point of the Montes de León, a mountain the Romans tied to a local war god, Mars Tilenus. Look for a broad, bare summit above the gold-mining country of El Bierzo and the plains of León.

name: Temetiu
blurb: The highest peak on Hiva Oa in the Marquesas at about 4,200 ft, the island where Paul Gauguin and Jacques Brel are buried. Look for a steep green ridge above the bays of the south coast.

name: Terra Nova National Park
blurb: Canada's easternmost national park, on the rocky inlets of Bonavista Bay. Look for long fingers of sea reaching into boreal forest and bog; in spring, icebergs may drift past the coast.

name: Tesso Nilo National Park
blurb: Created for Sumatran elephants, much of it has been cleared for illegal oil palm. Look for the ragged remnant forest surrounded by the gridded rows of plantations.

name: The Hague
blurb: The seat of the Dutch government and parliament, though Amsterdam is the capital, and home to the International Court of Justice in the Peace Palace. Look for Scheveningen's beach and pier on the North Sea.

name: Thompson Peak
blurb: About 9,000 ft, the highest peak in the Trinity Alps, holding a few small glaciers in northwestern California. Look for white granite and bits of ice above dark forest.

name: Thousand Islands National Park
blurb: One of Canada's smallest national parks, a scatter of granite islands in the St. Lawrence River where it leaves Lake Ontario. Look for dozens of wooded islands, many topped with a single cottage, threaded by shipping channels.

name: Thumb Peak
blurb: A rocky, thumb-shaped summit in the forested mountains of central Palawan near Puerto Princesa. Look for a lone crag poking up from an unbroken green ridge.

name: Thy National Park
blurb: Denmark's first national park, opened in 2008: dunes, heath and lakes behind the North Sea beaches of northwest Jutland. Look for the long straight coast with pale dunes and dark lakes inland.

name: Tiger Island
blurb: A near-perfect volcanic cone rising from the Gulf of Fonseca, where Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua meet. Look for the round island with the old port town of Amapala at its foot.

name: Tlemcen National Park
blurb: Wooded hills and waterfalls on the plateau above the old city of Tlemcen. Look for green slopes and gorges at the city's edge.

name: Toro Toro National Park
blurb: Thousands of dinosaur footprints, plus deep canyons and caves. Look for red folded rock and canyons.

name: Torre
blurb: The highest point in mainland Portugal at 6,539 ft, atop the Serra da Estrela. A stone tower was built on the summit to push the total to an even 6,562 ft, a round number in metric. Look for a bare granite plateau, sometimes snowy in winter.

name: Tortuguero National Park
blurb: Green sea turtles nest on its beach by the thousands, and there are no roads in: just boats and planes. Look for a ruler-straight Caribbean beach with canals running parallel behind it.

name: Trapper Peak
blurb: Highest peak of the Bitterroot Range at 10,157 ft, above the Bitterroot Valley south of Missoula. Look for a gray, granite crest with glacial cirques facing north.

name: Trask Mountain
blurb: A peak of about 3,400 ft in the northern Oregon Coast Range, in the forest of the old Tillamook Burn. Look for dark ridges between the Willamette Valley and the coast.

name: Troglav
blurb: About 6,300 ft, the highest peak of the Dinara range, just inside Bosnia near the Croatian border. Look for a long bare limestone ridge, pale gray against green and brown karst.

name: Truchas Peak
blurb: New Mexico's second-highest peak at about 13,100 ft, in the Pecos Wilderness. Look for a rocky crest above treeline north of Santa Fe.

name: Tsavo West National Park
blurb: Mzima Springs and the black Shetani lava flow are here, part of the vast Tsavo ecosystem. Look for volcanic cones and dark lava on red earth, with Kilimanjaro to the west.

name: Tsingy de Namoroka National Park
blurb: Razor-sharp limestone pinnacles and caves in western Madagascar. Look for a gray, pitted limestone plateau in dry forest.

name: Tuktut Nogait National Park
blurb: Calving ground for the Bluenose West caribou herd, east of Paulatuk in the western Arctic. Look for treeless tundra slashed by the deep canyon of the Hornaday River.

name: Tulsa
blurb: Once the Oil Capital of the World, with a downtown full of Art Deco built on oil money. Look for the Arkansas River and the Gathering Place, a large riverside park opened in 2018.

name: Ubajara National Park
blurb: One of Brazil's smallest national parks, known for a limestone cave reached by cable car from the Ibiapaba cliffs. Look for green escarpment above the dry sertão.

name: Udzungwa Mountains National Park
blurb: Part of the Eastern Arc, ancient forested mountains with species found nowhere else, including two endemic monkeys. Look for the steep green escarpment rising above the Kilombero valley and the Sanje waterfall.

name: Ukkusiksalik National Park
blurb: Surrounds Wager Bay, a nearly landlocked inlet of Hudson Bay with fierce reversing tidal rapids at its mouth. Look for a long arm of sea pushing into treeless rocky tundra.

name: Ulu Temburong National Park
blurb: Pristine rainforest in Brunei's Temburong district, cut off from the rest of the country by Malaysia. Look for unbroken canopy on steep hills.

name: Uncompahgre Peak
blurb: At 14,309 ft the highest peak in the San Juan Mountains, with a gentle south side and a sheer north face. Look for a tilted, flat-topped summit that looks chopped off on one side.

name: Upemba National Park
blurb: One of Africa's oldest parks, spanning a high plateau and the Upemba Depression, a basin of lakes and papyrus marsh along the Lualaba River. Look for the chain of lakes and swamps in the lowland.

name: Vaganski vrh
blurb: About 5,760 ft, the highest point of Croatia's Velebit range, which runs along the Adriatic coast above Paklenica's canyons. Look for a bare gray limestone crest right above the sea and its islands.

name: Valmiki National Park
blurb: Bihar's only tiger reserve, on the Nepal border next to Chitwan. Look for the forest belt along the foothills.

name: Vansda National Park
blurb: A small block of moist forest in south Gujarat near the Maharashtra border, along the Ambika River. Look for green hills amid farmland.

name: Vavul Mala
blurb: A summit of the Western Ghats on the edge of Wayanad, rising above Kerala's coastal plain. Look for a steep green escarpment and plantations climbing its slopes.

name: Virachey National Park
blurb: Remote forest in Cambodia's northeast corner, bordering Laos and Vietnam. Look for unbroken jungle hills.

name: Vogelsberg
blurb: The largest continuous basalt area in Central Europe, an old volcano worn down into a broad dome of forest and pasture in Hesse. Look for a wide, round upland with streams radiating out like spokes.

name: Vuntut National Park
blurb: Covers part of Old Crow Flats, a vast wetland of thousands of lakes north of the Arctic Circle in the Vuntut Gwitchin homeland. Look for the plain speckled with countless small ponds.

name: Wapusk National Park
blurb: One of the largest polar bear denning areas in the world, on the Hudson Bay coast south of Churchill. Look for flat tundra pocked with thousands of small lakes, edged by a bay that freezes white in winter.

name: Washington
blurb: Laid out in 1791 by Pierre L'Enfant with diagonal avenues over a grid. Look for the National Mall, a 2-mile green strip from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, with the Washington Monument as a white needle.

name: Waza National Park
blurb: Sahel floodplain south of Lake Chad, with seasonal marshes that draw elephants and birds. Look for flat grassland and pans.

name: West Spanish Peak
blurb: About 13,600 ft, the taller of the twin Spanish Peaks, ringed by hundreds of volcanic dikes that radiate across the plains like spokes. Look for the twin summits standing alone, with long rock walls running out from them.

name: Wheeler Peak
blurb: New Mexico's highest point at 13,161 ft, just above Taos Ski Valley. Look for bare summits above the ski runs, with the Rio Grande Gorge cutting the plateau to the west.

name: Whitewater Baldy
blurb: Highest point of the Mogollon Mountains at about 10,900 ft, in the Gila, the world's first designated wilderness area (1924). Look for a forested range scarred by recent wildfires.

name: Wicklow Mountains National Park
blurb: The mountains behind Dublin, with Glendalough's monastic valley. Look for Lough Tay, a dark lake with a pale sandy beach that looks like a pint of Guinness.

name: Wild Nephin National Park
blurb: Blanket bog and the empty Nephin Beg mountains in Mayo, one of the darkest skies in Europe and part of a certified dark sky park. Look for brown bog with almost no roads or houses.

name: Wilpattu National Park
blurb: Sri Lanka's largest national park, named for its villus: dozens of round, rain-fed lakes scattered through dry forest. Look for the shallow water bowls dotting the green near the northwest coast.

name: Wilsons Promontory National Park
blurb: The southernmost point of mainland Australia, a granite peninsula of mountains, white beaches and rocky islands. Look for the knob of land hanging off the coast on a thin sandy neck.

name: Winnipeg
blurb: Grew at The Forks, where the Red and Assiniboine rivers meet, in the middle of the continent. A 29-mile floodway dug in the 1960s diverts the Red River around town; look for the channel on the east side.

name: Wyoming Peak
blurb: At 11,378 ft the highest summit of the Wyoming Range, south of Jackson. Look for a bald gray crest above long forested ridges running north to south.

name: Wŏnsan
blurb: A port on North Korea's east coast where the government built the Kalma beach resort on the sandy peninsula next to the old airport. Look for the long spit and high-rise hotels along the bay.

name: Yacurí National Park
blurb: High páramo and cloud forest on Ecuador's southern border with Peru, dotted with small glacial lakes. Look for treeless ridges above the forest line.

name: Yangudi Rassa National Park
blurb: Afar desert set aside largely for the critically endangered African wild ass. Look for dry lava plains and the dormant cone of Mount Yangudi.

name: Yankari National Park
blurb: Best known for Wikki Warm Springs, a clear spring that stays near 88 degrees F year-round, and one of West Africa's larger elephant herds. Look for savanna woodland cut by the Gaji River.

name: Yekaterinburg
blurb: Founded in 1723 on the eastern slope of the Urals, near the line between Europe and Asia, and where the last tsar and his family were executed in 1918. Look for the dammed Iset River widening into a pond downtown.

name: Zaamin National Park
blurb: Juniper forest and mountain meadows on the Turkestan Range, among Uzbekistan's oldest protected areas. Look for the dark green slopes above the dry plains to the north.

name: Zardak Peak
blurb: High point of the Kirthar Range near the Sindh-Balochistan border. Look for long, parallel brown ridges above the desert.

name: Zavodovski Island
region: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
blurb: A volcanic island at the north end of the South Sandwich chain, home to one of the world's largest penguin colonies, chinstraps by the hundreds of thousands. Look for a small dark island with a steaming summit.

name: Ängsö National Park
blurb: One of Sweden's first national parks, from 1909: a small island in the Stockholm archipelago kept as traditional meadow and pasture, famous for spring flowers. Look for open fields on an island amid dark wooded skerries.

name: Île Amsterdam
blurb: One of the most isolated islands on Earth, in the southern Indian Ocean, home to a small French research station and the rare Amsterdam albatross, found nowhere else. Look for a lone volcanic island with sheer western cliffs.

name: Île Saint-Paul
blurb: A volcano whose crater broke open to the sea, leaving a near-circular natural harbor inside the island. Look for the ring of cliffs with a narrow gap on the east side.

name: Ølfjellet
blurb: A mountain in Nordland near the Svartisen glacier, among Norway's largest icefields. Look for ice-capped summits above deep valleys.

name: Øvre Pasvik National Park
blurb: Old-growth pine forest and bogs in the far northeast corner of Norway, wedged between Finland and Russia. Look for flat taiga laced with lakes along the Pasvik River.

name: İzmir
blurb: Turkey's third-largest city, wrapped around the long Gulf of İzmir. Look for the narrow bay, the old Kadifekale castle on its hill, and salt pans near the gulf's mouth.

name: Žemaitija National Park
blurb: Lake Plateliai and the Plokštinė Soviet nuclear missile base, now a Cold War museum. Look for the lake and its islands in dense forest.

name: Zhengzhou
blurb: Henan's capital, where China's main north-south and east-west rail lines cross; Foxconn's giant iPhone plant sits near the airport. Look for the Yellow River's wide braided channel just north of the city.

name: Baoding
blurb: Old provincial capital that guarded the southern approach to Beijing for centuries, now home of Great Wall Motors. Look for a flat grid on the North China Plain, with Baiyangdian, the region's largest lake, to the east.

name: Shijiazhuang
blurb: Hebei's capital grew from a village to a city of millions mainly because railways crossed here in the early 1900s. Look for a broad grid on the flat plain with the Taihang Mountains rising to the west.

name: Nanyang
blurb: City in the Nanyang Basin of southwest Henan. The central route of the South-North Water Transfer starts in its territory at Danjiangkou Reservoir. Look for the straight canal heading north across the plain.

name: Wenzhou
blurb: Famous across China for its entrepreneurs, who built empires in shoes, lighters and buttons. The city lines the Ou River estuary, hemmed in by green mountains and mudflats.

name: Weifang
blurb: Calls itself the kite capital of the world and hosts an international kite festival every spring. Look for a big flat city on the plain south of Laizhou Bay, with salt pans and fish ponds along the coast to the north.

name: Xuzhou
blurb: Crossroads city in northern Jiangsu, home of the Han dynasty founder's clan. Han tombs here yielded a small terracotta army. Look for Yunlong Lake against the hills just southwest of downtown.

name: Changchun
blurb: China's car capital: First Automobile Works rolled out the country's first trucks here in 1956, and the city was the capital of Japan's puppet state Manchukuo. Look for wide, ruler-straight boulevards and the lake of Nanhu Park.

name: Ganzhou
blurb: Where the Zhang and Gong rivers meet to form the Gan. Its Song dynasty wall still lines the riverbanks, and the region is a major rare earth source. Look for the old town on the point between the rivers.

name: Quanzhou
blurb: A medieval port that Marco Polo knew as Zayton, one of the largest in the world in the Song and Yuan dynasties and now a UNESCO site. Look for the Jin River delta spreading into Quanzhou Bay.

name: Jining
blurb: Hub of Confucius country: his hometown of Qufu is part of the prefecture. Look for the Grand Canal passing through and the long, shallow Nansi lakes to the south.

name: Fuzhou
blurb: Fujian's capital lies in a basin on the Min River, ringed by hills, nicknamed the Banyan City for its trees. Look for the wide river splitting around islands as it heads to the sea.

name: Fuyang
blurb: A huge farming-region city on the North China Plain in northern Anhui, along the Ying River. Look for a dense urban core set in a patchwork of flat green fields.

name: Veracruz
blurb: Mexico's oldest port and still one of its busiest, founded by Cortés in 1519. Look for the fortress of San Juan de Ulúa on an island in the harbor.

name: Shangqiu
blurb: Ancient city in eastern Henan whose walled Ming-era old town is ringed by a wide moat-lake. Look for the square town sitting in a ring of water, south of the modern city.

name: Nantong
blurb: City on the north bank of the Yangtze near its mouth. The Sutong Bridge, the world's longest cable-stayed span when it opened in 2008, crosses here. Look for its two tall towers over the wide brown river.

name: Tangshan
blurb: In 1976 an earthquake leveled the city and killed at least 240,000 people, one of the deadliest of the 20th century. Rebuilt as a steel town; look for mills and the Caofeidian port on the Bohai coast to the south.

name: Cangzhou
blurb: Grand Canal city famous for martial arts and for a cast iron lion over 1,000 years old, one of the largest in China. Look for the canal looping through town on the flat plain near the Bohai coast.

name: Yantai
blurb: A port on the north coast of the Shandong Peninsula and the heart of China's wine country. Look for the city along the sea with orchards and vineyards in the hills behind.

name: Luoyang
blurb: Capital of more than a dozen dynasties. South of town, the Longmen Grottoes hold tens of thousands of Buddha statues carved into riverside cliffs starting in the 5th century. Look for the gorge where the Yi River cuts the hills.

name: Jinhua
blurb: Home of Jinhua ham, and its territory includes Yiwu, the world's biggest wholesale market for small goods. A basin city in central Zhejiang ringed by low mountains.

name: Zhanjiang
blurb: A port city on the Leizhou Peninsula, China's southern mainland tip, with a deep harbor used by the South Sea Fleet. Look for the long sheltered bay and Donghai Island across the water.

name: Bijie
blurb: Hilly city in northwest Guizhou near the Baili Rhododendron forest, miles of wild azaleas that bloom red and pink each spring. Look for a town squeezed into steep, terraced karst hills.

name: Yangon
blurb: The gilded Shwedagon Pagoda, about 325 ft tall on a hill above the city, has dominated Yangon for centuries. Look for the gold spire flashing in the sun and the lakes of Inya and Kandawgyi.

name: Yancheng
blurb: Its coastal tidal flats, part of a UNESCO site, shelter millions of migratory birds and a reserve for the once-extinct-in-China Pere David's deer. Look for the vast mudflats and salt pans along the Yellow Sea.

name: Hengyang
blurb: Where the Zheng and Lei rivers join the Xiang. To the north rises Mount Heng, the southern of China's Five Great Mountains. Look for the river junction and the mountain ridge beyond.

name: Taizhou
blurb: Coastal Zhejiang city (not the Taizhou in Jiangsu) of private manufacturing, with Mount Tiantai, birthplace of a major school of Chinese Buddhism, in its hills. Look for a coastline of islands and reclaimed mudflats.

name: Zunyi
blurb: At the 1935 Zunyi Conference, during the Long March, Mao Zedong became the Communist Party's leading figure. Moutai liquor is distilled in nearby Maotai town. Look for the city spread along a valley among green karst hills.

name: Shaoyang
blurb: Central Hunan city on the Zi River in rolling hill country. Look for the river curving through town among terraced green hills.

name: Huanggang
blurb: City on the north bank of the Yangtze downstream from Wuhan, facing Ezhou across the river. Look for the broad river, lakes and the Dabie foothills to the north.

name: Santiago
blurb: About 7 million people in a valley walled by the Andes, with peaks over 17,000 ft just 30 miles east. Look for the bare hills like San Cristóbal inside the city and the snowy wall of mountains above.

name: Xinxiang
blurb: Henan city on the flat plain just north of the Yellow River. Look for a grid of streets, irrigation canals and the Taihang foothills rising to the northwest.

name: Xinyang
blurb: Southern Henan city famous for Xinyang Maojian green tea grown on the hills around it. Look for tea terraces and reservoirs in the Dabie foothills, with Nanwan Reservoir to the southwest.

name: Pune
blurb: A university, auto and IT hub about 1,800 ft up on the Deccan Plateau, where the Mula and Mutha rivers meet. Look for forested hills and Maratha hill forts like Sinhagad on the southwest skyline.

name: Maoming
blurb: A petrochemical city in western Guangdong, grown on oil shale mining. Look for refineries and the long sandy coast to the south.

name: Huizhou
blurb: A Pearl River Delta city known for West Lake, a scenic lake in the center, and a big petrochemical complex at Daya Bay. Look for the lakes downtown and the East River curving past.

name: Prayagraj
blurb: Hindu holy city where the Ganges and Yamuna meet, host of the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest gatherings of people on Earth. Look for the muddy Ganges and greener Yamuna joining at the Sangam.

name: Liaocheng
blurb: The water city of the North China Plain: its old town sits on an island in Dongchang Lake, and the Grand Canal passes nearby. Look for the square old center surrounded by water.

name: Surat
blurb: Most of the world's diamonds, by common estimate about 90%, are cut and polished here. The Tapi River bends through the city toward the Arabian Sea; the Surat Diamond Bourse is among the largest office buildings anywhere.

name: Yulin
blurb: Inland Guangxi city known for one of China's biggest traditional medicine markets and, notoriously, a summer dog-meat festival. Look for a compact city in a basin of low green hills.

name: Changde
blurb: City on the Yuan River near Dongting Lake, known for its long flood wall carved with classical poems. Look for the river's broad bend and the lake country stretching east.

name: Ankara
blurb: Turkey's capital since 1923, chosen by Atatürk for its central position on the Anatolian plateau. Look for Anıtkabir, his massive hilltop mausoleum, and the old citadel on its rocky outcrop.

name: Yueyang
blurb: Where Dongting Lake drains into the Yangtze. Yueyang Tower is one of the Three Great Towers of southern China. The lake swells in summer and shrinks to channels and grassland in winter.

name: Qujing
blurb: Eastern Yunnan's industrial hub on a plateau above 6,000 ft. The Pearl River system, which reaches the sea beside Hong Kong, traditionally traces its source to the hills here.

name: Addis Ababa
blurb: Ethiopia's capital and home of the African Union, about 7,700 ft up in the highlands. Look for eucalyptus groves around the city and the Entoto mountains rising on the north side.

name: Xiangyang
blurb: Twin city on the Han River with a Song-era wall and one of China's widest city moats. Its fall to the Mongols in 1273, after a five-year siege, opened the way to the conquest of the Song.

name: Dezhou
blurb: A Grand Canal city on Shandong's northern edge, known for braised chicken and a solar-power industry park called Solar Valley. Look for flat farmland running to the horizon in every direction.

name: Nanchong
blurb: An old silk city on the Jialing River in the Sichuan Basin. Look for the river's broad meanders looping around the city.

name: Jieyang
blurb: A Chaoshan region city on the Rong River, sharing an airport with Shantou. Look for the dense lowland city among canals and green paddy.

name: Jingzhou
blurb: Old Yangtze city whose brick wall, ringed by a moat, is one of the best preserved in China. Look for the wall's rectangle of water and greenery in the middle of town.

name: Shantou
blurb: One of China's first four special economic zones, in 1980, at the mouth of the Han River. Look for the large bay with the city on its north shore and bridges reaching across to the south bank.

name: Anyang
blurb: Site of Yin, the late Shang dynasty capital, where oracle bones inscribed more than 3,000 years ago preserve the earliest known Chinese writing. Look for the Huan River winding through the city on the flat plain.

name: Tai'an
blurb: The city at the foot of Mount Tai, China's most sacred mountain, climbed by emperors for over 2,000 years. Look for the 5,000-ft massif rising straight up from the town's north edge.

name: Dazhou
blurb: An industrial city in northeast Sichuan with large natural gas fields nearby. Look for the city along a river valley between the long, parallel ridges of eastern Sichuan.

name: Langfang
blurb: Sits between Beijing and Tianjin. Beijing Daxing International, whose terminal looks like a giant starfish, straddles its border with Beijing. Look for the five-armed terminal north of town.

name: Suihua
blurb: Farm city on the Songnen Plain, in the heart of Heilongjiang's black-soil grain belt. Look for huge flat fields of corn, soybeans and rice stretching to the horizon.

name: Jiaxing
blurb: Halfway between Shanghai and Hangzhou, threaded by the Grand Canal. China's Communist Party finished its founding congress in 1921 on a tour boat on the city's South Lake, hiding from police.

name: Qiqihar
blurb: Northern city on the Nen River near Zhalong, a vast reed marsh that is a breeding ground for red-crowned cranes. Look for wetlands and the braided river spreading across the flat plain.

name: Khartoum
blurb: Where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet. Look for the two rivers joining, the darker Blue Nile running side by side with the paler White Nile for a stretch before they mix.

name: Kabul
blurb: A city of millions in a high basin about 5,900 ft up, ringed by bare mountains with houses climbing their slopes. Look for the flat brown sprawl hemmed in by ridges.

name: Taiyuan
blurb: Shanxi's capital, a coal and steel city with over 2,000 years of history. Look for the Fen River running north to south through the middle, lined with long riverside parks.

name: Yongzhou
blurb: Southern Hunan city where the Xiao River joins the Xiang. Look for the two rivers meeting among green hills and karst outcrops.

name: Changzhou
blurb: Grand Canal city between Nanjing and Shanghai, with a large dinosaur theme park. Look for the canal cutting through town and Lake Ge and Lake Tai's northern edge to the south.

name: Shaoxing
blurb: A canal city of stone bridges and black-roofed houses, famous for Shaoxing rice wine and as the hometown of writer Lu Xun. Look for waterways laced through the flat plain south of Hangzhou Bay.

name: Zhaotong
blurb: Northeastern Yunnan city on a high, cold plateau above 6,000 ft, known for apples. In 2014 an earthquake in its Ludian County killed more than 600 people; look for terraced farmland on deeply folded hills.

name: Guilin
blurb: Limestone towers rise straight out of the city and the river flats, the scenery on China's 20-yuan note. Look for hundreds of green sugarloaf peaks poking up like teeth, with the Li River winding between them toward Yangshuo.

name: Zhangzhou
blurb: A city on the Jiulong River delta west of Xiamen, known for oranges, narcissus flowers and the earthen tulou roundhouses in its hills. Look for the river winding through green fruit farms.

name: Pingdingshan
blurb: Coal city in central Henan. In its Lushan County stands the Spring Temple Buddha, about 420 ft tall including its pedestal, one of the tallest statues in the world. Look for mine heaps and reservoirs among the hills.

name: Suqian
blurb: Hometown of Xiang Yu, the warlord who fought Liu Bang for the empire, and of Yanghe liquor. Look for the city between Luoma Lake and Hongze Lake, two big sheets of water on the plain.

name: Huaihua
blurb: Rail junction in the Wuling hills of western Hunan, on the Yuan River. Look for the city in a valley crossed by rail lines, with forested ridges all around.

name: Xiaogan
blurb: City on the flat Jianghan Plain northwest of Wuhan, its name meaning filial piety. Look for lakes, paddy fields and the Han River's plain spreading to the south.

name: Yibin
blurb: Where the Min River meets the Jinsha and the Yangtze officially takes its name, and the home of Wuliangye liquor. Look for the two rivers joining at a point of land in the city.

name: Mianyang
blurb: China's western science city, home to the national nuclear weapons research academy. Look for the Fu River winding through town at the north end of the Chengdu plain, with mountains to the west.

name: Kaifeng
blurb: Capital of the Northern Song, when it was among the largest cities in the world. Yellow River floods have buried several older cities beneath its streets. Look for the walled old town with lakes inside it.

name: Jiangmen
blurb: The ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, especially Chinese Americans and Canadians. Look for the fortified watchtowers called diaolou in Kaiping, and the river delta fish ponds around the city.

name: Chenzhou
blurb: Southern Hunan city near the Guangdong border. Nearby Dongjiang Lake, a reservoir in steep green hills, is famous for morning mist drifting over the water. Look for the long winding reservoir east of town.

name: Zibo
blurb: Capital of the ancient state of Qi, later a ceramics and chemicals town, and the site of a viral barbecue craze in 2023. Look for a sprawling city of separate districts strung across hills and plain.

name: Jeddah
blurb: Saudi Arabia's Red Sea gateway, where pilgrims bound for Mecca have landed for centuries. Look for the long corniche along the sea and, when it's running, King Fahd's Fountain, one of the tallest fountains in the world.

name: Weinan
blurb: A city on the Wei River plain east of Xi'an, not far from where the Wei joins the Yellow River. Look for flat farmland along the river with the granite ridges of Mount Hua rising to the southeast.

name: Jiujiang
blurb: Yangtze city at the outlet of Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake. Look for the lake meeting the river and the steep ridge of Mount Lushan rising just to the south.

name: Lianyungang
blurb: Seaport at the eastern end of the rail land bridge across Asia to Europe. Huaguo Mountain nearby is said to be the Monkey King's home in Journey to the West. Look for the port and the long breakwater to Xilian Island.

name: Kanpur
blurb: A big industrial city on the Ganges, long known for leather and textiles. Look for the wide river running along the city's northern edge, with sandbars in the dry season.

name: Yangzhou
blurb: Grand Canal city that grew rich on salt; Marco Polo claimed to have governed it. Look for Slender West Lake's narrow winding water through parkland, and the canal on the east side.

name: Huai'an
blurb: Birthplace of Zhou Enlai, where the Grand Canal crosses the Huai River. Look for Hongze Lake to the west and the canal and rivers crossing on the flat plain.

name: Taizhou
blurb: Old city in central Jiangsu north of the Yangtze, among canals and flat rice country. Look for a web of waterways and fish ponds around town.

name: Kolkata
blurb: Capital of British India until 1911, now a metro of roughly 15 million on the Hooghly River. Look for the Howrah Bridge's steel cantilever and the Maidan, a huge green park beside downtown.

name: Hengshui
blurb: Known across China for an intensely strict high school that turns out top exam scores, and for Hengshui Lake, a large wetland reserve next to the city. Look for the lake's reedy shallows south of town.

name: Zhongshan
blurb: Named after Sun Yat-sen, born nearby, it sits in the heart of the Pearl River Delta. Look for a flat landscape of rivers, fish ponds and factories with low green hills in the middle of the city.

name: Yiyang
blurb: Hunan city on the Zi River just south of Dongting Lake. Look for the river and the flat lake country with paddies and fish ponds to the north.

name: Jilin City
blurb: The Songhua River swings through town in a wide S-curve. In winter, warm water from the Fengman Dam upstream fogs the cold air and coats riverside trees in white rime ice, a famous sight.

name: Guigang
blurb: River port on the Yu River, one of the busiest inland ports in southwest China, shipping cargo downstream toward Guangzhou. Look for the wide river lined with barges and flat sugarcane country around it.

name: Lu'an
blurb: A city in western Anhui where the North China Plain meets the Dabie Mountains, known for Lu'an Guapian green tea. Look for the reservoirs and hills rising to the southwest.

name: Xuchang
blurb: Where Cao Cao kept the last Han emperor as his puppet. Today it makes a large share of the world's human-hair wigs. Look for a compact city amid flat wheat fields.

name: Meizhou
blurb: Called the world capital of the Hakka people, in the hilly northeast of Guangdong. Look for a city along the Mei River's curves, ringed by green hills.

name: Lanzhou
blurb: The first big city on the Yellow River, squeezed into a narrow valley between bare loess hills. Look for the city stretched for miles along the river, and terraced brown hills on both sides.

name: Kano
blurb: One of the oldest cities in West Africa, a Saharan trade hub for a thousand years. Its Kofar Mata dye pits have been used for centuries; look for the walled old city with mud-brown roofs.

name: Zhangjiakou
blurb: Co-host of the 2022 Winter Olympics, with ski events at Chongli in the mountains to the north. Long a Great Wall gateway to Mongolia. Look for the city in a narrow valley and wind turbines lining the ridges.

name: Chifeng
blurb: Inner Mongolia city named for Hongshan, the Red Mountain, which also named the 5,000-year-old Hongshan culture found here. Look for the bare red hill beside town and the dry grassland around.

name: Bamako
blurb: Mali's capital straddles the Niger River, one of the fastest-growing cities in Africa. Look for the wide brown river with bridges crossing it and rocky cliffs on the north side of town.

name: Anqing
blurb: An old river port on the north bank of the Yangtze, once Anhui's provincial capital. Look for the wide brown Yangtze with lakes scattered across the plain behind the city.

name: Liuzhou
blurb: Industrial city wrapped in a giant U-bend of the Liu River, home to the SAIC-GM-Wuling plant that builds China's mini vans and tiny EVs, and to sour luosifen snail noodles. Look for the river looping almost all the way around downtown.

name: Zhaoqing
blurb: A city on the Xi River known for the Seven Star Crags, limestone peaks rising from lakes in the middle of town. Look for the karst hills reflected in the lake just north of the center.

name: Guang'an
blurb: Deng Xiaoping's hometown; his family house is now the centerpiece of a memorial park. Look for the Qu River winding through low hills in the eastern Sichuan Basin.

name: Ürümqi
blurb: Often called the farthest city from any ocean, more than 1,500 miles from the nearest coast. The Tian Shan rises right behind it; look for 17,864-ft Bogda Peak's snow to the east.

name: Zhuzhou
blurb: Rail and industrial city on the Xiang River, home of CRRC's big electric locomotive works. Look for rail yards and factories along the river's broad bends.

name: Yichang
blurb: Gateway to the Three Gorges. About 25 miles upriver stands the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station, nearly 1.5 miles long. Look for its five-step ship locks beside the dam.

name: Amman
blurb: Founded on seven hills, now spread over about 19, and nearly every building is faced in pale limestone by law. Look for a beige city poured over ridges and wadis, with the Roman theater downtown.

name: Chuzhou
blurb: A fast-growing city in eastern Anhui, close enough to Nanjing to be part of its commuter belt. Look for low wooded hills, including Langya Mountain, on the city's southwest edge.

name: Qingyuan
blurb: A city on the North River just north of Guangzhou, at the edge of the Pearl River Delta's flatland. Look for the river winding north into green mountains.

name: Xianyang
blurb: China's first imperial capital under Qin Shi Huang in the third century BC, now nearly fused with Xi'an. Look for the Wei River and the earthen pyramid mounds of Han emperors' tombs dotting the plateau north of the city.

name: Loudi
blurb: Coal and steel city in central Hunan. Look for the steel works and mining scars among the hills.

name: Kumasi
blurb: Capital of the Ashanti kingdom and Ghana's second city, on hilly forest land. Look for the huge Kejetia market at the center, one of the largest in West Africa, and red-roofed neighborhoods across the hills.

name: Deyang
blurb: A heavy-industry city on the Chengdu plain that builds power-plant generators and turbines; towns in its mountains were devastated by the 2008 earthquake. Look for the flat plain meeting the Longmen Mountains to the west.

name: Zaozhuang
blurb: A coal city in southern Shandong; the Grand Canal runs past Taierzhuang, scene of a major 1938 Chinese victory over Japan. Look for the canal and the rebuilt canal-side old town.

name: Cape Town
blurb: Table Mountain's flat top, about 2 miles long, rises some 3,500 ft directly above downtown. Look for the tablecloth of cloud spilling over its edge, Robben Island in the bay, and the Cape Peninsula running south.

name: Puyang
blurb: Northeast Henan city that grew up around the Zhongyuan Oil Field, near the Yellow River. Look for pumpjacks and well pads scattered across the flat farmland.

name: Neijiang
blurb: The Sweet City, named for its sugar cane, on the Tuo River about halfway between Chengdu and Chongqing. Look for the river meandering through low reddish hills.

name: Berlin
blurb: Rebuilt and reunited since the Wall fell in 1989. Look for the green Tiergarten, the Spree winding through the center, the 1,207-ft TV Tower at Alexanderplatz, and the huge empty field of old Tempelhof airport.

name: Wuhu
blurb: A Yangtze River port and car-making city in southern Anhui, home to Chery Automobile. Look for the wide river bending past the city and the bridges crossing it.

name: Yulin
blurb: A coal and gas boomtown in northern Shaanxi, near the Great Wall where the Mu Us Desert meets the loess hills. Look for sand dunes on one side, eroded yellow hills on the other, and mines and chemical plants around town.

name: Jiaozuo
blurb: Former coal city at the foot of the Taihang Mountains; Yuntai Mountain's red cliffs and waterfalls lie just north. Look for the city on the plain pressed right up against the mountain wall.

name: Port Harcourt
blurb: The hub of Nigeria's oil industry, in the creeks and mangroves of the Niger Delta. At night look for gas flares burning around the city in the dark delta.

name: Chengde
blurb: Summer retreat of the Qing emperors: the Mountain Resort is one of China's largest imperial gardens, and the Eight Outer Temples include a copy of Lhasa's Potala Palace. Look for the big walled park north of town.

name: Hohhot
blurb: Inner Mongolia's capital, its name meaning Blue City in Mongolian; dairy giants Yili and Mengniu are based here. Look for the city on a plain with the Daqing Mountains rising along its north side.

name: Shiyan
blurb: Mountain city built from scratch in the late 1960s for China's Second Automobile Works, now Dongfeng Motor. The Taoist temples of the Wudang Mountains lie just east. Look for factories filling narrow valleys.

name: Siping
blurb: A rail crossroads on the flat Songliao Plain, fought over four times in China's civil war in the late 1940s. Today it sits in a sea of corn; look for the rail lines converging on town.

name: Lucknow
blurb: Capital of Uttar Pradesh and city of the Nawabs, known for its Mughal-era monuments. Look for the Gomti River winding through the center.

name: Jinzhong
blurb: The prefecture holds Pingyao, one of China's best-preserved walled towns, and the mansions of Shanxi's old merchant bankers. Look for the flat, farmed Fen River plain edged by mountains.

name: Huzhou
blurb: On the south shore of Lake Tai, one of China's largest freshwater lakes at about 870 square miles. Look on the shoreline for a ring-shaped hotel tower, the "Horseshoe," standing over the water.

name: Changzhi
blurb: A city on a high basin in southeast Shanxi, enclosed by the Taihang Mountains at about 3,000 ft. Look for an upland plain with coal mines and power plants scattered around it.

name: Anshan
blurb: Home to Anshan Iron and Steel, one of China's oldest and largest steelworks. Look for mills, rail yards and slag heaps covering the south side of town, and the hills of Qianshan to the southeast.

name: Baoji
blurb: An industrial city at the western end of the Wei River plain, where the Qinling Mountains close in. Look for the city stretched in a long strip along the river valley between steep ridges.

name: Datong
blurb: Capital of the Northern Wei dynasty, which carved the Yungang Grottoes, some 50,000 Buddhist statues in cliff caves west of town. Look for the rebuilt city wall boxing in the old center.

name: Qinzhou
blurb: Guangxi port on the Gulf of Tonkin, with a deepwater container port on a peninsula south of the city. Look for the Maowei Sea, a drowned bay full of oyster rafts and small green islands.

name: Tongren
blurb: Gateway to Fanjingshan, a UNESCO-listed mountain known for Red Clouds Golden Summit, a sheer rock pillar topped by two small temples. Look for the city strung along the Jin River among forested ridges.

name: Bengbu
blurb: A rail junction city on the Huai River, the line often used to divide north and south China. Look for the river running east-west through the flat plain beside Longzi Lake.

name: Bazhong
blurb: A mountain city in the Daba range of northeast Sichuan, known for its Buddhist cliff carvings. Look for a town strung along a river valley between forested ridges.

name: Suining
blurb: A city on the Fu River in the middle of the Sichuan Basin. Look for the river spreading into wide channels through town, surrounded by low farmed hills.

name: Leshan
blurb: Home to the Leshan Giant Buddha, carved into a riverside cliff in the 8th century; at 233 ft it's the largest stone Buddha in the world. Look for the meeting of the Min, Dadu and Qingyi rivers below it.

name: Chittagong
blurb: Bangladesh's main seaport, on the Karnaphuli River near the Bay of Bengal. Look for ships anchored offshore, and on the coast to the north the shipbreaking beaches where huge vessels are run aground to be scrapped.

name: Casablanca
blurb: Morocco's largest city. The Hassan II Mosque stands partly over the Atlantic, its 689-ft minaret one of the tallest in the world; look for it on the shore west of the port.

name: Hanzhong
blurb: A fertile basin on the upper Han River, walled off from the north by the Qinling Mountains. Liu Bang ruled here as King of Han before founding the Han dynasty. Look for a flat green basin between two mountain ranges.

name: Putian
blurb: A coastal city in central Fujian, the home of the sea goddess Mazu, whose main temple is on nearby Meizhou Island. Look for the indented coast, aquaculture rafts and islands offshore.

name: Zhenjiang
blurb: Where the Grand Canal crosses the Yangtze, famous for black vinegar. Look for Jiaoshan, a wooded island in the river, and Jinshan's pagoda on its hill by the bank.

name: Cần Thơ
blurb: The Mekong Delta's biggest city sits on the Hau River amid a mesh of canals and rice paddies. Look for the long cable-stayed Can Tho Bridge, where a 2007 construction collapse killed more than 50 workers.

name: Faisalabad
blurb: Laid out by the British around a clock tower, with eight bazaars radiating from it in the pattern of the Union Jack. Look for the starburst of streets at the center of the old town.

name: Ningde
blurb: A city in northeast Fujian, home of battery giant CATL. Look for the sheltered bay full of floating fish farms, thousands of rafts covering the water like a pale grid.

name: Tongliao
blurb: City in eastern Inner Mongolia on the edge of the Horqin Sandy Land, where grassland turned to dunes and is now being replanted. Look for sandy patches and shelterbelts of trees around farmland.

name: Qinhuangdao
blurb: Where the Great Wall meets the sea at Old Dragon Head. Also one of China's biggest coal ports and home to the beach resort of Beidaihe. Look for long coal piers and the wall running down to the water.

name: Jinzhou
blurb: A port city on the Bohai Sea, taken in 1948 in the pivotal battle of the campaign that won the Communists Manchuria. Look for the coastline of salt pans and aquaculture ponds to the south.

name: Santa Cruz de la Sierra
blurb: Bolivia's biggest city sits in the tropical lowlands, far from the Andean image of the country. Look for its distinctive concentric ring roads circling the center on flat green plains.

name: Vadodara
blurb: Formerly Baroda, seat of the Gaekwad princes. Their Laxmi Vilas Palace is often said to be four times the size of Buckingham Palace. Look for the palace's large green grounds inside the city.

name: Jaipur
blurb: The Pink City: its planned 1727 grid was painted terracotta pink to welcome the Prince of Wales in 1876. Look for the walled old city's grid and the hilltop forts along the ridges north of town.

name: Wuzhou
blurb: Where the Gui River joins the Xi River at the Guangdong border, long the gateway between Guangxi and Canton. Its old riverfront streets are lined with arcaded shophouses. Look for two rivers meeting at the city.

name: Huainan
blurb: A coal city on the Huai River, long one of China's big mining centers. Look for flooded subsidence lakes where old mines collapsed, scattered across the farmland.

name: Liupanshui
blurb: Coal and steel city in western Guizhou, built up in the 1960s as part of Mao's Third Front industrial push. High on the plateau, it markets itself on cool summers. Look for mines and plants in narrow valleys.

name: Brasília
blurb: Built from scratch and inaugurated in 1960, laid out in the shape of an airplane or bird. Look for the long Monumental Axis as the fuselage, curved residential wings, and the big artificial Lake Paranoá.

name: Kuwait City
blurb: On the south shore of Kuwait Bay, in one of the hottest places on Earth, where summer highs pass 120°F. Look for the Kuwait Towers, needles skewering blue-green spheres on the waterfront.

name: Tianshui
blurb: An ancient city on the Wei River in southeastern Gansu, near the Maijishan Grottoes cut into a haystack-shaped cliff. Look for the long valley city between loess hills.

name: Rizhao
blurb: A Yellow Sea port whose name means sunshine. Look for long sandy beaches and a big bulk port, one of China's main terminals for iron ore and coal.

name: Sanaa
blurb: One of the world's highest capitals, at about 7,400 ft, and inhabited for more than 2,500 years. The Old City's mud-brick tower houses are trimmed in white gypsum, packed inside the walls of a high mountain basin.

name: Tashkent
blurb: Central Asia's biggest city, largely rebuilt after a 1966 earthquake. Look for wide Soviet avenues, canals off the Chirchiq River, and the tall TV tower standing over the city.

name: Weihai
blurb: Near the tip of the Shandong Peninsula, where China's Beiyang Fleet was destroyed by Japan in 1895. Look for Liugong Island guarding the bay and a coastline of beaches and rocky headlands.

name: Daqing
blurb: Built on China's largest oil field, discovered in 1959. Look for pumpjacks scattered among countless shallow lakes and marshes across the flat plain.

name: Bursa
blurb: The first capital of the Ottoman Empire, at the foot of Uludağ, an 8,300-ft mountain with ski slopes. Look for the city spread along the mountain's base, with the green Bursa plain below.

name: Jingmen
blurb: City on the edge of the Jianghan Plain. A tomb at nearby Guodian yielded bamboo slips with the oldest known text of the Tao Te Ching. Look for the Han River to the east and farmland ringed by hills.

name: Haikou
blurb: Hainan's capital, on the island's north coast facing the Qiongzhou Strait and mainland Guangdong. Look for ferries crossing the strait and Haidian Island, separated from downtown by a thin channel at the river mouth.

name: Chaoyang
blurb: The hills around this western Liaoning city produced many of the world's feathered-dinosaur fossils. Look for dry, eroded brown hills and a city strung along the Daling River valley.

name: Xiangtan
blurb: Mao Zedong's birthplace, Shaoshan, lies within its prefecture. Look for the Xiang River making a big bend through town between Changsha and Zhuzhou.

name: Yinchuan
blurb: An oasis on the Yellow River fed by canals over 2,000 years old, with the Helan Mountains walling off the desert to the west. Look for the beehive-shaped Western Xia royal tombs at the mountains' foot.

name: Shaoguan
blurb: Northern Guangdong city where the Zhen and Wu rivers join to form the Bei (North) River. Danxia Shan, the red sandstone mountain that gave its name to a whole type of landform, lies to the northeast. Look for the rivers meeting in a Y downtown.

name: Heyuan
blurb: River city on the Dongjiang below Xinfengjiang Reservoir, one of Guangdong's largest lakes, which helps feed the water supply of Shenzhen and Hong Kong. Look for the big island-dotted reservoir in the green hills northwest of town.

name: San Luis Potosí
blurb: A colonial silver-mining city on Mexico's dry central plateau at about 6,000 ft. Look for the old center in a basin ringed by bare sierra, with industrial parks and car plants spreading on the outskirts.

name: Da Nang
blurb: Central Vietnam's beach city: a long straight run of sand facing the South China Sea, with the forested Son Tra peninsula hooking out to the north. Look for the Han River and its string of bridges through the middle.

name: Mudanjiang
blurb: Southeast Heilongjiang city on the Mudan River. Upstream to the southwest lies Jingpo Lake, dammed by an ancient lava flow, with a waterfall at its outlet. Look for the river through town and forested hills around it.

name: Douala
blurb: Cameroon's biggest city and main port, on the Wouri River estuary in a sprawl of mangrove swamp. Look for the long bridge across the river and the dark green delta channels around the docks.

name: Rome
blurb: Nearly 3,000 years of history along the Tiber. Look for St. Peter's dome and the Vatican's walls on the west bank, the oval of the Colosseum, and the river's S-bends through the center.

name: Shanwei
blurb: Coastal city on Guangdong's east coast between Shenzhen and Shantou, with fishing harbors and long sandy bays. Look for the town wrapped around a sheltered bay on the South China Sea.

name: Longyan
blurb: A mountain city in western Fujian at the heart of Hakka country, with round earthen tulou fortress homes in the hills nearby. Look for a city squeezed into a narrow green valley.

name: Tieling
blurb: A farming and coal city north of Shenyang, famous across China as the hometown of comedian Zhao Benshan and the butt of countless sketches. Look for the Liao River plain spreading flat around it.

name: Baotou
blurb: Steel city that refines rare earths from Bayan Obo, about 90 miles north, the world's largest rare earth deposit. Look for the Yellow River to the south and a big gray tailings lake west of town.

name: Dingxi
blurb: A city on the dry Loess Plateau of central Gansu, long one of China's poorest regions. Look for hillsides carved into contour terraces in every direction.

name: Damascus
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Look for the green Ghouta oasis against the desert, bare Mount Qasioun rising over the city to the northwest, and the old walled city at the center.

name: Nanping
blurb: A northern Fujian city on the Min River, which governs the Wuyi Mountains, famous for oolong tea and red sandstone peaks. Look for the river winding between steep forested hills.

name: Zigong
blurb: China's salt capital for 2,000 years, where brine wells were drilled more than 3,000 ft deep by hand in the 1830s, and a dinosaur fossil hotspot. Look for a hilly city along a winding river.

name: Gazipur
blurb: A garment-factory city just north of Dhaka, packed with clothing plants that supply brands worldwide. Look for big factory roofs mixed into green paddy and scraps of sal forest.

name: Xianning
blurb: South Hubei city known for hot springs and osmanthus trees; the Red Cliff battlefield of the Three Kingdoms lies within its prefecture. Look for green hills and reservoirs.

name: Guayaquil
blurb: Ecuador's largest city and main port on the west bank of the Guayas River. Look for the wide brown river, the riverside Malecón 2000, and mangrove-lined estuary channels running south to the Pacific.

name: Huludao
blurb: A shipbuilding port on the Bohai Sea, where China builds many of its submarines. Next door, Xingcheng keeps a complete Ming city wall; look for the coast of beaches, piers and islands.

name: Yangjiang
blurb: Long known as China's capital of knives and scissors. Offshore Hailing Island has long beaches and a museum built around the Nanhai One, a Song dynasty merchant ship raised whole from the seabed in 2007.

name: Ziyang
blurb: A city on the Tuo River between Chengdu and Chongqing, next door to Chengdu's new Tianfu International Airport. Look for the river and, to the west, the airport's big terminals and runways.

name: Fortaleza
blurb: A big Atlantic coast city near Brazil's northeast tip, lined with urban beaches and high-rises. Look for the long white beaches, dunes and lagoons to the south, and wind farms along the coast.

name: Chaozhou
blurb: Old walled city on the Han River and heartland of Teochew culture and cooking. Its Guangji Bridge, begun in the 12th century, has a pontoon middle section that swings open for boats. Look for the river bending past the old town.

name: Ibadan
blurb: Once among the largest cities in Africa, sprawled over hills in a sea of rust-brown corrugated roofs. Its 1965 Cocoa House was West Africa's first skyscraper; look for it rising from the low roofs.

name: Jiamusi
blurb: Port city on the wide Songhua River in China's far northeast, at the edge of the Sanjiang Plain, once a vast wetland now largely drained for rice and soybeans. Look for the river and the endless flat fields.

name: Medellín
blurb: A city of about 2.5 million filling a narrow Andean valley about 4,900 ft up. Look for brick-colored neighborhoods climbing the valley walls and the cable cars that serve them.

name: Havana
