blurb: Founded by the Spanish in 1519, its narrow harbor entrance is guarded by El Morro fortress. Look for the curving Malecón seawall along the shore and the old city's tight blocks by the harbor.

name: Luanda
blurb: Angola's capital curves around a bay sheltered by the Ilha, a long thin sandspit. Look for the spit's line of sand and the old Portuguese fortress on the headland.

name: Sanming
blurb: An inland Fujian city built up as an industrial base in the 1950s, spread along the Sha River valley. Look for long narrow urban strips following the river through forested mountains.

name: Guangyuan
blurb: Birthplace of Wu Zetian, China's only reigning empress, and the gateway on the old Shu Roads into Sichuan. Look for the Jialing River cutting through a mountain gorge.

name: Huangshi
blurb: Steel and mining city on the Yangtze. Copper has been mined at nearby Tonglushan for some 3,000 years. Look for open-pit scars and lakes between the hills and the river.

name: Cali
blurb: Colombia's third-largest city lies on the floor of the Cauca Valley, backed by the Western Cordillera. Look for the flat green sugarcane fields of the valley and the mountains rising steeply to the west.

name: Anshun
blurb: Gateway to Huangguoshu, one of China's biggest waterfalls at roughly 250 ft tall, and to the Dragon Palace caves. Look for karst cones dotting the plain around the city like upturned bowls.

name: Xining
blurb: At about 7,400 ft, the gateway to the Tibetan Plateau and the start of the railway to Lhasa. Look for the city strung along a narrow valley of the Huangshui River between bare brown hills.

name: Lusaka
blurb: Zambia's capital since 1935, laid out on a plateau about 4,200 ft up, which keeps it cooler than its latitude suggests. Look for the city spreading over flat savanna with few landmarks around it.

name: Ouagadougou
blurb: A low, sprawling capital on the Sahel plateau, mostly single-story buildings in reddish earth tones. Look for the large reservoirs (barrages) just north of the center.

name: Dandong
blurb: On the Yalu River facing North Korea. The Broken Bridge, bombed by US planes in 1950, still stops halfway across; at night look for the lit Chinese bank against the near-black Korean side.

name: Daegu
blurb: South Korea's fourth-largest city sits in a bowl ringed by mountains, which makes it famously the hottest big city in the country in summer. Look for the dense basin hemmed in by ridges, with Palgongsan to the north.

name: Yaoundé
blurb: Cameroon's capital spreads over seven hills about 2,500 ft up in the rainforest belt. Look for red-earth neighborhoods spilling down the green slopes and the spiraling Reunification Monument.

name: Baoshan
blurb: Western Yunnan valley city on the old Southern Silk Road and the WWII Burma Road. The Mekong and Salween gorges cut parallel north-south trenches through the mountains on either side.

name: Yingkou
blurb: A port where the Liao River meets the Bohai Sea, opened to foreign trade in the 1860s. Look for the river mouth, grey mudflats and the long piers of the new harbor.

name: Antalya
blurb: The main city of the Turkish Riviera, built on cliffs above its bay with the Taurus Mountains rising behind. Look for the cliff edge along the old town and long Konyaaltı Beach to the west.

name: Beirut
blurb: Built on a headland pushing into the Mediterranean, with Mount Lebanon rising steeply behind. The 2020 port explosion was one of the largest non-nuclear blasts ever; look for the harbor on the north shore.

name: Longnan
blurb: Gansu's southernmost city, in steep mountains where the Loess Plateau gives way to the greener Qinling foothills. Look for towns strung along the Bailong River gorge.

name: Nagpur
blurb: Sits almost exactly at the geographic center of India, marked by the British-era Zero Mile stone, and is famous for its oranges. Look for the lakes scattered through town on the flat central plain.

name: Pu'er City
blurb: Called Simao until 2007, when it renamed itself after the fermented tea traded from here for centuries. Look for tea terraces and tropical forest on the hills of far southern Yunnan.

name: Yunfu
blurb: Inland western Guangdong city near the Xi (West) River, known for quarrying and carving stone. Look for low green hills scarred by quarries and the broad brown Xi River to the north.

name: Luohe
blurb: Food-processing city in central Henan and home of Shuanghui, China's biggest pork producer, which bought Smithfield Foods in 2013. Look for the Sha and Li rivers meeting in town.

name: Algiers
blurb: Algiers rises in white tiers from its bay, which is why it's called Algiers the White. Look for the Casbah on the hill and the Martyrs' Memorial, three concrete palm leaves above the harbor.

name: Belo Horizonte
blurb: Planned in the 1890s as a new state capital, with a street grid overlaid by diagonal avenues and wrapped in mountains. Look for Lake Pampulha with Oscar Niemeyer's curving modernist buildings on its shore.

name: Manaus
blurb: A city of about 2 million in the middle of the rainforest, reachable mainly by air or river. Just downstream the dark Rio Negro and the tan Solimões run side by side for miles without mixing. Look for the two-color line.

name: Yan'an
blurb: The Communist Party's base from the late 1930s until 1947, when Mao and his leadership lived in caves dug into the loess hills. Look for a city threaded through narrow valleys in deeply eroded yellow-brown plateau.

name: Quzhou
blurb: Western Zhejiang city on the Qu River, home to the southern branch of Confucius's family, which fled here in the 1100s and built its own ancestral temple. Green hills close in on all sides.

name: Lincang
blurb: The name means "near the Lancang," China's name for the Mekong, which cuts a deep gorge along its edge. Rolling tea country in southwestern Yunnan, close to the Myanmar border.

name: Konya
blurb: The city of Rumi and the whirling dervishes, in the middle of a high plateau that's Turkey's breadbasket. Look for wheat fields stretching dead flat for miles around the city.

name: Almaty
blurb: Kazakhstan's biggest city sits at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau, with snowy peaks above 15,000 ft close enough to see from downtown. Look for the street grid tilting uphill toward the mountain wall.

name: Qingyang
blurb: A city on one of the largest intact patches of the Loess Plateau, where some people still live in cave houses dug into the earth. Look for flat-topped loess tablelands cut by deep gullies.

name: Santo Domingo
blurb: Founded in 1496, the oldest continuously inhabited European city in the Americas, on the Caribbean coast at the mouth of the Ozama River. Look for the river mouth and the seafront Malecón.

name: Jincheng
blurb: A coal-mining city in the southern Taihang Mountains of Shanxi, near the Henan border. Look for a city spread over hills and valleys, with mines and coal-fired plants around it.

name: Dongying
blurb: Built on the Yellow River delta, still pushing out into the Bohai Sea, and home to the Shengli Oilfield, China's second largest. Look for pumpjacks across the flats and the river's muddy plume reaching into the sea.

name: Lomé
blurb: Togo's capital sits hard against the Ghana border on the Gulf of Guinea. Look for the deepwater port to the east and a lagoon running behind the city.

name: Ma'anshan
blurb: A steel city on the Yangtze just upstream of Nanjing, built around a big ironworks. Look for the mills and rail yards along the river's east bank.

name: Harare
blurb: Called Salisbury until 1982, Zimbabwe's capital sits on the highveld at about 4,900 ft. Look for a compact downtown surrounded by leafy suburbs, jacaranda-lined streets and granite outcrops.

name: Phnom Penh
blurb: Cambodia's capital sits where the Mekong meets the Tonlé Sap River, the river that reverses direction each rainy season. Look for the wide brown rivers forming an X at the city's east edge.

name: Haiphong
blurb: Northern Vietnam's main seaport, spread along river channels near the Gulf of Tonkin. Ha Long Bay's thousands of limestone islands start just to the east; look for container docks lining the brown river.

name: Mogadishu
blurb: Somalia's capital, an Indian Ocean trading port since medieval times. Look for the old town of pale buildings along the coast, with sand dunes running behind the shoreline.

name: Rawalpindi
blurb: The older twin of Islamabad and headquarters of Pakistan's army. Look for the dense old city south of the planned capital, with the Margalla Hills rising to the north.

name: Pingliang
blurb: A city on the Jing River in eastern Gansu, below Kongtong Mountain, a Taoist holy peak. Look for the narrow valley city framed by loess terraces and the forested mountain to the west.

name: Rajkot
blurb: Gandhi spent his boyhood here, where his father served as chief minister to the local prince. Today it is an engineering and auto-parts hub. Look for the Aji River and the reservoirs ringing town.

name: Shangluo
blurb: A mountain city in the Qinling range of southeastern Shaanxi, along the Dan River. Look for a narrow valley town wedged between forested ridges.

name: Visakhapatnam
blurb: A major port and naval base on the Bay of Bengal, wrapped around a natural harbor between green hills. Look for the long beachfront and the Dolphin's Nose headland guarding the harbor mouth.

name: Sanmenxia
blurb: Named for the Sanmenxia Dam, the first big dam on the Yellow River, finished around 1960; it silted up so fast it had to be rebuilt. Look for the reservoir upstream, where swans winter by the thousands.

name: Gujranwala
blurb: An industrial city north of Lahore, birthplace of Sikh ruler Ranjit Singh and famous for wrestlers and food. Look for a dense, low city on the flat, irrigated Punjab plain.

name: Aleppo
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, built around a citadel on a huge mound. Much of the old city was wrecked in the civil war. Look for the oval citadel and its moat at the center.

name: Puning
blurb: County-level city on the Chaoshan plain of eastern Guangdong, a big textile and garment-trading center. Look for dense low-rise town spreading over flat farmland west of Shantou.

name: Minsk
blurb: Almost completely destroyed in World War II and rebuilt in grand Soviet style. Look for wide straight avenues, the Svislach River and its reservoirs, and the diamond-shaped National Library on the northeast side.

name: Indore
blurb: Ranked India's cleanest city in the national survey year after year. It sits on the Malwa Plateau of central India, a sprawl of low rooftops spreading over flat dark farmland.

name: Şanlıurfa
blurb: Traditionally the birthplace of Abraham, and close to Göbekli Tepe, carved stone pillars more than 11,000 years old. Look for a dry plain around the city, irrigated green in patches by water from the Atatürk Dam to the north.

name: Kananga
blurb: A large city on the savanna of the central Congo basin, once a rail hub on the line to Katanga. Look for the low sprawl and red earth gullies cut into the grassland around it.

name: Huaibei
blurb: A coal-mining city on the far north edge of Anhui, where old subsidence pits have been turned into parks and lakes. Look for irregular water bodies dotting the plain.

name: Peshawar
blurb: One of the oldest cities in South Asia, the last stop before the Khyber Pass into Afghanistan. Look for the Bala Hisar fort on its mound and mountains closing in on the west.

name: Tijuana
blurb: Pressed right against the US border, with San Diego just north. Look for the border fence running straight up the hills to the Pacific, and dense neighborhoods covering every canyon south of it.

name: Isfahan
blurb: Its Naqsh-e Jahan Square is one of the largest city squares in the world, built in the 1600s. Look for the Zayandeh River and its arched old bridges, often over a dry riverbed.

name: Irbid
blurb: Jordan's second city by many counts and home to Yarmouk University, on a plateau near the Syrian border. To the west the land drops away toward the Jordan Valley, well below sea level.

name: Tainan
blurb: Taiwan's oldest city and its capital for more than two centuries under Dutch, Koxinga and Qing rule. Look for lagoons, fish ponds and old salt pans along the coast to the west.

name: Multan
blurb: The City of Saints, known for Sufi shrines like the tomb of Shah Rukn-e-Alam, whose great brick dome dates to the 1300s. Look for mango orchards around the city on the hot Punjab plain.

name: Hamburg
blurb: Germany's biggest port, about 60 miles up the Elbe from the North Sea. Look for the Binnenalster and Aussenalster lakes in the city center, the container terminals, and the wave-topped Elbphilharmonie.

name: Jixi
blurb: Coal-mining city in southeast Heilongjiang near the Russian border. Lake Khanka, split between China and Russia, lies to the southeast. Look for mine waste heaps in the hills and farmland on the valley floor.

name: Fushun
blurb: Built on coal: the West Open-Pit Mine on the south side of town is miles long and one of the largest open-pit mines in Asia. Look for the vast terraced gash next to the city.

name: Liaoyang
blurb: One of the oldest cities in Northeast China, more than 2,000 years old, with a 13-story brick pagoda from the Liao dynasty. Look for the Taizi River curving past the city on the flat plain.

name: Beihai
blurb: Seaside city at the tip of a peninsula on the Gulf of Tonkin, known for the pale sand of Silver Beach. Weizhou, a volcanic island, sits about 20 miles offshore. Look for the long white beach on the south shore.

name: Fuxin
blurb: A coal city whose Haizhou open-pit mine, worked out and turned into a mining park, is a huge stepped hole beside town. Look for the terraced pit and the dry hills of western Liaoning.

name: Wuwei
blurb: An oasis city on the Hexi Corridor, the old Silk Road route, where the famous bronze Flying Horse of Gansu was dug up. Look for green irrigated fields pressed between the Qilian Mountains and desert.

name: Pingxiang
blurb: Coal city on the Hunan border. The 1922 strike at its Anyuan mines was an early Communist labor victory. Look for mine scars and the town among green hills.

name: Bhopal
blurb: The City of Lakes: the Upper Lake was made by damming a river around the 11th century. In 1984 a gas leak at the Union Carbide plant here killed thousands, the worst industrial disaster on record.

name: Mosul
blurb: City on the Tigris facing the ruins of ancient Nineveh. Held by ISIS from 2014 to 2017, its old city was largely destroyed in the battle to retake it. Look for the river cutting the city in two.

name: Lubumbashi
blurb: The capital of Congo's copper belt, founded in 1910 by Belgian mining interests. Look for the huge black slag heap of the old smelter, one of the city's landmarks, on the west side.

name: Accra
blurb: Ghana's capital stretches along the Gulf of Guinea. Look for the coastal lagoons, the busy port of Tema to the east, and the black star arch of Independence Square by the sea.

name: Benin City
blurb: Capital of the old Kingdom of Benin, famous for the Benin Bronzes looted by the British in 1897. Its earthen walls and moats once ranked among the largest earthworks in the world.

name: Curitiba
blurb: Invented bus rapid transit in 1974; its riders still board from glass tube stations. About 3,000 ft up, it is known for parks and umbrella-shaped araucaria pines; look for green spaces scattered through town.

name: Adana
blurb: Turkey's cotton capital, on the Seyhan River. Look for the Sabancı Mosque's six minarets on the riverbank and the flat, farmed Çukurova plain around the city.

name: Quito
blurb: At about 9,350 ft, one of the highest capitals in the world, stretched in a narrow valley along the flank of Pichincha volcano. Look for the long, thin city with green slopes rising to the west.

name: Monrovia
blurb: Founded in 1822 by freed American slaves and named for President James Monroe. Look for the city on the narrow Cape Mesurado peninsula, between the Atlantic surf and the Mesurado River's mangrove lagoon.

name: Garoua
blurb: A river port on the Benue in northern Cameroon, connected to Nigeria by the river in the wet season. Look for the wide sandy river bed and the Lagdo Reservoir upstream to the south.

name: Kigali
blurb: Rwanda's capital spreads over ridge after ridge, true to the land of a thousand hills. Look for red-roofed neighborhoods along the ridgelines, with green wetlands and farm plots in the valleys between.

name: Diyarbakır
blurb: Its black basalt city walls, about 3.5 miles around, are among the longest surviving city walls in the world. Look for the dark ring of the walls above the Tigris valley.

name: Bucharest
blurb: Home to the Palace of the Parliament, built for Ceaușescu and one of the largest and heaviest buildings in the world. Look for its enormous white bulk at the end of a long boulevard, and a chain of lakes across the north of the city.

name: Shuozhou
blurb: A coal city in northern Shanxi, between lines of the Great Wall, and home to Antaibao, one of China's largest open-pit coal mines. Look for huge terraced pits cut into the hills.

name: Benxi
blurb: A steel town in the mountains on the Taizi River. In 1942 the Honkeiko colliery here suffered the deadliest coal-mine disaster ever, killing 1,549. Look for the city squeezed into green valleys.

name: Baiyin
blurb: A city built in the 1950s around a big copper mine near the Yellow River. Look for mining pits and smelter works in bare, brown hills.

name: Abuja
blurb: Purpose-built to replace Lagos as Nigeria's capital in 1991. Look for Aso Rock, a bare granite monolith about 1,300 ft high behind the government district, and the gold dome of the National Mosque.

name: Patna
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, ancient Pataliputra, strung along the south bank of the Ganges. Look for the very wide river and the long Mahatma Gandhi Setu bridge.

name: Gaziantep
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities, famous for pistachios and baklava, and hit hard by the 2023 earthquakes. Look for the castle mound at the center and pistachio orchards on the hills around.

name: Kampala
blurb: Uganda's capital, traditionally built on seven hills. Look for red-roofed hills rising out of green valleys, and the vast sheet of Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa, to the south.

name: Heihe
blurb: Faces the Russian city of Blagoveshchensk directly across the Amur River, linked by a road bridge opened in 2022. Look for two cities staring at each other across the water.

name: Conakry
blurb: Guinea's capital grew along a long, narrow peninsula pushing into the Atlantic, so the city is a strip miles long and only a few wide. Look for that finger of land, with the Iles de Loos just offshore.

name: Masvingo
blurb: The ruins of Great Zimbabwe, a stone-walled city built from the 11th to 15th centuries that gave the country its name, lie less than 20 miles southeast. Look for Lake Mutirikwi spreading behind its dam nearby.

name: Novosibirsk
blurb: Russia's third-largest city, grown from a camp built in the 1890s for the Trans-Siberian Railway's bridge over the Ob. Look for the wide river and the Ob Sea reservoir to the south.

name: Jingdezhen
blurb: China's porcelain capital for over 1,000 years; it supplied the imperial court. Look for the Chang River through town and kiln smoke stacks among the hills that once yielded the kaolin clay.

name: Ludhiana
blurb: Punjab's largest city and industrial engine, known for bicycles and knitwear. Look for a dense sprawl on the flat plain south of the Sutlej River, ringed by wheat and rice fields.

name: Fukuoka
blurb: Its airport sits just a few minutes by subway from downtown, among the most convenient anywhere. Look for Hakata Bay's curve and the long sand spit of Uminonakamichi closing it off.

name: Agra
blurb: Home of the Taj Mahal, completed in the mid-1600s. Look for the white marble tomb on a bend of the Yamuna, and the red sandstone walls of Agra Fort a mile or so upstream.

name: León de Los Aldama
blurb: A leather and shoe capital of Mexico on the high Bajío plain, about 5,900 ft up. Look for the flat grid of a large city surrounded by farmland and dry mountains to the north.

name: Meerut
blurb: Where the Indian Rebellion of 1857 began, among sepoys at the British cantonment. Look for a big flat city on the Ganges plain northeast of Delhi.

name: Hebi
blurb: Small industrial city in northern Henan at the foot of the Taihang Mountains. Look for the Qi River running along the hills west of town.

name: Madurai
blurb: A temple city for over 2,000 years, built around the Meenakshi Amman Temple and its towering gateway towers covered in painted figures. Look for the temple complex at the center with old streets laid out in squares around it.

name: Jamshedpur
blurb: India's first planned industrial city, built by Tata Steel from 1907 and still largely run by the company. Look for the steel works where the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers meet, with the Dalma hills to the north.

name: Maracaibo
blurb: Venezuela's oil capital, on the strait to Lake Maracaibo. Look for the Rafael Urdaneta Bridge, over 5 miles long, and oil platforms dotting the lake.

name: Zhangjiajie
blurb: Thousands of sandstone pillars, some hundreds of feet tall, rise from the forest here; they inspired the floating mountains in Avatar. Look for the pillar forest in the hills north of the city.

name: Rui'an
blurb: County-level city under Wenzhou on the Feiyun River, a dense belt of family workshops, many making auto and motorcycle parts. Look for the river estuary meeting reclaimed coastal flats.

name: Guiping
blurb: Where the Qian and Yu rivers merge to form the Xun. In the nearby village of Jintian, the Taiping Rebellion began in 1851, a civil war that killed tens of millions. Look for the river confluence beside town.

name: Ya'an
blurb: The Rain City, one of the wettest places in China, at the edge of the Tibetan highlands. The giant panda was first described to Western science from this area in 1869. Look for the Qingyi River valley with mountains rising west.

name: Munich
blurb: Bavaria's capital, with the Alps visible on clear days about 50 miles south. Look for the Olympic Park's tent roofs and tower to the north, the long English Garden along the Isar, and the Allianz Arena's inflated shell.

name: New Cairo
blurb: A planned desert suburb east of Cairo, growing on bare plateau since 2000. Look for gated compounds, golf course greens and broad roads cut into the beige desert, and the New Administrative Capital farther east.

name: Niamey
blurb: Niger's capital on the Niger River, in the Sahel and one of the hottest capitals on Earth. Look for the broad river with green rice fields and islands, and sandy plateau stretching away on both sides.

name: Gwangju
blurb: Remembered for the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, a pro-democracy revolt crushed by the military and now a national memorial. Look for the city spreading across a basin below Mudeungsan, the rounded mountain on its east side.

name: Recife
blurb: Named for the reefs that run parallel to its shore, it is called the Venice of Brazil for its rivers, islands and bridges. Look for high-rises along Boa Viagem beach and the line of reef offshore.

name: Nashik
blurb: A holy city on the Godavari that hosts the Kumbh Mela every 12 years, and India's wine capital. Look for the river through town and neat rows of vineyards on the surrounding plain.

name: Valencia
blurb: Venezuela's industrial heartland. Look for Lake Valencia to the east, the country's largest freshwater lake, with the city spread across the valley between the coastal mountains.

name: Onitsha
blurb: A trading city on the east bank of the Niger, with one of the largest markets in West Africa. Look for the Niger Bridge and the wide brown river below the town.

name: Daejeon
blurb: South Korea's science city, home to the Daedeok research complex and the 1993 Expo. Look for a planned city in a broad valley where the main rail lines from Seoul split toward Busan and the southwest.

name: Kyoto
blurb: Japan's imperial capital from 794 to 1869, with well over a thousand temples. Look for the strict grid laid out on a Chinese model, ringed by forested hills, with the Kamo River running north to south.

name: Shuangyashan
blurb: Coal city in eastern Heilongjiang whose name means Twin Duck Mountain. Look for mines and waste heaps among the flat farmland of the Sanjiang Plain.

name: Yueqing
blurb: Under Wenzhou, it calls itself China's electrical equipment capital, home of makers like Chint. The jagged Yandang Mountains, a UNESCO geopark, rise behind the coast of Yueqing Bay.

name: Nouakchott
blurb: Mauritania's capital was a village of a few thousand around 1960 and now holds over a million people. Look for a flat, sandy grid on the Atlantic coast, with Sahara dunes pressing in from the east.

name: Dakar
blurb: The westernmost city of mainland Africa, on the Cap-Vert peninsula. Look for the hook of land jutting into the Atlantic, Gorée Island just offshore, and the giant African Renaissance Monument on one of the twin Mamelles hills.

name: Goiânia
blurb: A planned city founded in the 1930s as Goiás's new capital, with an art deco center and many parks. Look for its radial avenues meeting at the central square amid flat cerrado farmland.

name: Guyuan
blurb: A city on the Loess Plateau in southern Ningxia, beneath the Liupan Mountains. Look for terraced fields contoured across eroded yellow-brown hills.

name: Muscat
blurb: Oman's capital is strung along coves between bare, jagged Hajar mountains and the sea, kept low and mostly white by building rules. Look for the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque and the Mutrah corniche.

name: Pointe-Noire
blurb: Congo-Brazzaville's oil capital and only major seaport, end of the Congo-Ocean Railway, built in the 1920s and 30s at a terrible cost in workers' lives. Look for the harbor breakwater on the Atlantic and offshore platforms beyond.

name: Wenling
blurb: Coastal city in Taizhou known for pumps and machinery. Its Shitang fishing village claimed mainland China's first sunrise of the new millennium in 2000; look for rocky headlands and island-dotted bays.

name: Medina
blurb: Islam's second holiest city and burial place of the Prophet Muhammad. Look for the vast white courtyards and minarets of the Prophet's Mosque at the center, ringed by hotels, with black lava fields around the city.

name: Faridabad
blurb: Industrial satellite of Delhi on the Yamuna, part of the National Capital Region. Look for factory blocks along the Delhi-Agra highway and the scrubby Aravalli hills to the west.

name: Ulaanbaatar
blurb: The coldest national capital on Earth, holding nearly half of Mongolia's people. Look for the Tuul River valley and hillsides covered in ger districts: fenced plots of round white felt tents and small houses.

name: Panjin
blurb: Built on the Liaohe oil field in the Liao River delta. Each autumn its coastal marsh turns crimson with a salt-loving seepweed, the Red Beach; look for nodding oil pumps among rice paddies.

name: Kayseri
blurb: Sits below Mount Erciyes, a 12,800-ft extinct volcano. Look for the snowy cone towering south of the city over the Cappadocian plateau.

name: Porto Alegre
blurb: Southern Brazil's biggest city sits on the Guaíba, a broad freshwater estuary that flooded much of the city in May 2024. Look for the wide water to the west, opening south into the Lagoa dos Patos, the largest lagoon in Brazil.

name: Adelaide
blurb: Laid out in 1837 by Colonel William Light, its square city center is completely ringed by parkland. Look for the green belt around downtown and the long straight beaches of Gulf St Vincent.

name: Guadalajara
blurb: Mexico's second largest metro and the homeland of mariachi and tequila, with the town of Tequila nearby. Look for Lake Chapala, Mexico's largest lake, to the south, and the deep Huentitan canyon at the city's northern edge.

name: Samsun
blurb: Turkey's main Black Sea port, where Atatürk landed in 1919 to start the war of independence. Look for the Kızılırmak and Yeşilırmak river deltas jutting into the sea on either side of the city.

name: Kisangani
blurb: A river port at the farthest navigable point of the Congo below Boyoma Falls, the old Stanleyville. Look for the wide brown river cutting through unbroken rainforest.

name: Tbilisi
blurb: Georgia's capital stretches along the Kura River gorge for miles, with old houses stacked on the slopes. Look for the Narikala fortress on a ridge above the old town and the big TV tower on Mtatsminda.

name: Huangshan
blurb: Gateway city to the Yellow Mountains, granite peaks famous in Chinese painting for their pines and seas of cloud. Look for the jagged range north of town and white-walled Huizhou villages in the valleys.

name: Kazan
blurb: Capital of Tatarstan, where the white-walled Kremlin holds both an Orthodox cathedral and the big Kul Sharif mosque. Look for the Kazanka River meeting the Volga, here widened into a reservoir.

name: Gaozhou
blurb: Western Guangdong city famous for lychees and longans, with orchards covering the surrounding hills. Look for the Jian River running through town and the patchwork of fruit groves around it.

name: Barranquilla
blurb: Colombia's main Caribbean port, near the mouth of the Magdalena River, the country's longest. Look for the river spilling brown water into the blue Caribbean and the long breakwaters at Bocas de Ceniza.

name: Basra
blurb: Iraq's port on the Shatt al-Arab, formed where the Tigris and Euphrates join, and home of the fabled Sinbad. Look for the wide river lined with date palms running southeast to the Gulf.

name: Yangquan
blurb: A coal and industrial city deep in the Taihang Mountains, on the main route from Taiyuan to the North China Plain. Look for neighborhoods packed into narrow valleys between steep ridges.

name: Tongling
blurb: A copper city on the Yangtze, mining the metal for about 3,000 years. Look for open pits and tailings in the hills near the river.

name: Belém
blurb: The gateway to the Amazon, on a bay at the mouth of the Pará River. Look for the wide brown water, the Ver-o-Peso market's turrets on the waterfront, and forested islands across the bay.

name: Montevideo
blurb: Home to nearly half of Uruguay's people. Look for the Rambla, a waterfront promenade running for miles along the Río de la Plata, and the Cerro, the lone hill across the bay.

name: Nova Iguaçu
blurb: A big working-class city of roughly 800,000 in the Baixada Fluminense, the lowland north of Rio. Look for dense low-rise neighborhoods running up against forested hills on either side.

name: Tripoli
blurb: Libya's capital wraps around a Mediterranean harbor, with the Red Castle fortress at the edge of the old walled medina and a Roman arch of Marcus Aurelius inside it. Look for palm-lined waterfront and the curve of the port.

name: Tangier
blurb: Sits at the Atlantic mouth of the Strait of Gibraltar, with Spain visible across the water on a clear day. Look for the whitewashed medina above a crescent bay and the giant Tanger Med container port to the east.

name: Antananarivo
blurb: Madagascar's capital climbs a ridge of hills about 4,200 ft up, with the queen's palace on the highest one. Look for heart-shaped Lake Anosy downtown and green rice paddies flooding the valleys right into the city.

name: Jabalpur
blurb: On the Narmada River in central India. Just downstream at Bhedaghat, the river cuts a gorge through gleaming white marble cliffs about 100 ft high; look for the pale rock walls along the water.

name: Yongcheng
blurb: Coal town in far eastern Henan near Mangdang Mountain, where legend says Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty, slew a white serpent. Look for coal mines amid flat wheat fields.

name: Yuyao City
blurb: The Hemudu site here, about 7,000 years old, holds some of the world's earliest evidence of rice farming. Also the hometown of philosopher Wang Yangming; flat paddy country west of Ningbo.

name: Lijiang
blurb: Its Old Town of Naxi tile roofs and canals is a UNESCO site. Look for 18,360-ft Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, with glaciers, rising abruptly from the plain just north of town.

name: Balıkesir
blurb: A market city in northwest Turkey on the uplands between the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean. Look for a compact city surrounded by farmland, with olive groves on the hills.

name: Huế
blurb: Seat of Vietnam's last emperors, the Nguyen dynasty, from 1802 to 1945. Look for the moated, star-cornered Citadel, a square about 1.5 miles a side, on the north bank of the Perfume River.

name: Lufeng
blurb: Coastal town in eastern Guangdong, part of Shanwei. Look for a grid of low-rise blocks on the flat coastal plain, with fish ponds and the South China Sea a few miles south.

name: Suwon
blurb: Ringed by Hwaseong Fortress, a 1790s wall about 3.5 miles around and a World Heritage site. Look for the stone wall looping over a hill through the middle of the city, and Samsung's big campus to the east.

name: Hargeisa
blurb: Capital of Somaliland, which declared independence in 1991 and runs its own government with almost no formal recognition. Look for a city on the high plateau spread along a mostly dry riverbed.

name: Mandalay
blurb: Myanmar's last royal capital. The palace sits in a walled square more than a mile per side, inside a wide moat; look for the perfect moated square and Mandalay Hill beside the Irrawaddy.

name: Vasai-Virar
blurb: Mumbai's fast-growing northern commuter belt. The ruins of a 16th-century Portuguese fort stand at Vasai; look for tidal creeks, mangroves and grey-white salt pans between the towns.

name: Panzhihua
blurb: A steel and mining city built from scratch in the 1960s on one of the world's largest vanadium-titanium iron ore deposits. Look for the city stacked on steep slopes above the Jinsha River gorge, with open-pit mines nearby.

name: Campinas
blurb: A tech and university city about 60 miles northwest of São Paulo, home to Unicamp and Viracopos airport. Look for a sprawling city on rolling hills of red soil and sugar cane.

name: Sofia
blurb: One of Europe's oldest cities, about 1,800 ft up in a basin at the foot of Mount Vitosha. Look for the dark massif rising to over 7,000 ft directly south of the city.

name: Beiliu
blurb: County-level city in southeast Guangxi known for making everyday porcelain. Look for a compact town on a flat river valley among low hills.

name: Mombasa
blurb: The old city is an island, tied to the mainland by bridges, a causeway and a ferry. The Portuguese built Fort Jesus here in 1593; look for the harbor at Kilindini, East Africa's busiest port.

name: Xinyu
blurb: A steel and solar-panel town on the Yuan River in western Jiangxi, ringed by low green hills and rice paddies. Look for the river cutting east through the city and the industrial yards along its banks.

name: Zhangye
blurb: A Hexi Corridor oasis near the Danxia landforms, hills striped in red, orange and yellow like a layer cake. Look for green fields against desert, with the snowy Qilian Mountains to the south.

name: Varanasi
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world and Hinduism's holiest. Look for the crescent of ghats, stone steps lining the west bank of the Ganges, facing an empty sandy shore on the other side.

name: Nizhny Novgorod
blurb: Founded in 1221 where the Oka meets the Volga. Look for the red brick walls of the Kremlin climbing the high bluff above the confluence, and the long cable car over the Volga.

name: Hiroshima
blurb: Destroyed by the first atomic bomb used in war, on August 6, 1945. Look for the river delta splitting the city into fingers of land, and Miyajima island in the bay to the southwest.

name: Chiang Mai
blurb: Northern Thailand's capital, founded in 1296, its old city a square ringed by a moat. Look for the moat-and-wall square and Doi Suthep, the mountain to the west with a gold-spired temple near its top.

name: Belgrade
blurb: Built where the Sava flows into the Danube, a spot fought over so often the city has been razed and rebuilt many times. Look for Kalemegdan fortress on the bluff at the confluence and the grid of New Belgrade across the Sava.

name: Maiduguri
blurb: The largest city in Nigeria's far northeast, on the dry plains of the Lake Chad basin near the borders of Niger, Chad and Cameroon. Look for a flat, sandy city in thin savanna scrub.

name: Shymkent
blurb: Kazakhstan's third-largest city, in the far south near the Uzbek border, where the steppe meets irrigated cotton and orchards. The western Tian Shan foothills rise to the east.

name: Bishkek
blurb: A leafy Soviet grid laid out on the plain below the Kyrgyz Ala-Too range, whose peaks top 15,000 ft just south of town. Look for the white wall of mountains rising straight off the city's edge.

name: Ahvaz
blurb: Oil city on the Karun, Iran's largest river by flow, and one of the hottest cities on Earth, with summer highs above 120 F. Look for the river looping through town and gas flares in the desert around it.

name: Srinagar
blurb: Kashmir's summer capital at about 5,200 ft. Look for Dal Lake lined with wooden houseboats and floating gardens, terraced Mughal gardens on its shore, and the Jhelum winding through the old city.

name: Aurangabad
blurb: The gateway to the rock-cut Buddhist and Hindu caves of Ajanta and Ellora. Its Bibi Ka Maqbara, a 17th-century tomb, copies the Taj Mahal; look for the white dome in a walled garden.

name: Fez
blurb: Its old medina, Fes el-Bali, is one of the largest car-free urban areas in the world, and al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is often called the oldest university still running. Look for a dense maze of flat roofs inside walls.

name: Naypyidaw
blurb: Built from scratch and made Myanmar's capital in 2005, it covers far more ground than its population needs. Look for a 20-lane boulevard with almost no traffic and widely scattered government compounds.

name: Aba
blurb: A commercial and manufacturing hub in southeast Nigeria, famous for its cobblers, tailors and the huge Ariaria market. Look for dense rooftops in green palm country.

name: Amritsar
blurb: Home of the Golden Temple, the holiest Sikh shrine, set in a square sacred pool. The Wagah border crossing with Pakistan is about 17 miles west; look for the gilded temple glinting in the water.

name: Zhoushan
blurb: China's largest archipelago, roughly 1,400 islands, now chained to the mainland by long bridges. Look for Mount Putuo, a Buddhist pilgrimage island, and fishing fleets crowding the harbors.

name: Krasnodar
blurb: The capital of Russia's breadbasket, on the Kuban River amid some of the richest black soil in the world. Look for the river looping around the south side of town and the endless flat fields beyond.

name: Aden
blurb: Its oldest quarter, still called Crater, sits inside an extinct volcano. Look for the dark volcanic peninsula wrapping around one of the finest natural harbors on the Arabian Sea, a British port from 1839 to 1967.

name: Samara
blurb: Sits on the Samara Bend, where the Volga loops around the Zhiguli Hills. In WWII it was the Soviet Union's backup capital. Look for the wide river and the long embankment along the city's edge.

name: Yingtan
blurb: A rail junction and copper-smelting town on the Xin River. Just south lies Longhushan, the red sandstone cliffs that are a cradle of Taoism; look for rust-red Danxia ridges rising out of green farmland.

name: Leiyang
blurb: County-level city in southern Hunan, birthplace of Cai Lun, the Han court official credited with inventing paper around 105 AD. Look for the Lei River and green hills.

name: Yichun
blurb: Forest city in the Lesser Khingan range, built on logging until commercial cutting of natural forest stopped in 2014. Look for dense forest on rolling hills and the town strung along the Tangwang River.

name: Ufa
blurb: Bashkortostan's capital sits on a ridge where the Ufa River meets the Belaya. Look for the rivers wrapping around the long city and its oil refineries spread to the north.

name: Rostov-on-Don
blurb: One of southern Russia's biggest cities, on the Don about 30 miles above the Sea of Azov. Look for the wide river along the city's south edge, with low floodplain marshes on the far bank.

name: Monterrey
blurb: Mexico's industrial capital, ringed by mountains. Look for Cerro de la Silla, the saddle-shaped peak on the east side, and the old blast furnaces preserved in Parque Fundidora.

name: Maputo
blurb: Mozambique's capital, called Lourenço Marques under the Portuguese, on a large bay. The Maputo-Katembe Bridge, opened in 2018, is the longest suspension bridge in Africa; look for it spanning the bay mouth.

name: Van
blurb: On the eastern shore of Lake Van, Turkey's largest lake and a salty soda lake with no outlet. Look for the deep blue water and the old Van Fortress on its long rock by the shore.

name: Ulsan
blurb: Hyundai's company town: one of the world's largest car plants, the world's largest shipyard and a giant petrochemical complex. Look for ships under construction in dry docks along the coast and refineries around the harbor.

name: Guwahati
blurb: The largest city of India's northeast, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra, one of the world's widest rivers. Look for the braided river with sandbars and green hills pressing in on the city.

name: Yerevan
blurb: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, founded as a fortress in 782 BC, built largely of pink volcanic stone. On a clear day Mount Ararat towers to the south across the Turkish border.

name: Biên Hòa
blurb: Industrial satellite of Ho Chi Minh City across the Dong Nai River, packed with factory parks. Its air base was one of the busiest US bases of the Vietnam War and still carries Agent Orange contamination.

name: Maracay
blurb: A garden city and military town on the northern edge of Lake Valencia. Look for the lake to the south and Henri Pittier National Park's forested mountains to the north.

name: Omsk
blurb: One of Siberia's largest cities, where the Om River joins the Irtysh. Dostoevsky served four years of prison here; look for the two rivers meeting downtown and refinery tanks on the north side.

name: Jiuquan
blurb: A Hexi Corridor oasis near the western end of the Great Wall at Jiayuguan. The Jiuquan launch center, China's first spaceport, is actually far to the north in Inner Mongolia. Look for green fields against gravel desert.

name: Krasnoyarsk
blurb: Spread along the Yenisei, one of the great Siberian rivers. Warm outflow from the dam upstream keeps the river from freezing through the city in winter; look for steaming open water amid the snow.

name: Gongzhuling
blurb: Its name means Princess Tomb. A farm city on the black-soil plain between Changchun and Siping, in the heart of China's corn belt, surrounded by a patchwork of huge flat fields.

name: N'Djamena
blurb: Chad's capital sits where the Logone joins the Chari River, directly across from Kousséri in Cameroon. Look for the two rivers meeting and the low tan city on flat Sahel land.

name: Astana
blurb: Built up from a provincial town into the capital after 1997, on open steppe that ranks it among the coldest capitals on Earth. Look for the Baiterek tower and the slanted tent of Khan Shatyr.

name: Ranchi
blurb: Jharkhand's capital on a plateau about 2,100 ft up, with waterfalls on the rivers around it. Look for green hills, rocky outcrops and Kanke and Dhurwa dams' reservoirs at the city's edges.

name: Gwalior
blurb: Crowned by a hilltop fort running about 2 miles along a sheer sandstone plateau some 300 ft above the city. Look for the long flat-topped mesa with walls along its rim.

name: Zhongwei
blurb: At Shapotou the dunes of the Tengger Desert run straight down to the Yellow River. Look for checkerboard straw grids pinning the sand along the railway, a technique pioneered here in the 1950s.

name: Barquisimeto
blurb: Venezuela's capital of folk music, on a dry plateau where the Andes meet the coastal ranges. Look for a big grid city surrounded by arid scrub and cactus country.

name: Hegang
blurb: Coal city in northeast Heilongjiang that became famous in China for some of the country's cheapest apartments after mining declined. Look for open-pit mines and waste heaps at the edge of town.

name: Tegucigalpa
blurb: Honduras' capital sits in a mountain bowl about 3,300 ft up. Its Toncontin airport had one of the world's trickiest approaches, a hard turn around hills onto a short runway, until international flights moved to Palmerola in 2021.

name: Chandigarh
blurb: One of the few cities planned from scratch by Le Corbusier in the 1950s, laid out in rectangular sectors. Look for the tidy grid against the Shivalik foothills and Sukhna Lake at the northeast corner.

name: Jerusalem
blurb: The Old City, inside walls built by the Ottomans in the 1530s, covers barely a third of a square mile. Look for the gold Dome of the Rock on its broad stone platform inside the walls.

name: Vijayawada
blurb: A big rail and commercial hub on the Krishna River, where the Prakasam Barrage stretches across the water. Look for the long dam line and rocky hills rising from the city.

name: Fangchenggang
blurb: Port city at the western end of China's mainland coastline, where it meets Vietnam. Look for the port's piers on a peninsula and the domes of a nuclear plant on the coast.

name: Voronezh
blurb: Peter the Great built Russia's first navy in shipyards here in the 1690s. Look for the long Voronezh Reservoir running north to south and splitting the city in two.

name: Mersin
blurb: One of Turkey's main Mediterranean ports, on a coast lined with citrus orchards and greenhouses. Look for the busy container port and white greenhouse roofs across the coastal plain.

name: São Luís
blurb: The only Brazilian state capital founded by the French, in 1612, on an island in a bay with some of the biggest tides in Brazil. Its old center is tiled in Portuguese azulejos; look for mudflats at low tide.

name: Jodhpur
blurb: The Blue City: much of the old town is washed in indigo. Mehrangarh Fort sits on a rock outcrop about 400 ft above it; look for the blue houses clustered under the fort at the edge of the Thar Desert.

name: Ogbomosho
blurb: One of the larger Yoruba cities of southwest Nigeria, a sprawl of low rust-colored roofs in farm and savanna country between Ibadan and Ilorin.

name: Ashgabat
blurb: Holds the record for the most white marble buildings of any city. Look for gleaming white towers on the edge of the Karakum Desert, with the Kopet Dag mountains on the Iranian border behind.

name: Ilorin
blurb: Capital of Kwara State, on the line between Nigeria's Yoruba south and Hausa north. Look for low tin roofs spreading over gently rolling savanna.

name: Enugu
blurb: The Coal City, founded on coal mining in the early 1900s and briefly the capital of breakaway Biafra in 1967. Look for the green escarpment of the Udi Hills on the west side of town.

name: Denizli
blurb: A textile city just south of Pamukkale, the white travertine terraces built up by hot springs. Look for the bright white hillside north of the city.

name: Perm
blurb: A big industrial city on the Kama River in the western foothills of the Urals, the jumping-off point for Siberia in the old days. Look for the broad river and the dark taiga around town.

name: Cologne
blurb: A Roman city on the Rhine, whose twin-spired cathedral took over 600 years to finish and survived heavy wartime bombing. Look for the dark Gothic spires beside the Hohenzollern rail bridge.

name: Ottawa
blurb: Parliament's Gothic towers stand on a bluff above the Ottawa River. In winter the Rideau Canal through downtown becomes a 4.8-mile skating rink; look for the canal running south from Parliament Hill.

name: San Jose
blurb: The Bay Area's largest city and Silicon Valley's hub, a flat grid of low buildings at the south end of the Bay. Look for the airport right next to downtown and the colored salt ponds along the Bay shore to the north.

name: Volgograd
blurb: As Stalingrad it saw the deadliest battle of World War II in 1942 and 1943. The city strings out some 50 miles along the Volga; look for the Motherland Calls statue, sword raised, on the Mamayev Kurgan hill.

name: Raipur
blurb: Chhattisgarh's capital, a center of steel and rice milling on the flat Chhattisgarh plain. Look for many small tanks (ponds) dotting the city and the planned new capital, Nava Raipur, to the southeast.

name: Arequipa
blurb: The White City, built from pale volcanic sillar stone, sits at the foot of El Misti, a near-perfect volcanic cone about 19,100 ft high. Look for the cone, often snow-tipped, northeast of town.

name: Marrakech
blurb: The Red City: walls and buildings in ochre earth, with the snowy High Atlas rising beyond. Look for the 12th-century Koutoubia minaret and the green squares of olive groves and gardens around the walls.

name: Kota
blurb: India's exam-coaching capital, where huge numbers of students cram for the national engineering and medical entrance tests. Look for the Chambal River curving through town, with a barrage and dams along it.

name: Quetta
blurb: Sits about 5,500 ft up in a bowl of bare mountains. An earthquake in 1935 flattened the city and killed tens of thousands; look for brown peaks walling in the valley on all sides.

name: Bareilly
blurb: A city on the Ramganga River in western Uttar Pradesh. Look for a flat sprawl surrounded by farmland, with the Himalayan foothills sometimes visible far to the north.

name: Guatemala City
blurb: Central America's largest city spreads across a plateau at about 4,900 ft, cut by deep ravines. Look for the volcanoes Agua, Fuego and Pacaya on the southern skyline, Fuego often smoking.

name: Xingning
blurb: A Hakka city in the mountains of northeast Guangdong. Look for the town spread along a river valley between green hills.

name: Lilongwe
blurb: Malawi's capital, a planned city that took over from Zomba in 1975. Look for spread-out, leafy suburbs on a high plateau.

name: Port-au-Prince
blurb: Haiti's capital climbs from the bay into steep hills; the 2010 earthquake killed well over 100,000 people here. Look for dense neighborhoods covering the slopes above the harbor.

name: Kirkuk
blurb: Sits on one of the world's oldest giant oil fields, struck in 1927. At nearby Baba Gurgur gas has burned for thousands of years; look for flames and oil works around the city.

name: Ruzhou
blurb: Gave its name to Ru ware, the pale blue-green porcelain prized by the Song emperors. Look for the town in the Ru River valley with hills to the north and south.

name: Dnipro
blurb: One of Ukraine's biggest cities, a rocket and steel center on a wide bend of the Dnipro River. Look for the long bridges and islands crossing a river roughly half a mile wide.

name: Asmara
blurb: At about 7,600 ft, a city built largely by Italy in the 1930s, its modernist buildings now a UNESCO site. Look for a flat high plateau that drops off steeply to the Red Sea.

name: Campo Grande
blurb: A planned grid city on Brazil's cattle plains and the gateway to the southern Pantanal. Look for red earth and wide pastures around wide avenues.

name: Coimbatore
blurb: Called the Manchester of South India for its textile mills. Look for the Western Ghats rising abruptly to the west and the Palakkad Gap, a break in the mountains.

name: Danzhou
blurb: A sprawling, mostly rural city in western Hainan, a center of the island's rubber plantations. Look for green estates and red earth running down to the Gulf of Tonkin coast.

name: Solapur
blurb: A textile city in Maharashtra known for cotton towels and bedsheets. Look for a flat, dry plain with lakes on the city's edge.

name: Freetown
blurb: Founded in 1792 as a home for freed slaves, on one of the largest natural harbors in the world. Look for the city climbing green mountains at the tip of a peninsula above the wide Sierra Leone River estuary.

name: Seongnam
blurb: Fast-growing suburb south of Seoul that includes Pangyo, home to tech giants like Naver and Kakao. Look for clusters of identical high-rise apartment blocks among wooded hills.

name: Dushanbe
blurb: Tajikistan's capital, whose name means Monday, after the market day of the village it grew from. Look for the huge flagpole, once the tallest in the world, and the Varzob River cutting through.

name: Kermanshah
blurb: Near Bisotun, where Darius the Great had a huge trilingual inscription carved into a cliff. Look for the city on a high plain beneath the long ridges of the Zagros.

name: Salé
blurb: Twin city to Rabat, facing it across the mouth of the Bou Regreg river. Look for the river mouth and the old walled medina beside the Atlantic.

name: Yingde
blurb: Known across China for its black tea and its limestone. Look for the Bei River winding past steep green karst hills and quarries.

name: Kingston
blurb: Jamaica's capital, on one of the largest natural harbors in the world, sheltered by the long Palisadoes spit. Look for the airport out on that spit and the Blue Mountains behind the city.

name: Managua
blurb: Nicaragua's capital on Lake Managua, its center flattened by a 1972 earthquake and never fully rebuilt. Look for round crater lakes like Tiscapa inside the city.

name: Luoding
blurb: A county-level city in western Guangdong's hill country. Look for the town on a river plain hemmed in by green hills and farmland.

name: Kitakyūshū
blurb: Japan's steel city since the Yawata works opened in 1901, at Kyushu's northern tip. Look for the industrial bay crossed by the red Wakato Bridge, and the Kanmon Strait separating it from Honshu.

name: Aguascalientes City
blurb: Named for its hot springs, this colonial city hosts the San Marcos Fair, Mexico's largest. Look for big auto plants on its outskirts, including Nissan's, set on the high dry plateau.

name: Khulna
blurb: Bangladesh's third city and the gateway to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest. Look for brown tidal rivers and shrimp ponds giving way to dense green to the south.

name: Chihuahua City
blurb: Capital of Mexico's largest state, on the high Chihuahuan Desert. Pancho Villa's house is a museum here, and the Copper Canyon railway starts from the city.

name: Mysore
blurb: Former seat of the Wodeyar maharajas, whose palace is lit by nearly 100,000 bulbs on festival nights. Look for Chamundi Hill rising southeast of town.

name: Qitaihe
blurb: A coal city in eastern Heilongjiang. Look for mine works and spoil heaps around the town among rolling farmland and forest.

name: Trujillo
blurb: Founded in 1534 beside Chan Chan, the Chimú capital and the largest adobe city of the pre-Columbian Americas. Look for the old city's oval ring road where the walls stood, between green fields and desert.

name: Tiruchirappalli
blurb: Known for the Rock Fort temple on a huge rock outcrop, and for Srirangam, one of the largest functioning Hindu temples in the world. Look for the island between two arms of the Kaveri.

name: Cartagena
blurb: Its colonial old town sits inside about 7 miles of stone walls, built to fend off pirates. Look for the walled core, the high-rise Bocagrande peninsula next to it, and the San Felipe fortress on a hill.

name: Naples
blurb: Spread around its bay beneath Vesuvius, which buried Pompeii in 79 AD. Look for the volcano's broken cone east of the city and the islands of Capri and Ischia offshore.

name: Owerri
blurb: Capital of Imo State in southeastern Nigeria. Look for a city of low rooftops surrounded by forest and farmland.

name: Bobo-Dioulasso
blurb: Burkina Faso's second city. Its Grand Mosque, built of mud in the 1880s with wooden beams sticking out of the walls, is the classic Sahel style.

name: Lubango
blurb: Angola's southern highland city at about 5,800 ft, watched over by a Christ statue on the hill. Look west for the Serra da Leba road's tight hairpins down the escarpment.

name: Dammam
blurb: Heart of Saudi Arabia's oil industry: the kingdom's first commercial oil came from Dammam Well No. 7 nearby in 1938. Its King Fahd International is one of the largest airports in the world by area.

name: Donetsk
blurb: A coal and steel city in the Donbas, under Russian control since 2014. Look for the cone-shaped slag heaps, spoil piles from the mines, rising around the city.

name: Libreville
blurb: Gabon's capital, strung along the Komo estuary where it meets the Gulf of Guinea, just north of the equator. Look for the city lining the shore with rainforest pressing in behind.

name: Mérida
blurb: Yucatán's capital, the White City, built from the stones of the Maya town of T'hó. Look for a flat limestone plain covered in low scrub, with no rivers at all: water flows underground through cenotes.

name: Bangui
blurb: The Central African Republic's capital, on the Ubangi River. Look for the river forming the border, with Congo's Zongo directly across the water.

name: Abeokuta
blurb: Built around Olumo Rock, a granite outcrop that sheltered the Egba people during 19th-century wars. Look for bare gray domes of rock poking out of rust-red roofs beside the Ogun River.

name: Cancun
blurb: Planned by the Mexican government and built from scratch starting around 1970. Look for the hotel zone, a 7-shaped barrier strip between the turquoise Caribbean and the lagoon behind it.

name: Moradabad
blurb: Called the Brass City for its huge metalware export trade, on the Ramganga River in western Uttar Pradesh. Look for dense town on the flat Ganges plain, laced with canals and farm plots.

name: Tabuk
blurb: Saudi garrison city near the Jordanian border, in the region where the NEOM megaproject is being built. Look for green center-pivot farm circles dotting the brown desert.

name: El Alto
blurb: At about 13,600 ft, one of the highest big cities in the world, perched on the Altiplano rim above La Paz. Look for its cable-car lines dropping over the edge into the canyon.

name: Sulaymaniyah
blurb: The cultural capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, in a valley ringed by the Zagros at about 2,900 ft. Look for the city laid against the long ridge of Goyzha mountain to the northeast.

name: Klang
blurb: Selangor's royal town and home to Port Klang, Malaysia's busiest port. Look for container terminals and oil palm plantations along the lower Klang River.

name: Jamnagar
blurb: Next door sits the world's largest oil refinery complex, run by Reliance. Look for its huge grid of tanks and process units west of town on the Gulf of Kutch.

name: Gurugram
blurb: Farmland in the 1990s, now Delhi's glass-tower office suburb, officially renamed Gurugram. Look for clusters of new towers and expressways southwest of Delhi, near the airport.

name: Yangchun
blurb: A western Guangdong city set among limestone karst, with big caves nearby. Look for the Moyang River and the sharp green peaks around town.

name: Ramadi
blurb: Capital of Anbar province on the Euphrates, fought over repeatedly in the Iraq war and again against ISIS. Look for the river and its green strip of farms cutting through tan desert.

name: Aligarh
blurb: Known for its locks and for Aligarh Muslim University, founded in 1875. The city spreads across the flat farmland between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers.

name: Barinas
blurb: A cattle-ranching city on the Venezuelan llanos, the vast plains at the foot of the Andes, and hometown of Hugo Chávez. Look for flat grassland stretching east and mountains rising to the west.

name: Jalandhar
blurb: Punjab city that makes a large share of India's sports gear, from cricket bats to hockey sticks. Look for a dense city set in a flat green grid of wheat and rice fields.

name: Eskişehir
blurb: A university city on the Anatolian plateau in western Turkey, split by the Porsuk River, which has canals and tram lines running through the center. Look for the grid spreading across a broad dry plain.

name: Teresina
blurb: Often called Brazil's hottest state capital, and the only northeastern capital not on the coast. Look for the city on the strip of land between the Parnaíba and Poti rivers.

name: Lhasa
blurb: Tibet's capital at about 11,975 ft, one of the highest cities in the world. Look for the white and red Potala Palace on its hill above the Lhasa River valley, with bare mountains on all sides.

name: Ipoh
blurb: Built on the tin rush in the Kinta Valley, ringed by limestone hills full of cave temples. Look for old tin-mining pools dotting the valley floor.

name: Viana
blurb: A sprawling municipality on Luanda's eastern edge, an industrial and rail zone mixed with dense informal neighborhoods. Look for rows of warehouses and packed tin roofs.

name: Saltillo
blurb: At about 5,200 ft with the Sierra Madre Oriental behind it, the "Detroit of Mexico" builds cars and trucks for GM and Stellantis. Look for big assembly plants on the flat plain.

name: Hermosillo
blurb: Capital of Sonora in the Sonoran Desert, one of Mexico's hottest cities. Look for the antenna-topped Cerro de la Campana right beside downtown, and the desert pressing in on every side.

name: Mexicali
blurb: Border twin of Calexico and capital of Baja California. Look for irrigated fields in bright green against the desert and the border line running dead straight between the two cities.

name: Cheongju
blurb: Where the Jikji was printed in 1377, the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type. Look for the city on a basin plain, with its airport to the northeast.

name: Akure
blurb: Capital of Ondo State in Nigeria's southwestern forest belt. Look for smooth granite inselbergs, bare domes of rock, rising out of green bush around the city's sprawl of tin roofs.

name: Erbil
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited places on Earth: its citadel mound rises about 100 ft above downtown. Look for the oval mound with rings of roads spreading out around it.

name: Kathmandu
blurb: In a bowl-shaped valley at about 4,600 ft, with the Himalaya on the northern horizon. Look for the white domes of the Boudhanath and Swayambhunath stupas.

name: Huambo
blurb: Planned by the Portuguese as Nova Lisboa and once meant to be the colonial capital. At about 5,600 ft in the central highlands, it was devastated in Angola's civil war.

name: Turin
blurb: Home of Fiat and host of the 2006 Winter Olympics, on the Po with the Alps on three sides. Look for the old Lingotto factory with its rooftop test track, and the spire of the Mole Antonelliana.

name: Saratov
blurb: Volga city where Yuri Gagarin came down after the first human spaceflight in 1961, landing in a field across the river. Look for the long road bridge spanning the very wide Volga to Engels.

name: Bhubaneswar
blurb: The Temple City of India: hundreds of medieval temples still stand, and its modern half was laid out in 1948 as Odisha's new capital. Look for the tall curved tower of the Lingaraj temple in the old town.

name: Tongchuan
blurb: Coal mining city north of Xi'an on the Loess Plateau. Look for yellow loess hills carved into terraces and deep gullies around the town.

name: João Pessoa
blurb: Sits beside Ponta do Seixas, the easternmost point of mainland South America. Building heights are capped near the beach, so look for a long low seafront with towers stepping up farther inland.

name: Trabzon
blurb: An old Black Sea port backed by steep green mountains, once capital of the Byzantine Empire of Trebizond. Look for the city stacked on hillsides above a long seawall and the airport runway along the shore.

name: Jos
blurb: Sits on the Jos Plateau at about 4,000 ft, noticeably cooler than the plains below. A century of tin mining pocked the land around it; look for scattered water-filled pits and spoil heaps among rocky hills.

name: Mira-Bhayandar
blurb: A dense suburb at Mumbai's northern edge, between Sanjay Gandhi National Park and the tidal creeks. Look for mangroves and salt pans along the waterways.

name: Culiacán
blurb: Capital of Sinaloa, center of one of Mexico's richest farm valleys. Look for the spot downtown where two rivers join to form the Culiacán River.

name: Kraków
blurb: Poland's capital until 1596 and one of the few big Polish cities that came through World War II mostly intact. Look for Wawel Castle above a bend in the Vistula and the green ring of park where the old walls stood.

name: Oran
blurb: Algeria's second city, a Mediterranean port where Camus set The Plague. Look for the Santa Cruz fort and chapel perched on the mountain directly above the harbor.

name: Bandar Lampung
blurb: At Sumatra's southern tip on Lampung Bay, across the Sunda Strait from Java; the 1883 Krakatoa tsunami swept this shore. Look for the bay and port with green hills behind.

name: Blantyre
blurb: Malawi's commercial center, founded by Scottish missionaries and named for David Livingstone's birthplace. Look for the city in the Shire Highlands, with Mulanje's massif on the eastern horizon.

name: Shigatse
blurb: Tibet's second city at about 12,600 ft, seat of the Panchen Lama's Tashilhunpo Monastery. Look for the town where the Nyang River meets the broad, braided Yarlung Tsangpo.

name: Bordeaux
blurb: Its crescent bend in the Garonne earned it the name Port of the Moon. Look for the river's curve, the stone quays and the vineyards spreading outside the city.

name: Laiyang
blurb: Small city in Shandong's Jiaodong Peninsula, known across China for its pears. Look for orchards and farmland in rolling hills around the town.

name: Santiago de Querétaro
blurb: Its colonial center is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and an 18th-century stone aqueduct of 74 arches still crosses the east side. Look for the aqueduct's line and the aerospace and auto plants on the outskirts.

name: Port Said
blurb: Founded in 1859 to build the Suez Canal, at its Mediterranean entrance. Look for the canal running ruler-straight south and Port Fouad facing the city across the water.

name: Niigata
blurb: The biggest city on Japan's Sea of Japan coast, at the mouth of the Shinano, the country's longest river. Look for the river mouth and endless rice paddies on the plain.

name: Hamamatsu
blurb: Birthplace of Yamaha, Suzuki and Kawai, a city of instruments and motorcycles. Look for Lake Hamana just west of town, a lagoon with a narrow opening to the Pacific.

name: Gongyi
blurb: Home to the Northern Song imperial tombs, where the Luo River meets the Yellow River west of Zhengzhou. Look for the Yellow River's wide sandy bed to the north and loess terraces around town.

name: Kashgar
blurb: China's westernmost city, a Silk Road oasis for more than 2,000 years, closer to Baghdad than to Beijing. Look for green oasis fields at the edge of the Taklamakan Desert with the Pamirs rising to the west.

name: Goma
blurb: On Lake Kivu beneath Nyiragongo, home to one of the world's largest lava lakes. Lava flows have reached the city, most recently in 2021; look for black lava fields among the houses.

name: Cotonou
blurb: Benin's largest city, sandwiched between the Atlantic and Lake Nokoue. Look on the lake for Ganvie, a village built entirely on stilts.

name: Homs
blurb: Syria's third city, heavily damaged during the civil war. Look for the Orontes River on the west side and the oil refinery near town.

name: Valencia
blurb: After a 1957 flood the Turia River was diverted around the city and its old bed became a 5-mile park. Look for that green ribbon ending at the white City of Arts and Sciences.

name: Hamhung
blurb: North Korea's second-largest city and its chemical industry hub. In December 1950 nearly 100,000 civilians were evacuated by sea from its port, Hungnam.

name: La Plata
blurb: A planned provincial capital founded in 1882 on a perfect square grid. Look for diagonal avenues slicing an X through the grid and a forest park on its northeast edge.

name: Erzurum
blurb: One of Turkey's highest cities at about 6,300 ft, with famously harsh winters and a ski mountain, Palandöken, on its southern edge. Look for the city on a bare, high plain, often snow-covered.

name: Zagreb
blurb: Croatia's capital, on the Sava River beneath Medvednica mountain. Look for the red roofs of the hilltop Upper Town and the spires of the cathedral.

name: Al Ain
blurb: The UAE's Garden City, an oasis town on the Oman border with ancient falaj irrigation channels. Look for Jebel Hafeet, a lone 4,000-ft ridge rising from the desert just south of town.

name: Zaria
blurb: One of the old Hausa city-states, with a walled old city centuries old, and home to Ahmadu Bello University, one of the largest universities in Africa. Look for the dense mud-brown core of the old town.

name: Bahawalpur
blurb: Former princely state capital on the edge of the Cholistan Desert, known for its white palaces. Look for the sharp line where green irrigated fields end and tan desert begins.

name: Uberlândia
blurb: The agribusiness hub of Minas Gerais' Triângulo Mineiro. Look for the city's grid on a cerrado plateau, ringed by soy and sugarcane fields.

name: Chamdo
blurb: An eastern Tibetan town squeezed into a narrow valley where two rivers join to form the Mekong. Look for the confluence below steep, bare mountains.

name: Kaduna
blurb: Built by the British in the early 1900s as the capital of Northern Nigeria, on a river whose Hausa name refers to crocodiles. Look for the Kaduna River looping through town and the oil refinery on the south side.

name: Maturín
blurb: An oil-industry city on the eastern Venezuelan plains, set among savanna and moriche palm swamps. Look for a flat green landscape cut by slow, winding rivers.

name: Shizuishan
blurb: Coal and industry city on the Yellow River in northern Ningxia, squeezed between the Helan Mountains and the desert. Look for the river's green strip of irrigated fields against brown desert.

name: Ciudad Guayana
blurb: A planned industrial city built from 1961 where the Caroní River meets the Orinoco, home to steel and aluminum plants. Look for the dark Caroní water meeting the muddy Orinoco in a visible two-tone line.

name: Natal
blurb: The Corner of South America, the continent's closest big city to Africa and a key WWII air base for ferrying planes across the Atlantic. Look for the huge dunes of Genipabu and the star-shaped fort at the river mouth.

name: Thiruvananthapuram
blurb: Kerala's capital near India's southern tip; India's first rockets were launched at Thumba on its edge. Look for coconut palms covering everything right to the beach and the runway along the coast.

name: Nampula
blurb: The main city of northern Mozambique, in country famous for granite inselbergs. Look for bare dome-shaped rock hills rising out of the plain.

name: Pretoria
blurb: South Africa's executive capital, called the Jacaranda City for the thousands of trees that turn its streets purple in October. Look for the Union Buildings on their hill and the ridges framing the city.

name: Calabar
blurb: Old slave-trading and palm-oil port near the Cameroon border, now known for its December carnival. Look for the city on high ground between two rivers, with mangrove creeks spreading toward the sea.

name: Bouaké
blurb: Ivory Coast's second-largest city, the rebel capital during the country's 2002 to 2011 crisis. Sits on savanna in the center of the country.

name: Cabinda
blurb: Angola's exclave, cut off from the rest of the country by a strip of Congo's coast. Offshore wells here have produced a large share of Angola's oil; look for platforms and tankers off the beach.

name: Kumamoto
blurb: Home to Kumamoto Castle, badly damaged in the 2016 earthquakes. Look east for Mount Aso, one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world, with farms and towns inside its rim.

name: São José dos Campos
blurb: Home of Embraer, the world's third-largest builder of commercial jets, and Brazil's aerospace research center. Look for the long runway shared by Embraer and the air force's technical institute.

name: Urmia
blurb: Near the shore of Lake Urmia, once one of the largest salt lakes in the world, which has shrunk dramatically since the 1990s. Look for white salt flats and the causeway across the lake to the east.

name: Namyangju
blurb: Riverside suburb northeast of Seoul near where the North and South Han rivers join to form the Han. Look for high-rise apartment clusters tucked into folds of wooded hills along the water.

name: Ribeirão Preto
blurb: Capital of a rich farm region, first for coffee and now for sugarcane and ethanol. Look for the endless green squares of cane fields and red soil around the city.

name: Osogbo
blurb: Known for the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, a UNESCO World Heritage forest along the Osun River at the edge of town. Look for that dark block of old forest pressed against the city's tin roofs.

name: Tamale
blurb: Northern Ghana's largest city, a trading hub on the flat savanna. Look for low rooftops spreading across dry, tree-dotted grassland with hardly a tall building.

name: Jiyuan
blurb: At the foot of Wangwu Mountain, setting of the fable of the Foolish Old Man who moved the mountains. Look for the city on the plain where the Taihang and Wangwu ranges rise to the north.

name: Sagamihara
blurb: A Tokyo-area commuter city and home of JAXA's space science institute, which ran the Hayabusa asteroid missions. Look for the Sagami River and the Tanzawa mountains rising to the west.

name: Najaf
blurb: Holds the shrine of Imam Ali and Wadi al-Salam, one of the largest cemeteries in the world. Look for the gold dome and the vast gray sprawl of graves on the city's north side.

name: Sorocaba
blurb: Industrial city west of São Paulo, once a stop for mule trains heading south. Look for factories and housing spreading across rolling hills.

name: Okayama
blurb: Home to Korakuen, one of Japan's three great gardens, and the black "Crow Castle" beside it. Look for the Asahi River bending around the garden on the Seto Inland Sea plain.

name: San Pedro Sula
blurb: Honduras' industrial capital, packed with garment factories, on the flat Sula Valley floor. Look for the city butting up against the Merendón mountains, which rise abruptly to the west.

name: Mississauga
blurb: One of Canada's largest cities, though most of it is low suburbia beside Toronto, and home to Pearson, Canada's busiest airport. Look for the twin curvy Absolute World towers, nicknamed the Marilyn Monroe towers.

name: Oslo
blurb: Norway's capital sits at the head of the Oslofjord, about 60 miles from open sea, ringed by forested hills. Look for the white sloping roof of the opera house at the water and the Holmenkollen ski jump on the ridge above.

name: Shihezi
blurb: A planned city founded in 1950 by soldiers of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps. Look for a tidy grid surrounded by huge irrigated cotton fields north of the Tian Shan.

name: Suez
blurb: At the canal's southern end on the Gulf of Suez. Look for ships queued in the gulf, refinery tanks along the shore and the desert mountains of Sinai across the water.

name: Jaboatão dos Guararapes
blurb: Just south of Recife, site of two 17th-century battles that drove the Dutch out of Brazil, counted as the birth of the Brazilian army. Look for the long beach of Piedade lined with high-rises.

name: Zaporizhzhia
blurb: An industrial city on the Dnipro around Khortytsia, a large island that was the Cossacks' stronghold. Look for the DniproHES dam across the river and the island just downstream.

name: Zanzibar City
blurb: Stone Town, its old core, is a UNESCO World Heritage site and birthplace of Freddie Mercury. Look for the maze of old roofs on a point of land and dhows in the harbor.

name: Bhiwandi
blurb: A power-loom town turned India's warehouse capital, northeast of Mumbai. Look for row after row of warehouse roofs along the highways.

name: Latakia
blurb: Syria's main port, on the Mediterranean with the coastal mountains behind it. Look for the container docks and the city spread along the shore.

name: Bukavu
blurb: Built on fingers of land poking into the southern end of Lake Kivu. Look for the Ruzizi River marking the Rwandan border right beside the city.

name: Mwanza
blurb: Tanzania's second city, on Lake Victoria's southern shore. Look for granite boulders piled along the shore and in the lake, including Bismarck Rock.

name: Saharanpur
blurb: A wood-carving center in the far north of Uttar Pradesh, close to where the plains meet the Shivalik hills. On clear days, look north for the first ridges of the Himalayan foothills.

name: Warangal
blurb: Capital of the Kakatiya dynasty, known for Warangal Fort's carved stone gateways and the Thousand Pillar Temple. Look for the fort's ring of earthen walls on the plain.

name: Parachinar
blurb: Remote town in the Kurram Valley, on a finger of Pakistan that pokes deep into Afghanistan toward Kabul. Look for a green valley floor under the Safed Koh range on the Afghan border, often snow-capped.

name: Jeju
blurb: Capital of Jeju Island; the Seoul to Jeju air route is often ranked the busiest in the world. Look for Hallasan, South Korea's highest peak at 6,388 ft, rising behind the city.

name: Hama
blurb: Famous for its norias, giant wooden waterwheels on the Orontes that have lifted water for centuries. Look for the river winding through the city among green fields.

name: Helsinki
blurb: Built on a peninsula and islands. Look at the harbor mouth for Suomenlinna, an 18th-century sea fortress spread across several islands, a UNESCO site.

name: Turpan
blurb: An oasis in one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth, the Turpan Depression. Look for green vineyards and grape-drying sheds against bare desert, and the red Flaming Mountains to the east.

name: Bauchi
blurb: Capital of Bauchi State in Nigeria's northeastern savanna and the gateway to Yankari Game Reserve. Look for a low city of tin and mud roofs spread across dry grassland that turns green only in the rainy season.

name: Salem
blurb: Steel and mango city ringed by hills, including the Shevaroy Hills and the hill station of Yercaud. Look for the green ridges around the city.

name: Sinnuris
blurb: Farm town in the Faiyum, a desert depression watered by a branch canal from the Nile. Look for a green oasis of fields with salty Lake Qarun to the north.

name: Lokoja
blurb: Sits where the Niger and the Benue, Nigeria's two great rivers, meet, and was the first capital of colonial Nigeria. Look for the Y of the two wide, sandbar-streaked rivers below Mount Patti.

name: Cuiabá
blurb: Sits near the geodesic center of South America and is the gateway to the Pantanal wetlands. Look for the Cuiabá River winding through savanna and pasture.

name: Reynosa
blurb: Border city across the Rio Grande from McAllen, Texas, packed with factories. Look for the river winding along its north side and the bridges into Texas.

name: Torreón
blurb: Heart of the La Laguna cotton and dairy region, twinned with Gomez Palacio across the usually dry Nazas River. Look for the giant Christ statue on the Cerro de las Noas above town.

name: Karbala
blurb: A Shiite pilgrimage city built around the gold-domed shrine of Imam Husayn; millions walk here for Arbaeen each year. Look for the twin shrines in the center and palm groves around town.

name: Shizuoka
blurb: The center of Japan's green tea country, on Suruga Bay, with Mount Fuji to the northeast on a clear day. Look for tea terraces on the hills and the long pine-covered Miho spit.

name: Seville
blurb: Summer highs can top 110°F, and its cathedral is the largest Gothic church in the world. Look for the Guadalquivir River, the Giralda tower beside the cathedral, and the waffled Metropol Parasol.

name: Dairut
blurb: Upper Egypt town where the Bahr Yusuf canal, which feeds the Faiyum, branches off the main irrigation canal. Look for a thin green strip of fields between desert cliffs.

name: Rasht
