blurb: One of the wettest cities in Iran, on the green Caspian lowland of Gilan. Look for rice paddies and forest around town, with the Caspian shore to the north.

name: Kochi
blurb: A spice port for centuries, built on islands and peninsulas around a backwater harbor. Its airport was the first in the world to run entirely on solar power; look for the islands and lagoons at the harbor mouth.

name: Acapulco de Juárez
blurb: The jet-set resort of the 1950s, wrapped around a deep horseshoe bay on the Pacific; Hurricane Otis hit it at Category 5 in 2023. Look for hotel towers lining the curve of the bay.

name: Gorakhpur
blurb: An eastern Uttar Pradesh city near the Nepal border, named for the yogi Gorakhnath, with one of the world's longest railway platforms. Look for Ramgarh Tal, a large lake on the city's edge.

name: Chongjin
blurb: North Korea's third-largest city, a steel and port town on the Sea of Japan. It was among the places hardest hit by the 1990s famine.

name: Copenhagen
blurb: The Oresund link to Sweden starts as a tunnel, surfaces on an artificial island, then becomes a 5-mile bridge. Look for the star-shaped Kastellet fortress near the harbor.

name: Mar del Plata
blurb: This is Mar del Plata, Argentina's biggest beach resort, whose population swells every summer. Look for miles of beaches and breakwaters along the Atlantic, with the casino and hotels curving around the central bay.

name: Zaragoza
blurb: Spain's fifth city, halfway between Madrid and Barcelona on the Ebro. Look for the many towers and tiled domes of the Basilica del Pilar on the riverbank.

name: Bulawayo
blurb: Zimbabwe's second city, laid out by the British in the 1890s with streets wide enough to turn a span of oxen. Look for the grid of broad avenues and the granite hills of Matobo to the south.

name: Villavicencio
blurb: Gateway to the Llanos, where the eastern range of the Andes drops abruptly onto flat plains stretching to Venezuela. Look for that sharp line between mountains and grassland.

name: Tolyatti
blurb: Named after Italian Communist Palmiro Togliatti and home of AvtoVAZ, maker of the Lada. Look for the enormous car plant and the hydroelectric dam holding back the Volga.

name: Makhachkala
blurb: Dagestan's capital, squeezed between the Caspian Sea and the steep Tarki-Tau ridge. Look for the city strung along the coast below the hills.

name: Catia La Mar
blurb: A coastal town beside Caracas's Simón Bolívar International Airport, squeezed between the Caribbean and the steep Ávila range. Look for the runways along the shore and mountains rising straight behind.

name: Feira de Santana
blurb: Bahia's second city grew from a cattle fair at a crossroads of the interior. Look for major highways radiating from the city in all directions across flat farmland.

name: Hofuf
blurb: Main town of Al-Ahsa, one of the largest oases in the world, with well over 2 million date palms. Look for a dark green island of palm groves surrounded by sand.

name: Jalingo
blurb: Capital of Taraba State, a young city that grew fast after the state was created in 1991. Look for tin roofs spread through open savanna, with the highlands toward Cameroon on the eastern horizon.

name: Sargodha
blurb: Punjab farm town known as Pakistan's citrus capital for its kinnow oranges, and home to one of the country's main air bases. Look for orchards and canals laid out in a precise grid.

name: Bujumbura
blurb: On the northern tip of Lake Tanganyika, the world's longest freshwater lake at about 410 miles. Look for the lake running south out of sight between mountain walls.

name: Victoria de Durango
blurb: Hollywood shot dozens of westerns around this high-desert state capital, John Wayne's among them. Look for the Cerro del Mercado, a hill of iron ore on the north edge of town.

name: Jeonju
blurb: Home of bibimbap and a hanok village of more than 700 traditional tiled-roof houses. Look for the dark curving roofs of the hanok district next to the modern city.

name: Łódź
blurb: A 19th-century textile boomtown once called the Polish Manchester. Look for Piotrkowska Street running ruler-straight through the center for more than 2 miles, and the old red-brick mills.

name: Guntur
blurb: Known as India's chili capital, with one of Asia's largest chili markets. Look for red fields and drying yards in the flat farmland near the Krishna River, close to Amaravati, the planned state capital.

name: Athens
blurb: More than 3 million people fill a basin ringed by mountains, a near-solid sea of white concrete. Look for the Acropolis rising out of it, and Piraeus harbor on the Saronic Gulf.

name: Aracaju
blurb: One of Brazil's first planned cities, laid out on a grid in 1855 at the mouth of the Sergipe River. Look for the long, straight Atalaia beach running south of the river mouth.

name: Cochabamba
blurb: At about 8,400 ft in a fertile valley. Look for the Christ statue on the hill east of town, slightly taller than Rio's.

name: Benghazi
blurb: Libya's second city, on the Mediterranean, where the 2011 uprising began. Look for the harbor and salt lagoons inside the city, with desert beyond.

name: Palermo
blurb: Sicily's capital, on the Conca d'Oro, a plain squeezed between mountains and sea. Look for the bulk of Monte Pellegrino rising at the north end of the harbor.

name: Namangan
blurb: Uzbekistan's second- or third-largest city, in the north of the Fergana Valley, ringed by mountains. Look for a green, intensely irrigated valley floor of orchards and cotton fields.

name: Bhilai
blurb: Its steel plant, built with Soviet help in the late 1950s, has long been India's main maker of railway track. Look for blast furnaces and slag heaps beside a grid township.

name: Kitwe
blurb: Zambia's second-largest city and the hub of the Copperbelt. Look for the huge Nkana copper mine, smelter and tailings dams on the city's edge.

name: Mangaluru
blurb: A port on India's west coast where two rivers meet the Arabian Sea. Look for coconut palms, the river mouths, and the New Mangalore port's breakwaters north of town.

name: Mansoura
blurb: Delta city on the Damietta branch of the Nile. In 1250 the crusading French king Louis IX was defeated and captured here.

name: Barnaul
blurb: Founded in 1730 as a silver smelter for the Demidov industrial dynasty, on the Ob River. Look for the Ob's wide floodplain and forested sandbars along the city's eastern edge.

name: Düsseldorf
blurb: Capital of North Rhine-Westphalia and Germany's fashion and advertising hub, on a broad bend of the Rhine. Look for the Rhine Tower and the warped Gehry buildings of the Media Harbor on the riverbank.

name: Helwan
blurb: Cairo's southern industrial suburb on the Nile's east bank, long home to Egypt's steel and cement works. Look for factory smoke and quarries cut into the desert plateau.

name: Al Hudaydah
blurb: Yemen's main Red Sea port, a lifeline for food imports that has been heavily fought over in the civil war. Look for a flat, sandy coastal plain, the Tihamah, backed by mountains far inland.

name: Joinville
blurb: Founded by German settlers in 1851, it hosts the only branch of the Bolshoi ballet school outside Russia. Look for the mangroves and channels of Babitonga Bay east of the city.

name: Izhevsk
blurb: Home of the Kalashnikov rifle, the capital of Udmurtia in the Russian Urals foothills. Look for the long dammed pond on the Izh River that the city grew around.

name: Leipzig
blurb: The 1989 Monday demonstrations here helped bring down East Germany. Look for the old open-pit lignite mines south of town, now being flooded into a chain of new lakes.

name: Khabarovsk
blurb: A Russian Far East city on a high bank of the Amur, just across from the Chinese border. Look for the long bridge over the Amur and the river's huge braided channels.

name: Ta'izz
blurb: Yemen's third-largest city, set below Jabal Sabir, a mountain rising to about 10,000 ft right over it. Look for houses spreading across valleys at the mountain's foot.

name: Bucaramanga
blurb: Colombia's "City of Parks" on a plateau above deep valleys. The Chicamocha Canyon, one of the deepest in South America, lies to the south.

name: Kandahar
blurb: Afghanistan's second-largest city and the Taliban's birthplace, set in desert where the Arghandab River's green strip runs past. Look for the sprawling former NATO airfield to the southeast.

name: Ulyanovsk
blurb: Lenin's birthplace, set high on the Volga where the river is dammed into the very wide Kuybyshev Reservoir. Look for the city's long bridges crossing water that is miles wide.

name: Stuttgart
blurb: Home of Mercedes-Benz and Porsche, built in a steep bowl of vineyard-covered hills. Look for the center packed onto the valley floor, vines on the slopes, and the Neckar River to the east.

name: Kozhikode
blurb: Old Calicut, where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498 and opened the sea route from Europe to India. Look for the long palm-lined beach on the Arabian Sea.

name: Kuantan
blurb: The main city on the east coast of peninsular Malaysia, on the South China Sea. Look for the river mouth and long sandy beaches running up the coast.

name: Pyeongtaek
blurb: Home of Camp Humphreys, the largest US military base overseas, and a giant Samsung chip plant. Look for the base's huge grid and airfield west of town and the port on Asan Bay.

name: Cuttack
blurb: A 1,000-year-old city on a tongue of land where the Mahanadi splits in two, and Odisha's capital until 1948. Look for the city wedged between two wide, sandy river channels.

name: Irkutsk
blurb: A Siberian city on the Angara River, about 40 miles downstream of Lake Baikal, the deepest lake on Earth. Look for the river leaving the lake's southern tip and the dam reservoir just above the city.

name: Malanje
blurb: Gateway to Kalandula Falls, among Africa's biggest waterfalls by volume, and the giant boulders of Pungo Andongo. Malanje sits on a high plateau of savanna in northern Angola.

name: Kryvyi Rih
blurb: An iron-mining city that stretches more than 40 miles along a narrow ore belt, one of Europe's longest cities. Look for huge open pits and red-brown tailings beside it.

name: Djibouti
blurb: At the mouth of the Red Sea near Bab el-Mandeb, one of the busiest shipping lanes. It hosts a US base and China's first overseas military base; look for the port's container cranes.

name: Tianchang
blurb: Anhui city on the Jiangsu border, between Nanjing and Gaoyou Lake. Flat country of fish ponds, paddies and canals.

name: Tunis
blurb: Tunisia's capital sits on a shallow lagoon, Lake Tunis, crossed by a causeway that carries a canal and road to the sea. Ancient Carthage's ruins lie on the coast just northeast.

name: Dortmund
blurb: Once a heavyweight of coal and steel, now known worldwide for Borussia Dortmund and its 81,000-seat stadium with the Yellow Wall. Look for the yellow roof pylons of the stadium south of downtown.

name: Málaga
blurb: Picasso's birthplace and the main city of the Costa del Sol. Look for the Alcazaba and the Gibralfaro castle walls climbing the hill above the port.

name: Durban
blurb: Home to the busiest port in sub-Saharan Africa. Look for the arch of Moses Mabhida Stadium on the beachfront and the big enclosed harbor behind its narrow entrance.

name: Kagoshima
blurb: Faces Sakurajima across the bay, one of Japan's most active volcanoes, which dusts the city with ash most years. Look for the smoking cone across the water.

name: Irapuato
blurb: A farm city in Mexico's Bajío, famous for its strawberries. Look for the town's grid surrounded by flat, irrigated fields.

name: Dublin
blurb: Ireland's capital straddles the Liffey where it meets Dublin Bay. Look for the red-and-white Poolbeg chimneys at the port, and Phoenix Park, one of Europe's largest city parks, to the west.

name: El Mahalla El Kubra
blurb: Egypt's textile capital, home of the giant Misr Spinning and Weaving mill. Dense Delta city surrounded by bright green fields and canals.

name: Sialkot
blurb: Makes a large share of the world's hand-stitched soccer balls, along with surgical instruments and sporting goods. It sits near the Indian border; on clear days look for snowy Himalayan peaks beyond the plain.

name: Vladivostok
blurb: End of the Trans-Siberian Railway, about 5,770 miles from Moscow, and home of Russia's Pacific Fleet. Look for the Golden Horn bay and the bridge to Russky Island, one of the longest cable-stayed spans in the world.

name: Gaza City
blurb: Once home to more than half a million people in one of the densest urban areas on Earth, it was largely destroyed in the war that began in 2023. Look for it on the Mediterranean shore at the north end of the Gaza Strip.

name: Riga
blurb: The largest city in the Baltics, with one of the finest collections of Art Nouveau buildings anywhere. Look for the wide Daugava River and the old town's church spires on its east bank.

name: Bremen
blurb: A Hanseatic city-state for centuries, about 40 miles up the Weser River from the North Sea. Look for the Weser curving through town, lined downstream with port basins and shipyards.

name: Zahedan
blurb: Close to where Iran, Pakistan and Afghanistan meet, among bare desert mountains. Look for the city on a dry plain hemmed in by brown, rocky ridges.

name: Florianópolis
blurb: Mostly on Santa Catarina Island, with dozens of beaches. Look for the Hercílio Luz suspension bridge to the mainland and the long inland lagoon, Lagoa da Conceição.

name: Mbale City
blurb: An eastern Ugandan city at the foot of Mount Elgon, a huge extinct volcano on the Kenya border. Look for the mountain's massive green slopes rising to the northeast, with Wanale ridge right over town.

name: Merlo
blurb: A western suburb of Greater Buenos Aires, mostly low houses on a street grid. Look for the Reconquista River cutting across the flat pampas.

name: Vilnius
blurb: Lithuania's capital, with one of the largest baroque old towns in Eastern Europe. Look for the Neris River curving through wooded hills and the Gediminas Tower on its hill.

name: Londrina
blurb: Laid out in the 1930s by a British company selling coffee land, its name means little London. Look for rust-red soil around the city and Lake Igapó, a long artificial lake near downtown.

name: Ta'if
blurb: Mountain city at about 6,000 ft above Mecca, the kingdom's traditional summer retreat and famous for its roses. Look for the switchback road dropping down the escarpment toward Mecca.

name: Port Sudan
blurb: Sudan's main seaport, built by the British in the early 1900s, and the de facto seat of government since the war began in 2023. Look for the harbor and coral reefs in the Red Sea's clear water.

name: Serra
blurb: Industrial suburb of Vitoria, with a large port and steel complex at Tubarao on its edge. Look for the granite dome of Mestre Alvaro rising over it.

name: Tuxtla Gutiérrez
blurb: Chiapas's capital sits just south of Sumidero Canyon, whose walls rise up to about 3,300 ft above the river. Look for the canyon's deep slot cutting north through the mountains.

name: Dehradun
blurb: Uttarakhand's capital lies in the Doon Valley between the Shivalik hills and the Himalayan foothills. Look for the hill station of Mussoorie on the ridge above the city to the north.

name: Manfalut
blurb: Nile valley town in Asyut governorate. Look for the narrow green band of farmland pressed between the river and the desert cliffs.

name: Malegaon
blurb: A power-loom textile town in northern Maharashtra with its own homemade film industry, nicknamed Mollywood. Look for a dense town where the Girna and Mosam rivers meet.

name: Quebec City
blurb: Founded in 1608, it keeps the only surviving city walls in North America north of Mexico. Look for the green copper roofs of the Château Frontenac on the cliff above the St. Lawrence.

name: Puente Alto
blurb: Chile's most populous municipality, on Santiago's southeast edge at the foot of the Andes. Look for the Maipo River canyon opening into the mountains just beyond the last houses.

name: Essen
blurb: Seat of the Krupp steel empire, in the middle of the Ruhr sprawl. Its Zollverein coal mine is a World Heritage Site; look for the red steel winding tower and Lake Baldeney to the south.

name: Shibin el-Qanater
blurb: Farm town at the edge of the Delta north of Cairo, where the city's sprawl meets fields. Look for canals and bright green plots.

name: Hamilton
blurb: Steel town at the western tip of Lake Ontario. Look for mills and slag piles lining the harbor, the Niagara Escarpment (locally just the Mountain) cutting through the city, and the Burlington Skyway across the harbor mouth.

name: Surrey
blurb: Metro Vancouver's fast-growing suburb, on track to outnumber Vancouver itself. Look for the Fraser River along its north edge and a grid of farms and subdivisions running to the US border.

name: Ciudad Bolívar
blurb: A colonial river town on the Orinoco at its narrowest point, once called Angostura, which gave the bitters their name. Look for the Angostura suspension bridge just upstream.

name: Chișinău
blurb: Moldova's capital, a leafy Soviet-planned city on rolling hills. Look for its chain of lakes and parks, and vineyards in the countryside around.

name: Durgapur
blurb: A steel city built in the 1950s on the Damodar River in West Bengal. Look for the Durgapur Barrage across the river and big steel plants on the edge of town.

name: Albuquerque
blurb: On the Rio Grande at about 5,300 ft, with the 10,000-ft Sandia Mountains rising right behind it. Look for the green ribbon of cottonwoods along the river.

name: Asansol
blurb: A coal and steel city at the heart of the Raniganj coalfield in West Bengal. Look for open-cast mine scars and rail yards among the towns spreading along the Damodar River.

name: Yaroslavl
blurb: A Golden Ring city founded about 1010 where the Kotorosl River meets the Volga, with a UNESCO-listed center. Look for the arrow-shaped spit at the confluence and the domes along the riverbank.

name: Dresden
blurb: Allied firebombing in February 1945 gutted its baroque center; the domed Frauenkirche was rebuilt only in 2005. Look for the Elbe running through town between wide green meadows.

name: Asyut
blurb: Upper Egypt's largest city, on the Nile. Look for its barrage, a dam with locks across the river, built in 1902.

name: Benguela
blurb: Founded by the Portuguese in 1617 and a hub of the Atlantic slave trade. Look for its beaches along the Atlantic and the Benguela Railway heading inland toward the copper belt.

name: El-Obeid
blurb: Capital of North Kordofan and a trading hub for gum arabic, at the end of a railway across the Sahel. Look for a sprawl of low roofs in dry savanna.

name: Genoa
blurb: Italy's biggest port, squeezed into a strip between the Apennines and the sea. Look for docks running for miles along the shore, and the San Giorgio bridge that replaced the Morandi bridge after its 2018 collapse.

name: Ensenada
blurb: A port on Todos Santos Bay where cruise ships call. Look for the bay's sweep and its islands offshore; the Valle de Guadalupe wine country lies in the hills to the northeast.

name: Wuhai
blurb: A coal and chemical town on the Yellow River with desert on both banks. Look for the river, dammed into a long lake, running between sand dunes and bare brown hills.

name: Herat
blurb: A Silk Road oasis for 2,500 years on the green Hari River valley. Look for the massive Citadel walls in the old center and the leaning Musalla minarets standing alone on the north side.

name: Hamadan
blurb: One of the oldest cities in the world: this was Ecbatana, capital of the Medes. Look for the city at the foot of Mount Alvand, often capped with snow.

name: Rourkela
blurb: Steel city built in the 1950s with West German help around one of India's first big public sector steel plants. Look for the sprawling mill and its slag heaps beside the Brahmani River.

name: Chiclayo
blurb: Near the tomb of the Lord of Sipán, found in 1987 and one of the richest unlooted royal burials in the Americas. Look for a green irrigated valley floor squeezed between desert and the Pacific.

name: Meknes
blurb: One of Morocco's four imperial cities, wrapped in miles of walls built by Sultan Moulay Ismail. Look for vineyards and olive groves on the plain around it.

name: Amravati
blurb: A cotton-growing city in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region. Look for flat black-soil farmland with the Satpura hills to the north.

name: Naberezhnye Chelny
blurb: Home of KamAZ, Russia's biggest truck maker, built up from a village in the 1970s on the Kama River. Look for the vast truck plant and grid of Soviet apartment blocks.

name: Andijan
blurb: One of the oldest cities in the Fergana Valley, birthplace of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire. Look for canals and orchards across the flat valley floor with mountains beyond.

name: Nellore
blurb: Coastal Andhra city on the Penner River, ringed by rice paddies and shrimp ponds. Look for the grid of rectangular aquaculture ponds along the coast; India's rocket launch site at Sriharikota lies down the shore to the south.

name: Samarkand
blurb: One of Central Asia's oldest cities, a Silk Road hub and Tamerlane's capital. Look for the turquoise domes of the Registan and Bibi-Khanym mosque amid green oasis fields along the Zarafshan River.

name: Ibagué
blurb: Called Colombia's music capital, at the foot of the Central Andes. Look for the snowcap of 17,000-ft Nevado del Tolima to the northwest.

name: Tomsk
blurb: Founded in 1604, one of Siberia's oldest cities and a university town known for its wooden lace houses. Look for the city spread along the east bank of the broad Tom River, with taiga beyond.

name: Balashikha
blurb: A large suburb on Moscow's eastern edge, set among forests. Look for blocks of apartment towers broken up by woods.

name: Valledupar
blurb: Capital of vallenato music, between the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Perija range. Look for the mountains to the north and dry plains to the south.

name: Kemerovo
blurb: Capital of the Kuzbass, Russia's main coal basin. Look for open-pit mines around the city and the Tom River running through town.

name: Tucson
blurb: Saguaro National Park flanks the city on both sides. Look for Davis-Monthan's "Boneyard," where thousands of retired military aircraft sit in rows in the dry desert air.

name: Ajmer
blurb: Home to the shrine of the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti, one of the most visited in South Asia. Look for the Ana Sagar lake in town, ringed by the Aravalli hills, with Pushkar just over the ridge.

name: Fresno
blurb: The capital of the San Joaquin Valley, one of the most productive farm regions in the world. Look for a patchwork of orchards and vineyards, with the Sierra Nevada rising to the east.

name: Heroica Matamoros
blurb: Border city across the Rio Grande from Brownsville, Texas, near the river's mouth. Look for the river's tight meanders and SpaceX's Starbase on the coast to the east.

name: Mbeya
blurb: Highland city at about 5,500 ft in southwestern Tanzania, on the road and rail line to Zambia. Look for Mbeya Peak and the mountains around it.

name: Nasiriyah
blurb: On the Euphrates near the ruins of Ur, where a 4,000-year-old ziggurat still stands. Look for the river, and the Mesopotamian marshes spreading to the east.

name: Hillah
blurb: A few miles from the ruins of Babylon on the Euphrates. Look for the river lined with palm groves winding through flat farmland.

name: Juiz de Fora
blurb: A hilly city in the Paraibuna River valley, one of Brazil's early industrial centers. Look for the city filling a narrow valley between green hills.

name: Sekondi-Takoradi
blurb: A twin port city on Ghana's western coast and the onshore base for the country's offshore oil fields. Look for Takoradi harbor's breakwaters on the Gulf of Guinea.

name: Sahiwal
blurb: Farming city in Punjab between the Ravi and Sutlej, close to the ruins of Harappa, one of the great Indus Valley cities of about 4,500 years ago. Look for a perfect checkerboard of canal-fed fields.

name: Agadir
blurb: Rebuilt after an earthquake destroyed it in 1960. Look for the long curving beach and the Arabic for "God, Country, King" spelled out in giant letters on the hill above the port.

name: Kerman
blurb: A desert city at about 5,700 ft on Iran's central plateau, known for carpets and pistachios. Look for the city on a bare plain ringed by mountains.

name: Orenburg
blurb: Founded in 1743 as a fortress on the Ural River at the edge of the Kazakh steppe. The river is often treated as the line between Europe and Asia; look for it looping through the city into flat steppe.

name: Leeds
blurb: Built on wool and cloth in the Industrial Revolution, now a big finance and university city. Look for the River Aire and the Leeds and Liverpool Canal running through the center, with the Yorkshire Dales rising to the northwest.

name: Kassala
blurb: Border city near Eritrea, overlooked by the Taka Mountains, bare granite domes that rise straight out of town. Look for those rounded peaks beside the green strip of the Gash River.

name: Gimhae
blurb: Ancient capital of the Geumgwan Gaya kingdom, and the name behind Busan's main airport next door. Look for the wide Nakdong River delta and flat farmland around the runways.

name: Nuremberg
blurb: A medieval imperial city, later the stage for Nazi rallies and the postwar war-crimes trials. Look for the unfinished horseshoe of the Congress Hall beside a lake southeast of the center.

name: Beira
blurb: A port at the mouth of the Pungwe River that Cyclone Idai devastated in 2019. Look for the low-lying city on the coast and the port facing the estuary.

name: Yazd
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited towns on Earth, known for wind-catcher towers that cool its mud-brick houses. Look for the city between deserts, with the Shir Kuh peaks to the southwest.

name: Touba
blurb: Holy city of the Mouride Sufi brotherhood, founded by Amadou Bamba; millions arrive for the yearly Grand Magal pilgrimage. Look for the great mosque's tall minaret above flat sandy roofs.

name: Bikaner
blurb: Thar Desert city founded in 1488, known for Junagarh Fort and, nearby, the Karni Mata temple full of revered rats. Look for the fort's walls and the city's edge giving way to sand.

name: Novokuznetsk
blurb: The steel city of the Kuzbass coal basin, with huge mills on the Tom River. Look for smokestacks and coal pits around town and forested hills to the east.

name: Kosti
blurb: White Nile river port where the railway from Khartoum crosses the river. Look for the long bridge and the wide, lazy river spreading into wetlands.

name: Ndola
blurb: A Copperbelt city near the DR Congo border; UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld died in a plane crash nearby in 1961. Look for green miombo woodland around town and the Congo border just to the north.

name: Himeji
blurb: Home of Himeji Castle, the finest surviving original castle in Japan. Look for the white, layered keep, nicknamed the White Heron, on its hill north of the station.

name: Bandar Abbas
blurb: Iran's main port, on the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil passes. Look for docks along the shore and the islands of Qeshm and Hormuz offshore.

name: Santa Teresa del Tuy
blurb: A commuter town in the Tuy Valley south of Caracas, linked to the capital by a rail line. Look for hilly valley country with dense neighborhoods climbing the slopes.

name: Caxias do Sul
blurb: Founded by Italian immigrants in 1875, now the hub of Brazil's wine country and a big industrial city. Look for vineyards on the hills of the Serra Gaúcha around town.

name: Hanover
blurb: Capital of Lower Saxony and host of some of the world's largest trade fairs. Look for the Maschsee, a long man-made lake just south of downtown, and the vast fairground halls to the southeast.

name: Agartala
blurb: Capital of Tripura, almost surrounded by Bangladesh, whose border runs just a mile or two west of the city. Look for low green hills, ponds and rice paddies pressing in on every side.

name: Arak
blurb: An industrial city on Iran's plateau; a heavy-water reactor nearby has been central to nuclear talks. Look for the white salt crust of the Mighan wetland just northeast of town.

name: Paju
blurb: Right on the North Korean border, where the Imjin River meets the Han. Look for the wide estuary, with North Korea on the far bank.

name: Pohang
blurb: Steel town on Korea's east coast, home to POSCO, one of the world's largest steelmakers. Look for the huge steelworks filling the flat land along Yeongil Bay.

name: Ryazan
blurb: Old Russian city on the Oka River with a kremlin dating back to the 1400s. Look for the kremlin's domes on a bluff above the river and its wide floodplain meadows.

name: Campos dos Goytacazes
blurb: Old sugar city on the Paraíba do Sul River and onshore base for the Campos Basin, long Brazil's main offshore oil field. Look for the wide river winding through flat cane fields.

name: Utsunomiya
blurb: The gateway to Nikko, and Japan's self-declared gyoza capital. Look for the city on the flat Kanto plain with the Nikko mountains rising to the northwest.

name: Sheffield
blurb: The Steel City, famous for cutlery and stainless steel, built on seven hills where five rivers meet. Look for the Peak District's dark moorland starting right at the western suburbs.

name: Porto Velho
blurb: Grew around the Madeira-Mamoré railroad, built in the early 1900s at the cost of thousands of workers' lives. Look for the wide brown Madeira River and the Santo Antônio dam just upstream.

name: Makurdi
blurb: Capital of Benue State, straddling the wide Benue River. Look for the long road and rail bridges across the river and the pale sandbars that surface in the dry season.

name: Karaganda
blurb: Built on coal by Gulag prisoners in the 1930s on the bare Kazakh steppe. Look for spoil heaps and mine works around a grid city in flat grassland.

name: Ujjain
blurb: One of Hinduism's seven sacred cities, and a host of the Kumbh Mela on the Shipra River. Look for the river's bathing ghats and temples on the flat Malwa plateau.

name: Toulouse
blurb: The "Pink City," named for its terracotta brick, and the heart of Europe's aerospace industry: Airbus assembles jets here. Look for the Garonne curving through town and the giant assembly halls beside the airport at Blagnac.

name: Liverpool
blurb: A great Atlantic port on the Mersey estuary, home of the Beatles and two big football clubs. Look for miles of docks along the river, and the Wirral peninsula across the water.

name: Wolaita Sodo
blurb: Southern Ethiopian town on green hills below Mount Damota. Look for a patchwork of small farms and eucalyptus groves.

name: Amarah
blurb: On the Tigris at the edge of the marshes that Saddam Hussein drained in the 1990s, partly reflooded since 2003. Look for the river and marshland to the south.

name: Kenitra
blurb: A port city on the Sebou River, a few miles from the Atlantic. Look for the river meandering through flat farmland toward the coast.

name: Jhansi
blurb: Famous for Rani Lakshmibai, who led rebels against the British in 1857 from its hilltop fort. Look for the rocky outcrops and lakes scattered across the dry Bundelkhand plateau around the city.

name: Matsuyama
blurb: Shikoku's largest city, known for Dogo Onsen, one of Japan's oldest hot springs. Look for the castle on its hill in the middle of town and the Seto Inland Sea to the west.

name: Oujda
blurb: Morocco's eastern city, a few miles from the long-closed border with Algeria. Look for the city on a plain with dry mountains around it.

name: Santiago de Cuba
blurb: Cuba's second city, at the foot of the Sierra Maestra. Look for the pocket bay guarded by the Morro castle at its narrow entrance, a UNESCO site.

name: Santa Marta
blurb: Founded in 1525, Colombia's oldest surviving Spanish city; Simon Bolivar died here in 1830. The Sierra Nevada behind it rises to about 18,700 ft, the highest coastal range on Earth.

name: Nagqu
blurb: A high nomadic town at about 14,800 ft on the Changtang plateau, one of the highest towns in the world. Look for vast, flat grassland with no trees anywhere.

name: Mesa
blurb: About half a million people, more than Miami within city limits. Look for the Phoenix grid running east, crossed by canals that follow routes the Hohokam dug a thousand years ago.

name: São José do Rio Preto
blurb: Big inland city in São Paulo state's farm country. Look for a grid of streets in the middle of sugarcane fields, with lakes strung through the city.

name: Jammu
blurb: The "City of Temples," on the Tawi River where the Punjab plains meet the Himalayan foothills. Look for the first ridges rising just north of town.

name: Ile Ife
blurb: Held by the Yoruba to be where the world was created, and famous for lifelike bronze and terracotta heads made 600 or more years ago. Look for the large green campus of Obafemi Awolowo University northwest of town.

name: Mazatlán
blurb: Pacific port with a seafront malecón about 13 miles long, among the longest in the world. Look for the hill of El Faro, one of the highest natural lighthouses anywhere, at the south tip.

name: Duisburg
blurb: Home to one of the largest inland ports in the world, where the Ruhr flows into the Rhine. Look for docks and rail yards spread along the river and steelworks to the north.

name: Juba
blurb: Capital of South Sudan, the world's newest country since 2011. Look for the White Nile running past town, with its green islands and the bridge across it.

name: 10th of Ramadan City
blurb: A desert industrial city founded in 1977 between Cairo and Ismailia. Named for the day the 1973 war began; look for a grid of factories set on sand.

name: Sukkur
blurb: Sits on the Indus at the Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932 and feeding one of the largest irrigation systems in the world. Look for the long barrage across the river and the canals fanning out on both banks.

name: Gomel
blurb: Belarus's second city, on the Sozh River, less than 100 miles from Chernobyl, which hit the region hard with fallout in 1986. Look for a riverside park around the Rumyantsev palace.

name: Cheboksary
blurb: Chuvashia's capital on the Volga, where a dam backs up the river into a long reservoir. Look for the large Mother Patroness statue on the waterfront.

name: Florencio Varela
blurb: A southern suburb of Greater Buenos Aires where the city fades into market gardens and greenhouses. Flat, mostly low-rise grid on the pampas.

name: Nyala
blurb: The largest city in Darfur, a trading hub in the dry Sahel. Look for a sprawl of low roofs along a seasonal riverbed with the hills of Jebel Marra to the northwest.

name: Bissau
blurb: Guinea-Bissau's capital, on the Geba River estuary. Look for the city on a low point surrounded by mangroves and the braided tidal channels of the coast.

name: Kota Bharu
blurb: Kelantan's capital near the Thai border, on the delta of the Kelantan River. Look for the wide river and rice fields all around.

name: Larkana
blurb: Farming town in Sindh and home of the Bhutto family, about 17 miles from Mohenjo-daro, the 4,500-year-old Indus Valley city. Look for green rice fields fed by canals from the Indus.

name: Karamay
blurb: A Xinjiang oil city whose name means black oil in Uyghur, built in the 1950s at the edge of the Junggar Basin desert. Look for oil fields and pumpjacks scattered across bare, flat ground.

name: Ajman
blurb: The smallest of the seven emirates, wedged against Sharjah on the coast. Look for a creek and marinas cutting into the shoreline, with the city blending seamlessly into Sharjah and Dubai to the south.

name: Vinh
blurb: A provincial capital in north-central Vietnam, Ho Chi Minh's home region, heavily bombed in the war and rebuilt with East German help. Look for the Lam River and flat rice paddies running to the sea.

name: Kaliningrad
blurb: Once Königsberg, capital of East Prussia, now a Russian exclave between Poland and Lithuania. Look for the Pregolya River islands and the long Curonian and Vistula spits on the coast.

name: Belgaum
blurb: An old garrison town near the Goa and Maharashtra borders, at about 2,500 ft. Look for the fort and cantonment amid red-soil farmland.

name: Edinburgh
blurb: Scotland's capital is built around an extinct volcano: Castle Rock and Arthur's Seat, the 823-ft hill rising in a park beside the city. Look for the Forth bridges to the northwest.

name: Penza
blurb: Founded in 1663 as a frontier fortress on the Sura River. Look for apartment blocks along the river among the woods and farmland of the middle Volga region.

name: Gdańsk
blurb: World War II began here in 1939, and the Solidarity movement was born at its shipyard in 1980. Look for the shipyard cranes along the waterfront and the long thin Hel Peninsula across the bay.

name: Windhoek
blurb: Namibia's capital, at about 5,400 ft in a highland basin. Look for the city spread across dry hills, with the Auas Mountains to the south.

name: Sevastopol
blurb: Home of the Black Sea Fleet, annexed by Russia along with Crimea in 2014. Look for the long, deep bays cutting into the city from the sea.

name: Vellore
blurb: Known for Vellore Fort, a 16th-century granite fort with a water-filled moat, and Christian Medical College, a top Indian hospital. Look for the moat's rectangle in the center of town.

name: Lipetsk
blurb: A steel town with one of Russia's largest steel mills, NLMK. Look for the sprawling mill on the Voronezh River across from the city.

name: Zarqa
blurb: An industrial city just northeast of Amman and home to Jordan's only oil refinery. Look for dense concrete sprawl on the edge of the desert.

name: Bratislava
blurb: The only capital that borders two other countries, Austria and Hungary. Look for the square white castle with four corner towers above the Danube and the huge field of concrete blocks in Petržalka.

name: Bafoussam
blurb: A crossroads of Cameroon's western highlands, heart of the Bamileke people and their traditional chiefdoms. Look for red-earth roads and coffee and farm plots across green volcanic hills.

name: Sylhet
blurb: Tea country in Bangladesh's northeast, with estates covering the low hills. Most of Britain's Bangladeshi community traces its roots here; look for the Surma River winding through.

name: Colorado Springs
blurb: 14,115-ft Pikes Peak rises straight up from the west side of town. Look for the red rocks of Garden of the Gods and the Air Force Academy's spiky aluminum chapel to the north.

name: Ananindeua
blurb: A sprawling neighbor of Belém near the mouth of the Amazon. Look for dense low roofs threaded with creeks, with rainforest pressing in at the city's edge.

name: East London
blurb: South Africa's only river port, at the mouth of the Buffalo River; the coelacanth, a fish thought extinct for 66 million years, was identified from a 1938 catch here. Look for the river harbor and long beaches.

name: Chiniot
blurb: Old town on the Chenab River in Punjab, known for its carved wooden furniture. Look for low rocky hills poking out of the dead-flat plain right beside the river, a rare sight in Punjab.

name: Ōita-shi
blurb: On Beppu Bay next to Beppu, one of the most prolific hot-spring towns on Earth. Look for steam plumes rising from the hillsides just up the shore.

name: Kirov
blurb: An old trading town on the Vyatka River, which went by Vyatka until 1934. Look for the river looping through flat forest and the city on its high bank.

name: Gaya
blurb: Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment, is just south. Look for the wide sandy bed of the Phalgu River, often almost dry.

name: Sheikhupura
blurb: Industrial city northwest of Lahore, where the Mughal emperor Jahangir built the Hiran Minar, a tower honoring his pet antelope. Look for the minaret beside its big square water tank among farmland.

name: Piura
blurb: Founded by Pizarro in 1532, often called the first Spanish city in South America. Look for the Piura River crossing the city, frequently dry, in the middle of the Sechura Desert.

name: Vila Velha
blurb: Founded in 1535, Espirito Santo's oldest city. Look for the Penha convent on top of a granite rock above the bay, and the high bridge to Vitoria.

name: Bristol
blurb: An old port city where the River Avon cuts a deep gorge to the Severn estuary. Look for the Clifton Suspension Bridge across the gorge and the river's muddy, tidal banks.

name: Morogoro
blurb: Farm town at the foot of the Uluguru Mountains, west of Dar es Salaam. Look for the forested peaks rising straight up from the city's edge.

name: San Juan
blurb: A 1944 earthquake flattened this Andean foothill city, killing about 10,000. Perón met Eva Duarte at a relief benefit for it; look for irrigated vineyards against brown desert and the Ullum reservoir to the west.

name: Seeb
blurb: Muscat's largest suburb and home of its international airport, on the flat coastal plain between the Hajar Mountains and the Gulf of Oman. Look for a long strip of low white buildings along the beach with bare brown mountains behind.

name: Mazar-i-Sharif
blurb: Named for the blue-tiled shrine many Afghans believe holds the tomb of Ali. A flat oasis city on the plain that runs north to the Amu Darya and the Uzbek border.

name: Baqubah
blurb: Capital of Diyala province northeast of Baghdad, known for its orange and date groves along the Diyala River. Look for a dark green band of orchards on the tan plain.

name: Raleigh
blurb: North Carolina's capital, nicknamed the City of Oaks for its tree canopy, and one corner of the Research Triangle with Durham and Chapel Hill. Look for a small downtown cluster rising from a nearly unbroken carpet of trees.

name: Burayda
blurb: Capital of Qassim, Saudi Arabia's farm belt, and host of one of the largest date markets in the world. Look for green center-pivot circles packed around the city.

name: Long Beach
blurb: Its port, joined with LA's, forms the busiest container complex in the US. Look for the Queen Mary docked by the harbor and four palm-dotted oil islands, with drilling rigs dressed up as buildings.

name: Astrakhan
blurb: Near where the Volga splits into hundreds of channels to form Europe's largest delta before the Caspian. Look for the white walls of the Kremlin and a maze of waterways below the city.

name: Constantine
blurb: Built on a rock plateau ringed by the Rhumel gorge, up to about 650 ft deep, and crossed by a string of bridges. Look for the city's stone island cut off on nearly every side by the canyon.

name: Junagadh
blurb: An old princely-state capital at the foot of Girnar, a sacred mountain climbed by thousands of steps to Jain and Hindu temples. Look for the steep granite massif rising just east of town.

name: Jinchang
blurb: Built around one of the largest nickel mines in the world, it calls itself China's nickel capital. Look for the city and mine works on the dry Hexi Corridor plain, with the Qilian Mountains to the south.

name: Uijeongbu
blurb: Suburb north of Seoul long tied to US Army bases, and the birthplace of budae jjigae, a stew built from army surplus. Look for high-rises packed into a narrow valley between granite mountains.

name: Esna
blurb: Its Temple of Khnum sits about 30 ft below the modern street, revealing how much the town has risen. Look for Nile cruise boats queuing at the barrage locks.

name: Kanazawa
blurb: Its samurai and geisha districts escaped wartime bombing, and its Kenrokuen garden ranks among Japan's finest. Look for the castle park in the center and the Sea of Japan coast to the west.

name: Asunción
blurb: Paraguay's capital, founded in 1537 and one of the oldest cities in South America. Look for it on a bend of the Paraguay River, with a broad bay and the Chaco wetlands across the water.

name: Jalgaon
blurb: Called India's banana capital, and the nearest city to the Ajanta caves. Look for endless plantations on the Tapi River plain.

name: Fukuyama
blurb: A Seto Inland Sea port with one of the largest steelworks in Japan, built on reclaimed land. Look for the vast mill stretching along the waterfront.

name: Virginia Beach
blurb: Virginia's most populous city, with miles of Atlantic beach and the world's largest naval base at nearby Norfolk. Look for the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel snaking north across the bay mouth.

name: Kurnool
blurb: Briefly the capital of Andhra State from 1953 to 1956, on the Tungabhadra River. Look for rocky, boulder-strewn hills around the river crossing in the dry Deccan.

name: Tallinn
blurb: Its medieval Old Town keeps most of its walls and towers. Look for church spires and red roofs on Toompea hill above the harbor, where ferries run to Helsinki.

name: Tula
blurb: A historic arms-making city about 100 miles south of Moscow, famous for samovars, gingerbread and a 16th-century red-brick kremlin. Look for the Upa River winding through the center.

name: Malacca
blurb: A spice port seized by the Portuguese in 1511, then by the Dutch and the British. Look for land reclaimed out into the Strait of Malacca and the river through the old town.

name: Manizales
blurb: Built along steep ridges at about 7,000 ft in coffee country. Nevado del Ruiz looms to the southeast; its 1985 eruption buried the town of Armero, killing about 23,000.

name: Kota Kinabalu
blurb: Capital of Sabah on Borneo, with 13,435-ft Mount Kinabalu rising to the northeast. Look for the islands of the marine park just offshore.

name: Udaipur
blurb: The City of Lakes, where the white Lake Palace seems to float on Lake Pichola. Look for the long City Palace along the eastern shore and the Aravalli hills wrapped around the lakes.

name: Mogi das Cruzes
blurb: Eastern suburb of São Paulo with a large Japanese-Brazilian community and a farm belt growing vegetables and fruit. Look for the Serra do Mar's forested ridges to the south.

name: Stavropol
blurb: Founded in 1777 as a fortress on Russia's Caucasus frontier. Look for the city on high ground above rolling farm steppe.

name: Betim
blurb: An industrial suburb of Belo Horizonte, home to one of the largest Fiat car plants in the world. Look for the factory's acres of rooftops at the edge of town.

name: Sirajganj
blurb: On the west bank of the Jamuna, one of the world's widest braided rivers. Look for the 3-mile Bangabandhu Bridge crossing the shifting sandbars and channels.

name: Eslamshahr
blurb: A dense working-class suburb on Tehran's southwest edge. Look for tight grids of low buildings running into the capital, with the Alborz mountains to the north.

name: Rajshahi
blurb: On the Padma, as the Ganges is called here, right on the Indian border. Known for silk and mangoes; look for wide sandbars and the river forming the frontier.

name: Tigre
blurb: Gateway to the Parana Delta. Look for a maze of brown channels and green islands spreading north, crowded with rowing clubs, weekend houses and boats.

name: Ado Ekiti
blurb: Capital of Ekiti State, in the hilly Yoruba country of southwest Nigeria. Look for smooth granite hills rising around the city, the signature of the Ekiti landscape.

name: Batman
blurb: An oil town in southeastern Turkey, named for the nearby Batman River. Turkey's first oil field was found here in 1940; look for refinery tanks on the edge of a city in dry, rolling country.

name: Sochi
blurb: Host of the 2014 Winter Olympics, a subtropical resort strip on the Black Sea with ski slopes in the mountains inland. Look for the Olympic Park arenas on the flat coast near the airport at Adler.

name: Kahramanmaraş
blurb: Southern Turkish city known for its chewy ice cream, and near the epicenter of the February 2023 earthquakes that killed more than 50,000 people. It sits on a plain at the foot of rugged mountains.

name: Xalapa
blurb: Veracruz's capital, a misty university city at about 4,600 ft on the slopes rising to Cofre de Perote and Pico de Orizaba. The jalapeño pepper is named after it; look for green hills and coffee country all around.

name: Macapá
blurb: Sits right on the equator at the mouth of the Amazon. The local stadium's halfway line follows the equator, so each team defends a different hemisphere; look for the river miles wide and brown.

name: Korhogo
blurb: Center of the Senufo people in northern Ivory Coast, known for painted mud cloth. Look for granite domes rising out of the savanna.

name: Montes Claros
blurb: The main city of northern Minas Gerais, a trading hub on dry savanna. Look for the city on a plain surrounded by low hills and pasture.

name: Phrae
blurb: An old teak-trading town in northern Thailand, set in a flat valley of rice fields ringed by forested hills. Look for the oval outline of the old moat and city wall around the center.

name: Sunchon
blurb: Industrial city north of Pyongyang on the Taedong River, home to a giant vinylon chemical complex started in the 1980s. Look for cement plants and limestone quarries.

name: Sangli
blurb: India's biggest turmeric market, on the Krishna River. Look for sugarcane fields lining the river.

name: Siguiri
blurb: A gold-mining town on the Niger River in northeastern Guinea. Look for the river crossing the savanna and the scarred, pitted ground of the gold workings around town.

name: Lobito
blurb: A deep natural harbor sheltered by a sand spit about 3 miles long. It's the Atlantic end of the Benguela Railway, revived as the Lobito Corridor for Congo and Zambia's copper.

name: Ulan-Ude
blurb: The main square holds a giant bronze head of Lenin, said to be the world's largest. Look for the Selenga River and the Trans-Siberian line; Lake Baikal is about an hour's drive away.

name: Palma
blurb: Majorca's capital, with a Gothic cathedral right on the old seawall. Look for the cathedral above the bay and the round Bellver Castle on a wooded hill to the west.

name: Kursk
blurb: Gave its name to the 1943 battle, one of the largest tank battles in history. Look for the city on the Seym River among wide black-earth fields.

name: Surgut
blurb: The oil capital of West Siberia, base of Surgutneftegas. Look for the Ob River's floodplain and the long bridge across it, with lakes and bogs to the horizon.

name: Dutse
blurb: Capital of Jigawa State, created when the state was split from Kano in 1991, so much of the town is new. Look for bare granite outcrops near the center and dry savanna in every direction.

name: Zanjan
blurb: A northwest Iranian city on the road to Tabriz; nearby Soltaniyeh has one of the largest brick domes in the world. Look for the town in a long valley between bare ridges.

name: Khamis Mushait
blurb: Highland city in the Asir mountains next to Abha, home to the King Khalid Air Base. Look for terraced farms and rocky hills, much greener than the desert to the east.

name: Awka
blurb: Capital of Anambra State in Nigeria's southeast, long known for its blacksmiths. Look for dense sprawl along the expressway between Onitsha and Enugu.

name: Corrientes
blurb: On the Parana River, here more than a mile wide. Look for the General Belgrano cable-stayed bridge linking it to Resistencia on the far bank.

name: Uyo
blurb: Capital of Akwa Ibom State in the oil-producing southeast, rebuilt with broad new boulevards. Look for the big bowl of the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium amid oil palm country.

name: Changwon
blurb: An industrial city built around Masan Bay, which absorbed the port city of Masan in 2010. Look for the deep sheltered harbor and the planned grid of Changwon's center inland.

name: Tanta
blurb: The Delta's main city. The festival of Sufi saint Ahmad al-Badawi draws millions to his mosque every year.

name: Ismailia
blurb: Founded in 1863 as the Suez Canal's headquarters town, on Lake Timsah midway along the canal. Look for the lake's blue patch on the line of the canal.

name: Cusco
blurb: Capital of the Inca Empire, at about 11,150 ft, with Spanish churches built on Inca stone foundations. Look for the city filling a bowl in the Andes and the zigzag walls of Sacsayhuamán on the hill above.

name: Sokoto
blurb: Seat of the 19th-century Sokoto Caliphate founded by Usman dan Fodio; its sultan is still the spiritual leader of Nigeria's Muslims. Look for the green floodplain where the Sokoto and Rima rivers meet in dry, sandy country.

name: Kashiwa
blurb: A commuter city in Chiba, northeast of Tokyo. Look for dense suburbs with the Tone River to the north and Lake Teganuma to the south.

name: Malatya
blurb: Turkey's apricot capital, producing a large share of the world's dried apricots. Look for orchards around the city and the long reservoirs of the Euphrates to the east.

name: Aomori
blurb: At the northern tip of Honshu, one of the snowiest cities in the world. Look for the triangular ASPAM building on the bay and the Hakkoda mountains to the south.

name: Tepic
blurb: Capital of Nayarit, in a green valley near the dormant Sangangüey volcano. Look for forested mountains around the city.

name: Akola
blurb: A cotton market town in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region. Look for flat black-soil fields stretching around the town.

name: Piracicaba
blurb: Sugarcane city on a river that tumbles over rapids right through downtown. Look for the river's white water and the old sugar mill on its bank.

name: Tétouan
blurb: Its white medina, a World Heritage Site, spills down the foot of the Rif mountains. Look for whitewashed houses on the slope above the Martil valley.

name: Sumgait
blurb: A Soviet chemical town on the Caspian, once named among the most polluted places on Earth. Look for the shoreline north of Baku and industrial plants stretched along it.

name: Skopje
blurb: North Macedonia's capital, largely rebuilt after a 1963 earthquake destroyed most of the city. Look for the Vardar River through the center and the giant Millennium Cross on Mount Vodno above town.

name: Likasi
blurb: Congo's Copperbelt city near Shinkolobwe, the mine that supplied most of the uranium for the Manhattan Project. Look for copper smelters and tailings.

name: Toyota
blurb: Renamed in 1959 after the carmaker, which still has its headquarters here. Look for big assembly plants and test tracks among the green hills.

name: Elazığ
blurb: An eastern Turkish city on a plateau above Lake Hazar and the huge Keban Dam reservoir on the Euphrates. Look for the reservoir's branching blue arms north and east of town.

name: Hpa-An
blurb: Capital of Myanmar's Karen State, set among limestone karst peaks on the Salween River. Look for sharp, sheer peaks rising straight out of the rice paddies.

name: Gumi
blurb: Industrial city on the Nakdong River, built up around electronics plants, and home town of President Park Chung-hee. Look for factory complexes lining the river.

name: Rahim Yar Khan
blurb: Farming city in southern Punjab near the Indus, where the irrigated plain meets the Cholistan Desert. Look for a sharp edge between green fields and tan sand to the east.

name: Manisa
blurb: An ancient city in western Turkey at the foot of Mount Sipylus, once a training seat for Ottoman crown princes. Look for the city tucked against the steep mountain wall on the edge of the broad Gediz plain.

name: Seremban
blurb: Capital of Negeri Sembilan, whose Minangkabau heritage shows in buffalo-horn roofs. Look for the town among hills and plantations south of Kuala Lumpur.

name: Campina Grande
blurb: Inland city on the Borborema Plateau that throws one of the biggest São João festivals in Brazil every June. Look for the city spread over rolling dry hills at the edge of the sertão.

name: Santos
blurb: Busiest port in Latin America, and home of the club where Pelé played. Look for the long beach lined with gardens and the container docks along the estuary.

name: Petrolina
blurb: Desert irrigation success on the São Francisco River, shipping mangoes and grapes worldwide and even making wine in the semi-arid sertão. Look for green squares of orchards against gray scrub and the bridge to Juazeiro.

name: Taraz
blurb: One of the oldest cities in Kazakhstan, a Silk Road stop for centuries. Look for the town on the Talas River farmland, with the snowy Kyrgyz Alatau ridges to the south.

name: Mauá
blurb: Industrial suburb in Greater São Paulo, home to the Capuava oil refinery. Look for the refinery's tanks among dense hillside housing.

name: Luhansk
blurb: Ukraine's easternmost regional capital, a coal and locomotive-building city under Russian control since 2014. It sits in rolling steppe cut by small rivers, with mine waste heaps nearby.

name: Arusha
blurb: Safari capital and gateway to the Serengeti and Ngorongoro, at the foot of Mount Meru, 14,968 ft. Look for Meru's broken cone, and on clear days Kilimanjaro to the east.

name: Nuevo Laredo
blurb: Across the Rio Grande from Laredo, Texas, on one of the busiest trade crossings on the US-Mexico border. Look for long lines of trucks waiting at the bridges.

name: Jhang
blurb: Old Punjab town near where the Jhelum flows into the Chenab, and home of Heer, heroine of the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha. Look for wide braided river channels and canal-fed fields.

name: Boa Vista
blurb: The only Brazilian state capital entirely north of the equator, laid out in a fan from the riverbank. Look for streets splaying away from the Rio Branco like spokes.

name: Toyama
blurb: On Toyama Bay, with the nearly 10,000-ft Tateyama range rising behind it. Look for a wall of snowcapped Alps to the east, close enough to seem to loom over the city.

name: Tver
blurb: An old trading city halfway between Moscow and St. Petersburg, where the Volga, still young here, meets the Tvertsa. Look for the bridges stitching the city across the wide river.

name: Sanandaj
blurb: Capital of Iran's Kurdistan province, at about 5,000 ft in the Zagros. Look for the city spread across a valley beneath steep, folded ridges.

name: Gebze
blurb: An industrial hub on the Gulf of İzmit, east of Istanbul, packed with factories and logistics yards. Hannibal is said to have died near here; look for the Osmangazi suspension bridge crossing the gulf to the south.

name: Tirunelveli
blurb: Old city on the Thamirabarani River in southern Tamil Nadu, known for its halwa sweet. Look for the river and irrigated rice fields with the Western Ghats to the west.

name: Pasto
blurb: Sits under Galeras, one of Colombia's most active volcanoes, at about 8,300 ft. Its Blacks and Whites Carnival is on UNESCO's heritage list.

name: Ballari
blurb: Iron-ore mining country, near Hampi, the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Look for the red scars of mines cut into the rocky hills.

name: Bhagalpur
blurb: On the Ganges, a center of tussar silk weaving for centuries. Ruins of the ancient Vikramashila university lie nearby, and the river here is a sanctuary for Ganges dolphins.

name: Maringá
blurb: A planned city from the 1940s, often called one of the greenest in Brazil for its tree-lined streets. Look for the tall concrete cone of the cathedral, one of the tallest churches in South America, in the center.

name: Kom Ombo
blurb: Its double temple, dedicated to the crocodile god Sobek and the falcon god Horus, sits right on a bend of the Nile. Look for sugarcane fields stretching across the reclaimed plain.

name: Magnitogorsk
blurb: Built from scratch in the 1930s around a mountain of iron ore, and still home to one of Russia's biggest steelworks. Look for the plant's huge sprawl on the Ural River, the conventional line between Europe and Asia.

name: Patiala
blurb: Former princely state famous for its maharajas, the Patiala peg of whisky and the baggy Patiala salwar. Look for the Qila Mubarak fort in the old city and the big palace grounds of Moti Bagh.

name: Đà Lạt
blurb: A cool hill town at about 4,900 ft, built by the French as a resort. Look for Xuan Huong Lake in the center, pine forest, and hillsides covered in white greenhouses for flowers and vegetables.

name: Caruaru
blurb: Home to one of the largest open-air markets in Brazil and a June São João festival that rivals Campina Grande's. Look for a city sprawled across dry hills at the edge of the sertão.

name: Bakersfield
blurb: Oil country: the Kern River field just north is one of the largest in the US, and the city gave country music the Bakersfield sound. Look for grids of pump jacks and well pads on the hills north of town.

name: Qazvin
blurb: Persia's capital in the 16th century, on the plain below the Alborz. Look for a regular grid on flat farmland with the mountains rising sharply to the north.

name: Brno
blurb: The Czech Republic's second city. Look for Spilberk castle on its hill and the Masaryk Circuit's racetrack loop in the woods to the west.

name: Jundiaí
blurb: Grape-growing city between São Paulo and Campinas, below the Serra do Japi. Look for the forested ridge of the Serra above town.

name: Aswan
blurb: The High Dam, finished in 1970, backs up Lake Nasser for more than 300 miles into Sudan. Look for the river's granite islands and the dam's huge wall across the Nile.

name: Lekki
blurb: The Lagos boom peninsula, squeezed between a lagoon and the Atlantic, now home to the Dangote refinery, the largest in Africa. Look for gated estates along one long straight road, with a new port and refinery near the far end.

name: Bogura
blurb: Mahasthangarh, Bangladesh's oldest archaeological site, dating to the 3rd century BC, lies just north. Famous at home for sweet yogurt; look for the old fortified mound by the Karatoya River.

name: Wah Cantonment
blurb: Built around Pakistan Ordnance Factories, the country's main arms maker, on the Grand Trunk Road west of Islamabad. Next door are the ancient Buddhist ruins of Taxila; look for the planned town's wide, orderly streets.

name: Gifu
blurb: Known for cormorant fishing on the Nagara River, a tradition over 1,300 years old. Look for the castle perched on steep Mount Kinka above the river.

name: Montería
blurb: Colombia's cattle capital, on the meandering Sinu River. Look for the river's loops through flat pasture.

name: Maracanã Stadium
blurb: Built for the 1950 World Cup, it held an estimated 200,000 people the day Uruguay stunned Brazil in the final. It hosted the 2014 final too. Look for the white oval roof ring north of the Tijuca hills.

name: Camp Nou
blurb: Europe's largest stadium, long at about 99,000 seats, has been rebuilt since 2023 toward about 105,000. Look for the vast bowl in Les Corts, west Barcelona, near the end of the Diagonal.

name: Tower Bridge
blurb: A bascule bridge from 1894 whose two road leaves still lift for tall ships, hundreds of times a year. Look for the twin Gothic towers and blue walkways beside the Tower of London.

name: Old Trafford
blurb: Manchester United's home, the largest club ground in England at about 74,000 seats. Look for the big bowl beside the Manchester Ship Canal, at the edge of the Trafford Park industrial estate.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
blurb: When it opened in 1883 its 1,595-ft span was the longest in the world. Look for its Gothic granite towers and the web of cables fanning down from them over the East River.

name: Bernabéu
blurb: Real Madrid's home was wrapped in a skin of steel ribbons and given a retractable roof in a rebuild finished in 2024. Look for the silver box on the Paseo de la Castellana among north Madrid towers.

name: Allianz Arena
blurb: Bayern Munich's stadium is wrapped in about 2,800 inflated plastic panels that can glow red, blue or white. Look for the rubber-dinghy shape on the north edge of Munich beside the autobahn.

name: Wembley Stadium
blurb: England's national stadium seats 90,000 under a 436-ft white arch that holds up much of the roof, visible across north London. Look for the arch first; the bowl sits beneath it.

name: Millau Viaduct
blurb: The tallest bridge in the world: one mast tops out about 1,125 ft, taller than the Eiffel Tower, and the deck runs about 890 ft over the Tarn valley. Look for its seven masts striding across the gorge.

name: Stadio Olimpico
blurb: Built for the 1960 Olympics and shared by Roma and Lazio, about 70,000 seats. Look for the white-roofed bowl on the Tiber's west bank at the foot of Monte Mario.

name: Stade de France
blurb: France's national stadium, built for the 1998 World Cup, where France won the final, and the athletics venue of the 2024 Olympics. Its elliptical roof seems to float above the 80,000 seats. Look for it in Saint-Denis by the canal.

name: Øresund Bridge
blurb: About 5 miles of bridge from Malmö to an artificial island, where the road and railway dive into a tunnel for the last 2.5 miles to Copenhagen. Look for the line simply ending in the sea.

name: Akashi Kaikyō Bridge
blurb: Its center span of about 6,530 ft was the world's longest for 24 years. The 1995 Kobe earthquake moved its towers apart by about 3 ft during construction. Look for its towers over the Akashi Strait.

name: Luzhniki Stadium
blurb: Moscow's biggest stadium, about 81,000 seats, hosted the 1980 Olympics and the 2018 World Cup final. Look for the oval on the Moskva River's tight bend, below the Sparrow Hills and the spire of Moscow State University.

name: Beijing National Stadium
blurb: The Bird's Nest, centerpiece of the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Games. Look for its tangle of steel beams beside the blue box of the Water Cube on the Olympic Green.

name: Gazprom Arena
blurb: Zenit St. Petersburg's stadium, with a retractable roof and a sliding pitch, hosted 2018 World Cup matches and was famously years late and far over budget. Look for the silver spaceship-like disc at the tip of Krestovsky Island.

name: FNB Stadium
blurb: Africa's largest stadium, about 94,000 seats, styled after a calabash pot. It hosted the 2010 World Cup final, Nelson Mandela's last public appearance. Look for the round earth-toned bowl near Soweto's mine dumps.

name: Westfalenstadion
blurb: Germany's largest stadium, holding about 81,000, home of Borussia Dortmund. Its south stand, the Yellow Wall, is the largest standing terrace in European football at about 25,000. Look for the yellow pylons at the corners.

name: Eiffel Tower
blurb: 1,083 ft of wrought iron, built for the 1889 World's Fair. Look for the iron tower beside the Seine, with the long green Champ de Mars stretching away from it.

name: Dong Hoi Airport
blurb: Gateway to Phong Nha-Ke Bang, home of Son Doong, the largest cave passage known on Earth. Look for the narrow coastal strip with white sand and the limestone karst mountains to the west.

name: Tan Son Nhat International Airport
blurb: Vietnam's busiest airport, inside Ho Chi Minh City, was once Tan Son Nhut Air Base, among the busiest in the world during the Vietnam War. Look for old concrete aircraft shelters beside the runways.

name: Statue of Liberty
blurb: 305 ft from the ground to the torch, on Liberty Island in New York Harbor. Look for the green figure standing on an old star-shaped fort.

name: Colosseum
blurb: Finished in AD 80, the largest amphitheater the Romans ever built held about 50,000 people for gladiator fights. Look for the broken oval, its outer wall missing on one side, at the end of the Roman Forum.

name: Burj Khalifa
blurb: The world's tallest building at 2,717 ft, about twice the height of the Empire State Building. Look for the stepped silver needle rising far above the Dubai skyline, its base a three-lobed Y shape.

name: Empire State Building
blurb: 1,250 ft to the roof, the world's tallest building from 1931 to 1970. Look for the Art Deco spire on Midtown's skyline.

name: Da Nang International Airport
blurb: A major US air base during the Vietnam War, it now sits in the middle of Da Nang. Look for the long My Khe beach to the east and the Marble Mountains, five limestone hills poking up from the coast.

name: Cam Ranh International Airport
blurb: Built on the old Cam Ranh Bay naval and air base, used by the US and later the Soviet navy. Look for the long sandy peninsula, the deep sheltered bay and Nha Trang's beaches to the north.

name: Cà Mau Airport
blurb: Serves Cà Mau on Vietnam's southernmost peninsula, low and laced with canals. Look for mangrove forests, shrimp ponds and waterways in a flat green-and-brown patchwork.

name: London Heathrow Airport
blurb: One of the busiest airports in the world, run on just two parallel runways. Approaches from the east cross central London; look for the Thames, Windsor Castle to the west and the reservoirs around the field.

name: Willis Tower
blurb: At 1,451 ft, America's tallest building for decades. Look for the black tower of stepped boxes rising above Chicago's Loop.

name: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport
blurb: Schiphol sits about 11 ft below sea level on a drained lake bed where a naval battle was fought in 1573. Look for six runways spread in a pinwheel, with the remote Polderbaan far to the northwest.

name: Christ the Redeemer
blurb: A 98-ft statue with arms spanning 92 ft atop Corcovado's 2,300-ft peak. Look for the white figure on the steep green peak above the city.

name: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport
blurb: Terminal 1, opened in 1974, is a round concrete drum, nicknamed the Camembert, with glass-tube escalators crisscrossing its open center. Look for that circle with satellite pods around it, beside the long curved Terminal 2.

name: Petronas Towers
blurb: The world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004, at 1,483 ft, joined by a skybridge. Look for the silver twin spires above central Kuala Lumpur.

name: CN Tower
blurb: At 1,815 ft, the tallest freestanding structure in the world from 1976 to 2007. Look for the concrete needle on Toronto's lakeshore.

name: Anfield
blurb: Liverpool's home, with the famous Kop end, expanded to about 61,000 seats. Everton's old Goodison Park is just across Stanley Park. Look for the bowl at the park's edge in north Liverpool.

name: Emirates Stadium
blurb: Arsenal's home since 2006, about 60,000 seats, replacing Highbury a few blocks away, which became apartments around the old pitch. Look for the smooth oval bowl beside the railway lines in Holloway.

name: One World Trade Center
blurb: 1,776 ft, the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere. Look for the tapering glass tower at Lower Manhattan's tip.

name: Tokyo Skytree
blurb: At 2,080 ft, the tallest tower in the world. Look for the white lattice spire rising from flat east Tokyo near the Sumida River.

name: Rams Park
blurb: Galatasaray's home since 2011, on the European side of Istanbul north of the old city. Look for the bowl with a full roof amid the business towers and highways of Seyrantepe.

name: London Stadium
blurb: The main stadium of the 2012 Olympics, now West Ham's home. Look for the oval in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, next to the red, looping ArcelorMittal Orbit tower, among the rivers and canals of Stratford.

name: Tokyo Tower
blurb: The orange-and-white tower built in 1958, 1,092 ft tall. Look for it near the Shiba park among central Tokyo's towers.

name: Crimean Bridge
blurb: About 12 miles across the Kerch Strait, the longest bridge in Europe, opened by Russia in 2018 after it seized Crimea. Look for parallel road and rail lines and a high arch over the shipping channel.

name: Charles Bridge
blurb: Started in 1357 with 30 statues along its stone parapets, it was Prague's only river crossing for centuries. Look for the dark arched span over the Vltava beneath Prague Castle.

name: Shanghai World Financial Center
blurb: At 1,614 ft, its top is cut with an opening that earned it the nickname 'bottle opener.' Look for the slit tower in Pudong beside the Shanghai Tower.

name: Stari Most
blurb: Built by the Ottomans in 1566, destroyed by shelling in 1993 and rebuilt from the river's own stones in 2004. Divers still leap about 80 ft into the Neretva from its single arch.

name: St James’ Park
blurb: Newcastle's home sits on a hill in the heart of the city, with two huge stands and two small ones, so it looks lopsided from above. Look for the tall cantilevered roof above the city center.

name: Ostankino Tower
blurb: At 1,772 ft, the tallest freestanding structure in Europe. Look for the long concrete shaft north of central Moscow.

name: Estadio Azteca
blurb: The only stadium to host three World Cups: the 1970 and 1986 finals and the 2026 opener. Pelé won his third title and Maradona scored the Hand of God here. Look for the huge bowl in southern Mexico City.

name: Abraj Al Bait
blurb: The clock tower above Mecca's Grand Mosque, about 1,972 ft, has the largest clock faces in the world. Look for the huge clock tower beside the mosque.

name: Bosphorus Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1973 as the first bridge between Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus, with a main span of about 3,520 ft. Look for it just north of Istanbul's old core, with ships streaming beneath.

name: Lusail Stadium
blurb: The 2022 World Cup final stadium, about 89,000 seats, where Argentina beat France. Its golden facade echoes the patterns of traditional Arab bowls and lanterns; look for the gold disc in the new city of Lusail.

name: Forth Bridge
blurb: A 1.5-mile red steel cantilever railway bridge opened in 1890, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for its three giant diamond-shaped cantilevers beside two newer road bridges, one bridge from each of three centuries.

name: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge
blurb: Its towers are about 1.6 inches farther apart at the top than at the base, to allow for Earth's curve. Its 4,260-ft span was the world's longest from 1964 to 1981; look for it at the harbor mouth.

name: Canton Tower
blurb: At about 1,982 ft, one of the tallest towers in the world, with a twisted lattice waist. Look for the hourglass tower on the Pearl River's south bank.

name: Millennium Stadium
blurb: Wales's national stadium has a retractable roof and stands right in central Cardiff on the River Taff, opened for the 1999 Rugby World Cup. Look for the four tall white masts at its corners.

name: MetLife Stadium
blurb: Home to both the Giants and the Jets, and set to host the 2026 World Cup final. Look for the huge gray bowl in the Meadowlands marshes, next to the American Dream mall and the racetrack.

name: SoFi Stadium
blurb: Home of the Rams and Chargers, the most expensive stadium ever built at about $5 billion, sitting under the LAX approach. Look for the huge translucent roof canopy floating over the bowl in Inglewood.

name: Vasco da Gama Bridge
blurb: More than 7 miles long, opened in 1998 for the 500th anniversary of da Gama's sea route to India, and long the longest bridge in Europe. Look for the thread across the wide, shallow Tagus estuary.

name: Hashima Island
blurb: Battleship Island: a coal-mining island off Nagasaki that was once among the most densely populated places on Earth, abandoned in 1974. Look for the walled island of ruined concrete apartment blocks shaped like a warship.

name: George Washington Bridge
blurb: One of the busiest bridges in the world, with 14 lanes on two decks across the Hudson. Look for its gray towers between the Palisades cliffs and Manhattan, with a little red lighthouse under the east end.

name: AT&T Stadium
blurb: The Cowboys' stadium has one of the largest column-free interiors in the world, its roof hung from two giant arches. Look for the huge silver dome in Arlington, next to the Rangers' ballpark.

name: Westminster Bridge
blurb: Painted green to match the leather seats of the House of Commons, the end of Parliament nearest it. Look for it at the foot of Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament, with the London Eye beside it.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
blurb: About 100,000 seats, the biggest stadium in the Southern Hemisphere. It hosted the 1956 Olympics and stages the AFL Grand Final; look for the huge oval in parkland east of downtown.

name: Education City Stadium
blurb: Called the 'Diamond in the Desert,' its faceted triangle-patterned facade shifts color with the sun. Look for it in the Education City campus west of Doha.

name: Millennium Bridge
blurb: A steel footbridge that opened in 2000 and closed two days later because it swayed under walkers; it reopened in 2002 after dampers were fitted. Look for it linking St Paul's dome to Tate Modern's chimney.

name: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2016 near the Black Sea mouth of the Bosphorus, a hybrid suspension and cable-stayed design with towers about 1,050 ft tall and room for eight traffic lanes plus two rail tracks. Look for the fanned cables near the towers.

name: Panathenaic Stadium
blurb: The only stadium in the world built entirely of marble, rebuilt on an ancient site to host the first modern Olympics in 1896. Look for the long white horseshoe set into the hill near the National Garden.

name: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2022 across the Dardanelles with a main span of 6,637 ft, the longest suspension span in the world. Look for its red towers, roughly 1,040 ft tall, near the Gallipoli peninsula.

name: Vizcaya Bridge
blurb: Built in 1893, the world's oldest transporter bridge: a gondola hung from a high steel beam ferries cars and people across the river mouth. A UNESCO World Heritage Site near Bilbao.

name: Arrowhead Stadium
blurb: Home of the Chiefs since 1972, which once set a world record for crowd noise. It shares the Truman Sports Complex with Kauffman Stadium; look for the two stadiums side by side in a sea of parking.

name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1849 as the first permanent bridge over the Danube in Budapest, joining Buda and Pest. Look for its stone arch towers below Castle Hill and the tunnel entrance at the Buda end.

name: NRG Stadium
blurb: The Texans' stadium was the first in the NFL with a retractable roof. Look for the long white roof right beside the round Astrodome, south of downtown Houston.

name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
blurb: Home of the Falcons and Atlanta United, opened in 2017. Its roof opens like a camera aperture, eight triangular panels sliding apart. Look for the pinwheel roof just west of downtown.

name: Monumental Stadium, Buenos Aires
blurb: River Plate's home and the largest stadium in South America, about 85,000 seats and still expanding; it hosted the 1978 World Cup final. Look for the big bowl in the north of the city beside the Río de la Plata.

name: Atatürk Olympic Stadium
blurb: Turkey's largest stadium, with a big crescent-shaped roof over one side, where Liverpool came back from 3 to 0 down to win the 2005 Champions League final. Look for the crescent on Istanbul's far western edge.

name: International Stadium Yokohama
blurb: Japan's biggest stadium, about 72,000 seats, host of the 2002 World Cup final and the 2019 Rugby World Cup final. Look for the white oval with its long curved roof beside the Tsurumi River.

name: Lakhta Centre
blurb: At 1,516 ft, the tallest building in Europe, a twisting glass spire on the Gulf of Finland. Look for the needle on the shore northwest of St. Petersburg.

name: Estadio de La Cartuja
blurb: Seville's 1999 athletics stadium on the Cartuja island, used for Copa del Rey finals and big matches. Look for the white oval with a partial roof on the island across the Guadalquivir from the old city.

name: Azadi Stadium
blurb: Built for the 1974 Asian Games, Iran's national stadium once held 100,000 and still hosts the Esteghlal and Persepolis derby. Look for the huge open bowl beside a lake in west Tehran.

name: Twickenham Stadium
blurb: The world's largest stadium built for rugby union, about 82,000 seats, home of English rugby. Look for the big boxy bowl in southwest London's suburbs, a few miles southeast of Heathrow.

name: Croke Park
blurb: Headquarters of Gaelic games, with about 82,000 seats, one of Europe's biggest stadiums. British forces opened fire on a crowd here on Bloody Sunday in 1920; look for the huge bowl in north Dublin.

name: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
