blurb: The only stadium to host two Summer Olympics, 1932 and 1984, and set for a third in 2028. Look for the arched peristyle at the east end, next to the USC campus.

name: Caesars Superdome
blurb: Opened in 1975 as the largest fixed-dome structure in the world, home of the Saints. Thousands sheltered here during Hurricane Katrina; look for the huge round dome downtown.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
blurb: The largest cricket stadium in the world, holding about 132,000, and host of the 2023 Cricket World Cup final. Look for the huge round bowl beside the Sabarmati River in Ahmedabad.

name: Estádio do Morumbi
blurb: São Paulo FC's home, one of Brazil's biggest stadiums, set in the wealthy, leafy Morumbi district. Look for the huge round concrete bowl among green hills and gated mansions southwest of the center.

name: Cairo International Stadium
blurb: Egypt's national stadium in Nasr City, opened in 1960, one of the largest in Africa at about 75,000 seats. Look for the oval at the center of a large sports complex in eastern Cairo.

name: Zollverein Coal Mine Industrial Complex
blurb: Once the largest coal mine in Europe, its 1932 Shaft XII winding tower became a Bauhaus-style symbol of the Ruhr. Look for the red steel headframe over a long complex of brick buildings in Essen.

name: Chuquicamata
blurb: One of the largest open-pit mines on Earth, nearly 3 miles long and more than half a mile deep, dug for copper for over a century. Look for the giant terraced hole in the bare Atacama.

name: Gelora Bung Karno Stadium
blurb: Built in 1962 for the Asian Games with Soviet help, Indonesia's national stadium holds about 77,000. Look for the huge ring-shaped roof in the green Senayan complex in central Jakarta.

name: King Fahd Sports City
blurb: Riyadh's national stadium opened in 1987 under a white tensile roof of peaked fabric cones that looks like a ring of tents. Look for that spiky white crown on Riyadh's eastern edge.

name: National Stadium, Bukit Jalil
blurb: Southeast Asia's largest stadium, about 87,000 seats, built for the 1998 Commonwealth Games. Look for the white oval with a crown-like roof in the Bukit Jalil sports complex south of Kuala Lumpur.

name: Shanghai Stadium
blurb: Shanghai's big 1997 bowl in Xuhui, with a saddle-shaped white roof that dips and rises around the rim; it hosted 2008 Olympic football. Look for the white ring beside an elevated highway interchange.

name: Ford Field
blurb: Home of the Lions since 2002, built to absorb an old Hudson's warehouse along one side. Look for the dome downtown next to Comerica Park.

name: Empower Field at Mile High
blurb: The Broncos' home, opened in 2001 next to the site of old Mile High Stadium, sits right around 5,280 ft. Look for the bowl with its curved, wave-like upper rim beside I-25 and the South Platte River.

name: Big Hole
blurb: Dug largely by hand from 1871 to 1914, about 1,500 ft across, and long called the largest hand-dug hole on Earth. Look for the round water-filled pit inside Kimberley.

name: Bank of America Stadium
blurb: The Carolina Panthers' home since 1996, built right in Uptown Charlotte. Look for the open bowl with arched entry gates on the southwest edge of downtown's towers.

name: Popigai crater
blurb: An impact crater about 60 miles across, made around 35 million years ago, one of the largest on Earth. The impact turned graphite into diamonds; look for a broad circular basin in the Siberian tundra.

name: Majdanpek
blurb: A big open-pit copper mine in eastern Serbia, near the Danube's Iron Gates. Look for the terraced pit and waste dumps cut into forested hills beside the town.

name: Lambeau Field
blurb: The Packers have played here since 1957, making it the NFL's oldest continuously used stadium, in the smallest market in big-league sports. Look for the bowl among Green Bay's suburban houses.

name: Highmark Stadium
blurb: The Buffalo Bills' home in suburban Orchard Park, famous for snow games. The new stadium opened next to the old bowl in 2026. Look for the stadiums ringed by vast parking lots south of Buffalo.

name: M&T Bank Stadium
blurb: Home of the Ravens since 1998, beside Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Look for the two stadiums side by side just south of Baltimore's Inner Harbor.

name: Bingham Canyon Mine
blurb: One of the largest human-made excavations on Earth, about 2.5 miles across and three-quarters of a mile deep. A 2013 slide here was the largest non-volcanic landslide in modern North American history. Look for the terraced crater in the Oquirrh Mountains.

name: Kim Il-sung Stadium
blurb: Pyongyang's main stadium, opened in 1926 under Japanese rule and renamed for the country's founder in 1982. Kim Il-sung gave his 1945 homecoming speech here. Look for the oval on Moran Hill near the Arch of Triumph.

name: Michigan Stadium
blurb: 'The Big House' seats 107,601, the most of any stadium in the US. The field sits below ground level, so from above it looks like a bowl dug into the earth.

name: Borg El Arab Stadium
blurb: Egypt's largest stadium, seating about 86,000, built in the desert west of Alexandria. Look for the big bowl standing nearly alone amid sand and new development.

name: Center Parc Stadium
blurb: Built for the 1996 Olympics, converted into Turner Field for the Braves, and rebuilt as Georgia State's football stadium. Look for the stadium just south of downtown Atlanta by I-75/85.

name: Cotton Bowl
blurb: Opened in 1930 in Dallas's Fair Park, among art deco exhibition halls built for the 1936 Texas Centennial, and home of the annual Texas vs Oklahoma game. Look for the old open bowl beside the fairground's long esplanade.

name: Huntington Bank Field
blurb: The Cleveland Browns' stadium on the Lake Erie shore, built in 1999 on the site of the old Municipal Stadium. Look for the open bowl right on the lakefront, beside the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame's glass pyramid.

name: Ivittuut
blurb: For a century the world's only major source of natural cryolite, a mineral vital to early aluminum smelting, until it closed in 1987. Look for the flooded pit beside a fjord in southern Greenland.

name: Grasberg Mine
blurb: One of the largest gold and copper mines in the world, dug at about 13,000 ft near Puncak Jaya's glaciers. Look for the giant crater in bare gray rock high in the New Guinea mountains.

name: Ombilin coal mine
blurb: A Dutch colonial coal mine that built the town of Sawahlunto in the 1800s, now a UNESCO World Heritage site. Look for the old mining town in a narrow valley in the West Sumatra highlands.

name: Stade des Martyrs
blurb: One of Africa's largest stadiums, holding around 80,000, home of the DR Congo national team. The Martyrs are four politicians hanged on this site in 1966. Look for the big concrete bowl in Kinshasa.

name: Nou Mestalla
blurb: Valencia's new stadium was started in 2007, abandoned as a concrete shell in 2009 during the financial crisis, and only revived in the 2020s. Look for the big unfinished bowl in the north of the city.

name: İzmir Atatürk Stadium
blurb: İzmir's big multi-use stadium, built in the early 1970s for the Mediterranean Games. Look for the large open oval with a track east of the city center, back from the bay.

name: Aleppo International Stadium
blurb: Syria's largest stadium, opened in 2007 in Aleppo. Look for the big oval bowl on the edge of the city, with dry plain and rocky hills beyond.

name: Stade 5 Juillet 1962
blurb: Algeria's national stadium, named for its independence day, built in the hills west of central Algiers. Look for the big oval bowl in a sports complex above the bay.

name: Cerro Rico
blurb: The "rich mountain" whose silver bankrolled the Spanish Empire, so riddled with tunnels it has partly collapsed. Look for the reddish cone rising to nearly 16,000 ft over Potosí, one of the highest cities on Earth.

name: Mir diamond mine
blurb: A Soviet-era kimberlite pit about 1,700 ft deep and roughly three-quarters of a mile across, one of the largest holes ever dug. Look for the perfect spiral beside the town of Mirny.

name: Guangdong Olympic Center
blurb: Guangzhou's 80,000-seat stadium, opened in 2001, with seats in a rainbow of colors under a ribbon-like roof. Look for the long curving white roof strips in the city's eastern Tianhe district.

name: Udachnaya diamond mine
blurb: A diamond pit more than 1,900 ft deep just south of the Arctic Circle, among the deepest open pits in the world. Look for the stepped spiral in larch taiga.

name: U.S. Bank Stadium
blurb: Home of the Vikings, with a steep, ship-like roof of clear plastic film that lets in daylight. Look for the dark angular prow on the east edge of downtown Minneapolis.

name: Kumtor Gold Mine
blurb: A gold mine at about 13,000 ft in the Tian Shan, dug partly through glacier ice. Look for gray open pits and waste dumps among glaciers south of Lake Issyk-Kul.

name: Jakarta International Stadium
blurb: Opened in 2022 with a retractable roof and about 82,000 seats, home of Persija Jakarta. Look for the giant pale oval near the waterfront in North Jakarta.

name: Tangier Grand Stadium
blurb: Morocco's northern showpiece, rebuilt and expanded for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations with an eye on the 2030 World Cup. Look for the big open bowl on the southern edge of Tangier, inland from the Strait of Gibraltar.

name: Gansu Wind Farm
blurb: Part of the Jiuquan wind base, one of the largest wind complexes on Earth, spread across the Gobi along the Hexi Corridor. Look for thousands of turbines in grids across bare gray desert.

name: Estadio Monumental U
blurb: Universitario's home in Lima, at about 80,000 seats the largest stadium in Peru. Look for the big bowl ringed by private boxes in the dry eastern suburb of Ate.

name: Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium
blurb: The Longhorns' stadium seats about 100,000, one of the largest in the country. Look for the huge bowl on the University of Texas campus just north of the capitol dome.

name: Sanford Stadium
blurb: Georgia's home in Athens, seating about 93,000, famous for the privet hedges that line the field. Look for the big bowl set in a valley on campus.

name: Hassan II Stadium
blurb: Planned as one of the largest football stadiums on Earth, about 115,000 seats, to host matches at the 2030 World Cup that Morocco shares with Spain and Portugal. It sits in open country between Casablanca and Rabat.

name: Fântânele-Cogealac Wind Farm
blurb: About 240 turbines on the Dobruja plateau near the Black Sea, one of the largest onshore wind farms in Europe. Look for towers spread in a grid across vast open fields.

name: Ohio Stadium
blurb: Ohio State's 'Horseshoe,' opened in 1922 and seating over 100,000. Look for the U-shape, open at the south end, on the bank of the Olentangy River.

name: Bryant–Denny Stadium
blurb: Alabama's home, seating over 100,000, one of the largest stadiums in the world. Look for the huge steep-sided bowl on the University of Alabama campus in Tuscaloosa.

name: Tiger Stadium
blurb: Death Valley, LSU's 102,000-seat stadium, one of the loudest in college football; a 1988 touchdown here was famously picked up on a seismograph. Look for the towering bowl on campus near the Mississippi.

name: Notre Dame Stadium
blurb: Home of the Fighting Irish since 1930, about 78,000 seats. Look just north for the 'Touchdown Jesus' mural on the library and the golden dome nearby.

name: Neyland Stadium
blurb: Tennessee's stadium holds about 102,000, one of the biggest in the country. Fans arrive by boat as the "Vol Navy." Look for the giant bowl on the north bank of the Tennessee River in Knoxville.

name: Roscoe Wind Farm
blurb: When finished in 2009 it was the world's largest wind farm, over 600 turbines on Texas cotton land. Look for towers stretching to the horizon across a grid of fields.

name: Beaver Stadium
blurb: Penn State's stadium seats about 106,000, the second largest in the US. Look for the steel-framed bowl in the farm valley of State College, with the long Appalachian ridges on either side.

name: Husky Stadium
blurb: Home of the Washington Huskies, right on Lake Washington; fans arrive by boat and tie up off the stadium. Look for the cantilevered roofs pointed out over the water.

name: Kyle Field
blurb: Texas A&M's stadium seats about 102,000, one of the largest in college football, and students stand all game as the "12th Man." Look for the towering maroon-trimmed bowl on the College Station campus.

name: King Salman International Stadium
blurb: Planned as the centerpiece of Saudi Arabia's 2034 World Cup, a roughly 92,000-seat stadium meant to host the final, rising in north Riyadh. What you see may still be a construction site.

name: Williams-Brice Stadium
blurb: South Carolina's stadium seats about 77,000. Next door sits the Cockaboose Railroad, a line of old cabooses on a siding turned into tailgating suites. Look for the bowl beside rail tracks south of downtown Columbia.

name: Memorial Stadium, Clemson
blurb: Clemson's "Death Valley" seats about 81,000. Players rub Howard's Rock and run down a grassy hill onto the field. Look for the bowl on the campus, a short walk from an arm of Lake Hartwell.

name: Scout Moor Wind Farm
blurb: 26 turbines on the moors between Rochdale and Rawtenstall, England's largest onshore wind farm when built. Look for towers on brown moorland above the Manchester suburbs.

name: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium
blurb: The Swamp, the Florida Gators' home, seats about 88,500 and was built into a natural depression on campus. Coach Steve Spurrier named it. Look for the steep brick and steel bowl in Gainesville.

name: Memorial Stadium
blurb: Nebraska has sold out every home game since 1962, the longest streak in college football. On game day roughly 90,000 fans make the stadium the third-largest 'city' in the state. Look for the bowl on the north edge of downtown Lincoln.

name: Camp Randall Stadium
blurb: The Wisconsin Badgers' stadium, about 76,000 seats, famous for the whole crowd jumping to 'Jump Around.' Look for the bowl on the UW campus between the lakes of Madison.

name: Jordan–Hare Stadium
blurb: Auburn's home, seating about 88,000, more than the population of the town itself on game days. Look for the big bowl in the middle of the Auburn campus.

name: Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium
blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners' stadium in Norman, seating about 80,000, one of the largest in college football. Look for the big brick bowl in the middle of campus.

name: Doak Campbell Stadium
blurb: Florida State's home, with about 67,000 seats since a recent renovation, wrapped in brick Collegiate Gothic arches billed as the largest continuous brick structure in the US. Look for the red-brick bowl in Tallahassee.

name: Palace of Versailles
blurb: Louis XIV turned a hunting lodge into the seat of French power. The estate covers about 2,000 acres; look for the cross-shaped Grand Canal, about a mile long, pointing straight west from the palace.

name: Forbidden City
blurb: Home to 24 emperors from 1420 to 1912, about 180 acres behind a moat and walls. Look for the yellow-tiled roofs in a perfect rectangle at the dead center of Beijing's grid.

name: Château de Montsoreau
blurb: Built in the 1450s right at the edge of the Loire, unusual among the Loire châteaux for standing in the river's bed rather than on a hill. Look for the pale stone walls right on the riverbank.

name: Alhambra
blurb: The 13th and 14th century palace-fortress of Spain's last Muslim rulers, its name meaning "the red one" in Arabic. Look for the long reddish walls along a wooded ridge above Granada, with the Sierra Nevada behind.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
blurb: Ludwig II's fairy-tale castle on a crag in the Bavarian Alps, an inspiration for Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle. Look for white walls and towers on the forested ridge above two lakes.

name: Frankfurt Airport
blurb: Lufthansa's hub, carved out of the forest south of Frankfurt. Runway 18 West is used only for takeoffs to the south. Look for the city skyline just northeast and the Main river curving past.

name: Saint-Tropez
blurb: A fishing village that became the Riviera's most famous resort after Brigitte Bardot filmed "And God Created Woman" there in 1956. Look for superyachts lined up in the small harbor.

name: Potala Palace
blurb: Thirteen stories built up a hillside at about 12,000 ft, winter home of the Dalai Lamas until 1959. Look for the white outer palace and the red central palace stacked over Lhasa.

name: Windsor Castle
blurb: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world, a royal home for over 900 years, and often seen on the Heathrow approach. Look for the Round Tower and long walls above the Thames.

name: Ben Gurion Airport
blurb: Israel's main airport, at Lod on the coastal plain, with famously tight security. Look for three runways forming a rough triangle, with Tel Aviv's towers about 10 miles northwest.

name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
blurb: New York's main international gateway, built on marshland at the edge of Jamaica Bay. Look for the bay's wildlife refuge islands just west and the Rockaway beaches to the south.

name: Domodedovo International Airport
blurb: Once Russia's busiest airport, southeast of Moscow among birch forests. A 2011 suicide bombing in its arrivals hall killed 37 people. Look for the parallel runways cut through the woods.

name: Sheremetyevo International Airport
blurb: Russia's busiest airport and Aeroflot's hub, north of Moscow. Look for three parallel runways in the birch forest, with terminal complexes on both the north and south sides.

name: Disneyland
blurb: Walt Disney's original park, opened in Anaheim in 1955. Look for the snowcapped Matterhorn and the river around Tom Sawyer Island among parking structures and hotels.

name: Dubai International Airport
blurb: For years the world's busiest airport for international passengers and the home of Emirates. Look for two parallel runways and long concourses lined with A380s, right beside the city.

name: Stamford Bridge
blurb: Chelsea's home, squeezed onto a tight site between a railway cutting and the Fulham Road, which keeps it at about 40,000 seats. Look for the compact boxy stadium in dense west London.

name: Beijing Capital International Airport
blurb: Terminal 3, designed by Norman Foster for the 2008 Olympics, was among the largest buildings in the world when it opened. Look for its red-and-gold roof, more than a mile long and shaped loosely like a dragon.

name: Singapore Changi Airport
blurb: Built on reclaimed land at Singapore's eastern tip, it is home to the Rain Vortex, about 130 ft tall and the world's tallest indoor waterfall. Look for the glass doughnut dome of Jewel between the terminals.

name: Madrid-Barajas Airport
blurb: Terminal 4, by Richard Rogers, runs nearly a mile under a wavy bamboo-lined roof. Look for four runways in two parallel pairs set at an angle, around a field of long, gently rippling terminal roofs.

name: Tokyo International Airport
blurb: Tokyo's in-town airport and one of the world's busiest, built largely on reclaimed land in Tokyo Bay. Look for runways in a hashtag pattern, one of them partly on an offshore pier where the Tama River meets the bay.

name: London Gatwick Airport
blurb: The busiest single-runway airport in the world. Look for the one long runway in green Sussex countryside, with the North Terminal and South Terminal linked by a little shuttle train.

name: Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport
blurb: For most years the busiest airport in the world by passengers. Look for five parallel east-west runways and the long row of midfield concourses lined up between them.

name: Statue of Unity
blurb: At 597 ft, the tallest statue in the world, showing independence leader Sardar Patel. It is about twice the height of the Statue of Liberty with its pedestal. Look for the bronze figure on the Narmada River below the dam.

name: Heydar Aliyev International Airport
blurb: Baku's airport on the Absheron Peninsula, ringed by oil fields that have been pumping since the 1800s. Look for the triangular glass terminal opened in 2014, nodding donkeys and the Caspian shore.

name: Kansai International Airport
blurb: Built on an artificial island about 3 miles out in Osaka Bay, which has sunk more than 30 ft since it opened in 1994. Look for the mile-long terminal and the bridge linking the island to the mainland.

name: Los Angeles International Airport
blurb: Four parallel runways end right at the beach. Look for the Theme Building, the 1961 spider-legged flying saucer in the middle of the terminal loop, and planes taking off straight out over the Pacific.

name: Hong Kong International Airport
blurb: Built on Chek Lap Kok, an island flattened and extended by reclamation, replacing the old city airport at Kai Tak in 1998. Look for the two runways in the sea off Lantau's mountains.

name: Brussels Airport
blurb: Belgium's main airport at Zaventem, northeast of Brussels, struck by terrorist bombings in March 2016. Look for three runways, two parallel and one crossing, among suburbs and fields.

name: Wien-Schwechat Airport
blurb: Austria's hub, on flat ground east of Vienna near the Danube. Look for two crossing runways, the river and its floodplain forest to the north, and rows of wind turbines toward Lake Neusiedl.

name: Munich Airport
blurb: Built on drained moorland northeast of Munich, the Erdinger Moos. Look for the two widely spaced parallel runways with the terminals between them, and on a clear day the Alps to the south.

name: Kuala Lumpur International Airport
blurb: Opened in 1998 about 30 miles south of Kuala Lumpur, designed as an "airport in the forest" with trees planted around it. Look for the cross-shaped satellite terminal, linked by train to the main building.

name: O'Hare International Airport
blurb: One of the world's busiest airports, rebuilt over two decades so most of its eight runways run parallel east-west. Look for the long parallel strips with the terminal fingers in the middle and the Kennedy Expressway running straight in from downtown.

name: Suvarnabhumi Airport
blurb: Built on swampland once called Cobra Swamp, it has one of the largest single terminal buildings ever built. Look for the long curved glass-and-steel roof between two parallel runways.

name: Narita International Airport
blurb: Tokyo's main international airport, about 40 miles east of the city. Farmers fought its construction for decades, and a few holdout plots still sit by the runways. Look for the two runways cut through farmland and golf courses.

name: Roma Fiumicino Airport
blurb: Rome's main airport, on the coast at Fiumicino beside the ruins of Portus, Imperial Rome's harbor. Look for Trajan's six-sided harbor basin, now a hexagonal lake, just northeast of the runways.

name: Indira Gandhi International Airport
blurb: One of the busiest airports in Asia, and one of very few with an elevated taxiway where jets roll over a road. Look for four runways and the long terminal arcs on Delhi's southwestern edge.

name: Zurich Airport
blurb: Switzerland's largest airport, at Kloten north of Zurich. Look for three runways, two crossing, among woods and villages, and on clear days the white wall of the Alps to the south.

name: Shanghai Pudong International Airport
blurb: Built on reclaimed tidal flats at the edge of the East China Sea, it is linked to the city by the first commercial maglev, built to run over 250 mph. Look for several long parallel runways along the coastline.

name: Incheon International Airport
blurb: Built on land reclaimed between two islands in the Yellow Sea and opened in 2001, it is consistently ranked among the world's best airports. Look for the long bridges linking it to the mainland across the tidal flats.

name: Orly Airport
blurb: Paris's older airport, south of the city. Look for the long terminal buildings beside the Rungis wholesale food market, one of the largest in the world, just to the north.

name: Phu Quoc International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2012 on Phu Quoc, Vietnam's largest island, just off the Cambodian coast. Look for the east-west runway running inland from the west coast's long beaches, with forested hills beyond.

name: Istanbul Airport
blurb: Opened in 2018 on the Black Sea coast, built over old coal mines and quarries, and designed to grow into one of the largest airports in the world. Look for multiple parallel runways and flooded pits among the forests.

name: Melilla Airport
blurb: Melilla is a Spanish city on Morocco's north coast, so its small airport sits right against the border. Look for the runway between the city and the Moroccan hills, beside the tall layered border fence.

name: Villa Park
blurb: Aston Villa's home since 1897, with the big Holte End stand. Look for the boxy stadium beside the Victorian Aston Hall and its park, north of Birmingham's center.

name: Copenhagen Airport
blurb: Scandinavia's busiest airport, on Amager island beside the Øresund. Look for the runways right on the water and the road and rail link to Sweden diving into its tunnel just off the coast.

name: Lukoil Arena
blurb: Spartak Moscow's home, opened in 2014 in the northwest suburb of Tushino. Look for a red and white facade beside the Moscow Canal near the old Tushino airfield.

name: Vnukovo International Airport
blurb: Moscow's third big airport, southwest of the city, also used for Kremlin and government flights. Look for two crossing runways set among forest and dacha settlements.

name: Zayed International Airport
blurb: Renamed Zayed International in 2024, after the UAE's founding president. Its newest terminal, opened in 2023, is a huge X shape; look for it between the runways on the flat coastal sand.

name: London Stansted Airport
blurb: Its terminal, by Norman Foster, pioneered putting the building services under the floor so the roof could float on tree-like columns. Ryanair's biggest base; look for the long single runway in Essex farmland.

name: Sydney Airport
blurb: Australia's busiest airport, on Botany Bay, where Captain Cook landed in 1770. Look for two parallel runways built out into the bay on fill, with the container port beside them.

name: Boryspil International Airport
blurb: Ukraine's main airport, east of Kyiv. It has been closed to civilian flights since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. Look for the Dnipro River and the flat farmland and forest around the field.

name: Soekarno Hatta International Airport
blurb: Jakarta's main airport, one of the busiest in Southeast Asia. The original terminals were designed as clusters of Javanese pavilions with red-tiled roofs set in gardens; look for them between the long parallel runways.

name: Athens International Airport "Eleftherios Venizelos"
blurb: Opened in 2001 at Spata, east of Athens, to replace the old seaside Ellinikon airport ahead of the 2004 Olympics. Look for two parallel runways in the Mesogeia plain among vineyards and olive groves.

name: San Francisco International Airport
blurb: Its runways were built out into San Francisco Bay on fill. Look for the two pairs of crossing runways jutting into the water and, on the right day, two jets landing side by side on the close-set parallels.

name: Warsaw Chopin Airport
blurb: Poland's busiest airport lies inside Warsaw's city limits, only about 6 miles south of the center. Look for two runways crossing in an X, with the city's apartment blocks pressed close around it.

name: Veltins-Arena
blurb: Schalke 04's stadium in Gelsenkirchen, now the Veltins-Arena. Its retractable roof and a pitch that slides out on rails let the grass grow outside. Look for the boxy stadium in the old mining district.

name: Helsinki Airport
blurb: Finnair's hub, cut into flat forest north of Helsinki. Look for the three runways surrounded by dark pine woods, lakes and scattered farms.

name: LaGuardia Airport
blurb: Wedged against Flushing Bay, with runway ends on piers over the water. Look for Manhattan a few miles west and Citi Field, home of the Mets, just across the bay.

name: Disneyland Paris
blurb: Opened in 1992 in Marne-la-Vallée east of Paris, Europe's most-visited theme park. Look for the castle and the lake beside the TGV station.

name: Fernsehturm Berlin
blurb: The TV tower that rises 1,207 ft over central Berlin. Look for the silver sphere near Alexanderplatz.

name: Mineirão
blurb: Belo Horizonte's giant stadium, where Germany beat Brazil 7 to 1 in the 2014 World Cup semifinal. Look for the ring of concrete ribs beside Lake Pampulha.

name: Hampden Park
blurb: Scotland's national stadium drew nearly 150,000 to a 1937 match against England, a European record. Look for the open bowl in Glasgow's southern suburbs.

name: Milan–Malpensa "Silvio Berlusconi" Airport
blurb: Milan's main hub, about 30 miles northwest of the city on heathland by the Ticino River. Look for two long parallel runways, with Lake Maggiore and the Alps beyond to the north.

name: Pleiku Airport
blurb: Serves Pleiku in Vietnam's Central Highlands. Look for red basalt soil and green plantations of coffee, rubber and pepper in neat rows across the plateau.

name: Toronto Pearson International Airport
blurb: Canada's busiest airport, with five runways and the long curve of Terminal 1. Look for the CN Tower about 15 miles southeast and the Lake Ontario shoreline beyond downtown.

name: Kasubi Tombs
blurb: Burial ground of the kings of Buganda, under a huge thatched hut that burned in 2010 and was rebuilt with traditional grass and reed. Look for the domed thatch roof on a hilltop in Kampala.

name: Munich Olympic Stadium
blurb: Centerpiece of the 1972 Olympics, under a sweeping tent roof of acrylic panels hung from masts and cables. Look for the transparent web draped over the stadium, the lake and the 950-ft Olympic Tower beside it.

name: Stade Vélodrome
blurb: Olympique de Marseille's home, France's largest club stadium at about 67,000 seats. A 2014 rebuild added a white wave-shaped roof. Look for the rippled white roof in the city's southern quarter.

name: Václav Havel Airport Prague
blurb: Prague's airport at Ruzyně, on the western edge of the city. Look for the runways on a flat plateau among fields, with the city and the bends of the Vltava to the east.

name: London Luton Airport
blurb: easyJet's home base, on a hilltop just outside Luton about 30 miles north of London. Look for the single runway sitting on a ridge above the town.

name: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen International Airport
blurb: Istanbul's airport on the Asian side, about 30 miles east of the old city, and the base of Pegasus Airlines. Look for the Sea of Marmara coast and the Princes' Islands offshore.

name: Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport
blurb: Serbia's main airport, west of Belgrade in Surčin, is named for Nikola Tesla, born to Serb parents in what is now Croatia. Look east for the Sava meeting the Danube under Belgrade's fortress hill.

name: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport
blurb: Guangzhou's main airport, one of the busiest in China, well north of the city. Look for parallel runways and the big terminal buildings among farmland and low hills.

name: Oslo Airport
blurb: Norway's main airport at Gardermoen, about 30 miles north of Oslo, with a terminal built largely of wood. Look for two parallel runways in pine forest.

name: Josep Tarradellas Airport Barcelona-El Prat
blurb: Spread across the flat Llobregat River delta, with one runway laid right along the beach. Look for the port's container docks to the north and the city's grid climbing toward the hills behind.

name: London City Airport
blurb: Built in the Docklands on a strip between two old docks, with a steep 5.5-degree approach that only certain jets can fly. Look for the runway between two long strips of dock water, with Canary Wharf's towers just west.

name: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport
blurb: At about 27 square miles it is bigger than Manhattan. Look for seven runways, mostly running north and south, and the terminals strung along a central spine like a row of half-moons.

name: Dublin Airport
blurb: Ireland's busiest airport by far, north of the city by the M50 ring road. A second parallel runway opened in 2022. Look for the curved white 1940 terminal, still standing among the newer buildings.

name: Manchester Airport
blurb: The UK's busiest airport outside London, with two parallel runways south of the city. Look for Manchester's towers to the north and the Pennine hills rising to the east.

name: Phu Bai International Airport
blurb: Serves Huế, Vietnam's old imperial capital. Look for the Perfume River and, on its north bank, the square walled Citadel with its moats.

name: Berlin Brandenburg Airport
blurb: Opened in 2020, nine years late and billions over budget, after a long run of construction blunders. Look for the terminal between two parallel runways on Berlin's southeastern edge.

name: Walt Disney World Resort
blurb: About 25,000 acres, roughly the size of San Francisco, built on Florida swampland. Look for the lagoons, the parks, and resort hotels scattered through green forest.

name: Burgos Cathedral
blurb: Begun in 1221, one of Spain's great Gothic cathedrals, famous for its lacy open-work spires. Look for the twin pale spires rising over the old town on the Arlanzón river.

name: Volksparkstadion
blurb: Hamburger SV's stadium in the Volkspark in the west of the city, a 2006 World Cup venue. Look for the bowl in the green park, close to the autobahn and Hamburg's big arena.

name: MHPArena
blurb: VfB Stuttgart's stadium in the Neckar valley at Bad Cannstatt, beside the fairground of the Cannstatter Wasen beer festival. Look for the white membrane roof next to the Mercedes-Benz Museum and plant.

name: Cape Town Stadium
blurb: Built at Green Point for the 2010 World Cup, between Signal Hill and the Atlantic. Look for the white glassy bowl on the flat coast below the hill, with Table Mountain rising behind the city.

name: Johan Cruyff Arena
blurb: Ajax's home since 1996 and one of the first stadiums in Europe with a retractable roof. Look for the big box with a sliding roof in southeast Amsterdam, built over a road, beside the train station.

name: Deutsche Bank Park
blurb: Eintracht Frankfurt's stadium in the city forest, with a retractable fabric roof hung from a central cube. Look for the round bowl in the woods, a few miles from Frankfurt Airport's runways.

name: The Motherland Calls
blurb: At about 279 ft including the sword, the world's tallest statue when finished in 1967, marking the Battle of Stalingrad. Look for the sword-raising figure on the Mamayev Kurgan hill above the Volga.

name: Khalifa International Stadium
blurb: Qatar's oldest major stadium, opened in 1976 and rebuilt for the 2022 World Cup. Look for the two huge arches over the stands in the Aspire Zone, next to the tall Torch tower.

name: Estádio Nacional de Brasília
blurb: Rebuilt for the 2014 World Cup with a ring of 288 slim columns holding its roof, it's the second-largest stadium in Brazil. Look for the round white roof on Brasília's Monumental Axis.

name: BC Place
blurb: Home of the BC Lions and Vancouver Whitecaps, under one of the largest cable-supported retractable roofs in the world. Look for the white dome ringed by masts on False Creek downtown.

name: Kazimierz Górski National Stadium
blurb: Poland's national stadium, built for Euro 2012 in the bowl of an older stadium on the Vistula. Look for the red-and-white basket-weave facade, the national colors, on the river's east bank.

name: Moses Mabhida Stadium
blurb: Durban's 2010 World Cup stadium is spanned by a giant arch, with a cable car riding up to a viewing deck at the top. Look for the white arch soaring over the bowl near the beachfront.

name: Tower of Hercules
blurb: A Roman lighthouse nearly 1,900 years old and about 180 ft tall, the oldest Roman lighthouse still working. Look for the square tower alone on the headland at the tip of A Coruña.

name: Ernst-Happel-Stadion
blurb: Austria's national stadium, which hosted the Euro 2008 final, sits in the Prater park. Look for the big round bowl near the Danube, close to the giant Ferris wheel.

name: Ellis Park Stadium
blurb: Where Nelson Mandela, wearing a Springbok jersey, handed the 1995 Rugby World Cup to Francois Pienaar. Look for the steep bowl on the ridge just east of downtown Johannesburg's towers.

name: Rialto Bridge
blurb: A single stone arch from 1591, for centuries the only way across Venice's Grand Canal on foot. Look for it at the canal's midpoint, its roofline lined with shops.

name: Castelão
blurb: Fortaleza's big stadium, rebuilt for the 2014 World Cup with a roof that covers nearly every seat. Look for the oval ring with its pale canopy in the city's southern outskirts.

name: Charminar
blurb: Built in 1591, a square arch with four minarets rising about 180 ft over Hyderabad's old-city bazaars. Look for the pale square monument sitting in the middle of a busy crossroads.

name: Milad Tower
blurb: A 1,427-ft telecom tower in Tehran, one of the tallest in the world. Look for the pod near its top above the city, with the Alborz behind.

name: Loftus Versfeld Stadium
blurb: Pretoria's rugby fortress, home of the Bulls and of Mamelodi Sundowns, a Pretoria institution for generations. Look for the deep rectangular stadium squeezed into a suburban grid east of the city center.

name: Estádio da Luz
blurb: Benfica's home, at about 65,000 seats the largest stadium in Portugal, hosted the Euro 2004 final. Look for its roof hung from four big arches, a couple of miles southwest of Lisbon airport.

name: Parc Olympique Lyonnais
blurb: Olympique Lyonnais' stadium in Décines, east of Lyon, opened in 2016 and seating about 59,000. Look for the box with its translucent roof amid fields and parking, near the Rhône canal.

name: Ponte Vecchio
blurb: Shops have lined it since the Middle Ages, and it was the only Florence bridge the retreating Germans spared in 1944. Look for the buildings hanging off its sides over the Arno.

name: Gillette Stadium
blurb: Home of the Patriots and the Revolution in Foxborough, with a lighthouse tower at one end. Look for the stadium and its shopping strip along Route 1, among woods.

name: Al Bayt Stadium
blurb: Shaped like a Bedouin tent, it hosted the 2022 World Cup opening match. Look for the striped dark tent-like shell alone in the desert at Al Khor, north of Doha.

name: Celtic Park
blurb: Celtic's home, about 60,000 seats, the largest club stadium in Scotland. Look for the big bowl with a continuous roof in Parkhead, in Glasgow's East End.

name: Maiden Tower
blurb: A squat stone tower about 95 ft tall, probably from the 12th century, whose original purpose is still debated. Look for the round tower at the seaward edge of Baku's walled old city, near the Caspian promenade.

name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
blurb: At about 4.3 miles the longest track on the F1 calendar, winding through the Ardennes forest. Look for the famous Eau Rouge uphill sweep just past the pit straight.

name: Donbass Arena
blurb: Built for Shakhtar Donetsk and opened in 2009, it hosted a Euro 2012 semifinal. Damaged in the fighting of 2014, it has stood unused since. Look for the glassy oval set in a park.

name: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
blurb: Spurs' home since 2019 has a grass pitch that splits and slides away under the south stand to reveal an artificial field for NFL games. Look for the curved bowl in north London's Tottenham.

name: Merkur Spiel-Arena
blurb: Fortuna Düsseldorf's stadium on the Rhine, with a retractable roof, a 2024 Euros venue and host of Eurovision in 2011. Look for the boxy arena near the trade fair halls in the city's north.

name: Lumen Field
blurb: Home of the Seahawks and Sounders, its roof covers most seats but leaves the north end open to frame downtown. Look for the twin roof arches by the waterfront.

name: Estadio Centenario
blurb: Built for the first World Cup in 1930, it hosted the final, won by Uruguay. Look for the tall marble Tower of Homage rising over one stand, beside the green of Parque Batlle.

name: Hard Rock Stadium
blurb: The Dolphins' home in Miami Gardens, with a big canopy over the seats, has hosted six Super Bowls. For the Miami Grand Prix, an F1 circuit is laid out around it. Look for the canopy ringed by parking lots.

name: Stadion Maksimir
blurb: Home of Dinamo Zagreb and Croatia's national team. In 1990 a riot here between Dinamo and Red Star Belgrade fans became a symbol of Yugoslavia's breakup. Look for it beside Maksimir Park's woods and lakes.

name: Rajko Mitić Stadium
blurb: Red Star Belgrade's home is nicknamed the Marakana after Rio's Maracanã and is famous for some of Europe's loudest, smokiest derbies. Look for an open bowl sunk into the ground on the hill of Dedinje.

name: Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium
blurb: Fenerbahçe's home sits on the Asian side of Istanbul in Kadıköy, a short walk from the Sea of Marmara. Look for the steep, fully roofed stadium among dense neighborhoods near the Bosphorus's southern mouth.

name: Aviva Stadium
blurb: Built on Lansdowne Road, the world's oldest international rugby ground. The roof dips low at the north end so it doesn't shade the neighbors; look for the curved glassy wave beside the railway line.

name: De Kuip
blurb: Feyenoord's 1937 home in Rotterdam, nicknamed 'the Tub.' Its steel-and-concrete bowl was a model for modern stadium design. Look for the round bowl on the south bank of the Maas, east of the port.

name: Nürburgring
blurb: The 12.9-mile Nordschleife, "the Green Hell," twists through the Eifel forest with more than 150 turns. Look for the castle on the hill beside the modern Grand Prix track.

name: Silverstone Circuit
blurb: Built on a World War II bomber airfield, it hosted the first ever F1 world championship race in 1950. Look for the old runway pattern still traced inside the circuit.

name: Imola Circuit
blurb: Ayrton Senna died here in 1994 at the Tamburello curve, a crash that reshaped F1 safety. Look for the track looping along the Santerno River at the edge of town, set among vineyards and orchards.

name: Monza Circuit
blurb: The Temple of Speed, opened in 1922 and the fastest track on the F1 calendar. Look for the crumbling concrete banking of the old high-speed oval still standing in the trees of Monza Park.

name: Lincoln Financial Field
blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles' home since 2003, part of the South Philadelphia sports complex. Look for the bowl with two curving wing-shaped roof canopies, beside the Phillies' ballpark.

name: Bank of China Tower
blurb: I. M. Pei's 1,205-ft tower made of stacked triangles. Look for the sharp-edged glass spire among Hong Kong Island's skyscrapers.

name: Suzuka Circuit
blurb: Built by Honda in 1962, it's the only figure-eight track on the F1 calendar. Look for the overpass where the circuit crosses itself, and the amusement park Ferris wheel beside the paddock.

name: Maiden's Tower
blurb: A small tower on an islet at the mouth of the Bosporus, used over the centuries as a lighthouse, customs post and quarantine station. Look for the white tower on a rock just off the Asian shore at Üsküdar.

name: Space Needle
blurb: Built for the 1962 World's Fair, it stands 605 ft tall. Look for the flying-saucer top at Seattle Center, just north of downtown between Elliott Bay and Lake Union.

name: Estádio do Dragão
blurb: FC Porto's home, opened for Euro 2004. Look for the oval with its translucent roof on the eastern edge of Porto, beside the highway.

name: Bahrain International Circuit
blurb: The first Formula 1 track in the Middle East, opened in 2004. The race now runs at night under floodlights; look for the track and its tall sail-shaped tower in bare desert.

name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
blurb: Home of the Spanish Grand Prix since 1991 and the place F1 teams have done much of their winter testing. Look for the loop in the hills at Montmeló, north of Barcelona.

name: Colossi of Memnon
blurb: Two seated stone statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III, about 60 ft tall and roughly 3,400 years old, all that's left standing of his mortuary temple. Look for two dark figures in green fields on Luxor's west bank.

name: Levi's Stadium
blurb: The 49ers' home in Santa Clara, which hosted Super Bowl 50, has a green roof and solar panels on its suite tower. Look for it beside the Great America roller coasters, a few miles from San Jose airport.

name: Rio de Janeiro–Galeão International Airport
blurb: Rio's main airport sits on an island in Guanabara Bay, with a runway over 13,000 ft long. Look across the bay for Sugarloaf, the downtown towers and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado.

name: Rio-Antirrio bridge
blurb: A multi-span cable-stayed bridge about 1.8 miles long across the Gulf of Corinth, built to ride out earthquakes. Look for its four towers in a line across the strait.

name: Sepang International Circuit
blurb: Malaysia's F1 home from 1999 to 2017, right next to Kuala Lumpur's main airport, so it's easy to spot on approach. Look for two long parallel straights joined by a hairpin and the leaf-shaped grandstand roofs.

name: Sirius Autodrom
blurb: Built for Russia's F1 race, it loops around the 2014 Winter Olympic Park in Sochi. Look for the track wrapping the cluster of Olympic arenas and the white Fisht Stadium on the Black Sea shore.

name: King Baudouin Stadium
blurb: Formerly the Heysel, where 39 fans died in a wall collapse before the 1985 European Cup final. Look for it next to the Atomium, the giant steel model of an iron crystal.

name: San Mamés Stadium
blurb: Athletic Bilbao's home, "La Catedral," was rebuilt in 2013 with a white panel skin that glows at night. Look for the white stadium beside the Nervión estuary, downriver from the Guggenheim.

name: Estadio Akron
blurb: Chivas's stadium, built to look like a volcano with grass growing up its sloped outer walls. A 2026 World Cup venue; look for the green cone with a cloud-like roof in Zapopan.

name: Kingdom Centre
blurb: Riyadh's 992-ft tower, its top split by an inverted arch and spanned by a skybridge. Look for the bottle-opener shape above the city.

name: Afsluitdijk
blurb: A 20-mile dike, finished in 1932, that sealed off the Zuiderzee sea inlet and turned it into the freshwater IJsselmeer. Look for a ruler-straight line across open water, sea on one side, lake on the other.

name: Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge
blurb: The second Bosphorus bridge, opened in 1988 at the strait's narrowest point near the Rumeli Fortress. Look for the long span with the 1452 fortress walls on the European shore just south.

name: Europa-Park
blurb: Germany's largest theme park, in Rust near the French border, run by a family of ride makers. Look for coasters and themed areas in the Rhine valley.

name: King Fahd Causeway
blurb: A 16-mile causeway linking Saudi Arabia to Bahrain, opened in 1986. Look for the artificial island halfway across holding the border post and two tall towers.

name: Hockenheimring
blurb: Longtime home of the German Grand Prix. Its old layout ran miles through the forest; look for the abandoned straights, being reclaimed by trees, beside today's shorter track.

name: Hungaroring
blurb: Opened in 1986, the first Formula 1 track behind the Iron Curtain. Look for the twisty circuit in a shallow valley on the edge of Budapest, often called Monaco without the walls.

name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
blurb: Opened in 1909, the 2.5-mile oval holds about a quarter-million people, the largest seating of any sports venue. Look for the golf course holes inside the oval.

name: Yas Marina Circuit
blurb: Abu Dhabi's F1 season finale starts in daylight and ends under lights. Look for the hotel straddling the track, wrapped in a glowing lattice canopy, and the marina beside it.

name: Red Bull Ring
blurb: Home of the Austrian Grand Prix, one of the shortest F1 laps, set on a green Styrian hillside. Look for the track climbing the slope with a giant steel bull sculpture in the infield.

name: Freedom Monument
blurb: A 138-ft column in central Riga topped by a copper figure holding up three gold stars, unveiled in 1935 and left standing through Soviet rule. Look for it in the green strip along the old town canal.

name: Ibrox Stadium
blurb: Rangers' home behind a red-brick Archibald Leitch facade, with about 50,000 seats. Look for the boxy stadium south of the River Clyde in Glasgow's southwest.

name: Strawberry Arena
blurb: Sweden's national stadium in Solna, opened in 2012 as Friends Arena and renamed in 2024, with a retractable roof. Look for the big boxy roof beside the rail yards and new towers north of central Stockholm.

name: Estadio Monterrey
blurb: Monterrey's home since 2015, with an open end framing the twin-humped Cerro de la Silla mountain. Look for the silver bowl in the Guadalupe suburb, the saddle-shaped peak right behind it.

name: Chatham
blurb: The Royal Navy built ships here for over 400 years, including HMS Victory, until the dockyard closed in 1984. Look for long covered slipways and dry docks on the bend of the River Medway.

name: Russky Bridge
blurb: Its 3,622-ft main span was the longest cable-stayed span in the world when it opened in 2012, built for an APEC summit. Look for two tall A-shaped pylons linking Vladivostok to Russky Island.

name: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
blurb: Interlagos means between lakes: the track sits between two big reservoirs on São Paulo's south side. It runs counterclockwise; look for the loop hemmed in by dense city on all sides.

name: Istanbul Park
blurb: Famous for Turn 8, a long four-apex left-hander that punishes drivers' necks. Look for the track on the Asian side of Istanbul, in hilly country well east of the city.

name: Shanghai International Circuit
blurb: Its layout traces the Chinese character shang, the first syllable of Shanghai. Look for the main grandstand with two wing-like roofs bridging the track over the pit straight.

name: Cathedral of La Laguna
blurb: The cathedral of San Cristóbal de La Laguna, a town whose unwalled 1500s street grid became a model for colonial cities across the Americas. Look for the bell towers and dome in the old grid near Tenerife North airport.

name: Tivoli Gardens
blurb: Opened in 1843, one of the oldest amusement parks in the world, in central Copenhagen beside the main rail station. Look for a green garden of rides and a lake inside the city.

name: Efteling
blurb: One of Europe's oldest theme parks, opened in 1952 around a fairy-tale forest in Kaatsheuvel. Look for the forest of rides and lakes among Brabant farmland.

name: Fuji Speedway
blurb: Owned by Toyota and set at the foot of Mount Fuji, it hosted the 1976 F1 finale where James Hunt won the title in torrential rain. Look for the long main straight with the volcano behind it.

name: Tokyo Disneyland
blurb: Opened in 1983 on reclaimed land in Urayasu, the first Disney park outside the US. Look for Cinderella Castle near the shore of Tokyo Bay.

name: Buddh International Circuit
blurb: Built for the Indian Grand Prix, which ran only from 2011 to 2013. Look for the large loop in flat plains southeast of Delhi, near the Yamuna Expressway.

name: Soldier Field
blurb: Home of the Bears since 1971, built in 1924. A 2003 rebuild dropped a modern bowl inside the old colonnades; look for the glass and steel 'spaceship' between classical columns on the lakefront.

name: Estadio Benito Villamarín
blurb: Real Betis's home holds about 60,000, one of Spain's biggest grounds, and fans fill it with green and white. Look for the large bowl among the Heliópolis district beside the Guadalquivir in south Seville.

name: Stadio San Nicola
blurb: Renzo Piano's stadium for the 1990 World Cup, nicknamed the spaceship. The upper tier is split into 26 'petals' with gaps between them; look for a flower-like ring in the fields outside Bari.

name: Puskás Aréna
blurb: Budapest's 67,000-seat national stadium, opened in 2019 on the site of the old Népstadion and named for Ferenc Puskás. Look for the long arched roof and colonnade facade east of the city center.

name: Galata Bridge
blurb: Crosses the Golden Horn in Istanbul, its upper deck lined with people fishing and its lower level full of restaurants. Look for it linking the mosques of the old city to the Galata Tower side.

name: Worker and Kolkhoz Woman
blurb: An 80-ft stainless-steel pair holding a hammer and sickle aloft, made for the 1937 Paris World's Fair. Look for the silver figures striding atop a pavilion by the VDNKh entrance.

name: Dinamo Arena
blurb: Georgia's largest stadium, home of Dinamo Tbilisi, seats about 54,000. Look for the big oval bowl north of central Tbilisi.

name: La Bombonera
blurb: Boca Juniors' home, nicknamed the Chocolate Box. One side is nearly vertical, squeezed in by the neighborhood, so the stadium is D-shaped. Look for it among La Boca's dense blocks near the old port.

name: Menai Suspension Bridge
blurb: Thomas Telford's bridge to Anglesey, opened in 1826, was one of the first great suspension bridges. It was built high enough for tall sailing ships to pass beneath; look for the stone towers on the Menai Strait.

name: Sky Tower
blurb: At 1,076 ft, the tallest freestanding structure in the Southern Hemisphere. Look for the needle in Auckland's downtown on the harbor.

name: León Cathedral
blurb: A 13th-century Gothic cathedral with one of the largest collections of medieval stained glass in Europe, so much glass the walls barely seem to exist. Look for the twin spires over León's old town.

name: Mother Armenia
blurb: The 72-ft statue took the place of a giant Stalin in 1967, standing on the same tall pedestal. Look for the figure holding a sword crosswise in Victory Park, on the plateau above Yerevan.

name: Borussia-Park
blurb: Borussia Mönchengladbach's stadium, opened in 2004 on the city's southern edge. Look for the rectangular stadium standing almost alone among fields and parking lots by the autobahn.

name: Saitama Stadium 2002
blurb: Japan's largest soccer-only stadium, about 63,700 seats, home of the Urawa Reds and a 2002 World Cup semifinal venue. Look for the bowl with twin curved roofs in the rice fields north of Tokyo.

name: Hrazdan Stadium
blurb: Armenia's largest stadium, built into the side of the Hrazdan River gorge in Yerevan. Look for the bowl set into the canyon, with Mount Ararat rising to the south on a clear day.

name: Lotte World Tower
blurb: At 1,819 ft, the tallest building in South Korea. Look for the tapering glass tower beside Seoul's Lotte World park.

name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
blurb: Built by Emperor Hadrian in 134 AD to reach his mausoleum, now Castel Sant'Angelo, and lined with Bernini's angels. Look for the round fortress at its end on the Tiber.

name: Pont de Normandie
blurb: Its 2,808-ft span was the world's longest cable-stayed span when it opened in 1995. Look for two inverted-Y towers over the wide mouth of the Seine near Le Havre.

name: Bridge of the Americas
blurb: Opened in 1962, this steel arch crosses the Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal and carried the Pan-American Highway for decades. Look for ships lined up in the bay waiting their turn at the locks.

name: Bridge of the Slovak National Uprising
blurb: Locals call it the UFO bridge: a single slanted pylon topped by a saucer-shaped restaurant about 280 ft up. It crosses the Danube directly below Bratislava Castle; look for the white square castle on its hill.

name: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
blurb: Kim Il Sung's former official residence, now the mausoleum where he and Kim Jong Il lie embalmed. Look for the huge pale building behind a vast plaza and moat on the northeast side of Pyongyang.

name: Daegu Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2002 World Cup and host of the 2011 World Athletics Championships. Look for the big bowl with a white roof canopy in Suseong district on the city's east side.

name: Eden Park
blurb: New Zealand's biggest stadium hosted the Rugby World Cup final in both 1987 and 2011; the All Blacks won both. Look for it in Auckland's inner suburbs, between volcanic cones.

name: Salt Lake Stadium
blurb: Kolkata's giant, once listed at about 120,000 seats and still one of India's largest at roughly 68,000. Look for the huge oval in the planned grid of Salt Lake City.

name: Williamsburg Bridge
blurb: The world's longest suspension span when it opened in 1903, with steel towers rather than stone. Look for it crossing the East River from the Lower East Side to Williamsburg.

name: Danube Bridge
blurb: A double-deck road and rail truss across the Danube between Ruse and Giurgiu, for decades the only bridge linking Bulgaria and Romania. Look for its long steel line over the river.

name: Port of Singapore
blurb: One of the busiest ports on Earth. Look for hundreds of ships at anchor in the strait, waiting their turn, and cranes stretching along the south shore.

name: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
blurb: About 22 miles long, opened in 2008 in an S-shaped curve across the muddy bay. Look for the service platform with a tower near the middle, an island built for drivers to rest.

name: Alcántara Bridge
blurb: A Roman bridge built around 104 to 106 AD under Emperor Trajan, still standing over the Tagus with a triumphal arch at its center. Look for the stone arches just below a big modern dam and reservoir.

name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
blurb: A gray granite tomb completed in 1975 and modeled on Lenin's, holding Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body. Look for the boxy building facing the big green lawns of Ba Dinh Square.

name: Humber Bridge
blurb: When it opened in 1981 its 4,626-ft main span was the longest single span in the world, a record it held for 16 years. Look for the slender towers over the wide brown estuary near Hull.

name: Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Bridge
blurb: About 16 miles long across Jiaozhou Bay, it was among the longest bridges over water in the world when it opened in 2011. Look for a T-shaped junction where its arms split in the middle of the bay.

name: Öland Bridge
blurb: About 3.8 miles long, opened in 1972 from Kalmar to the island of Öland. Look for the hump near the mainland end where it rises high for shipping, with Kalmar Castle on the shore.

name: Si-o-se Pol
blurb: A two-level Safavid bridge of 33 arches built around 1602. The Zayandeh River beneath it is often dry now, so look for the long arcade crossing a sandy riverbed in Isfahan.

name: Seoul World Cup Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2002 World Cup, Asia's largest football-only stadium at the time. Its roof is shaped like a traditional Korean shield kite; look for it beside the Han River near the green mounds of Haneul Park, a former landfill.

name: 25 de Abril Bridge
blurb: A red suspension bridge from 1966 that people mistake for the Golden Gate, with a 3,323-ft main span and trains on a lower deck. Look for the Cristo Rei statue on the hill at its south end.

name: New Europe Bridge
blurb: The second bridge between Bulgaria and Romania, opened in 2013 between Vidin and Calafat. Look for a cable-stayed span over a wide stretch of the Danube.

name: The Iron Bridge
blurb: Built in 1779, the world's first major bridge made of cast iron, spanning the Severn in a wooded gorge. Its single arch gave Ironbridge its name and stands at the heart of a World Heritage Site.

name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
blurb: A white hall about 230 ft tall under a blue octagonal roof, finished in 1980, at the end of a vast plaza flanked by a theater and a concert hall. Look for the white-and-blue block at the head of the long plaza.

name: Aljafería
blurb: An 11th-century Islamic palace built by Zaragoza's Muslim kings, later a royal palace for Ferdinand and Isabella and now home of Aragon's parliament. Look for the square fortified walls and towers set in a green park.

name: Basilica of Candelaria
blurb: Shrine of the Virgin of Candelaria, patron saint of the Canary Islands, on a seafront plaza lined with bronze statues of Guanche kings. Look for the white basilica and broad plaza on Tenerife's east coast.

name: Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium
blurb: Córdoba's 57,000-seat stadium, built for the 1978 World Cup and named for that tournament's top scorer. Look for the big bowl in the park on the city's southwest side.

name: Workers Stadium
blurb: Beijing's football stadium, opened in 1959 and rebuilt from scratch in 2020 to 2023 as a modern football ground for Beijing Guoan. Look for the rectangular bowl in the Sanlitun area east of the center.

name: Tokyo Dome
blurb: The Big Egg, home of the Yomiuri Giants since 1988, holds its fabric roof up with air pressure. Look for the white dome beside a roller coaster that loops through a building.

name: Tsing Ma Bridge
blurb: A double-deck suspension bridge carrying road and rail to Hong Kong's airport, with a span of about 4,500 ft. Look for its towers between Tsing Yi and Ma Wan islands.

name: Confederation Bridge
blurb: About 8 miles long, the longest bridge in the world over ice-covered water, linking Prince Edward Island to the mainland since 1997. Look for a gently curving line across the Northumberland Strait.

name: The STRAT Hotel, Casino & SkyPod
blurb: At 1,149 ft, the tallest observation tower in the US. Look for the spire at the north end of the Las Vegas Strip.

name: Tian Tan Buddha
blurb: A 112-ft bronze Buddha on a hilltop on Lantau Island, close to Hong Kong's airport. Look for the seated figure on the ridge at the top of 268 steps, with the cable car climbing from Tung Chung.

name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
blurb: A 170-ft monument shaped like a ship's prow, with Henry the Navigator leading the explorers. Look for the white prow on the Tagus and the giant compass rose set in the pavement.

name: Spire of Dublin
blurb: A stainless-steel needle about 390 ft tall on O'Connell Street, put up in 2003 where Nelson's Pillar stood until the IRA blew it up in 1966. Look for a thin glint above the city center.

name: Chapel Bridge
blurb: Europe's oldest covered wooden bridge, built in the 1300s, badly burned in 1993 and restored. It angles across the Reuss beside an octagonal stone Water Tower where the river leaves Lake Lucerne.

name: State Farm Stadium
blurb: The Arizona Cardinals' home has both a retractable roof and a grass field that rolls outside on a tray to soak up sun. Look for the silver drum in Glendale, sometimes with the field sitting beside it.

name: Donghai Bridge
blurb: About 20 miles long, opened in 2005 to link Shanghai with the Yangshan deep-water port on offshore islands. Look for an S-curving line across the muddy brown East China Sea.

name: First Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1994 as the first bridge across the lower Mekong, linking Nong Khai to Vientiane. A railway runs down the middle of the road. Look for the wide brown Mekong separating Thailand and Laos.

name: Rio–Niterói Bridge
blurb: About 8.3 miles long across Guanabara Bay, opened in 1974; its center rises in a hump so ships can pass. Look for the long line from Rio's port toward Niterói, with Sugarloaf at the bay's mouth.

name: Queensboro Bridge
blurb: The 59th Street Bridge, a 1909 cantilever that crosses Roosevelt Island without touching down on it. Look for the red aerial tram running alongside it.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica of the Holy Saviour, Oviedo
blurb: A Gothic cathedral whose Holy Chamber holds relics that drew medieval pilgrims, and the starting point of the Camino Primitivo, the oldest route to Santiago. Look for its single tall spire over Oviedo's old town.

name: Segovia Cathedral
blurb: The last great Gothic cathedral built in Spain, begun in 1525 and nicknamed the Lady of Cathedrals. Look for the golden stone and tall tower on Segovia's ridge, with the Alcázar at the ridge's tip.

name: Lang Park
blurb: Better known by sponsor names like Suncorp Stadium, home of the Brisbane Broncos and the Queensland side in State of Origin rugby league. Look for the rectangular stadium just west of the city center.

name: Dodger Stadium
blurb: Opened in 1962 and cut into Chavez Ravine, it's the third-oldest park in the majors and has the largest seating capacity in baseball, about 56,000. Look for the bowl set among hills and parking lots just north of downtown.

name: Northwest Stadium
blurb: Home of the Washington Commanders since 1997, in Landover, Maryland, ringed by parking lots. Look for the big open bowl beside the Capital Beltway east of D.C.

name: Murrayfield Stadium
blurb: Scotland's largest stadium, about 67,000 seats, home of Scottish rugby. Look for the big open bowl west of Edinburgh's center, beside the Water of Leith.

name: Allegiant Stadium
blurb: The Raiders' $1.9 billion domed stadium, opened in 2020 just west of the Strip across I-15. Look for the glossy black roof next to Mandalay Bay and the giant curved 'lanai' wall of windows facing the Strip.

name: Gamla bron
blurb: The old bridge in Umeå, one of the crossings of the wide Ume River through the center of the city. Look for the river splitting the grid of northern Sweden's largest town.

name: Albert Bridge
blurb: A pink and pastel bridge from 1873 in Chelsea, nicknamed the Trembling Lady; signs still tell marching troops to break step. At night some 4,000 bulbs outline its cables over the Thames.

name: Pamplona Cathedral
blurb: A Gothic interior behind a neoclassical front, in the old town best known for the July running of the bulls. Look for the twin towers on the north edge of the old town above the Arga river.

name: Cathedral Basilica of the Virgin of Incarnation
blurb: Málaga's cathedral is nicknamed La Manquita, the one-armed lady, because its second tower was never finished. Look for one full tower beside a stump, a few blocks from the port.

name: Shizuoka Stadium
blurb: Ecopa, a 50,000-seat stadium built for the 2002 World Cup, in the hills of Fukuroi. Look for the big white crescent roof set in green woodland.

name: Nissan Stadium
blurb: The Titans' stadium sits on the east bank of the Cumberland, facing downtown Nashville. A new enclosed stadium is going up next door. Look for the open bowl across the river from the skyline.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium
blurb: Built for the 1982 Asian Games and given a white membrane roof for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, it's one of India's biggest stadiums. Look for the oval of white canopy in south-central Delhi.

name: Rainbow Bridge
blurb: A suspension bridge across Tokyo Bay to the artificial island of Odaiba, opened in 1993. Look for its white towers and, at night, the lights along its cables.

name: Huajiang Canyon Bridge
blurb: The world's highest bridge, opened in 2025 with its deck about 2,000 ft above the Beipan River. Look for a thin line slung across a deep gorge in Guizhou's karst hills.

name: Tacoma Narrows Bridge (2007)
blurb: The eastbound twin of the 1950 bridge that replaced Galloping Gertie, which twisted itself apart in the wind in 1940, four months after opening. Look for two parallel suspension spans over the Narrows.

name: Mária Valéria Bridge
blurb: Links Štúrovo in Slovakia to Esztergom in Hungary. Blown up in 1944, it stayed broken until 2001. Look for the huge domed Esztergom Basilica on the hill at the Hungarian end.

name: Glienicke Bridge
blurb: The Bridge of Spies: during the Cold War the US and Soviets swapped captured agents here, starting with U-2 pilot Gary Powers in 1962. Look for a green steel bridge over the Havel between Berlin and Potsdam.

name: Britannia Bridge
blurb: Robert Stephenson's 1850 tubular railway bridge to Anglesey burned in 1970 and was rebuilt with a road deck added above the tracks. Look for it a mile from Telford's suspension bridge on the Menai Strait.

name: Silesian Stadium
blurb: Poland's 'Witches' Cauldron' in Chorzów, once the national team's home, now with a roof over the stands. Look for it inside the large Silesian Park, a green island in the industrial Katowice sprawl.

name: Camping World Stadium
blurb: Orlando's old Citrus Bowl, opened in 1936 and rebuilt several times, still hosts bowl games. Look for the big bowl west of downtown Orlando, next to Lake Lorna Doone.

name: Acrisure Stadium
blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers' stadium on the North Shore, near where the Allegheny and Monongahela join to form the Ohio. Look for the open-ended bowl facing downtown across the river.

name: Stone Bridge in Skopje
blurb: A stone bridge over the Vardar from the Ottoman era, the symbol of Skopje. Look for its arches joining the main square to the old bazaar on the north bank.

name: Pelješac Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2022 to connect southern Dalmatia to the rest of Croatia without crossing Bosnia's short coast at Neum. Look for its cable-stayed span over the blue Mali Ston Bay.

name: Quebec Bridge
blurb: Still the longest cantilever span in the world at 1,800 ft, it collapsed twice during construction (1907 and 1916), killing 89 people before it opened in 1917. Look for the giant steel truss over the St. Lawrence west of Quebec City.

name: Lugou Bridge
blurb: The Marco Polo Bridge, carved with hundreds of stone lions, dates to the 1190s. A 1937 clash here began the full Sino-Japanese War. Look for the stone arches over the Yongding River.

name: Paton Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1953 over the Dnieper in Kyiv, it was the first all-welded bridge in the world, named for the welding engineer who built it. Look for the long low span across the wide river.

name: Burapha Withi Expressway
blurb: An elevated expressway on concrete pillars running about 34 miles east from Bangkok over the Bang Na road, among the longest bridges in the world. Look for the endless straight line heading toward the Gulf coast.

name: Incheon Munhak Sports Complex
blurb: Incheon's original sports complex, which hosted 2002 World Cup matches. Look for the stadium and baseball park side by side in the city's center.

name: Tianjin Olympic Center Stadium
blurb: Tianjin's 2008 Olympic football venue is nicknamed the Water Drop for its rounded shape, and it sits beside a lake. Look for the shiny teardrop roof reflected in the water in the city's southwest.

name: National Stadium
blurb: Its retractable roof is one of the largest domes in the world, a single span of about 1,000 ft. Look for the silver shell at Kallang on the waterfront east of the Marina Bay skyline.

name: José Amalfitani Stadium
blurb: Vélez Sarsfield's home in Liniers, a 1978 World Cup venue. Look for the bowl beside the rail line on the western edge of Buenos Aires.

name: Raymond James Stadium
blurb: The Buccaneers' home, famous for the 103-ft pirate ship in the north end zone that fires cannons on touchdowns. Look for the ship beside the stadium, just east of Tampa International.

name: Severn Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1966 with an aerodynamic box deck that set the pattern for suspension bridges worldwide. Look for it crossing the Severn and Wye mouths, with the newer Prince of Wales Bridge a few miles downstream.

name: Guri Dam
blurb: One of the largest hydro plants in the world, supplying most of Venezuela's electricity from the Caroní River. Its lake, Guri, is one of South America's biggest reservoirs; look for dark water flooding savanna and forest.

name: Atatürk Dam
blurb: Turkey's largest dam, a huge rockfill wall on the Euphrates finished in 1990. Its lake sends water through tunnels to irrigate the Harran plain; look for a big, branching reservoir in bare hills.

name: Erasmusbrug
blurb: Nicknamed the Swan for its bent white pylon, it opened in 1996 across the Maas in Rotterdam. Look for it beneath the towers of the Kop van Zuid.

name: Megyeri Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge on the M0 ring road at Budapest's northern edge, opened in 2008. Look for its inverted-Y towers over the Danube and Szentendre Island.

name: EverBank Stadium
blurb: The Jaguars' stadium on the St. Johns River, once known for its giant end-zone video boards and a pool deck in the stands. Look for the bowl right on the riverbank, east of downtown Jacksonville.

name: Great Strahov Stadium
blurb: Built for mass gymnastics displays, it's the largest stadium in the world by area, with a field big enough for several full-size soccer pitches. Sparta Prague now uses it for training. Look for the vast rectangle on the hill above the castle.

name: Mohammed V Stadium
blurb: Casablanca's main ground, home to the fierce Wydad and Raja derby, one of the loudest rivalries in African football. Look for the big concrete bowl in the dense city grid of the Maarif district.

name: Mosul Dam
blurb: Iraq's largest dam, built on soluble gypsum that needs constant grouting; US engineers once called it the most dangerous dam in the world. ISIS briefly seized it in 2014. Look for a long earthen dam across the Tigris.

name: New Little Belt Bridge
blurb: A 1970 suspension bridge carrying the motorway between Jutland and Funen. Look for its white towers spanning the narrow Little Belt strait.

name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
blurb: Designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel and finished after his death, opening in 1864. It hangs about 245 ft above the Avon Gorge; look for the stone towers spanning the steep wooded cliffs in Bristol.

name: Duge Bridge
blurb: Its deck hangs about 1,850 ft above the Beipan River, the highest bridge in the world from 2016 until a nearby rival opened in 2025. Look for the thin span between the walls of a deep karst gorge.

name: Suramadu Bridge
blurb: About 3.4 miles long, the longest bridge in Indonesia, linking Surabaya on Java to the island of Madura since 2009. Look for its cable-stayed center span over the Madura Strait.

name: Palace Bridge
blurb: A bascule bridge over the Neva beside the Hermitage, raised at night in the warm months so ships can pass. Look for it linking the Winter Palace to Vasilyevsky Island.

name: Commonwealth Stadium
blurb: Home of the CFL's Edmonton Elks and, at about 56,000 seats, the largest open-air stadium in Canada. Look for the big oval bowl just northeast of downtown, beside the river valley.

name: Lucas Oil Stadium
blurb: The Colts' retractable-roof stadium, opened in 2008 and host of Super Bowl XLVI. Look for the brick box with a huge window wall framing the downtown Indianapolis skyline.

name: Coors Field
blurb: The Rockies' park in LoDo, opened in 1995. Thin air makes it the most hitter-friendly park in baseball, and one row of purple seats in the upper deck marks exactly one mile above sea level.

name: Estadio Único Diego Armando Maradona
blurb: La Plata's Estadio Único, renamed for Maradona after his death in 2020, has a roof of white membranes on two linked rings. Look for the double-loop roof on the northwest side of the city.

name: Felix Houphouet Boigny Stadium
blurb: Abidjan's historic stadium, in the Plateau business district by the Ébrié Lagoon. Look for the oval right beside the lagoon and the downtown towers.

name: Stade Ahmadou Ahidjo
blurb: Cameroon's national stadium in Yaoundé, home to the Indomitable Lions for decades and a venue when Cameroon hosted the Africa Cup of Nations in 2022. Look for the oval bowl among the city's green hills.

name: Jalisco Stadium
blurb: Home of Atlas, a venue for both the 1970 and 1986 World Cups. Look for the big open bowl in northern Guadalajara, packed into city blocks.

name: The Helix Bridge
blurb: A footbridge on Marina Bay whose steel tubes twist in a double helix, inspired by DNA. Look for it near the Marina Bay Sands towers and their boat-shaped rooftop.

name: Gariep Dam
blurb: Holds back South Africa's largest reservoir, on the Orange River in the dry Karoo. Look for a big, branching lake in flat, tawny country.

name: Belo Monte Dam
blurb: One of the largest hydro plants on Earth by capacity, and one of the most contested, on the Xingu River in the Amazon. It diverts water away from the river's Big Bend; look for canals and reservoirs cut through rainforest.

name: Saint Petersburg Dam
blurb: A flood barrier about 15 miles long across the Gulf of Finland, carrying a ring road through Kronstadt island. Look for a long line of embankments across the bay with a ship gate in the middle.

name: Eshima Ohashi Bridge
blurb: Telephoto photos made it look like a near-vertical ramp, but its real slope is about 6 percent. Look for the high hump lifting over Lake Nakaumi between Eshima island and the port city of Sakaiminato.

name: Hammersmith Bridge
blurb: Joseph Bazalgette's ornate green suspension bridge from 1887, closed to cars since 2019 over cracks. It overlooks the Thames stretch used for the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.

name: Osmangazi Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2016 across the Gulf of Izmit, with a main span of about 5,090 ft, one of the longest in the world. It cut a long drive around the bay to a few minutes.

name: Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge
blurb: Joins Dandong in China to Sinuiju in North Korea across the Yalu. Next to it stands the Broken Bridge, bombed in the Korean War. At night, look for bright Dandong facing a nearly dark shore.

name: Samuel Beckett Bridge
blurb: Santiago Calatrava designed it in the shape of a harp lying on its side, a symbol of Ireland. It can swing 90 degrees to let boats pass; look for the white curving pylon over the Liffey.

name: Friendship Bridge
blurb: Links Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil to Ciudad del Este in Paraguay with a single concrete arch over the Paraná gorge. Look for the busy border city crowding the Paraguayan end.

name: Roman Bridge (Trier)
blurb: The oldest bridge in Germany still in use, its stone piers built by the Romans in the second century. Look for its arches crossing the Moselle at Trier.

name: Ponte Pietra
blurb: A Roman bridge in Verona, blown up by retreating Germans in 1945 and rebuilt from stones pulled out of the Adige. Look for it on the river's tight bend by the old town.

name: Pulteney Bridge
blurb: Designed by Robert Adam and finished in 1774, one of the few bridges in the world lined with shops on both sides. Look for the curved, stepped weir in the Avon just below it.

name: Europabrücke
blurb: Carries the Brenner motorway about 600 ft above the Sill valley south of Innsbruck, Europe's highest bridge when it opened in 1963. Look for its tall concrete piers striding across the valley.

name: Shenyang Olympic Sports Center Stadium
blurb: Built for 2008 Olympic soccer, about 60,000 seats under a crystal-like roof. Look for the faceted white shell in Shenyang's newer southern district.

name: Gaddafi Stadium
blurb: Lahore's main cricket ground, opened in 1959 and renamed for Libya's Muammar Gaddafi in 1974. Look for the oval in the center of the city.

name: Paycor Stadium
blurb: Home of the Cincinnati Bengals since 2000, right on the Ohio River with Kentucky across the water. Look for the open stadium with high side canopies on the riverbank west of downtown.

name: Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium
blurb: Rabat's national stadium, torn down and rebuilt for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations as a football-only arena of about 69,000 seats. Look for it inside a large sports complex surrounded by green space on the city's south side.

name: Dyke Kokaral
blurb: A 2005 dike that sealed off the North Aral Sea from the dying southern basin. Water levels rose and fish returned to a lake many had written off. Look for a thin line separating blue water from dry salt flats.

name: Karakaya Dam
blurb: A concrete arch dam on the Euphrates in eastern Turkey, between Keban and Atatürk on the river's staircase of reservoirs. Look for a long lake winding through arid canyons.

name: Arena do Grêmio
blurb: Grêmio's home since 2012, in the north of Porto Alegre near the Guaíba. Look for the boxy stadium with a translucent roof among low-lying neighborhoods.

name: Olympic Stadium of Radès
blurb: Tunisia's biggest stadium, built for the 2001 Mediterranean Games south of Tunis, holds about 60,000. Look for the large bowl in the Radès sports city near the Gulf of Tunis.

name: Estádio 11 de Novembro
