blurb: Angola's national stadium, named for its independence day and built for the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations. Look for the large bowl on Luanda's southern outskirts.

name: Lagos National Stadium
blurb: Built in Surulere for the 1973 All-Africa Games, once the heart of Nigerian football, later left to decay for years. Look for the big concrete bowl amid Lagos mainland's dense sprawl.

name: Mangla Dam
blurb: One of the world's largest earth-fill dams, built on the Jhelum River in the 1960s at the edge of the Himalayan foothills. Look for a big, many-armed reservoir filling the valleys.

name: National Stadium
blurb: Kaohsiung's World Games stadium, designed by Toyo Ito, curls like a dragon, and its roof is covered in about 8,800 solar panels. Look for the open C-shaped bowl in the northern suburbs.

name: Hiroshima Big Arch
blurb: Built for the 1994 Asian Games and named for its big arch-shaped roof. Look for the stadium in wooded hills northwest of central Hiroshima.

name: Abuja Stadium
blurb: Nigeria's 60,000-seat national stadium in Abuja, opened in 2003. Look for the bowl with its sweeping roof on the southwest side of the planned capital, with granite inselbergs around the city.

name: El Cilindro
blurb: Racing Club's home in Avellaneda, nicknamed the Cylinder for its round concrete shape. It sits a few blocks from rival Independiente's stadium; look for the two grounds almost side by side.

name: Keban Dam
blurb: The first of the big dams on the Euphrates, finished in 1974 just below where the Karasu and Murat rivers join. Look for a huge reservoir with arms reaching into dry mountains.

name: Banqiao Dam
blurb: Its 1975 failure in a typhoon set off one of the deadliest floods in history; estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to over 200,000. The rebuilt dam stands in the hills of southern Henan.

name: Perth Stadium
blurb: Perth's 60,000-seat stadium, opened in 2018 on the Burswood peninsula. Look for the bronze-colored shell inside a loop of the Swan River across from downtown.

name: Yadegar-e Emam Stadium
blurb: Tabriz's big stadium, home of Tractor, a club with one of Iran's loudest followings. Look for the open bowl on the city's edge in the high plain below Mount Sahand.

name: Thuwunna Stadium
blurb: Myanmar's national stadium in Yangon, a large open bowl that hosted the 2013 Southeast Asian Games opening events. Look for it east of the city center inside a sprawling sports complex.

name: Newlands Stadium
blurb: The Stormers' historic rugby home below Table Mountain hosted a Test as early as 1891, but rugby moved out in 2021 and a planned sale for redevelopment has stalled. Look for the old stands among leafy southern suburbs.

name: Stade Léopold Sédar Senghor
blurb: Dakar's national stadium, built in the 1980s as the Stadium of Friendship and renovated in recent years, where Senegal's national team plays its biggest games. Look for the big open bowl in the dense city near the old Yoff airport runways.

name: Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium
blurb: Kuwait's 60,000-seat national stadium, with a sweeping roof over the stands. Look for the large oval on the flat desert edge west of Kuwait City.

name: José María Minella Stadium
blurb: Mar del Plata's stadium, built for the 1978 World Cup, in the beach resort city on the Atlantic. Look for the bowl in the sports park a few miles inland from the coast.

name: Alassane Ouattara Stadium
blurb: Also called the Olympic Stadium of Ebimpé, it seats about 60,000 and hosted the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations final, won by Côte d'Ivoire. Look for the bowl with its sweeping roof north of Abidjan.

name: Benjamin Mkapa National Stadium
blurb: Tanzania's national stadium, opened in 2007 and built with Chinese help, holds about 60,000. Look for a large open bowl in Dar es Salaam's south side, beside the older Uhuru Stadium.

name: Olympic Stadium
blurb: Designed by Cambodian architect Vann Molyvann and opened in 1964, it never hosted an Olympics despite the name. Look for the big oval earthwork bowl with an indoor arena at one end, in central Phnom Penh.

name: Estadio Pedro Bidegain
blurb: San Lorenzo's home since 1993, called the New Gasómetro, in Bajo Flores. Look for the large concrete bowl surrounded by open land on the south side of Buenos Aires.

name: Tripoli Stadium International
blurb: Tripoli's main stadium, where Libya's biggest clubs and the national team play. Look for the large open bowl in the city south of the old port.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium
blurb: Kochi's big stadium at Kaloor, home of Kerala Blasters and once a cricket ground too, known for its loud yellow-clad crowds. Look for the bowl in the city's dense center.

name: Trepča Mines
blurb: A lead and zinc complex near Mitrovica worked since Roman times, once the backbone of Yugoslavia's mining industry. Look for mine buildings and waste heaps along the valley.

name: Moi International Sports Centre
blurb: Kasarani, Kenya's largest stadium, built for the 1987 All-Africa Games, about 60,000 seats. Look for the big open bowl beside the Thika highway in northeast Nairobi.

name: Estadio Monumental de Maturín
blurb: Built for the 2007 Copa América, it is one of the largest stadiums in Venezuela, on the edge of Maturín. Look for a big oval set in open savanna.

name: Wuhan Sports Center
blurb: A big sports complex in Wuhan's southwest suburbs with a main stadium of about 54,000 seats. Look for the oval roof shell and surrounding arenas near the Yangtze.

name: Shenzhen Universiade Sports Centre
blurb: Main stadium of the 2011 Summer Universiade, its roof a faceted shell of triangles that makes it look like a giant crystal. Look for the glittering white polygon in Longgang.

name: Estádio Serra Dourada
blurb: Goiânia's big stadium, opened in 1975 and once among Brazil's largest. Look for the large concrete oval in the planned capital of Goiás state.

name: Estádio do Arruda
blurb: Santa Cruz's home in Recife, one of Brazil's larger stadiums. Look for the big open concrete bowl in the dense northern neighborhoods.

name: Faro
blurb: A lead and zinc mine that once supported the town of Faro and closed in 1998, leaving one of Canada's largest mine cleanups. Look for the pits and tailings in the forested Pelly valley.

name: Bois du Cazier
blurb: Site of Belgium's worst mining disaster: a 1956 fire that killed 262 miners, many of them Italian immigrants. Look for the steel headframes standing over the old colliery at Marcinelle near Charleroi.

name: Erdenet Mining Corporation
blurb: One of the largest copper mines in Asia; the city of Erdenet was built around it in the 1970s with Soviet help. Look for the terraced pit and gray tailings on the steppe.

name: Kolubara lignite mines
blurb: Heart of the Kolubara lignite fields that feed Belgrade's power stations. Look for wide gray open-cut strips and spoil terraces in the flat farmland southwest of the city.

name: Sado Mine
blurb: Gold and silver were mined here from 1601 for nearly 400 years. Look for the Doyu no Warito, a mountain split in two by hand digging, on the west coast of Sado Island.

name: Huanglong Sports Center
blurb: Hangzhou's older sports center, a stadium with a dramatic cable-supported roof near the West Lake hills. Look for the bowl in the city's northwest, close to green hills.

name: Gelora Bung Tomo Stadium
blurb: Surabaya's big stadium, home of Persebaya and a venue for the 2023 U-17 World Cup. Look for the bowl surrounded by fish ponds and fields on the city's western edge.

name: Stadium at Olympia
blurb: The original Olympic stadium, used for the ancient games from at least the 5th century BC. Look for the rectangular grassy track with earth banks, entered through a stone tunnel next to the ruins of Zeus's temple.

name: Plovdiv Stadium
blurb: Bulgaria's second city's big stadium, opened in 1950 in the Rowing Canal park. Look for the oval beside the long straight rowing canal on the west side of Plovdiv.

name: Jinan Olympic Sports Center Stadium
blurb: Built for China's 2009 National Games, the main stadium's swept roof is meant to look like willow leaves, paired with a lotus-shaped arena: "East Lotus, West Willow." Look for the white leaf-shaped shell on Jinan's east side.

name: Stade du 26 Mars
blurb: Mali's 50,000-seat national stadium, built for the 2002 Africa Cup of Nations and named for the 1991 uprising. Look for it south of the Niger River in Bamako.

name: Stade 24 Fevrier 1956
blurb: The main stadium of Sidi Bel Abbès in western Algeria, home of the local club USM Bel Abbès. Look for the oval among the town's tight streets and farmland.

name: Ekana Cricket Stadium
blurb: One of India's largest cricket grounds, in Lucknow, and home of the Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL. Look for a big oval of green ringed by stands.

name: National Heroes Stadium
blurb: Zambia's national stadium, about 60,000 seats, opened in 2014 on the northwest side of Lusaka. Look for the large bowl on open ground at the city's edge.

name: Mogadishu Stadium
blurb: Built with Chinese help in the late 1970s, it was overrun and used as a militia base during Somalia's long civil war, and has since been brought back for football. Look for a big open bowl in the sandy, low-rise city.

name: Jwaneng diamond mine
blurb: Often called the richest diamond mine in the world by value. Look for the huge terraced open pit and pale waste dumps in the flat scrub of the Kalahari.

name: Berkeley Pit
blurb: A former copper pit about a mile across and roughly 1,800 ft deep, now flooding with acidic, metal-laden water. In 2016 thousands of snow geese died after landing on it. Look for the rust-red lake beside Butte.

name: Grand Hornu
blurb: An early-1800s coal mining complex built as a planned town, with workshops around a grand oval courtyard and rows of miners' houses. It's now a contemporary art museum; look for the oval in the brick village.

name: Sotk gold mine
blurb: A gold deposit on a high ridge straddling the Armenia-Azerbaijan border, east of Lake Sevan. Look for open-pit terraces and waste heaps scarring the bare mountainside.

name: Miike coal mine
blurb: A huge Mitsui coal mine at Omuta, part of Japan's Meiji industrial heritage, where a 1963 explosion killed 458 miners. Look for the old pitheads and the coal port on the Ariake Sea.

name: Ghadir Stadium
blurb: A large modern stadium in Ahvaz, the oil city on the Karun River in Iran's southwest. Look for the oval bowl on the flat, dusty Khuzestan plain.

name: National Sports Stadium
blurb: Zimbabwe's national stadium in Harare, about 60,000 seats, built with Chinese help in the 1980s. Look for the big oval west of the city center.

name: Estádio Parque do Sabiá
blurb: Uberlândia's big municipal stadium, set inside a large park. Look for the bowl among trees and lakes on the city's east side.

name: Pascua Lama
blurb: A gold and silver project straddling the Chile-Argentina border at high Andean altitude, halted after fights over damage to nearby glaciers. Look for roads and earthworks scraped into bare mountains.

name: Super Pit gold mine
blurb: Kalgoorlie's Fimiston Open Pit, about 2 miles long and over 1,600 ft deep, swallowed dozens of old underground gold mines. Look for the vast terraced gash on the edge of town.

name: Premier Mine
blurb: The Cullinan, the largest jewel-quality diamond ever found at 3,106 carats, came out of this pipe in 1905. Look for the big open hole beside the town of Cullinan.

name: The Sevens
blurb: Home of the Dubai Rugby Sevens, one of the sport's biggest annual parties, out in the desert on the road to Al Ain. Look for a cluster of green pitches in sand.

name: Yanacocha
blurb: The largest gold mine in South America, spread over bare highlands near Cajamarca at roughly 11,500 to 13,500 ft. Look for leach pads and pits carved across the puna.

name: Argyle diamond mine
blurb: Source of most of the world's pink diamonds until it closed in 2020. Look for the pit and dumps in red Kimberley ranges near Lake Argyle.

name: Rössing uranium mine
blurb: One of the longest-running open-pit uranium mines in the world, working the Namib Desert since 1976. Look for the huge terraced pit and pale waste dumps in bare rock and sand.

name: Escondida Mine
blurb: The world's largest copper mine by output, at around 10,000 ft in the Atacama Desert. Look for terraced pits, tailings and roads spread across the empty brown desert.

name: Catoca diamond mine
blurb: One of the largest diamond mines in the world, an open pit dug into a kimberlite pipe in northeastern Angola. Look for the round terraced pit in the savanna.

name: Oyu Tolgoi mine
blurb: A giant copper and gold mine in the South Gobi, one of the largest copper deposits found anywhere, much of it now worked by underground block caving. Look for the plant and tailings dam in empty desert.

name: Williamson diamond mine
blurb: One of the world's longest-running diamond mines, opened by John Williamson in 1940. It produced the pink diamond given to Princess Elizabeth as a wedding gift. Look for the pit and pale tailings near Shinyanga.

name: Mines of Laurium
blurb: Silver from these ancient mines paid for the Athenian fleet that beat the Persians at Salamis in 480 BC. Look for old spoil heaps and shafts in the hills near the southeastern tip of Attica.

name: Iron Knob
blurb: Iron ore was dug from this hill from the late 1890s, among Australia's earliest iron mines. Look for the stepped, reddish scars cut into an isolated hill on dry plains.

name: Kiruna Mine
blurb: The largest underground iron ore mine in the world, so big the town above it is being moved east to escape subsidence. Look for the dark Kiirunavaara ridge and its tailings next to town.

name: Ashio Copper Mine
blurb: The site of Japan's first major pollution disaster in the 1890s, when smelter fumes stripped the surrounding hills bare. Look for the mountainsides near Nikko still patchy with replanted forest.

name: Stade Tata Raphaël
blurb: Kinshasa's old stadium, where Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman in the 1974 Rumble in the Jungle. Look for the open oval near the Stade des Martyrs.

name: General Lansana Conté Stadium
blurb: A Chinese-built national stadium on the outskirts of Conakry, holding about 50,000. Look for the large bowl standing out in low-rise neighborhoods on Guinea's narrow coastal peninsula.

name: Bahir Dar Stadium
blurb: A big new stadium in Bahir Dar, the city at the south end of Lake Tana where the Blue Nile begins. Look for the bowl on the city's edge, with the big lake just to the north.

name: Estadio Latinoamericano
blurb: Havana's baseball cathedral, home of Industriales, opened in 1946 and where Obama and Raúl Castro watched the Rays play Cuba in 2016. Look for the big bowl in the Cerro district.

name: Semple Stadium
blurb: The spiritual home of hurling in Thurles, holding about 45,000 and famed for its Munster finals. Look for the big open ground in a small Tipperary town surrounded by farmland.

name: Palaran Stadium
blurb: Built in Samarinda for Indonesia's 2008 national games, a big bowl far out on the edge of the city. Look for it in green country near the Mahakam River in East Kalimantan.

name: Dalian Suoyuwan Football Stadium
blurb: A new soccer stadium on the Dalian waterfront at Suoyuwan bay, built for the 2023 Asian Cup that China later gave up. Look for the bowl right on the harbor edge.

name: Tavan Tolgoi
blurb: One of the world's largest untapped coking coal deposits, in the South Gobi. Look for open-cut pits and haul roads etched into the flat tan desert.

name: Diavik Diamond Mine
blurb: Diamonds mined from pipes under Lac de Gras, held back by dikes so the pits sit below lake level. Look for the island and its ring-walled pits in a land of countless lakes.

name: Olympic Dam mine
blurb: One of the largest uranium deposits in the world, also mined for copper and gold, mostly underground. Look for the processing plant and huge tailings ponds in red desert.

name: Ngwenya Mine
blurb: One of the oldest known mines in the world, where people dug red ochre tens of thousands of years ago; it was later worked for iron ore. Look for the reddish scars on a hillside near the South African border.

name: Rufaro Stadium
blurb: Where Bob Marley played at Zimbabwe's independence celebrations in 1980. Look for a modest stadium in Mbare, south of downtown Harare.

name: Hocine-Ait Ahmed Stadium
blurb: A new 50,000-seat stadium in Tizi Ouzou, home of JS Kabylie, one of Algeria's most successful clubs, set below the Djurdjura mountains. Look for the bright modern bowl on the edge of town.

name: Orapa diamond mine
blurb: One of the largest diamond mines in the world by area, opened in 1971 on the edge of the Kalahari. Look for the open pit and its company town in the flat bush west of the Makgadikgadi salt pans.

name: Aitik
blurb: One of Europe's largest open-pit copper mines, near Gällivare just north of the Arctic Circle. Look for the long terraced pit and vast tailings dams in the forest.

name: Ekati Diamond Mine
blurb: Canada's first diamond mine, opened in 1998 in the barren lands about 190 miles north of Yellowknife. Look for pits and an airstrip among thousands of tundra lakes.

name: Ranger Uranium Mine
blurb: A uranium mine set inside Kakadu National Park but excluded from it, mined from 1980 until 2021 and now being rehabilitated. Look for the pit and tailings dam ringed by tropical savanna.

name: Letseng diamond mine
blurb: One of the highest diamond mines in the world at about 10,000 ft, known for producing some exceptionally large stones. Look for the open pits in bare Maloti highlands.

name: Zollern II/IV Colliery
blurb: A Dortmund coal mine famous for its Art Nouveau machine hall, now a museum of industrial history. Look for the two headframes over a cluster of ornate brick buildings.

name: Porgera Gold Mine
blurb: A gold mine high in the Papua New Guinea highlands, at roughly 8,000 ft, with waste long discharged into the river system. Look for the raw pit in steep, cloud-wrapped jungle ridges.

name: Nakhlak Mine
blurb: An old lead mine in the desert of central Iran, worked since ancient times. Look for spoil heaps and mine buildings in the bare hills of Isfahan province's eastern desert.

name: Muruntau mine
blurb: One of the largest open-pit gold mines in the world, more than 2 miles long, in the Kyzylkum Desert. Look for the huge terraced pit and gray dumps in tan sand.

name: Pars Stadium
blurb: A newer large stadium in Shiraz, opened in the late 2010s on the city's outskirts. Look for the oval bowl at the edge of town, framed by the bare Zagros ridges.

name: Estadio Universidad San Marcos
blurb: The stadium of San Marcos, the oldest university in the Americas, founded in 1551. Look for it on the campus in western Lima, with the city's arid brown hills in the distance.

name: Toquepala Mine
blurb: A large open-pit copper mine in the desert mountains of southern Peru. Look for the deep terraced bowl and long tailings lines in bare brown slopes.

name: Cerrejón
blurb: One of the largest open-pit coal mines in the world, with its own railroad running about 90 miles to a port on the Caribbean. Look for the long dark gashes across the dry plains of La Guajira.

name: Pyhäsalmi Mine
blurb: A zinc and copper mine that reached about 4,700 ft underground, the deepest base metal mine in Europe, before ore production ended. Look for the old open pit and mine buildings among Finnish lakes and forest.

name: Bois-du-Luc
blurb: One of the most complete coal-mining villages in Europe, with a colliery and planned workers' housing laid out in the 1840s. Look for the neat brick terraces around the old pithead.

name: Sarcheshmeh
blurb: One of the largest copper deposits in the world, mined from a big open pit high in the mountains of Kerman province. Look for the terraced pit and tailings in the bare brown ranges.

name: Blegny-Mine
blurb: A coal mine near Liège that closed in 1980 and now takes visitors underground. Look for the headframe and a dark spoil heap in green farmland.

name: Panguna mine
blurb: Once one of the largest open-pit copper mines in the world, shut in 1989 when the dispute over it became Bougainville's civil war. Look for the huge abandoned pit in the rainforest.

name: Tarfaya Wind Farm
blurb: One of the largest wind farms in Africa, on Morocco's Atlantic coast near Tarfaya, where the desert meets the sea. Look for long rows of turbines on flat sand just behind the shore.

name: Tafila Wind Farm
blurb: Jordan's first utility-scale wind farm, perched on the high plateau above the Dead Sea Rift, where winds rush up from the valley below. Look for turbines on bare brown highlands at the rim of the escarpment.

name: Golan Heights Wind Farm
blurb: On the Golan plateau near the Syrian frontier, on a basalt ridge among old volcanic cones. Look for turbines on dark rocky upland above the plateau's orchards.

name: Sweetwater Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the Callahan Divide near Sweetwater, part of the giant West Texas wind belt. Look for rows of towers on flat-topped mesas above cotton fields.

name: Jaisalmer Wind Park
blurb: One of India's largest wind parks, spread across the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer. Look for hundreds of turbines scattered over sandy, sparsely settled desert.

name: Smøla Wind Farm
blurb: On Smøla, a flat, low island off Norway's west coast, where the turbines are notorious for killing white-tailed sea eagles. Look for towers spread across bare moorland dotted with ponds.

name: Sheringham Shoal Offshore Wind Farm
blurb: 88 turbines in the North Sea about 10 miles off the north Norfolk coast. Look for a grid of white towers in open water off Cromer and Sheringham.

name: Trtar-Krtolin Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the karst plateau behind Šibenik, in the stony Dalmatian hinterland. Look for white towers on gray limestone scrub a few miles inland from the island-studded coast.

name: Lake Turkana Wind Power Station
blurb: The largest wind farm in Africa, 365 turbines in a desert gap between mountains east of Lake Turkana, where winds blow almost nonstop. Look for grids of towers on bare volcanic ground near the jade-colored lake.

name: Peñascal Wind Power Project
blurb: Turbines on the Kenedy Ranch near Baffin Bay on the South Texas coast. Look for white towers spread across flat brushland near the Laguna Madre.

name: Burgos Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the coastal hills of Burgos at the northern tip of Luzon, among the largest wind farms in the Philippines. Look for towers on green ridges above the South China Sea.

name: Osório wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the coastal plain near Osório in southern Brazil, among the largest in Latin America when opened in 2006. Look for rows of towers between lagoons and the Atlantic beach.

name: Rampion Wind Farm
blurb: 116 turbines off the Sussex coast, clearly visible from Brighton beach. Look for a long band of white towers on the horizon south of the city.

name: Triton Knoll Wind Farm
blurb: About 90 turbines in the North Sea, roughly 20 miles off the Lincolnshire coast. Look for a grid of white towers in open water far from shore.

name: West of Duddon Sands Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines in the Irish Sea off Barrow-in-Furness, one of several big arrays here. Look for a grid of white towers in open water near Walney Island.

name: Karścino wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the Pomeranian coastal plain near Białogard, one of Poland's main wind districts. Look for towers scattered across a patchwork of farm fields and woods.

name: Borssele offshore wind farm
blurb: A cluster of offshore wind farms in the North Sea off Zeeland, about 1.5 gigawatts, among the largest in the Netherlands. Look for a grid of turbines standing in open water, far from shore.

name: Muppandal Wind Farm
blurb: India's biggest wind cluster, where a gap in the Western Ghats near Kanyakumari funnels monsoon winds onto the plain. Look for thousands of turbines spread across fields below the mountains.

name: Maranchon Wind Farm
blurb: One of Spain's largest wind farms, spread over the high, bare plateau of Guadalajara. Look for dozens of towers on open ground above deep valleys.

name: Noordoostpolder wind farms
blurb: The Netherlands' biggest onshore wind farm when built, with turbines along the dikes of the Noordoostpolder and some standing in the IJsselmeer itself. Look for rows of towers lining the shore and marching out into the water.

name: Ellern wind farm
blurb: One of many wind farms on the Hunsrück plateau, among the most turbine-dense landscapes in Germany. Look for rows of towers spread across fields and forest strips near Frankfurt-Hahn airport.

name: Sidi Daoud Wind Farm
blurb: Tunisia's first wind farm, on the tip of Cap Bon facing Sicily across the strait. Look for white towers on hills near the end of the peninsula.

name: Alto Minho Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the granite hills of the Minho in Portugal's far north near the Spanish border, among the largest onshore wind projects in Europe when built. Look for towers along high bare ridges.

name: Tyupkildy wind park
blurb: Bashkortostan's first wind farm, a small set of turbines on a hilltop near Tuymazy, one of the earliest in Russia. Look for a few turbines on a ridge above farmland and oil country.

name: Tarkhankut Wind Farm
blurb: Stands on the windswept Tarkhankut Peninsula, Crimea's flat, dry western tip, ringed by limestone cliffs. Look for small turbines spread across steppe near the coast.

name: Nygårdsfjellet Wind Farm
blurb: In the mountains above Narvik, well north of the Arctic Circle and close to the Swedish border. Look for turbines on bare fell above a fjord.

name: Hama Wing
blurb: A single turbine at Yokohama's port, put up by the city in 2007. Look for one white tower on the waterfront among docks and warehouses.

name: Hitra Wind Farm
blurb: On Hitra, an island at the mouth of Trondheimsfjord. Look for turbines on rocky heath, with skerries and salmon farms offshore.

name: Jhimpir Wind Power Plant
blurb: Part of the Gharo-Jhimpir wind corridor in Sindh, Pakistan's main wind belt, near Keenjhar Lake east of Karachi. Look for rows of turbines across dry, brown scrubland.

name: Lamma Winds
blurb: Not a farm but a single turbine, Hong Kong's first commercial-scale wind turbine, on a hill on Lamma Island. Look for one white tower on the island's green ridge, near the tall stacks of the island's power station.

name: Cijin Wind Turbine Park
blurb: A few turbines on Cijin island, the long sandbar that shelters Kaohsiung harbor. Look for white towers on the narrow island between the port and the open sea.

name: Westermost Rough Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines in the North Sea off the Holderness coast north of Hull. Look for a grid of white towers in open water off the long eroding clay cliffs.

name: White Hill Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the rolling sheep country of northern Southland near Mossburn. Look for towers on tussock-covered hills.

name: Parc eòlic Milà
blurb: Menorca's only wind farm, a small group of turbines on low hills near Mahón. Look for white towers above a patchwork of stone-walled fields.

name: Seto Windhill
blurb: Turbines along the spine of the Sadamisaki peninsula, a skinny 25-mile finger of land pointing at Kyushu. Look for the long line of towers marching down the narrow ridge.

name: Sierra del Trigo
blurb: Turbines on a ridge in the Jaén hills of Andalusia, surrounded by endless olive groves. Look for towers along the crest above rows of dotted green trees.

name: Vader Piet Wind Farm
blurb: A row of turbines on Aruba's rugged, windward east coast, where the trade winds blow nearly all year. Look for white turbines lined up along the dry, rocky shore facing the open Caribbean.

name: Botievo wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the steppe near the Sea of Azov, once Ukraine's largest wind farm, now in Russian-occupied territory. Look for rows of towers on flat farmland near the coast.

name: Østerild Wind Turbine Test Field
blurb: Denmark's national test field for the world's biggest turbines, a row of giant prototypes in a clearing cut through a plantation forest in Thy. Look for an unusually tall line of towers running across dark woods.

name: Hesselbach Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the wooded hills of the Rothaar range region in western Germany. Look for towers rising above dark ridgetop forest.

name: Taltal wind farm
blurb: Built in the Atacama, the driest nonpolar desert on Earth, where turbines stand on bare brown hills above the Pacific. Look for white towers against the coastal escarpment with nothing green in sight.

name: Ngong Hills Wind Farm
blurb: On the Ngong Hills, the ridge of knuckled peaks southwest of Nairobi made famous by Out of Africa. Look for turbines along the crest above the Rift Valley escarpment.

name: Braes of Doune Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the moorland above Doune near Stirling, at the edge of the Highlands. Look for white towers on brown hills above the Forth valley.

name: Tajiat Olympic Stadium
blurb: A stadium in Taji, north of Baghdad, on the flat farmland along the Tigris. Look for an open bowl in the patchwork of fields and canals.

name: Schneebergerhof Wind Park
blurb: Turbines on the uplands of the North Palatinate near the Donnersberg, the region's highest peak. Look for towers on open farmland on the hilltops.

name: Jade wind farm
blurb: On the shore of the Jade Bight at Wilhelmshaven, Germany's only deepwater port. Look for turbines along the dikes beside the tidal mudflats.

name: Windpark A7
blurb: Turbines along the A7 motorway in Friesland, near Sneek. Look for a line of towers following the highway across flat green pastures and canals.

name: Tauern wind farm
blurb: One of the highest wind farms in Europe, set on an alpine ridge in Styria above 6,000 ft. Look for turbines strung along a bare mountain crest above forested valleys.

name: Windpark Holtriem
blurb: One of the bigger onshore wind farms in East Frisia, a flat land of polders and drainage ditches near the North Sea. Look for a dense cluster of turbines on dead-flat green fields.

name: Spremberg Wind Park
blurb: In Lusatia, the lignite-mining country of eastern Germany. Look for turbines near the edge of huge open-pit mines and their flooded lakes.

name: Dutch Hill/Cohocton Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the ridges of Steuben County in New York's Southern Tier, near the Finger Lakes. Look for towers along wooded hilltops above long valleys.

name: Panther Creek Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines in the West Texas plains near Big Spring. Look for rows of white towers on flat, dry ranchland and cotton fields.

name: Blue Canyon Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines lining the Slick Hills north of the Wichita Mountains in southwest Oklahoma. Look for white towers along low, rocky ridges that stand out from flat wheat country.

name: Novoazovsk wind farm
blurb: Turbines near Novoazovsk on the Sea of Azov, in territory held by Russian-backed forces since 2014. Look for white towers on flat steppe above the coastal cliffs.

name: Aapua Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on a forested hill near Övertorneå in Swedish Lapland, close to the Finnish border along the Torne River. Look for white towers above dark spruce and the river valley.

name: Alltwalis Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the hills of Carmarthenshire north of Carmarthen. Look for white towers on green upland above wooded valleys.

name: Binalood wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the Binalood mountains near Mashhad, Iran's second-largest city. Look for towers on the dry foothills.

name: Blood Hill wind farm
blurb: A small group of turbines on the flat Norfolk farmland near the coast at Winterton. Look for white towers in fields near the dunes and the Broads.

name: Blyth Harbour Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines along the harbor pier at Blyth, where Britain's first offshore turbines also went up nearby in 2000. Look for a line of towers on the breakwater.

name: Buffalo Ridge Wind Farm
blurb: Along Buffalo Ridge, a long glacial ridge in southwest Minnesota that became one of the first big wind regions in the Midwest. Look for long lines of turbines on the low rise above the prairie.

name: Bukowsko–Nowotaniec wind farm
blurb: Turbines in the hills of far southeast Poland near Sanok, in the foothills leading to the Bieszczady Mountains. Look for white towers on rolling ridges between forest and fields.

name: Coopers Gap Wind Farm
blurb: Australia's largest wind farm when it was finished, with over 120 turbines on ridges of the South Burnett near Kingaroy. Look for towers along a line of high country above the farm plains.

name: EDP Peștera Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the Dobruja farmland near the Danube, close to Cernavodă. Look for white towers on gently rolling fields near the river and its canal to the Black Sea.

name: Emu Downs Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the coastal plain north of Perth near Badgingarra. Look for white towers on low hills above sandy heathland and farmland.

name: Great Eppleton Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on farmland near Hetton-le-Hole between Sunderland and Durham. Look for white towers on gentle hills among old mining villages.

name: Kisigmánd Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the gentle hills of northwest Hungary near Komárom, close to the Danube and the Slovak border. Look for towers over large open fields.

name: Meadow Lake Wind Farm
blurb: One of the larger wind farms in the Midwest, spread over flat White County farmland north of Lafayette, Indiana. Look for hundreds of turbines across the grid of fields.

name: Mill Creek Wind Farm
blurb: On the hills above Ohariu valley just northwest of Wellington. Look for turbines on the bare ridges, with Cook Strait close by.

name: Project West Wind
blurb: At Makara on Wellington's windy west coast, facing Cook Strait. Look for turbines on the bare hills above steep cliffs, often in the path of Wellington approaches.

name: Lori 1 Wind Farm
blurb: Armenia's first wind farm, a small cluster of turbines on a high mountain pass in the north of the country. Look for a few white turbines on a grassy ridge.

name: Sōyamisaki Wind Farm
blurb: Near Cape Sōya, the northernmost point of Japan's main islands, where Russia's Sakhalin is visible on clear days. Look for dozens of turbines on rolling green hills above the strait.

name: Tymień Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the coastal farmland of Pomerania near Koszalin, part of the dense wind belt behind Poland's Baltic coast. Look for evenly spaced towers among large fields.

name: Bessakerfjellet Wind Farm
blurb: On a coastal mountain in Trøndelag facing the open Norwegian Sea. Look for turbines on bare rock above the fjords.

name: Markbygden Wind Farm
blurb: Planned to become one of Europe's largest onshore wind farms, with hundreds of turbines in the forests west of Piteå. Look for towers spread over dark forest and bog.

name: Manjil Wind Farm
blurb: In the Manjil gap, where winds funnel through the Alborz mountains along the Sefid Rud valley, Iran's windiest corner. Look for turbines on bare hills near the Manjil dam.

name: St. Leon Wind Farm
blurb: Manitoba's first wind farm, set on the prairie near the Pembina escarpment south of Winnipeg. Look for turbines in rows over a grid of flat fields.

name: Te Āpiti Wind Farm
blurb: Above the Manawatu Gorge, where a river cuts straight through New Zealand's main mountain spine. Look for turbines on green farmland at the top of the gorge.

name: Te Uku Wind Farm
blurb: Near Raglan on New Zealand's North Island west coast. Look for turbines on green hill-country farms above the harbor.

name: Totoral Wind Farm

name: Talinay wind farm
blurb: Sits on coastal hills near Fray Jorge, where Pacific fog keeps a patch of rainforest alive in the middle of semi-desert. Look for turbines on the bluffs above the long, empty beach.

name: Rivière-du-Moulin Wind Project
blurb: One of Quebec's larger wind farms, spread over forested uplands between Saguenay and Charlevoix. Look for white towers in clearings across dark boreal forest.

name: Windpark Sohl
blurb: Turbines on the forested hills of the Siegerland region in western Germany. Look for towers above dark ridges.

name: Wysocko Wielkie Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the farmland of Greater Poland near Ostrzeszów in the south of the region. Look for white towers spaced across a quilt of narrow fields.

name: Slufterdam wind farm
blurb: On the Maasvlakte at the seaward end of Rotterdam's port, the busiest in Europe. Look for a line of turbines along the dike of the Slufter, a huge ringed basin for contaminated dredged silt.

name: Riutunkari wind farm
blurb: At the port of Oulu on the Gulf of Bothnia, where the sea freezes every winter. Look for turbines on the harbor shoreline and breakwaters at the mouth of the city's river.

name: Parc eòlic del Collet dels Feixos
blurb: Turbines on dry hills in southern Catalonia, inland from the Ebro valley. Look for white towers along scrubby ridgelines above olive groves and terraces.

name: Pampa Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the rolling grassland of Tacuarembó in central Uruguay, a country that gets a large share of its power from wind. Look for towers across open cattle range.

name: Monte Mesa Wind Farm
blurb: On the plateau between Lake Garda and the Adige valley near Rivoli Veronese. Look for turbines on a ridge with the lake's long blue water to the west.

name: Bogdanci wind turbines
blurb: North Macedonia's first wind farm, near Bogdanci on the Greek border, in the Vardar valley. Look for turbines on dry hills above the valley.

name: Schwarzenberg wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the wooded uplands of central Hesse. Look for towers rising above ridgetop forest.

name: Windkraftwerk Juvent
blurb: Switzerland's largest wind farm, on the Mont-Crosin pastures of the Bernese Jura. Look for white towers on long green ridges dotted with farms and wood pastures.

name: Paraguaná Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the Paraguaná peninsula in northwest Venezuela, a flagship project that was never fully finished. Look for white towers on dry, scrubby flatland near the sea.

name: Pililla Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the hills of Rizal overlooking Laguna de Bay east of Manila, popular enough with day-trippers to have become a tourist stop. Look for towers on grassy ridges above the big lake.

name: Pollupalai and Vallimunai Wind Farms
blurb: Turbines on the flat coastal land of the Jaffna region in Sri Lanka's far north. Look for white towers on sandy ground near lagoons and palmyra palms.

name: Thambapavani Wind Farm
blurb: Sri Lanka's largest wind farm, on Mannar Island in the strait toward India. Look for a line of turbines along a flat sandy island near the start of Adam's Bridge shoals.

name: Høg-Jæren Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the Jæren highlands south of Stavanger, the moorland rising behind Norway's flattest farming coast. Look for white towers on brown heath inland from long sandy beaches.

name: Ytre Vikna wind farm
blurb: The outer phase of the Vikna island turbines off Rørvik, set on bare rock facing the open Norwegian Sea. Look for white towers scattered over a low, treeless archipelago.

name: Pamsendorf wind farm
blurb: In Bavaria's Upper Palatinate near the Czech border. Look for turbines on rolling hills of fields and spruce woods.

name: Windpark Gries
blurb: One of the highest wind farms in Europe, at about 7,600 ft on the Gries Pass beside the Griessee reservoir. Look for turbines on bare rock above a milky turquoise lake.

name: Windpark Gütsch
blurb: Turbines on the Gütsch ridge above Andermatt at about 7,500 ft, among the highest wind turbines in Europe. Look for towers on the bare ridge above the Urseren valley.

name: Peuchapatte Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the Franches-Montagnes plateau in the Swiss Jura, horse-breeding country of pastures and spruce. Look for a few white towers on open, rolling upland.

name: Korday Wind Farm
blurb: Near Kazakhstan's border with Kyrgyzstan, at the foot of the Tian Shan foothills across from Bishkek. Look for turbines on the dry steppe below the mountains.

name: Kilgallioch Wind Farm
blurb: One of Scotland's larger wind farms, spread across forestry and moor in the Galloway uplands. Look for white towers over dark forest blocks and brown hills.

name: Lubartów Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the flat farmland of the Lublin region in eastern Poland. Look for white towers among long, narrow strip fields typical of the area.

name: Viru-Nigula wind farm
blurb: Turbines on Estonia's northern coast near Kunda, on the flat limestone shelf above the Gulf of Finland. Look for towers among farmland and forest close to the sea cliffs.

name: Taichung Port Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines along the breakwaters of Taichung port on Taiwan's west coast. Look for a row of white towers following the harbor walls and reclaimed land.

name: Cerová wind farm
blurb: One of Slovakia's few wind farms, a handful of turbines near the foot of the Little Carpathians. Look for white towers on farmland at the edge of forested hills.

name: Huxi Windpower Plant
blurb: Turbines on Penghu, a low, flat archipelago in the Taiwan Strait whose winter monsoon winds are among Taiwan's strongest. Look for white towers on bare island ground near the sea.

name: Ovenden Moor Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on the moors above Halifax in the West Yorkshire Pennines. Look for white towers on brown moorland above reservoirs and stone mill towns.

name: Ararat Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on farmland northeast of Ararat in western Victoria, near the Grampians. Look for white towers spread over flat, open grazing country.

name: Fraisthorpe Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on farmland behind the coast just south of Bridlington. Look for white towers in flat fields near the long Holderness beaches.

name: Longmen Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on Penghu's main island in the Taiwan Strait, where strong winter winds sweep the low, treeless islands. Look for white towers on flat ground near the coast.

name: Trumau Wind Farm
blurb: A wind farm on the flat Vienna Basin south of the city, among fields and gravel pits. Look for a cluster of white turbines on open farmland near the A3 motorway.

name: Windpark Nordschwarzwald
blurb: Turbines on the ridges of the northern Black Forest, high above the spa towns of the Enz valley. Look for towers in clearings in dense dark forest.

name: Valley of Tears Wind Farm
blurb: Named for the Valley of Tears, a major tank battlefield of the 1973 Yom Kippur War on the northern Golan. Look for turbines on the basalt plateau near the Syrian line.

name: Paldiski wind farm
blurb: On the Pakri peninsula, once part of a closed Soviet naval base, ending in limestone cliffs over the Baltic. Look for turbines along the flat, bare headland west of Tallinn.

name: Kvitfjell Raudfjell Vindkraftverk
blurb: On Kvaløya island west of Tromsø, far above the Arctic Circle, among the northernmost large wind farms in the world. Look for turbines along bare mountain ridges between deep fjords.

name: Windpark Sternwald
blurb: Turbines on the forested ridges of the Bohemian Forest borderlands, just south of the Czech frontier in Upper Austria. Look for white towers poking above dark spruce woods.

name: Boulenouar Wind Power Station
blurb: Near Nouadhibou on Mauritania's Atlantic coast, where Saharan trade winds blow hard and steady. Look for turbines on flat sandy desert near the coast.

name: Korlat Wind Farm
blurb: On the dry limestone plateau near Benkovac, in the Zadar hinterland. Look for turbines on gray scrubland broken by stone walls and small fields.

name: Pottendorf Wind Farm
blurb: A wind farm on the open Vienna Basin farmland south of Vienna, one of several in the area. Look for a cluster of white turbines among fields and small villages.

name: Romblon Wind Farm
blurb: A small set of turbines on Romblon island in the middle of the Philippine archipelago. Look for white towers on a green hilly island surrounded by blue sea.

name: Ghoubet Wind Power Station
blurb: Djibouti's first wind farm, set near the Ghoubet gulf in the Afar Rift, one of the windiest and hottest corners of Africa. Look for turbines on black volcanic ground beside the blue inlet, with Lake Assal's salt pan nearby.

name: Øyfjellet Wind Park
blurb: Over 70 turbines on a plateau above Mosjøen, built over objections from Sami reindeer herders whose winter grazing land it covers. Look for towers and gravel roads on high, open fell.

name: Frederikshavn Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines at the harbor town of Frederikshavn, near Denmark's northern tip, where ferries leave for Sweden and Norway. Look for towers on the breakwaters and flat land by the port.

name: Mesihovina wind farm
blurb: Bosnia and Herzegovina's first wind farm, on a high karst plateau near Tomislavgrad. Look for turbines strung across a bare, rocky upland with stone-walled fields.

name: Harlingerode wind farm
blurb: Near Bad Harzburg at the north edge of the Harz mountains. Look for turbines on flat farmland right where the wooded mountains rise abruptly.

name: Schlewecke wind farm
blurb: At the northern foot of the Harz near Goslar, a medieval mining town. Look for turbines on the plain below the steep, forested mountain front.

name: Coonooer Bridge Wind Farm
blurb: A small group of turbines on flat wheat country in north-central Victoria. Look for a few white towers among wide, open paddocks.

name: Kandrich wind farm
blurb: At the edge of the Hunsrück above the Rhine near Bingen. Look for turbines on wooded heights over the river gorge.

name: Windpark Immenrode
blurb: On farmland at the northern edge of the Harz mountains near Goslar. Look for turbines on the plain, with the forested mountain wall to the south.

name: Knabs Ridge Wind Farm
blurb: Turbines on farmland near Harrogate in North Yorkshire. Look for white towers on a ridge among green fields and hedgerows.

name: Orlivska wind farm
blurb: Turbines on the steppe near the Sea of Azov, completed by DTEK in 2019 and now in occupied territory. Look for rows of towers on flat fields.

name: Freiländeralm Wind Farm
blurb: An alpine wind farm in western Styria, on a high pasture ridge. Look for a short line of turbines on an open mountain crest above dense forest.

name: Zelengrad Wind Farm
blurb: On the karst uplands near Obrovac, at the foot of the Velebit range above the Zrmanja canyon. Look for turbines on bare stony hills inland from Zadar.

name: Ovidiopol wind farm
blurb: Turbines near Ovidiopol, southwest of Odesa by the Dniester estuary. Look for white towers on flat farmland near the wide estuary and the Black Sea.

name: San Pedro Wind Farm
blurb: On Chiloé Island, a rainy, green land of wooden churches and stilt houses in Chile's south. Look for white turbines on forested hills in the island's interior, a rare industrial touch in farm country.

name: South Fork Wind Farm
blurb: The first commercial offshore wind farm in US federal waters, 12 turbines southeast of Block Island, sending power to Long Island since 2024. Look for a tidy grid of towers in open ocean.

name: Taiba N'Diaye Wind Power Station
blurb: West Africa's largest wind farm, set along the coast between Dakar and Saint-Louis. Look for rows of turbines among sand dunes and vegetable plots near the Atlantic beach.

name: Krnovo Wind Farm
blurb: On the Krnovo plateau near Nikšić, Montenegro's first large wind farm. Look for turbines on high, bare karst pastures among the mountains.

name: Dubai International Cricket Stadium
blurb: Dubai's 25,000-seat cricket ground, which hosted IPL seasons and the 2021 T20 World Cup final. Look for the white ring roof of floodlights in Dubai Sports City.

name: Harvard University
blurb: Founded in 1636, the oldest college in the US. Look for the red brick houses along the Charles and, across the river, Harvard Stadium, a 1903 concrete horseshoe.

name: University of Oxford
blurb: Teaching here dates to at least 1096, making it the oldest university in the English-speaking world. There is no campus: its colleges fill the city center. Look for the round Radcliffe Camera among the spires.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
blurb: Look for the Great Dome over Killian Court facing the Charles River. The Harvard Bridge next to it is measured as 364.4 smoots plus an ear, after a 1958 fraternity prank.

name: Lomonosov Moscow State University
blurb: Its main building, about 790 ft tall, is the tallest of Stalin's Seven Sisters and was the tallest building in Europe until 1990. Look for the spire on the Sparrow Hills above a bend of the Moskva River.

name: Yale University
blurb: Founded in 1701, the third-oldest college in the US, with Gothic quads in downtown New Haven. Look for Harkness Tower among the courtyards, a short way inland from Long Island Sound.

name: Princeton University
blurb: Gothic stone campus founded in 1746. Look for Lake Carnegie on its southern edge, a long narrow lake built for the rowing team with money from Andrew Carnegie.

name: Cornell University
blurb: Sits on a hill above the south end of Cayuga Lake, one of the long Finger Lakes, between two deep gorges with waterfalls. Look for the long narrow lake stretching north.

name: Columbia University
blurb: Founded in 1754 and on Morningside Heights since 1897. Look for the domed Low Library above a grand quad in Upper Manhattan's grid, with the Hudson a few blocks west.

name: University of Chicago
blurb: Gothic stone quads on the South Side, home of the first controlled nuclear chain reaction in 1942. Look for the long green Midway Plaisance strip running between Washington and Jackson parks.

name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
blurb: Its Mount Scopus campus has looked out over Jerusalem since 1925; Albert Einstein was a founder and left it his papers. Look for the tall tower on the ridge, with the Judean Desert dropping away to the east.

name: California Institute of Technology
blurb: A small campus in Pasadena with only about 2,400 students, linked to dozens of Nobel laureates. It manages NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a few miles north at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains.

name: Johns Hopkins University
blurb: Founded in 1876 as the first US research university, with a red brick Georgian campus at Homewood in north Baltimore. Look for brick quads and green lawns among rowhouse neighborhoods.

name: Peking University
blurb: Founded in 1898 and among the most selective universities in China, on the old Yenching campus. Look for Weiming Lake and the Boya Pagoda, a water tower disguised as a pagoda, near the Summer Palace.

name: Duke University
blurb: Look for the 210-ft tower of Duke Chapel above the Gothic stone of West Campus, ringed by the thousands of acres of Duke Forest. Founded as Trinity College and renamed in 1924.

name: Brown University
blurb: Founded in 1764, the seventh-oldest college in the US, on College Hill above downtown Providence. Look for brick buildings and green quads on the slope east of the river.

name: ETH Zurich
blurb: Einstein's alma mater, founded in 1855. Its main building by Gottfried Semper sits on the slope above the old town; look for its long facade and dome facing the Limmat and the lake.

name: Nalanda Mahavihara
blurb: Ruins of a Buddhist monastic university that drew students from across Asia for about 700 years, until its destruction around 1200. Look for long rows of red-brick monastery foundations in green Bihar farmland.

name: Summer Palace
blurb: An imperial garden where Kunming Lake covers about three quarters of the grounds, its dug-out earth piled up to form Longevity Hill. Look for the big lake in northwest Beijing with a 17-arch bridge out to its island.

name: Belvedere
blurb: Two baroque palaces built for Prince Eugene of Savoy, facing each other across terraced gardens; the upper one holds Klimt's The Kiss. Look for the long garden axis stepping downhill between the two buildings.

name: Ak Bars Arena
blurb: Kazan's 2018 World Cup stadium, also built for the 2013 Universiade, has one of Europe's largest outdoor screens on its facade. Look for the oval near the Kazanka River in the north of the city.

name: Golestan Palace
blurb: The Qajar royal palace in central Tehran, among the city's oldest buildings and a UNESCO site. Look for its walled gardens and long pools in the dense center near the Grand Bazaar.

name: Hawa Mahal
blurb: A five-story pink sandstone facade with 953 small windows, built in 1799 so royal women could watch street life unseen. Look for the pink honeycomb front in the old city.

name: Malbork Castle
blurb: Built by the Teutonic Knights, the largest castle in the world by land area. Look for the sprawling red-brick fortress along the Nogat River.

name: Wartburg
blurb: Martin Luther hid in this hilltop castle in 1521 and translated the New Testament into German. Look for the castle on the wooded ridge above Eisenach.

name: Rostov Arena
blurb: Built on the Don's quiet left bank for the 2018 World Cup, facing the city across the river. Look for the oval stadium on open flatland just south of the river from downtown Rostov.

name: Leicester City Stadium
blurb: Leicester City's home, where the club won the 2016 Premier League title at 5,000 to 1 odds. Look for the boxy stadium south of the city center, beside the River Soar.

name: Catherine Palace
blurb: The blue-and-white palace at Tsarskoye Selo houses the rebuilt Amber Room, whose original panels vanished after the Nazis looted them in 1941. Look for a blue facade nearly 1,000 ft long beside a large landscaped park.

name: Mordovia Arena
blurb: Built for the 2018 World Cup in Saransk, a small city that had never hosted anything close to that scale. Look for the orange and red bowl, colors meant to echo the Mordovian sun, near the Insar River.

name: Kronborg Castle
blurb: Shakespeare's Elsinore, the castle where Hamlet is set, guarding the narrowest point of the Oresund about 2.5 miles from Sweden. Look for the star-shaped bastions on the point at Helsingor.

name: Rostec Arena
blurb: Kaliningrad's stadium, built for the 2018 World Cup on an island in the Pregolya River. Look for the white rectangular stadium on flat reclaimed ground near the city center.

name: Samara Arena
blurb: Samara's 2018 World Cup stadium has a ribbed glass dome meant to evoke a spacecraft, a nod to the city's rocket industry, which built the Soyuz launchers. Look for the silvery domed disc on the city's northern edge.

name: Juventus Stadium
blurb: Juventus's own ground, opened in 2011 on the site of the old Delle Alpi. Look for the rectangular roof hung from two tall masts on Turin's northwest edge, with the Alps behind.

name: Neo Química Arena
blurb: Corinthians' home in the eastern district of Itaquera hosted the opening match of the 2014 World Cup. Look for the boxy stadium with a sloping glass facade beside the railway in the eastern suburbs.

name: Central Stadium Yekaterinburg
blurb: Yekaterinburg's 1950s stadium kept its Stalin-era facade for the 2018 World Cup, and temporary stands poked out beyond the old walls like bleachers on stilts. Look for the long classical facade around a modern bowl.

name: Newark Liberty International Airport
blurb: Opened in 1928 on the Newark meadows, the first major airport in the New York area. Look for the container cranes of Port Newark-Elizabeth just east, and Manhattan's skyline beyond.

name: Cairo International Airport
blurb: One of the busiest airports in Africa, on the desert edge of northeast Cairo. Look for the sharp line where the green city stops and bare sand begins.

name: Lien Khuong Airport
blurb: Serves the hill town of Đà Lạt from about 3,000 ft up in the Central Highlands. Look for pine forest, greenhouses glinting white across the valleys, and terraced vegetable farms.

name: Stockholm Arlanda Airport
blurb: Sweden's largest airport, about 25 miles north of Stockholm. Look for three runways cleared out of dense pine forest, with lakes and red farmhouses scattered around.

name: Parken Stadium
blurb: Denmark's national stadium in Copenhagen's Østerbro, home of FC Copenhagen, with a retractable roof. It hosted Eurovision in 2001. Look for the boxy stadium next to the Fælledparken green.

name: RheinEnergie Stadion
blurb: FC Köln's stadium in the Müngersdorf sports park. Look for the four glowing corner towers that hold up its roof, set in the green belt on Cologne's western side.

name: Estádio Couto Pereira
blurb: Coritiba's home in central Curitiba, a classic concrete bowl dating to 1932. Look for it tucked into the city grid in the Alto da Glória neighborhood.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport
blurb: One of India's busiest airports, with two crossing runways squeezed into the city and slums pressing on the fences. Look for the X of runways and Terminal 2's curving roof, inspired by peacock feathers.

name: Taoyuan International Airport
blurb: Taiwan's main international gateway, near the west coast about 25 miles from Taipei. Look for two parallel runways close to the shore and rows of wind turbines along the coast.

name: Vancouver International Airport
blurb: Built on Sea Island in the Fraser River delta, with the Coast Mountains rising steeply behind the city to the north. Look for the parallel runways on flat delta farmland bordered by river channels and tidal flats.

name: Denver International Airport
blurb: At 53 square miles it is the largest airport in the US by area, more than twice the size of Manhattan. Look for the white peaked tent roof, meant to echo the snowy Rockies, and the pinwheel of runways.

name: Sanssouci Palace
blurb: Frederick the Great's summer palace in Potsdam, a single-story yellow palace on top of terraced vineyards. Look for the stepped terraces climbing to the palace in a large park of avenues and fountains.

name: Dolmabahçe Palace
blurb: The sultans' European-style palace from the 1850s, its marble front running about a third of a mile along the Bosporus. Atatürk died here in 1938, and its clocks were stopped at 9:05.

name: Hampton Court Palace
blurb: Henry VIII's favorite palace, later extended by Christopher Wren, with the oldest surviving hedge maze in Britain. Look for the red-brick Tudor courts on the Thames with avenues of trees fanning out across the park.

name: Luxembourg Palace
blurb: Built for Marie de' Medici in the 1610s and now home of the French Senate. Look for the formal gardens and big octagonal pond south of the palace, the main green patch on the Left Bank.

name: Can Tho International Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Mekong Delta, built on the old Tra Noc air base. Look for a single runway set among rice paddies, fish ponds and the brown braids of the Hau River.

name: Kabul International Airport
blurb: Sits at about 5,900 ft in a bowl of bare mountains, the scene of the chaotic US evacuation in August 2021. Look for the single long runway on the flat valley floor north of the city.

name: Riga International Airport
blurb: The largest airport in the Baltic states and home of airBaltic. Look for it southwest of Riga, with the Daugava River and the old town's spires to the northeast.

name: Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport
blurb: Budapest's airport, on flat land southeast of the city. Look for the two parallel runways among farmland, with the Danube winding through the city to the west.

name: Vilnius Airport
blurb: Lithuania's main airport, about 4 miles south of Vilnius old town. Look for the 1950s Stalinist terminal with its columns, and the baroque spires of the old town to the north.

name: Hamburg Airport
blurb: Opened in 1911, one of the oldest airports in the world still at its original site, now surrounded by the city. Look for the crossing runways inside residential Hamburg.

name: Tho Xuan Airport
blurb: Serves Thanh Hoa province on a field shared with the Vietnamese air force. Look for one long runway in flat rice country with limestone hills rising to the west.

name: Geneva International Airport
blurb: The runway runs right along the French border, and the airport has a French sector reachable without entering Switzerland. Look for Lake Geneva and the Jet d'Eau, a fountain shooting about 460 ft high.

name: Tirana International Airport Nënë Tereza
blurb: Albania's main gateway, in farm country northwest of Tirana. It is named for Mother Teresa, who was ethnic Albanian. Look for the runway on the valley floor with hills rising on both sides.

name: Ministro Pistarini International Airport
blurb: Buenos Aires' main international airport, about 20 miles southwest of the center in Ezeiza. Look for the runways set among flat pampa, woodland and the green of the surrounding reserve.

name: Free State Stadium
blurb: Bloemfontein's main stadium, home of the Cheetahs rugby side and a 2010 World Cup venue. Look for an open bowl with a partial roof on the flat Free State plain.

name: Pulkovo Airport
blurb: St. Petersburg's airport, on flat land south of the city below the Pulkovo Heights, home of a famous observatory. Look for the two parallel runways and the long straight avenue running north into the city.

name: Paro Airport
blurb: Only a small number of specially certified pilots are allowed to land here. The runway sits at about 7,300 ft in a narrow valley with ridges close on both sides and steep turns on the way in.

name: Bergamo-Il Caravaggio
blurb: A Ryanair stronghold and one of Italy's busiest airports, just southeast of Bergamo. Look for Città Alta, the walled hilltop old town, on the ridge north of the runway.

name: Minsk National Airport
blurb: Set in forest well east of Minsk, Belarus's only major international airport. Look for the runways cut into dark pine woods with almost nothing else around.

name: Venice Marco Polo Airport
blurb: Built on the edge of the lagoon, so you can leave by water taxi. Look for Venice itself floating in the lagoon a few miles south, tied to the mainland by a long road and rail bridge.

name: Beijing Daxing International Airport
blurb: Zaha Hadid's starfish-shaped terminal, opened in 2019, is one of the largest single terminal buildings in the world, nearly 30 miles south of Tiananmen. Look for the five arms radiating from a central hub.

name: Tallinn Airport
blurb: Named for Lennart Meri, Estonia's first post-Soviet president, and only a couple of miles from Tallinn's medieval old town. Look for the runway next to Lake Ülemiste, the city's reservoir.

name: Hamad International Airport
blurb: Built largely on land reclaimed from the Persian Gulf and opened in 2014 as Qatar Airways' hub. Look for two long parallel runways jutting into the turquoise shallows east of Doha.

name: Palace of Culture and Science
blurb: Stalin's gift to Warsaw, 778 ft, finished in 1955. Look for the wedding-cake spire in the city's center.

name: Mariinskyi Palace
blurb: A Baroque palace from the 1750s by Rastrelli, the ceremonial residence of Ukraine's president, next to the parliament. Look for the turquoise-and-white palace in the park on the bluff above the Dnipro.

name: Peter Mokaba Stadium
blurb: Polokwane's 2010 World Cup stadium, with roof supports inspired by the baobab tree. Look for a square, boxy bowl on open ground at the edge of the city.

name: Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium
blurb: Sevilla's home in the Nervión district hosted the famous 1982 World Cup semifinal between West Germany and France. Look for the big bowl with a mural over its main entrance among dense city blocks.

name: St Mary's Stadium
blurb: Southampton's home since 2001, built on the site of an old gasworks by the River Itchen. Look for the compact bowl near the river's waterfront on the city's east side.

name: Gdańsk Arena
blurb: Built for Euro 2012, its facade is clad in amber-colored panels, a nod to the Baltic amber trade. Look for the glowing gold shell in the flat Letnica district north of Gdańsk's shipyards.

name: EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg
blurb: One of the few airports in the world run jointly by two countries. It sits entirely in France, but a fenced customs road links it straight to Switzerland. Look for the Rhine and the Black Forest to the east.

name: Humberto Delgado Airport
blurb: One of Europe's most central big-city airports: approaches pass low over Lisbon's rooftops just a few miles from downtown. Look for the wide Tagus estuary and the red 25 de Abril Bridge.

name: King Abdulaziz International Airport
blurb: The Hajj Terminal is a sea of white fiberglass tents, one of the largest roofed structures in the world, built to shelter pilgrims bound for Mecca. Look for the rows of white tent peaks on the airport's north side.

name: Jomo Kenyatta International Airport
blurb: East Africa's busiest airport and Kenya Airways' hub. Nairobi National Park is right next door, so giraffes graze in sight of the runway. Look for the park's open grassland stretching toward the city skyline.

name: Düsseldorf Airport
blurb: A fire in 1996 killed 17 people and led to major changes in fire safety at German airports. Look for the runways squeezed between Düsseldorf's suburbs and the Rhine.

name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport
blurb: Hemmed in on every side by Metro Manila, it is one of Asia's most congested big airports, with two runways crossing in an X. Look for dense rooftops right up to the fence and Manila Bay to the west.

name: Karlštejn Castle
blurb: Founded in 1348 by Emperor Charles IV to guard the imperial crown jewels. Look for Gothic towers stacked up a wooded limestone hill above the Berounka valley southwest of Prague.

name: Bran Castle
blurb: Marketed as Dracula's castle, though Vlad the Impaler likely never stayed there. Look for white walls and red roofs on a rock at the Bran pass.

name: Takht-e Soleyman
blurb: A Sasanian royal sanctuary and fire temple built around a deep spring-fed lake on a hilltop in northwest Iran. Look for the round lake inside an oval ring of walls.

name: Changdeokgung
blurb: A Joseon palace from 1405, built to follow the hills, with a large wooded Secret Garden behind. Look for the green forested grounds in central Seoul.

name: Stadium 974
blurb: Built from about 974 shipping containers and designed to be taken apart after the 2022 World Cup. Look for the colorful boxy stadium on the waterfront east of central Doha, across from the skyline.

name: Mestalla Stadium
blurb: Valencia's home since 1923, with some of the steepest stands in Spanish football. Look for a tall, tight rectangle hemmed in by apartment blocks just east of the old city's dry riverbed park.

name: Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2010 World Cup beside North End Lake in Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), with a roof of white petal-like panels. Look for the white flower-shaped bowl next to the water.

name: Nizhny Novgorod Stadium
blurb: Nizhny Novgorod's 2018 World Cup stadium on the spit where the Oka meets the Volga. Look for the white columned ring right at the confluence, across the water from the old kremlin's red walls.

name: St. Jakob-Park
blurb: FC Basel's home, Switzerland's largest football stadium, with a shell that can glow in red and blue at night. Look for the boxy stadium on Basel's southeastern edge, in a city that touches both France and Germany.

name: Red Bull Arena
blurb: RB Leipzig's stadium, built inside the earth bowl of the old Zentralstadion, which once held 100,000. Look for the modern stadium sitting inside the larger ring of grassy banks west of the city center.

name: Miami International Airport
blurb: One of the busiest airports in the US for international cargo, especially to Latin America. Look for the airport packed into the city, with the Everglades starting a few miles west.

name: Melbourne Airport
blurb: At Tullamarine about 14 miles northwest of downtown Melbourne. Look for flat volcanic plains, grassland and suburbs to the south, with the skyline and Port Phillip Bay beyond.

name: Kempegowda International Airport
blurb: Bengaluru's airport, opened in 2008 about 25 miles north of the city. Its second terminal is wrapped in hanging gardens and bamboo. Look for two parallel runways on the open Deccan plateau.

name: Henri Coandă International Airport
blurb: Romania's busiest airport, at Otopeni about 10 miles north of Bucharest. It is named for Henri Coandă, the Romanian aviation pioneer behind the Coandă effect, the way a jet stream hugs a curved surface.

name: Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez
blurb: Sits inside Mexico City at about 7,300 ft, so landings skim low over dense neighborhoods. Look for the two parallel runways boxed in by the city, with dry Lake Texcoco beds to the east.

name: Mir Castle Complex
blurb: A red-brick castle begun in the early 1500s with five towers around a courtyard, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for the square castle beside a small pond in flat Belarusian farmland.

name: Kernavė
blurb: Lithuania's early medieval capital, a group of five steep hillfort mounds above the Neris River valley. Look for the grassy, terraced mounds beside the river bend.

name: Arena Amazônia
blurb: Built in the middle of the rainforest city of Manaus for the 2014 World Cup, with a woven white facade meant to suggest a basket. Look for the white shell in the city's low sprawl near the Rio Negro.

name: Estádio Beira-Rio
blurb: Internacional's home, set on reclaimed land right on the Guaíba lakeshore, renovated for the 2014 World Cup. Look for the curving white roof canopy sitting on the water's edge.

name: Ahmad bin Ali Stadium
blurb: Al Rayyan's 2022 World Cup stadium, its facade patterned on Qatari desert motifs. Look for the rounded box on the western outskirts of Doha at the edge of the desert.

name: Mbombela Stadium
blurb: Mbombela's 2010 World Cup stadium has 18 roof supports shaped and painted like orange-and-black giraffes, a nod to the nearby Kruger National Park. Look for a bowl alone in open bush on the city's edge.

name: Royal Bafokeng Stadium
blurb: Near Rustenburg, built by the Bafokeng people with platinum royalties. In 2010 it hosted England's 1 to 1 draw with the US. Look for an open bowl amid the mine dumps and platinum workings of the bushveld.

name: Molineux Stadium
blurb: Wolverhampton Wanderers' home since 1889. Look for the compact stadium just north of the city center ring road.

name: Washington Dulles International Airport
blurb: Eero Saarinen's 1962 terminal has a roof that sags between leaning columns like a hammock. Look for it at the head of the runways, and the Udvar-Hazy space shuttle hangar just south.

name: Ufa International Airport
blurb: The main airport of Bashkortostan, on flat ground south of Ufa near the Belaya River. Look for the runways among birch woods and fields on the western edge of the Urals foothills.

name: Keflavík Airport
blurb: Built by the US military in World War II and a NATO base until 2006. Look for runways set on the black lava fields of the Reykjanes Peninsula, often near the steaming vents of recent eruptions.

name: Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport
blurb: Iran's main international gateway, about 25 miles south of Tehran in bare desert. The Revolutionary Guard shut it on its opening day in 2004 over a foreign operating contract. Look for Khomeini's gold-domed mausoleum along the highway toward the city.

name: Nice Côte d'Azur Airport
blurb: Its runways were built out into the Mediterranean on reclaimed land. Look for the airport jutting into the sea at the mouth of the Var, with the Baie des Anges curving toward Nice.

name: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
blurb: Three parallel east-west runways only about 3 miles from downtown Phoenix, unusually close for a hub this busy. Look for the airfield squeezed between downtown towers, the Salt River bed and the Papago Buttes.

name: Zvartnots International Airport
blurb: Armenia's main airport, on the Ararat plain west of Yerevan. On a clear day snowcapped Mount Ararat, 16,854 ft, dominates the view to the south across the border in Turkey.

name: Stuttgart Airport
blurb: Stuttgart's airport, on a plateau south of the city, right next to the trade fair halls. Look for the runway beside the Messe buildings and the Autobahn running alongside.

name: Enea Stadion
blurb: Lech Poznań's home, rebuilt for Euro 2012. Look for the rectangular stadium in the city's western neighborhoods, near the Bułgarska street park.

name: Gibraltar International Airport
blurb: The runway cuts straight across the isthmus to Spain, and for decades the main road crossed it, stopping for every landing. Look for the strip jutting into the sea at the foot of the 1,400-ft Rock.

name: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport
blurb: Hub of Ethiopian Airlines, at about 7,600 ft. Look for the runways surrounded by the city, with eucalyptus-covered hills and the Entoto range to the north.

name: Seattle–Tacoma International Airport
blurb: The third runway, opened in 2008, sits on a massive earthen fill that raised it high above the valley floor. Look for three parallel north-south runways with Puget Sound just to the west.

name: Linate Airport
blurb: Milan's city airport, about 5 miles from the Duomo. In 2001 an airliner hit a small jet in fog on its runway, Italy's deadliest air disaster. Look for the Idroscalo, a long straight rowing lake just east.

name: Tribhuvan International Airport
blurb: Nepal's main international airport, in the Kathmandu Valley at about 4,400 ft, so approaches thread between hills. Look for the white wall of the Himalaya along the northern horizon on a clear day.

name: Crypto.com Arena
blurb: Home of the Lakers, Kings and Sparks, opened in 1999 as Staples Center. Look for the oval roof beside the LA Live complex and convention center at the south edge of downtown.

name: Hohenzollern Castle
blurb: The ancestral seat of the Hohenzollerns, the family of the Prussian kings and German emperors, rebuilt in the 1850s on a cone-shaped hill. Look for the turreted castle on the lone peak at the edge of the Swabian Alb.

name: Nesvizh Castle
blurb: The Radziwill family palace, one of the grandest noble seats of the old Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and now a UNESCO site. Look for the palace ringed by ponds and a landscaped park.

name: Arena Fonte Nova
blurb: Salvador's World Cup stadium, built in 2013 on the site of the old Fonte Nova and open at one end toward a lagoon. Look for the horseshoe bowl beside the Dique do Tororó lake in the old city.

name: São Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport
blurb: The busiest airport in South America, about 15 miles northeast of central São Paulo. Look for a seemingly endless carpet of high-rises to the southwest; the metro area is home to more than 20 million people.

name: Lyon–Saint-Exupéry Airport
blurb: Its TGV station, designed by Santiago Calatrava, is shaped like a giant bird with spread wings. Look for that white steel shell beside the terminals, east of Lyon among flat fields.

name: Pristina International Airport Adem Jashari
blurb: Kosovo's only international airport, west of Pristina. In 1999 Russian troops raced in from Bosnia to seize it ahead of NATO forces. Look for the single runway on the open Kosovo plain.

name: Zagreb Airport
blurb: Zagreb's airport on the flat Sava valley southeast of the city. Look for the wavy roof of the terminal opened in 2017 and the Medvednica hills rising behind the city.

name: Logan International Airport
blurb: Built mostly on landfill in Boston Harbor, so approaches skim the water. Look for runways poking into the harbor, with downtown just across the water about 2 miles west.

name: Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport
blurb: Shanghai's older airport, in the western suburbs, is part of a giant transport hub with one of Asia's largest high-speed rail stations next door. Look for rail tracks fanning out beside the terminals.

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport
blurb: Ahmedabad's airport, on the northern edge of the city near the Sabarmati River. Look for the runway surrounded by dense city and the river's long riverfront embankments to the west.

name: Glasgow Airport
blurb: Sits beside the River Clyde about 8 miles west of central Glasgow, near Paisley. Look for the Clyde and the old shipbuilding cranes downstream, with the Highlands rising to the north.

name: Chubu Centrair International Airport
blurb: Built on an artificial island off Tokoname in Ise Bay and opened in 2005. Look for the island sitting off the coast, linked to the shore by a road and rail bridge.

name: Sharjah International Airport
blurb: Sharjah's original airfield, opened in 1932, was the first airport in the Gulf. Today's airport, east of the city, is home to Air Arabia. Look for the desert meeting the edge of the city.

name: Edinburgh Airport
blurb: Scotland's busiest airport, west of the city. Look north for the three Forth bridges side by side, including the red cantilever Forth Bridge of 1890, and Arthur's Seat rising out of the city.

name: Birmingham Airport
blurb: East of Birmingham, right next to the National Exhibition Centre. Look for the NEC's big halls around a lake beside the runway, with the city's spread of brick suburbs to the west.

name: Harry Reid International Airport
blurb: Sits right at the south end of the Strip, so you see the casinos on approach. Look for the black glass pyramid of the Luxor just northwest, and at night its beam pointing straight up.

name: Tashkent International Airport
blurb: Sits inside Tashkent, Central Asia's largest city, just south of the center. Look for the green grid of the city and the snowy Tian Shan foothills on the horizon to the northeast.

name: Phu Cat Airport
blurb: A former US air base from the Vietnam War, now the airport for the coastal city of Quy Nhon. Look for the runway on dry plains a few miles inland from the sea.

name: Würzburg Residence
blurb: A baroque prince-bishop's palace whose staircase ceiling by Tiepolo is often called the largest fresco in the world. Look for the U-shaped palace around a big forecourt at the edge of the old town.

name: Palais des Papes
blurb: One of the largest Gothic palaces in Europe, home to the popes in Avignon in the 1300s. Look for the fortress walls on the rock above the Rhône, near the old bridge that stops halfway across.

name: Reales Alcázares
blurb: Seville's royal palace, still used by the Spanish royal family, a Mudéjar maze of courtyards and gardens that played Dorne in Game of Thrones. Look for the walled gardens just south of the cathedral.

name: Durham Castle
blurb: A Norman castle begun in the 1070s that now houses university students, sharing a hilltop with the cathedral. Look for both inside a tight wooded loop of the River Wear.

name: Arena Pantanal
blurb: Cuiabá's arena, built for the 2014 World Cup in the city closest to the geographic center of South America. Look for the boxy stadium in the hot, flat savanna city.

name: Stade Bollaert-Delelis
blurb: RC Lens' stadium seats around 38,000, more than the population of Lens itself, a former coal-mining town. Look for the steep boxy stands in town, with the mining slag heaps nearby.

name: Cardiff City Stadium
blurb: Cardiff City's home since 2009, built opposite the site of its old Ninian Park ground. Look for the boxy stadium beside the railway in west Cardiff.

name: Astana Arena
blurb: A 30,000-seat stadium with a retractable roof, essential in a capital where winters drop well below 0 F. Look for the round dome on the steppe-flat south side of Astana.

name: Al Thumama Stadium
blurb: Shaped like the gahfiya, the woven cap worn by Arab men. Look for the round white dome with a lattice pattern in south Doha.

name: Tarczyński Arena Wrocław
blurb: Wrocław's Euro 2012 stadium, wrapped in a translucent skin that glows at night. Look for the rounded box on the city's northwest edge beside the ring road.

name: Malta International Airport
