blurb: Malta's only airport, in the south of the main island. Look for honey-colored stone villages pressing on the runways and the fortified harbors of Valletta a few miles northeast.

name: Montréal–Trudeau International Airport
blurb: Montreal's main airport, in Dorval about 12 miles west of downtown, took back international flights from far-off Mirabel in the 1990s. Look for Mount Royal rising in the middle of the island.

name: Sofia Airport
blurb: Sofia's airport, on the eastern edge of the city, with Vitosha mountain rising to about 7,500 ft just south of town. Look for the runway between the city grid and the Balkan range to the north.

name: Larnaca International Airport
blurb: Sits beside the Larnaca Salt Lake, which floods in winter and draws flocks of flamingos. Look for the white, sometimes pink, salt lake next to the runway and the old mosque on its shore.

name: Bahrain International Airport
blurb: On Muharraq Island just off Bahrain's main island, home base of Gulf Air. Look for the airport bordered by reclaimed land, causeways and turquoise shallows of the Gulf.

name: George Bush Intercontinental Airport
blurb: Houston's largest airport, about 20 miles north of downtown. Look for five runways cut through thick pine forest, with the terminals clustered in the middle.

name: Chennai International Airport
blurb: One of India's busiest airports, in Chennai's southwest suburbs. Look for St. Thomas Mount, a small hill beside the runway, and the long Marina Beach on the Bay of Bengal to the east.

name: OR Tambo International Airport
blurb: One of Africa's busiest airports sits on the Highveld at about 5,500 ft. The thin air calls for a runway about 14,500 ft long. Look for flat-topped gold-mine dumps along the ridge to the southwest.

name: King Khalid International Airport
blurb: Riyadh's airport covers about 87 square miles of desert, much of it empty buffer. The terminals are arranged around a large mosque; look for the cluster of triangular buildings in the middle of open sand.

name: Antalya Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Turkish Riviera and one of Turkey's busiest airports in summer. Look for the Taurus Mountains rising steeply behind the coast and the long hotel-lined beaches of Lara to the south.

name: Tbilisi International Airport
blurb: Georgia's main airport, on a dry plain east of Tbilisi. Look for the runway with the city spread along the Kura River to the west and the Caucasus on the northern horizon.

name: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport
blurb: Bali's gateway, a single runway across the narrow isthmus south of Kuta. Look for the end of the runway built out into the sea on reclaimed land, with beaches lining the shore on either side.

name: Ljubljana Jože Pučnik Airport
blurb: Sits at Brnik about 15 miles north of Ljubljana, right below the Kamnik Alps. It is named for Jože Pučnik, a dissident who helped lead Slovenia to independence. Look for the peaks just north of the runway.

name: Cologne Bonn Airport
blurb: Once the government airport for Bonn, now one of Germany's largest cargo hubs. Look for the runways in the Wahner Heide heathland, with Cologne Cathedral and the Rhine to the northwest.

name: Citadel of Salah Ed-Din
blurb: A Crusader castle on a ridge between two ravines, where builders cut a ditch nearly 90 ft deep through solid rock and left one needle of stone to carry a bridge. Saladin took it anyway in 1188.

name: Palace of the Parliament
blurb: Ceaușescu's palace, one of the largest and heaviest buildings in the world. Look for the massive white block at the end of a long boulevard.

name: Gyeongbokgung
blurb: Seoul's main Joseon palace, built in 1395, under Bugaksan mountain. Look for the large walled courtyards at the end of Gwanghwamun Square with green mountains behind.

name: Livadia Palace
blurb: Site of the 1945 Yalta Conference, where Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin settled the shape of postwar Europe. Look for the white palace on a hillside above the sea just outside Yalta.

name: Stadio Luigi Ferraris
blurb: One of Italy's oldest grounds, in use since 1911 and shared by Genoa and Sampdoria. Look for the boxy red stadium with corner towers wedged in the narrow Bisagno valley.

name: Arena Lviv
blurb: Built for Euro 2012 on Lviv's southern edge, a modern bowl surrounded by open fields. Look for the oval roof standing apart from the city.

name: Niedersachsenstadion
blurb: Hannover 96's stadium beside the Maschsee lake, a 1974 and 2006 World Cup venue. Look for the bowl right next to the long artificial lake south of the city center.

name: Arena das Dunas
blurb: Natal's 2014 World Cup stadium, its roof built of curved panels meant to evoke the area's sand dunes. Look for the white petal-like shell in the city's south.

name: Arena Cidade da Copa
blurb: Built for the 2014 World Cup in São Lourenço da Mata, out in the countryside west of Recife. Look for the oval set alone among green fields and new roads.

name: Allianz Riviera
blurb: OGC Nice's stadium, opened in 2013, its roof and skin a translucent membrane over a lattice of wood and steel. Look for it in the Var valley west of Nice, a few miles from the airport's runways on the sea.

name: Stadio Renzo Barbera
blurb: Palermo's stadium, set at the foot of Monte Pellegrino. Look for the open bowl in the north of the city with the rocky mountain rising just behind it.

name: Elland Road
blurb: Leeds United's home since 1919. Look for the big boxy stadium beside the M621 motorway, south of the city center.

name: Karaiskakis Stadium
blurb: Olympiacos's stadium in Piraeus, on the site where 21 fans died in a crush at Gate 7 in 1981. Look for the red stadium by the shore near Neo Faliro.

name: Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport
blurb: Named for radio pioneer Guglielmo Marconi, a Bologna native. Look for the runway northwest of the city, with the red-roofed old center and its medieval towers a few miles southeast.

name: Marseille Provence Airport
blurb: Sits beside the Étang de Berre, a big saltwater lagoon, next to Airbus Helicopters' main factory. Look for the runways right on the lagoon shore, with refineries along the water.

name: Palma de Mallorca Airport
blurb: One of Spain's busiest airports in summer, on the Bay of Palma just east of the city. Look for Palma's Gothic cathedral on the waterfront and the long hotel-lined beach of the Platja de Palma.

name: John Paul II International Airport Kraków-Balice
blurb: Named for Pope John Paul II, who was archbishop of Kraków before he became pope. It sits about 7 miles west of the old city, on rolling farmland above the Vistula valley.

name: Baghdad International Airport
blurb: Built in the 1980s as Saddam International, it was seized by US forces in 2003 and renamed. Look for the long runways west of Baghdad, with the palace lakes of the former Camp Victory alongside.

name: Sharm el-Sheikh International Airport
blurb: The gateway to the Red Sea reefs at the southern tip of Sinai. Look for bright turquoise water fringed with coral, resorts along the shore and the rust-red mountains behind.

name: Rome Ciampino Airport
blurb: Rome's older airport, now a budget-airline base at the foot of the Alban Hills. Look for the ancient Appian Way and the arches of Roman aqueducts crossing the green fields just northwest.

name: Podgorica Airport
blurb: Montenegro's capital airport, just south of Podgorica. Look for the runway on the flat Zeta plain, with Lake Skadar, the largest lake in the Balkans, spreading to the south.

name: Amber Fort
blurb: A hilltop fort-palace of honey-colored stone above Maota Lake, northeast of Jaipur. Look for walls snaking along the ridges up to Jaigarh Fort.

name: Sforza Castle
blurb: The 15th-century fortress of the dukes of Milan, now museums holding Michelangelo's last Pietà. Look for the square brick castle with a tall gate tower, Sempione Park spreading behind it.

name: Metalist Stadium
blurb: Kharkiv's main ground, rebuilt as a Euro 2012 venue. Look for the rectangular stands set among Soviet-era housing blocks in the city's southeast.

name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
blurb: Main venue of the 1952 Olympics. Its slender white tower, about 240 ft tall, is one of Helsinki's landmarks. Look for the white functionalist bowl and its tower in the parkland north of downtown.

name: Stadio Artemio Franchi
blurb: Pier Luigi Nervi's 1931 concrete stadium, home of Fiorentina, with a slender Marathon Tower and a famous cantilevered roof. Look for the D-shaped plan in the Campo di Marte district.

name: Stadium Municipal
blurb: Toulouse FC's stadium sits on an island in the Garonne River, the Île du Ramier, and hosted 1998 World Cup matches. Look for the stadium wrapped by river channels just south of the city center.

name: Charlotte Douglas International Airport
blurb: American Airlines' second-biggest hub. Look for the parallel north-south runways and the Charlotte skyline about 6 miles northeast, with the arms of Lake Wylie to the southwest.

name: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport
blurb: Kolkata's airport has an old mosque on its land so close to a runway that the airfield was built around it. Look for flat, watery delta country and the city's dense sprawl to the southwest.

name: Ankara Esenboğa Airport
blurb: Serves the capital, Ankara, from the dry Anatolian steppe about 18 miles northeast of the city. Look for bare tan hills and wheat fields stretching in every direction.

name: Sarajevo International Airport (SJJ)
blurb: During the 1992 to 1995 siege, the runway cut besieged Sarajevo off from free territory, and residents dug a tunnel underneath it to bring in food and weapons. Look for the runway in the valley below the Igman ridge.

name: Philadelphia International Airport
blurb: Built along the Delaware River in south Philadelphia. Look for the old Navy Yard, the stadiums of the Eagles, Phillies, Flyers and 76ers just northeast, and the downtown skyline beyond.

name: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport
blurb: Terminal 3, designed by Massimiliano Fuksas, has a honeycomb skin and is shaped like a manta ray. Look for that long white shell beside the runways on reclaimed land along the Pearl River estuary.

name: Bandaranaike International Airport
blurb: Sri Lanka's main gateway sits at Katunayake, about 20 miles north of Colombo. Look for the wide Negombo Lagoon just west of the runway, laced with fishing boats and mangroves.

name: Chișinău International Airport
blurb: Moldova's main airport, southeast of Chișinău, in one of Europe's least-visited countries. Look for the single runway among rolling vineyards and farmland.

name: Almaty International Airport
blurb: Kazakhstan's busiest airport, on the plain northeast of Almaty. Look for the snowy wall of the Trans-Ili Alatau rising behind the city, with peaks around 16,000 ft.

name: Orlando International Airport
blurb: Sprawls over a huge area southeast of Orlando, the main gateway to Walt Disney World. Look for four parallel runways and the central terminal surrounded by lakes and wetlands.

name: Kazan International Airport
blurb: Serves Kazan, capital of Tatarstan, on the Volga. Look for the wide river and, in the city, the white walls of the Kazan Kremlin above the riverbank.

name: Muscat International Airport
blurb: Oman's main airport, with a huge terminal opened in 2018 on the coastal plain. Look for the bare, dark Hajar Mountains rising behind Muscat.

name: Hurghada International Airport
blurb: Serves a strip of Red Sea resorts on the Egyptian coast. Look for the runway in bare desert, with turquoise reefs and a long line of hotels along the shore.

name: Mehrabad International Airport
blurb: Tehran's original airport, now swallowed by the city and used mostly for domestic flights. Look for the runways inside the sprawl, with the white Azadi Tower standing just east at the end of a main avenue.

name: Toompea Castle
blurb: The hilltop castle above Tallinn's Old Town now houses Estonia's parliament. Look for the pink baroque facade on the limestone bluff over the medieval red rooftops.

name: Khotyn Fortress
blurb: Stone walls and towers on the bank of the Dniester, where a Polish-Lithuanian army held off the Ottomans in 1621. Look for the fortress on the cliff edge above a sweep of the river.

name: Shanhai Pass
blurb: The fortified pass where the Great Wall meets the sea, long called the First Pass Under Heaven. Look for the wall running south to the coast, ending at Old Dragon's Head in the Bohai.

name: Royal Castle in Warsaw
blurb: Blown up by the Germans in 1944 and rebuilt from rubble in the 1970s. Look for the salmon-colored palace with a clock tower on Castle Square above the Vistula.

name: Stirling Castle
blurb: Perched on a volcanic crag that guarded the main crossing between Lowland and Highland Scotland. Look for the castle on its cliff above the flat Forth valley, with the Wallace Monument tower on a hill to the northeast.

name: Volkswagen Arena
blurb: VfL Wolfsburg's stadium, across the canal from Volkswagen's giant main factory, the club's owner. Look for the arena by the Mittelland Canal and the plant's four tall brick chimneys.

name: Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport
blurb: One of three big airports serving Baltimore and Washington, set among woods south of Baltimore. Look for the Chesapeake's inlets to the east and the trail that loops all the way around the airport.

name: Queen Alia International Airport
blurb: Jordan's main airport, about 20 miles south of Amman on the desert plateau. Look for the terminal roof by Foster + Partners: a grid of shallow concrete domes meant to echo Bedouin tents.

name: Pyongyang International Airport
blurb: North Korea's main airport, served by only a handful of flights a week, mostly Air Koryo. Look for the large terminal opened in 2015 and the runway sitting nearly empty among farm fields.

name: Entebbe International Airport
blurb: Sits on a peninsula in Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake. In 1976 Israeli commandos flew here to free hostages from a hijacked airliner. Look for the lake's open water almost all around.

name: M. R. Štefánik Airport
blurb: Named for Milan Rastislav Štefánik, a Slovak astronomer and general. Bratislava and Vienna are only about 35 miles apart, the closest pair of national capitals in Europe outside Rome and the Vatican.

name: Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport
blurb: Bangladesh's main airport, on the northern edge of Dhaka, one of the most densely populated cities on Earth. Look for the runway surrounded by packed neighborhoods, lakes and rivers on a flat delta plain.

name: Kuwait International Airport
blurb: Kuwait's only international airport, south of the city in flat desert. Look for the huge three-armed Terminal 2, by Foster + Partners, beside the older terminals.

name: Perth Airport
blurb: Home of the nonstop flights to London, among the longest scheduled routes in the world at about 17 hours. Look for crossed runways on sandy plain between the Swan River and the hills of the Darling Range.

name: Luxembourg Airport
blurb: The Grand Duchy's only airport, on a plateau east of the city, home of Cargolux, one of Europe's biggest cargo airlines. Look for rows of 747 freighters by the long runway.

name: Sochi International Airport
blurb: Gateway to the 2014 Winter Olympics, on the Black Sea coast at Adler. Look for the Olympic Park's stadium and arenas on the shore just southeast, with the Caucasus rising inland.

name: Vágar Airport
blurb: Built by the British in World War II, it is the only airport in the Faroe Islands. Look for nearby lake Sørvágsvatn, which seems to hover above the ocean from certain angles, ending at sea cliffs.

name: Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport
blurb: Zhengzhou's airport sits beside a huge Foxconn plant that assembles a large share of the world's iPhones. Look for the runways among flat fields on the North China Plain.

name: Skopje International Airport
blurb: North Macedonia's main airport, east of Skopje. Look for the bare hills ringing the valley and the Vardar River running through the city to the west.

name: Eindhoven Airport
blurb: Shares its runway with a big Dutch air force base, home of Europe's joint air transport command. Look for it west of Eindhoven, the city Philips built.

name: Hannover Airport
blurb: Hannover's airport, north of the city on flat lowland. Look for the parallel runways among fields and woods, with the city's trade fair grounds, among the largest in the world, to the south.

name: Lake Retba
blurb: Lac Rose: algae that thrive in its extreme saltiness tint the water pink, and workers wade in to harvest salt by hand. It was long the finish of the Dakar Rally. Look for the pink oval behind the dunes.

name: Zwinger
blurb: Dresden's baroque palace complex of galleries around a garden courtyard, rebuilt after the 1945 firebombing. Look for the rectangular courtyard of lawns and fountains near the Elbe.

name: Brighton Community Stadium
blurb: Brighton's home since 2011, under the green South Downs at Falmer, with curved roofs that rise to the sides. Look for the white swoop of the stadium beside the university campuses north of the city.

name: Al Janoub Stadium
blurb: Designed by Zaha Hadid, its curved roof is meant to evoke the sails of traditional dhow boats. Look for the swooping shell in Al Wakrah, south of Doha.

name: Weserstadion
blurb: Werder Bremen's stadium on the bank of the Weser, its facade and roof covered in solar panels. Look for the stadium right on the river east of the old town.

name: Bramall Lane
blurb: Sheffield United's home has hosted football since 1862, the oldest major stadium in the world still hosting professional matches. Look for the boxy stadium south of Sheffield's center.

name: City Ground
blurb: Nottingham Forest's home on the south bank of the River Trent, facing Notts County's Meadow Lane across the water: the two closest league grounds in England. Look for both on the river.

name: BayArena
blurb: Bayer Leverkusen's stadium, the club founded by workers of the Bayer chemical company. Look for the compact stadium with its curved roof, near the Rhine and the sprawling Bayer works.

name: Red Bull Arena
blurb: Home of Red Bull Salzburg, a regular in the Champions League. Look for the stadium in the flat outskirts west of Salzburg, near the airport.

name: Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport
blurb: Chengdu's original airport, southwest of the city on the flat, fertile Sichuan Basin. Look for two parallel runways surrounded by dense suburbs; mountains rim the basin on clear days.

name: Princess Juliana International Airport
blurb: Landings pass only a few dozen feet over Maho Beach, where sunbathers line up to be blasted by jet wash. Look for the strip of sand right at the runway's end, with crowds by the fence.

name: Belfast International Airport
blurb: Northern Ireland's main airport, at Aldergrove about 15 miles from Belfast. Look west for Lough Neagh, at about 150 square miles the largest lake in the British Isles.

name: Bristol Airport
blurb: Sits on a hilltop at about 620 ft south of Bristol, which makes low cloud and fog a regular problem. Look north for the city and the Severn estuary with its two long bridges to Wales.

name: Pisa International Airport 'Galileo Galilei'
blurb: Tuscany's busiest airport, shared with a military base and barely a mile from Pisa. On approach, look for the white marble of the Field of Miracles, with the cathedral and Leaning Tower in the city's northwest corner.

name: Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport
blurb: Lebanon's only commercial airport, on the Mediterranean shore south of Beirut. Look for a runway built out into the sea, with the city's crowded hills just north.

name: Brisbane Airport
blurb: Built on reclaimed flats beside Moreton Bay. Its second runway, opened in 2020, sits on millions of tons of sand pumped up from the bay floor. Look for the Brisbane River mouth just to the south.

name: Auckland Airport
blurb: New Zealand's busiest airport, on the shore of the Manukau Harbour. Look for the dozens of grassy volcanic cones dotting Auckland and the Sky Tower's needle to the north.

name: Naples International Airport
blurb: One of Europe's closest airports to a city center, in Naples' northern districts. Look for Vesuvius, the volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79, rising about 9 miles southeast.

name: Con Dao Airport
blurb: The islands it serves held one of Vietnam's most notorious prisons, used by both the French and South Vietnam. Look for a short runway squeezed onto a green, mountainous island in open sea.

name: Cape Town International Airport
blurb: Set on the sandy Cape Flats about 12 miles east of the city center. Look west for Table Mountain's long flat top, often draped in a white tablecloth of cloud.

name: Alicante Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Costa Blanca, set just inland from the coast south of Alicante. Look for the Santa Pola salt pans next door, rectangles of water that sometimes turn pink.

name: Jinnah International Airport
blurb: Pakistan's busiest airport, inside Karachi, the country's largest city. Look for the sprawl stretching to the Arabian Sea coast to the southwest.

name: Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
blurb: Squeezed onto the Potomac shore across from the Monuments, it has some of the shortest runways of any big US airport. The river approach follows the Potomac, with the Washington Monument close off the wing.

name: Mohammed V International Airport
blurb: Morocco's main hub, about 20 miles south of Casablanca. On approach, look for the Hassan II Mosque on the ocean shore, its minaret about 690 ft tall, among the tallest in the world.

name: Linderhof Palace
blurb: The smallest of Ludwig II's palaces and the only one he lived to see finished. Look for the white palace with terraced gardens and a long pool in a remote Alpine valley.

name: Château de Vincennes
blurb: A royal castle at the edge of Paris whose keep, about 170 ft tall, is considered the tallest medieval fortified tower in Europe. Look for the long rectangular walls beside the Bois de Vincennes.

name: Khan's Palace
blurb: Seat of the Crimean khans from the 1500s, whose Fountain of Tears inspired a Pushkin poem. Look for low walled courtyards and minarets in the narrow valley of Bakhchysarai.

name: Stade de Genève
blurb: Servette's home since 2003, used for Euro 2008 matches. Look for a compact boxy stadium in the flat south of Geneva near the French border.

name: Stadion Poljud
blurb: Hajduk Split's stadium, opened in 1979, has a roof shaped like a giant seashell, two arched canopies over the long sides. Look for the pale clamshell by the harbor on the north side of Split.

name: Portman Road
blurb: Ipswich Town's home since 1884. Look for the compact stadium close to the town center and rail station, a few minutes' walk from the waterfront.

name: Madeira Cristiano-Ronaldo Airport
blurb: One of the world's trickiest approaches. To lengthen the runway, Madeira built it out over the sea on 180 concrete columns, some about 230 ft tall. Look for the runway on stilts along the cliff coast.

name: Málaga-Costa del Sol
blurb: Opened in 1919, it is often cited as the oldest Spanish airport still in operation. Look for the Costa del Sol's wall of white apartment blocks along the shore and the mountains rising right behind.

name: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport
blurb: Santiago's airport, in Chile's Central Valley northwest of the city. Look for the Andes rising like a wall to the east, often snowcapped, with peaks well over 15,000 ft.

name: Xi'an Xianyang International Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Terracotta Army, set on the loess plain north of the Wei River. Look for the flat-topped earthen mounds dotting the fields around it: tombs of Han dynasty emperors and nobles.

name: Liverpool John Lennon Airport
blurb: Named for John Lennon; its motto, "Above us only sky," is painted on the terminal roof. Look for the wide Mersey estuary beside the runway and the city's waterfront to the north.

name: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport
blurb: Its Reef Runway was built offshore on fill and shares the field with Hickam Air Force Base. Look for the long runway in the turquoise water beside Pearl Harbor.

name: Catania-Fontanarossa Airport
blurb: Sicily's busiest airport, at the foot of Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano. Eruptions sometimes close it with ash. Look for the volcano's broad dark slopes and lava flows rising north of the city.

name: El Dorado International Airport
blurb: At about 8,360 ft, one of the highest major airports in the world, on the Sabana de Bogotá. Look for flat high plain dotted with greenhouses growing cut flowers for export.

name: Noi Bai International Airport
blurb: Hanoi's main airport, about 15 miles north of the city across the Red River. Look for two parallel runways and the long Japanese-built terminal opened in 2015.

name: Cochin International Airport
blurb: In 2015 it became the world's first airport to run entirely on solar power. Look for acres of solar panels laid out beside the runway among Kerala's coconut palms.

name: Salzburg Airport
blurb: A short drive from Mozart's old town and right on the German border. Look for the runway pinned between the city and the Untersberg massif, with the Alps close enough that approaches feel like a valley flight.

name: Manas International Airport
blurb: Kyrgyzstan's main airport, northwest of Bishkek. It hosted a US air base supplying Afghanistan until 2014. Look for the runway on the plain under the snowy wall of the Kyrgyz Range to the south.

name: Damascus International Airport
blurb: Sits in open desert about 15 miles southeast of Damascus, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities. Look for green farmland of the Ghouta oasis fading into bare brown plain.

name: Salt Lake City International Airport
blurb: Its new terminal and concourses opened in 2020, replacing buildings from the 1960s. Look for the Great Salt Lake's shoreline to the west and the Wasatch Range rising abruptly to the east.

name: Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport
blurb: Wedged between Minneapolis, St. Paul and Fort Snelling. Look for the Minnesota River meeting the Mississippi just east of the runways, and the Mall of America to the southeast.

name: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport
blurb: Built at Shamshabad, about 15 miles south of Hyderabad, with one of the longest runways in India. Look for the rocky granite boulder country of the Deccan Plateau around it.

name: Gothenburg-Landvetter Airport
blurb: Landvetter sits about 12 miles east of Gothenburg in forested hills full of small lakes. Look for granite outcrops and dark woods on every side of the runway.

name: Hostomel Airport
blurb: The Antonov company's test airfield, where the An-225 Mriya, the largest airplane ever built, was destroyed in the battle here in February 2022. Look for the runway in pine forest northwest of Kyiv.

name: Bern Airport
blurb: A small airport at Belp in the Aare valley south of Bern. Look for the green river valley leading toward the Bernese Alps, with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau on the horizon.

name: Tenzing-Hillary Airport
blurb: Lukla, often called the world's most dangerous airport: a runway about 1,700 ft long sloping steeply uphill at 9,300 ft, with a cliff at one end and a mountainside at the other. Gateway for Everest treks.

name: Turin Airport
blurb: Turin's airport at Caselle, on the plain north of the city that hosted the 2006 Winter Olympics. Look for the Alps closing in on three sides and the sharp pyramid of Monviso to the southwest on a clear day.

name: Tolmachevo Airport
blurb: Siberia's busiest airport, west of Novosibirsk. Look for the wide Ob River through the city and the huge reservoir called the Ob Sea to the south.

name: Brussels South Charleroi Airport
blurb: Sold by budget airlines as Brussels, it actually sits about 30 miles south near Charleroi, an old coal and steel town. Look for black slag heaps, the conical spoil tips of old mines, around the city.

name: Frankfurt-Hahn Airport
blurb: A former US Air Force base in the Hunsrück hills, sold as Frankfurt yet about 75 miles away. Look for the long runway on a forested ridge far from any city.

name: Leipzig/Halle Airport
blurb: One of Europe's largest cargo airports, DHL's main European hub, busiest overnight. Look for long parallel runways and the huge hub buildings with rows of freighters.

name: Dubai World Central – DWC
blurb: Al Maktoum International, planned to become the world's largest airport. Look for long runways in empty desert southwest of Dubai, near the Jebel Ali port and free zone.

name: Eltz Castle
blurb: Owned by the same family for more than 800 years and hidden in a wooded valley rather than on a hilltop. Look for the cluster of towers on a rock in a forested bend of the Elzbach.

name: Heidelberg Castle
blurb: A red sandstone ruin on the hillside above Heidelberg and the Neckar, wrecked by French troops in the late 1600s and never fully rebuilt. Look for the red ruin above the old town and Old Bridge.

name: Capital One Arena
blurb: Home of the Wizards, Capitals and Mystics, in Chinatown. Look for the big arena roof in the downtown grid, about halfway between the White House and the Capitol.

name: Hwaseong Fortress
blurb: A small palace in central Seoul mixing traditional halls with Western-style stone buildings. Look for the walled grounds across from City Hall.

name: Conwy Castle
blurb: Built by Edward I in just four years in the 1280s, with nearly a mile of town walls still intact. Look for eight round towers at the river mouth, where three bridges cross side by side.

name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
blurb: Begun in 1077, it's one of the largest fully preserved medieval castles in Europe, on a hilltop above Salzburg's old town. Look for the white fortress walls on the ridge beside the Salzach River.

name: Vaduz Castle
blurb: Home of the reigning Prince of Liechtenstein, on a ledge above the capital. Look for the white castle with its square tower on the hillside above Vaduz and the Rhine valley.

name: Stadio Renato Dall'Ara
blurb: Bologna's stadium since 1927, with brick arcades and a tall Marathon Tower. Look for the bowl west of the old town under the green hills of San Luca.

name: Wörthersee Stadion
blurb: Klagenfurt's stadium, built for Euro 2008, and later briefly the site of an art installation that planted a forest on the pitch. Look for it near the east end of the long blue Wörthersee lake.

name: Stade de la Beaujoire
blurb: FC Nantes' stadium, opened in 1984 for the Euro tournament France hosted that year, near the Erdre River. Look for the oval bowl in the northeast of Nantes near the river.

name: Cancún International Airport
blurb: Mexico's second-busiest airport and the gateway to the Caribbean coast. Look east for Cancún's hotel zone, a thin 7-shaped strip of sand and towers between turquoise sea and Nichupté Lagoon.

name: Innsbruck Airport
blurb: One of the most demanding approaches in Europe: a narrow Inn valley with peaks above 7,000 ft on both sides, so pilots need special training to fly in. Look for the runway along the river with the Nordkette wall right above the city.

name: Thessaloniki Airport "Makedonia"
blurb: Its main runway extends out into the Thermaic Gulf. Look for the strip running into the sea south of Thessaloniki, with Mount Olympus visible across the gulf on clear days.

name: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport
blurb: Delta's hub, where the McNamara Terminal's mile-long concourse has a tram running overhead along it. Look for six runways, four of them parallel, among the suburbs southwest of Detroit.

name: Nursultan Nazarbayev International Airport
blurb: Serves Astana, the capital built up from scratch on the steppe since the late 1990s. Look for the futuristic skyline north of the airport, including the giant tilted tent of the Khan Shatyr.

name: Nuremberg Airport
blurb: Nuremberg's airport, on the northern edge of the city. Look for the runway in a clearing of the Sebald Forest, with the old walled city and its castle to the south.

name: Phuket International Airport
blurb: Its runway ends right at Mai Khao Beach, so landing jets pass low over the sand. Look for the long beach on Phuket's northwest coast and the Andaman Sea just past the runway threshold.

name: Bălți International Airport
blurb: A former Soviet military airfield in northern Moldova with little or no scheduled passenger service. Look for the long runway in flat farmland outside Bălți.

name: King Fahd International Airport
blurb: By land area the largest airport in the world, about 300 square miles, roughly the size of neighboring Bahrain. Almost all of it is empty desert around a compact terminal and two runways.

name: Paris–Le Bourget Airport
blurb: Charles Lindbergh landed here in 1927 at the end of the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight. Now a business-jet airport and home of the Paris Air Show. Look for the old aircraft at the Air and Space Museum.

name: Toulouse-Blagnac
blurb: Home of Airbus's final assembly lines, where A350s are put together. Look for the giant hangars beside the runways and freshly painted jets parked on the aprons.

name: José Martí International Airport
blurb: Havana's airport, about 10 miles south of the city among farmland and red soil. Look for the runway in green countryside, with the Malecón seawall and the old city on the coast to the north.

name: Kunming Changshui International Airport
blurb: Kunming's airport sits at about 6,900 ft, one of the highest major airports in China. Look for its huge terminal, one of the largest in the country, and red earth in the hills around.

name: Tunis–Carthage International Airport
blurb: Sits just a few miles from the ruins of ancient Carthage, Rome's great rival. Look for the shallow Lake of Tunis, crossed by a causeway, between the airport and the white medina.

name: Circuit Zandvoort
blurb: Carved into the coastal dunes a few hundred yards from the North Sea, it returned to F1 in 2021 with steeply banked corners. Look for the track winding through sand hills right behind the beach town.

name: Pena Palace
blurb: A 19th-century Romantic palace painted red and yellow on a hilltop above Sintra. Look for its colors poking out of the forested ridge.

name: Eggenberg Castle, Graz
blurb: A baroque palace laid out as a model of the cosmos: four corner towers for the seasons, 365 windows for the days, 24 state rooms for the hours. Look for the square palace with corner towers in a big park on the west edge of Graz.

name: Caernarfon Castle
blurb: Edward I's showpiece, begun in 1283 with banded walls and many-sided towers, and the site of the 1969 investiture of the Prince of Wales. Look for it at the mouth of the Seiont on the Menai Strait.

name: Hermann Castle
blurb: Narva's castle faces Russia's Ivangorod fortress across the narrow Narva River, two medieval strongholds staring at each other over what is now the EU's eastern border. Look for the square tower right on the riverbank.

name: Swallow's Nest
blurb: A tiny neo-Gothic castle built in 1912 right at the edge of a sea cliff about 130 ft high. Look for the little white turret perched over the Black Sea west of Yalta.

name: Mukden Palace
blurb: The palace of the early Qing rulers in Shenyang before they took Beijing in 1644, a smaller cousin of the Forbidden City. Look for walled courtyards and yellow-tiled roofs in the old center.

name: Kuressaare Castle
blurb: On Saaremaa island, one of the best-preserved medieval castles in the Baltics, a square 14th-century stone fortress. Look for the square keep inside star-shaped earthen ramparts and a moat near the shore.

name: Baku Crystal Hall
blurb: Built in a matter of months to host the 2012 Eurovision Song Contest, on a point jutting into the Caspian Sea. At night its facade lights up in shifting colors; look for it beside the giant flagpole on the waterfront.

name: Royal Palaces of Abomey
blurb: Earthen palaces of the kings of Dahomey, built from the 1600s to the 1800s and now a UNESCO site. Look for low compounds with rust-red earth walls in the town of Abomey.

name: Fritz Walter Stadium
blurb: Kaiserslautern's stadium on the Betzenberg, a hill above the city, named for the captain of West Germany's 1954 World Cup winners. Look for the stadium perched on the hilltop.

name: Philips Stadion
blurb: PSV's home in central Eindhoven, named for the electronics company that founded the club in 1913. Look for a boxy stadium tucked into the city's street grid, unusual for being right downtown.

name: Carriel Sur International Airport
blurb: Serves Concepción and Talcahuano near the mouth of the Biobío, Chile's widest river. Look for the runway among wetlands and pine plantations a short way from the Pacific coast.

name: Cardiff Airport
blurb: Wales's main airport, at Rhoose on the cliffs above the Bristol Channel. Look for the channel's brown, fast-moving tidal water, among the world's biggest tides, and Somerset across it.

name: Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International Airport
blurb: Sits between the Atlantic and the Everglades, right next to the cruise terminals of Port Everglades. Look for the elevated runway that crosses over a highway and railroad tracks.

name: Ürümqi Tianshan International Airport
blurb: Ürümqi is often called the city farthest from any ocean on Earth, over 1,500 miles inland. Look for the snowy Tian Shan rising south of the city and desert beyond.

name: Faro Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Algarve, set on the edge of the Ria Formosa lagoon. Look for the maze of barrier islands, tidal channels and rectangular salt pans spreading out along the coast.

name: Berlin-Tempelhof Airport
blurb: Hub of the 1948 to 1949 Berlin Airlift, closed in 2008 and now a huge park where Berliners bike and skate on the old runways. Look for the curved terminal, one of the largest buildings in the world.

name: Tenerife South Airport
blurb: Opened in 1978, partly in response to the fog-bound Los Rodeos disaster of 1977 on the island's north side. Look inland for Mount Teide, Spain's highest peak at about 12,200 ft.

name: Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport
blurb: Chongqing's main airport, on hills north of a mountainous megacity of more than 30 million in its municipality. Look for multiple runways cut into terraced green hills and fields.

name: Nanjing Lukou International Airport
blurb: Jiangsu's main airport, about 20 miles south of Nanjing. Look for two parallel runways among farmland and canals, with the Yangtze curving past the city to the north.

name: Svalbard Airport
blurb: The world's northernmost airport with scheduled flights, at about 78 degrees north. Look for the snowy peaks and glaciers around Isfjorden and the colored houses of Longyearbyen.

name: Gran Canaria Airport
blurb: Shares its field with the Gando air base on Gran Canaria's dry east coast. Look south for the Maspalomas dunes, a patch of golden Sahara-like sand on the island's tip.

name: Don Mueang International Airport
blurb: One of the oldest airports in Asia, flying since 1914. Look for the golf course laid out between its two parallel runways, a famously unusual use of the infield.

name: Paphos International Airport
blurb: Western Cyprus's airport, on a coastal plain near Paphos. Look for the runway right by the sea with banana plantations and farm terraces around it.

name: Julius Nyerere International Airport
blurb: Named for Julius Nyerere, Tanzania's founding president. It sits about 8 miles southwest of Dar es Salaam; look for the harbor and the turquoise Indian Ocean shoreline lined with palms.

name: London Southend Airport
blurb: A small airport on the north shore of the Thames estuary. Look for the estuary's mudflats and Southend Pier, the longest pleasure pier in the world at about 1.3 miles.

name: Girona-Costa Brava Airport
blurb: A low-cost gateway to the Costa Brava, about 60 miles north of Barcelona. Look for wooded hills and farmland around the runway and the rocky, cove-cut coast to the east.

name: Odesa International Airport
blurb: Serves the Black Sea port of Odesa from the city's southwest edge. Closed to civilian flights since Russia's 2022 invasion. Look for the long sandy coast and the estuaries (limans) on either side of the city.

name: Dortmund Airport
blurb: A small airport on the eastern edge of Dortmund, mostly budget flights. Look for the runway among fields, with the Ruhr cities running together to the west.

name: Circuit Paul Ricard
blurb: Known for its red and blue striped runoff areas, which replace gravel. Look for the long Mistral straight on a high limestone plateau above the Mediterranean.

name: Circuit of the Americas
blurb: Turn 1 climbs a 133-ft hill, the steepest on the F1 calendar. Look for the red observation tower and the track a few miles from the Austin airport runways.

name: Miramare Castle
blurb: Built in the 1850s and 1860s for Archduke Maximilian, later executed as Emperor of Mexico. Look for the white castle on a rocky point over the Gulf of Trieste.

name: Rosenborg Castle
blurb: Built by King Christian IV in the early 1600s, it still holds the Danish crown jewels. Look for the red-brick Renaissance castle and its formal garden in central Copenhagen.

name: Nippon Budōkan
blurb: Built for judo at the 1964 Olympics, made famous by the Beatles in 1966. Look for the octagonal roof crowned with a golden ornament in Kitanomaru Park by the Imperial Palace.

name: Malmö Arena
blurb: Malmö's indoor arena, opened in 2008, which hosted Eurovision in 2013 and 2024. Look for the boxy building in the new Hyllie district, by the rail line toward the Øresund Bridge.

name: Kamianets-Podilskyi Castle
blurb: A castle on a rock bridge over a deep canyon of the Smotrych River, which loops almost all the way around the old town. Look for the towers at the neck of the river loop.

name: Gripsholm Castle
blurb: Gustav Vasa began this red-brick castle in 1537; it now holds Sweden's national portrait collection. Look for the round towers on a point in Lake Mälaren beside the small town of Mariefred.

name: Lubart's Castle
blurb: A 14th-century brick castle in Lutsk's old town, named for the Lithuanian prince who built it. Look for the square of red walls with three towers on a bend of the Styr river.

name: Belgrade Arena
blurb: One of Europe's larger indoor arenas, it hosted the 2008 Eurovision Song Contest and big basketball finals. Look for a huge oval roof in the gridded towers of New Belgrade, across the Sava from the old city.

name: Stade de la Mosson
blurb: Montpellier HSC's stadium, named for the river beside it, which flooded the pitch badly in 2014. Look for the bowl in the city's western suburbs by the riverbank.

name: Coventry Building Society Arena
blurb: Coventry's stadium opened in 2005 north of the city, with an exhibition hall and casino built in. Look for the big boxy stadium beside the M6 motorway.

name: Julio Martínez Prádanos National Stadium
blurb: Chile's national stadium, host of the 1962 World Cup final, was used as a detention and torture center after the 1973 coup. Look for the oval bowl in Ñuñoa, with the Andes rising behind Santiago.

name: Estádio Nilton Santos
blurb: Built for the 2007 Pan American Games and the athletics venue of the 2016 Olympics, now home of Botafogo. Look for the roof hung from four big arches, one over each corner.

name: Anoeta Stadium
blurb: Real Sociedad's ground in San Sebastián, where the old running track was removed and the stands pushed to the pitch around 2019. Look for a tidy box beside the Urumea River south of the city center.

name: RCDE Stadium
blurb: Espanyol's home since 2009, a few miles from Barcelona's El Prat airport. Look for the boxy stadium amid suburban sprawl and motorways between the city and the airport.

name: Tofiq Bahramov Stadium
blurb: Baku's Republican stadium, named for the linesman who allowed England's disputed third goal in the 1966 World Cup final. Look for the classic oval with a colonnaded entrance north of the city center.

name: Graz Airport
blurb: Styria's airport, on the flat Mur valley floor just south of Graz. Look for the runway among fields and villages, with wooded hills rising on both sides of the valley.

name: Velana International Airport
blurb: On its own island, Hulhulé, next to Malé, one of the most densely packed capitals on Earth. Look for the runway filling a strip of reclaimed land, the Sinamalé Bridge, and turquoise reef flats all around.

name: Leeds Bradford Airport
blurb: At about 680 ft, the highest airport in England, perched on a ridge between Leeds and Bradford. Look for Yorkshire's stone-walled fields and the moors to the north and west.

name: Vladivostok International Airport
blurb: Russia's main Pacific gateway, about 25 miles north of Vladivostok near the head of Amur Bay. Look for the long peninsula of the city to the south, hung with bridges.

name: Shannon Airport
blurb: Once the transatlantic refueling stop, it opened the world's first duty-free shop in 1947, and Irish coffee was invented at the nearby Foynes flying-boat base. Look for the long runway on the Shannon Estuary's north shore.

name: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport
blurb: On Mauritius's southeast coast near Mahébourg. Look for the turquoise lagoon inside the reef right beside the runway, and the jagged volcanic peaks of the island's interior.

name: Tampa International Airport
blurb: Pioneered the landside-airside design in 1971: a central terminal with shuttle trains to separate airside buildings. Look for the satellites around the central hub beside Old Tampa Bay.

name: Kyiv Zhuliany International Airport
blurb: Kyiv's smaller city airport sits inside the city, only about 5 miles from the center. Closed to civilian flights since 2022. Look for the Dnipro River and the gold domes of the old city to the east.

name: Francisco de Sá Carneiro Airport
blurb: Porto's airport sits near the Atlantic about 7 miles north of the city and is regularly voted one of Europe's best. Look south for the Douro River cutting through the city to the sea.

name: Murtala Muhammed International Airport
blurb: Nigeria's busiest airport, on the Lagos mainland. Look for the sprawl of one of Africa's largest cities, its lagoons, and the long Third Mainland Bridge curving across to Lagos Island.

name: Christchurch International Airport
blurb: Base for the US and New Zealand Antarctic programs, so military planes fly to McMurdo from here. Look for the patchwork of the Canterbury Plains and the Southern Alps rising to the west.

name: Jorge Chávez International Airport
blurb: Peru's main gateway sits on the coastal desert in Callao, where it almost never rains. Look for the runway running parallel to the Pacific shore, with Lima's gray sprawl and bare brown hills behind it.

name: Batumi International Airport
blurb: Right on the Black Sea next to Batumi, a few miles from the Turkish border. Look for the runway along the beach, with green mountains rising behind and new high-rises along the shore.

name: San Diego International Airport
blurb: One of the busiest single-runway airports in the US. The approach drops low over downtown and Balboa Park, close enough to see into office windows. Look for the runway between the bay and the city's high-rises.

name: Calgary International Airport
blurb: Its 14,000-ft runway, opened in 2014, is the longest in Canada. Look for the airfield on flat prairie northeast of downtown, with the Rockies lined up on the western horizon on a clear day.

name: Katowice International Airport
blurb: Serves Upper Silesia, Poland's old coal and steel heartland, from Pyrzowice about 20 miles north of Katowice. Look for the runway cut through farmland and forest, with industrial towns to the south.

name: Burgas Airport
blurb: The gateway to Bulgaria's Black Sea resorts such as Sunny Beach. Look for the runway beside shallow coastal lakes and salt pans just north of Burgas, with the long curve of beach beyond.

name: Kaunas Airport
blurb: Lithuania's second airport and a budget-airline base, northeast of Kaunas. Look for the old town to the southwest where the Neris River meets the Nemunas.

name: Reykjavík Airport
blurb: Reykjavík's domestic airport, sitting right in the city. Look for the crossing runways at the edge of downtown, ending near the water, with the city's colorful roofs around them.

name: Split Airport
blurb: Split's airport, squeezed onto a strip of coast between the Bay of Kaštela and limestone hills, close to the old town of Trogir. Approaches skim low over the water.

name: Dubrovnik Ruđer Bošković Airport
blurb: Its runway sits on a plateau above the Adriatic cliffs south of Dubrovnik. Look for the walled old city up the coast and the bare limestone mountains rising right behind the runway.

name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
blurb: Laid out on Île Notre-Dame, an artificial island built for Expo 67 in the St. Lawrence River. Look for the track running beside the straight 1976 Olympic rowing basin, just across from downtown Montreal.

name: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
blurb: Mexico City's F1 track, at about 7,300 ft, where the cars run through a converted baseball stadium. Look for the circuit inside a big park beside the airport, with the stadium bowl on the infield.

name: Bellevue Palace
blurb: The official residence of Germany's president, a white neoclassical palace on the Spree at the edge of the Tiergarten. Look for the white wings around a courtyard facing the river.

name: Acrocorinth
blurb: A fortified rock rising to nearly 1,900 ft above ancient Corinth, with walls ringing the summit. Look for the bare, steep-sided mountain with its line of walls a few miles from the Corinth Canal.

name: Minsk-Arena
blurb: Home of the KHL's Dinamo Minsk, a huge ice arena with a velodrome and speed-skating oval beside it. Look for the round silver dome with a flying-saucer look in the northwest of Minsk.

name: Akershus Fortress
blurb: Oslo's medieval castle and fortress, begun around 1300 on a point in the harbor. Look for the green ramparts and stone walls on the headland just west of the Opera House.

name: Beaumaris Castle
blurb: Edward I's last castle in Wales, begun in 1295 and never finished, yet considered the most perfect concentric castle in Britain. Look for the symmetrical walls-within-walls and moat on Anglesey's shore.

name: Trakai Island Castle
blurb: A red-brick castle from the 1400s on an island in Lake Galvė, west of Vilnius. Look for the red castle on its island, linked to shore by wooden footbridges.

name: Estadio Municipal de Abanca Riazor
blurb: Deportivo La Coruña's ground sits right behind Riazor beach on the Atlantic, one of the most seaside stadiums in Europe. Look for the stadium at the edge of the sand on the city's narrow peninsula.

name: SNP Arena
blurb: TSG Hoffenheim's stadium outside Sinsheim, a town of about 35,000, built with backing from SAP co-founder Dietmar Hopp. Look for the stadium in open fields next to the A6 autobahn.

name: WWK Arena
blurb: FC Augsburg's stadium on the southern edge of the city, opened in 2009. Look for the stadium in open farmland beside the B17 highway.

name: Wuhan Tianhe International Airport
blurb: Wuhan's airport, north of the city on lake-dotted plains near the Yangtze. Look for the runway among fish ponds and lakes.

name: Algiers Houari Boumediene Airport
blurb: Algeria's main airport, on the coastal plain east of Algiers, named for Houari Boumediene, the country's second president. Look for the curve of the Bay of Algiers and the white city climbing the hills to the west.

name: Accra International Airport
blurb: Ghana's main airport, inside Accra near the city center. Look for the runway surrounded by the city, with the Atlantic coast a few miles to the south.

name: Gimpo International Airport
blurb: Seoul's original airport, on the south bank of the Han River in the city's west, now handles mostly domestic and short-haul flights. Look for the wide Han curving toward the Yellow Sea.

name: İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport
blurb: Serves Izmir, Turkey's third-largest city, from just south of the city on the Aegean. Look for the long Gulf of Izmir reaching inland, ringed by hills of apartment blocks.

name: Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa Airport
blurb: Named for Lech Wałęsa, the shipyard electrician who led the Solidarity strikes in Gdańsk in 1980. It sits on wooded hills west of the city, a few miles from the Baltic shore.

name: Rhodes International Airport "Diagoras"
blurb: Rhodes' airport, on the island's northwest coast. Look for the runway right along the shore, with the medieval walled town at the island's northern tip.

name: Allama Iqbal International Airport
blurb: Lahore's airport, east of the city and only about 10 miles from the India border at Wagah. Look for the Ravi River and the red sandstone Badshahi Mosque by the old walled city.

name: Tenerife North Airport
blurb: Site of the deadliest accident in aviation history: in 1977 two Boeing 747s collided on this runway in fog, killing 583 people. Look for the plateau between ridges where clouds often pour through.

name: Zadar Airport
blurb: Zadar's airport, inland from a coastal city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast. Look for the runway among olive groves and stone walls, with long chains of islands lined up offshore.

name: Stockholm Skavsta Airport
blurb: Sold by budget airlines as Stockholm, though it is about 60 miles south of the city near Nyköping. Look for a single runway among farmland, forest and the inlets of the Baltic coast.

name: Verona Villafranca Airport
blurb: Verona's airport, southwest of the city on the Po plain. Look for the Roman arena in the old town to the northeast and the southern shore of Lake Garda about 10 miles to the northwest.

name: Mactan–Cebu International Airport
blurb: Sits on Mactan Island, joined to Cebu City by bridges, and shares its runway with an air base. Terminal 2 has a wavy roof of curved timber arches, designed to feel like a resort.

name: Chania International Airport
blurb: Western Crete's airport, on the Akrotiri peninsula, sharing the field with a Greek military air base. Look for the runway on a rocky headland above Souda Bay, a big natural harbor.

name: Valencia Airport
blurb: At Manises, west of Valencia. Look east for the city and the Turia, an old riverbed turned into a 5-mile park ending at the white, futuristic City of Arts and Sciences.

name: Heraklion International Airport "Nikos Kazantzakis"
blurb: Crete's main airport, right on the coast east of Heraklion, with a runway ending almost at the water. A replacement is being built inland at Kastelli. Look for the strip between the city and the sea.

name: Cork Airport
blurb: Sits on high ground south of Cork at about 500 ft, which makes it notoriously prone to fog. Look for the runway on farmland above the city, with Cork Harbour, one of the world's largest natural harbors, to the east.

name: Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport
blurb: Built on bay fill on the east shore of San Francisco Bay, renamed in 2024 to stress its Bay Area location. Look for the long south runway hugging the water, used by heavy cargo jets.

name: Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport
blurb: Hangzhou's airport sits on flat reclaimed land by the Qiantang River estuary, famous for one of the world's largest tidal bores. Look for the river's huge funnel-shaped mouth opening east.

name: Kutaisi International Airport
blurb: A low-cost base in western Georgia, with a modern terminal by the Dutch firm UNStudio. Look for the runway on the Colchis plain, with the Greater Caucasus rising to the north.

name: Rijeka Airport
blurb: Sits on the island of Krk, linked to the mainland by the Krk Bridge. Look for the runway on the barren, rocky north end of the island and the bridge's big concrete arches.

name: Wrocław – Copernicus Airport
blurb: Named for Copernicus, born in Toruń but claimed across Poland. It sits on flat farmland west of Wrocław, a city threaded with Oder River channels and more than 100 bridges.

name: Peleș Castle
blurb: Romania's royal summer castle, built from 1873 to 1914 in the Carpathians above Sinaia. Look for the turrets in a forested valley.

name: Dover Castle
blurb: The largest castle in England, on top of the White Cliffs, with tunnels below where the 1940 Dunkirk evacuation was planned. Look for the square keep above the cliffs and the busy ferry port.

name: Helsinki Halli
blurb: Finland's biggest indoor arena, opened in 1997 as Hartwall Arena and host of the 2007 Eurovision Song Contest. Look for the big oval roof beside the rail yards north of central Helsinki.

name: Royal Pavilion
blurb: George IV's seaside pleasure palace, remodeled by John Nash in an Indian style in the 1810s and 1820s. Look for the cluster of white onion domes in a garden a few blocks from Brighton's seafront.

name: La Rosaleda Stadium
blurb: Málaga's ground beside the usually dry Guadalmedina riverbed, just north of the old city. Look for the bowl next to the channel among the city's apartment blocks.

name: Quatro de Fevereiro Airport
blurb: Luanda's old airport, now swallowed by the city it serves. Look for the runways boxed in by dense neighborhoods, with the Atlantic and the long Ilha de Luanda sandspit just to the northwest.

name: Ercan International Airport
blurb: Recognized only by Turkey, so every flight to it must touch down in Turkey first. Look for the dry Mesaoria plain of central Cyprus and the jagged Kyrenia range to the north.

name: Beauvais-Tillé Airport
blurb: Sold by budget airlines as Paris, it is more than 50 miles north of the city. Look for the runway among the flat fields of Picardy near the town of Beauvais.

name: Tabriz International Airport
blurb: Northwest Iran's main airport, shared with an air force base on the plain beside Tabriz. Look for the runway with the bare volcanic massif of Mount Sahand to the south.

name: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport
blurb: One of the busiest cargo airports in the world, a refueling stop for freighters on the great-circle route between Asia and North America. Look for Lake Hood next door, the busiest seaplane base anywhere, lined with floatplane docks.

name: Carrasco International Airport
blurb: Its terminal, by Rafael Viñoly, sits under one long, gently curved roof, like a wing. Look for the wide brown Río de la Plata coast and Montevideo's beaches to the west.

name: Adelaide Airport
blurb: Only about 4 miles from downtown Adelaide, unusually close for a state capital, and barely a mile from the beach. Look for the straight line of Gulf St Vincent sand running north and south past Glenelg.

name: Tianjin Binhai International Airport
blurb: Serves Tianjin, the port city about 70 miles southeast of Beijing, from its eastern suburbs. Look for the Hai River winding toward the Bohai Sea and the high-rises of the Binhai new district on the coast.

name: Calicut International Airport
blurb: Built on a leveled hilltop, its tabletop runway drops away at both ends. In 2020 a landing Air India Express 737 overran it in rain and broke apart. Look for the plateau among green Kerala hills.

name: Simferopol International Airport
blurb: Crimea's main airport, north of Simferopol, with a large new terminal opened in 2018. It has been closed to civilian flights since February 2022. Look for the runways on flat steppe farmland.

name: Tivat Airport
blurb: On the shore of the Bay of Kotor, so approaches wind between steep mountains over the fjord-like bay. Look for the walled town of Kotor deep in the inner bay, often with a cruise ship moored off it.

name: Shenyang Taoxian International Airport
blurb: The main airport for Shenyang, the big industrial city of China's northeast. Look for the runway on flat Liaoning farmland south of the city's spreading grid.

name: Chu Lai Airport
blurb: Built by the US Marines in 1965 on beach sand, it still sits right against the coast of Quang Nam. Look for the runway running parallel to a long white beach.

name: Mashhad International Airport
blurb: One of Iran's busiest airports, carrying millions of pilgrims to the Imam Reza shrine, the country's holiest site. Look for the shrine's golden dome in the city center northwest of the runways.

name: Tocumen International Airport
blurb: The biggest hub in Central America and Copa Airlines' base. On approach, look for ships waiting off the Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal and Panama City's towers along the bay.

name: Ibiza Airport
blurb: Sits on the island's flat southern tip beside the Ses Salines salt flats. Look for pink and white evaporation ponds just south of the runway and the long beaches beyond.

name: César Manrique Lanzarote Airport
blurb: Named for César Manrique, the artist who persuaded Lanzarote to stay low, white and unbillboarded. Look for black lava fields and dark volcanic cones, with whitewashed villages on top.

name: Kokshetau International Airport
blurb: A small regional airport on the flat steppe outside Kokshetau in northern Kazakhstan, near the pine-and-lake resort area of Burabay. Look for the lone runway on open grassland.

name: Madurodam
blurb: The Netherlands at 1:25 scale in The Hague, with tiny canals, windmills and an airport. Look for a patch of tiny buildings among dunes near the coast.

name: Pombia Safari Park
blurb: A drive-through safari park in woodland south of Lake Maggiore, close to Milan Malpensa. Look for animal enclosures in clearings among the trees.

name: Jerez-Ángel Nieto Circuit
blurb: Packed every spring for MotoGP, and the scene of the 1997 F1 title decider where Michael Schumacher was disqualified for ramming Jacques Villeneuve. Look for the loop in sherry country outside Jerez.

name: Kroměříž Castle
blurb: The archbishops' baroque palace and gardens are a UNESCO site, and its halls stood in for Vienna in the film Amadeus. Look for the square tower and the geometric Flower Garden at the edge of town.

name: Herrenchiemsee
blurb: Ludwig II's copy of Versailles, built on an island in the Chiemsee, Bavaria's largest lake. He stayed there only about ten days. Look for the palace and long gardens on the wooded island.

name: Corvin Castle
blurb: A Gothic castle on a rock above a stream in Hunedoara, reached by a tall wooden bridge. Look for the pointed roofs beside the old steel works.

name: Warwick Castle
blurb: Founded by William the Conqueror in 1068 on a bluff above the River Avon. Look for the walls and towers on the riverbank beside Warwick's town center, with landscaped parkland stretching south.

name: Norbulingka
blurb: The Dalai Lamas' summer palace, a walled park of pavilions and gardens, from which the 14th Dalai Lama fled in 1959. Look for the green walled park on Lhasa's west side.

name: Konopiště Castle
blurb: Country home of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, whose 1914 assassination set off World War I; thousands of his hunting trophies still line the halls. Look for round towers in woods beside a pond south of Prague.

name: Castel Nuovo
blurb: The medieval castle on Naples's harbor, begun in 1279 under Charles of Anjou. Look for the dark round towers by the ferry port, with Vesuvius across the bay.

name: Elmina Castle
blurb: Built by the Portuguese in 1482, the oldest European building south of the Sahara, later a hub of the Atlantic slave trade. Look for the white fortress on the point beside the fishing harbor.

name: Yanmar Stadium Nagai
blurb: Home of Cerezo Osaka and a 2002 World Cup venue, where Japan beat Tunisia to reach the knockout round. Look for the big bowl in green Nagai Park in southern Osaka.

name: Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi
blurb: Home of Hellas Verona, a 1990 World Cup venue. Look for the open bowl west of the old town, not far from the Roman Arena.

name: Ullevi
blurb: Gothenburg's big 1958 World Cup stadium, now best known for huge concerts; Bruce Springsteen has played it many times. Look for the big oval in the events district east of the center, near the Liseberg amusement park.

name: Stade Chaban-Delmas
blurb: Bordeaux's 1938 stadium, a listed art deco ground and former World Cup venue, now home of the rugby club Union Bordeaux Bègles. Look for the old bowl in the city's western quarter.

name: Asim Ferhatović Hase Stadium
blurb: Sarajevo's Koševo stadium held the opening ceremony of the 1984 Winter Olympics. Look for the oval in a valley on the north side of the city, surrounded by cemeteries from the 1990s siege.

name: Hong Kong Disneyland
blurb: One of Disney's smallest parks, opened in 2005 on reclaimed land at Penny's Bay on Lantau Island. Look for the castle and the lake by the water on Lantau's northeast shore.

name: Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours
blurb: Home of the French Grand Prix from 1991 to 2008, in farm country in central France. Look for the circuit among fields and woods near the Allier River.

name: Oscar and Juan Gálvez Race Track
blurb: Buenos Aires' circuit, where hometown hero Juan Manuel Fangio raced the Argentine Grand Prix. Look for the loops of track around a lake in the city's southern parks.

name: Brands Hatch
blurb: Set in a natural bowl in the Kent countryside, it alternated with Silverstone as home of the British Grand Prix until 1986. Look for the track looping through the woods in a hollow.

name: Devín Castle
blurb: A ruined castle on a cliff above the meeting of the Danube and Morava rivers, a spot that marked the Iron Curtain for decades. Look for the rock spur at the river junction, just west of Bratislava.

name: Accor Arena
blurb: Paris's big indoor arena at Bercy, opened in 1984. Its sloping sides are covered in grass, so it looks like a green pyramid cut off at the top. Look for it on the Seine's right bank by the Finance Ministry.

name: Palácio do Planalto
blurb: The Brazilian president's office, another Niemeyer design with slender curved white columns, on the Three Powers Plaza. Look for the low glass box beside the twin Congress towers.

name: Książ Castle and park complex
blurb: One of Poland's largest castles, on a rocky crag above a gorge. The Nazis dug tunnels under it in World War II. Look for the castle on the forested ridge north of Wałbrzych.

name: Barclays Center
blurb: The Brooklyn Nets' arena, opened in 2012 above a rail yard at Atlantic Avenue. Look for the rust-brown weathered steel lattice and a green planted roof.

name: Estádio Municipal de Braga
blurb: Carved into the face of a granite quarry, with stands only on the two long sides and bare rock at one end. Look for the pitch between two slabs of seating and the cliff.

name: Roazhon Park
blurb: Stade Rennais' stadium beside the Vilaine River, in the west of Rennes. Look for the compact stadium right on the riverbank.

name: Vasil Levski National Stadium
blurb: Bulgaria's national stadium, named for the 19th-century independence hero. Look for the oval in Borisova Gradina, the big park in central Sofia.

name: De Grolsch Veste
blurb: FC Twente's stadium in Enschede, near the German border. Look for a rectangular ground in flat green countryside on the edge of town.

name: Korean International Circuit
blurb: Built on reclaimed land at Yeongam for an F1 race that lasted only four seasons, 2010 to 2013. Look for the large loop on flat ground near the port city of Mokpo.

name: Circuito do Estoril
blurb: Portugal's F1 venue from 1984 to 1996, where Ayrton Senna won his first Grand Prix in pouring rain in 1985. Look for the loop in scrubby hills just inland from the Cascais coast west of Lisbon.

name: Rocket Arena
blurb: The Cleveland Cavaliers' arena, connected to the Guardians' ballpark in the Gateway district. Look for the boxy arena right next to the baseball diamond.

name: Yıldız Palace
blurb: A sprawl of pavilions in a large wooded park, home of Sultan Abdulhamid II in the late 1800s. Look for the big green park on the slope above the Bosporus, behind Beşiktaş.

name: Kalmar Castle
blurb: Once called the key to Sweden, a Renaissance castle on an islet by the town where the Kalmar Union was signed in 1397. Look for the moated castle with round towers by the shore, near the long Öland Bridge.

name: Egeskov Castle
blurb: Europe's best-preserved Renaissance water castle, finished in 1554 and built on oak piles in a small lake. Look for the red castle in its moat, surrounded by hedge mazes and gardens on Funen.

name: Rundāle Palace
blurb: A baroque palace by Rastrelli, architect of St. Petersburg's Winter Palace, out in the Latvian countryside. Look for the U-shaped palace and geometric gardens in flat farmland.

name: Pembroke Castle
blurb: Birthplace of Henry VII in 1457, with a round keep about 75 ft tall. Look for the castle on a rocky ridge with water on three sides, at the end of Pembroke's main street.

name: Nuremberg Castle
blurb: The imperial castle on a sandstone ridge above Nuremberg's old town, where Holy Roman Emperors stayed. Look for the long castle on the hill at the north edge of the walled city.

name: Chehel Sotun
blurb: A 17th-century Safavid pavilion in Isfahan. Its 20 wooden columns reflect in a long pool, which is how it got the name Forty Columns. Look for the long rectangular pool in a walled garden.

name: Estádio D. Afonso Henriques
blurb: Vitória de Guimarães' home, rebuilt for Euro 2004 in the town considered the birthplace of Portugal. Look for the stadium on the edge of the compact town.

name: GelreDome
blurb: Built in 1998 with a roof that closes and a grass pitch that slides out of the stadium on rails to get sunlight, the first of its kind in Europe. Look for it beside the A12 on the edge of Arnhem.

name: Gran Canaria Stadium
blurb: Las Palmas's home since 2003; a 2014 to 2016 rebuild tore out its running track and pulled the stands up to the pitch. Look for the oval on high ground in Las Palmas's upper suburbs, with the Atlantic beaches below.

name: Kashima Soccer Stadium
blurb: Home of Kashima Antlers, one of Japan's most successful clubs, and a 2002 World Cup venue. Look for the square stadium by the coastal steelworks along the Pacific.

name: Stade Maurice Dufrasne
blurb: Standard Liège's home, known as Sclessin, famous for one of the loudest crowds in Belgium. Look for it squeezed between steelworks and the Meuse on the city's industrial south side.

name: Jeonju World Cup Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2002 World Cup, its roof shaped like a traditional folding fan. Home of Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors; look for it among rice paddies on the city's north edge.

name: Namsan Seoul Tower
blurb: A broadcast tower on Namsan, the forested mountain in the middle of Seoul. Look for the spire on a green hill rising from the city.

name: Losail International Circuit
blurb: MotoGP has raced here at night under floodlights since 2008, and F1 joined in 2021. Look for the track on flat desert north of Doha; after dark the whole loop glows.

name: Cecilienhof
blurb: Built to look like an English Tudor country house, it hosted the 1945 Potsdam Conference where Truman, Stalin and Churchill (then Attlee) settled postwar Germany. Look for the half-timbered house in the lakeside park.

name: Palace of Tau
blurb: The archbishop's palace beside Reims Cathedral, where French kings stayed for their coronation feasts. Look for the cathedral's huge Gothic nave and twin towers, with the palace tucked against it.

name: Deoksugung
blurb: An 18th-century fortress wall about 3.5 miles around in Suwon. Look for the wall ringing the old city center and climbing the hill on its west side.

name: Honda Center
blurb: The Anaheim Ducks' arena since 1993, just across the Orange Freeway from Angel Stadium. Look for the glass-fronted oval next to the Santa Ana River channel.

name: Forum di Milano
blurb: Milan's big indoor arena in Assago, home of Olimpia Milano basketball and a venue for the 2026 Winter Olympics. Look for the large box beside the ring road on the southern edge of the city.

name: Saint Michael's Castle
blurb: Emperor Paul I built it as a moated fortress against assassins, then was murdered inside in 1801, about 40 days after moving in. Look for the square reddish castle with an octagonal courtyard.

name: Vorontsov Palace
blurb: A mix of Scottish Gothic and Moorish styles by Edward Blore, backed by the jagged Ai-Petri cliffs; Churchill stayed here during the Yalta Conference. Look for the gray stone palace and terraced park above the sea at Alupka.

name: Hochosterwitz Castle
blurb: A hilltop castle on a lone, steep limestone crag in Carinthia, reached by a road through 14 gates. Look for walls and towers spiraling up the rock above flat farmland.

name: Leeds Castle
blurb: Not in Leeds at all but in Kent, a castle built across two islands in a lake, home over the centuries to six medieval queens. Look for the pale walls rising straight out of the water in rolling parkland.

name: Xiaomi Arena
blurb: Riga's main indoor arena, built for the 2006 Ice Hockey World Championship and home of Dinamo Riga through its KHL years. Look for the large box in the Skanste district just north of the old town.

name: Liechtenstein Castle
blurb: The medieval seat that gave the princely Liechtenstein family its name, long before they had a country. Look for a pale castle on a rock at the edge of the Vienna Woods, just south of the city.

name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
blurb: Home of the Grimaldis, who have ruled Monaco on and off since 1297. Look for the palace on the Rock, the flat headland jutting into the sea beside the yacht-filled port.

name: Arundel Castle
blurb: Founded in 1067 and home to the Dukes of Norfolk for over 400 years. Look for the long battlemented walls and round keep on the hill above the River Arun, beside the town's tall cathedral.

name: Kadriorg Palace
blurb: Peter the Great built this baroque palace in the 1720s for his wife Catherine, and the park around it still bears her name. Look for the red-and-white palace and formal gardens in the green park east of Tallinn's center.

name: Suwon World Cup Stadium
blurb: A 2002 World Cup stadium, home of Suwon Samsung Bluewings, its roof meant to look like a bird spreading its wings. Look for it on the city's east side.

name: Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero
blurb: Elche's ground, built in 1976 and a 1982 World Cup venue. Look for the open bowl on the city's edge, among the palm groves Elche is known for.

name: Q&A Stadium Miyagi
blurb: Miyagi Stadium, built for the 2002 World Cup and used for the Tokyo 2020 Olympic soccer. Look for the crescent roof over the main stand in the hills outside Sendai.

name: Mewa Arena
blurb: Mainz 05's stadium, opened in 2011 on the city's southwestern edge. Look for the stadium among farm fields near the autobahn, away from the old town on the Rhine.

name: Uber Arena
blurb: Berlin's big indoor arena, home of Alba Berlin and Eisbären Berlin, opened in 2008. Look for it on the Spree right next to the East Side Gallery, the longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall.

name: Kaseya Center
blurb: The Miami Heat's arena on Biscayne Bay. Look for the big white roof right on the water, next to Bayside Marketplace and the downtown towers.

name: Haapsalu Castle
blurb: A 13th-century bishop's castle in a small seaside resort on Estonia's west coast, now mostly ruined walls around a park. Look for the long stone ruin and church tower beside the shallow bay.

name: Margat
blurb: A Knights Hospitaller fortress of dark basalt that held out against Saladin. Look for the black walls crowning a triangular hilltop above the Mediterranean coast near Baniyas.

name: Palace of Mafra
blurb: A baroque palace, convent and basilica with a facade about 720 ft wide, paid for with Brazilian gold. Look for the long pale building with twin bell towers in the middle of a small town.

name: Tintagel Castle
blurb: Ruins on a sea-battered Cornish headland tied to the legend of King Arthur's conception. Look for the rocky near-island joined to the mainland by a thin footbridge, opened in 2019 across the chasm.

name: Turku Castle
blurb: Founded around 1280, one of the oldest buildings still in use in Finland, guarding the mouth of the Aura River. Look for the long white stone castle near the harbor and ferry terminals.

name: Prudential Center
blurb: The New Jersey Devils' arena in downtown Newark, opened in 2007. Look for the dark red brick and glass box a few blocks from Newark Penn Station.

name: Palau Sant Jordi
blurb: Barcelona's main indoor arena, designed by Arata Isozaki for the 1992 Olympics, with a low gray dome. Look for the curved roof beside the Olympic stadium on Montjuïc.

name: Ljubljana Castle
blurb: Slovenia's capital grew up around this hilltop castle, reached by a funicular from the old town. Look for the walls and lookout tower on the wooded hill inside the Ljubljanica river bend.

name: National Palace
blurb: Seat of Mexico's president, on the site of Moctezuma's palace, with Diego Rivera's murals in its stairwell. Look for the long red stone facade filling the east side of the Zocalo, one of the largest city squares in the world.

name: Castle of Saint George
blurb: A Moorish castle on a hilltop above Lisbon's Alfama district. Look for the battlements and pine trees on the hill over the old town and the river.

name: Gediminas' Tower
blurb: The last tower of Vilnius's upper castle, on a hill above the old town where the Vilnia meets the Neris. Look for the red-brick octagonal tower and flag on the wooded hill.

name: Putin's Palace
blurb: A huge Italianate palace on the Black Sea cliffs near Gelendzhik, made famous by a 2021 Navalny investigation that tied it to Putin, who denies owning it. Look for the large building above the forested coast.

name: Fenway Park
blurb: Home of the Red Sox since 1912, the oldest ballpark in the majors. Look for the 37-ft Green Monster wall in left field and the odd angles squeezed into city blocks.

name: Denka Big Swan Stadium
blurb: Niigata's World Cup stadium, home of Albirex, named because its white roof suggests a swan. Look for it beside a lagoon in the flat rice plain of Niigata.

name: Wrigley Field
blurb: Home of the Cubs since 1916 and the second-oldest park in the majors, opened in 1914. Look for the ivy-covered outfield walls and rooftop bleachers on the apartment buildings across the street.

name: Ajinomoto Stadium
blurb: Home of FC Tokyo and Tokyo Verdy, and host of the 2019 Rugby World Cup opener. Look for the white bowl in western Tokyo beside the small Chofu airfield.

name: Plenitude Arena
blurb: Europe's largest indoor arena, a stadium-sized box at La Défense that holds rugby club Racing 92 and hosted Olympic swimming in 2024. Look for the long building at the foot of the Grande Arche.

name: 3Arena
blurb: Stockholm's retractable-roof football stadium, opened in 2013 as Tele2 Arena, home of Hammarby and Djurgården. Look for the big box right beside the white ball of the Globe south of the center.

name: Teddy Stadium
blurb: Home of Beitar Jerusalem, named for Teddy Kollek, the city's longtime mayor. Look for it in the Malha valley next to the Malha shopping mall in southwest Jerusalem.

name: Circuit de la Sarthe
blurb: Home of the 24 Hours of Le Mans since 1923. Most of its 8.5-mile lap is public road; look for the long, straight Mulsanne road running through the countryside south of Le Mans.

name: Anderstorp Raceway
blurb: Hosted the Swedish Grand Prix in the 1970s, and its long back straight doubles as an airstrip. Look for the runway-like strip in the flat forest and marsh of southern Sweden.

name: Mugello Circuit
blurb: Ferrari's own track, tucked into the Tuscan hills north of Florence and home of the Italian MotoGP round. Look for the gray ribbon of tarmac curling over green, rolling slopes.

name: Autódromo Internacional do Algarve
