blurb: Known for wild elevation changes that riders compare to a rollercoaster, it hosted F1 in 2020 and 2021. Look for the track draped over bare hills a few miles inland from Portimão.

name: Žalgiris Arena
blurb: The biggest indoor arena in the Baltics, home of the beloved Žalgiris basketball club. Look for it on Nemunas Island where the Nemunas and Neris rivers meet in Kaunas.

name: Citadel of Aleppo
blurb: One of the oldest and largest castles in the world, on a mound occupied for thousands of years. Look for the oval hill in the middle of the old city, ringed by a moat and sloping stone glacis.

name: Chinon Castle
blurb: Joan of Arc met the future Charles VII here in 1429 and talked him into backing her. Look for the long ruined fortress strung along the ridge above the Vienne River and the town's slate roofs.

name: Olavinlinna Castle
blurb: A castle begun in 1475 on a rock island in the strait between two lakes at Savonlinna. Look for its round towers rising straight out of the water, with the town on either side.

name: Harlech Castle
blurb: Edward I's 1280s fortress on a crag above the dunes; the sea once reached its foot. Its long siege in the Wars of the Roses is said to have inspired the song Men of Harlech.

name: Palace of Moncloa
blurb: Official residence of Spain's prime minister since 1977, set in a walled, wooded compound in northwest Madrid near the university campus. Look for low buildings among trees off the A-6 highway.

name: Hever Castle
blurb: Anne Boleyn's childhood home, a small moated castle that William Waldorf Astor restored, adding an Italian garden and a 38-acre lake. Look for the square moat and lake in Kent woodland.

name: Rock of Cashel
blurb: Seat of the medieval kings of Munster: a limestone outcrop crowned by a round tower, a Gothic cathedral and a Romanesque chapel. Look for the gray ruin on a lone rock above flat Tipperary farmland.

name: Canadian Tire Centre
blurb: The Ottawa Senators' arena, out in suburban Kanata about 15 miles west of downtown. Look for it beside Highway 417 surrounded by parking and new subdivisions.

name: Tauride Palace
blurb: Built for Prince Potemkin, Catherine the Great's favorite, it later housed Russia's first parliament, the State Duma, from 1906. Look for the long, low yellow classical building with a domed center beside the Tauride Garden.

name: Dignity Health Sports Park
blurb: Home of the LA Galaxy, the most decorated club in MLS, on the Cal State Dominguez Hills campus in Carson. Look for the soccer stadium among a cluster of practice fields and a tennis stadium.

name: Estádio Nacional
blurb: Portugal's national stadium in Jamor, opened in 1944 and home of the Portuguese Cup final. Look for the white classical stands set in a wooded valley west of Lisbon.

name: Ulsan Munsu Football Stadium
blurb: Ulsan's 2002 World Cup stadium, home of Ulsan HD, set in a park beside a reservoir. Look for the bowl framed by trees and water.

name: Gwangju World Cup Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2002 World Cup, where South Korea beat Spain on penalties to reach the semifinal. Look for the bowl in the city's west.

name: Kyalami
blurb: South Africa's Grand Prix track for decades, now surrounded by the sprawl of Midrand between Johannesburg and Pretoria. Look for the loop in the hills with suburbs pressing in on every side.

name: Magic Kingdom
blurb: The original Disney World park, opened in 1971. Look for Cinderella Castle at the hub and the big Seven Seas Lagoon between the park and the parking lots.

name: Universal Studios Japan
blurb: Opened in 2001 on Osaka Bay's industrial waterfront, now with a Super Nintendo World. Look for the park on reclaimed land by the harbor.

name: Ōita Stadium
blurb: Nicknamed the Big Eye, a Kisho Kurokawa dome whose roof slides open like an eyelid. Look for the round white dome in hills outside Oita, built for the 2002 World Cup.

name: Oracle Park
blurb: The Giants' waterfront park, opened in 2000. Home runs to right field can splash into McCovey Cove, where fans wait in kayaks. Look for the brick park on the bay south of the Bay Bridge.

name: Marrakesh Stadium
blurb: A 45,000-seat bowl on the northern edge of Marrakesh, opened in 2011. Look for the red-ochre walls, matching the city's color, set in flat dry ground with the High Atlas on the horizon.

name: Jeju World Cup Stadium
blurb: A 2002 World Cup stadium in Seogwipo on Jeju's south coast, its roof shaped like a fishing net. Look for it close to the sea with Hallasan's slopes behind.

name: Stadio Via del Mare
blurb: Lecce's stadium, on the road that runs to the sea. Look for the open bowl among olive groves on the flat Salento heel of Italy.

name: Santa Claus Village
blurb: Santa's official village on the Arctic Circle at Rovaniemi, with a painted line marking the latitude. Look for a cluster of cabins in snowy forest beside the airport.

name: Walibi Holland
blurb: A theme park on Flevoland, land pumped dry from the sea in the 1950s. Look for coaster tracks amid flat fields cut by straight drainage ditches.

name: Jardin d'Acclimatation
blurb: A garden and play park opened in 1860 in the Bois de Boulogne. Look for the glass sails of the Fondation Louis Vuitton right beside it.

name: City of Space
blurb: Toulouse's space park, with a full-size Ariane 5 rocket replica and a Mir space station backup. Look for the tall white rocket on the city's eastern edge.

name: Circuit Ricardo Tormo
blurb: Built like a stadium: the whole track is visible from its grandstands, which pack in MotoGP crowds for the season finale. Look for the compact loop ringed by stands west of Valencia.

name: Estádio Algarve
blurb: Built for Euro 2004 midway between Faro and Loulé, shared by the two cities. Look for a lone bowl in the Algarve countryside, a few miles inland from the beaches.

name: Estádio do Pacaembu
blurb: A 1940 art deco stadium in a leafy valley, home of Brazil's Football Museum, reopened in 2025 after a rebuild. Look for the horseshoe bowl at the foot of the Pacaembu valley, west of downtown.

name: Zayed Sports City Stadium
blurb: Abu Dhabi's national stadium, about 43,000 seats, with soaring concrete arches over the stands. It hosted the 2019 Asian Cup final; look for the oval and its arches.

name: Mohammed Bin Zayed Stadium
blurb: Home of Al Jazira club in central Abu Dhabi, enlarged for the 2019 Asian Cup. Look for an oval of stands among the city's grid of towers.

name: Estádio Municipal de Aveiro – Mário Duarte
blurb: Aveiro's Euro 2004 stadium, painted in a riot of bright colors. Look for the multicolored stands on the outskirts of town.

name: Bunyodkor Stadium
blurb: Tashkent's flagship football stadium, opened in 2012 and home of the national team. Look for the oval with a distinctive curved roof near the city's southwest.

name: Polish Army Stadium
blurb: Legia Warsaw's home, rebuilt in 2011 on the site of the 1930 original on Łazienkowska Street. Look for the compact rectangular stadium southeast of the city center, near the Łazienki Park greenery.

name: Carlos Tartiere Stadium
blurb: Real Oviedo's home, opened in 2000 to replace an older ground of the same name. Look for a big boxy stadium on the city's edge with the Cantabrian mountains beyond.

name: Poti Sea Port
blurb: Georgia's main port on the Black Sea, at the mouth of the Rioni River. Look for the brown river plume fanning into the sea beside the breakwaters.

name: Sheerness
blurb: Port on the Isle of Sheppey, now a big car-import terminal. Just offshore lies the wreck of the SS Richard Montgomery, still holding about 1,400 tons of WWII explosives; look for its masts above the water.

name: Puerto Madero
blurb: Buenos Aires' old 1890s docks, now a district of glass towers and restaurants along four brick-lined basins. Look for the long rectangular water basins between downtown and the green ecological reserve on the river.

name: Circuit Zolder
blurb: Gilles Villeneuve was killed here in qualifying for the 1982 Belgian Grand Prix. Look for the circuit winding through pine forest and sandy heath in Flanders.

name: Aintree Racecourse
blurb: Laid out inside Aintree Racecourse, home of the Grand National, it hosted the British Grand Prix five times; Stirling Moss won his first there in 1955. Look for the racecourse on Liverpool's north edge.

name: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca
blurb: Famous for the Corkscrew, a blind turn that drops about five stories in a few hundred feet. Look for the track on bare golden hills above Monterey Bay.

name: Okayama International Circuit
blurb: A tight mountain track in rural western Japan that briefly hosted F1 as the Pacific Grand Prix in 1994 and 1995. Look for the gray loop cut into forested hills.

name: Dijon-Prenois
blurb: Scene of the famous 1979 French Grand Prix duel in which Villeneuve and Arnoux banged wheels for second place. Look for a short, hilly track in Burgundy farmland.

name: Pakhtakor Markaziy Stadium
blurb: Pakhtakor's home and Tashkent's historic central stadium, set in parkland near the city center. Look for an oval among trees and wide Soviet avenues.

name: Daejeon World Cup Stadium
blurb: Built for the 2002 World Cup, where South Korea beat Italy in extra time. Look for the bowl on the north side of Daejeon.

name: Estadio El Campín
blurb: Bogotá's main stadium, home of Millonarios and Santa Fe, at about 8,600 ft in Colombia's high capital. Look for the oval bowl in the middle of the city, near the Simón Bolívar Park greenbelt.

name: Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Meléndez
blurb: Colombia's national team stadium in Barranquilla, picked partly for the heavy Caribbean heat visiting teams must play in. Look for the large oval bowl on the city's southern side.

name: National Stadium of Peru
blurb: Peru's national stadium in central Lima, rebuilt in 2011. Look for the oval beside the Paseo de la República expressway, about a mile south of the old center.

name: Muuga Harbour
blurb: Estonia's largest cargo port, east of Tallinn, handling oil, grain and containers. Look for tank farms and long piers on a forested Baltic shore.

name: Parc Astérix
blurb: A theme park based on the Astérix comics, in forest north of Paris near Charles de Gaulle Airport. Look for coaster tracks among the trees.

name: Prince George Circuit
blurb: A seaside road course in East London that hosted the South African Grand Prix in the 1960s. Look for the track running along the coast with the Indian Ocean right beside it.

name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
blurb: Under a vast red roof printed with the Ferrari logo, home of one of the world's fastest coasters. Look for the red triangle on Yas Island.

name: Disney's Animal Kingdom
blurb: The largest Disney park by area, a zoo and theme park. Look for the Expedition Everest mountain and big grassy savannas full of animals.

name: Disney's Hollywood Studios
blurb: Disney's movie park, home to the Tower of Terror and a Star Wars land. Look for the tall tower and the rocky spires of Galaxy's Edge.

name: Sebring International Raceway
blurb: Home of the 12 Hours of Sebring since 1952, built on a WWII bomber training field. Look for the track using old concrete runways next to the working airport.

name: Madring
blurb: Madrid's new F1 venue, part street circuit and part purpose-built track around the IFEMA trade fair grounds, with a steeply banked turn. It sits right next to Barajas Airport, so you may fly straight over it.

name: National Stadium, Dhaka
blurb: Bangladesh's main stadium in the heart of Dhaka, where independence-era cricket and football were played. Look for the oval with tall floodlight towers in the dense Motijheel business district.

name: Estadio Defensores del Chaco
blurb: Paraguay's national stadium in Asunción, the country's biggest. Look for the open concrete bowl in the city's eastern neighborhoods, inland from the Paraguay River.

name: Tropicana Field
blurb: The Rays' domed park with a roof tilted at 6.5 degrees; Hurricane Milton shredded its fabric in 2024. Look for the slanted white disc west of downtown St. Petersburg.

name: Adrar Stadium
blurb: Agadir's 45,000-seat stadium, opened in 2013 on the eastern outskirts, inland from the beach resort. Look for the oval bowl in dry ground a few miles from the bay.

name: Sammy Ofer Stadium
blurb: Haifa's 30,000-seat stadium, opened in 2014 and shared by Maccabi and Hapoel Haifa. Look for the bowl south of the city near the coast, below Mount Carmel.

name: Estadio Olímpico Atahualpa
blurb: Quito's main stadium, at about 9,100 ft, where visiting teams have long struggled with the altitude. Look for the oval in the long, narrow city squeezed between volcanic slopes.

name: Akhmat-Arena
blurb: Grozny's stadium, opened in 2011 and home of FC Akhmat. Look for the round bowl in the rebuilt Chechen capital.

name: Estadio Hernando Siles
blurb: At about 11,900 ft in La Paz, one of the highest international stadiums in the world, where visiting teams famously struggle to breathe. Look for the bowl in the bottom of the canyon city.

name: Corregidora Stadium
blurb: Querétaro's stadium, built for the 1986 World Cup. Look for the bowl on the city's edge, ringed by parking and new suburbs.

name: Port of Beirut
blurb: On August 4, 2020, ammonium nitrate stored here exploded in one of the largest non-nuclear blasts ever, wrecking much of the city. Look for the shattered grain silos beside the docks.

name: Watkins Glen International
blurb: Hosted the US Grand Prix for 20 years through 1980 and still holds NASCAR road races. Look for the track twisting across wooded hills above the south tip of Seneca Lake.

name: Charade Circuit
blurb: Built on the slopes of an extinct volcano above Clermont-Ferrand, it hosted the French Grand Prix in the 1960s and 70s. Look for the twisting road course among the Chaîne des Puys domes.

name: MotorLand Aragón
blurb: A Tilke-designed track in the dry, red hills near Alcañiz, used for MotoGP and World Superbikes. Look for the gray loop on bare desert-like terrain far from any city.

name: Misano World Circuit Marco Simoncelli
blurb: Named for the Italian MotoGP rider killed in a 2011 race crash, it sits just inland from the Adriatic beach towns of Riccione and Rimini. Look for the compact loop a couple of miles from the coast.

name: Masaryk Circuit
blurb: Brno's track, long home of MotoGP's Czech Grand Prix, set in wooded hills west of the city. Look for the swooping circuit and its big grass spectator banks.

name: TT Circuit Assen
blurb: The Cathedral of motorcycle racing: the Dutch TT has run at Assen since 1925, longer than any other Grand Prix event. Look for the loop in flat farmland south of town.

name: Sydney Cricket Ground
blurb: Cricket has been played here since the 1840s. Look for the oval in Moore Park beside the Allianz Stadium, with Victorian-era pavilions on one side.

name: Accra Sports Stadium
blurb: Ghana's historic stadium, home of Hearts of Oak. In 2001 a crush here killed 126 people, Africa's worst stadium disaster. Look for the oval in central Accra, close to the coast.

name: Ghazi Stadium
blurb: Kabul's main stadium, notorious under Taliban rule in the 1990s as a site of public executions, and now home to Afghan football again. Look for the oval bowl in the city's dense low-rise center.

name: Mandela National Stadium
blurb: Uganda's national stadium at Namboole, on the eastern edge of Kampala, built with Chinese help and opened in the late 1990s. Look for the oval bowl on a low hill among red-earth suburbs.

name: My Dinh National Stadium
blurb: Vietnam's national stadium on Hanoi's western side, built for the 2003 Southeast Asian Games. Look for the arched roof over the main stand.

name: Estadio Nacional de Costa Rica
blurb: Built by China as a gift and opened in 2011, it stands in La Sabana park on the site of San José's old airport. Look for the curved white roof shells inside the green park west of downtown.

name: Yokohama Stadium
blurb: Home of the BayStars, set in Yokohama Park near Chinatown and the harbor. Look for the tightly packed round ballpark among downtown streets.

name: Suita Stadium
blurb: Gamba Osaka's soccer stadium, paid for largely by donations and opened in 2015. Look for it next to the Expo '70 park and Taro Okamoto's Tower of the Sun.

name: Dnipro Arena
blurb: A compact modern stadium near the center of Dnipro, opened in 2008. Look for the boxy enclosed stands set among city blocks near the river.

name: Stade Océane
blurb: Le Havre AC's stadium, opened in 2012, wrapped in a translucent blue skin that glows at night. Look for the blue shell among the port's docks and warehouses.

name: Roman Bridge of Córdoba
blurb: Roman foundations with 16 arches across the Guadalquivir, rebuilt over centuries. It leads straight to the Mezquita; look for the great mosque-cathedral's square block at the north end of the bridge.

name: Kyiv Metro Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1965, it carries metro trains and cars over the Dnieper from the high right bank to Hydropark island. Look for the trains gliding across the river below the green hills of the old city.

name: Port of Odesa
blurb: Ukraine's largest port. Look for the docks below the city's grand boulevards and the Potemkin Stairs leading down to the harbor.

name: Ambassador Bridge
blurb: A 1929 suspension bridge that carries more trade than any other US to Canada crossing. Look for its green towers over the Detroit River just west of downtown.

name: Port of Antwerp
blurb: Europe's second-largest port, about 50 miles up the Scheldt from the North Sea, with one of the world's biggest petrochemical clusters. Look for docks and locks stretching north of the city toward the Dutch border.

name: Port of Kaohsiung
blurb: Taiwan's largest port. Look for a long sandbar island shielding the harbor, with container cranes along its inner shore and the city's 85 Sky Tower behind.

name: Pamban Bridge
blurb: India's first sea bridge, opened in 1914 to carry trains to Rameswaram island. A new vertical-lift bridge opened alongside it in 2025. Look for twin lines across turquoise shallows dotted with fishing boats.

name: Octávio Frias de Oliveira Bridge
blurb: Two curving decks cross each other in an X under a single pylon about 450 ft tall, opened in 2008 over the Pinheiros River. Look for the lone white spike rising above São Paulo's dense towers.

name: Petőfi Bridge
blurb: A steel bridge across the Danube in southern Budapest, rebuilt after its demolition in 1945. Look for it linking the inner boulevard on the Pest side to the university district in Buda.

name: Penang Bridge
blurb: About 8.4 miles long, linking Penang island to the mainland since 1985. Look for its long line across the strait with George Town to the north.

name: Afghanistan–Uzbekistan Friendship Bridge
blurb: Soviet troops left Afghanistan across this bridge in 1989, with their commander the last to walk over. Look for a road and rail bridge crossing the braided Amu Darya on the border.

name: Ada Bridge
blurb: A single-pylon cable-stayed bridge over the Sava opened in 2012, its pylon about 650 ft tall, anchored on the tip of Ada Ciganlija island. Look for the lone spike at the head of the island, just upstream of the Sava's mouth.

name: Suez Canal Bridge
blurb: Lifts a highway about 230 ft over the Suez Canal so the largest ships can pass beneath, built with Japanese aid. Look for the long ramps climbing out of flat desert on both banks.

name: Jerusalem Chords Bridge
blurb: A Santiago Calatrava cable-stayed bridge from 2008 that carries the light rail at the city's western entrance. Its single white mast and fanned cables were meant to suggest a harp.

name: Baluarte Bridge
blurb: Its deck hangs about 1,300 ft above the canyon floor, the highest cable-stayed bridge in the world when it opened in 2012. Look for it spanning a deep gorge in the Sierra Madre on the Durango to Mazatlán highway.

name: Gardaland
blurb: Italy's biggest theme park, just off the southeastern shore of Lake Garda. Look for coaster tracks and a fairy-tale castle near the lake.

name: Cedar Point
blurb: Known for its record-setting roller coasters, on a peninsula jutting into Lake Erie at Sandusky. Look for the tangle of coaster tracks on the narrow spit of land.

name: Krk Bridge
blurb: Two concrete arches link Krk island to the mainland, hopping across a rocky islet. When opened in 1980 the larger arch was the longest concrete arch in the world.

name: Mobility Resort Motegi
blurb: Honda's circuit complex in the hills of Tochigi, with a road course and a former oval. Look for the racetrack loops carved into green forest.

name: Jarama Circuit
blurb: Spain's Grand Prix track through much of the 1960s and 70s, just north of Madrid. Look for the twisting loop in dry scrubland a few miles beyond Barajas Airport.

name: Fiorano Circuit
blurb: Ferrari's private test track, opened in 1972 right beside the factory in Maranello, where the company develops its F1 and road cars. Look for the small twisting loop next to the plant.

name: Daytona International Speedway
blurb: Home of the Daytona 500, a 2.5-mile tri-oval with 31-degree banking. Look for the 29-acre Lake Lloyd in the infield, dug for the dirt to build the banks.

name: Nationals Park
blurb: The Nationals' park, opened in 2008 on the Anacostia River waterfront in Navy Yard. Look for the field angled toward the Capitol dome, which is visible from the upper deck.

name: Rice–Eccles Stadium
blurb: Home of the Utah Utes, it hosted the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2002 Winter Olympics. Look for the bowl at the foot of the Wasatch on the university's slope.

name: Hong Kong Stadium
blurb: For decades the home of the Hong Kong Sevens, set in a green bowl in So Kon Po above Causeway Bay. Look for the white roof arches tucked into the hillside among towers.

name: Petco Park
blurb: The Padres' downtown park, opened in 2004, built around the old Western Metal Supply building, whose corner forms part of the left-field stands. Look for it just across from the convention center and bay.

name: Agia Sophia Stadium
blurb: AEK Athens' stadium in Nea Filadelfeia, opened in 2022 on the site of the club's old ground, with a facade inspired by Byzantine design. Look for the arched stadium in the northern suburbs.

name: Estadio Universitario
blurb: Tigres' home, nicknamed 'El Volcán' for its steep, loud stands, on the university campus in San Nicolás de los Garza. Look for the open concrete bowl in the dense northern suburbs.

name: Allianz Parque
blurb: Palmeiras's home since 2014 and one of Brazil's busiest concert venues. Look for the boxy stadium on the club's old site in Perdizes, west of downtown São Paulo.

name: Thani bin Jassim Stadium
blurb: Home of Al-Gharafa, used for the 2011 Asian Cup. Look for the stadium in Doha's northwestern suburbs.

name: Dasarath Rangasala Stadium
blurb: Nepal's national stadium in central Kathmandu, a modest open ground used for football and big public events. Look for the oval near the old Tundikhel parade ground, with the Himalaya on the northern horizon.

name: Toyota Stadium
blurb: Kisho Kurokawa's stadium on the Yahagi River, home to Nagoya Grampus at times. Look for the four tall masts hanging the roof, beside a long bridge in Toyota City.

name: Mes Bridge
blurb: An 18th-century Ottoman stone bridge near Shkodër, one of the longest of its era in the Balkans. Look for a humped line of arches over a gravel riverbed.

name: Port of Eilat
blurb: Israel's only Red Sea port, at the top of the Gulf of Aqaba, side by side with Aqaba in Jordan. Look for docks beside the beach resorts, with Egypt and Jordan both in view.

name: Sidu River Bridge
blurb: Its deck hangs about 1,600 ft above the Sidu River gorge, the world's highest bridge when it opened in 2009. Look for the thin line between two limestone cliffs in Hubei.

name: Tatara Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge on the Shimanami Kaido island chain, the longest cable-stayed span in the world when it opened in 1999. Look for its pale towers between green islands.

name: Centennial Bridge, Panama
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge opened in 2004 across the Culebra Cut, the canal's narrow channel through the continental divide. Look for its two pylons above the canal, with ships passing underneath.

name: Everland
blurb: South Korea's largest theme park in Yongin, south of Seoul, with a wooden coaster built into the hills. Look for rides in a wooded valley.

name: Puente del Alamillo
blurb: Santiago Calatrava built it for Seville's Expo '92: a single pylon leaning back at a steep angle, holding the deck by its own weight with no back cables. Look for the white slanted spike over the river.

name: Árpád Bridge
blurb: Budapest's longest bridge, crossing the Danube and the north tip of Margaret Island. Look for its long concrete line with a ramp down to the island.

name: EuroSpeedway Lausitz
blurb: A rare European banked oval with a road course inside, built on reclaimed mining land. Look for the tri-oval among the lakes of old brown-coal pits.

name: Estadio Cuauhtémoc
blurb: Puebla's big stadium, built for the 1970 World Cup and used again in 1986. Look for the oval in the city's north, with Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl volcanoes on the horizon.

name: LoanDepot Park
blurb: The Marlins' park, built on the site of the Orange Bowl in Little Havana and opened in 2012, with a retractable roof. Look for the white roof panels a mile or two west of downtown Miami.

name: Target Field
blurb: Home of the Twins since 2010, squeezed onto a tight downtown lot over rail lines. Look for the open ballpark on the northwest side of downtown Minneapolis.

name: Olympic Stadium
blurb: Ashgabat's white marble Olympic stadium, built for the 2017 Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games, is topped by a giant sculpted head of an Akhal-Teke horse, Turkmenistan's national breed. Look for the white bowl in the city's south.

name: Addis Ababa Stadium
blurb: Ethiopia's old national stadium in central Addis Ababa, at about 7,700 ft, where Ethiopia won the 1962 Africa Cup of Nations. Look for the oval near Meskel Square.

name: Kuban Stadium
blurb: Krasnodar's older city stadium, home of the Kuban club through the Soviet years. Look for the open bowl among low blocks in the city center.

name: Stade d'Angondjé
blurb: Also called the Stade de l'Amitié, built with Chinese help for the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations and host of its final. Look for the white stadium on the coast north of Libreville.

name: Ciudad de los Deportes Stadium
blurb: A Mexico City soccer stadium long the home of Cruz Azul and Atlante, sitting right beside the Plaza México, the world's largest bullring. Look for the two bowls side by side in the Nápoles district.

name: Estadio Monumental (Chile)
blurb: Home of Colo-Colo, Chile's most successful club, in Macul in southeastern Santiago. Look for the large open oval bowl, with the Andes close by to the east.

name: Port of Haifa
blurb: Israel's largest port, below Mount Carmel. Look for the gold-domed Baha'i Shrine and its terraced gardens running straight down the mountain toward the docks.

name: Allenby Bridge
blurb: The main crossing between the West Bank and Jordan, a short span over the Jordan River near Jericho. The river here is a narrow green thread through bare desert, more than 1,000 ft below sea level.

name: Tay Rail Bridge
blurb: About 2 miles long, it replaced the first Tay Bridge, which collapsed in a storm in 1879 with a train on it. Look for the stumps of the old piers still standing in the water beside it.

name: Runyang Yangtze River Bridge
blurb: A 2005 crossing of the Yangtze near Zhenjiang whose suspension span was the longest in China at the time. Look for its towers over the wide brown river.

name: Puente Nuevo
blurb: Finished in 1793, it spans El Tajo gorge, splitting Ronda's old and new towns, with its arches rising roughly 300 ft above the canyon floor. Look for the whitewashed town perched on the cliff edges.

name: Juscelino Kubitschek bridge
blurb: Three asymmetrical steel arches skip across Lake Paranoá in Brasília. Look for the white arches leaping diagonally over the deck like a skipped stone.

name: Shanghai Disneyland Park
blurb: Opened in 2016, its castle is the tallest at any Disney park. Look for the park and the resort's lake in flat land near Pudong Airport.

name: Canadian Tire Motorsport Park
blurb: Still widely called Mosport, it hosted the Canadian Grand Prix through much of the 1960s and 70s. Look for the loop over rolling farmland northeast of Toronto, near Lake Ontario.

name: Ramoji Film City
blurb: One of the largest film studio complexes in the world, spread over more than 1,600 acres east of Hyderabad. Look for sets and gardens scattered across rocky hills.

name: Circuit Mont-Tremblant
blurb: A hilly forest track in the Laurentians that hosted the Canadian Grand Prix in 1968 and 1970. Look for the loop in the woods below the ski hill.

name: Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit
blurb: MotoGP riders race toward the sea here: the track sits on clifftops above Bass Strait. Look for the loop on the island's south coast, with surf breaking just beyond.

name: Sachsenring
blurb: Home of MotoGP's German Grand Prix, near Chemnitz, famous for its long run of left-hand turns. Look for the tight circuit on a hillside surrounded by grass spectator banks.

name: Rate Field
blurb: Home of the White Sox since 1991, built across the street from old Comiskey Park, whose home plate is marked in the parking lot. Look for the ballpark beside the Dan Ryan Expressway.

name: Rizal Memorial Stadium
blurb: Manila's historic stadium, opened in 1934 for the Far Eastern Games. Look for the old concrete oval in the sports complex just off Manila Bay.

name: Gigante de Arroyito Stadium
blurb: Rosario Central's home, a 1978 World Cup venue, sitting near the bank of the Paraná River. Look for the bowl in the Arroyito neighborhood, north of downtown Rosario.

name: Kyocera Dome Osaka
blurb: Home of the Orix Buffaloes since 1997, often likened to a UFO for its layered silver roof. Look for the dome by the river in western Osaka.

name: Baba Yara Stadium
blurb: Kumasi's stadium, home of Asante Kotoko, one of Africa's most successful clubs. Look for the oval in the center of the Ashanti capital's dense neighborhoods.

name: Hassanal Bolkiah National Stadium
blurb: Brunei's national stadium, named for its sultan, in a sports complex on the edge of Bandar Seri Begawan. Look for the oval among green lawns and forest.

name: Stade El Menzah
blurb: Tunis's older Olympic stadium, built for the 1967 Mediterranean Games, in the El Menzah district north of the center. Look for an oval with a track in a sports complex among the city's white blocks.

name: Estadio de Bata
blurb: Bata's stadium, built for the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations co-hosted by Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. Look for the modern bowl near the coast in the country's largest city.

name: Al Salam Stadium
blurb: A newer soccer stadium in the desert suburbs of eastern Cairo, used by Al Ahly and for Africa Cup of Nations matches. Look for the bowl on the city's sandy fringe.

name: Stadion Rujevica
blurb: HNK Rijeka's small modern stadium, built beside the club's training center on the hills above the city. Look for the compact stands on a hillside with Kvarner Bay below.

name: Metallurg Stadium
blurb: Krylia Sovetov's old home, a Soviet-era bowl with a running track, used before the club moved to the newer World Cup arena. Look for an open oval with a track in a wooded park in the city.

name: Estadio Olímpico Pascual Guerrero
blurb: Cali's historic stadium, home of América de Cali, and host of the 1971 Pan American Games. Look for the oval in the dense city center, with the western cordillera rising behind it.

name: Capanda Dam
blurb: One of the big dams on Angola's Kwanza River, about 360 ft tall, built with Brazilian and Russian help and finished in the 2000s after the civil war delayed it. Look for a concrete dam across a river in green savanna country.

name: Krasnoyarsk Dam
blurb: A 400-ft concrete dam on the Yenisei River, pictured on Russia's 10-ruble note, with an inclined ship lift that carries boats past it in a water-filled tub. Look for the dam's long gray wall in a forested valley.

name: Bratsk Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: Its dam on the Angara River created one of the largest reservoirs in the world, a winding lake hundreds of miles long through the Siberian taiga. Look for a long concrete dam with a railway across the top.

name: Hardanger Bridge
blurb: Its suspension span of about 4,300 ft is the longest in Norway, crossing the Hardangerfjord since 2013. Look for the span between mountains that drop straight into the fjord.

name: Port of Busan
blurb: South Korea's largest port and one of the busiest container ports in the world. Look for cranes lining the bays below steep green hills packed with apartment towers.

name: Cần Thơ Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge over the Hau branch of the Mekong, opened in 2010 with a main span of about 1,800 ft. In 2007 an approach section collapsed during construction, killing more than 50 workers.

name: Bolshoy Obukhovsky Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed crossing of the Neva and the only one in the city that doesn't open for ships. Look for its tall white towers on the outer ring road.

name: Millennium Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge over the Morača River in Podgorica, opened in 2005 as a symbol of the new Montenegro. Look for its single leaning white pylon.

name: Sutong Yangtze River Bridge
blurb: Its 3,570-ft span made it the world's longest cable-stayed bridge when it opened in 2008. Look for its two very tall towers across the Yangtze not far from the river's mouth.

name: Zhivopisny Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge over the Moskva with a huge red arch and a glass pod hung beneath it. Look for the red arch on the river's loop in northwest Moscow.

name: Tromsø bridge
blurb: A 1960 cantilever bridge about two-thirds of a mile long linking Tromsø island to the mainland. Look for the white triangular Arctic Cathedral at its eastern end.

name: Waldschlösschen Bridge
blurb: Building this bridge cost Dresden's Elbe Valley its UNESCO World Heritage status in 2009. Look for the low steel arch across the green meadows lining the river.

name: Dubai Autodrome
blurb: Dubai's purpose-built racing circuit, the centerpiece of the Motor City development in the desert south of downtown. Look for the gray loop with new apartment blocks along its edges.

name: Motorsport Arena Oschersleben
blurb: A compact road course on the flat farmland of Saxony-Anhalt, used for touring cars and superbikes. Look for the circuit set among fields with little else around.

name: Yanggakdo Stadium
blurb: A soccer stadium on Yanggak Island in the Taedong River, near the 47-story Yanggakdo International Hotel where most foreign visitors are kept. Look for the oval on the island in the river.

name: Henryk Reyman Municipal Stadium
blurb: Wisła Kraków's home, one of Poland's oldest football grounds. Look for the stadium beside Błonia, the huge open meadow west of Kraków's old town.

name: Franso Hariri Stadium
blurb: Erbil's main stadium, renamed for Franso Hariri, a Kurdish Christian governor of the city assassinated in 2001. Look for the oval in the city's ring-road layout around the ancient citadel.

name: Polideportivo Cachamay
blurb: A Copa América 2007 venue in Ciudad Guayana, near where the Caroní meets the Orinoco. Look for the stadium beside the Cachamay park and the river falls.

name: Fukushima Azuma Baseball Stadium
blurb: Hosted the very first event of the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, a softball game, as a nod to the region's recovery after the 2011 disaster. Look for the ballpark in the wooded Azuma sports park.

name: McMahon Stadium
blurb: Home of the CFL's Calgary Stampeders and site of the 1988 Winter Olympics opening ceremony. Look for the open bowl beside the University of Calgary, north of downtown.

name: Krasnodar Stadium
blurb: Built by FC Krasnodar's billionaire owner and opened in 2016, with a giant video screen wrapping the whole inside of the roof. Look for the oval set in a large landscaped park.

name: Sultan Qaboos Sports Complex
blurb: Oman's national sports complex in Bawshar, west of central Muscat, built in 1985. Look for the stadium and running track against the brown, bare Hajar mountains.

name: Stade de l'Amitié
blurb: Benin's national stadium in Cotonou, Chinese-built and named for that friendship. Look for the oval in the flat coastal city near the lagoon.

name: Anji Arena
blurb: Built in Kaspiysk on the Caspian shore for Anzhi Makhachkala, the club a billionaire briefly bankrolled with stars like Samuel Eto'o. Look for the stadium near the sea, just south of Makhachkala.

name: Estadio José Pachencho Romero
blurb: Maracaibo's main football stadium, a 2007 Copa América venue. Look for an oval among the low, sun-baked sprawl of Venezuela's oil capital.

name: Estadio Hidalgo
blurb: Pachuca's stadium, home of the Tuzos, a club from the city where English miners brought soccer to Mexico. Look for the bowl tucked against the bare, windswept hills of Hidalgo.

name: Europa-Park-Stadion
blurb: SC Freiburg's stadium, opened in 2021 beside the small Freiburg airfield on the city's northwest edge. Look for the boxy stadium next to the small airfield's runway, with the Black Forest rising to the east.

name: Fukuoka Dome
blurb: Japan's first retractable-roof stadium, opened in 1993, home of the SoftBank Hawks. Look for the silver dome on the Momochi waterfront next to the slim Fukuoka Tower.

name: Iron Gate I Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: Dams the Danube in the Iron Gates gorge on the Serbia-Romania border, one of Europe's largest hydro plants. Its 1972 reservoir drowned the island town of Ada Kaleh; look for the river squeezed between cliffs.

name: Skopje Aqueduct
blurb: A long stone aqueduct of dozens of arches on the northern edge of Skopje. Its age is debated, possibly Ottoman. Look for a tan arched line across dry ground.

name: Tishrin Dam
blurb: A hydro dam on the Euphrates in northern Syria, finished in 1999 and fought over repeatedly in the civil war. Look for the reservoir pooling in the river valley through dry plains.

name: Dyavolski most
blurb: A 16th-century stone arch over the Arda in the Rhodopes, so steep and slender that legend credits the devil. From the air it's a tiny pale hump in a forested river gorge.

name: Kanmon Bridge
blurb: A 1973 suspension bridge across the Kanmon Strait between Honshu and Kyushu. Look for the narrow channel crowded with ships and the cities on both sides.

name: Port of Ashdod
blurb: One of Israel's two main cargo ports, built on dunes in the 1960s. Look for a long breakwater and container yards on a straight sandy coast.

name: Port of Baku
blurb: Port on the Caspian, the world's largest inland body of water, serving ships to Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan. Look for terminals on a flat, dry coast dotted with oil infrastructure.

name: Yangshan Port
blurb: Shanghai's deep-water port, built on islands about 20 miles offshore and linked by the Donghai Bridge. Look for the long bridge running out to sea and the islands covered in container yards.

name: Port of Ventspils
blurb: An ice-free Latvian port on the Baltic, long a major oil export terminal. Look for tank farms along the mouth of the Venta River and two long breakwaters.

name: Sky Bridge 721
blurb: About 2,365 ft long, the world's longest pedestrian suspension bridge when it opened in 2022. Look for a thin line hung across a forested valley in the Králický Sněžník hills.

name: Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan
blurb: The world's busiest port by cargo tonnage. Look for terminals scattered among the green Zhoushan islands and crowds of ships in the channels.

name: Dublin Port
blurb: Ireland's busiest port, at the mouth of the Liffey. Look for the red-and-white Poolbeg chimneys at the base of the long South Wall breakwater.

name: San Juanico Bridge
blurb: At about 1.3 miles, the longest bridge over sea water in the Philippines, opened in 1973 between Samar and Leyte. Look for its curving line threaded across a strait dotted with small islands.

name: Port of Kobe
blurb: The 1995 Kobe earthquake wrecked most of its quays. Look for Port Island and Rokko Island, big man-made rectangles in Osaka Bay built from mountain soil.

name: Rama VIII Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge opened in 2002 with a single inverted-Y pylon to one side, its cables fanning to one bank. Look for the lone tall pylon over the Chao Phraya near Bangkok's old royal quarter.

name: Korea–Russia Friendship Bridge
blurb: The only land link between Russia and North Korea, a low rail bridge over the Tumen River just upstream of the Sea of Japan. China's border lies a few miles upstream; look for the river and the marshy delta.

name: Wild Wadi Water Park
blurb: A water park beside the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab on Dubai's coast. Look for the blue slides and pools next to the hotel's island.

name: Gröna Lund
blurb: Stockholm's amusement park since 1883, on the waterfront of Djurgården. Look for coaster tracks and drop towers right on the water facing the city across the water.

name: 6th October Bridge
blurb: An elevated highway that snakes for miles through Cairo and leaps the Nile across Gezira Island. Look for it threading the city's tan rooftops to the river.

name: Universal Studios Singapore
blurb: Part of Resorts World Sentosa, on the island just south of Singapore's city. Look for the park beside the harbor and the container port.

name: Six Flags Magic Mountain
blurb: The park with the most roller coasters in the world, carved into the hills of Valencia. Look for tangled white and colored coaster tracks on the brown hillside beside Interstate 5.

name: Astrid Lindgren's World
blurb: A park built around Astrid Lindgren's stories in her hometown of Vimmerby. Look for small storybook houses in woodland.

name: Futuroscope
blurb: A futuristic park near Poitiers with angular glass buildings. Look for the crystal-like structures beside the A10 motorway.

name: 30 June Stadium
blurb: Cairo's Air Defense Stadium, used for big matches in the eastern suburbs. Look for the stadium amid the low desert neighborhoods off the ring road.

name: Stade du 4 Août
blurb: Burkina Faso's national stadium in Ouagadougou, named for the date of Thomas Sankara's 1983 revolution. Look for the oval in the flat, red-earth city.

name: Estádio Ilha do Retiro
blurb: Sport Recife's home, in the riverside Ilha do Retiro neighborhood that gives it its name. Look for the compact ground hemmed in by city blocks near the Capibaribe River.

name: Western Sydney Stadium
blurb: Opened in 2019 on the site of the old Parramatta Stadium, home to the Parramatta Eels and Western Sydney Wanderers. Look for the steep stands under a jagged roof beside the Parramatta River.

name: Forsyth Barr Stadium
blurb: One of the only fully enclosed stadiums with natural grass, built in 2011 in Dunedin. Look for a clear plastic roof, letting in the light the grass needs, near the head of Otago Harbour.

name: Estadio Deportivo Cali
blurb: Deportivo Cali's own stadium, one of the largest in Colombia, standing among sugarcane fields near Palmira, outside Cali. Look for the big bowl surrounded by green cane plantations.

name: Fez Stadium
blurb: A large, mostly open bowl on the outskirts of Fez, opened in 2007 and upgraded for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Look for it in the flat plain away from the walled medina's maze of rooftops.

name: Estadio Cuscatlán
blurb: El Salvador's largest stadium and one of the biggest in Central America, opened in 1976 with room for about 45,000. Look for the large bowl in southwestern San Salvador, under the San Salvador volcano.

name: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
blurb: About 3.5 miles across the Ganges from Patna to Hajipur, it was among India's longest river bridges when it opened in 1982. Look for its long concrete line over the wide, sandy river.

name: Sanjō Ōhashi Bridge
blurb: The old end point of the Tokaido road from Edo, crossing the Kamo River in Kyoto. The bridge itself is small; look for the river and its walking banks cutting through the city.

name: Roseires Dam
blurb: Dams the Blue Nile near Sudan's border with Ethiopia, raised in 2013 to hold more water for irrigation and power. Look for a wide reservoir in flat savanna.

name: Hirakud Dam
blurb: Across the Mahanadi River, finished in 1957, and with its dikes about 16 miles long, one of the longest earthen dams in the world. Look for the huge reservoir sprawling behind a long embankment.

name: Dragon River Bridge
blurb: A yellow steel bridge shaped like a dragon, opened in 2013 over the Han River in Da Nang. On weekend nights the head breathes fire and water; look for the undulating arches running toward the beach.

name: Robert F. Kennedy Bridge
blurb: The old Triborough, three bridges meeting on Randalls Island to link Manhattan, Queens and the Bronx. Look for the Y-shaped junction over the island's sports fields.

name: Adolphe Bridge
blurb: A 1903 stone bridge whose great arch was the largest of its kind in the world when built. Look for it spanning the deep green Pétrusse valley in Luxembourg City.

name: Port of Nagoya
blurb: Japan's largest port by cargo volume, shipping Toyota cars worldwide. Look for car carriers and acres of parked vehicles on reclaimed land at the head of Ise Bay.

name: Old Little Belt Bridge
blurb: A 1935 steel truss carrying rail and road across the Little Belt, Denmark's first big bridge. Look for its dark girder line about a mile and a half west of the newer suspension bridge.

name: Europoort
blurb: The western end of Rotterdam, Europe's largest port, built out into the North Sea. Look for the Maasvlakte, new land covered in container terminals, and miles of refineries along the Nieuwe Waterweg.

name: Sami Bridge
blurb: Crosses the Teno River between Finland and Norway at Utsjoki, far above the Arctic Circle. Look for a slim span over a salmon river winding through bare tundra hills.

name: Sunshine Skyway Bridge
blurb: Rebuilt after a freighter knocked down the old span in 1980, killing 35 people. Look for the bright yellow cables fanning from its central towers high over the mouth of Tampa Bay.

name: Incheon Bridge
blurb: About 13 miles long, opened in 2009 to link Incheon Airport's island to the Songdo district. If you're flying into ICN, look for a thin line crossing the tidal flats with a cable-stayed section in the middle.

name: General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge
blurb: About 5.4 miles long across the outlet of Lake Maracaibo, opened in 1962. In 1964 an oil tanker struck it and brought down part of the span. Look for oil platforms dotting the lake beside it.

name: Dyrehavsbakken
blurb: Bakken, the oldest operating amusement park in the world, dating to 1583, inside a royal deer park north of Copenhagen. Look for a cluster of rides amid forest.

name: Governor Nobre de Carvalho Bridge
blurb: The first bridge from Macau to Taipa island, opened in 1974. Look for its distinctive raised hump in the middle, where ships pass beneath.

name: Särkänniemi
blurb: Tampere's amusement park on a lakeside point, crowned by the Näsinneula observation tower. Look for the tall needle on the shore of Lake Näsijärvi.

name: Second Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2006 between Mukdahan and Savannakhet, the first link in an East-West Economic Corridor from Myanmar to Vietnam. Look for a straight line over the wide Mekong.

name: Zhaozhou Bridge
blurb: The oldest open-spandrel stone arch bridge in the world, built around 600 AD and still standing. From above it's a small pale arch over a narrow river in flat farmland.

name: Auckland Harbour Bridge
blurb: Its traffic outgrew it within a decade, so in 1969 lanes were bolted onto both sides, nicknamed the Nippon clip-ons after the Japanese firm that built them. Look for the steel truss hump across the Waitematā.

name: El Ferdan Railway Bridge
blurb: The longest swing bridge in the world, a road and rail span that rotates to clear the Suez Canal. It usually sits swung open, parallel to the bank, so look for two long steel arms lining the water.

name: Apollo Bridge
blurb: A steel arch bridge over the Danube in Bratislava, opened in 2005; the arch was built on the bank and swung into place across the river. Look for the white arch rising above the deck.

name: Chang International Circuit
blurb: Thailand's MotoGP track in Buriram, in the flat rice country of the northeast, built next to the city's football stadium. Look for the loop in open farmland.

name: Puy du Fou
blurb: A history theme park in the Vendée famous for its huge night show. Look for forest clearings, a lake and arenas amid farmland.

name: Universal Studios Hollywood
blurb: A theme park on a working movie studio, terraced into the hills above the Cahuenga Pass. Look for soundstages below and the backlot's streets and sets spread down the slope.

name: Universal Studios Florida
blurb: Universal's original Orlando park, opened in 1990, beside a lagoon. Look for soundstages and rides around the water with Islands of Adventure next door.

name: Sentul International Circuit
blurb: Indonesia's main racetrack, in the hills south of Jakarta near Bogor. Look for the circuit carved into green slopes amid expanding suburbs.

name: Moscow Raceway
blurb: A modern Tilke-designed circuit in the countryside about 60 miles west of Moscow, built for touring car and superbike racing. Look for the gray loop in open fields and birch forest.

name: Estadio Tomás Adolfo Ducó
blurb: Huracán's home in Parque Patricios, with a striking art-deco tower on the main stand. Look for the oval in the dense grid of southern Buenos Aires.

name: Cluj Arena
blurb: Cluj-Napoca's modern 2011 arena, home of Universitatea Cluj, sits beside the Someș River next to Central Park. Look for a tidy rectangular roof ring on the riverbank west of the old town.

name: Mount Smart Stadium
blurb: Home of the New Zealand Warriors rugby league team, built in an old volcanic scoria quarry in south Auckland. Look for the ground sunk among the low hills.

name: Estadio Atanasio Girardot
blurb: Medellín's main stadium, shared by Atlético Nacional and Independiente Medellín, part of a sports complex in the Aburrá Valley. Look for the oval next to arenas and pools along the city's main river corridor.

name: Princess Auto Stadium
blurb: Home of the Winnipeg Blue Bombers since 2013, on the University of Manitoba campus. Look for the stadium inside a bend of the Red River in south Winnipeg.

name: Stade de la Paix
blurb: Bouaké's stadium, renovated as a host venue for the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. Its name, the Peace Stadium, nods to the city's role as the rebel capital during the civil war.

name: New Antalya Stadium
blurb: Antalya's modern stadium, built in 2015 with a roof covered in solar panels. Look for the boxy stadium in the city's north, between the resort coast and the Taurus Mountains.

name: Estadio Doroteo Guamuch Flores
blurb: Guatemala's national stadium, long known as the Mateo Flores, home to the national team in the heart of Guatemala City. Look for the open bowl set in a ravine-cut city ringed by volcanoes.

name: Chornomorets Stadium
blurb: Home of FC Chornomorets in Odesa, set in a park just above the port and the Black Sea shore. Look for the oval between green parkland and the harbor.

name: Kamuzu Stadium
blurb: Blantyre's old national ground, named for Hastings Kamuzu Banda, Malawi's first president. Look for the open oval in the city's hilly center.

name: Great Bridge of Hrazdan
blurb: A Soviet-era arch bridge carrying one of Yerevan's main roads over the deep Hrazdan gorge. Look for the river canyon cutting through the city's west side.

name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
blurb: One of the largest masonry dams in the world, on the Krishna River, completed in the late 1960s. Look for a long stone wall holding back a sprawling reservoir, with irrigation canals fanning out across farmland.

name: Yi Sun-sin Bridge
blurb: A suspension bridge opened in 2012 with a main span of about 5,070 ft, one of the longest in the world, and towers about 890 ft tall. Named for the admiral who beat the Japanese navy in these waters.

name: Dez Dam
blurb: A concrete arch more than 600 ft tall in a gorge of the Dez River, finished in 1963, supplying irrigation to the plains of Khuzestan. Look for a curved wall in a narrow rocky canyon above flat farmland.

name: Jamuna Bridge
blurb: About 3 miles long, it was among the longest bridges in South Asia when it opened in 1998. Look for it crossing the huge braided channel of the Jamuna and its sandbars.

name: Volga Hydroelectric Station
blurb: Once Europe's largest hydro plant, opened in 1961 just upstream of Volgograd. Look for the long dam across the Volga, with the Volga-Akhtuba floodplain's green maze of channels below.

name: Manantali Dam
blurb: A large dam on the Bafing River in western Mali, built in the 1980s to regulate the Senegal River for three countries. Look for a big reservoir in dry, open savanna.

name: Farakka Barrage
blurb: A 1.4-mile barrage across the Ganges, built to push water into the Hooghly and keep Kolkata's port from silting up. It has strained relations with Bangladesh for decades; look for the long concrete line across a vast river.

name: Sup'ung Dam
blurb: Built by the Japanese in 1941 on the Yalu River between China and North Korea, once one of the largest dams in Asia. Look for a long concrete dam across the border river with a big winding reservoir.

name: Kainji Dam
blurb: Dams the Niger River in western Nigeria, completed in 1968, creating Kainji Lake, one of the country's largest. Look for the wide reservoir spreading north through savanna.

name: Xihoumen Bridge
blurb: A suspension bridge in the Zhoushan archipelago opened in 2009 with a main span of about 5,410 ft, at the time second only to Japan's Akashi Kaikyo Bridge. Look for it linking two green islands.

name: Jiangyin Yangtze River Bridge
blurb: A 1999 suspension bridge across the Yangtze at Jiangyin, among the first of China's big modern spans. Look for its towers over a narrow reach of the busy river.

name: Magampura Mahinda Rajapaksa Port
blurb: Better known as Hambantota, built with Chinese loans and leased to a Chinese company for 99 years in 2017. Look for a basin cut inland from the southern coast, often with few ships.

name: Lions Gate Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1938 and paid for by the Guinness brewing family to reach their land on the North Shore. Look for its green towers springing from Stanley Park across the harbor narrows.

name: Vincent Thomas Bridge
blurb: A green 1963 suspension bridge linking San Pedro to Terminal Island in the Port of Los Angeles. Look for it above the cranes and stacked containers.

name: Vinh Cam Ranh
blurb: One of the best deep-water natural harbors in Southeast Asia, used by US forces during the Vietnam War and by the Soviet navy after. Look for a large enclosed bay sheltered by a long peninsula.

name: Port of Koper
blurb: Slovenia's only cargo port, on a coastline under 30 miles long. Look for car terminals and container stacks beside the old town, once an island.

name: Port of Klaipėda
blurb: Lithuania's only seaport, sheltered behind the Curonian Spit, a 60-mile ribbon of dunes. Look for the narrow channel where the lagoon meets the Baltic.

name: Zea harbor
blurb: Piraeus' round harbor, once the main base of the ancient Athenian navy with sheds for nearly 200 warships. Look for a nearly circular marina full of yachts on the east side of Piraeus.

name: Port of Tokyo
blurb: Tokyo's harbor, much of it built on landfill in the bay. Look for the white Rainbow Bridge and the Odaiba waterfront, with container terminals on the islands beyond.

name: Mala Rijeka Viaduct
blurb: A railway viaduct about 650 ft over a gorge on the Belgrade to Bar line, once the highest railroad bridge in the world. Look for tall concrete piers across a rugged canyon north of Podgorica.

name: Rosslare Europort
blurb: Ireland's main ferry port for Wales and France, at the southeast tip of the country. Look for a long pier sticking out from a low, sandy coast.

name: Alexandria Port
blurb: Egypt's main seaport for over 2,000 years. The Pharos lighthouse, a Wonder of the Ancient World, stood at its mouth where Qaitbay Citadel stands now; look for the fort on the point between the two harbors.

name: Port of Amsterdam
blurb: Linked to the North Sea by a canal, it is one of Europe's largest ports for gasoline and cocoa. Look for docks lining the straight North Sea Canal west of the city.

name: Franjo Tuđman Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge over the Dubrovnik river inlet just above Gruž harbor. Look for its single white pylon on the approach, with cruise ships docked below.

name: Yokohama Bay Bridge
blurb: A double-deck cable-stayed bridge over the entrance to Yokohama harbor, opened in 1989. Look for its pale H-shaped towers above the port's piers and container docks.

name: Rama IX Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1987 for the King's 60th birthday, it held one of the longest cable-stayed spans in the world at the time. Look for the yellow cables in a single central plane over the Chao Phraya.

name: Yangpu Bridge
blurb: When it opened in 1993, its roughly 1,975-ft main span was the longest cable-stayed span in the world. Look for its diamond-shaped towers over the Huangpu northeast of the Bund.

name: Padma Bridge
blurb: Bangladesh's largest bridge, over 3.8 miles of road and rail across the Padma, opened in 2022. Look for its long straight line across one of the world's most powerful rivers.

name: Bandra–Worli Sea Link
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge curving about 3.5 miles across Mahim Bay, linking Bandra to Worli. Look for its tall towers rising out of the sea off Mumbai's west coast.

name: Branko's Bridge
blurb: One of Belgrade's main road bridges over the Sava, linking the old city to New Belgrade. Look for the low span crossing the river just upstream of where the Sava meets the Danube below the fortress.

name: Dollywood
blurb: Dolly Parton's park in Pigeon Forge, in the foothills of the Smoky Mountains. Look for coaster tracks winding through forested hills.

name: Lanfranconi Bridge
blurb: The westernmost of Bratislava's Danube bridges, carrying the motorway across the river just upstream of the old town and castle. Look for the long span where the Little Carpathians meet the river.

name: Moominworld
blurb: The world of the Moomins on Kailo, a small island off Naantali. Look for a blue Moominhouse among trees on the island in the archipelago.

name: Taman Mini Indonesia Indah
blurb: A park of Indonesian culture in east Jakarta, with pavilions in the style of every province. Look for the lake holding a miniature map of the archipelago's islands.

name: Gazela Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1970, it carries Serbia's main motorway over the Sava in central Belgrade and is the busiest bridge in the city. Look for the concrete arch with the New Belgrade blocks on one side.

name: Storseisundet Bridge
blurb: The bridge on the Atlantic Ocean Road, which seems to end in midair from some angles. Look for the road hopping over low islets and skerries in the open sea.

name: Stone Bridge (Regensburg)
blurb: Built in the 1100s with 16 stone arches across the Danube, a model for medieval bridges across Europe. Look for it leading into Regensburg's old town by the twin cathedral spires.

name: Saratov Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1965 and about 1.7 miles long, it was among the longest bridges in the Soviet Union. Look for the straight line across the broad Volga from Saratov to Engels.

name: Autódromo Termas de Río Hondo
blurb: Home of MotoGP's Argentine Grand Prix since 2014, in a small spa town in Santiago del Estero. Look for the circuit beside the big reservoir in flat, dry scrub.

name: Legoland Billund
blurb: The first Legoland, opened in 1968 next to Lego's hometown headquarters. Look for colorful rides and a miniature town just beside Billund Airport's runway.

name: Talladega Superspeedway
blurb: At 2.66 miles NASCAR's longest oval, with turns banked 33 degrees, and home of the sport's biggest multi-car wrecks. Look for the huge tri-oval and its long grandstand beside an old airstrip.

name: Mons Claudianus
blurb: A Roman quarry deep in Egypt's Eastern Desert, worked for gray granite columns shipped all the way to Rome. Look for the ruined fort and quarry scars in the barren mountains.

name: Estadio Polideportivo de Pueblo Nuevo
blurb: Home of Deportivo Táchira in San Cristóbal, in the Andean foothills near the Colombian border. Look for an oval wedged into a hilly valley city.

name: Estadio Sergio León Chávez
blurb: Club León's stadium, often still called the Nou Camp, a 1970 and 1986 World Cup venue. Look for the oval in León, Mexico's shoe-making capital.

name: Naghsh-e-Jahan Stadium
blurb: Isfahan's main stadium, home of Sepahan, named for the city's famous square. Look for the open bowl north of the city on the dry plain.

name: Sarusajai Stadium (Guwahati)
blurb: Guwahati's main sports complex and home ground of NorthEast United in the Indian Super League. Look for the oval in the city's southern sprawl, near the hills above the Brahmaputra.

name: R. Premadasa Stadium
blurb: Colombo's big cricket ground, where Sri Lanka made 952 for 6 against India in 1997, still the highest total in Test history. Look for the bright oval among the dense neighborhoods north of the city center.

name: Estadio Rommel Fernández
blurb: Panama's national stadium in Panama City, named for a local football star. Look for the oval on the city's east side, away from the Bay of Panama skyline.

name: Papara Park
blurb: Trabzonspor's stadium sits right on the Black Sea shore west of central Trabzon, on reclaimed land beside the coastal highway. Look for the roofed bowl at the water's edge with the green Pontic hills rising behind.

name: Independence Park
blurb: Jamaica's National Stadium, built for independence in 1962 and home of the Reggae Boyz. Look for the open bowl in Kingston's north side, the Blue Mountains behind.

name: DY Patil Stadium
blurb: A large stadium in Navi Mumbai used for IPL cricket and the 2017 U-17 World Cup. Look for the bowl in the new city across the harbor from Mumbai.

name: Stadionul Ion Oblemenco
blurb: Craiova's 2017 rebuild, named for local football hero Ion Oblemenco, with a lit facade that glows in color at night. Look for the oval roof inside a large green park on the city's west side.

name: Kadir Has Stadium
blurb: Kayseri's stadium, opened in 2009 on the city's edge. On a clear day, look for the snowy cone of Mount Erciyes, a 12,800-ft volcano, rising just south of the city.

name: Konya Büyükşehir Stadium
blurb: Konyaspor's home on the flat Anatolian plateau, opened in 2014. Look for the roofed stadium in an open park on the edge of the flat, sprawling city.

name: Corona Stadium
blurb: Santos Laguna's stadium, the Territorio Santos Modelo, opened in 2009 in Torreón. Look for the modern bowl in the desert-edge city, with dry ranges of the Comarca Lagunera around it.

name: Estadio Metropolitano de Fútbol de Lara
blurb: Barquisimeto's stadium, built for the 2007 Copa América on the city's outskirts. Look for a big bowl ringed by open ground.

name: Marcelo Bielsa Stadium
blurb: Newell's Old Boys' home, named for the coach who came out of the club. Look for the bowl inside Parque de la Independencia, Rosario's big central park.

name: Baihetan Dam
blurb: The world's second-largest hydro plant after Three Gorges, finished in 2022 on the Jinsha River (the upper Yangtze). Its curved arch wall stands about 950 ft tall; look for it wedged into a deep canyon.

name: Kadiran Dam
blurb: A dam on the Euphrates in northern Syria, downstream of the big Tabqa Dam and Lake Assad. Look for the river widening behind a low barrier, a green ribbon through dry steppe.

name: Sanmenxia Dam
blurb: The first big dam on the Yellow River, finished in 1960 and almost immediately clogged by the river's heavy silt, forcing years of rebuilding. Look for a concrete dam across a brown river in loess country.

name: Merowe Dam
blurb: Built across the Nile at the Fourth Cataract and finished in 2009, displacing tens of thousands of people. Look for a long reservoir in pure desert, the only blue for hundreds of miles.

name: Salto Grande Dam
blurb: Built jointly by Argentina and Uruguay on the Uruguay River, with a road and railway running across its crest between the two countries. Look for a long dam across a wide river with a big reservoir upstream.

name: Askøy Bridge
blurb: Bergen's link to the island of Askøy, a suspension bridge opened in 1992 with a main span of about 2,800 ft, long one of the longest in Norway. Look for twin towers over the fjord just northwest of the city.

name: Port of Mariupol
blurb: A steel-exporting port on the Sea of Azov, besieged and taken by Russia in 2022. Look for the vast Azovstal steelworks on the shore beside the docks.

name: Port of Melilla
blurb: Harbor of a Spanish city on the North African coast, surrounded on land by Morocco. Look for the walled old town on its headland above the docks and the border fence curving inland.

name: Egyptian Bridge
blurb: A small footbridge over the Fontanka guarded by sphinxes. The original collapsed in 1905 as cavalry crossed. From the air look for the curving canal rather than the bridge.

name: Port of Houston
blurb: At the head of a 50-mile ship channel, the busiest US port by foreign tonnage. Look for the ship channel lined with refineries and the Barbours Cut container terminal on Galveston Bay.

name: Port of New York and New Jersey
blurb: The busiest port on the East Coast. Look for Port Newark and Elizabeth, a sea of containers beside Newark airport, and ships passing under the Bayonne Bridge.

name: Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1968, the first Yangtze bridge designed and built by China itself, carrying road above and rail beneath. Look for its long steel truss across the river north of the city.

name: Pančevo Bridge
blurb: A combined road and rail bridge over the Danube at Belgrade, for decades the city's only Danube crossing. Look for the long low span crossing the wide river below the old fortress, with flat farmland beyond.

name: Vidyasagar Setu
blurb: Opened in 1992, a cable-stayed bridge across the Hooghly in Kolkata with a main span of about 1,500 ft, among the longest in India. Look for the fanned cables a little downstream of the old steel Howrah Bridge.

name: Prince of Wales Bridge
blurb: About 3.2 miles long, opened in 1996 as the Second Severn Crossing. Its cable-stayed center sits over the shipping channel; the Severn's tides here are among the largest in the world.

name: James Joyce Bridge
blurb: A Calatrava bridge over the Liffey, named for the writer and opened on Bloomsday in 2003. Look for its tilted white arches on Dublin's western quays.

name: New River Gorge Bridge
blurb: A 3,030-ft steel arch hung 876 ft above the New River, once the longest single-span arch in the world. Every October, Bridge Day lets BASE jumpers leap off it; look for the rust-brown arch over the forested gorge.

name: Đurđevića Tara Bridge
blurb: A 1940 concrete arch bridge about 560 ft above the Tara River canyon. In 1942 its own engineer helped blow up an arch to stop the Italian advance. Look for the white arches over the deep green gorge.

name: Incheon Asiad Main Stadium
blurb: The main stadium of the 2014 Asian Games, in Incheon's northwest. Look for the asymmetric roof covering mostly one side of the bowl.

name: Stade Olympique de Sousse
blurb: Étoile du Sahel's home in Sousse, a coastal city of beaches and an old walled medina. Look for an open oval in the city a short way back from the Mediterranean shore.

name: Abbasiyyin Stadium
blurb: Damascus's big multi-use stadium, used for decades for national team matches and military parades. Look for the open oval among the dense city east of the old walled center.

name: Sree Kanteerava Stadium
blurb: Bengaluru's main athletics and soccer stadium, home of Bengaluru FC, in the heart of the city. Look for the oval track next to the green expanse of Cubbon Park.

name: National Stadium
blurb: Freetown's national stadium, known for years as Siaka Stevens Stadium, packed for Leone Stars matches. Look for an open bowl in the crowded city on the hills above the harbor.

name: King Abdulaziz Sports City
blurb: Mecca's main stadium complex, home of Al-Wehda, set among the bare rocky hills that ring the holy city. Look for an oval bowl surrounded by sandy-brown peaks and dense housing.

name: Estadio Ciudad de Lanús Néstor Díaz Pérez
blurb: Club Lanús' home, nicknamed La Fortaleza, in the southern suburbs of Buenos Aires. Look for the compact bowl in the low-rise grid of Lanús.

name: Estadio José Antonio Anzoátegui
blurb: A 2007 Copa América venue in Puerto La Cruz on Venezuela's Caribbean coast. Look for the oval a short way inland from the marinas and beaches.

name: Usoi Dam
blurb: The tallest dam on Earth, natural or man-made: a 1911 earthquake brought down a mountainside about 1,800 ft high, blocking a river and creating Sarez Lake. Look for the long turquoise lake in the Pamirs.

name: Katse Dam
blurb: A double-curvature arch over 600 ft high in Lesotho's highlands, part of a scheme that sends water by tunnel to Johannesburg. Look for a thin, curved concrete wall in steep, treeless mountains.

name: Vanderkloof Dam
blurb: The tallest dam wall in South Africa, on the Orange River downstream of Gariep. Look for the concrete arch tucked into a narrow gorge with a long lake behind it.

name: Koyna Dam
blurb: Its reservoir is blamed for setting off the 1967 Koynanagar earthquake, one of the best-known cases of a dam triggering a quake. Look for a long, narrow lake in the forested Western Ghats.

name: Inga Dams
blurb: The Congo River drops about 300 ft here at Inga Falls, the greatest hydropower potential of any site on Earth. The giant Grand Inga scheme is still unbuilt; Inga I and II already run. Look for rapids and a canal-fed reservoir beside the wide river.

name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge
blurb: Twin spans about 4.3 miles across the Chesapeake, often listed among the scariest bridges in America for its height and length. Look for the two parallel lines rising over the shipping channel near Annapolis.

name: Port Zayed
blurb: Abu Dhabi's original port, now mainly a cruise terminal since cargo moved to Khalifa Port. Look for docks between the city's island and the mainland channels.

name: Benjamin Franklin Bridge
blurb: When it opened in 1926 its 1,750-ft main span was the longest suspension span in the world. It links Philadelphia to Camden; look for the blue-gray cables crossing the Delaware just north of Center City's skyline.

name: Tanger-Med
blurb: One of the largest container ports in Africa and the Mediterranean, on the Strait of Gibraltar. Look for vast terminals on a steep coast with Spain visible about 9 miles across the water.

name: Saint Thomas of Castilla
blurb: Guatemala's main Caribbean port on the Bay of Amatique, next to Puerto Barrios. Look for container yards on a sheltered bay ringed by green hills.

name: Port of Constanța
blurb: The largest port on the Black Sea, linked to the Danube by canal. Look for long breakwaters enclosing huge basins south of the city.

name: Höga Kusten Bridge
blurb: A suspension bridge from 1997 with a main span of about 3,970 ft, a few dozen feet shorter than the Golden Gate. Look for its tall towers over the mouth of the Ångerman River on the forested High Coast.

name: Port of Tianjin
blurb: Beijing's gateway to the sea and one of the world's busiest ports. In 2015 warehouse explosions here were felt miles away; look for reclaimed land and endless container yards on Bohai Bay.

name: 516 Arouca
blurb: A pedestrian suspension bridge about 1,690 ft long, hung roughly 570 ft above the Paiva River gorge; it was the world's longest when it opened in 2021. From the air it's a hairline across a wooded valley.

name: Port of Mongla
blurb: Bangladesh's second seaport, on the Pasur River at the edge of the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest. Look for ships anchored in a brown river winding through dark green swamp.

name: Port of Long Beach
blurb: Together with neighboring Los Angeles, the busiest port complex in the US. Look for stacked containers on reclaimed land, the white cable-stayed bridge, and the Queen Mary moored at the edge.

name: Puerto San José
blurb: An old Pacific port on Guatemala's flat, black-sand coast; modern cargo and cruise ships use nearby Puerto Quetzal. Look for the straight shoreline and lagoons behind it.

name: Peace Bridge
blurb: A 1927 arched bridge across the Niagara River between Buffalo and Fort Erie, built to mark peace between the US and Canada. Look for its steel arches where Lake Erie drains into the river.

name: Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge
blurb: The first bridge ever across the Yangtze, opened in 1957, carrying road on top and rail beneath. Look for its steel truss between Turtle and Snake hills in central Wuhan.

name: Stonecutters Bridge
blurb: Its 3,340-ft span crosses the entrance to Kwai Tsing container port, one of the world's busiest. Look for two tall slender towers fanning cables over the shipping channel.

name: Tabiat Bridge
blurb: A footbridge that winds over a Tehran expressway to join two hillside parks, designed by a young architect in her twenties. Look for its branching, tree-like steel structure.

name: Rio Negro Bridge
blurb: About 2.2 miles long, it opened in 2011 as the first bridge across the Rio Negro, linking Manaus to Iranduba on the far bank. Look for a cable-stayed span over the tea-colored river.

name: Liberty Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge over the Danube in Novi Sad, destroyed by NATO bombing in 1999 and rebuilt by 2005. Look for twin pylons near the Petrovaradin Fortress on the opposite bank.

name: Alton Towers
blurb: A theme park around the ruins of a Gothic mansion in the Staffordshire countryside. Look for coaster tracks among woods and a castle-like ruin.

name: Santa Monica Pier
blurb: The pier at the end of Route 66, with a solar-powered Ferris wheel and a roller coaster. Look for the wooden pier jutting out from the beach below the bluffs.

name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel
blurb: About 17.6 miles shore to shore, opened in 1964, it dives into two mile-long tunnels under the shipping channels. Look for the road ending on small artificial islands in the open bay.

name: Amizade Bridge
blurb: A long concrete bridge linking the Macau peninsula to Taipa, with a high section for ships. Look for it beside the two other crossings over the channel.

name: Neeltje Jans
blurb: An artificial island built for the Oosterschelde storm-surge barrier, the biggest of the Delta Works. Look for the barrier's piers striding across the estuary.

name: Bhumibol Bridge
blurb: Two cable-stayed bridges opened in 2006 that cross the Chao Phraya twice where it loops south of Bangkok, joined by an elevated interchange. Look for the two sets of pylons on either side of the green Bang Krachao bend.

name: Fourth Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
blurb: Joins Chiang Khong in Thailand to Houayxay in Laos across the Mekong, opened in 2013. Look for a modest concrete span over the brown river among green hills.

name: Bayonne Bridge
blurb: A steel arch to Staten Island whose roadbed was raised in 2019 so the largest container ships could pass under. Look for the arch over the Kill Van Kull.

name: Birchenough Bridge
blurb: A steel arch from 1935 over the Save River, designed by Ralph Freeman, who also designed the Sydney Harbour Bridge. It looks like a smaller version; look for the silver arch over the wide sandy riverbed.

name: Fehmarn Sound Bridge
blurb: A 1963 arch bridge to the island of Fehmarn, nicknamed the coat hanger for its shape. Look for the white steel arch over the narrow sound on the route to Denmark.

name: Miloud Hadefi Stadium
blurb: Oran's Olympic Stadium, seating about 40,000, opened in 2021 and the main venue of the 2022 Mediterranean Games. Look for the large bowl in Bir El Djir on the city's eastern side.

name: Bogyoke Aung San Stadium
blurb: Yangon's old downtown stadium, a compact ground from the colonial era near the Sule Pagoda area. Look for the green pitch squeezed into the dense city blocks.

name: Nelson Mandela Stadium
blurb: A 40,000-seat Chinese-built stadium in Baraki on the south side of Algiers, opened in January 2023 for the African Nations Championship. Look for the modern bowl among new housing blocks.

name: Stade Omar Bongo
blurb: Libreville's older national stadium, named for Gabon's long-serving president. Look for the oval in the capital's dense center near the Gabon estuary.

name: Estadio Félix Capriles
blurb: Cochabamba's main stadium, in a green valley at about 8,400 ft. Look for the oval near the city center, with the Tunari range rising behind.

name: Estadio Campeón del Siglo
blurb: Peñarol's own stadium, opened in 2016 on the open fields northeast of Montevideo near the airport. Look for an isolated bowl in farmland.

name: Stade Général Seyni Kountché
blurb: Niger's national stadium in Niamey, near the Niger River. Look for the oval green pitch and running track standing out against the dusty, sand-colored city.

name: Gaziantep Stadium
blurb: Gaziantep's modern stadium, opened in 2017 on the city's edge. Look for the boxy stadium amid the pistachio-growing country of southeastern Turkey.

name: Estadio Nacional Jose de la Paz Herrera
blurb: Honduras's national stadium in Tegucigalpa, home to Olimpia and Motagua's derby. Look for the open bowl beside the river in a city spread over steep, crowded hills.

name: Estadio Hernán Ramírez Villegas
blurb: Pereira's stadium, home of Deportivo Pereira, in Colombia's coffee country. Look for the oval bowl on the city's green hillsides.

name: Orlando Stadium
blurb: Soweto's own stadium, home of Orlando Pirates, rebuilt in 2008 on the site of the original ground. Look for a compact bowl among the township's tight rows of small houses.

name: Davtashen Bridge
blurb: One of Yerevan's bridges across the Hrazdan gorge in the northwest of the city. Look for the green ribbon of the canyon cutting through the apartment blocks.

name: Tekezé Dam
blurb: One of the tallest arch dams in Africa, about 600 ft high, in a deep canyon of the Tekezé River in northern Ethiopia. Look for a curved wall jammed into a steep, arid gorge with a long, thin reservoir behind it.

name: Pont del Diable
blurb: A medieval bridge on Roman foundations over the Llobregat at Martorell, with a steep pointed central arch and a small Roman arch at one end. Legend says the devil built it overnight.

name: Sennar Dam
blurb: Built on the Blue Nile in 1925 to irrigate the Gezira Scheme, one of the world's largest irrigation projects. Look for the green grid of fields spreading north from the river.

name: Gezhouba Dam
blurb: The first dam ever built across the Yangtze, finished in the 1980s at Yichang, about 25 miles downstream of the Three Gorges Dam. Look for a long, low barrier with ship locks spanning the wide river beside the city.

name: Mratinje Dam
blurb: A concrete arch about 720 ft tall in the canyon of the Piva River, one of the tallest dams in Europe. Look for a thin curved wall wedged into a deep limestone gorge with a turquoise lake behind it.

name: Kyiv Hydroelectric Power Plant
blurb: Dams the Dnieper just north of Kyiv, creating the huge Kyiv Reservoir that locals call the Kyiv Sea. Look for the long dam where the broad lake narrows back into the river.

name: Vaal Dam
