blurb: The reservoir that keeps Johannesburg and much of Gauteng supplied with water, on the Vaal River since 1938. Look for a sprawling, many-armed lake south of the city.

name: Srisailam Dam
blurb: A big dam on the Krishna River, in a gorge through the Nallamala hills, with a famous Shiva temple nearby. Look for a curved wall in a deep forested canyon and a long, winding reservoir behind it.

name: Wudongde Hydropower Station
blurb: A thin double-curved arch dam nearly 900 ft tall in a deep gorge of the Jinsha River, the upper Yangtze. Look for the pale curve of concrete between steep, bare canyon walls.

name: Shasta Dam
blurb: At 602 ft tall it backs up Shasta Lake, California's largest reservoir, and holds water for much of the Central Valley. Look for a curved concrete wall below a many-armed lake, with snowy Mount Shasta to the north.

name: Kölnbrein Dam
blurb: Austria's tallest dam, about 650 ft high, a concrete arch sitting high in the Hohe Tauern mountains. Look for a curved white wall at the head of an alpine valley, with a turquoise lake behind it.

name: Pivnichnyi Bridge
blurb: Kyiv's northern cable-stayed bridge over the Dnieper, opened in 1976 as the Moscow Bridge and renamed in 2018. Look for its single tall pylon above the river's islands and sandbars.

name: Port of Durrës
blurb: Albania's largest port, with ferries across the Adriatic to Bari and Ancona. Look for breakwaters and cranes beside an old town that still has a Roman amphitheater.

name: Humen Pearl River Bridge
blurb: A 1997 suspension bridge across the Pearl River estuary, which famously rippled up and down in 2020 from wind and closed for checks. Look for its towers above the estuary's shipping lanes.

name: Kvalsund Bridge
blurb: One of the northernmost suspension bridges in the world, crossing a sound well above the Arctic Circle near Hammerfest. Its main span is about 1,700 ft; look for a thin line between bare, treeless hills.

name: Bronx–Whitestone Bridge
blurb: A 1939 suspension bridge across the East River where it opens into Long Island Sound. Look for its slim gray towers between the Bronx and Queens.

name: Loschwitz Bridge
blurb: The Blue Wonder, an 1893 steel bridge painted blue, which survived the end of World War II intact. Look for its truss crossing the Elbe below Dresden's villas.

name: PortMiami
blurb: The world's busiest cruise port, on Dodge Island between downtown and Miami Beach. Look for a row of giant white cruise ships, especially on weekends.

name: Port of Tanjung Pelepas
blurb: One of the world's busiest container ports, across the Strait of Johor from Singapore. Look for long straight quays of cranes cut into mangrove coast at the Pulai River mouth.

name: Port of Casablanca
blurb: Morocco's largest port. Look for the Hassan II Mosque next to it, built partly over the sea with a minaret of nearly 700 ft.

name: Port Kavkaz
blurb: Ferry port on the Chushka Spit facing Crimea across the narrow Kerch Strait. Look for a thin sand spit pointing west and the long Crimean Bridge to the south.

name: Shahid Rajai Port
blurb: Iran's largest container port, west of Bandar Abbas on the Strait of Hormuz. In April 2025 a huge chemical explosion tore through it; look for container yards on the flat shore facing Qeshm Island.

name: Port of Karachi
blurb: Pakistan's largest and busiest port, on a natural harbor sheltered by Manora island. Look for docks along channels through mangroves west of the city.

name: Labadee
blurb: A private beach resort leased by Royal Caribbean on Haiti's north coast. Look for a cruise ship docked at a green peninsula with white beaches.

name: Helgeland bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge opened in 1991 that carries the coast road to Sandnessjøen, with a main span of about 1,400 ft. Look for its two tall concrete pylons against the jagged Seven Sisters peaks.

name: Strömsund Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1956 in Strömsund, Jämtland, it is usually called the first modern cable-stayed bridge, the design behind thousands built since. From the air it's a small span over a lake narrows in endless forest.

name: Uddevalla Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge opened in 2000 carrying the E6 motorway over the fjord at Uddevalla. Look for its tall pylons crossing the water on Sweden's rocky west coast.

name: Rande Bridge
blurb: A cable-stayed bridge from 1981 crossing the Vigo estuary at its narrowest point. When it was widened in 2017, extra lanes were hung off the outside of the existing deck. Look for the mussel rafts on the water.

name: Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge
blurb: The Second Penang Bridge, about 15 miles long and among the longest bridges in Southeast Asia, opened in 2014. Look for its thin line across the strait well south of the first bridge.

name: Queensferry Crossing
blurb: Opened in 2017, about 1.7 miles long and the longest three-tower cable-stayed bridge in the world. Look for it beside the red Forth Bridge and the 1964 road bridge, three centuries in a row.

name: Saint-Nazaire Bridge
blurb: About 2 miles long, it crosses the mouth of the Loire with a high central span for ships. Look for its long curving ramps between Saint-Nazaire's shipyards and the south bank.

name: High Chaparral Theme Park
blurb: A Wild West theme park in the forests of Småland. Look for a frontier town in the woods.

name: Richmond Bridge
blurb: Built by convicts in the 1820s, it is the oldest bridge in Australia still in use. Its sandstone arches cross the Coal River in a small Georgian town north of Hobart.

name: Malaysia–Singapore Second Link
blurb: Opened in 1998 at Singapore's western tip to relieve the jammed Causeway to Johor. Look for a low bridge across the narrow Johor Strait, with Tuas shipyards and reclaimed land nearby.

name: Črni Kal Viaduct
blurb: Slovenia's longest viaduct, about 0.7 miles, opened in 2004 on the motorway down to Koper. Its Y-shaped piers stand up to roughly 300 ft tall above a valley on the edge of the karst plateau.

name: Phantasialand
blurb: A compact theme park packed into Brühl near Cologne, with rides stacked over and under each other. Look for tight-packed rides among trees.

name: Knott's Berry Farm
blurb: Began in the 1920s as a roadside berry stand and chicken dinner restaurant in Buena Park, now a big theme park. Look for coaster tracks among the suburban grid.

name: Krungthep Bridge
blurb: A bascule bridge opened in 1959 over the Chao Phraya in Bangkok, with a center section built to lift for ships. Look for the low span among the river's busy barge traffic.

name: Third Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
blurb: Spans the Mekong between Nakhon Phanom in Thailand and Thakhek in Laos, opened in 2011. Look for it crossing the wide river with limestone peaks rising on the Lao side.

name: Kanuni Sultan Suleiman bridge
blurb: A stone bridge commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by Mimar Sinan, finished in the 1560s. Its chain of arches hops across the mouth of the Büyükçekmece lagoon west of Istanbul, beside the modern road.

name: Seven Mile Bridge
blurb: About 6.8 miles over open water in the Florida Keys, one of the longest bridges in the US. Look for the old 1912 railroad bridge running alongside it in broken pieces.

name: Third Mainland Bridge
blurb: About 7 miles long across the Lagos Lagoon, among the longest bridges in Africa. Look for the Makoko stilt village sprawling in the water beside it.

name: Queen Louise Bridge
blurb: Only the ornate stone portal survived when the bridge was blown up in 1944. Look for a short span across the Neman between Sovetsk, the old Tilsit, and Lithuania.

name: Bolsheokhtinsky Bridge
blurb: Peter the Great Bridge, a blue-gray 1911 bascule bridge over the Neva near the Smolny Cathedral. Look for its two lighthouse-like control towers in the middle of the span.

name: Legoland Malaysia
blurb: The first Legoland in Asia, opened in 2012 in Johor across the strait from Singapore. Look for colorful rides and a lake among new developments.

name: Penrhyn Quarry
blurb: Once the largest slate quarry in the world, its stepped galleries reach about 1,200 ft deep beside Bethesda. Look for the gray amphitheater of terraces cut into the mountainside.

name: Honor Stadium
blurb: Oujda's main stadium, near Morocco's closed border with Algeria in the far northeast. Look for an open athletics bowl ringed by a running track.

name: Estadio Agustín Tovar
blurb: The main stadium in Barinas, on the edge of the llanos plains, used in the 2007 Copa América. Look for an oval in flat green ranch country.

name: Al-Merrikh Stadium
blurb: Al-Merrikh's home in Omdurman, nicknamed the Red Castle for the club's red colors. Look for an open bowl in the low, sandy city on the Nile's west bank, across from Khartoum.

name: Sultan Ibrahim Stadium
blurb: Johor Darul Ta'zim's 40,000-seat stadium, opened in 2020 in Iskandar Puteri, with a facade patterned like a woven royal headdress. Look for the bowl in the new city across from Singapore.

name: Sarawak Stadium
blurb: Kuching's main stadium, in the Petra Jaya sports complex north of the Sarawak River. Look for the open bowl among green hills and low suburbs.

name: Independence Stadium
blurb: The Gambia's national stadium in Bakau, near the Atlantic coast just west of Banjul. Look for an open oval among the low rooftops of the coastal towns.

name: Pakansari Stadium
blurb: A 30,000-seat stadium in Cibinong, south of Jakarta, used by the national team. Look for the oval with a tall roof among rice fields and new suburbs of Bogor regency.

name: Estadio Palogrande
blurb: Manizales' stadium, home of Once Caldas, set on a ridge in a city built along steep Andean crests. Look for the oval bowl among dense neighborhoods on the ridgeline.

name: Tan Sri Dato Haji Hassan Yunos Stadium
blurb: Larkin Stadium, the longtime home of Johor soccer in Johor Bahru. Look for the open bowl in the city's northern suburbs, a short hop from Singapore.

name: Estadio Metropolitano de Mérida
blurb: Built for the 2007 Copa América in Mérida, high in a valley of the Venezuelan Andes. Look for the bowl with mountains rising on both sides.

name: TEDA Football Stadium
blurb: A football-only stadium in Tianjin's Binhai development zone near the port, with stands close to the pitch. Look for the boxy stadium in the planned grid of the coastal new town.

name: Estadio Olímpico Metropolitano
blurb: The biggest stadium in Honduras, about 37,000 seats in San Pedro Sula, where the national team plays its World Cup qualifiers. Look for the bowl on the flat Sula Valley floor.

name: Estadio Rodrigo Paz Delgado
blurb: LDU Quito's stadium in the north of the city, at roughly 9,000 ft; LDU won the first leg of the 2008 Copa Libertadores final here on the way to the title. Look for the bowl with Pichincha volcano rising to the west.

name: Ombaka National Stadium
blurb: Built in Benguela on Angola's coast for the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations. Look for the modern bowl near the shore south of Lobito.

name: Iron Gate II Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: The second Danube dam below the Iron Gates gorge, shared by Serbia and Romania. Look for the dam and locks crossing the wide river as it leaves the mountains for the plains.

name: Gilgel Gibe III Dam
blurb: One of the tallest dams in Africa, about 800 ft high, on Ethiopia's Omo River. Critics worry it starves Kenya's Lake Turkana downstream of water. Look for a massive wall across a forested gorge.

name: El Chocón Dam
blurb: An embankment dam on the Limay River in Patagonia. The nearby lakeshore yielded Giganotosaurus, one of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs. Look for a big blue reservoir in dry, tan steppe.

name: Boguchany Dam
blurb: One of the largest hydroelectric dams in Russia, on the Angara River, finished in the 2010s after decades of delays. Look for a dam across a wide river in endless Siberian taiga.

name: Soo Locks
blurb: Ships drop or climb 21 ft here between Lake Superior and the lower lakes; the biggest lock handles 1,000-ft lake freighters. Look for parallel lock chambers beside the rapids of the St. Marys River.

name: Nampo Dam
blurb: The West Sea Barrage, a barrier about 5 miles long across the mouth of the Taedong River, finished in 1986 with locks for ships. Look for a long straight line across the estuary below Pyongyang.

name: Pak Mun Dam
blurb: Built across the Mun River near where it meets the Mekong, finished in 1994, it became a byword for fisheries lost to dams. Look for the low barrier across the river in flat rice country.

name: Toktogul Dam
blurb: Kyrgyzstan's largest dam, on the Naryn River, its reservoir the biggest in Central Asia's mountains and central to water fights with downstream neighbors. Look for a big blue lake among dry, brown peaks.

name: Hardap Dam
blurb: Namibia's largest reservoir, on the Fish River just outside Mariental. In a country this dry the lake is hard to miss: look for a broad sheet of water spreading across flat semi-desert.

name: Kozjak Hydro Power Plant
blurb: A tall dam on the Treska River west of Skopje, backing up a long, narrow reservoir through a steep forested canyon. Look for a thin snake of blue-green water in the hills.

name: Djorf Torba Dam
blurb: A dam on the Oued Guir near Béchar, holding water in the Algerian Sahara. Look for a blue reservoir in a bare, rocky desert valley, a rare patch of water for hundreds of miles.

name: Kaniv Hydroelectric Power Plant
blurb: One of the Dnieper's chain of dams, at Kaniv south of Kyiv. Look for the dam across the wide river, with a long reservoir stretching north.

name: ZOZO Marine Stadium
blurb: Home of the Chiba Lotte Marines, sitting right on Tokyo Bay, where sea winds make fly balls unpredictable. Look for the open bowl by the shore at Makuhari.

name: Al-Shaab Stadium
blurb: Baghdad's 'People's Stadium', opened in 1966 and long the home of the Iraqi national team. Look for the open bowl in the city's eastern districts.

name: Meiji Jingu Stadium
blurb: Opened in 1926, home of the Yakult Swallows; Babe Ruth played here on a 1934 tour. Look for the old ballpark beside the National Stadium in the Jingu Gaien gardens.

name: Hang Jebat Stadium
blurb: Melaka's main stadium, named for a legendary Malay warrior. Look for the open bowl in the outskirts of the old trading port.

name: Ahmadu Bello Stadium
blurb: Kaduna's main stadium, in northern Nigeria. Look for the oval with a running track in the city's center, near the Kaduna River.

name: Darul Aman Stadium
blurb: Home of Kedah soccer in Alor Setar, in the heart of Malaysia's rice bowl. Look for the stadium surrounded by flat green paddies.

name: Khartoum Stadium
blurb: Khartoum's main stadium, used by the national team and the city's clubs, close to where the Blue and White Niles meet. Look for an open oval in the low city near the river.

name: Kardinia Park
blurb: Geelong Cats' ground, the AFL's home stadium in Geelong. Look for an oval in parkland near Corio Bay.

name: Manahan Stadium
blurb: Solo's main stadium, home of Persis Solo, renovated in 2020 and a venue for the 2023 U-17 World Cup. Look for the bowl amid the low red roofs of central Surakarta.

name: Athlone Stadium
blurb: A stadium on the Cape Flats, used as a training venue for the 2010 World Cup and home to local football. Look for an open oval among the flat suburbs east of Cape Town's mountains.

name: Benghazi International Stadium
blurb: Benghazi's main stadium, rebuilt on the site of the city's old ground after years of war. Look for the large bowl near the coast in Libya's second city.

name: Wunna Theikdi Stadium
blurb: The centerpiece of Naypyidaw, Myanmar's purpose-built capital, built for the 2013 Southeast Asian Games. Like much of the city it's oversized for the crowds; look for the bowl amid wide, nearly empty boulevards.

name: Darul Makmur Stadium
blurb: Home of Pahang soccer in Kuantan, the main city on Malaysia's east coast. Look for the open bowl in low town blocks near the South China Sea.

name: Levy Mwanawasa Stadium
blurb: Built with Chinese help in Ndola and opened in 2012, it seats about 49,000. Look for the oval on the outskirts of the Copperbelt city.

name: Republican Spartak Stadium
blurb: Vladikavkaz's main football ground, in the North Caucasus. Look for the open bowl in the city on the Terek River, with the wall of the Greater Caucasus rising just to the south.

name: Victoria Stadium
blurb: Home of Necaxa, one of Mexico's oldest top-flight clubs, in the city of Aguascalientes. Look for the compact bowl among the city's low-rise neighborhoods.

name: Estadio Modelo Alberto Spencer Herrera
blurb: Guayaquil's municipal stadium, named for Ecuador's greatest goal scorer, the record holder in the Copa Libertadores. Look for the oval near the airport in the flat river port city.

name: Hanazono Rugby Stadium
blurb: Japan's first stadium built just for rugby, opened in 1929 in Higashiosaka. Look for the rectangular ground in a city of small factories at the foot of the Ikoma hills.

name: Nagoya Dome
blurb: Home of the Chunichi Dragons since 1997. Look for the large silver dome, ribbed like a shell, in northeast Nagoya.

name: Harsprånget hydroelectric power station
blurb: Sweden's largest hydro power station, on the Lule River above the Arctic Circle. Look for the river and reservoirs threading through dark forest, often frozen white in winter.

name: Bekhme Dam
blurb: A giant dam on the Great Zab River in Iraqi Kurdistan, started in the 1980s and never finished. Look for a deep limestone gorge where construction scars mark the abandoned site.

name: Birecik Dam
blurb: A Euphrates dam near the Syrian border whose reservoir flooded part of ancient Zeugma, famous for its Roman mosaics. Look for the river widening into a lake in pale limestone country.

name: Tungabhadra Dam
blurb: A big masonry dam on the Tungabhadra River at Hosapete, close to the ruins of the medieval city of Hampi. Look for a long dam with a huge reservoir behind it and green irrigated fields spreading below.

name: Santo Antônio Dam
blurb: A run-of-river hydro dam on the Madeira, one of the Amazon's biggest tributaries, right at the edge of Porto Velho. Look for the long concrete line across a wide brown river.

name: Saratov Hydroelectric Station
blurb: One of the chain of dams that turned the Volga into a staircase of reservoirs, this one at Balakovo. Look for the long dam and locks across a very wide river.

name: King Talal Dam
blurb: Jordan's largest dam, on the Zarqa River, storing water for the Jordan Valley farms below. Look for an earthen dam and a narrow reservoir in dry, brown hills north of Amman.

name: Kremenchuk Hydroelectric Power Plant
blurb: Holds back the Kremenchuk Reservoir, the largest lake on the Dnieper by area. Look for an enormous, shallow body of water in flat Ukrainian farmland.

name: Kidatu Dam
blurb: A hydro dam on the Great Ruaha River in central Tanzania, one of the country's main power sources. Look for the river and reservoir between forested hills.

name: Almatti Dam
blurb: A large dam on the Krishna River in northern Karnataka, part of a big irrigation project for the dry Deccan plateau. Look for a long concrete wall with a sprawling reservoir and canals.

name: Nalubaale Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: Formerly Owen Falls Dam, built in 1954 at Jinja where the White Nile pours out of Lake Victoria. Look for the dam at the lake's outlet, the start of a river that runs over 4,000 miles to the Mediterranean.

name: Ilha Solteira Dam
blurb: One of Brazil's largest hydro plants, built across the Paraná River in the 1970s. Look for the long dam across a very wide river, with a huge reservoir behind it.

name: Bloemhof Dam
blurb: A wide reservoir on the Vaal River where it meets the Vet, on the border of the Free State and North West. Look for a broad lake spreading over flat farmland.

name: Salma Dam
blurb: Also called the Afghan-India Friendship Dam, built with Indian funding and opened in 2016 on the Hari River east of Herat. Look for a reservoir of blue-green water winding through bare, brown mountains.

name: Gardiner Dam
blurb: One of the largest embankment dams in Canada, built across the South Saskatchewan River in the 1960s to create Lake Diefenbaker. Look for a long, skinny lake running through flat prairie.

name: Mohamed V Dam
blurb: Morocco's big dam on the Moulouya River in the dry northeast, holding back water for irrigation of the plains toward the Mediterranean. Look for a long reservoir winding through bare brown hills.

name: Jatiluhur Dam
blurb: Holds Indonesia's largest reservoir, built from 1957 to 1967 on the Citarum River, supplying water to Jakarta and the rice fields of West Java. Look for a reservoir dotted with floating fish farms among green hills.

name: Estadio Pedro Marrero
blurb: Havana's main soccer stadium, built in 1929, in the Playa district on the west side of the city. Look for the small oval near the Almendares River and the coast.

name: Shandong Provincial Stadium
blurb: Jinan's older provincial stadium in the city center, the longtime home of Shandong football before the Olympic Sports Center opened. Look for a big open oval among the dense blocks below the hills.

name: Estadio Ramón Tahuichi Aguilera
blurb: Bolivia's second-largest stadium, in lowland Santa Cruz, named for a local football hero. Look for the bowl in the ring-road city on the flat plains.

name: Barthélemy Boganda Stadium
blurb: The national stadium of the Central African Republic, named after the country's founding father. Look for the open oval in Bangui, the capital on the Ubangi River.

name: Markaziy Stadium
blurb: The central stadium in Namangan, in the Fergana Valley. Look for a modest oval among tree-lined streets and irrigated fields.

name: Homs Municipal Stadium
blurb: The football stadium of Homs, central Syria's main city on the Orontes plain. Look for an open oval among the low, dense city blocks.

name: Takhti Stadium (Tehran)
blurb: Named for Gholamreza Takhti, Iran's beloved Olympic wrestling champion, an older stadium in east Tehran. Look for the open bowl in dense city blocks.

name: Estádio do Zimpeto
blurb: Maputo's national stadium, built with Chinese funding for the 2011 All-Africa Games, on the city's northern outskirts. Look for a pale oval bowl in open ground away from the dense center.

name: Estadio Jesús Bermúdez
blurb: Oruro's stadium sits at about 12,200 ft on the Altiplano. Look for the oval in the treeless brown city on the high plateau.

name: Estadio Garcilaso
blurb: Cusco's stadium sits around 11,000 ft up in the Andes, where visiting teams famously struggle for breath. Look for it in the valley on the city's southeast side.

name: Althawra Sports City Stadium
blurb: Yemen's main stadium in Sana'a, part of a sports complex on the north side of the city. Look for an oval among the city's mud-brown sprawl, ringed by mountains.

name: Estádio Estadual Jornalista Edgar Augusto Proença
blurb: Belém's big stadium, known as Mangueirão, rebuilt in 2023. Look for the oval amid the green, humid sprawl near the mouth of the Amazon.

name: Karbala Sports City
blurb: A modern sports complex outside Karbala, the shrine city of Imam Hussein. Look for the stadium bowl standing alone on the desert edge.

name: Stade Modibo Kéïta
blurb: Bamako's older stadium, named for Mali's first president. Look for the open bowl in the city's dense northern districts.

name: Stade de Kégué
blurb: Lomé's main stadium, used by Togo's national team, on the north side of the capital. Look for an open bowl in the flat, sandy outskirts near the lagoon.

name: Estádio Alfredo Jaconi
blurb: Home of Juventude, the club of Caxias do Sul, a hilly city in the Serra Gaúcha wine country settled by Italian immigrants. Look for a compact open bowl tucked into a dense hillside neighborhood.

name: Estadio George Capwell
blurb: Home of Emelec, one of Guayaquil's two big clubs, in the Centenario neighborhood. Look for the stadium wedged tight into the city blocks south of downtown.

name: Osman Ahmed Osman Stadium
blurb: Home of Arab Contractors club in Nasr City, named after the founder of Egypt's biggest construction company. Look for the small oval among the dense blocks of eastern Cairo.

name: Stade de la Réunification
blurb: Douala's main stadium, built for the 1972 Africa Cup of Nations hosted by Cameroon. Look for the open concrete bowl in Cameroon's largest city, near the Wouri estuary.

name: Estadio 15 de Abril
blurb: Home of Unión de Santa Fe, whose fierce rival Colón plays across the same city. Look for the bowl in Santa Fe's grid, with the Paraná river wetlands spreading out to the east.

name: Estadio Jorge "El Mágico" González
blurb: San Salvador's national stadium, renamed for El Salvador's most beloved footballer. Look for the oval in the city's Flor Blanca district, near the volcano rising to the west.

name: Seibu Dome
blurb: Home of the Seibu Lions, an open-air ballpark that later got a roof with open sides, so it is hot in summer and cold in spring. Look for it in wooded hills by Lake Sayama.

name: Jebba Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: A hydro dam on the Niger downstream of Kainji, the second step in harnessing Nigeria's biggest river. Look for the dam wall and power station where the river widens into a lake.

name: Koman Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: Its reservoir, Lake Koman, fills a winding, cliff-lined gorge on the Drin River and is crossed by a ferry often compared to a Norwegian fjord trip. Look for a narrow green ribbon of water snaking through steep mountains.

name: Xiangjiaba Dam
blurb: The last of the giant dams on the Jinsha River before it becomes the Yangtze proper, one of China's largest hydro plants. Look for the massive gravity wall across the river near Yibin.

name: El Cajón Dam
blurb: A concrete arch dam over 700 ft tall in the mountains of Honduras, one of the tallest in Latin America. Look for a curved wall in a steep green canyon with a long, branching reservoir behind it.

name: Balbina Dam
blurb: Often cited as one of the worst dams ever built: its reservoir flooded around 900 square miles of rainforest to produce a modest amount of power. Look for a vast maze of drowned forest and thousands of islands.

name: Jirau Dam
blurb: A run-of-river dam on the Madeira upstream of Porto Velho, one of Brazil's largest hydro plants. Look for the concrete barrier across a broad, muddy river in the rainforest.

name: Seyhan Dam
blurb: Built in 1956 on the Seyhan River right at the northern edge of Adana. Look for a big reservoir pressed against the city, with the irrigated Çukurova plain spreading south.

name: Chixoy Hydroelectric Dam
blurb: Guatemala's largest hydroelectric dam, built in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Hundreds of Maya villagers who refused to leave the flood zone were massacred at Río Negro in 1982. Look for a reservoir in steep, green mountains.

name: Nam Ngum Dam
blurb: Laos's first big hydro dam, finished in 1971 north of Vientiane, selling power to Thailand. Look for a large reservoir full of forested islands in green hills.

name: Itezhi-Tezhi Dam
blurb: Dams the Kafue River in Zambia to store water for the power plants downstream at Kafue Gorge. Look for a reservoir at the edge of Kafue National Park's flat bush.

name: Stornorrfors Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: One of Sweden's largest hydro plants, on the Ume River just upstream of Umeå. Look for the dam and the old rocky riverbed beside it, left mostly dry except for a fish ladder.

name: Bureya Dam
blurb: A large hydroelectric dam in Russia's Far East. In 2018 a huge landslide blocked the river upstream, and the army used explosives to cut a channel through it. Look for a concrete gravity dam across a forested river valley.

name: Sobradinho Dam
blurb: Its reservoir on the São Francisco River is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world by area. Look for an enormous sheet of water spreading across the dry scrubland of Brazil's northeast.

name: Gilgel Gibe I Power Station
blurb: An earlier Ethiopian hydro plant on the Gilgel Gibe River, feeding water to downstream plants on the same cascade. Look for a reservoir among green hills and farmland in southwestern Ethiopia.

name: Zhiguli Hydroelectric Station
blurb: Dams the Volga at Tolyatti, creating the Kuybyshev Reservoir, the largest reservoir in Europe by area. Look for the dam where the river squeezes past the forested Zhiguli Hills.

name: Gove Dam
blurb: A dam on the upper Cunene River in Angola's central highlands, regulating water for the river's lower power plants. Look for a broad reservoir among the savanna and farmland of the high plateau.

name: Mujib Dam
blurb: A dam in Wadi Mujib, the dramatic canyon that drains into the Dead Sea. Look for a small reservoir in barren, deeply cut desert hills just east of the Dead Sea's shore.

name: Caruachi Dam
blurb: A hydro dam on the Caroní River downstream of the giant Guri, part of the chain that powers Venezuela. Look for the dam across a dark, tea-colored river.

name: Fierza Hydroelectric Power Station
blurb: One of the largest hydroelectric plants in Albania, on the Drin River, holding back a long reservoir reaching toward Kosovo. Look for a tall embankment dam at the head of a winding mountain lake.

name: Sterkfontein Dam
blurb: A huge off-river reservoir high in the Drakensberg foothills, filled by water pumped over the escarpment from KwaZulu-Natal to feed the Vaal system. Look for a big lake in open highland grass.

name: Parker Dam
blurb: Often called the deepest dam in the world: most of its 320-ft height lies below the original riverbed, dug down to bedrock. Look for a small concrete wall on the Colorado River at the foot of Lake Havasu.

name: Imboulou Dam
blurb: A Chinese-built hydro dam on the Léfini River north of Brazzaville, one of the Republic of the Congo's main power sources. Look for the dam where the river cuts through grassy plateau country.

name: Al-Wehda Dam
blurb: A joint Syrian-Jordanian dam on the Yarmouk River, which forms their border here. Look for a small reservoir in a deep basalt gorge.

name: Estadio Olímpico Patria
blurb: Sucre's main stadium, in Bolivia's constitutional capital, at about 9,200 ft. Look for the oval in the white-walled colonial city's sprawl.

name: Estadio Jorge Luis Hirschi
blurb: Estudiantes de La Plata's home, rebuilt and reopened in 2019. Look for the compact stadium on the edge of La Plata's big wooded park.

name: Jamsil Baseball Stadium
blurb: Shared by two KBO teams, the LG Twins and Doosan Bears, in the 1988 Seoul Olympic sports complex. Look for the ballpark beside the Olympic Stadium near the Han River.

name: Tuanku Abdul Rahman Stadium
blurb: Negeri Sembilan's stadium at Paroi in Seremban, named for Malaysia's first king. Look for the bowl among green hills and plantations south of Kuala Lumpur.

name: Imam Reza Stadium
blurb: Mashhad's modern stadium, named for the Shia imam whose shrine draws millions of pilgrims to the city each year. Look for the oval roof on the city's western edge.

name: May 22 Stadium
blurb: Aden's main stadium, in the port city on Yemen's south coast. Look for a modest oval among dry volcanic hills and the harbor.

name: Century Lotus Stadium
blurb: Foshan's stadium, its roof designed to suggest a lotus flower, with petal-like fabric panels around the bowl. Look for the white petal-ringed roof among Foshan's dense districts.

name: Yuvileiny Stadium
blurb: The main stadium in Sumy, in northeastern Ukraine, a modest ground used by local clubs. Look for a small rectangular bowl near the city's edge.

name: Albertão
blurb: Teresina's big stadium, in one of Brazil's hottest cities. Look for the concrete bowl in the city that sits between the Parnaíba and Poti rivers.

name: Bingu National Stadium
blurb: Malawi's 40,000-seat national stadium in Lilongwe, built by China and opened in 2017. Look for the big oval with a pale curved roof on the city's edge.

name: Sheikh Mohamed Laghdaf Stadium
blurb: Laayoune's stadium, in the Western Sahara city on the edge of the desert near the Atlantic. Look for a green rectangle of pitch standing out sharply against the sand-colored town.

name: Qatar University Stadium
blurb: A stadium on Qatar University's campus in north Doha. Look for it among the campus's spread-out buildings between the city and the new towers of Lusail.

name: Likas Stadium
blurb: Sabah's main stadium in Kota Kinabalu, near the shore of Likas Bay. Look for the open bowl by the water, with Mount Kinabalu sometimes visible far inland.

name: Nyayo National Stadium
blurb: Built in 1983, a compact national stadium close to central Nairobi. Look for the bowl at the busy junction where the airport road meets the city, near Nairobi National Park.

name: Samsun 19 Mayıs Stadium
blurb: Samsun's stadium on the Black Sea coast, named for May 19, 1919, the day Atatürk landed here to start Turkey's war of independence. Look for the bowl on the city's eastern side.

name: Barradão
blurb: Esporte Clube Vitória's home in Salvador, set in a hollow among hilly working-class neighborhoods. Look for the concrete bowl surrounded by tightly packed hillside houses.

name: Tsentralnyi Profsoyuz Stadion
blurb: Voronezh's central stadium and home of Fakel. Look for an older oval near the river in the city center.

name: Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex
blurb: Liberia's national stadium outside Monrovia, built with Chinese help in the 1980s. Look for the big bowl in low ground near the Atlantic coast.

name: Stadionul Steaua
blurb: The army club's ground in Bucharest's Ghencea district, completely rebuilt and reopened in 2021. Look for a compact rectangular stadium with a full roof ring among the low blocks of the city's southwest.

name: Arequipa Stadium
blurb: Arequipa's main stadium, about 7,500 ft up, a 2004 Copa América venue. Look for the bowl on the city's edge with the near-perfect cone of El Misti volcano behind.

name: Gelora Bandung Lautan Api Stadium
blurb: A 38,000-seat stadium in eastern Bandung, named for the 1946 'Bandung Sea of Fire', when residents burned their own city. Look for the bowl in the flat paddies of Gedebage.

name: Foolad Khuzestan Stadium
blurb: Home of Foolad, the steel company's club, in Ahvaz on the Khuzestan plain. Look for the compact stadium near industrial ground on the city outskirts.

name: New Minaa Stadium
blurb: A new stadium in Basra for Al-Minaa, the 'Port' club named for the city's docks. Look for the bowl near the Shatt al-Arab in a flat, palm-dotted city.

name: Mosaic Stadium
blurb: The Saskatchewan Roughriders moved here in 2017 from their old ground next door; Rider fans make it a sea of green. Look for the bowl with a curved roof canopy on Regina's flat western edge.

name: Estadio Monumental José Fierro
blurb: Atlético Tucumán's home in San Miguel de Tucumán, with the forested Aconquija foothills rising just west of the city. Look for the bowl in the dense city grid.

name: Stade Frederic Kibassa Maliba
blurb: Lubumbashi's stadium, in the heart of the DR Congo's copper belt. Look for the oval amid the mining city's grid.

name: Barbourfields Stadium
blurb: Home of Highlanders FC in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe's second city. Look for a stadium among the wide streets and suburbs west of the center.

name: Estadio Víctor Agustín Ugarte
blurb: At about 13,000 ft in Potosí, one of the highest stadiums in the world, below the silver mountain Cerro Rico. Look for the oval in the city with the cone-shaped, mine-riddled peak above it.

name: Maguwoharjo Stadium
blurb: Home of PSS Sleman, a compact stadium on Yogyakarta's northeast side, not far from the old airport. Look for the bowl among rice fields and villages under Mount Merapi.

name: Amigão
blurb: Campina Grande's main stadium, in the interior of Paraíba. Look for the open oval in the dry hill country's biggest city.

name: Estádio da Cidadela
blurb: Luanda's Cidadela Desportiva was Angola's main stadium for decades before the national stadium opened in 2010. Look for the older concrete oval in the dense city.

name: Castelão
blurb: São Luís's big stadium, one of the largest in Brazil's northeast. Look for the open bowl on the island city amid low suburbs and mangrove-lined rivers.

name: Stade Alphonse Massemba-Débat
blurb: Brazzaville's main stadium, a large open bowl that has hosted the national team and big public events. Look for the oval in the city, with Kinshasa's skyline visible across the Congo River.

name: National Football Stadium
blurb: Belarus's new national football stadium in Minsk, a modern rectangular ground. Look for it among the apartment blocks on the city's southeast side.

name: Sutro Tower
blurb: A 977-ft broadcast tower, three red-and-white legs on top of a hill in San Francisco. Look for the trident shape above the fog.

name: Puna Pau
blurb: The small volcanic crater where Easter Islanders quarried red scoria for the topknots placed on the moai. Look for the low reddish crater inland from Hanga Roa.

name: Mons Porphyrites
blurb: The only source of imperial purple porphyry, the stone Roman emperors reserved for their own statues and tombs. Look for quarry roads and ruins high in the bare Red Sea mountains.

name: Serejão
blurb: Taguatinga's stadium in the satellite cities west of Brasília's Plano Piloto. Look for the open oval among the dense grid of neighborhoods.

name: Peoples Football Stadium
blurb: A football ground in Karachi's Lyari district, a neighborhood famous for its love of the game. Look for the pitch hemmed in by dense city blocks.

name: Colonel Lotfi Stadium
blurb: The main stadium of Tlemcen in far western Algeria, home of WA Tlemcen. Look for the oval within the city below the hills.

name: Shaanxi Province Stadium
blurb: Xi'an's main provincial stadium, a large open bowl south of the walled old city that hosts Shaanxi football. Look for the oval roof ring in the dense grid just outside the ancient wall.

name: Sultan Mohammad IV Stadium
blurb: Home of Kelantan soccer in Kota Bharu, known for packed, noisy crowds. Look for the stadium in the low town near the mouth of the Kelantan River.

name: Shenzhen Stadium
blurb: One of Shenzhen's older sports venues, an open bowl in the Futian district hemmed in by the city's dense towers. Look for the oval of stands and running track among high-rises.

name: Gajayana Stadium
blurb: One of Indonesia's oldest stadiums, dating to the Dutch colonial era, in the middle of Malang. Look for the open oval near the city center in the cool highland basin.

name: Estadio Manuel Murillo Toro
blurb: Ibagué's stadium, home of Deportes Tolima, in the city known as Colombia's musical capital. Look for the oval bowl at the foot of the Central Cordillera.

name: Olympia Park
blurb: A sports park in Rustenburg with an older open stadium, near the newer Royal Bafokeng arena. Look for an oval with a track in the town below the Magaliesberg ridge.

name: General Santander
blurb: Cúcuta's stadium, home of Cúcuta Deportivo, a few miles from the Venezuelan border. Look for the oval bowl in the hot, low city on the Pamplonita River.

name: Julio Cesar Villagra Stadium
blurb: Belgrano's home in Córdoba, known as the Gigante de Alberdi after its neighborhood. Look for the bowl tightly packed into the blocks west of downtown.

name: Sajik Baseball Stadium
blurb: Home of the Lotte Giants in Busan, known for some of the most fervent fans in Korean baseball. Look for the ballpark beside the city's athletics stadium.

name: Tinsulanonda Stadium
blurb: Songkhla's provincial stadium in southern Thailand, near the coast and the Songkhla lagoon. Look for an open oval with a running track in the low city.

name: Penang State Stadium
blurb: Penang's stadium on the mainland at Batu Kawan, near the second Penang Bridge. Look for the bowl in flat newly developed land by the strait.

name: Al-Madina Stadium
blurb: A newer stadium in eastern Baghdad, in the dense districts off the Army Canal. Look for the oval roof amid flat-roofed housing.

name: Juan Domingo Perón Stadium
blurb: Instituto's home in the Alta Córdoba neighborhood of Córdoba. Look for the compact stadium in the low-rise blocks north of the city center.

name: Almeidão
blurb: João Pessoa's main stadium, near the easternmost point of the Americas. Look for an open concrete bowl in the city's southern neighborhoods, inland from the Atlantic beaches.

name: Aramco Stadium
blurb: A new stadium on the Gulf coast near Dammam and Al Khobar, built by the oil giant Aramco for the 2027 Asian Cup and the 2034 World Cup. It may still be under construction.

name: Dinorwic Quarry
blurb: A slate quarry whose terraces climb the mountainside above Llanberis; a pumped-storage power station is hidden inside the mountain. Look for the gray staircase of galleries above the lakes.

name: Höwenegg
blurb: An extinct volcano in the Hegau, quarried for basalt and known for fossils of early three-toed horses. Look for the flooded quarry lake on a wooded hill north of Lake Constance.

name: Puy de Lemptégy
blurb: A small volcano in the Chaîne des Puys quarried for cinders until its insides were exposed; it's now a visitor site. Look for the scooped-out cone among the round wooded volcanoes west of Clermont-Ferrand.

name: Bayan Obo mine
blurb: The world's largest rare earth deposit, source of a big share of the elements in magnets and electronics. Look for the open pits and huge pale tailings ponds in the Inner Mongolian steppe.

name: Limhamns kalkbrott
blurb: A big limestone pit on Malmö's south edge, quarried for cement until the 1990s and now a nature reserve. Look for the deep pale hole among the city's suburbs near the Öresund.

name: LianHua Hill
blurb: A sandstone hill quarried for some 2,000 years, leaving dramatic cliffs and caves, now a park with a gold Guanyin statue about 130 ft tall. Look for the red cliffs and statue above the Pearl River in Panyu.

name: Pitinga Mine
blurb: A tin mine carved out of the Amazon rainforest north of Manaus, also producing niobium and tantalum. Look for bare tailings ponds and roads cut into unbroken green jungle.

name: Rummu Quarry
blurb: A flooded limestone quarry once worked by prisoners, with parts of the Soviet-era prison now underwater and popular with divers. Look for clear turquoise water beside a huge gray hill of quarry waste.

name: Velká Amerika
blurb: A flooded limestone quarry nicknamed the Czech Grand Canyon, with sheer pale walls dropping into blue-green water. Look for it in the wooded hills near Karlštejn Castle, southwest of Prague.

name: Mamut Mine
blurb: A copper mine near the foot of Mount Kinabalu in Sabah, closed around 1999. Look for the abandoned open pit, now partly flooded, scarring the green hills.

name: Amiantifera di Balangero
blurb: Once the largest asbestos mine in Western Europe, closed in 1990. Look for the bare gray-green pit and waste slopes in the hills north of Turin.

name: Callow Rock Quarry
blurb: A limestone quarry in the Mendip Hills near Cheddar. Look for a pale terraced cut in the green hills.

name: Rubislaw Quarry
blurb: The granite pit that built Aberdeen, the Granite City, about 466 ft deep and filled with water since it closed in 1971. Look for a small dark pool among the West End streets.

name: Römersteinbruch Sankt Margarethen
blurb: A quarry worked since Roman times whose limestone helped build Vienna's St. Stephen's Cathedral; it now hosts an opera festival. Look for the pale cut cliffs in vineyards near Lake Neusiedl.

name: Wodgina mine
blurb: A lithium and tantalum mine in the Pilbara. Look for pale pits and waste dumps among red spinifex hills.

name: s'Hostal quarries
blurb: Sandstone quarries on Menorca where blocks were cut for the island's buildings, now a garden of sheer-walled pits. Look for rectangular cuts in the countryside near Ciutadella.

name: San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge
blurb: Two bridges joined by a tunnel through Yerba Buena Island: twin 1936 suspension spans to the west, and to the east the 2013 replacement built after a deck section collapsed in the 1989 quake. Look for the single white tower of the new span.

name: San Mateo-Hayward Bridge
blurb: About 7 miles long, the longest bridge in California, most of it a low trestle just above the bay. Look for the high-rise hump where it lifts over the shipping channel.

name: Dumbarton Bridge
blurb: The southernmost bridge across San Francisco Bay, crossing salt marsh between Fremont and Menlo Park. Look for the low concrete line beside the old, broken rail bridge.

name: Richmond-San Rafael Bridge
blurb: A 1956 double-deck cantilever about 5.5 miles long, with two high humps and a dip between. Look for the roller-coaster profile next to the San Quentin prison point.

name: Oakland Coliseum
blurb: Home of the Raiders until 2019 and the A's until 2024, it was the last stadium shared by NFL and MLB teams. Look for the sunken concrete bowl beside the BART line and I-880, near the bay.

name: Chase Center
blurb: The Warriors' arena, opened in 2019 in Mission Bay after the team left Oakland. Look for the rounded white arena beside the bay, a short way south of Oracle Park.

name: Apple Park
blurb: Apple's ring building is a mile around, 2.8 million square feet of curved glass on 175 acres, opened in 2017. Look for the giant circle with a wooded center in Cupertino.

name: Googleplex
blurb: Google's headquarters, by the bay in Mountain View. Look for the low campus beside the white peaked tent of Shoreline Amphitheatre and the salt marsh edge.

name: Moffett Field and Hangar One
blurb: Hangar One was built in 1933 to house the Navy airship USS Macon and covers about 8 acres, one of the largest freestanding structures in the world. Look for its huge curved shell, plus two even bigger wartime blimp hangars nearby.

name: Port of Oakland
blurb: One of the busiest container ports on the West Coast, across the bay from San Francisco. Look for a long row of giant cranes along the Outer Harbor, just south of the Bay Bridge touchdown.

name: San Jose International Airport
blurb: Barely two miles from downtown San Jose, so close that flights pass low over the city and building heights downtown are capped for them. Look for the parallel runways right beside the Guadalupe River.

name: Alcatraz Island
blurb: A federal prison from 1934 to 1963; no one is confirmed to have escaped successfully. Look for the small rocky island in the bay with the long white cellhouse and lighthouse on top.

name: Stanford University
blurb: About 8,000 acres of land, one of the largest campuses in the US. Look for the sandstone buildings and red tile roofs around the Main Quad, 285-ft Hoover Tower, and the long straight Palm Drive.

name: Big Bear Lake
blurb: A reservoir at about 6,750 ft in the San Bernardino Mountains, first dammed in 1884. Look for a long, narrow lake in pine forest, with the ski runs of Bear Mountain and Snow Summit on the slopes to the south.

name: Lake Arrowhead
blurb: A private mountain lake at about 5,100 ft where only local residents may boat. Look for a small, branching blue lake ringed by pines and big houses, just above the San Bernardino basin.

name: San Gorgonio Pass Wind Farm
blurb: Thousands of turbines crowd this pass between two 10,000-ft peaks, where cool coastal air rushes toward the hot desert. Look for a field of white towers along Interstate 10 just west of Palm Springs.

name: Altamont Pass Wind Farm
blurb: One of the first big wind farms in the US, built in the early 1980s on the hills between the Bay Area and the Central Valley. Look for turbines on the grassy ridges along Interstate 580 east of Livermore.

name: Alta Wind Energy Center
blurb: One of the largest wind farms in the US, about 1,500 megawatts, spread across the Tehachapi Pass. Look for rows of turbines climbing the brown hills between the Mojave Desert and the Tehachapi Mountains.

name: Oakland
blurb: Home to one of the busiest container ports on the West Coast. Look for the port's giant cranes (rumored, wrongly per George Lucas, to have inspired the Star Wars walkers), the round Lake Merritt by downtown, and the Bay Bridge.

name: Hollywood Sign
blurb: Built in 1923 as 'HOLLYWOODLAND', an ad for a housing development; the 'LAND' came down in 1949. Each letter is about 45 ft tall; look for the white row on the south face of Mount Lee.

name: Griffith Observatory
blurb: Opened in 1935, it claims more people have looked through its public telescope than any other on Earth. Look for the white building with three copper-green domes on the hillside east of the Hollywood Sign.

name: Getty Center
blurb: Richard Meier's hilltop museum, opened in 1997 and clad in about 16,000 tons of Italian travertine. Look for the cluster of white and beige buildings on a ridge above the 405 at the Sepulveda Pass.

name: Crystal Springs Reservoir
blurb: Two long, narrow reservoirs sitting directly on the San Andreas Fault, storing Hetch Hetchy water for San Francisco. Look for the straight line of lakes beside Interstate 280, tracing the fault.

name: South San Francisco Sign
blurb: Giant white letters spelling 'SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO THE INDUSTRIAL CITY' on Sign Hill, there since 1923. Look for them on the hillside north of SFO, easy to read on approaches from the north.

name: SLAC Linear Accelerator
blurb: A 2-mile linear accelerator, often called the straightest object in the world, running dead straight under Interstate 280.

name: Oracle Headquarters
blurb: Oracle's headquarters at Redwood Shores, a cluster of round glass towers grouped around a man-made lake. Look for the blue-green cylinders beside the Bay just off US 101.

name: Meta Headquarters
blurb: Meta's campus at the Menlo Park end of the Dumbarton Bridge, including a Frank Gehry building topped by a 9-acre rooftop park. Look for the long green roof beside the salt ponds.

name: California's Great America
blurb: A theme park in Santa Clara, right next to Levi's Stadium. Look for coaster loops and a lake beside the stadium and the bayside office parks.

name: South Bay Salt Ponds
blurb: Ponds at the south end of San Francisco Bay, colored red, orange and green by salt-loving microbes as brine evaporates. Look for the patchwork of bright pastel rectangles on the bay's edge.

name: Stanford Dish
blurb: A 150-ft radio dish completed in the 1960s, used early on to study Soviet radar, on the grassy hills behind Stanford. Look for the white dish in golden grassland just east of Interstate 280.

name: Transamerica Pyramid
blurb: 853 ft tall, San Francisco's pointed-top skyscraper since 1972. Look for the white spike at the edge of downtown.

name: Oakland California Temple
blurb: An LDS temple dedicated in 1964, with five white spires high in the Oakland hills, floodlit at night. Look for the white building and spires above the 580 freeway, visible from much of the East Bay.

name: USS Hornet
blurb: This aircraft carrier fought through World War II, then picked up the Apollo 11 and 12 crews after splashdown in 1969. Look for the long gray flight deck moored at the old Alameda Naval Air Station.

name: Tesla Fremont Factory
blurb: The former GM and Toyota NUMMI plant, more than 5 million square feet under one roof and one of the largest car factories in North America. Look for the enormous white roof between Interstate 880 and the rail yards.

name: Claremont Hotel
blurb: A sprawling white resort hotel opened in 1915, at the foot of the Berkeley hills on the Oakland line. Look for the long white building with a tower against the dark green hillside.

name: University of California, Berkeley
blurb: Founded in 1868, the oldest campus of the UC system. Look for 307-ft Sather Tower, the Campanile, and Memorial Stadium in the hills above, built straight across the Hayward Fault.

name: Lick Observatory
blurb: The world's first permanently occupied mountaintop observatory, opened in 1888. Founder James Lick is buried beneath its main telescope. Look for white domes on the summit of Mount Hamilton east of San Jose.

name: NVIDIA Headquarters
blurb: NVIDIA's two newest buildings, Endeavor and Voyager, are giant triangles, a nod to the triangles of computer graphics. Look for the angular roofs in Santa Clara.

name: Shoreline Amphitheatre
blurb: An outdoor concert venue under a white peaked tent roof, opened in 1986 on a former landfill next to Google's campus. Look for the white peaks beside the bay marshes near Moffett Field.

name: SAP Center
blurb: Home of the San Jose Sharks since 1993, nicknamed the Shark Tank. Look for the steel-and-glass arena at the west edge of downtown, close to the San Jose Diridon train station and a few miles from SJC.

name: Port of Los Angeles
blurb: The busiest container port in the US, sharing San Pedro Bay with Long Beach. Look for Terminal Island covered in containers and the green Vincent Thomas suspension bridge.

name: Queen Mary
blurb: The 1936 ocean liner, retired to Long Beach in 1967 and now a hotel. Look for the black hull and three red funnels across the harbor from downtown.

name: Long Beach International Gateway
blurb: Replaced the Gerald Desmond Bridge in 2020 so the biggest container ships could pass beneath. Look for two tall white towers fanning cables over the port's back channel.

name: Marina del Rey
blurb: One of the largest man-made small-boat harbors in North America, dredged from wetlands in the 1960s. Look for finger-shaped basins packed with white boats just north of the LAX runways.

name: Kia Forum
blurb: The Lakers' home from 1967 to 1999, where Showtime played, now a concert venue. Look for the round drum ringed by white columns, a few blocks north of SoFi and the Intuit Dome.

name: Rose Bowl
blurb: Opened in 1922 and host of the 1994 World Cup final and five Super Bowls. Look for the oval bowl in the Arroyo Seco below the San Gabriel Mountains in Pasadena, ringed by a golf course.

name: Mount Wilson Observatory
blurb: Edwin Hubble used its 100-inch telescope in the 1920s to show that other galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way and that the universe is expanding. Look for white domes and TV towers on the San Gabriel crest above Pasadena.

name: Hollywood Bowl
blurb: A natural amphitheater that has hosted concerts since 1922 and seats about 17,500. Look for the white concentric band shell in a canyon just off the 101, southwest of the Hollywood Sign.

name: Christ Cathedral
blurb: Built in 1980 as the Crystal Cathedral, Philip Johnson's church of more than 10,000 glass panes, later sold to the Catholic Church. Look for the shimmering, star-shaped glass building near the 5 and 22 freeways.

name: University of Southern California
blurb: Founded in 1880, its red brick campus sits in South LA next to Exposition Park. Look for the LA Memorial Coliseum, the Trojans' home stadium, just south of campus.

name: University of California, Los Angeles
blurb: Red brick Romanesque buildings in Westwood between Bel Air and the Wilshire towers. Look for Royce Hall's twin towers and the athletic fields of the north campus.

name: Pepperdine University
blurb: A Malibu campus of white buildings with red tile roofs on a bare hillside, all facing the Pacific. Look for the big green lawn running down toward Pacific Coast Highway.

name: Angel Stadium
blurb: Home of the Angels since 1966. Look for the giant red A with a halo standing in the parking lot, beside the Orange Freeway and across from the Honda Center.

name: Intuit Dome
blurb: The Clippers' own arena, opened in 2024 right next to SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. Its fan section, the Wall, is a single steep bank of seats behind one basket. Look for the curved roof beside SoFi's huge canopy.

name: BMO Stadium
blurb: LAFC's stadium, opened in 2018 in Exposition Park, on the site of the old Sports Arena. Look for its steep canopy-covered stands right beside the much larger LA Memorial Coliseum.

name: Leonard P. Zakim Bunker Hill Memorial Bridge
blurb: Its inverted-Y towers were designed to echo the nearby Bunker Hill Monument. Built as part of the Big Dig, it carries I-93 over the Charles. Look for the white fan of cables north of downtown.

name: TD Garden
blurb: Home of the Celtics and Bruins, sitting on top of North Station's train platforms. Look for the arena at the north edge of downtown, near the Zakim Bridge's white cables.

name: Deer Island Egg Digesters
blurb: Twelve giant egg-shaped digesters process Greater Boston's sewage on Deer Island at the harbor mouth. Look for the cluster of silver eggs just off the ends of Logan's runways.

name: Fort Independence
blurb: A granite five-sided fort on Castle Island in South Boston, where Edgar Allan Poe served as a young soldier. Look for the star-shaped fort at the end of a causeway loop across the harbor from Logan.

name: Tobin Bridge
blurb: A green cantilever truss about 2 miles long, the longest bridge in New England, carrying Route 1 over the Mystic River. Look for it arching from Charlestown to Chelsea.

name: Yankee Stadium
blurb: The Yankees' home since 2009, built across the street from the 1923 original, whose site is now a park. Look for the limestone-colored bowl beside the Major Deegan Expressway in the Bronx, just across the Harlem River from Manhattan.

name: Citi Field
blurb: The Mets' home since 2009, built in the old Shea Stadium parking lot. Look for it next to the giant Unisphere and the US Open courts in Flushing Meadows, often under LaGuardia approaches.

name: Madison Square Garden
blurb: The fourth Madison Square Garden, opened in 1968 directly on top of Penn Station. Look for the round drum with a white cable-supported roof, an unusual circle amid Midtown's rectangles.

name: Arthur Ashe Stadium
blurb: The world's largest tennis stadium, about 23,000 seats, home of the US Open final since 1997. A retractable roof was added in 2016. Look for it beside Citi Field and the Unisphere in Queens.

name: Sports Illustrated Stadium
blurb: Home of the New York Red Bulls, formerly Red Bull Arena, on the Passaic River in Harrison across from Newark. Look for the curved translucent roof wrapping all four sides of a compact soccer box.

name: UBS Arena
blurb: The New York Islanders' arena, opened in 2021 at Belmont Park racetrack on the Queens border. Look for it at the edge of the huge oval horse-racing track.

name: Belmont Park
blurb: Home of the Belmont Stakes, the final leg of the Triple Crown, with a 1.5-mile main dirt oval, the largest in American thoroughbred racing. Look for the huge brown oval right beside UBS Arena on the Queens line.

name: Central Park
blurb: 843 acres, 2.5 miles long and half a mile wide. Look for the perfect green rectangle cut into Manhattan's grid, with the big reservoir in its upper half.

name: Manhattan Bridge
blurb: Blue-painted, carrying subway trains as well as cars. Look for it just upriver of the Brooklyn Bridge, framing the DUMBO neighborhood at its Brooklyn end.

name: Coney Island
blurb: Brooklyn's seaside amusement strip, with the 1920 Wonder Wheel and the 1927 Cyclone coaster. Look for the boardwalk and the old Parachute Jump tower above the beach.

name: Rikers Island
blurb: New York City's main jail complex, on an island in the East River beside LaGuardia, which the city has committed to close. Look for the island of low jail buildings right off the runway ends.

name: Intrepid Museum
blurb: A World War II aircraft carrier docked on the Hudson, now a museum with the space shuttle Enterprise on board. Look for the flight deck lined with jets beside the West Side Highway.

name: Chicago Midway International Airport
blurb: Squeezed into one square mile of Chicago's bungalow grid, so runways end at city streets. In 2005 a landing 737 slid off the end in snow and into an intersection. Look for the airport filling one neat block of the grid.

name: United Center
blurb: Home of the Bulls and Blackhawks, the arena where Michael Jordan won three titles in the 1990s. Look for the big rectangular roof ringed by parking on the Near West Side, west of the Loop.

name: Navy Pier
blurb: A pier reaching about 3,300 ft into Lake Michigan, opened in 1916. Look for the long pier and its Ferris wheel off the downtown lakefront.

name: Museum Campus
blurb: The Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium and Adler Planetarium share a lakefront peninsula built on landfill, next to Soldier Field. Look for the planetarium at the tip of the point jutting into Lake Michigan.

name: Six Flags Great America
blurb: A Six Flags park in Gurnee, between Chicago and Milwaukee. Look for coaster tracks beside Interstate 94.

name: Fermilab
blurb: Home of the Tevatron, the world's most powerful particle collider until 2009. Look for the 4-mile ring of its tunnel traced by a circular road and pond, and Wilson Hall's twin-towered high-rise.

name: Bahá'í House of Worship
blurb: The oldest surviving Bahá'í temple in the world, a white nine-sided domed building finished in 1953. Look for the lacy white dome by the lakeshore in Wilmette, north of Chicago.

name: Northwestern University
blurb: Its Evanston campus runs along Lake Michigan, and in the 1960s it grew by filling in part of the lake. Look for the lagoon and the lakefill peninsula jutting into the water.

name: Nu Stadium
blurb: Inter Miami's new soccer stadium at Miami Freedom Park, on the former Melreese golf course right next to Miami International. Look for the stadium right beside the airport's south side.

name: Hard Rock Guitar Hotel
blurb: A 450-ft hotel tower shaped like two guitar bodies stacked back to back, built by the Seminole Tribe and opened in 2019. At night its outline lights up in moving color.

name: Port Everglades
blurb: One of the busiest cruise ports in the world, right next to the Fort Lauderdale airport. Look for cruise ships in a deep turning basin behind the beach.

name: Gulfstream Park
blurb: Thoroughbred track in Hallandale Beach, home of the Pegasus World Cup, one of the richest races in the world. Look for the oval with a lake in the infield, between I-95 and the beach.

name: Homestead-Miami Speedway
blurb: A 1.5-mile oval with progressive banking that lets drivers pick their line, at the edge of the Everglades. Look for the oval surrounded by farm fields and canals.

name: Amerant Bank Arena
blurb: The Florida Panthers' arena in Sunrise, at the edge of the Everglades. Look for the arena beside the vast Sawgrass Mills outlet mall, with the sawgrass marshes just west.

name: Turkey Point Cooling Canals
blurb: Roughly 168 miles of looping canals cool the Turkey Point nuclear plant on the edge of Biscayne Bay. From the air they look like a giant zigzag grid etched into the flats south of Miami.

name: T-Mobile Park
blurb: The Mariners' home, where a retractable roof rolls on rails and parks over the train tracks when open. It covers the field but never seals it. Look for the big roof panels south of downtown.

name: Climate Pledge Arena
blurb: Home of the NHL's Kraken, built under the preserved sloping roof of the 1962 World's Fair arena. Look for the swooping roof just west of the Space Needle.

name: Boeing Everett Factory
blurb: The largest building in the world by volume, about 472 million cubic feet, where 747s, 767s and 777s are built. Look for the enormous white building at Paine Field with giant airplane murals on its doors.

name: Boeing Field
blurb: Where Boeing has flown its airliners since the 1930s, still used for 737 test and delivery flights. Look for the Museum of Flight and its outdoor jets on the west side of the field.

name: Port of Seattle
blurb: A major container port at the mouth of the Duwamish, just south of downtown. Look for the cranes on Harbor Island and the stadiums beside the yards.

name: Gas Works Park
blurb: A gas plant that closed in 1956, its rusted towers kept as sculpture when it became a park in 1975. Look for the dark industrial towers and grassy kite hill on the north shore of Lake Union.

name: Evergreen Point Floating Bridge
blurb: At 7,710 ft, the longest floating bridge in the world, opened in 2016 on concrete pontoons across Lake Washington. Look for the low, flat line across the lake between Seattle and Bellevue.

name: Tacoma Dome
blurb: One of the largest wood domes in the world, opened in 1983. Look for the low gray dome beside Interstate 5 in Tacoma.

name: Stanley Park
blurb: About 1,000 acres of forest at the tip of downtown Vancouver, larger than New York's Central Park and ringed by a 5.5-mile seawall. Look for the dark green peninsula with the Lions Gate Bridge leaving its north end.

name: Rogers Arena
blurb: Home of the Vancouver Canucks, right beside BC Place on the edge of downtown. Look for the smaller round arena next to the big white dome.

name: Canada Place
blurb: Its five white fabric sails, built for Canada's pavilion at Expo 86, now top the city's cruise ship terminal and convention center. Look for the white sails jutting into Burrard Inlet, often beside a cruise ship.

name: Roberts Bank Superport
blurb: Canada's largest coal export terminal and a big container port, built on a causeway miles out into the Strait of Georgia. Look for black coal piles at the end of a long straight causeway beside the Tsawwassen ferry terminal.

name: University of British Columbia
blurb: Sits at the very tip of the Point Grey peninsula, ringed on the land side by the forest of Pacific Spirit Park and on three sides by water. Wreck Beach lies below its cliffs.

name: Science World
blurb: A geodesic dome built for Expo 86 and covered in reflective panels. Look for the shiny golf ball at the east end of False Creek.

name: Richmond Olympic Oval
blurb: Built for speed skating at the 2010 Winter Olympics, with a roof made from pine-beetle-killed wood. Look for the long curved roof on the Fraser River bank just east of YVR.

name: Ball Arena
blurb: Home of the Nuggets and Avalanche, opened in 1999 on the old railyards along the South Platte. Look for the round arena surrounded by parking lots between Empower Field and downtown.

name: Dick's Sporting Goods Park
blurb: The Colorado Rapids' stadium in Commerce City, surrounded by about two dozen soccer fields. Look for the small stadium inside a big grid of green pitches next to the Rocky Mountain Arsenal wildlife refuge.

name: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
blurb: A 9,500-seat amphitheater set between two red sandstone monoliths taller than Niagara Falls. Look for curved rows of seats in red rock in the foothills west of Denver.

name: Scotiabank Saddledome
blurb: Its roof is a true saddle shape, a hyperbolic paraboloid, built for the 1988 Winter Olympics and home of the Calgary Flames. Look for the curving concrete roof next to the Stampede grounds.

name: Canada Olympic Park
blurb: Built for the 1988 Winter Olympics, it still has the ski jump towers and the bobsled and luge track. Look for the tall jump towers and a small ski hill on Calgary's west edge beside the Trans-Canada Highway.

name: Truist Park
blurb: The Braves' park, opened in 2017 in Cobb County. Look for it in the middle of The Battery, a district of shops and apartments, at the junction of I-75 and I-285.

name: State Farm Arena
blurb: The Atlanta Hawks' arena, built in 1999 on the site of the Omni. Look for the arena between CNN Center and Mercedes-Benz Stadium's pinwheel roof.

name: Six Flags Over Georgia
blurb: A Six Flags park west of Atlanta near the Chattahoochee River. Look for coaster tracks winding through forest.

name: Stone Mountain
blurb: A bare granite dome rising about 825 ft above the Georgia Piedmont, with the largest bas-relief carving in the world on its north face. Look for the gray rock in the green forest east of Atlanta.

name: Globe Life Field
blurb: The Rangers' ballpark opened in 2020 with a retractable roof against Texas heat, and the team won the World Series there in 2023. Look for the big brick-and-glass box beside the Cowboys' silver dome in Arlington.

name: American Airlines Center
blurb: Home of the Mavericks and the Stars, a brick arena with a high arched roof in the Victory Park district. Look for the curved roof just north of downtown Dallas, beside the freeways and rail lines.

name: Six Flags Over Texas
blurb: The original Six Flags park, opened in 1961 in Arlington. Look for the coaster tracks next to AT&T Stadium and the Rangers' ballpark.

name: Texas Motor Speedway
blurb: A 1.5-mile quad-oval north of Fort Worth with seating for well over 100,000 at its peak. Look for the big gray bowl beside the runways and warehouses of Alliance Airport.

name: Toyota Stadium
blurb: FC Dallas's home in Frisco, which also houses the National Soccer Hall of Fame. Look for the open-ended stadium in a park of youth soccer fields in the fast-growing northern suburbs.

name: Astrodome
blurb: Opened in 1965 as the world's first domed stadium, billed as the Eighth Wonder of the World, and gave its name to AstroTurf. Unused for years, it still stands. Look for the round gray dome beside the NRG Stadium roof.

name: Daikin Park
blurb: The Astros' ballpark, called Minute Maid Park until 2025, was built into Houston's old Union Station, with a retractable roof and a full-size locomotive that runs along the outfield wall. Look for the roof at downtown's east edge.

name: Toyota Center
blurb: The Houston Rockets' arena on the south side of downtown, next door to the convention center. Look for the big boxy arena among the parking lots and towers of downtown's southeast edge.

name: Shell Energy Stadium
blurb: Home of the Houston Dynamo and Dash, an orange-trimmed soccer stadium in East Downtown. Look for the compact open box just east of the freeway that rings downtown, a few blocks from the Astros' ballpark.

name: NASA Johnson Space Center
blurb: Home of Mission Control since 1965, the "Houston" every astronaut has called. Look for the campus of boxy buildings beside Clear Lake, with a full Saturn V rocket lying in a long shed.

name: San Jacinto Monument
blurb: At 567 ft, the world's tallest monumental column, a few feet taller than the Washington Monument, topped by a 220-ton star. It marks the 1836 battle that won Texas independence, beside the Houston Ship Channel.

name: William P. Hobby Airport
blurb: Houston's original airport, about 7 miles southeast of downtown, and a Southwest Airlines stronghold. Look for the downtown skyline to the northwest and the refinery-lined Ship Channel to the east.

name: Chase Field
blurb: The Diamondbacks' home has a retractable roof and air conditioning, plus a swimming pool beyond the outfield wall. Look for the big boxy hangar at the southeast corner of downtown Phoenix.

name: Footprint Center
blurb: Home of the Phoenix Suns and Mercury, a block west of Chase Field downtown. Look for the arena's flat roof next to the much bigger ballpark.

name: Phoenix Raceway
blurb: A one-mile NASCAR oval with an odd dogleg on the backstretch, in the desert west of Phoenix. It hosted NASCAR's championship finale for several years; look for the lopsided oval by the Gila River.

name: Camelback Mountain
blurb: Its 2,704-ft summit and red rock humps look like a kneeling camel, surrounded on all sides by Phoenix and Scottsdale houses. Look for the hump and head shape between downtown Phoenix and Scottsdale.

name: Sphere
blurb: A 366-ft venue wrapped in about 1.2 million LEDs, the largest spherical structure in the world. Look for the glowing ball just east of the Strip, showing anything from an eyeball to the moon.

name: T-Mobile Arena
blurb: The Vegas Golden Knights' arena, between the Park MGM and New York-New York on the Strip. Look for the angular bronze and glass box set back from the boulevard.

name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway
blurb: A 1.5-mile NASCAR oval in the open desert about 15 miles northeast of the Strip, next door to Nellis Air Force Base. Look for the gray D-shaped bowl against the tan desert floor.

name: Luxor Las Vegas
blurb: A 30-story black glass pyramid that shoots what is billed as the strongest beam of light on Earth from its tip at night. Look for the dark pyramid and sphinx at the south end of the Strip.

name: Mall of America
blurb: One of the largest malls in the US, with a full theme park indoors. Look for the huge boxy building and parking ramps just east of MSP's runways.

name: Xcel Energy Center
blurb: Home of the Minnesota Wild in downtown St. Paul. Look for the arena near the Mississippi bluffs and the domed State Capitol to the north.

name: Allianz Field
blurb: Minnesota United's soccer stadium since 2019, wrapped in a translucent skin that can glow at night. Look for the pale oval beside I-94 in St. Paul's Midway district.

name: Comerica Park
blurb: Home of the Tigers since 2000, with giant tiger statues at the gates. Look for the ballpark opening toward the downtown Detroit skyline beside Ford Field.

name: Little Caesars Arena
blurb: Home of the Red Wings and Pistons since 2017, with a glass-roofed concourse wrapped around the bowl. Look for it just north of Comerica Park.

name: Ford River Rouge Complex
blurb: Henry Ford's 1920s complex where iron ore went in one end and cars came out the other, once the largest industrial complex in the world. Its truck plant has a living roof of about 10 acres.

name: Gordie Howe International Bridge
blurb: Its 2,800-ft cable-stayed span is the longest in North America, linking Detroit and Windsor downriver from the Ambassador Bridge. Look for its two tall A-shaped towers over the Detroit River.

name: Citizens Bank Park
blurb: The Phillies' ballpark, opened in 2004 in the South Philadelphia sports complex. Look for the brick and steel diamond beside the Eagles' stadium and the arena, near the Navy Yard.

name: Xfinity Mobile Arena
blurb: Home of the Flyers and 76ers, formerly the Wells Fargo Center, in the South Philadelphia sports complex. Look for the big arena among the parking lots beside the two stadiums.

name: Subaru Park
blurb: Philadelphia Union's soccer stadium in Chester, right on the Delaware River. Look for it directly beneath the blue Commodore Barry Bridge.

name: Philadelphia Navy Yard
blurb: The old Philadelphia Naval Shipyard on League Island, where the Navy still keeps decommissioned warships. Look for gray ships tied up along the piers just east of the airport.

name: Battleship New Jersey
blurb: The most decorated US battleship, serving from World War II to the end of the Cold War, now a museum on the Camden waterfront. Look for the long gray hull across the Delaware from Philadelphia.

name: The Pentagon
blurb: One of the world's largest office buildings, built in about 16 months during World War II, with five rings and some 17 miles of corridors. Look for the five-sided shape beside I-395, just north of Reagan National.

name: Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center
blurb: The Smithsonian's giant hangar holding Space Shuttle Discovery, an SR-71 Blackbird and the Enola Gay. Look for the long curved-roof hangar on the south edge of Dulles Airport.

name: Audi Field
blurb: D.C. United's stadium, opened in 2018 on Buzzard Point, where the Anacostia meets the Potomac. Look for the canopy-topped soccer box a few blocks south of Nationals Park.

name: Palace of Westminster
blurb: Rebuilt after an 1834 fire, home of both houses of Parliament. Big Ben is the bell; its clock tower is 316 ft. Look for the long Gothic Revival block on the Thames with the tower at its north end.

name: London Eye
blurb: A 443-ft observation wheel that opened in 2000 and was meant to stay five years. Look for the white wheel on the South Bank, directly across the Thames from Parliament.

name: Tower of London
blurb: William the Conqueror's White Tower dates to the 1070s, and the fortress still guards the Crown Jewels. Look for the square white keep inside rings of walls, right next to Tower Bridge.

name: St Paul's Cathedral
blurb: Christopher Wren's cathedral, finished in 1710, with a 365-ft dome that stayed London's tallest building into the 1960s. Look for the gray dome rising out of the City just north of the Millennium footbridge.

name: Battersea Power Station
blurb: One of the largest brick buildings in Europe, the coal plant from Pink Floyd's Animals cover, now shops and flats. Look for four white chimneys at the corners of a brick block on the Thames.

name: Buckingham Palace
blurb: The monarch's London home has 775 rooms and a 39-acre garden, one of the largest private gardens in London. Look for the pale palace at the end of The Mall, with the round Victoria Memorial in front.

name: Lord's Cricket Ground
blurb: The Home of Cricket, on this site since 1814. Look for the white pod of the Media Centre, a space-age aluminum capsule above the pitch, in leafy St John's Wood near Regent's Park.

name: The Oval
blurb: Hosted the first Test match in England in 1880, against Australia. Look for the oval cricket ground in Kennington, south London, next to a pair of old Victorian gasholder frames.

name: The O2
blurb: Built as the Millennium Dome, now one of the world's busiest concert venues; its 12 yellow masts stand for the months of the year. Look for the white tent filling the Greenwich Peninsula in a loop of the Thames.

name: Thames Barrier
blurb: Ten steel gates that swing up from the riverbed to keep North Sea surges out of London, working since 1982. Look for the row of shiny silver shell-shaped hoods strung across the river at Woolwich.

name: Craven Cottage
blurb: Fulham's home since 1896, on the north bank of the Thames by Putney. The odd name comes from the little brick cottage pavilion still standing in one corner; look for the stands hugging the riverbank.

name: Ascot Racecourse
blurb: Founded by Queen Anne in 1711 and home of Royal Ascot, where the royal family arrives by horse-drawn carriage. Look for the long green racecourse and the curving white grandstand near Windsor.

name: Epsom Downs Racecourse
blurb: The Derby has been run here since 1780 and gave its name to races worldwide. Look for the horseshoe-shaped course on the open green downs south of London.

name: Thorpe Park
blurb: A theme park built on flooded gravel pits west of London, near the Heathrow approaches. Look for coaster tracks on islands in the lakes.

name: Legoland Windsor
blurb: A Lego theme park near Windsor, in rolling woods. Look for colorful rides on the hillside a few miles from Windsor Castle.

name: Selhurst Park
blurb: Crystal Palace have played here since 1924, packed into the terraced streets of South Norwood. Look for a tight rectangle of stands boxed in by rows of houses.

name: Gtech Community Stadium
blurb: Brentford's ground, opened in 2020 and squeezed into a triangle of railway lines near Kew Bridge. Look for the compact stadium hemmed in on all sides by tracks.

name: Arc de Triomphe
blurb: Napoleon ordered it in 1806; it stands 164 ft tall at the center of a star of 12 avenues. Look for the white arch with avenues radiating like spokes, the Champs-Élysées running straight toward the Louvre.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
blurb: The Gothic cathedral on an island in the Seine, begun in 1163. Its roof and spire burned in 2019 and it reopened in December 2024. Look for the twin square towers and rebuilt spire on the Île de la Cité.

name: Sacré-Cœur
blurb: It sits on Montmartre, the highest hill in Paris, and stays white because its travertine stone bleaches in the rain. Look for the bright white domes on the hill in the north of the city.

name: Les Invalides
blurb: Louis XIV's hospital for old soldiers, now home to Napoleon's tomb. Look for the gilded dome, about 350 ft tall, gleaming above the long lawn of the Esplanade.

name: Louvre
blurb: The world's most visited museum, a former royal palace whose long wings run along the Seine. Look for I.M. Pei's glass pyramid in the courtyard between the wings, with the Tuileries garden stretching west.

name: Parc des Princes
