blurb: Paris Saint-Germain's home since 1974, ringed by curving concrete ribs that hold up the roof. Look for the oval of ribbed concrete next to the Périphérique, at the edge of the Bois de Boulogne.

name: Stade Roland Garros
blurb: Home of the French Open, the only Grand Slam on red clay. Look for the rust-orange courts and the big Court Philippe-Chatrier, which got a retractable roof in 2020, beside the Bois de Boulogne.

name: Grande Arche
blurb: A hollow cube about 360 ft high at La Défense, lined up with the Arc de Triomphe and the Louvre along Paris's historic axis. Notre-Dame could almost fit inside. Look for the open white cube at the end of the towers.

name: Longchamp Racecourse
blurb: Home of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Europe's richest flat horse race. Look for the green oval in the Bois de Boulogne beside the Seine, with the Eiffel Tower a few miles east.

name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
blurb: Four concentric 17th-century canals wrap Amsterdam's center in a half-moon. Look for the horseshoe of rings opening onto the waterfront behind Central Station.

name: Keukenhof and the bulb fields
blurb: In spring the bulb fields between Leiden and Haarlem turn into stripes of red, yellow and purple, and Keukenhof garden plants about 7 million bulbs a year. Look for the color bands from mid-March to mid-May.

name: Tokyo Imperial Palace
blurb: The emperor's home stands on the site of Edo Castle, ringed by moats and stone walls. Look for the big island of forest and moat in central Tokyo next to the Marunouchi towers.

name: Tokyo Big Sight
blurb: Japan's largest convention center, on reclaimed land in Tokyo Bay. Look for four upside-down pyramids perched on legs on the waterfront near Odaiba.

name: Tokyo DisneySea
blurb: Disney's sea-themed park beside Tokyo Disneyland on the bay. Look for the volcano, Mount Prometheus, rising from a central lagoon.

name: Umihotaru
blurb: A rest-stop island in the middle of Tokyo Bay where the Aqua-Line switches from a 6-mile undersea tunnel to a nearly 3-mile bridge. Look for the ship-shaped island where the bridge ends.

name: Japan National Stadium
blurb: Kengo Kuma's stadium for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, wrapped in tiers of wooden eaves and planted with greenery. Look for the round bowl in the Meiji Jingu Gaien gardens.

name: USS Midway Museum
blurb: The longest-serving US aircraft carrier of the 20th century, in service from 1945 to 1992. Look for the long gray flight deck with parked jets on San Diego's downtown waterfront.

name: San Diego–Coronado Bridge
blurb: Over 2 miles long, it curves through a wide arc and climbs about 200 ft so Navy carriers can pass beneath. Look for its blue span sweeping across the bay to Coronado.

name: Hotel del Coronado
blurb: Opened in 1888, it's one of the largest wooden buildings in the US. Look for the white Victorian hotel with red turreted roofs on the Coronado beach, across the bay from downtown San Diego.

name: SeaWorld San Diego
blurb: Opened in 1964 on the shore of Mission Bay. Look for the observation tower and blue pools on the bay's south shore.

name: Moda Center
blurb: The Portland Trail Blazers' arena, just across the Willamette from downtown in the Rose Quarter. Look for the curved roof beside the river's east bank.

name: Providence Park
blurb: Home of the Timbers and Thorns, used for sports since 1926 and squeezed into a city block downtown. Look for a narrow stadium tucked among the streets just west of the city center.

name: St. Johns Bridge
blurb: A green steel suspension bridge from 1931 with Gothic-arched towers, often called Portland's most beautiful. It crosses the Willamette at a gap below Forest Park; look for the green towers above the river's industrial banks.

name: Utah State Capitol
blurb: A granite capitol finished in 1916 on a hill at the head of State Street. Look for the dome above downtown Salt Lake City, with the Wasatch Range rising behind.

name: Salt Lake Temple
blurb: Took 40 years to build, from 1853 to 1893, from granite hauled out of Little Cottonwood Canyon. Look for the six gray spires, the tallest topped by a gold angel, in Temple Square downtown.

name: Delta Center
blurb: Home of the Utah Jazz and the NHL's Utah team, a big boxy arena in downtown Salt Lake City. Look for a large flat rectangle roof a few blocks west of Temple Square.

name: Spectrum Center
blurb: The Charlotte Hornets' arena in Uptown, opened in 2005. Look for the brick and glass building a few blocks from the Panthers' stadium.

name: Charlotte Motor Speedway
blurb: Home of the Coca-Cola 600, NASCAR's longest race, on a 1.5-mile quad-oval in Concord. Look for the big gray bowl with the zMAX drag strip straight across the road.

name: Epcot
blurb: Its 180-ft Spaceship Earth geodesic sphere is the park's signature. Look for the silver ball at the front and the countries of World Showcase ringing a lagoon behind it.

name: Epic Universe
blurb: Universal's newest Orlando park, opened in 2025. Look for a ring of themed worlds around a central lake, a few miles south of the original Universal parks.

name: SeaWorld Orlando
blurb: A marine park on the south side of Orlando's tourist district. Look for the tall coaster tracks and pools around a central lake.

name: Kia Center
blurb: The Orlando Magic's downtown arena, opened in 2010. Look for the big arena roof in downtown Orlando, a few blocks east of the Inter&Co soccer stadium.

name: Inter&Co Stadium
blurb: Orlando City and the Orlando Pride's soccer stadium, opened in 2017 in the Parramore neighborhood. Look for the compact rectangular stadium with purple seats just west of downtown.

name: Rogers Centre
blurb: Opened in 1989 as the SkyDome, the first stadium with a fully retractable motorized roof. Home of the Blue Jays, it sits at the foot of the CN Tower; look for the white segmented dome.

name: Scotiabank Arena
blurb: Home of the Maple Leafs and Raptors, built inside a 1940s postal building near Union Station. Look for it at the south edge of downtown's towers, by the rail corridor.

name: BMO Field
blurb: Home of Toronto FC and the Argonauts, at Exhibition Place on the lakeshore. Look for the rectangle among the exhibition grounds' old halls, west of downtown.

name: Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport
blurb: On the Toronto Islands, a few hundred yards from downtown and linked by a pedestrian tunnel. Look for the CN Tower right beside you and Lake Ontario's breakwaters.

name: Canada's Wonderland
blurb: Canada's biggest theme park, north of Toronto. Look for an artificial mountain at the center, with coaster tracks around it beside Highway 400.

name: Olympic Stadium (Montreal)
blurb: Built for the 1976 Olympics, with the world's tallest inclined tower, leaning at 45 degrees over the stadium. Its roof was meant to hang from the tower but took until 1987 to finish. Look for the shell and the slanted spire.

name: Bell Centre
blurb: Home of the Montreal Canadiens since 1996, downtown near the old Forum. Look for the boxy arena near the base of the downtown towers.

name: Jacques Cartier Bridge
blurb: A 1930 steel cantilever bridge crossing the St. Lawrence via Saint Helen's Island, lit since 2017 with lights that change color with the seasons. Look for the green truss hopping the island between downtown and the south shore.

name: Samuel De Champlain Bridge
blurb: Opened in 2019 to replace a crumbling 1962 bridge, it is one of the busiest crossings in Canada. Look for its single tuning-fork-shaped pylon, about 550 ft tall, and harp of cables over the St. Lawrence southwest of downtown Montreal.

name: Saint Joseph's Oratory
blurb: Canada's largest church, with one of the largest domes in the world, on the slope of Mount Royal. Look for the green copper dome on the hillside.

name: Montreal Biosphere
blurb: Buckminster Fuller's geodesic dome, the US pavilion at Expo 67. Its acrylic skin burned in 1976, leaving the steel lattice. Look for the steel sphere on Île Sainte-Hélène.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
blurb: One of the most visited Catholic shrines in the world, drawing millions of pilgrims a year. Look for the round modern basilica of 1976 beside the old, visibly tilting baroque one at the foot of Tepeyac hill.

name: Teotihuacan
blurb: An ancient city that may have held 100,000 people around 500 AD, centuries before the Aztecs found it in ruins. Look for the Pyramid of the Sun beside the long, straight Avenue of the Dead.

name: Estadio Olímpico Universitario
blurb: Centerpiece of the 1968 Olympics, built on a lava field in UNAM's campus. A Diego Rivera relief decorates the front. Look for the low oval of earth embankments by the campus's central library.

name: Chapultepec Castle
blurb: The only castle in North America that housed reigning monarchs, Emperor Maximilian and Empress Carlota in the 1860s. Look for it on a hilltop inside Chapultepec Park, one of the largest city parks in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Royal Palace of Madrid
blurb: The largest royal palace in Western Europe by floor area, with about 3,400 rooms, though the king lives elsewhere. Look for the white quadrangle above the Campo del Moro gardens, facing Almudena Cathedral.

name: Sagrada Família
blurb: Under construction since 1882, Gaudí's basilica becomes the world's tallest church when its central tower tops out at about 566 ft. Look for the cluster of spires and cranes filling a whole block of Barcelona's grid.

name: Port of Barcelona
blurb: One of the busiest cruise ports in the Mediterranean. Look for the sail-shaped W hotel at the harbor mouth and cruise ships docked below Montjuïc hill.

name: Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys
blurb: Built in 1929 on Montjuïc, rebuilt as the main stadium of the 1992 Olympics, and home to Barcelona while Camp Nou was rebuilt. Look for the oval with a track on the hill above the port.

name: Nymphenburg Palace
blurb: Munich's baroque summer palace for the Wittelsbach rulers, its facade more than 2,000 ft wide. Look for the long canal running straight to the palace and the big park behind it.

name: Letzigrund
blurb: Zurich's athletics and football stadium, home of the Weltklasse meet where many world records have fallen, and of FC Zurich and Grasshoppers. Look for a low oval with a track among the rail lines west of the center.

name: Rhine Falls
blurb: Europe's most powerful plain waterfall, only about 75 ft high but some 490 ft wide. Look for the white churn on the Rhine below the castle of Laufen, just downstream of Schaffhausen.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
blurb: The largest church in the world by interior space, with Michelangelo's dome rising about 450 ft. Look for the keyhole-shaped square ringed by colonnades at the end of a straight avenue from the Tiber.

name: Circus Maximus
blurb: Ancient Rome's chariot track held well over 100,000 spectators. Today it's a long grassy oval about 2,000 ft long between the Palatine and Aventine hills.

name: Castel Sant'Angelo
blurb: Built as Emperor Hadrian's tomb around 130 AD and later turned into a papal fortress. Look for the round drum inside angular bastion walls on the Tiber, an angel statue on top.

name: Portus Hexagon
blurb: Trajan's six-sided harbor basin, dug about 1,900 years ago for imperial Rome's port, still holds water. Look for a perfect hexagonal lake right beside Fiumicino airport's runways.

name: Hagia Sophia
blurb: Finished in 537, it was the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years, its dome about 100 ft across. Look for the great dome and four minarets at the tip of the old city, facing the Blue Mosque.

name: Blue Mosque
blurb: Built from 1609 to 1616 for Sultan Ahmed I, and unusual for its six minarets. Look for the cascade of domes facing Hagia Sophia across the park in Sultanahmet.

name: Topkapı Palace
blurb: Seat of the Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years, on the point where the Bosporus, Golden Horn and Sea of Marmara meet. Look for the courtyards and pavilions among trees at the very tip of the old city.

name: Süleymaniye Mosque
blurb: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece for Suleiman the Magnificent, finished in 1557. Look for the huge dome and four minarets crowning the hill above the Golden Horn, the old city's dominant silhouette.

name: The World Islands
blurb: About 300 artificial islands shaped like a map of the world, a few miles off Dubai's coast; most are still bare sand. Look for continent outlines dotted in the Gulf inside an oval breakwater.

name: Burj Al Arab
blurb: A 1,053-ft hotel shaped like a dhow's sail, standing on its own artificial island since 1999. Look for the white sail at the end of a short causeway on Jumeirah Beach.

name: Marina Bay Sands
blurb: Three 55-story hotel towers joined at the top by a ship-shaped SkyPark about 1,120 ft long, with an infinity pool on the roof. Look for the flat deck spanning the towers on Marina Bay.

name: Jewel Changi Airport
blurb: A glass doughnut of a dome holding the world's tallest indoor waterfall, about 130 ft, falling through a hole in the roof into a terraced forest. Look for the round glass dome in front of Terminal 1.

name: Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge
blurb: A 34-mile bridge and tunnel system across the Pearl River estuary, the longest sea crossing in the world. Look for the artificial islands where the road dives underwater.

name: Kai Tak Stadium
blurb: Built on the old Kai Tak airport, where jets once banked low over Kowloon rooftops. The 50,000-seat stadium opened in 2025 with a retractable roof; look for it on the old airport land beside the harbor.

name: Ocean Park Hong Kong
blurb: A park split by a ridge on Hong Kong Island's south side, joined by a cable car. Look for the cable car linking the lowland and the headland over the sea.

name: Sydney Opera House
blurb: Its sail-like shells are covered in more than a million white and cream tiles. Look for the white shells on Bennelong Point, just across Circular Quay from the Harbour Bridge.

name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
blurb: Opened in 1932 and nicknamed the Coathanger, its steel arch spans about 1,650 ft and rises about 440 ft above the harbor. Look for the Opera House's white shells just across Sydney Cove.

name: Accor Stadium
blurb: Sydney's 2000 Olympic stadium, at Homebush. It held 110,000 for the Games before being cut down to about 80,000. Look for the saddle-shaped roof amid the Olympic Park's grid of venues.

name: Port Botany
blurb: Sydney's main container port, in Botany Bay where James Cook landed in 1770. Look for cranes right beside the airport's runway that juts into the bay.

name: Riyadh Air Metropolitano
blurb: Atlético Madrid's home since 2017, rebuilt from an old athletics stadium; it hosted the 2019 Champions League final. Look for the oval with a floating white roof on Madrid's eastern edge near the airport.

name: Texas State Capitol
blurb: Built of pink granite in 1888 and, at about 303 ft, taller than the US Capitol, as Texans will tell you. Look for the dome at the head of Congress Avenue in downtown Austin.

name: Q2 Stadium
blurb: Austin FC's home since 2021, a steep, roughly 20,000-seat soccer stadium famous for its loud supporters' end. Look for the open box in north Austin, near the Domain.

name: Tesla Gigafactory Texas
blurb: One of the largest factory buildings in the world, with more than 10 million square feet of floor space, where Tesla builds the Model Y and Cybertruck. Look for the vast white box beside the Colorado River just east of Austin's airport.

name: Bridgestone Arena
blurb: The Nashville Predators' arena, one block off the honky-tonks of Lower Broadway, known for its loud, catfish-throwing crowds. Look for the arena with a tall spire at the corner of downtown.

name: Gaylord Opryland
blurb: One of the largest non-casino hotels in the US, with about 2,900 rooms and 9 acres of indoor gardens and waterways under glass. Look for the glass atrium roofs inside a bend of the Cumberland River east of downtown Nashville.

name: GEODIS Park
blurb: Nashville SC's home, the largest soccer-specific stadium in the US at about 30,000 seats, opened in 2022 at the state fairgrounds. Look for the open box south of downtown.

name: Lenovo Center
blurb: The Carolina Hurricanes' arena in west Raleigh, opened in 1999 and shared for years with NC State basketball. Look for it beside NC State's Carter-Finley football stadium and the state fairgrounds.

name: Benchmark International Arena
blurb: The Tampa Bay Lightning's arena on the downtown waterfront, opened in 1996. Look for the arena right beside the Channelside cruise terminal and the Garrison Channel.

name: Busch Gardens Tampa Bay
blurb: An Africa-themed park and zoo in Tampa with a big open savanna of animals. Look for the grassy plain beside white coaster tracks.

name: PNC Park
blurb: The Pittsburgh Pirates' home on the Allegheny, often rated one of the best ballparks in baseball. Look for the low, open outfield facing downtown and the yellow Roberto Clemente Bridge.

name: PPG Paints Arena
blurb: The Pittsburgh Penguins' arena, opened in 2010 in the Hill District just east of downtown. Look for the glass-fronted arena across the street from the site of the old dome-roofed Civic Arena, now a new office tower and lots.

name: Point State Park
blurb: The triangle where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers join to form the Ohio. Look for the fountain at the tip, which shoots up to 150 ft.

name: Busch Stadium
blurb: Home of the Cardinals since 2006, framed by the Gateway Arch beyond the outfield. Look for the red brick ballpark in downtown St. Louis near the Mississippi.

name: Enterprise Center
blurb: Home of the St. Louis Blues, a few blocks west of Busch Stadium downtown. Look for the arena a short walk from Union Station and its old train shed.

name: Energizer Park
blurb: Home of St. Louis CITY SC, the MLS club that arrived in 2023, built in the Downtown West neighborhood just off the rail yards west of downtown. Look for a compact, steep-sided soccer bowl next to the highway.

name: Six Flags St. Louis
blurb: A Six Flags park in Eureka, west of St. Louis, beside Interstate 44 and the Meramec valley. Look for coaster tracks winding through wooded hills.

name: St. Louis Lambert International Airport
blurb: Once a TWA hub, its 1956 terminal of concrete vaults was designed by Minoru Yamasaki, later architect of the World Trade Center. Look for the Gateway Arch about 14 miles southeast.

name: Kauffman Stadium
blurb: Home of the Royals since 1973, known for its outfield fountains and waterfalls. Look for the ballpark next to Arrowhead in the Truman Sports Complex.

name: Children's Mercy Park
blurb: Home of Sporting Kansas City, on the Kansas side of the metro. Look for the stadium with a translucent roof in the Village West area by the NASCAR speedway.

name: Kansas Speedway
blurb: A 1.5-mile NASCAR tri-oval on the western edge of Kansas City, with a casino built into the grounds. Look for the gray D-shaped oval next to the big shopping and stadium district at Village West.

name: Kansas City International Airport
blurb: A single new terminal opened in 2023, replacing three horseshoe-shaped ones. Look for the runways on rolling farmland north of the Missouri River, about 15 miles from downtown.

name: Frost Bank Center
blurb: The San Antonio Spurs' arena on the city's east side, next to the rodeo and livestock show grounds. The team plans a new arena downtown. Look for the boxy arena among wide parking lots east of downtown.

name: SeaWorld San Antonio
blurb: A marine park west of San Antonio. Look for pools, rides and a lake on the brushy western edge of the city.

name: Six Flags Fiesta Texas
blurb: Built in a former limestone quarry in San Antonio, its rides are ringed by cliff walls. Look for the bowl of white rock with coaster tracks inside it.

name: San Antonio International Airport
blurb: Sits inside the city, about 8 miles north of downtown San Antonio. Look for dense neighborhoods all around and the green Hill Country rising to the northwest.

name: Golden 1 Center
blurb: The Sacramento Kings' downtown arena, opened in 2016 and powered largely by solar. Look for its angular glass entrance and big roof among the downtown blocks near Old Sacramento and the river.

name: California State Capitol
blurb: Completed in 1874, its white dome topped with a gold ball sits in a 40-acre park at the east end of the Capitol Mall. Look for the dome straight down the Mall from Tower Bridge.

name: Tower Bridge (Sacramento)
blurb: A gold-painted 1935 vertical lift bridge over the Sacramento River by Old Sacramento. Look for its two tall towers and the Ziggurat building beside it.

name: Sacramento International Airport
blurb: Set in the Sacramento River floodplain amid flat farmland, much of it rice. Look for flooded rice paddies around the airport in spring, shining like mirrors, and the river levee to the west.

name: Pearl Harbor
blurb: The Japanese attack on December 7, 1941 brought the US into World War II. Look for Ford Island in the middle of the harbor and the white USS Arizona Memorial spanning the sunken battleship.

name: Rogers Place
blurb: Home of the Edmonton Oilers since 2016, part of a new entertainment district that revived the north edge of downtown. Look for the arena's curving silver roof among the towers.

name: West Edmonton Mall
blurb: Once the largest mall in the world and still the largest in North America, with an indoor water park, a roller coaster and a skating rink under its roof. Look for the long, pale roof sprawl in west Edmonton.

name: Alberta Legislature Building
blurb: Completed in 1913, its domed Beaux-Arts building sits high on the bank of the North Saskatchewan River. Look for the dome above formal grounds and fountains, just south of downtown Edmonton.

name: Edmonton International Airport
blurb: By land area one of the largest airports in Canada, set in open farmland well south of Edmonton. Look for the runways surrounded by a patchwork of fields and the highway running north to the city.

name: Parliament Hill
blurb: Canada's Parliament on a bluff above the Ottawa River, with the 302-ft Peace Tower. Look for the green copper roofs and Gothic towers on the cliff edge.

name: TD Place Stadium
blurb: The Ottawa Redblacks' stadium at Lansdowne Park beside the Rideau Canal. Look for the rippling wooden veil wrapping the south stand.

name: Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport
blurb: Serves Canada's capital, south of Ottawa. Look for the Gothic towers of Parliament on their bluff over the Ottawa River and the Rideau Canal snaking through the city.

name: Poolbeg Chimneys
blurb: Two red-and-white striped chimneys about 680 ft tall at the old Poolbeg power station, among the tallest structures in Ireland. Look for the twin stacks at the mouth of the Liffey.

name: Edinburgh Castle
blurb: Sits on Castle Rock, the plug of an extinct volcano, and has guarded Edinburgh for about 900 years. Look for the castle on its crag at the top of the Royal Mile, with Princes Street Gardens below.

name: Arthur's Seat
blurb: An extinct volcano 823 ft high, sitting in a park barely a mile from Edinburgh Castle. Look for the bare, rugged hill with red cliffs, Salisbury Crags, rising straight out of the city.

name: Etihad Stadium
blurb: Manchester City's home, built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games and later enlarged. Look for the stadium with tall roof masts and cables in east Manchester's sports campus.

name: Jodrell Bank Observatory
blurb: The Lovell Telescope's 250-ft dish was finished in 1957, just in time to track the rocket that launched Sputnik. Look for the white dish in the Cheshire fields south of Manchester Airport.

name: Royal Albert Dock
blurb: Opened in 1846 as the first dock warehouses built without structural wood, the largest group of Grade I listed buildings in the UK. Look for the red-brick warehouses around a square basin on Liverpool's Mersey waterfront.

name: Hill Dickinson Stadium
blurb: Everton's new home, opened in 2025, was built on the filled-in Bramley-Moore Dock on the Mersey waterfront, with about 53,000 seats. Look for the brick-and-steel box at the water's edge north of Liverpool's center.

name: CopenHill
blurb: A waste-to-energy power plant with a year-round artificial ski slope running down its roof. Look for the long, sloping gray building with a green ski run on Copenhagen's industrial harbor edge.

name: Middelgrunden Wind Farm
blurb: Twenty turbines in a gentle arc on a shoal off Copenhagen, built in 2000 and half owned by thousands of local residents. Look for the curved line of white towers in the Øresund just off the harbor.

name: Oslo Opera House
blurb: Its white marble roof slopes down into the fjord, and people walk right up it to the top. Look for the angled white slab at the edge of the harbor.

name: Holmenkollen Ski Jump
blurb: A steel ski jump towering over Oslo, rebuilt in 2010 at a site that has held jumping contests since 1892. Look for the ramp cantilevered out from the ridge above the city.

name: Ullevaal Stadion
blurb: Norway's national football stadium, in north Oslo. Look for the compact rectangular ground beside the ring road, with forested hills behind it.

name: Avicii Arena
blurb: The Globe, the world's largest hemispherical building, about 280 ft tall, now named for the late DJ Avicii. It's the Sun in a scale model of the solar system spread across Sweden. Look for the white ball south of the city.

name: Stockholm City Hall
blurb: Site of the Nobel Prize banquet, a red-brick hall finished in 1923 with a 348-ft tower topped by three gold crowns. Look for the tower at the water's edge on the tip of Kungsholmen.

name: Suomenlinna
blurb: An 18th-century sea fortress spread across a cluster of islands at the mouth of Helsinki harbor, built by Sweden to guard against Russia. Look for the star-shaped bastions and green ramparts the ferries pass on the way in.

name: Helsinki Cathedral
blurb: The white, green-domed Lutheran cathedral at the top of Senate Square, finished in 1852 and Helsinki's best-known landmark. Look for the big green central dome and four smaller ones above the white columns.

name: Vienna
blurb: The old imperial capital is ringed by the Ringstrasse, a boulevard built where the city walls stood. Look for the Danube and its long thin Donauinsel island, and the vineyards on the hills to the north.

name: Schönbrunn Palace
blurb: The Habsburg summer palace has 1,441 rooms, and its grounds hold the oldest zoo still operating in the world, opened in 1752. Look for the long yellow palace, formal gardens, and the colonnaded Gloriette on the hill behind.

name: Prater and the Riesenrad
blurb: Vienna's old amusement park, with its 1897 Riesenrad Ferris wheel about 212 ft tall, famous from 'The Third Man.' Look for the wheel at the edge of the long green Prater park.

name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
blurb: Its south tower rises about 446 ft, and its steep roof is covered in roughly 230,000 glazed tiles laid in zigzags and a double-headed eagle. Look for the colorful roof in the dead center of Vienna.

name: Prague Castle
blurb: By Guinness reckoning, the largest ancient castle complex in the world, about 1,800 ft long. Look for the long ridge of palaces above the Vltava, with the spires of St. Vitus Cathedral rising from the middle.

name: Lisbon
blurb: Spread over hills above the Tagus estuary. Look for the red 25 de Abril suspension bridge, a near twin of the Golden Gate, and upstream the 7.6-mile Vasco da Gama Bridge across the river's wide mouth.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
blurb: Built in the 1500s with spice-trade money, and the burial place of Vasco da Gama. Look for the long white limestone monastery in Belém facing the Tagus.

name: Cristo Rei
blurb: A Christ statue with outstretched arms on a pedestal, about 360 ft tall in all, inspired by Rio's. Look for the figure on the south bank of the Tagus beside the red 25 de Abril Bridge.

name: Estádio José Alvalade
blurb: Sporting's home, opened for Euro 2004, with a facade in bright blocks of green, yellow and blue. Look for it a short way northeast of Benfica's stadium, close to the airport.

name: Acropolis of Athens
blurb: The Parthenon has stood on this limestone rock above Athens for nearly 2,500 years. Look for the flat-topped rock with the honey-colored temple rising out of the white city sprawl.

name: Olympic Stadium of Athens
blurb: Main stadium of the 2004 Olympics, with a roof of two huge steel arches by Santiago Calatrava. Look for the white arches north of central Athens in the sports complex at Marousi.

name: Museum of Islamic Art
blurb: I.M. Pei designed this cream limestone museum on its own artificial island in Doha Bay, opened in 2008. Look for the stacked cubist block at the end of a causeway.

name: The Pearl-Qatar
blurb: An artificial island of roughly 1,000 acres off Doha, with marinas, towers and a lacy coastline. Look for the ring-shaped Porto Arabia marina and looping islets north of West Bay.

name: India Gate
blurb: A 138-ft war memorial arch carrying the names of more than 13,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army. Look for the arch at the east end of the long Kartavya Path, with the president's palace at the other end.

name: Lotus Temple
blurb: A Bahai house of worship opened in 1986, made of 27 white marble petals in clusters of three forming nine sides. Look for the white lotus flower ringed by nine blue pools in south Delhi.

name: Qutub Minar
blurb: At about 240 ft, the tallest brick minaret in the world, begun around 1199. Look for the slim red tower and ruined mosque among the trees of south Delhi.

name: Akshardham
blurb: Opened in 2005 and listed by Guinness as the world's largest comprehensive Hindu temple. Look for the pink sandstone domed temple inside a big rectangular courtyard near the east bank of the Yamuna.

name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
blurb: Built for the British viceroy and finished in 1929, now the president's house, with about 340 rooms. Look for the big domed building at the west end of Kartavya Path, with formal gardens behind.

name: Wankhede Stadium
blurb: Where India won the 2011 Cricket World Cup on a six by M.S. Dhoni. Look for the white-canopied ground near Marine Drive and Churchgate, just inland from the sea wall.

name: Atal Setu
blurb: About 13.5 miles over Mumbai harbor, India's longest sea bridge, opened in 2024. Look for its long line across the mudflats and mangroves of the eastern bay.

name: Marine Drive
blurb: A 2-mile seafront boulevard curving around Back Bay; its streetlights at night earn it the name Queen's Necklace. Look for the C-shaped curve of the bay lined with art deco apartments.

name: Grand Palace (Bangkok)
blurb: Home of Siam's kings since 1782 and of the Emerald Buddha, Thailand's holiest image. Look for the cluster of gold spires and orange-and-green roofs inside white walls on the east bank of the Chao Phraya.

name: Wat Arun
blurb: The Temple of Dawn, whose steep central spire is covered in pieces of colored porcelain. Look for the tall pale prang on the west bank of the Chao Phraya, directly across from the Grand Palace.

name: Rajamangala Stadium
blurb: Thailand's national stadium in east Bangkok, built for the 1998 Asian Games and the country's largest stadium. Look for the big oval with a partial roof among the sprawl and canals of the eastern suburbs.

name: Putrajaya
blurb: Malaysia's planned government capital, built since the 1990s around a man-made lake. Look for the pink-domed Putra Mosque and the long boulevard leading to the Prime Minister's green-domed office.

name: Batu Caves
blurb: A Hindu shrine in limestone caves north of Kuala Lumpur, guarded by a 140-ft gold statue of Lord Murugan. Look for the gold figure at the foot of the cliff and 272 steps climbing to the cave mouth.

name: Taipei 101
blurb: At 1,667 ft it was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010, and a steel ball of more than 700 tons inside damps typhoon sway. Look for the stacked segments, styled like a bamboo stalk, towering over Taipei.

name: Grand Hotel Taipei
blurb: A palace-style hotel with red columns and a golden-tiled Chinese roof, built in 1973 on a hill over the Keelung River. Look for the red building on the slope just north of Songshan Airport.

name: Taipei Songshan Airport
blurb: Sits right in the middle of Taipei, one of the most central airports in Asia. Look for Taipei 101's stacked-bamboo silhouette just a few miles south of the runway.

name: Temple of Heaven
blurb: Emperors came here to pray for good harvests, and its grounds are several times larger than the Forbidden City. Look for the round, triple-roofed blue hall at the north end of the long, tree-filled park.

name: Tiananmen Square
blurb: One of the largest city squares in the world, about 100 acres of pavement with Mao's mausoleum in the middle. Look for the huge pale rectangle directly south of the Forbidden City.

name: CCTV Headquarters
blurb: Rem Koolhaas's 768-ft loop: two leaning towers joined at the top by a cantilevered overhang, nicknamed 'big pants' by locals. Look for the angular dark-glass loop in the Central Business District.

name: Oriental Pearl Tower
blurb: At 1,535 ft it was China's tallest structure when it opened in 1994. Look for the pink spheres strung on a concrete tripod in Pudong, right across the Huangpu River bend from the Bund.

name: The Bund
blurb: A mile of 1920s and 1930s banks and trading houses on the west bank of the Huangpu, staring across at Pudong's towers. Look for the curving riverfront opposite the Oriental Pearl Tower.

name: Melbourne Park
blurb: Home of the Australian Open, with Rod Laver Arena's retractable roof at its center. Look for a cluster of round arenas and blue courts beside the Yarra and the rail yards.

name: Marvel Stadium
blurb: Melbourne's Docklands stadium, about 53,000 seats, with a roof that slides shut over the oval. Look for the big box on the west edge of downtown by the rail yards.

name: Albert Park Circuit
blurb: Melbourne's F1 track is public road for most of the year, looping around a lake in a city park about 2 miles from downtown. Look for the lake with the road ringing it.

name: Flemington Racecourse
blurb: Home of the Melbourne Cup since 1861, the race that stops a nation on the first Tuesday of November. Look for the pear-shaped track on a bend of the Maribyrnong River.

name: West Gate Bridge
blurb: A span collapsed during construction in 1970, killing 35 workers, the worst industrial accident in Australian history. It finally opened in 1978; look for the high deck over the Yarra and Melbourne's docks.

name: Port of Melbourne
blurb: Australia's busiest container port, at the mouth of the Yarra River. Look for the high West Gate Bridge arching over the docks.

name: Rangitoto Island
blurb: Auckland's youngest volcano, erupting out of the sea only about 600 years ago. Look for the near-perfect, symmetrical green cone in the harbor just off the city.

name: Aeroparque Jorge Newbery
blurb: A domestic and regional airport right on the Río de la Plata waterfront, a few miles from downtown. The runway runs along the shore of a river estuary so wide it looks like sea, and so brown it looks like coffee.

name: Monserrate
blurb: A peak of about 10,300 ft rising some 1,600 ft above Bogota, topped by a white church reached by cable car and funicular. Look for the church on the green summit right against the city's east side.

name: Cerro San Cristóbal
blurb: A hill rising roughly 1,000 ft above Santiago, topped by a white statue of the Virgin Mary and part of one of Latin America's largest urban parks. Look for the green ridge just north of the city center.

name: Cancún Hotel Zone
blurb: A barrier island shaped like the number 7, about 14 miles long, between the Caribbean and Nichupté Lagoon. Look for hotels lined along the 7 with turquoise water on one side and dark lagoon on the other.

name: Union Buildings
blurb: Seat of South Africa's government, finished in 1913 to a Herbert Baker design, where Nelson Mandela was inaugurated in 1994. Look for the sandstone crescent with twin domed towers above terraced gardens in Pretoria.

name: Voortrekker Monument
blurb: A 130-ft granite block from 1949 honoring the Afrikaner pioneers of the Great Trek; at noon each December 16 a sunbeam lands on the cenotaph inside. Look for the square monument on a hilltop south of Pretoria.

name: Robben Island
blurb: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison here, a few miles off Cape Town. Look for the flat, low island about 2 miles long in Table Bay, ringed by surf.

name: V&A Waterfront
blurb: Cape Town's working harbor turned shopping and hotel district, built around basins begun in 1860 when Queen Victoria's son Alfred tipped in the first load of stone. Look for the docks with Table Mountain rising behind.

name: Grand Egyptian Museum
blurb: The largest archaeological museum in the world devoted to a single civilization, fully opened in 2025 about a mile from the pyramids. Look for the huge triangular glass facade angled toward Giza.

name: Cairo Citadel
blurb: Saladin began this hilltop fortress in the 1170s, and it stayed Egypt's seat of government for nearly 700 years. Look for the domes and pencil minarets of the Muhammad Ali Mosque on the ridge above the city.

name: Chengdu Tianfu International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2021 about 30 miles southeast of Chengdu, one of the largest airports China has built from scratch. Look for three long runways laid across reshaped green hills.

name: Jeju International Airport
blurb: Jeju to Seoul is the busiest air route on Earth by number of flights. Look for Hallasan, a 6,388-ft volcano and South Korea's highest peak, rising from the middle of the island.

name: Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport
blurb: Built at the north end of Xiamen Island. Look for the runway running almost to the water, with bridges and tunnels linking the island city to the mainland and Kinmen, Taiwan-held, a few miles offshore.

name: Changsha Huanghua International Airport
blurb: Changsha's airport, east of the city on the Liuyang River. Look for the runway among red-earth hills, rice paddies and fields.

name: Fukuoka Airport
blurb: One of the world's most convenient airports, two subway stops from Fukuoka's main station. Height limits under the approach keep downtown low. Look for the runway pressed inside the city, with Hakata Bay beyond.

name: Nashville International Airport
blurb: Nashville's airport sits about 8 miles southeast of downtown. Look for the Cumberland River winding through town and Percy Priest Lake's long fingers just east of the runways.

name: Caracas Simón Bolívar International Airport
blurb: Sits on the Caribbean coast at Maiquetía, separated from Caracas by the mountain wall of El Ávila, over 7,000 ft high. Inside, the floor is a famous op-art mosaic by Carlos Cruz-Diez. Look for the sea on one side and mountains on the other.

name: Qingdao Liuting International Airport
blurb: Closed to airline flights in 2021, when Qingdao moved to the new Jiaodong airport, about 25 miles northwest of downtown. The old field sits near the northeast shore of Jiaozhou Bay, crossed by one of the world's longest sea bridges.

name: Sapporo New Chitose Airport
blurb: Hokkaido's gateway; its route to Tokyo is one of the busiest in the world. Look for two parallel runways on flat land between Sapporo and Tomakomai, right beside the runways of the Chitose air base.

name: Haikou Meilan International Airport
blurb: Haikou's airport, in the north of Hainan island across the strait from mainland China. Look for the runway among farmland and tropical trees southeast of the city.

name: Congonhas-São Paulo Airport
blurb: Sits in the middle of São Paulo, with approaches skimming over apartment towers. Its short runway was the scene of a 2007 crash in which an Airbus overran into a building, killing 199.

name: Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport
blurb: Actually in Kentucky, about 13 miles southwest of Cincinnati. It's Amazon Air's main hub and a big DHL hub too. Look for the parallel north-south runways and the Ohio River looping past to the north.

name: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport
blurb: Built on the former Bergstrom Air Force Base, which closed in the 1990s, and opened to airlines in 1999. Look for two parallel runways southeast of town and Austin's growing skyline along the Colorado River.

name: Guiyang Longdongbao International Airport
blurb: Guiyang's airport, on a high plateau of karst hills east of the city. Look for the runway cut into green cone-shaped limestone hills.

name: Naha Airport
blurb: Okinawa's main airport, sharing its runways with Japan's air force. A second runway, built offshore on reclaimed land, opened in 2020. Look for the parallel strips along the coast just south of Naha.

name: Surabaya Juanda International Airport
blurb: East Java's main airport, sharing its runway with an Indonesian navy air base. Look for it on the flat coastal plain south of Surabaya, among the fish ponds that line the shore of the Madura Strait.

name: Harbin Taiping International Airport
blurb: Harbin's airport, southwest of the city on the flat Songhua plain. Look for the runway among farmland, often white with snow in a city famous for its ice festival.

name: Pittsburgh International Airport
blurb: Its X-shaped airside terminal, opened in 1992, became a model for later airports. Look for the X among wooded hills about 15 miles west of downtown.

name: Jinan Yaoqiang International Airport
blurb: Serves Jinan, the City of Springs, from farmland northeast of town. Look for the Yellow River, brown with silt and held between long levees, running past the city on its way to the sea.

name: Sanya Phoenix International Airport
blurb: Gateway to China's tropical beach resorts, on the southern tip of Hainan. Look for the runway near the coast, with bays lined with hotels and green mountains inland.

name: Dalian Zhoushuizi International Airport
blurb: One of China's more cramped airports, hemmed inside Dalian on its peninsula. A replacement is being built offshore on an artificial island. Look for the runway threading the city between hills.

name: Portland International Airport
blurb: Its terminal roof, finished in 2024, is a huge wooden canopy built from Northwest timber. Look for the Columbia River right beside the runways and Mount Hood rising to the east.

name: Brasília International Airport
blurb: Brasília itself was laid out in the shape of an airplane, or a bird, in the 1950s. Look for the city's long curved wings and straight central axis beside an artificial lake, east of the runways.

name: Osaka Itami Airport
blurb: Osaka's original airport, deep in the northern suburbs and limited to domestic flights by noise rules. Look for runways surrounded on every side by dense housing, with planes landing low over rooftops.

name: Changchun Longjia International Airport
blurb: Serves Changchun, the center of China's car industry and home of carmaker FAW. Look for the runway on the flat farmland of the northeast plain, often snow-covered in winter.

name: Guadalajara International Airport
blurb: One of Mexico's busiest airports, south of Guadalajara. Look for Lake Chapala, the country's largest lake, spreading broad and shallow about 15 miles to the south.

name: Dallas Love Field
blurb: Southwest Airlines' home and headquarters, only about 6 miles from downtown Dallas. For decades the Wright Amendment limited where flights from here could go. Look for the downtown towers to the southeast.

name: Gimhae International Airport
blurb: Busan's airport sits on the flat Nakdong River delta west of the city and shares its runways with an air force base. Mountains crowd the approach, so pilots sometimes fly a tight circling turn to land.

name: Ningbo Lishe International Airport
blurb: Serves Ningbo, whose port with neighboring Zhoushan is among the busiest in the world by cargo tonnage. Look for flat, canal-laced farmland and the hills to the south.

name: Fuzhou Changle International Airport
blurb: Fuzhou's airport, near the coast at Changle, at the mouth of the Min River. Look for the runway between farmland and the sea, with fish farms in the shallow bays.

name: Nanning Wuxu International Airport
blurb: Nanning's airport, southwest of the capital of Guangxi. Look for the runway among sugarcane fields and low red-earth hills.

name: Raleigh–Durham International Airport
blurb: Serves Raleigh, Durham and Research Triangle Park, the big research campus next door. Look for the parallel runways among pine woods, with Umstead State Park's forest just to the east.

name: Lanzhou Zhongchuan International Airport
blurb: Far from the city it serves, roughly 40 miles north of Lanzhou. Look for the runways among bare, deeply eroded loess hills, yellow and gullied.

name: Taiyuan Wusu International Airport
blurb: Serves Taiyuan, capital of Shanxi, China's coal province, from the flat Fen River valley southeast of the city. Look for mountains walling the valley on both sides.

name: Nanchang Changbei International Airport
blurb: Jiangxi's main airport, north of Nanchang. Look for Poyang Lake, China's largest freshwater lake, to the northeast; it swells and shrinks hugely between the wet and dry seasons.

name: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport
blurb: Sits about 4 ft above sea level between Lake Pontchartrain and the Mississippi. A new terminal opened on the north side in 2019. Look for the lake's broad water to the north and the river curving to the south.

name: Makassar Sultan Hasanuddin International Airport
blurb: Gateway to Sulawesi and a key transfer point for eastern Indonesia, on flat land north of Makassar. Look for the runways among green rice paddies, with the Makassar Strait coast to the west.

name: Monterrey International Airport
blurb: Monterrey's airport, northeast of the city. Look for Cerro de la Silla, Saddle Mountain, with its notched double crest rising above the city to the south.

name: Cleveland Hopkins International Airport
blurb: Next door to NASA's Glenn Research Center, where aircraft engines and space propulsion are tested. Look for downtown Cleveland and the Lake Erie shore about 10 miles northeast.

name: Medellín José María Córdova International Airport
blurb: Sits at about 7,000 ft on a plateau at Rionegro, over a mountain ridge from Medellín, which lies in a valley below. Look for green rolling hills, farms and greenhouses around the runway.

name: Hohhot Baita International Airport
blurb: Inner Mongolia's main airport, east of the regional capital Hohhot on the edge of the grassland. Look for the runway on a flat plain, with the bare ridges of the Daqing Mountains to the north.

name: Wenzhou Longwan International Airport
blurb: Wenzhou's airport sits on the coastal flats at the mouth of the Ou River. Look for mudflats, fish ponds and the runway running along the edge of the East China Sea.

name: Zhuhai Jinwan Airport
blurb: Home of Airshow China, the country's biggest air show, held every two years. Look for the runway on the coast at Jinwan, with the islands of the Pearl River mouth offshore.

name: Hefei Xinqiao International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2013 in farmland northwest of Hefei, replacing a cramped airport inside the city. Look for the runway among flat fields and fish ponds of the Yangtze-Huai plain.

name: Tijuana International Airport
blurb: The runway runs right along the US-Mexico border fence. The Cross Border Xpress footbridge lets passengers walk from a terminal in San Diego straight into the airport. Look for the line of the wall beside the runway.

name: San Juan Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport
blurb: The Caribbean's busiest airport sits right behind the Isla Verde beach strip just east of San Juan. Look for the runway running parallel to the surf, with a row of hotels and a lagoon beside it.

name: Kaohsiung International Airport
blurb: Serves Kaohsiung, Taiwan's biggest port city, from the south side of town near the coast. Look for the busy harbor and container cranes just north and the Taiwan Strait to the west.

name: Shijiazhuang Zhengding International Airport
blurb: Shijiazhuang's airport, on the flat North China Plain northeast of the city. Look for the runway among endless wheat and corn fields.

name: Viracopos International Airport
blurb: Near Campinas, about 60 miles northwest of São Paulo, and a hub for Azul and for air cargo. Look for the single long runway surrounded by sugarcane and pasture.

name: Medina Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz Airport
blurb: Gateway for pilgrims to Medina, Islam's second-holiest city. Look for the black basalt lava fields and dark volcanic cones that ring the city on several sides.

name: Memphis International Airport
blurb: Home of the FedEx global hub, one of the world's busiest cargo airports. Most of the action comes overnight, when purple-tailed jets land in waves for the sort; look for rows of them on the ramps.

name: John Wayne Airport
blurb: Known for its noise-abatement departures: jets climb steeply, then throttle back over Newport Beach. The main runway is only about 5,700 ft long. Look for the airport hemmed in by Irvine office parks and the Newport Back Bay.

name: Chiang Mai International Airport
blurb: Only about 3 miles from Chiang Mai's moated old city. Look for the square moat and Doi Suthep mountain to the west, with its gold-spired temple on the slope.

name: Belo Horizonte Confins International Airport
blurb: Belo Horizonte's main airport, about 25 miles north of the city on a plateau. Look for the runway among red-earth hills and the scrubby cerrado typical of Minas Gerais.

name: Wuxi Shuofang Airport
blurb: Shared with a military base, it serves both Wuxi and nearby Suzhou. Look for Lake Tai, one of China's largest freshwater lakes, spreading to the southwest.

name: Indianapolis International Airport
blurb: Its arched glass midfield terminal opened in 2008 between the parallel runways. Look for it, and nearby one of FedEx's biggest hubs, with rows of purple-tailed jets.

name: Yinchuan Hedong International Airport
blurb: Ningxia's airport, east of Yinchuan across the Yellow River. Look for the river's broad channel, green irrigated fields, and the Helan Mountains forming a wall against the desert to the west.

name: Southwest Florida International Airport
blurb: Fort Myers' airport, built in pine flatwoods and wetlands east of the city. Look for the runway among green swamp, canals and the long straight lines of Florida's new subdivisions.

name: Santos Dumont Airport
blurb: Squeezed onto landfill at the edge of downtown Rio, its short runway ends in Guanabara Bay. Approaches swing right past Sugarloaf Mountain, one of the most scenic landings anywhere.

name: Yantai Penglai International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2015 to replace Yantai's old city airport, near Penglai on the tip of the Shandong peninsula. Look for the Bohai Strait coast and patchwork fruit orchards on the low hills.

name: Medan Kualanamu International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2013 to replace Medan's old Polonia airport, which sat in the middle of the city. It lies about 25 miles east of Medan; look for the long runway among oil-palm plantations on the coastal plain.

name: Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport
blurb: Milwaukee's airport sits about a mile from the Lake Michigan shore. Look for the long blue edge of the lake to the east and the city's grid running north to downtown.

name: Seville Airport
blurb: Serves Seville from the flat Guadalquivir valley northeast of the city, one of the hottest parts of Europe in summer. Look for the river and the grid of olive groves and farm plots around it.

name: Kota Kinabalu International Airport
blurb: Gateway to Sabah and Mount Kinabalu, Borneo's highest peak at about 13,435 ft. Look for the runway along the South China Sea coast, with the mountain rising inland to the northeast.

name: Salvador International Airport
blurb: Salvador's airport, set among dunes and Atlantic coastal forest north of the city, with an access road famous for its tunnel of arching bamboo. Look for the runways between green forest and the white sand coast.

name: Punta Cana International Airport
blurb: The Caribbean's resort gateway, with terminals roofed in thatched palm fronds. Look for the runway near the coast lined with all-inclusive resorts and white sand beaches.

name: John Glenn Columbus International Airport
blurb: Named for John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth and an Ohio native. Look for downtown Columbus about 6 miles west and Ohio State's horseshoe stadium to the northwest.

name: Recife International Airport
blurb: Close to Recife's beaches at Boa Viagem. Look for the wall of towers along the shore and the offshore reef that gave the city its name.

name: Guilin Liangjiang International Airport
blurb: Approaches pass over some of China's most famous scenery: karst towers rising out of flat farmland along the Li River. Look for the green limestone peaks scattered across the plain.

name: President Donald J. Trump International Airport
blurb: Serves the Palm Beaches, close enough that Mar-a-Lago sits under some of its approach paths. Look for the runway just west of the Intracoastal Waterway and the barrier island beach.

name: Lampung Radin Inten II Airport
blurb: The airport for Bandar Lampung, on Sumatra's southern tip just across the Sunda Strait from Java. Look for the runway among farmland and plantations north of the city.

name: Kahului Airport
blurb: Sits on the isthmus between Haleakalā and the West Maui Mountains. Look for the runway on the north shore, with Haleakalā's huge slope rising to 10,023 ft to the southeast.

name: Quanzhou Jinjiang Airport
blurb: Serves Quanzhou, an ancient Maritime Silk Road port, and shares its runway with military aircraft. Look for the dense factory towns of Jinjiang around the field.

name: Yogyakarta Adisucipto Airport
blurb: Shares its runway with Indonesia's air force academy and sits in Yogyakarta's eastern suburbs. Since 2020 most flights have moved to the new Yogyakarta International on the coast; look for the runway hemmed in by city.

name: Porto Alegre International Airport
blurb: The catastrophic 2024 floods in Rio Grande do Sul put the runway underwater and closed the airport for about five months. Look for the wide Guaíba estuary and the vast Lagoa dos Patos to the south.

name: Penang International Airport
blurb: On the southeast corner of Penang Island. Look for the two long Penang Bridges spanning the strait to the mainland, and George Town's old harbor to the north.

name: Yekaterinburg Koltsovo Airport
blurb: Serves Yekaterinburg just east of the low Ural Mountains, which mark the boundary between Europe and Asia. Look for dark birch and pine forest and lakes around the city.

name: Wanzhou Wuqiao Airport
blurb: Built on a leveled hilltop above Wanzhou, a river city on the Three Gorges Reservoir. Look for the runway on a flattened ridge, with the wide Yangtze winding through steep hills below.

name: Bari Karol Wojtyła Airport
blurb: Puglia's main airport, named for Pope John Paul II, near the Adriatic shore north of Bari. Look for the olive groves that stretch inland in neat rows across one of Italy's biggest olive-oil regions.

name: Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport
blurb: Bordeaux's airport, on the city's western edge, home to Dassault and other aerospace plants. Look for the runways among pine woods, with vineyards of the Médoc and Graves country close by.

name: Balikpapan Sepinggan International Airport
blurb: Serves the oil city of Balikpapan and Nusantara, the new Indonesian capital being built inland. Look for the runway running right along the Makassar Strait shore on Borneo's east coast.

name: Macau International Airport
blurb: Its runway sits offshore on reclaimed land off Taipa, linked to the terminal by taxiway bridges. Look for the strip lying in the water, with the Cotai casino strip just to the west.

name: Lijiang Sanyi Airport
blurb: The gateway to Lijiang's old town, at over 7,000 ft on a plateau. On a clear day look for Jade Dragon Snow Mountain's glaciated peaks rising to the north.

name: Los Cabos International Airport
blurb: The gateway to Cabo, set in desert scrub between San José del Cabo and the mountains of the Sierra de la Laguna. Look for the runway in brown desert a few miles inland from the Sea of Cortez.

name: Jacksonville International Airport
blurb: Jacksonville's airport, in pine forest well north of downtown. Look for the runways cut into dark woods and marshland, with the wide St. Johns River off to the east.

name: Jakarta Halim Perdanakusuma Airport
blurb: Jakarta's international airport until Soekarno-Hatta opened in 1985, and still an air force base with VIP and some domestic flights. Look for its runway inside the dense sprawl of East Jakarta.

name: Bradley International Airport
blurb: Serves Hartford and Springfield, in the Connecticut River valley where shade tobacco is grown under cloth. Look for the New England Air Museum next to the field and the white tobacco netting nearby.

name: Jieyang Chaoshan International Airport
blurb: Serves the Chaoshan region of eastern Guangdong, Shantou, Chaozhou and Jieyang. Look for the runway among flat rice fields and river channels inland from the coast.

name: Curitiba Afonso Pena International Airport
blurb: Curitiba's airport, in São José dos Pinhais just southeast of the city. Look for the plateau dotted with umbrella-shaped araucaria pines and the city's many parks.

name: Nantes Atlantique Airport
blurb: Nantes' airport, just southwest of the city. Look for the runway near Lake Grand-Lieu, a big shallow lake and nature reserve, among fields and hedgerows.

name: Xining Caojiabao Airport
blurb: Serves Xining on the northeast edge of the Tibetan Plateau at about 7,000 ft, high enough that planes need longer takeoff runs. Look for terraced brown loess hills; Qinghai Lake lies farther west.

name: Fortaleza Airport
blurb: Fortaleza's airport, a few miles inland from the Atlantic in northeast Brazil. Look for the runway inside the sprawling city, with white dunes and the coast just to the north and east.

name: Cali International Airport
blurb: Cali's airport, at Palmira in the wide Cauca Valley. Look for the runway surrounded by sugarcane fields stretching to the Andes ranges on both sides of the valley.

name: Ontario International Airport
blurb: In the heart of the Inland Empire, a huge regional hub for cargo. Look for the long parallel runways surrounded by acres of white-roofed warehouses, with the San Gabriel Mountains rising behind.

name: Palermo Falcone–Borsellino Airport
blurb: Named for the two anti-Mafia judges killed in 1992; the bomb that killed Falcone went off on the airport highway. Look for the runway squeezed between steep limestone mountains and the sea.

name: Cartagena Rafael Núñez International Airport
blurb: The runway runs right along the Caribbean shore, a short way from Cartagena's walled colonial old city. Look for the beach, the lagoon beside the airport and the high-rises of Bocagrande to the south.

name: Mexico City Felipe Ángeles International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2022 on the Santa Lucía air base, about 30 miles north of Mexico City. Construction dug up the bones of more than 200 mammoths, now shown in an on-site museum. Look for the runways on the dry plain of the Valley of Mexico.

name: Bilbao Airport
blurb: The terminal, by Santiago Calatrava, is nicknamed La Paloma (the dove) for its white winged roof. Bilbao is also home to the titanium-clad Guggenheim; look for the green hills folding down to the estuary.

name: Fuerteventura Airport
blurb: Its runway runs right along the beach on Fuerteventura's east coast, the Canaries island closest to Africa. Look for bare brown volcanic hills and, to the north, the white dunes of Corralejo.

name: Reno–Tahoe International Airport
blurb: In a high desert valley at about 4,400 ft under the Sierra Nevada. Look for downtown's casinos just north and the deep blue of Lake Tahoe over the mountains to the southwest.

name: Albuquerque International Sunport
blurb: At about 5,350 ft, the Sunport shares its runways with Kirtland Air Force Base. Look for the long ridge of the Sandia Mountains east of the city and the green ribbon of the Rio Grande to the west.

name: Puerto Vallarta International Airport
blurb: Serves the resort coast on Banderas Bay, one of the largest bays in Mexico. Look for the runway near the shore, the marina and cruise piers just south, and the jungle-covered Sierra Madre behind.

name: Bergen Airport
blurb: Norway's second-busiest airport, south of Bergen, one of Europe's rainiest cities. Look for fjords and islands to the west and Bergen's harbor among its seven mountains to the north.

name: Hang Nadim International Airport
blurb: Its runway, over 13,000 ft, is one of Indonesia's longest, built for an industrial island across the strait from Singapore. Look for the very long strip on Batam's northeast side among green hills.

name: Gold Coast Airport
blurb: Its runway straddles the Queensland and New South Wales border at Coolangatta. Look for Gold Coast towers marching north along the beaches and the Tweed River winding just south.

name: San José Juan Santamaría International Airport
blurb: Costa Rica's main airport, in the Central Valley at Alajuela. Look for coffee country on the slopes around it and volcanoes, including Poás, rising to the north.

name: Wellington Airport
blurb: Notorious for gusty landings: a short runway across a narrow isthmus with sea at both ends. Look for Lyall Bay's surf beach at the south end and the city's harbor just north.

name: Marrakesh Menara Airport
blurb: Close to Marrakesh's walled medina, with a terminal clad in a big geometric diamond pattern. Look for the snowy peaks of the High Atlas rising about 40 miles south.

name: Kagoshima Airport
blurb: Sits on a plateau north of Kagoshima, near the Kirishima volcanoes. Look for Sakurajima, the volcano in Kagoshima Bay that erupts often, puffing ash to the south.

name: Phnom Penh International Airport
blurb: Phnom Penh's longtime airport, on the western edge of the city. Look for the runway among rice fields and spreading suburbs, with the Mekong and Tonle Sap meeting downtown to the east.

name: Hollywood Burbank Airport
blurb: Next to the site of Lockheed's old Burbank plant, birthplace of the Skunk Works. Look for the two crossing runways tucked against the Verdugo Mountains, with the San Fernando Valley grid spreading west.

name: Guayaquil José Joaquín de Olmedo Airport
blurb: Guayaquil's airport, only a few miles from downtown, beside the wide brown Guayas River. Look for the runway in the middle of the city, with mangrove estuaries spreading to the south.

name: Kuching International Airport
blurb: Serves Kuching, Sarawak's capital on Borneo. Look for the Sarawak River winding through the city to the north, past the gold umbrella roof of the state assembly building.

name: Rhode Island T. F. Green International Airport
blurb: In Warwick about 6 miles south of Providence, close to the head of Narragansett Bay. Look for the bay's coves and inlets to the east and Providence's small downtown to the north.

name: Lucknow Chaudhary Charan Singh Airport
blurb: Serves Lucknow, capital of Uttar Pradesh, from the southern edge of the city. Look for the flat Ganges plain stretching out in every direction, with the Gomti River winding through the city.

name: Semarang Ahmad Yani International Airport
blurb: Central Java's coastal airport, west of Semarang, a city where the ground is sinking several inches a year. Look for the runway on low flats by the Java Sea, ringed by fish ponds.

name: Dalaman Airport
blurb: Gateway to resorts like Fethiye and Marmaris on Turkey's southwest coast. Look for the Dalaman River delta's farmland and lagoons and the pine-covered mountains dropping to the sea.

name: Adana Şakirpaşa Airport
blurb: Adana's city-center airport, flying since the 1930s, lost its airline flights in 2024 when the new Çukurova airport opened to the southwest. Look for the Seyhan River and its dam lake north of the city.

name: Newcastle International Airport
blurb: Northwest of Newcastle, close to Ponteland. Look for the River Tyne and its cluster of bridges in the city, and the Northumberland hills rolling north.

name: East Midlands Airport
blurb: Between Derby, Nottingham and Leicester, it is one of the UK's busiest cargo airports, with a large DHL hub. Look for the M1 motorway running past and the River Trent valley to the north.

name: Quito Mariscal Sucre International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2013 on the Tababela plateau to replace Quito's old airport inside the city. Look for deep river canyons around the runway and, on a clear day, snowcapped volcanoes such as Cotopaxi to the south.

name: Abuja Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport
blurb: Serves Abuja, Nigeria's purpose-built capital since 1991. Look for Aso Rock, a giant granite monolith above the government district, about 20 miles to the northeast.

name: Durban King Shaka International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2010 in time for the football World Cup, replacing Durban's old airport south of the city. Look for green sugarcane fields rolling right up to the runway and the Indian Ocean surf just east.

name: Xishuangbanna Gasa International Airport
blurb: China's tropical southwest corner, near the Mekong and the borders of Laos and Myanmar. Look for the runway above the city of Jinghong among rubber plantations on the hills.

name: Buffalo Niagara International Airport
blurb: Buffalo's airport, east of the city near the end of Lake Erie. Look for the lake and downtown to the west, and Niagara Falls about 20 miles northwest.

name: Çukurova International Airport
blurb: Opened in 2024 between Adana and Mersin near Tarsus, the birthplace of St. Paul, replacing Adana's crowded city airport. Look for the flat, fertile Çukurova plain, among Turkey's main cotton and citrus regions.

name: Jaipur International Airport
blurb: Gateway to the Pink City, set at Sanganer on the dry plains south of Jaipur. Look north for the rocky Aravalli ridges that carry the city's old forts and walls.

name: Charleston International Airport
blurb: Shares its runways with Joint Base Charleston, home to big C-17 cargo jets, and Boeing builds 787 Dreamliners on the field. Look for the huge white Boeing assembly halls on the north side.

name: Santo Domingo Las Américas International Airport
blurb: Santo Domingo's main airport, on the Caribbean coast east of the city. Look for the runway right along the shore, with the bright blue sea on one side and green farmland on the other.

name: Montego Bay Sangster International Airport
blurb: Jamaica's busiest airport, where most of the island's tourists arrive. The runway runs along the shore, so approaches skim turquoise water. Look for Montego Bay's hotel strip just to the south.

name: Cagliari Elmas Airport
blurb: Sardinia's main airport, beside the Santa Gilla lagoon west of Cagliari, where flamingos feed. Look for the lagoon's salt pans and wetlands right along the runway, with the city on its hill to the east.

name: Boise Airport
blurb: Boise's airport, south of the city, also home to the Idaho Air National Guard. Look for the runways on sagebrush plain, with the foothills rising north of the city.

name: Palembang Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II Airport
blurb: South Sumatra's airport, north of Palembang, the river city on the Musi. It handled athletes for the 2018 Asian Games, co-hosted with Jakarta. Look for the runway amid green plantation land.

name: Omaha Eppley Airfield
blurb: Sits on a bend of the Missouri River. Beside it, Carter Lake is a piece of Iowa stranded on the Nebraska side after the river jumped course in 1877. Look for the oxbow lake and downtown about 3 miles southwest.

name: Krasnodar International Airport
blurb: Southern Russia's farm-belt hub, closed to civil flights since 2022 because of the war in Ukraine. Look for the Kuban River winding past Krasnodar among some of Russia's richest black-earth fields.

name: Kaliningrad Khrabrovo Airport
blurb: Russia's airport in its Baltic exclave, cut off from the rest of the country by Lithuania and Poland. Look for the runway north of Kaliningrad, with the dunes of the Curonian Spit to the northeast.

name: Moscow Kremlin
blurb: A walled triangle about 1.4 miles around with 20 towers on the Moskva River. Look for the red brick walls beside Red Square and the colorful domes of St. Basil's at its corner.

name: Mount Tamalpais
blurb: Only 2,571 ft, but it rises almost straight from the ocean north of the Golden Gate, and its fire roads are where mountain biking was born in the 1970s. Look for a long ridge with a sharp east peak above Marin's fog.

name: Mount Diablo
blurb: At 3,849 ft it stands alone above the East Bay, and on a clear day you can see an enormous sweep of Northern California from the top, all the way to the Sierra. Look for a twin-summited peak, green in winter and gold in summer.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain
blurb: A bare granite dome about 1,300 ft high standing at the mouth of Guanabara Bay, with a cable car to the top since 1912. Look for the gray thumb of rock beside the crescent of Botafogo beach.

name: Krakatoa
blurb: Its 1883 eruption was heard nearly 3,000 miles away, and its tsunamis killed over 36,000 people. Look for the broken ring of islands in the Sunda Strait around Anak Krakatau, the child volcano that rose in 1927.

name: Mount Bromo and the Tengger Caldera
blurb: A smoking crater inside the Tengger caldera, whose floor is a sea of volcanic sand about 20 square miles in area. Look for the gray sand plain, several nested cones, and Semeru smoking in the distance.

name: Kata Tjuta
blurb: A cluster of 36 domed rocks whose tallest, Mount Olga, stands about 1,800 ft above the plain, taller than nearby Uluru. Look for a knot of rounded red humps with narrow green gorges between them.

name: Richat Structure
blurb: The Eye of the Sahara: about 25 miles of concentric rock rings, visible from cruise. Long taken for an impact crater, it's an eroded dome. Look for the bullseye in flat desert.

name: Okavango Delta
blurb: A river delta that never reaches the sea: the Okavango spreads into thousands of square miles of channels and islands in the Kalahari and evaporates. Look for a green fan of waterways in dry red sand.

name: Caspian Sea
blurb: The largest lake on Earth, about 143,000 square miles, bigger than Germany. Its surface sits about 90 ft below sea level. Look for the Absheron Peninsula poking into it, with oil platforms off the coast.

name: Chesapeake Bay
blurb: The largest estuary in the US, about 200 miles long, fed by more than 150 rivers. Look for the 17-mile Bay Bridge-Tunnel crossing its mouth, a thread of road that disappears into the water twice.

name: Glacier Bay
blurb: When George Vancouver sailed past in 1794 this bay was a wall of ice; the glaciers have since retreated more than 60 miles. Look for long fjord arms with tidewater glaciers at their heads.

name: Taal Volcano
blurb: An island volcano inside a lake that fills an ancient caldera, about 40 miles south of Manila. Its 2020 eruption blanketed nearby towns in ash; look for Volcano Island in the middle of Taal Lake and the crater ridge of Tagaytay above it.

name: Mount Kailash
blurb: Sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Bon, about 21,800 ft and never climbed. Pilgrims walk a 32-mile circuit around its base; look for the dark pyramid with a vertical gash on its south face.

name: Taklamakan Desert
blurb: One of the largest shifting-sand deserts on Earth, ringed by mountains on three sides. A highway crosses it lined with irrigated shrubs; look for a thin green thread through endless dunes.

name: Mekong Delta
blurb: The Mekong ends its 2,700-mile run here, splitting into channels the Vietnamese call the Nine Dragons. Look for brown rivers fanning toward the sea through a dense patchwork of rice paddies and canals.

name: Twelve Apostles
blurb: Limestone stacks rising up to about 150 ft out of the Southern Ocean beside the Great Ocean Road. There were never twelve, and waves keep knocking them down; one collapsed in 2005. Look for pale pillars standing off golden cliffs.

name: Whitsunday Islands
blurb: 74 islands off Queensland, and Whitehaven Beach has silica sand so white it squeaks. Look for the swirling white and turquoise patterns at Hill Inlet.

name: K'gari (Fraser Island)
blurb: The world's largest sand island, about 75 miles long, with freshwater lakes perched in its dunes. Look for a long, sandy island with bright blue lakes and white beaches.

name: Whakaari / White Island
blurb: New Zealand's most active volcano, an island 30 miles offshore in the Bay of Plenty; a 2019 eruption killed 22 people visiting the crater. Look for a steam plume rising from a bare gray island.

name: Lake Wānaka
blurb: A glacier-carved lake below the Southern Alps, with a small resort town at its southern end. Look for a long, deep blue lake framed by bare golden hills and snowy peaks rising to Mount Aspiring.

name: Nile Delta
blurb: The fan of farmland where the Nile splits into two branches before reaching the Mediterranean, home to tens of millions of people. Look for the sharp edge where intensely green fields meet tan desert.

name: Angel Falls
blurb: The world's highest waterfall at about 3,200 ft, nearly 20 times the drop of Niagara, pouring off the flat top of Auyán-tepui. It is named for Jimmie Angel, a US pilot who flew over it in 1933.

name: Atacama Desert
blurb: The driest nonpolar desert on Earth; some weather stations here have never recorded rain. Look for bare brown and white ground with no vegetation at all, and giant open-pit copper mines.

name: Fitz Roy
blurb: An 11,171-ft granite spire above El Chaltén, named for the Beagle's captain. The Tehuelche called it Chaltén, smoking mountain, for the cloud plume that usually streams off the top. Look for a sheer gray tooth among ice fields.

name: Maldives Atolls
blurb: More than 1,000 coral islands in 26 atolls, with an average elevation of about 5 ft, the lowest country on Earth. Look for turquoise rings scattered across deep blue ocean like spilled pearls.

name: Shark Bay
blurb: A UNESCO site holding the world's best-known living stromatolites, rocklike mats of microbes like those that put the first oxygen in the air. Look for two long peninsulas, turquoise shallows and huge pale seagrass banks.

name: Osaka Castle
blurb: Toyotomi Hideyoshi built the original in the 1580s; the current main tower is a 1931 concrete rebuild. Look for the white and green tower on its stone base inside broad moats in a large park.

name: Daisenryō Kofun (Nintoku tomb)
blurb: Japan's largest burial mound, about 1,600 ft long, built for a 5th-century emperor. Look for the keyhole-shaped wooded mound wrapped in moats in the middle of Sakai's suburbs.

name: Sapporo Dome
blurb: A dome with a soccer pitch that slides in and out on a cushion of air, so the grass can grow outside. Look for the silver shell and the pitch parked beside it in Sapporo's southeast.

name: Moerenuma Park
blurb: A former garbage dump turned into a park designed by sculptor Isamu Noguchi, with a stepped earth pyramid and a glass pyramid. Look for the round park wrapped by a river loop on Sapporo's northeast edge.

name: Okurayama Ski Jump
blurb: The ski jump used for the 1972 Sapporo Winter Olympics, on the mountainside above the city. Look for the long white ramp cut straight down the forested slope.

name: ES CON Field Hokkaido
blurb: Home of the Fighters since 2023, a retractable-roof ballpark with real grass and a huge glass outfield wall. Look for the sloped roof amid fields in Kitahiroshima.

name: Kadena Air Base
blurb: Often called the largest and busiest US Air Force base in the Pacific, filling a big part of central Okinawa. Look for two long parallel runways, with the town of Kadena pressed against the fence.

name: Gwangan Bridge
blurb: A double-deck suspension bridge about 4.6 miles long, curving across the bay in front of Gwangalli Beach. At night it runs a color light show; look for the arc of light against the dark sea.

name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
blurb: Sunrise Peak, a tuff cone that erupted from the sea about 5,000 years ago and is now joined to Jeju by a strip of land. Look for a green bowl with a perfectly round crater on Jeju's eastern tip.

name: New Century Global Center
blurb: Billed as the world's largest building by floor area when it opened in 2013, with an indoor water park and artificial beach inside. Look for the long block with a wavy glass roof in southern Chengdu.

name: Raffles City Chongqing
blurb: Eight towers on the point where the Jialing meets the Yangtze, four of them joined near the top by a horizontal glass 'skyscraper' nearly 1,000 ft long. Look for the glass bar lying across the towers.

name: Xi'an City Wall
blurb: A Ming-dynasty wall about 8.5 miles around, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. Look for the rectangle with moat around the city center.

name: Terracotta Army
blurb: Some 8,000 clay soldiers buried around 210 BC to guard China's first emperor, found in 1974 by farmers digging a well. Look for the big arched hangars over the pits east of Xi'an.

name: West Lake (Hangzhou)
blurb: Celebrated in Chinese poetry and painting for more than a thousand years and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Look for the long Su and Bai causeways crossing the water, with Hangzhou's towers right up against the east shore.

name: Hangzhou Olympic Sports Center Stadium
blurb: The 80,000-seat 'Big Lotus,' built for the 2022 Asian Games, its roof made of curved petal shapes. Look for the white flower-shaped bowl on the south bank of the Qiantang River.

name: Philippine Arena
blurb: The world's largest indoor arena, about 55,000 seats, built by the Iglesia ni Cristo church and opened in 2014. Look for the enormous gray dome in rural Bocaue, north of Manila.

name: Intramuros
blurb: The walled Spanish city of Manila, begun in the late 1500s and covering about 160 acres. Look for the wall line and the golf course laid in the old moat beside the Pasig River.

name: National Monument (Monas)
blurb: A 433-ft obelisk in the middle of Merdeka Square, topped with a flame covered in gold leaf. Look for the white tower centered in the huge square park.

name: Istiqlal Mosque
blurb: The largest mosque in Southeast Asia, built across the street from Jakarta's Catholic cathedral. Look for the big white dome and single minaret just northeast of the Monas obelisk.

name: Long Biên Bridge
blurb: A cantilever bridge built by the French and opened in 1903 over the Red River, bombed repeatedly in the Vietnam War and patched ever since. Look for the long rusty truss beside newer road bridges.

name: Diriyah (At-Turaif)
blurb: The mud-brick capital of the first Saudi state, destroyed by Ottoman-Egyptian forces in 1818. Look for tan ruins on the bluff above Wadi Hanifa.

name: King Fahd's Fountain
blurb: The tallest fountain in the world, shooting up to about 1,000 ft above the Red Sea off Jeddah. Look for the white plume off the corniche.

name: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
blurb: One of the fastest street circuits ever built, with 27 corners squeezed along the Red Sea waterfront. Look for the long thin course hugging the shoreline north of the city center.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
blurb: One of the largest mosques in the world, with 82 white marble domes and one of the largest hand-knotted carpets ever made. Look for the white domes and four minarets on the mainland side of the bridges into Abu Dhabi.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
