blurb: Jean Nouvel's museum, opened in 2017 under a lattice dome about 590 ft across that scatters sunlight like palm fronds. Look for the flat silver dome floating over the water on Saadiyat Island.

name: Emirates Palace
blurb: A palace hotel opened in 2005, with more than 100 domes and its own long private beach. Look for the sand-colored building with a big central dome at the western tip of Abu Dhabi island.

name: Dome of the Rock
blurb: Finished in 691, the oldest surviving major Islamic monument. Look for the golden dome on the big stone platform in Jerusalem's Old City.

name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour
blurb: One of the tallest Orthodox churches in the world. Stalin blew up the original in 1931; the site became an open-air swimming pool before the church was rebuilt in the 1990s. Look for gold domes on the river.

name: VDNKh
blurb: A vast Soviet exhibition park of ornate pavilions and gilded fountains, opened in 1939. Look for the long axis of fountains near the 1,772-ft Ostankino TV tower.

name: Peter and Paul Fortress
blurb: Its founding in 1703 marks the birth of St. Petersburg, and its cathedral's gold spire rises about 400 ft. Look for the six-bastioned fortress on its island in the Neva, with the needle spire in the middle.

name: Winter Palace (Hermitage)
blurb: The tsars' green-and-white winter home, now part of the Hermitage, one of the largest art museums in the world. Look for the long green building on the Neva facing Palace Square and the Alexander Column.

name: Peterhof Palace
blurb: Peter the Great's seaside palace, whose Grand Cascade fountains run without pumps, fed by gravity from springs uphill. Look for the gold-trimmed palace above a canal running straight to the Gulf of Finland.

name: Saint Isaac's Cathedral
blurb: Its gilded dome, covered with about 220 pounds of gold, is among the largest of any cathedral in the world. Look for the bright gold dome rising over the center of St. Petersburg.

name: Budapest
blurb: The Danube splits hilly Buda from flat Pest. Look for the neo-Gothic Parliament on the Pest bank, Castle Hill opposite, and long Margaret Island in midstream. At night the bridges are lit like strings of pearls.

name: Hungarian Parliament Building
blurb: The largest building in Hungary, a Gothic Revival parliament stretching about 880 ft along the Danube. Look for the red dome and white spires on the Pest bank.

name: Buda Castle
blurb: The royal palace on Castle Hill above the Danube, rebuilt several times after sieges and wars. Look for the long domed palace on the hill, facing Parliament across the river.

name: Atomium
blurb: Built for the 1958 World's Fair, a 335-ft model of an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times. Look for nine shiny steel spheres in a cube shape near the Heysel exhibition grounds in north Brussels.

name: Palais de Justice (Brussels)
blurb: When finished in 1883 it was the largest building constructed in the 19th century, bigger than St. Peter's in Rome. Look for its huge dome above the Marolles, wrapped in scaffolding that has stood for decades.

name: Jet d'Eau
blurb: A fountain that throws lake water about 460 ft into the air at over 120 mph. Look for the white plume, often bent by the wind, at the end of Lake Geneva where it narrows into the city.

name: Palace of Nations
blurb: Built in the 1930s for the League of Nations and the UN's European headquarters since 1946. Look for the long pale stone wings in a park sloping down to Lake Geneva.

name: Milan Cathedral
blurb: It took nearly six centuries to finish, with 135 spires and a gilded Madonna on top. Look for the white marble roof bristling with spires on the big square at the center of Milan.

name: San Siro
blurb: Shared by Inter and AC Milan, about 75,000 seats. Look for the red roof girders and the 11 round spiral ramp towers around the bowl, the shape everyone in Milan knows.

name: Monaco
blurb: The world's second-smallest country, about 0.8 square miles, almost all of it built over. Look for superyachts packed into Port Hercule and the Formula 1 street circuit winding along the harbor.

name: Port Hercule
blurb: Monaco's harbor, ringed by the Grand Prix circuit. Look for superyachts packed into the basin below the Rock of Monaco, with the swimming pool chicane on the waterfront.

name: Reichstag Building
blurb: Germany's parliament building, burned in 1933 and topped with a new glass dome in 1999. Look for the glass dome on the square stone building at the edge of the Tiergarten, just north of the Brandenburg Gate.

name: Olympiastadion Berlin
blurb: Built for the 1936 Olympics and host of the 2006 World Cup final. Its track is blue, matching Hertha BSC. Look for the oval sunk into the ground with a gap at the west end facing the bell tower.

name: Teufelsberg
blurb: A hill built from the rubble of bombed Berlin, rising about 260 ft, topped by an abandoned Cold War listening station. Look for the white radar domes poking out of the Grunewald forest.

name: Tropical Islands
blurb: An indoor rainforest resort inside a former airship hangar south of Berlin, one of the largest free-standing halls in the world. Look for the huge silver half-cylinder on an old Soviet airfield.

name: Elbphilharmonie
blurb: A glass concert hall with a wave-shaped roof, set on top of an old brick warehouse at the tip of a harbor peninsula. It opened in 2017, years late and far over budget. Look for the wavy roof on the Elbe.

name: Port of Hamburg
blurb: Germany's largest port, some 70 miles up the Elbe from the North Sea. Look for container terminals across the river from the city and the wave-roofed Elbphilharmonie concert hall on the old harbor.

name: Köhlbrand Bridge
blurb: A 1974 cable-stayed bridge that climbs high over Hamburg's port, planned for replacement as ships outgrew it. Look for its long ramps arching over container terminals and the Elbe channel.

name: Cologne Cathedral
blurb: Its twin spires reach 515 ft. Begun in 1248 and finished in 1880, it was briefly the tallest building in the world. Look for the dark spires right beside the main train station and the Rhine bridge.

name: Garzweiler Mine
blurb: An open-pit lignite mine so large that whole villages have been moved out of its path, worked by giant bucket-wheel excavators. Look for a vast terraced pit of brown earth west of Cologne.

name: Hambach Mine
blurb: Germany's deepest open pit, more than 1,300 ft deep, where some of the world's largest land machines dig lignite. Look for the huge gray-brown crater west of Cologne, with the remnant Hambach Forest on its edge.

name: National Congress of Brazil
blurb: Oscar Niemeyer's parliament: twin towers flanked by an upturned bowl for the Chamber and a dome for the Senate. Look for the H-shaped towers at the end of the Monumental Axis, the nose of the airplane-shaped city plan.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
blurb: Oscar Niemeyer's cathedral: 16 curved concrete columns rising like hands reaching skyward, with glass between them. Look for the round crown shape beside the Esplanade of Ministries.

name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
blurb: I.M. Pei's glass pyramid on the Lake Erie shore in downtown Cleveland, opened in 1995. Look for the glass tent on the waterfront next to the football stadium.

name: Progressive Field
blurb: The Cleveland Guardians' ballpark, opened in 1994 at the edge of downtown. Look for the white steel light towers and exposed framing next to the Cavaliers' arena.

name: Smoothie King Center
blurb: Home of the Pelicans, tucked right beside the Superdome. Look for the smaller round arena in the dome's shadow in downtown New Orleans.

name: Crescent City Connection
blurb: Twin cantilever bridges crossing the Mississippi between downtown New Orleans and the West Bank. Look for their gray steel trusses over the river's tight bend by the French Quarter.

name: Great American Ball Park
blurb: The Cincinnati Reds' home on the Ohio River, opened in 2003. Look for the riverfront ballpark next to the Bengals' stadium, with Kentucky across the river.

name: Kings Island
blurb: Near Cincinnati, famous for its scale replica Eiffel Tower. Look for the tower at the head of a fountain-lined mall, coaster tracks behind it.

name: TQL Stadium
blurb: FC Cincinnati's soccer stadium, opened in 2021 in the West End. Look for the glowing white fin-like facade around a compact rectangular bowl.

name: Gainbridge Fieldhouse
blurb: Home of the Pacers and the Fever, built to look like an old Indiana high school gym. Look for the brick arena with an arched roof a few blocks northeast of Lucas Oil Stadium.

name: Nationwide Arena
blurb: The Columbus Blue Jackets' arena in the Arena District, opened in 2000. Look for it at the north edge of downtown beside the MLS stadium.

name: Lower.com Field
blurb: Columbus Crew's soccer stadium, opened in 2021 in the Arena District. Look for the compact bowl near the hockey arena and the rail lines.

name: Molokini
blurb: A crescent-shaped volcanic crater sticking up off Maui, its sunken half forming a sheltered bay. Look for the near-perfect half ring with clear turquoise water inside.

name: Story Bridge
blurb: A steel cantilever bridge from 1940, modeled on Montreal's Jacques Cartier Bridge, and Brisbane's best-known landmark. Look for it spanning a tight bend in the Brisbane River at the edge of the CBD.

name: The Gabba
blurb: Brisbane's cricket and AFL ground in Woolloongabba, the source of its nickname. Look for the round bowl just south of the river from the city's towers.

name: Rottnest Island
blurb: A low island about 12 miles off Fremantle, named "rat's nest" by a Dutch captain in 1696 who mistook its quokkas for giant rats. Look for pink and white salt lakes in the island's interior.

name: Cerro de la Silla
blurb: Monterrey's saddle-shaped mountain, nearly 6,000 ft high and the city's symbol. Look for the ridge with a dip between two summits on the east side of the city.

name: Badain Jaran Desert
blurb: Home to the tallest stationary sand dunes on Earth, some rising around 1,600 ft, with more than 100 small lakes tucked between them. Look for blue and green pools at the feet of giant dunes.

name: Rub' al Khali
blurb: The Empty Quarter: the largest continuous sand desert on Earth, bigger than France. Look for endless orange dunes, some the size of hills, with nothing human in sight but the odd oil field.

name: Svalbard
blurb: An Arctic archipelago where about 60% of the land is under glacier ice and polar bears roam. Look for white ice caps, dark mountains and fjords.

name: Cape Canaveral
blurb: America's main spaceport since the 1950s: Apollo 11 and the Space Shuttle launched from Kennedy Space Center next door. Look for the giant Vehicle Assembly Building and launch pads lined up along the beach.

name: Cape of Good Hope
blurb: Not Africa's southern tip, despite the legend, but the point where ships begin heading more east than south. Bartolomeu Dias rounded it in 1488. Look for the rocky end of the Cape Peninsula south of Table Mountain.

name: Danakil Desert
blurb: One of the hottest places on Earth, much of it below sea level, where salt is still mined by hand. Look for white salt flats and the neon yellow and green hot springs of Dallol.

name: Grand Erg Occidental
blurb: A vast sand sea in western Algeria, roughly the size of South Carolina. Look for a honeycomb of dunes with tall star dunes, ringed by oasis towns along its edges.

name: Mojave Desert
blurb: The smallest of North America's deserts and the home ground of the Joshua tree, with Las Vegas near its heart. Look for dry lake beds shining white between dark mountain ranges.

name: Painted Desert
blurb: Eroded mesas and hills in outback South Australia near Oodnadatta, streaked red, ochre and white. Look for flat-topped hills in bands of color on otherwise stony desert.

name: Simpson Desert
blurb: Long parallel red sand dunes, many running unbroken for dozens of miles, in the dead center of Australia. Look for orange stripes ruled across the land, with pale salt lakes between.

name: Sinai Peninsula
blurb: The triangle between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba, linking Africa and Asia. Its granite mountains reach over 8,000 ft at Mount Catherine; look for the two gulfs forming a V around it.

name: Ténéré Desert
blurb: The Tuareg name means desert, so this is the desert within the Sahara. It was home to the Tree of Ténéré, once called the most isolated tree on Earth, until a truck hit it in 1973. Look for endless pale sand.

name: Harding Icefield
blurb: About 700 square miles of ice capping the Kenai Mountains and feeding more than 30 glaciers. Look for a white plateau with black rock peaks poking through and glaciers spilling down to the fjords.

name: Juneau Icefield
blurb: About 1,500 square miles of ice behind Juneau, feeding the Mendenhall, Taku and dozens of other glaciers, and one reason no road leaves the city. Look for an unbroken white plateau running into British Columbia.

name: Aeolian Islands
blurb: Seven volcanic islands north of Sicily, including Stromboli, erupting almost constantly for at least 2,000 years. Look for cone-shaped islands, with Stromboli often trailing a plume.

name: Cyclades
blurb: About 220 islands that the ancient Greeks saw as a circle around sacred Delos. Santorini's flooded volcanic caldera is the standout. Look for dry brown islands scattered across deep blue sea.

name: Franz Josef Land
blurb: An archipelago of nearly 200 islands, almost all ice-covered, the northernmost land in Europe and Asia. Look for white domes and dark cliffs in a frozen sea.

name: Isle of Skye
blurb: Scotland's second-largest island, about 640 square miles, with the jagged black Cuillin ridge rising straight from the sea. Look for the arched Skye Bridge linking it to the mainland at Kyle of Lochalsh.

name: Kauaʻi
blurb: The oldest of the main Hawaiian islands, where Waimea Canyon cuts more than 3,000 ft deep and the Na Pali cliffs drop straight into the ocean. Look for deeply fluted green ridges along the north shore.

name: Lanzarote
blurb: Covered in black lava fields, with Timanfaya's volcanic cones from the 1730s eruptions. Look for dark lava and white villages, with vines planted in black ash pits.

name: Lord Howe Island
blurb: A volcanic remnant in the Tasman Sea with the world's southernmost coral reef. Nearby Ball's Pyramid, about 1,800 ft tall, is the world's tallest sea stack. Look for twin peaks at the island's south end.

name: Marquesas Islands
blurb: Jagged volcanic islands with almost no fringing reef, where Paul Gauguin spent his final years. Look for towering green peaks and sheer cliffs dropping straight into deep blue water.

name: Socotra
blurb: Isolated for millions of years, about a third of its plants grow nowhere else, including the umbrella-shaped dragon's blood tree. Lying closer to Somalia than to Yemen, it shows as a long, rugged island with white dunes along parts of its coast.

name: Tuamotus
blurb: The largest chain of atolls in the world, about 80 rings of coral spread across an area the size of Western Europe. Look for thin loops of white sand around turquoise lagoons.

name: Beachy Head
blurb: The highest chalk sea cliff in Britain, about 530 ft. A red-and-white striped lighthouse stands on the beach below. Look for the white cliff face of the Seven Sisters running west from Eastbourne.

name: Cap de Formentor
blurb: The wild northern tip of Mallorca, where cliffs rise more than 1,000 ft straight from the sea and a winding road leads to a lighthouse. Look for a long, narrow rocky spine jutting northeast into the Mediterranean.

name: Cape Byron
blurb: The easternmost point of mainland Australia, crowned by a white lighthouse above Byron Bay. Humpback whales pass close offshore on their winter migration. Look for a green headland with long curving surf beaches on both sides.

name: Cape Farewell
blurb: Greenland's southern tip, on an island at the end of the world's largest island, known for some of the windiest seas on Earth. Look for jagged mountains, glaciers and drifting ice.

name: Cape Reinga / Te Rerenga Wairua
blurb: In Māori tradition, the place where spirits of the dead leap into the sea to begin the journey to their homeland. Look for the white lighthouse on the tip and, on rough days, a line of clashing surf where the Tasman Sea meets the Pacific.

name: Cape Wrath
blurb: The northwest tip of mainland Britain, with no road link to the rest of the country and part of it used as a military bombing range. Look for empty moorland ending in high cliffs and a lone lighthouse.

name: Cape York
blurb: A headland in northwest Greenland where the Inuit made tools for centuries from iron meteorites, including a 31-ton fragment, Ahnighito, that Robert Peary hauled to New York in 1897. Look for a bare, icy coast.

name: Hel Peninsula
blurb: A sandspit about 22 miles long curling into the Baltic, in places only a few hundred feet wide. Look for the thin pale arc sealing off the Bay of Puck, with the town of Hel at its tip.

name: Land's End
blurb: The far western tip of mainland England, the traditional start of the 874-mile route to John o' Groats. Look for granite cliffs at the end of Cornwall, with the Longships lighthouse on a rock offshore.

name: North Cape
blurb: A sheer cliff about 1,000 ft high, sold for centuries as the northern tip of Europe, though a neighboring point is actually a bit farther north. In summer the sun never sets here. Look for a flat-topped plateau ending abruptly in the Barents Sea.

name: Arabian Desert
blurb: Covers most of the Arabian Peninsula, from rock and gravel plains to giant sand seas. Look for tan and orange desert, broken by dark lava fields and wadis that rarely see water.

name: Aralkum
blurb: The world's newest desert, on the dried bed of the Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest lake on Earth. Look for ghostly old shorelines and white salt where fishing fleets once sailed.

name: Black Rock Desert
blurb: The playa where Burning Man is held each summer, and where Thrust SSC set the land speed record of 763 mph in 1997. Look for a huge, flat, pale lake bed, and in late summer the ring of Black Rock City.

name: Gran Desierto de Altar
blurb: The largest active field of sand dunes in North America, at the head of the Gulf of California. Look for golden dunes wrapped around the dark lava and round craters of the Pinacate volcanic field.

name: Great Sandy Desert
blurb: Red parallel dunes across northwest Australia, home to Wolfe Creek Crater, a nearly perfect meteor crater. Look for orange dune stripes running for hundreds of miles toward the Indian Ocean.

name: Great Victoria Desert
blurb: Australia's largest desert, where Britain tested nuclear weapons at Maralinga in the 1950s. Look for red sand ridges and salt lakes running for hundreds of miles with no sign of people.

name: Judaean Desert
blurb: Drops from Jerusalem's hills about 4,000 ft down to the Dead Sea, the lowest land on Earth. The Dead Sea Scrolls were found here at Qumran; look for bare, creased hills ending at the Dead Sea's blue.

name: Kalahari Desert
blurb: Covers most of Botswana in red sand, though it gets enough rain for grass and acacia, so it's more dry savanna than true desert. Look for endless flat red-brown country dotted with shrubs and pans.

name: Karakum Desert
blurb: Covers about 70% of Turkmenistan. Near its center the Darvaza gas crater has been burning since 1971, the Door to Hell. Look for the Karakum Canal's green line cutting across the sand.

name: Khongoryn Els
blurb: The singing dunes of the Gobi, named for the hum the sand makes in wind, running for about 60 miles along the base of a mountain range. Look for a long tan band of tall dunes.

name: Kumtag Desert
blurb: A sand desert east of Lop Nur in western China, its dunes shaped by wind into feathery patterns. Look for pale sand rippled in fine, swept lines against dark gravel.

name: Libyan Desert
blurb: The eastern Sahara, one of the driest places on Earth, with the Great Sand Sea and the Gilf Kebir plateau. Look for long parallel dune ridges and a few oases in otherwise featureless ground.

name: Murzuq Desert
blurb: A great sand sea in southwest Libya, one of the most remote parts of the Sahara. Look for a vast field of orange dunes broken by dark rocky plateaus.

name: Negev
blurb: Covers more than half of Israel's land area. Its Makhtesh Ramon is a 25-mile erosion crater, not an impact; look for the long, sheer-walled depression in pale desert.

name: Nubian Desert
blurb: The sandstone desert east of the Nile in Sudan, where the river swings through its great S-bend. Look for a flat, featureless plain with the Nile's green strip curving along its western edge.

name: Salvador Dalí Desert
blurb: Named for rock formations that look lifted from a Dalí painting, in Bolivia's high Andes above 14,000 ft. Look for bare, rust and ochre ground beneath snow-dusted volcanoes near the Chilean border.

name: Sonoran Desert
blurb: The only place on Earth where saguaro cactus grows wild, and one of North America's hottest deserts. Look for jagged mountain ranges rising like islands from flat desert, with Phoenix and Tucson's grids between.

name: Wahiba Sands
blurb: A compact sand sea in Oman, with dunes running north to south and some rising a few hundred feet. Look for orange and honey-colored ridges ending near the Arabian Sea coast.

name: ad-Dahna Desert
blurb: A narrow arc of red sand roughly 800 miles long, linking the Nafud in the north to the Empty Quarter in the south. Look for a distinct band of red-orange dunes cutting across paler ground.

name: Bagley Icefield
blurb: More than 100 miles of ice along the crest of the Chugach and St. Elias Mountains, feeding the Bering Glacier, one of the largest in North America. Look for a long white highway of ice between dark ridges.

name: Barnes Ice Cap
blurb: A remnant of the Laurentide Ice Sheet that once buried most of Canada, still about 2,300 square miles of ice in central Baffin Island. Look for a long white dome in flat, lake-speckled tundra.

name: Quelccaya Ice Cap
blurb: One of the largest ice caps in the tropics, sitting at about 18,000 ft in the Peruvian Andes. Its ice cores record about 1,500 years of climate, and it is shrinking fast. Look for a flat white cap ending in steep ice cliffs.

name: Wapta Icefield
blurb: About 30 square miles of ice straddling the Continental Divide, feeding Peyto and Bow Glaciers and the headwaters of the Bow River. Look for the white cap above turquoise Peyto Lake along the Icefields Parkway.

name: Bikini Atoll
blurb: The US tested 23 nuclear weapons here, including Castle Bravo in 1954, the largest US blast ever. Look for a thin ring of islets around a lagoon, with the bomb crater as a dark blue hole on its northwest edge.

name: Corfu
blurb: A green, olive-covered Ionian island with a Venetian old town and a runway that runs right past a lagoon. Look for Kanoni and Mouse Island at the runway's end.

name: Fernando de Noronha
blurb: A Brazilian archipelago with clear water and a tall rock spire, Morro do Pico. Look for a small, green island with turquoise coves and that dark spire rising over it.

name: Funafuti
blurb: The capital atoll of Tuvalu, among the lowest-lying nations on Earth. The airstrip takes up a big share of the main island. Look for a thin coral ring around a wide lagoon.

name: Gran Canaria
blurb: Called a continent in miniature, it packs green ravines, a central volcanic peak and big dunes at Maspalomas. Look for a round island with pale sand dunes at its southern tip.

name: Ibiza
blurb: A Balearic island, part of a UNESCO site for its seagrass meadows. Look for a hilly island with sandy coves and the old walled town on a hill above the harbor.

name: Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego
blurb: Split between Chile and Argentina, it sits at the bottom of South America across the Strait of Magellan. Ushuaia, on its south shore, calls itself the southernmost city. Look for snowy mountains in the south and flat steppe in the north.

name: Kerguelen Islands
blurb: Nicknamed the Desolation Islands, a French territory far down in the windy Southern Ocean. Look for a ragged, fjord-cut coastline with a white ice cap on the west side.

name: Kiritimati
blurb: The largest coral atoll by land area, among the first places to see each new year. Britain tested hydrogen bombs here in 1957 and 1958. Look for a huge, pale lagoon with lakes inside the land ring.

name: Komodo Island
blurb: Home to the Komodo dragon, the largest living lizard, which can top 10 ft. Look for dry, golden-brown hills and coves with pink-tinged beaches.

name: Kuril Islands
blurb: A chain of about 56 volcanic islands stretching from Japan to Kamchatka, disputed since 1945. Look for a string of snowy cones and islands curving across the sea.

name: Lombok Island
blurb: Dominated by Mount Rinjani, at 12,224 ft one of Indonesia's highest volcanoes, with a crater lake inside it. Look for the big cone on the north side and the tiny Gili Islands off the northwest coast.

name: Mahé
blurb: The largest of the Seychelles, made of granite rather than coral, rare for an ocean island. Look for steep green hills and boulder-lined beaches, with the airport on reclaimed land.

name: Outer Hebrides
blurb: A chain of islands strung out for about 130 miles off Scotland's northwest coast, with Atlantic beaches of white sand and turquoise water. Look for Lewis, speckled with thousands of small dark lochans.

name: Saint Helena
blurb: A remote South Atlantic island where Napoleon was exiled and died in 1821. Look for steep, dark volcanic cliffs and a green interior.

name: São Miguel Island
blurb: The largest Azores island, known for the twin lakes of Sete Cidades in a volcanic crater, one blue and one green. Look for the round crater at the island's west end.

name: Zakynthos
blurb: Home to Navagio, the Shipwreck Beach, a rusted wreck on white sand inside a cove of sheer cliffs. Look for tall white limestone cliffs along the west coast and turquoise water at their base.

name: Akamas
blurb: A wild peninsula at Cyprus's western tip, largely protected and mostly empty of roads. Look for rugged green scrubland ending in white cliffs and the turtle-nesting beaches of Lara Bay.

name: Cabo Frio
blurb: A cape where cold, nutrient-rich water wells up from the deep, keeping the sea clear and chilly by Brazilian standards. Look for brilliant white sand, salt flats and lagoons behind a rocky island point.

name: Cabo da Roca
blurb: The westernmost point of mainland Europe, where cliffs rise more than 400 ft above the Atlantic. Look for a rocky promontory west of Sintra's wooded hills, with a red-roofed lighthouse near the edge.

name: Cap Corse
blurb: Corsica's mountainous northern finger, about 25 miles long and only about 6 to 9 miles wide. Look for a spine of green ridges with old Genoese watchtowers on the headlands and villages tucked into the coves.

name: Cap Gris Nez
blurb: The closest point in France to England, about 21 miles from the white cliffs of Dover. On a clear day look for England across the busiest shipping lane in the world, the Strait of Dover.

name: Cape Adare
blurb: A dark volcanic headland at the entrance to the Ross Sea, site of the first buildings on the Antarctic continent in 1899. It also hosts one of the largest Adélie penguin colonies.

name: Cape Agulhas
blurb: The true southern tip of Africa and the official dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Look for a low, rocky point with no dramatic cliffs, about 100 miles east of the Cape of Good Hope.

name: Cape Arkona
blurb: The northern tip of Rügen, Germany's largest island, with chalk cliffs over 100 ft high and a lighthouse. A Slavic temple fortress stood here until the Danes destroyed it in 1168; look for the white cliffs.

name: Cape Comorin
blurb: India's southern tip at Kanyakumari, where the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal meet. Look for two rocky islets just offshore, one holding the Vivekananda memorial and the other a 133-ft statue of the poet Thiruvalluvar.

name: Cape Dezhnyov
blurb: The easternmost point of mainland Asia, facing Alaska across the 50-mile-wide Bering Strait. Look for the rocky headland and the two Diomede Islands offshore, one Russian, one American.

name: Cape Finisterre
blurb: The Romans thought it was the end of the world, and its name says so. Pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago still walk on here to burn their boots. Look for a rocky granite headland on Galicia's wild Atlantic coast.

name: Cape Gata
blurb: The southernmost point of Cyprus, almost entirely occupied by RAF Akrotiri, a British sovereign base. Look for the runway and the large salt lake just north of the cape.

name: Cape Guardafui
blurb: The tip of the Horn of Africa, where the Gulf of Aden meets the Indian Ocean. Look for a sharp, arid point of land with brown mountains ending at the sea.

name: Cape Hatteras
blurb: The Graveyard of the Atlantic: shifting shoals here have wrecked hundreds of ships. Its striped lighthouse, the tallest brick lighthouse in the US, was moved 2,900 ft inland in 1999. Look for the sharp elbow where the Outer Banks turn west.

name: Cape Leeuwin
blurb: Australia's most southwesterly point, where Australians mark the meeting of the Indian and Southern Oceans. Look for a rocky cape with a white lighthouse at the southern end of the Margaret River coast.

name: Cape Mendocino
blurb: The westernmost point of California, where three tectonic plates meet at the Mendocino Triple Junction, making it one of the most earthquake-prone spots in the US. Look for bare green ridges falling to a rugged shore.

name: Cape Ortegal
blurb: The point where the Bay of Biscay meets the open Atlantic. Some of Europe's highest sea cliffs rise nearby, around 2,000 ft. Look for dark rock headlands with jagged islets off the tip.

name: Cape St. Vincent
blurb: Europe's southwestern corner, where ships rounding Iberia have changed course for millennia and several naval battles were fought offshore. Look for flat-topped cliffs at the point where the Algarve coast turns north.

name: Cape of Creus
blurb: The easternmost point of mainland Spain, a wind-blasted rocky peninsula whose twisted shapes inspired Salvador Dalí, who lived nearby. Look for bare, crinkled rock ending in the Mediterranean north of the Bay of Roses.

name: Capelinhos
blurb: A 1957 to 1958 undersea eruption built new land onto the island of Faial and buried most of the local lighthouse in ash. Look for a bare gray-brown wedge of volcanic cone and dunes at the island's western tip.

name: Dyrhólaey
blurb: Iceland's southern headland, a 400-ft promontory with a huge natural sea arch big enough for boats. Look for the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks just east.

name: Grenen
blurb: Denmark's northern tip, a shifting sand spit where the Skagerrak and Kattegat seas collide. Look for waves meeting at an angle along a visible line off the point.

name: Mull of Kintyre
blurb: The tip of the Kintyre peninsula, immortalized in Paul McCartney's 1977 song, just 12 miles from Northern Ireland. Look for high, rounded moorland ending at the sea, with Ireland's coast clearly visible across the channel.

name: Point Barrow
blurb: The northernmost point of the United States, a thin gravel spit poking into the Arctic Ocean beyond Utqiaġvik. Look for the spit dividing the Chukchi and Beaufort seas, often edged with sea ice.

name: Pointe du Raz
blurb: The westernmost tip of Brittany, a rocky blade pointing into the Atlantic over notoriously violent currents. Look for the Île de Sein and lighthouses strung out in the sea beyond the point.

name: Punta de Tarifa
blurb: The southernmost point of mainland Europe, about 9 miles from Morocco across the Strait of Gibraltar. Look for a small island linked to the town by a causeway, with Africa's mountains plainly visible beyond.

name: Sounion
blurb: Athens's southern tip, crowned by the 5th-century BC Temple of Poseidon on a cliff above the Aegean. Lord Byron carved his name in one of its columns; look for the white columns on the headland.

name: Alvord Desert
blurb: A dry lake bed in the shadow of Steens Mountain, which rises nearly a mile above it. Kitty O'Neil set a women's land speed record here in 1976. Look for a pale, flat playa below a steep escarpment.

name: Baja California Desert
blurb: The Vizcaíno and central Baja deserts, home to the boojum tree, which grows wild almost nowhere else. Look for the long peninsula's dry spine, with the Pacific on one side and the Gulf of California on the other.

name: Black Desert
blurb: Orange sand peppered with black volcanic stone, and hills capped in dark rock, south of Egypt's Bahariya Oasis. Look for dark-topped cone hills scattered across tan desert.

name: Chalbi Desert
blurb: A dry lake bed in northern Kenya, east of Lake Turkana, that floods briefly in the rains and bakes hard the rest of the year. Look for a pale, flat pan ringed by lava hills.

name: Channeled Scablands
blurb: Carved by ice-age floods when glacial Lake Missoula repeatedly burst its ice dam. Dry Falls, once a waterfall about 3.5 miles wide, is here; look for bare rock channels and buttes scoured into wheat country.

name: Chara Sands
blurb: A patch of real sand dunes in the middle of Siberian taiga, surrounded by larch forest and permafrost below the Kodar Mountains. Look for a pale yellow island in dark green, often snow-covered in winter.

name: Chihuahuan Desert
blurb: The largest desert in North America, much of it high plateau, from Big Bend into central Mexico. Look for creosote flats and mountain ranges, with the Rio Grande cutting deep canyons.

name: Colorado Desert
blurb: The low, hot western edge of the Sonoran Desert, much of it below sea level around the Salton Sea. Look for the bright green grid of the Imperial Valley's fields ending sharply at bare sand.

name: Eastern Desert
blurb: Rugged mountains between the Nile and the Red Sea, where Romans quarried purple porphyry and granite. Look for dark, jagged ranges cut by dry wadis, with the green Nile on one edge and blue sea on the other.

name: El Djouf
blurb: A remote sand sea in eastern Mauritania and Mali, among the emptiest corners of the Sahara. Look for orange dune fields with no roads, towns or green at all.

name: Gibson Desert
blurb: Named after Alfred Gibson, who vanished here during an 1874 expedition. Gravel plains and red sand in the heart of Western Australia; look for rust-colored ground dotted with spinifex.

name: Harrat al-Sham
blurb: A vast field of black basalt lava spanning Syria, Jordan and Saudi Arabia. It's dotted with ancient stone hunting traps called desert kites; look for dark, boulder-strewn ground.

name: Kaokoveld
blurb: Remote northwest Namibia, home of the Himba people and desert-adapted elephants, running down to the Skeleton Coast. Look for red mountains and dry riverbeds fading into fog off the Atlantic.

name: Kebira Crater
blurb: A ring about 19 miles across straddling the Egypt-Libya border, spotted on satellite images in the mid-2000s and proposed as an impact crater, though field visits have cast doubt on that. Look for a faint circular rim in flat sand.

name: Kyzyl Kum
blurb: Its name means red sand: a desert between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers, home to Muruntau, one of the largest open-pit gold mines on Earth. Look for reddish sand and a giant terraced pit.

name: La Guajira Desert
blurb: The northern tip of South America, where cactus scrub and sand dunes run straight into the Caribbean. Home of the Wayuu people. Look for tan desert meeting turquoise sea with almost no green.

name: Lop Desert
blurb: Site of China's nuclear test grounds and the dried-up Lop Nur lake, whose rings of old shorelines look like a giant ear from space. Look for that ear: concentric pale bands on brown desert.

name: Maspalomas Dunes
blurb: A small field of real sand dunes at the southern tip of Gran Canaria, wedged between resorts and the Atlantic. Look for a golden patch of rippled sand beside the beach and lighthouse.

name: Ramlat al-Sab`atayn
blurb: A sand desert in central Yemen, between Marib, once capital of the kingdom of Sheba, and the Hadramawt valley. Look for orange dunes with oil field roads cutting across them.

name: Registan Desert
blurb: A sea of red-orange sand dunes in southern Afghanistan between Kandahar and the Pakistan border. Look for the reddish dune ridges ending abruptly at the green Helmand River valley.

name: Sechura Desert
blurb: A coastal desert in northern Peru where it almost never rains, except in strong El Niño years when floods can briefly create a lake. Look for tan sand running to the Pacific, with green river valleys crossing it.

name: Sturt Stony Desert
blurb: Gibber plains covered in polished stones that shine in the sun, named for explorer Charles Sturt, who crossed it in the 1840s. Look for dark, shiny, flat ground between red dunes.

name: Syrian Desert
blurb: Steppe and gravel desert spanning Syria, Iraq and Jordan, with the ancient oasis city of Palmyra near its heart. Look for flat brown plains, dry wadis and the odd green oasis.

name: Tanami Desert
blurb: One of Australia's most remote deserts, red sand and spinifex in the Northern Territory, crossed by a single dirt track. Look for red ground with dull green clumps of spinifex.

name: Tanezrouft
blurb: The name means land of thirst: one of the flattest, emptiest parts of the Sahara, with no water and almost no life. Look for featureless gravel plain stretching to every horizon.

name: Andaman Islands
blurb: A chain of more than 300 islands in the Bay of Bengal, closer to Myanmar than to mainland India. Look for green, forested islands edged with coral reefs and turquoise shallows.

name: Antigua
blurb: Famous for claiming 365 beaches, one for every day of the year. Look for a scalloped coastline of white coves around English Harbour, where Nelson's 18th-century dockyard still stands.

name: Ascension Island
blurb: A volcanic island in the mid-Atlantic, once barren, where Green Mountain was planted with trees in the 1800s. Look for a red-black lava island with a green summit.

name: Bornholm
blurb: A Danish island far out in the Baltic, closer to Sweden than to Denmark, known for its medieval round churches. Look for a granite north coast and farm fields in a patchwork across the rest.

name: Cephalonia
blurb: The largest Ionian island, nearly leveled by an earthquake in 1953. Look for the peak of Mount Ainos and a long, ragged coastline with turquoise bays.

name: Chagos Archipelago
blurb: Remote coral atolls in the middle of the Indian Ocean, including Diego Garcia, a US-UK military base. Look for thin rings of reef and sand around pale lagoons in deep blue water.

name: Fuerteventura
blurb: The closest Canary Island to Africa, about 60 miles away, known for its beaches and dunes. Look for a long, dry, brown island with pale dunes in the northeast.

name: Guam
blurb: A US territory in the western Pacific with the Mariana Trench, the deepest ocean on Earth, just offshore. Look for a long island with a coral-fringed coast and Andersen Air Force Base on the north plateau.

name: Heligoland
blurb: Germany's only true offshore island, a red sandstone block about 40 miles out in the North Sea. In 1947 the British set off one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history here. Look for red cliffs and the sea stack Lange Anna.

name: Hvar
blurb: A long, thin island on the Dalmatian coast known for lavender fields and its walled harbor town. Look for a narrow spine of rocky, scrubby hills with small coves along the edges.

name: Isle of Arran
blurb: Called "Scotland in miniature" because the Highland Boundary Fault crosses it: rugged mountains in the north, rolling farmland in the south. Look for granite Goatfell, 2,866 ft, above the Firth of Clyde.

name: Isles of Scilly
blurb: About 140 low granite islands and rocks some 28 miles off Land's End, only five of them inhabited. Look for white sand and shallow turquoise water between the islands, more Caribbean than Cornish.

name: Juan Fernández Islands
blurb: Alexander Selkirk was marooned here for four years in the early 1700s, the inspiration for Robinson Crusoe; one island now bears that name. Look for steep green peaks rising from empty ocean.

name: Kangaroo Island
blurb: Australia's third-largest island. Bushfires in 2019 and 2020 burned about half of it. Look for a long, flat island with bare cliffs and scrub along the south coast.

name: Kavaratti
blurb: Capital of Lakshadweep, India's smallest union territory, a coral island in the Arabian Sea. Look for a thin, palm-covered island beside a turquoise lagoon.

name: Ko Samui
blurb: A Thai island in the Gulf of Thailand, known for coconut palms and beaches. Look for a green, hilly island with white beaches and a small airport amid the palms.

name: Kodiak Island
blurb: The second-largest island in the US, about 3,600 square miles, home to the giant Kodiak brown bear. Look for a rugged, fjord-cut coastline and green mountains rising straight from the sea.

name: Langkawi
blurb: An archipelago of 99 islands off Malaysia's northwest coast, known for limestone peaks and a curved sky bridge. Look for jungle-covered hills and mangrove-lined inlets.

name: Malta
blurb: A small, dense island nation whose capital, Valletta, was founded in 1566 by the Knights of St. John. Look for honey-colored stone towns, deep harbors and terraced fields.

name: Marajó
blurb: A massive island at the mouth of the Amazon, about the size of Switzerland. Look for flat, muddy wetlands on the east and forest on the west, with brown river water all around.

name: Menorca
blurb: A Balearic island and UNESCO biosphere reserve, with prehistoric stone monuments. Look for a low, green island with deep harbors, including Mahón's long inlet.

name: Milos
blurb: A volcanic island where the Venus de Milo was found in 1820. Look for the big horseshoe-shaped bay, a flooded caldera, and bright white rock along the north coast at Sarakiniko.

name: Mykonos
blurb: A dry, rocky Cycladic island famous for its whitewashed town and line of windmills. Look for clusters of white cubes against brown hills and a ring of beaches.

name: Nantucket
blurb: The center of the whaling trade in the early 1800s, now a summer haven with strict rules on building style. Look for the low, sandy, crescent-shaped island south of Cape Cod.

name: Okinawa
blurb: The largest Ryukyu island, scene of the bloodiest battle in the Pacific in 1945, now home to several big US bases. Look for a long, narrow island fringed with coral reefs.

name: Orkney Islands
blurb: About 70 islands off Scotland's north tip, home to Skara Brae, a stone village older than the pyramids. Look for Scapa Flow, the sheltered bay ringed by islands where the German fleet scuttled itself in 1919.

name: Phú Quốc
blurb: Vietnam's largest island, lying closer to Cambodia than to the Vietnamese mainland, and famous for its fish sauce. Look for long beaches on the west coast and forested hills running down the spine.

name: Rodrigues
blurb: A small volcanic island in the Indian Ocean, part of Mauritius, about 350 miles east of the main island. Look for a hilly island surrounded by an unusually large lagoon.

name: Rügen
blurb: Germany's largest island, known for its white chalk cliffs on the Baltic. Look for a coastline of lagoons and peninsulas, with bright white cliffs along the northeast shore.

name: Saipan
blurb: The capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, scene of a brutal 1944 battle. Look for a long island with a white-sand lagoon on its west side and cliffs on the north tip.

name: Shetland Islands
blurb: Britain's northernmost islands, about 100 of them, closer to Bergen than to Edinburgh. Look for long narrow inlets (voes) cutting deep into treeless green-brown land.

name: Surtsey
blurb: Born from the sea in a volcanic eruption that began in 1963. Scientists keep it off-limits to watch how life colonizes new land. Look for a small dark island south of the Westman Islands.

name: Sylt
blurb: Germany's northernmost island, a long, thin strip of beaches and dunes linked to the mainland by a rail-only causeway. Look for its T-shape against the North Sea and the straight causeway line.

name: Tarawa
blurb: In 1943 one of the bloodiest battles of the Pacific was fought over a tiny islet here. Look for a narrow, L-shaped strip of islands around a large lagoon.

name: Upolu
blurb: Samoa's most populous island, home to the capital Apia and To Sua, a sinkhole swimming hole. Look for a green, mountainous island with coral reefs along the coast.

name: Wake Island
blurb: A V-shaped atoll of three islets around a lagoon, under 3 square miles of land in the middle of the Pacific. Its Marine garrison held off a Japanese invasion for two weeks in December 1941. Look for the long runway along the southern arm.

name: Yakushima
blurb: A round, mountainous island covered with ancient cedar forests, some trees thought to be thousands of years old. It inspired the forests in Princess Mononoke. Look for steep green peaks rising straight from the sea.

name: Cabo Polonio
blurb: A village with no roads, no grid power and no running water, reached only by four-wheel-drive across the dunes, and home to a big sea lion colony. Look for a rocky point and lighthouse in a sea of bare sand dunes.

name: Cabo de la Vela
blurb: A remote desert cape on Colombia's La Guajira peninsula, sacred to the Wayuu people and a kitesurfing spot. Look for red-brown desert meeting turquoise Caribbean water with almost no green.

name: Cap Bon
blurb: A peninsula reaching northeast toward Sicily, about 90 miles away, separating the Gulf of Tunis from the Gulf of Hammamet. Look for a green finger of farmland and hills pointing across the Mediterranean.

name: Cap Fréhel
blurb: Pink sandstone cliffs about 230 ft high on Brittany's north coast, topped by heather moorland and a lighthouse. Look for Fort la Latte, a medieval castle on the next headland east.

name: Cap-Vert
blurb: The westernmost point of mainland Africa, a hook-shaped peninsula holding Dakar. Look for the city packed onto a triangle of land pointing into the Atlantic, with Gorée Island just offshore.

name: Cape Ann
blurb: Rocky headland north of Boston holding Gloucester, one of America's oldest fishing ports, and Rockport. Look for a granite knob jutting into the Atlantic with a busy harbor on its southwest side and old quarry ponds inland.

name: Cape Aya
blurb: A rocky headland on Crimea's south coast, with steep wooded cliffs dropping into the Black Sea. Look for a forested ridge ending in pale cliffs between Balaklava and the coastal resort towns.

name: Cape Bojador
blurb: For medieval European sailors this was the edge of the known world, with shoals and currents said to make return impossible, until Gil Eanes rounded it in 1434. Look for flat Saharan desert ending in a low bulge of coast.

name: Cape Chelyuskin
blurb: The northernmost point of mainland Eurasia, on the Taymyr Peninsula at about 77.7 degrees north. Look for low, barren tundra meeting sea ice for most of the year.

name: Cape Columbia
blurb: The northernmost point of land in Canada, about 475 miles from the North Pole. Robert Peary set off from here in 1909 on his disputed dash to the Pole. Look for a low ice-bound headland at the edge of the Arctic Ocean pack.

name: Cape Cross
blurb: Home to one of the world's largest Cape fur seal colonies, tens of thousands strong, on the bleak Skeleton Coast. Portuguese explorer Diogo Cão planted a stone cross here in 1486. Look for a small point where tan desert meets cold surf.

name: Cape Fear
blurb: Named by sailors for Frying Pan Shoals, which reach miles offshore. It marks the mouth of the Cape Fear River below Wilmington. Look for the triangular point of Bald Head Island with pale shoals trailing out to sea.

name: Cape Froward
blurb: The southernmost point of mainland South America, on the Strait of Magellan. Look for a forested headland topped by a large cross, with the strait bending sharply here.

name: Cape Greco
blurb: The southeastern tip of Cyprus, a low limestone headland of sea caves and natural arches beside the resort of Ayia Napa. Look for pale rock and clear turquoise water around the point.

name: Cape Maleas
blurb: The southeastern tip of the Peloponnese, so feared for its winds that ancient sailors said to forget home when rounding it. Look for a steep, bare headland plunging into the sea.

name: Cape Matapan
blurb: The southernmost point of mainland Greece, at the tip of the Mani peninsula. Ancient Greeks placed an entrance to the underworld here; look for the bare, rocky finger reaching into deep blue water.

name: Cape Morris Jesup
blurb: Greenland's northernmost mainland point, at about 83.6 degrees north, one of the closest points of land to the North Pole. Look for barren ground meeting permanent sea ice.

name: Cape Prince of Wales
blurb: The westernmost point of mainland North America, only about 50 miles from Siberia across the Bering Strait. Look for the Diomede Islands in the strait between the two continents.

name: Cape Race
blurb: Its Marconi wireless station picked up the Titanic's distress calls in April 1912 and relayed them to the world. Look for the southeast tip of Newfoundland's Avalon Peninsula, a bare headland with a lighthouse, often wrapped in fog.

name: Cape Spear
blurb: The easternmost point of North America outside Greenland, just southeast of St. John's. Its 1836 lighthouse is the oldest surviving in Newfoundland. Look for a rocky knuckle of land facing the open Atlantic, next to the narrow harbor mouth of St. John's.

name: Cape Sōya
blurb: Japan's northernmost point, at the tip of Hokkaido. Sakhalin, Russia, is about 27 miles across the strait; look for it on the horizon on a clear day.

name: Cape Zhelaniya
blurb: The northern tip of Novaya Zemlya, the Russian Arctic island chain where the Soviet Union tested the Tsar Bomba. Its name means Cape of Desire; look for a bare, ice-fringed headland between the Barents and Kara seas.

name: Capo Vaticano
blurb: A granite headland on Calabria's Tyrrhenian coast with white beaches and clear water. On a clear day look for Stromboli's volcanic cone out to sea.

name: Cà Mau Peninsula
blurb: The southern tip of Vietnam, a flat maze of mangroves, canals and shrimp ponds that keeps growing seaward from Mekong silt. Look for a dense green fringe of forest and a checkerboard of brown ponds.

name: Kaliakra
blurb: A narrow cape on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, with red limestone cliffs about 230 ft high and the ruins of a medieval fortress on top. Look for the long, thin finger of land pointing into the sea.

name: Malin Head
blurb: The northernmost point of the island of Ireland, on Donegal's Inishowen peninsula, a regular name in BBC shipping forecasts. Look for a bare green headland facing open Atlantic.

name: Mizen Head
blurb: Ireland's southwesternmost point, a cliff headland where an arched footbridge crosses a deep gorge to an old signal station. Look for the rugged tip of the peninsula and the open Atlantic beyond.

name: Mull of Galloway
blurb: The southernmost point of Scotland, a cliff-bound headland with a white lighthouse. Look for the hammerhead tip of the Rhins peninsula, with Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man visible on clear days.

name: Pointe du Hoc
blurb: A cliff between Omaha and Utah beaches that US Army Rangers scaled with ropes and ladders on D-Day, June 6, 1944. Look for the ground still pitted with bomb craters on top.

name: Scala dei Turchi
blurb: A brilliant white marl cliff on Sicily's south coast, eroded into natural steps. Look for the white staircase against the blue sea near Realmonte, west of Agrigento.

name: South East Cape
blurb: The southernmost point of mainland Tasmania, facing the Southern Ocean with nothing beyond but Antarctica. Look for wild forested coastline with no roads, inside the Southwest National Park.

name: Betpak-Dala
blurb: A vast clay and stone desert in central Kazakhstan, between Lake Balkhash and the Chu River. Look for flat, gray-brown plains with almost nothing on them.

name: Bolsón de Mapimí
blurb: A closed desert basin in the Chihuahuan Desert, with no outlet to the sea. Part of it is the so-called Zone of Silence, subject of radio-blackout legends. Look for pale dry lake beds between bare ranges.

name: Cholistan Desert
blurb: Sand desert in Pakistan's Punjab, running into India's Thar. Look for tan dunes south of the irrigated plains, and the massive square walls of Derawar Fort.

name: Dasht-e Margo
blurb: Its name means Desert of Death: a barren gravel and sand plain in southwest Afghanistan. Look for flat, tan emptiness cut by the green thread of the Helmand River.

name: Gurbantünggüt Desert
blurb: China's largest area of fixed dunes, held in place by saxaul shrubs, in the Junggar Basin north of the Tian Shan. Look for gray-green speckled dunes north of Ürümqi.

name: Kharan Desert
blurb: A sand desert in Balochistan where Pakistan carried out one of its 1998 nuclear tests. Look for tan dune fields between dark, rugged mountain ranges.

name: Kubuqi Desert
blurb: A sand desert inside the Yellow River's great northern loop, now a showcase for tree planting and solar farms, including one laid out in the shape of a galloping horse. Look for tree lines and panels on sand.

name: Little Sandy Desert
blurb: Red dunes and spinifex in Western Australia, crossed by the Canning Stock Route, a famously rough outback track. Look for parallel orange dune ridges and white salt lakes.

name: Monegros Desert
blurb: A semi-desert in Aragon, eroded into gullies and badlands that look more like Arizona than Spain. Look for bare, pale, creased hills between irrigated fields.

name: Monte Desert
blurb: A scrubby desert in the rain shadow of the Andes, stretching through western Argentina around San Juan and Mendoza. Look for gray-green brush and dry riverbeds, with irrigated vineyards in green patches.

name: Mu Us Desert
blurb: Once shifting sand on the Ordos Plateau, now largely stabilized by decades of tree and grass planting. Look for a patchwork of green and pale sand, with planted grids holding dunes in place.

name: Muyunkum Desert
blurb: A sand desert in southern Kazakhstan between the Chu and Talas rivers. Look for low, scrub-covered dune ridges stretching toward the mountains on the Kyrgyz border.

name: Owyhee Desert
blurb: High sagebrush desert where Nevada, Idaho and Oregon meet, cut by deep river canyons. Look for gray-green plateaus split by dark, winding gorges, with almost no roads.

name: Ryn Desert
blurb: Sand between the Volga and Ural rivers on the Caspian lowland, much of it below sea level. Look for pale sand patches and salt pans in flat steppe north of the Caspian.

name: Saryesik-Atyrau Desert
blurb: A sand desert south of Lake Balkhash, crossed by long parallel dune ridges. Look for ribbed sand running toward the lake, with the green delta of the Ili River on one side.

name: Smoke Creek Desert
blurb: A flat playa north of Reno, next door to Pyramid Lake and the Black Rock Desert. Look for a pale dry lake bed between bare ranges, sometimes holding a sheet of shallow water.

name: Strzelecki Desert
blurb: Parallel red dunes in the corner where South Australia, Queensland and New South Wales meet, crossed by the Strzelecki Track. Look for orange ridges with pale clay flats between them.

name: Thal
blurb: A sandy desert between the Indus and Jhelum rivers in Pakistan's Punjab, now partly greened by irrigation canals. Look for dunes giving way to straight-lined fields along the canals.

name: Tirari Desert
blurb: Red dunes and salt lakes east of Lake Eyre, whose dry beds have yielded fossils of extinct giant animals. Look for parallel dunes running between bright white salt pans.

name: Cambria Icefield
blurb: An icefield in the Coast Mountains above Stewart, BC, and Hyder, Alaska. Look for white ice crowning jagged peaks with glaciers spilling into green valleys.

name: Flade Isblink
blurb: An ice cap in far northeast Greenland, separate from the main ice sheet. Look for a white dome rising from bare brown coastal land.

name: Santa Ines Island Icefield
blurb: Caps Santa Inés Island off the western mouth of the Strait of Magellan. Look for white ice crowning dark rugged mountains surrounded by channels.

name: Barbuda
blurb: A flat, low limestone island known for its pink-sand beaches and a huge frigatebird colony. Hurricane Irma forced the whole island to evacuate in 2017. Look for a long lagoon on its west side.

name: Chios
blurb: Known as the only place in the world where mastic trees yield their prized resin. Look for a big, mountainous island just a few miles off the Turkish coast.

name: Clipperton Island
blurb: The only coral atoll in the eastern Pacific, a lonely ring of land around a closed lagoon about 670 miles off Mexico. Look for a thin loop of sand and a dark lagoon.

name: Djerba
blurb: A flat island off Tunisia, said to be where Odysseus met the lotus-eaters, and where Star Wars filmed Tatooine scenes. Look for a low, sandy island linked to the mainland by a causeway.

name: Gotland
blurb: Sweden's largest island, home to Visby, whose medieval town walls still circle the old town. Look for a flat, limestone island with sea stacks along the coast.

name: Isole Tremiti
blurb: A tiny archipelago in the Adriatic off Italy's Gargano coast. Look for a few small, pine-covered rocky islands with sheer cliffs and clear water.

name: Karpathos
blurb: A long, mountainous island between Rhodes and Crete, where traditional villages still keep old dress and dialect. Look for a rocky spine running north to south.

name: Kos
blurb: Home island of Hippocrates, the father of medicine. Look for a long, low island lying parallel to Turkey's Bodrum Peninsula, just a few miles away.

name: Lampedusa
blurb: Italy's southernmost island, closer to Tunisia than to Sicily. Look for a flat, bare limestone island with cliffs on its north side and pale coves on the south.

name: Lesbos
blurb: Greece's third-largest island, home of the poet Sappho and a petrified forest more than 15 million years old. Look for two deep bays cutting nearly through the island.

name: Long Island
blurb: About 118 miles long, the longest island in the contiguous US. Look for its fish shape stretching east from New York City, with long barrier beaches on the south shore.

name: Macquarie Island
blurb: The only place on Earth where rock from the deep ocean mantle is exposed above sea level, home to millions of penguins. Look for a long, thin island in the Southern Ocean.

name: North Sentinel Island
blurb: Home to the Sentinelese, one of the last uncontacted peoples on Earth, who have repelled outsiders for centuries. Visiting is illegal. Look for a small, flat, forested island ringed by a wide coral reef.

name: Patmos
blurb: Where St. John is said to have written the Book of Revelation. Look for a small, ragged island with a thin waist and a fortified monastery on the hilltop above the harbor.

name: Saaremaa
blurb: Estonia's largest island, home to the Kaali crater field, made by a meteorite impact a few thousand years ago. Look for a flat, forested island with a ragged coastline.

name: Samos
blurb: Birthplace of Pythagoras, who has a town named after him here, about a mile from the Turkish coast. Look for green mountains, unusual for the Aegean, and a narrow strait.

name: Sark
blurb: A tiny Channel Island where cars are banned and people get around by tractor, bicycle and horse cart. Look for a green plateau ringed by sheer cliffs, joined at a high, narrow isthmus.

name: Terschelling
blurb: One of the Dutch Wadden Islands, mostly dunes and nature reserve. Look for a long, sandy island with tidal mudflats on its south side and North Sea beaches on its north.

name: Tobago
blurb: A small Caribbean island north of Trinidad, with one of the oldest protected rainforests in the Western Hemisphere, set aside in 1776. Look for a ridged green spine.

name: Wrangel Island
blurb: The last place woolly mammoths lived, until about 4,000 years ago, and now home to one of the densest populations of polar bear dens. Look for a bare tundra island in the Arctic Ocean.

name: Almería greenhouses (Sea of Plastic)
blurb: Roughly 150 square miles of plastic-roofed greenhouses that grow a big share of Europe's winter vegetables. Look for a white sheet covering the coastal plain around El Ejido, bright enough to reflect sunlight back up.

name: Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport
blurb: Qingdao's airport since 2021, replacing Liuting. Look for the starfish terminal, five spokes off a central hub, between two parallel runways in flat farmland northwest of the city.

name: Techo International Airport
blurb: Phnom Penh's new airport, opened in 2025 about 12 miles south of the city on reclaimed wetland. Look for the long terminal beside a new runway, all inside a ring road cut into rice paddies.

name: Permian Basin gas flares
blurb: The most productive oil field in the US burns off gas it cannot pipe away, so after dark West Texas and southeastern New Mexico glitter far from any town. Look for a dense scatter of lights across otherwise empty desert.

name: Bakken gas flares
blurb: At the height of the North Dakota oil boom so much gas was flared that the empty prairie around Williston glowed in night satellite images like a big city. Look for a wide scatter of bright dots with no town attached.

name: South Pars gas field flares
blurb: South Pars, shared with Qatar's North Field, is part of the largest natural gas field on Earth. At night the refineries along Iran's Gulf coast flare in clusters of bright orange points; look for them on the shore.

name: Niger Delta gas flares
blurb: Oil fields across the delta burn off unwanted natural gas around the clock, a practice Nigeria has promised to end for decades. After dark look for scattered orange points across the swamps, brighter than the villages around them.

name: Khanty-Mansiysk oil field flares
blurb: Western Siberia's oil heartland, among the biggest oil-producing regions on Earth. At night gas flares burn as scattered bright orange points across dark taiga and swamp, far from any town.

name: Westland greenhouses
blurb: One of the densest glasshouse districts on Earth, between The Hague and Rotterdam. At night grow lights make it glow, often orange or pink, so brightly the sky above lights up; look for a vivid blob among the cities.

name: Nile Valley lights
blurb: After dark, Egypt is basically one line: the towns along the Nile light up a thin bright strip running hundreds of miles through black desert. Look for that ribbon, widening into a glowing fan toward Cairo.

name: India-Pakistan border lights
blurb: Floodlights along the fenced border make an orange line hundreds of miles long, one of the few national borders you can actually see from the air. Look for the unbroken strand of light cutting across the dark Thar Desert.
